title: Stepped run silently collapses to ONE atomic dispatch when every break phase is trimmed — per-group settings and group sequencing are discarded
area: AREA 1 — Queue construction (queue/queue_engine.py get_enabled_rooms_in_order + build_queue_from_managed_rooms, and the planning path that feeds them: planning/run_plan.py _build_effective_start_plan / _build_steps_phases / _build_dispatch_phases, profiles/room_profiles.py resolve+gate, rooms/access_graph.py exclusion, rooms/room_defaults.py + adapters/roborock)
observed_behavior:
`_build_steps_phases` ends with a fallback:
```
if not any(p.get("phase_type") in _BREAKS or p.get("phase_type") == "zone" for p in collapsed):
    all_ids = [rid for p in collapsed for rid in p.get("queue_room_ids", [])]
    return self._build_dispatch_phases(..., managed_rooms=effective_rooms,
                                       queue_room_ids=all_ids or sorted(included_room_ids), ...)
```
Two compounding defects.

(a) `all_ids` is ALWAYS `[]`. The room_group phases in `collapsed` come from `_build_dispatch_phases` -> engine `build_payload`, and every engine returns exactly `{vacuum_entity_id, map_id, payload, resolved_rooms, room_count}` (queue_engine.py:357-363; dispatch_engines.py:211-217, 273-280, 390-396). There is no `queue_room_ids` key on a dispatch phase — only the charge_wait/wait/zone phases set it (run_plan.py:851,858,877). So `all_ids or sorted(included_room_ids)` unconditionally takes the right-hand branch.

(b) The fallback passes `managed_rooms=effective_rooms` — the GLOBAL room view — discarding the `group_managed` per-group overlay built at run_plan.py:834-841, and merges every group into a single phase.

Reachability: line 1352 only enters `_build_steps_phases` when `_run_steps` contains a charge_wait/wait/zone, but the trim at 884-887 then pops LEADING and TRAILING charge_wait/wait, and an unresolvable zone is `continue`d at 872. So a profile `[charge_wait(100), groupA, groupB]` -> after trim `[dispatchA, dispatchB]` -> no breaks -> collapse to one phase.
user_impact: A saved run profile such as "charge to 100%, then bedrooms on quiet, then kitchen on max" runs as a single batch. On Roborock the per-phase `global_pre_calls` (fan / mop-intensity select, adapters/roborock/adapter.py:132-153,366) then fire ONCE max-wins over the merged room set, so the bedrooms are physically vacuumed at max suction instead of quiet — and a mixed vacuum/mop profile falls into the `mixed_mode_water_policy: safest` branch and under-mops instead of running the two groups at their own water levels. Where the same room appears in two groups ("vacuum the kitchen, then mop the kitchen" — the case _build_steps_phases exists to support) the room is dispatched ONCE with the last group's settings, so the vacuum pass never happens. No error is shown; preflight reports the run as ready.
guards_checked: run_plan.py:884-887 trim (`_BREAKS` is charge_wait/wait only — it does NOT protect against the collapse that follows); run_plan.py:898-901 `if not any(...)` (correctly includes "zone", but that only decides WHETHER to collapse, not what it collapses to); run_plan.py:828 `if not group_ids: continue` (only skips empty groups); `_build_dispatch_phases` honors_clean_order gate at run_plan.py:771-776 (folds strict_order to False on Eufy — does not restore group boundaries on either brand); `build_room_clean_payload` candidate sort by (order, name) at queue_engine.py:245-250 (this DOES preserve room ordering, so the loss is grouping/per-phase settings, not room order); `advance_active_job_phase` (queue_engine.py:441-443 returns None for a <2-phase job, so nothing downstream restores the lost phases).

confirmations: Confirmed at run_plan.py:898-908. Engine envelopes (dispatch_engines.py:211-217, 273-280, 390-396 and queue_engine.py:357-363) return exactly {vacuum_entity_id,map_id,payload,resolved_rooms,room_count} — no queue_room_ids key — so `all_ids` is unconditionally [] and the `or sorted(included_room_ids)` branch is the only reachable one. The fallback also passes managed_rooms=effective_rooms, discarding the group_managed overlay built at 834-841. Reachability confirmed: line 1352 gates on a charge_wait/wait/zone being PRESENT, and the 884-887 trim then pops leading/trailing breaks, so [charge_wait, groupA, groupB] collapses to one atomic phase.

Reproduced: profile [charge_wait(100), groupA, groupB]. run_plan.py:884-885 pops the leading charge_wait; collapsed then has no _BREAKS/zone so 898-908 fires. Engine envelopes (dispatch_engines.py:211-217/273-280, queue_engine.py:357-363) carry no queue_room_ids, so all_ids is unconditionally [] and sorted(included_room_ids) is the only reachable branch — dead code confirmed. group_managed (834-841) is discarded. BUT the per-group SETTINGS impact is largely rescued: profiles/manager.py:1236-1240 (apply_run_profile) already persists each group room's settings onto the stored room before start, so a room in ONE group keeps its group settings via effective_rooms. The surviving real defect is loss of phase SEQUENCING: on Eufy (honors_clean_order True) two groups merge into one batch dispatch; on both brands a room named in TWO groups ('vacuum the kitchen, then mop the kitchen') is dispatched ONCE with the LAST group's settings, so the vacuum pass never happens. Finder's 'bedrooms run at max instead of quiet' claim does not reproduce.

title: _match_profile_from_fields is structurally brand-blind and rewrites every Roborock room's profile_name to "custom" on every start
area: AREA 1 — Queue construction (queue/queue_engine.py get_enabled_rooms_in_order + build_queue_from_managed_rooms, and the planning path that feeds them: planning/run_plan.py _build_effective_start_plan / _build_steps_phases / _build_dispatch_phases, profiles/room_profiles.py resolve+gate, rooms/access_graph.py exclusion, rooms/room_defaults.py + adapters/roborock)
observed_behavior:
`_match_profile_from_fields(self, room)` takes NO `vacuum_entity_id`, so it cannot consult the adapter. It sources candidates from `self.get_room_profiles()["profiles"]`, which calls `get_default_room_profiles()` with no catalog (profiles/manager.py:225) -> the in-code EUFY `BUILT_IN_ROOM_PROFILES`; and it resolves each candidate with `resolve_room_profile_for_room(room_config=candidate_config, stored_profiles=stored_profiles)` (manager.py:157-162) — again with no `catalog=`, so floor-type fan/water defaults are Eufy's too.

`_build_effective_start_plan` calls it on every included room while building the queue:
```
updated_room = self._manager.protected_room_config({**room_data, **updates})
matched_profile = self._manager._match_profile_from_fields(updated_room)
updated_room["profile_name"] = matched_profile if matched_profile else "custom"
effective_rooms[room_key] = updated_room
```
(run_plan.py:1309-1312). Roborock's `vacuum_quick` declares `fan_speed: "balanced"` (adapters/roborock/vocabulary.py:114) while Eufy's declares `"Standard"`; `_normalize_profile_match_value` only lowercases (manager.py:113-135), so "balanced" != "standard" and NO profile matches -> `"custom"`. `vacuum_deep` matches only by the coincidence that both brands spell max suction "max"/"Max".
user_impact: A Roborock room the user set to "Vacuum Only Quick" is reported as a Custom profile everywhere the start plan feeds: `queue_state["queue_rooms"][].profile_name` (queue_engine.py:127), `resolved_rooms[].selected_profile_name` (queue_engine.py:319), the frozen active-job record, and the card's profile label (`_settings_profile_display` flips `is_custom` True, run_plan.py:125). Dispatched settings are unaffected (the room's own stored fields still win in the resolver), so this is a wrong user-visible label and a wrong job/learning record with no error shown — and the seam is structurally unable to be fixed without a signature change, since the function has no way to reach the brand catalog.
guards_checked: `_protected_room_config` (manager.py:84-111 — runs before the match and normalizes nothing brand-specific except forcing water "Off"); `_normalize_profile_match_value` (manager.py:113-135 — lowercases and coerces "off"/booleans/numbers, but does not translate vocabularies); `resolve_profile_catalog` (room_profiles.py:156-173 — exists and IS threaded correctly into `build_room_clean_payload` at queue_engine.py:220-224, so the dispatch path is catalog-aware while this labeling path is not); `get_room_profile`'s catalog fallback chain (room_profiles.py:281-291 — never reached with a catalog here).

confirmations: Confirmed. _match_profile_from_fields (manager.py:137-179) takes no vacuum_entity_id; candidates come from get_room_profiles() which calls get_default_room_profiles() with NO catalog (manager.py:225) -> Eufy BUILT_IN_ROOM_PROFILES, and resolve_room_profile_for_room is called at 157-162 with no catalog=. Verified it is called on every included room at run_plan.py:1310-1311. Roborock's vacuum_quick declares fan_speed 'balanced' (vocabulary.py:114). The mismatch is actually WIDER than reported: every stored room carries clean_intensity as '' (RoomConfig dataclass default, models.py:208, emitted by asdict), while the Eufy candidate resolves to 'Quick'/'Deep', so vacuum_deep does NOT match either — every Roborock room falls to 'custom'.

Reproduced on a fresh Roborock room. profiles/manager.py:148 get_room_profiles() -> merge_profile_dicts(built_in_profiles=get_default_room_profiles()) with NO catalog -> room_profiles.py:191 returns the Eufy BUILT_IN_ROOM_PROFILES; candidates resolved at 157-162 also without catalog. A Roborock room created via room_defaults carries fan_speed 'balanced' (vocabulary.py:114) and clean_intensity '' (RoomConfig default), while every Eufy candidate resolves to 'Standard'/'Max' + 'Quick'. _normalize_profile_match_value only lowercases, so no candidate matches on fan_speed OR clean_intensity -> run_plan.py:1311 writes 'custom'. _finalize_room_update (manager.py:195) runs the same match on every room save, so 'custom' is also PERSISTED. Label-only: the room's own stored fields still drive dispatch. Signature genuinely cannot reach the brand catalog (no vacuum_entity_id parameter).

title: A run profile whose first step is a zone is permanently unstartable and reports "Room-clean payload is missing or invalid"
area: AREA 1 — Queue construction (queue/queue_engine.py get_enabled_rooms_in_order + build_queue_from_managed_rooms, and the planning path that feeds them: planning/run_plan.py _build_effective_start_plan / _build_steps_phases / _build_dispatch_phases, profiles/room_profiles.py resolve+gate, rooms/access_graph.py exclusion, rooms/room_defaults.py + adapters/roborock)
observed_behavior:
The leading-phase trim is deliberately narrowed to breaks only: `_BREAKS = ("charge_wait", "wait")` and `while phases and phases[0].get("phase_type") in _BREAKS: phases.pop(0)` (run_plan.py:883-885). A zone phase is therefore never trimmed, so for steps `[zone, room_group]` `phases[0]` is the zone phase, which is built as `{"phase_type": "zone", ..., "payload": {}, "room_count": 0}` (run_plan.py:873-879).

`payload_state = phases[0]` (run_plan.py:1379) then propagates a `room_count` of 0 into `get_start_status`, which passes it to `build_start_blocker_from_lifecycle(payload_room_count=int(payload_state.get("room_count", 0)))` (core/manager.py:2863) where `if int(payload_room_count or 0) <= 0:` returns `{"reason": "invalid_payload", "blocked": True}` (jobs/job_monitor.py:268-273). `start_selected_rooms` returns early on `start_status["blocked"]` (core/manager.py:4943).

The docstring three lines above the trim claims the opposite: "Leading/trailing/duplicate charge phases (nothing to bracket) are dropped so phase 0 is always a real clean the initial dispatch can send" (run_plan.py:806-808). A zone IS a real clean but is not one `_dispatch_clean_payload` can send. `normalize_run_profile_steps` (profiles/manager.py:751-809) imposes no ordering constraint, so a zone-first profile is authorable and `apply_run_profile` accepts it (the room_group supplies `_profile_rooms`, so `applied` is True).
user_impact: A saved run profile that begins with a saved-zone step (e.g. "spot-clean under the table, then clean the downstairs") can never be started. The user gets "Room-clean payload is missing or invalid." — a message about a corrupt payload, pointing at nothing they can fix. The feature is dead for that authoring order with no diagnostic naming the zone step.
guards_checked: run_plan.py:883-887 leading/trailing trim (`_BREAKS` excludes zone by design — step_types.py:23-25 documents that narrowing as intentional); run_plan.py:898-901 zone-aware collapse guard (prevents collapsing a zone away, so the zone phase survives into phases[0]); jobs/job_monitor.py:261 `no_rooms_selected` (does not fire — queue_room_ids is non-empty); jobs/phase_runner.py:996-1008 `_dispatch_active_phase` zone branch and 914-928 zone confirm branch (both correct, but unreachable because the start is blocked before any phase runs); core/manager.py:2834 `all_selected_rooms_blocked` (does not fire — rooms are included).

confirmations: Confirmed end-to-end. _BREAKS = ('charge_wait','wait') at run_plan.py:883 excludes zone; a zone phase is built with room_count 0 (run_plan.py:873-879); payload_state = phases[0] (1379); get_start_status passes int(payload_state.get('room_count',0)) into build_start_blocker_from_lifecycle (core/manager.py:2857-2863); job_monitor.py:268-273 returns {'reason':'invalid_payload','blocked':True} for <=0; start_selected_rooms returns early on blocked (manager.py:4943). normalize_run_profile_steps (profiles/manager.py:751-809) is shape-only with no ordering constraint, so a zone-first profile is authorable. This finding is also the reason DQ-ACT-4 / DQ-PH-4 are false.

Reproduced and it is the CORRECT account of the zone-first case (it refutes DQ-ACT-4/DQ-PH-4). normalize_run_profile_steps (profiles/manager.py:765-809) enforces shape only, so steps=[{type:zone},{type:room_group}] normalizes cleanly and start_run_profile stashes it (manager.py:1306-1316). _BREAKS = ('charge_wait','wait') at run_plan.py:883, so the zone survives at phases[0] with room_count 0 (873-879); payload_state = phases[0] (1379). start_selected_rooms calls get_start_status FIRST (core/manager.py:4937), which itself builds the plan (2765-2769, peek) and passes payload_room_count=0 to build_start_blocker_from_lifecycle (2863) -> job_monitor.py:268-273 'invalid_payload'. start_selected_rooms returns early at 4943. The run is unstartable with 'Room-clean payload is missing or invalid.' — no empty dispatch ever reaches the device.

title: normalize_room_profile re-injects the Eufy literal "Quick" for clean_intensity, defeating Roborock's deliberate omission of the axis
area: AREA 1 — Queue construction (queue/queue_engine.py get_enabled_rooms_in_order + build_queue_from_managed_rooms, and the planning path that feeds them: planning/run_plan.py _build_effective_start_plan / _build_steps_phases / _build_dispatch_phases, profiles/room_profiles.py resolve+gate, rooms/access_graph.py exclusion, rooms/room_defaults.py + adapters/roborock)
observed_behavior:
`normalize_room_profile` fills every key unconditionally:
```
"clean_intensity": normalize_clean_intensity(source.get("clean_intensity", d.get("clean_intensity", "Quick"))),
```
where `d = (catalog or {}).get("normalize_defaults")`. Roborock's `normalize_defaults` is `CUSTOM_ROOM_PROFILE`, which declares NO `clean_intensity` (adapters/roborock/vocabulary.py:153-162), and none of its four `ROOM_PROFILES` declare it either (vocabulary.py:110-151, with the comment at 107-109 stating the omission is deliberate: "An omitted key means the room stores nothing for it, rather than an inert 'Quick' nobody can act on"). So `d.get("clean_intensity", "Quick")` hits the hardcoded Eufy literal, and `normalize_clean_intensity("Quick")` passes it through ("quick" is not in `_DEAD_CLEAN_INTENSITY`, room_profiles.py:115-120).

Consequences: `get_room_profile` returns `normalize_room_profile(profile, catalog)` (room_profiles.py:291), so EVERY Roborock built-in comes back carrying `clean_intensity: "Quick"`; and `apply_room_profile_to_config` writes it straight onto the stored room — `updated["clean_intensity"] = normalized["clean_intensity"]` (room_profiles.py:566), reached from the apply-profile-to-room action at profiles/manager.py:672-677.

The recently-changed new-room path is the one that gets it RIGHT: `resolve_new_room_defaults` reads `builtins.get(profile_name)` raw and copies only declared fields (rooms/room_defaults.py:77-84), so a freshly created Roborock room correctly has no intensity from the brand — it is the profile-APPLY path that re-adds it.
user_impact: Applying a room profile to a Roborock room stamps `clean_intensity="Quick"` — a value from a brand whose intensity option list (`clean_intensity_options`) is deliberately absent (adapters/roborock/adapter.py:241). The card's intensity chip row has no matching option to select, so the room shows a value the user cannot change or clear, and the "one source, no second vocabulary" contract that rooms/room_defaults.py was written to establish is broken on the second write path. Wire-inert today (Roborock's GenericRoomIdsEngine discards the Eufy-shaped payload, dispatch_engines.py:188-197), so no wrong physical action.
guards_checked: rooms/room_defaults.py:81-83 `if field in profile` (correct — this is why NEW rooms are clean, and why the defect only surfaces on the apply path); models/models.py:208 `clean_intensity: str = ""` (RoomConfig emits the key as empty, so `resolve_room_profile_for_room`'s `room_config.get("clean_intensity", ...)` at room_profiles.py:416-418 lets the room's own "" win — until apply_room_profile_to_config overwrites it with "Quick"); queue_engine.py:301 `_write_room_field(..., "clean_intensity", ...)` (unconditional, no capability gate, but harmless for Roborock because its engine discards the payload); `apply_capability_gate` (room_profiles.py:496 — normalizes but never drops an undeclared axis).

confirmations: The code fact is real: room_profiles.py:209 hardcodes the Eufy literal 'Quick' as the last-resort default, and Roborock's normalize_defaults (CUSTOM_ROOM_PROFILE) omits the key, so get_room_profile returns every Roborock built-in carrying clean_intensity 'Quick'. BUT the operative literal in the described user scenario is not this line: apply_room_profile hands normalize_room_profile the EUFY profile dict (get_room_profiles() takes no catalog, manager.py:225/631), which DECLARES clean_intensity, so `source.get(...)` wins and line 209's fallback never fires there. That path is DQ-PAY-1's mechanism. Line 209 is otherwise wire-inert (RoomConfig always emits the key, so the resolver's profile fallback at room_profiles.py:416-418 never reaches it). Downgraded to latent.

The code fact at room_profiles.py:209 is real — d.get('clean_intensity','Quick') hits the hardcoded Eufy literal because Roborock's normalize_defaults (CUSTOM_ROOM_PROFILE, vocabulary.py:153-162) omits the key — and get_room_profile:291 does return every Roborock built-in carrying 'Quick'. But the stated apply-path is misattributed: apply_room_profile (profiles/manager.py:631-632) sources its profile from get_room_profiles(), which is the EUFY catalog (see DQ-PAY-1), so the 'Quick'/'Deep' stamped on the room comes from the Eufy profile's own declared key, not from normalize's default. With the catalog actually threaded (resolve_room_profile_for_room), the room's own stored clean_intensity ('' from RoomConfig) always wins, so the normalize default never reaches a stored room or the wire. Outcome reproduces; the operative line is manager.py:225, not room_profiles.py:209. Subsumed by DQ-PAY-1.

title: A map rebuild silently auto-enables AND auto-approves rooms that never existed before, adding them to the clean queue unseen
area: AREA 1 — Queue construction (queue/queue_engine.py get_enabled_rooms_in_order + build_queue_from_managed_rooms, and the planning path that feeds them: planning/run_plan.py _build_effective_start_plan / _build_steps_phases / _build_dispatch_phases, profiles/room_profiles.py resolve+gate, rooms/access_graph.py exclusion, rooms/room_defaults.py + adapters/roborock)
observed_behavior:
`rebuild_map_bucket` sets `previous = existing_rooms.get(room_id_key, {}) if preserve_existing_settings else {}` (line 148), then:
```
enabled=bool(previous.get("enabled", True)),
...
is_configured=bool(previous.get("is_configured", True)),
```
(lines 181, 197). For a room that is newly present in `discovered_rooms` and absent from `existing_rooms`, `previous` is `{}`, so BOTH defaults fire: the room enters `enabled=True, is_configured=True`.

`get_enabled_rooms_in_order` filters only on `bool(room.get("enabled", False))` (queue_engine.py:86-90) and there is no `is_configured` gate anywhere in the queue path — `is_configured` is consumed only by entity creation (entity_helpers.py:98) and the drift tracker (setup/drift.py:241). So the new room is in the queue immediately, ordered by `index` (map_manager.py:182).

The comment directly above these lines asserts the opposite behaviour: "a rebuild must PRESERVE whatever approval already existed — a rebuilt room must not read as unconfigured ... and equally must not silently auto-approve" (map_manager.py:160-165). It does silently auto-approve. `setup/drift.py:229-231` states the intended contract explicitly: "new rooms enter False and require the save_rooms step to flip them."
user_impact: After a Rebuild Map, any segment that appeared since the last rebuild — a room the user renamed into existence in the vendor app, or on Eufy a phantom segment the CV segmenter split off — is cleaned on the next Start without ever appearing in the setup flow or the drift report. The user pressed Start expecting their configured room set and the robot cleans an extra room. With `preserve_existing_settings=False` the same two defaults apply to EVERY room, so the user's enable/disable selections are wholesale replaced by "everything on".
guards_checked: rooms/room_manager.py:96,112 `build_managed_rooms` (the wizard path, which correctly gates on `enabled_room_ids` at line 61 and is an explicit approval); setup/drift.py:224-247 `_list_configured_room_ids` (filters on is_configured, but only reports drift — it never removes a room from the queue, and a rebuilt room is already stamped True so it is invisible to drift); entity_helpers.py:98 is_configured filter (entity creation only); adapters/roborock/adapter.py:452 `new_room_confirmation_passes: 1` and the Eufy equivalent (these gate room DISCOVERY, not rebuild — `rebuild_map_bucket` takes `discovered_rooms` already resolved); queue_engine.py:86-90 and 237-243 (neither reads is_configured).

confirmations: Confirmed verbatim at map_manager.py:148/181/197: previous = {} for a newly discovered room, then enabled=bool(previous.get('enabled', True)) and is_configured=bool(previous.get('is_configured', True)) — both default TRUE. The comment at 160-165 explicitly claims a rebuild 'must not silently auto-approve'; the code does. get_enabled_rooms_in_order (queue_engine.py:86-90) and build_room_clean_payload's candidate filter (242) read only `enabled`; grepped is_configured — consumed only by entity_helpers and setup/drift, never in the queue path. A comment asserting a guard is a claim, and here it is false.

Reproduced by reading map_manager.py:148/181/197: for a room absent from existing_rooms, previous = {} so enabled=bool({}.get('enabled', True)) = True and is_configured=bool({}.get('is_configured', True)) = True. The comment at 160-165 asserts the opposite ('must not silently auto-approve'). Verified there is NO is_configured gate anywhere in the queue path (grep over queue/ and planning/ returns zero hits); get_enabled_rooms_in_order (queue_engine.py:86-90) and build_room_clean_payload (240) filter on 'enabled' only. Concrete case: user renames a segment into existence in the vendor app, presses Rebuild Map (rooms/room_crud.py:422, preserve_existing_settings=True by default) -> the new segment enters enabled+approved and is cleaned on the next Start without appearing in setup or drift.

title: apply_capability_gate and _protected_room_config hardcode Eufy display literals for the framework's 'no water' / 'default path' concepts
area: AREA 1 — Queue construction (queue/queue_engine.py get_enabled_rooms_in_order + build_queue_from_managed_rooms, and the planning path that feeds them: planning/run_plan.py _build_effective_start_plan / _build_steps_phases / _build_dispatch_phases, profiles/room_profiles.py resolve+gate, rooms/access_graph.py exclusion, rooms/room_defaults.py + adapters/roborock)
observed_behavior:
`apply_capability_gate` — the capability gate the payload builder calls for every room (queue_engine.py:271-276) — writes brand literals directly rather than reading the catalog it was handed:
```
if not supports_mop and clean_mode in {"mop","vacuum_mop"}: ... water_level = "Off"   # line 509
if clean_mode == "vacuum": water_level = "Off"                                       # line 516
if not supports_water: water_level = "Off"                                           # line 520
if not supports_path: path_type = "wide"                                             # line 524
```
The function receives `catalog=` (line 477) and uses it for the mop-downgrade profile lookup at line 507, so the seam is present and simply not applied to these four assignments. `_protected_room_config` does the same twice (`protected["water_level"] = "Off"` at profiles/manager.py:104 and 108), and its output IS `effective_rooms` in the queue-construction path (run_plan.py:1309).

This is the exact defect the resolver was already fixed for: room_profiles.py:429-431 and 438-442 carry comments explaining that a literal `"Off"` "wrote Eufy casing into a Roborock resolution, where the value is 'off'" and that a strict `== "Off"` "meant this guard never fired on Roborock". The gate one function below was not given the same treatment.

On Roborock today the damage is absorbed: `_run_global_pre_calls` lowercases before the rank lookup (`value = str(room.get(field) or "").strip().lower()`, dispatch/manager.py:409), `_normalize_water_level_key` lowercases (run_plan.py:206), and the GenericRoomIdsEngine discards the water field entirely.
user_impact: No wrong physical action on either shipped brand. Structural: the framework's "no water" concept is expressed as the string `"Off"` in the one function every brand's payload must pass through, so a brand whose no-water value is not case-insensitively "off" (an integer 0, "none", "dry") receives an unmappable value it must special-case in its own value_map — and the `resolved_rooms` record persisted to learning/history carries Eufy casing for every brand.
guards_checked: dispatch/manager.py:409 and :400-402 (`.strip().lower()` before `rank.index` — this is what rescues the Roborock global mop pre-call); dispatch/manager.py:418-430 OFF-fallback (also compares lowercase); planning/run_plan.py:206-220 `_normalize_water_level_key` (lowercases, rescuing the water estimator); dispatch_engines.py:188-197 GenericRoomIdsEngine (discards the Eufy-shaped payload, so the literal never reaches the Roborock wire); queue_engine.py:303-307 `supports_water`/`supports_edge` gates (skip writing the field, but only after the literal has already been written into `gated` and into `resolved_rooms` at queue_engine.py:328); room_profiles.py:432-436 catalog-sourced carpet/floor water defaults (correct — and the direct proof that the catalog seam exists and was simply not used in the gate).

confirmations: Confirmed at room_profiles.py:509/516/520/524 — literal 'Off' three times and 'wide' once, inside a function that receives and USES catalog three lines earlier (507) for the mop-downgrade lookup. profiles/manager.py:104/108 repeat 'Off' with no catalog parameter at all. The rescue is real and I verified it: dispatch/manager.py:409 lowercases before rank.index and RoborockSegmentEngine discards the Eufy-shaped payload, so no shipped brand is harmed today. Correctly scoped as structural.

title: Applying a built-in room profile to a Roborock room writes EUFY vocabulary onto the room; the fresh room_defaults fix covers creation only
area: AREA 2 — Payload building (queue/queue_engine.py build_room_clean_payload, queue/dispatch_engines.py, dispatch/manager.py, dispatch/zone_dispatch.py) and the profile-resolution inputs that feed it
observed_behavior: `get_room_profiles()` (profiles/manager.py:220-233) builds its list with `merge_profile_dicts(built_in_profiles=get_default_room_profiles(), stored_profiles=stored_profiles)` — NO `catalog=` argument. `get_default_room_profiles(catalog=None)` (room_profiles.py:190-191) therefore returns `deepcopy(BUILT_IN_ROOM_PROFILES)`, the in-code EUFY catalog (`vacuum_deep` = fan_speed "Max", water_level "Off", clean_intensity "Deep"). `apply_room_profile` (profiles/manager.py:631-632) then does `profiles = self.get_room_profiles()["profiles"]; profile = profiles.get(profile_name)` and hands that EUFY dict to `apply_room_profile_to_config(room_config=room, profile=profile, catalog=catalog)` at :671-676. The Roborock catalog IS passed there, but it only reaches `normalize_room_profile`, whose every field reads `source.get(field, d.get(field, ...))` (room_profiles.py:204-214) — `source` is the Eufy profile and it declares every key, so the catalog's `normalize_defaults` (Roborock's lowercase CUSTOM_ROOM_PROFILE) is never consulted. Result stored on the Roborock room: `fan_speed="Max"`, `water_level="Off"`, `clean_intensity="Deep"`. At dispatch, `build_room_clean_payload` (queue_engine.py:265-269) calls `resolve_room_profile_for_room`, where `room_config.get("fan_speed", ...)` wins (room_profiles.py:422), so `resolved_rooms[i]["fan_speed"] == "Max"`. Roborock's only per-room actuation is `dispatch.per_room_live_settings`, and `get_per_room_live_setting_calls` filters on `options_key` with strict membership — `valid = {str(o.get("value")) for o in vocabulary["fan_speed_options"]}` (jobs/active_job.py:1385-1391) — whose values are lowercase (`gentle/quiet/balanced/turbo/max`). "Max" is not in that set, the call is dropped, and `vacuum.set_fan_speed` is never issued.
user_impact: On a Roborock, choosing any built-in room profile (e.g. "Vacuum Only Deep") for a room stores an unusable capitalized suction value. The room then cleans at whatever fan speed the device happened to be left on — the user's profile choice has zero effect on suction, with no error, no warning, and no log line. The card's chip row (strict `===` against the lowercase option values) also renders no selection, so the room looks unconfigured.
guards_checked: (1) `_PROTECTED_ROOM_PROFILE_NAMES` (profiles/manager.py:302-309) — blocks OVERWRITING the built-ins, does not scope them per brand, so it does not help. (2) `rooms/room_defaults.resolve_new_room_defaults_for_vacuum` — the recently-shipped fix; it is only wired into room CREATION, and `apply_room_profile` overwrites the correct fresh values it produced. (3) `resolve_profile_catalog` at profiles/manager.py:659-662 — it IS resolved and passed, but as shown it only fills keys the profile OMITS, and the Eufy built-ins omit none. (4) `dispatch.room_fields` / `_write_room_field` value_map (queue_engine.py:176-185) — Roborock declares no `room_fields` block at all, so nothing renames or re-maps the value. (5) `apply_capability_gate` (room_profiles.py:472-541) — it never touches `fan_speed`; the value passes through untouched. (6) `per_room_live_settings.options_key` — this is the filter that silently swallows the bad value, not a rescue.

confirmations: Confirmed the full chain. profiles/manager.py:224-227 calls get_default_room_profiles() with NO catalog -> deepcopy(BUILT_IN_ROOM_PROFILES) (room_profiles.py:190-191), the Eufy catalog. apply_room_profile:631-632 takes that dict and passes it to apply_room_profile_to_config with catalog= (671-676); normalize_room_profile (204-214) reads source.get(field, d.get(...)) and the Eufy profile declares EVERY key, so the Roborock normalize_defaults is never consulted. apply_room_profile_to_config:564 writes updated['fan_speed'] = 'Max' onto the Roborock room. active_job.py:1385-1391 then drops the call on strict membership against lowercase fan_speed_options. This re-creates the exact failure the Roborock vocabulary header (vocabulary.py:95-109) and room_defaults.py's module docstring were written to eliminate — on the second write path they did not cover.

Fully reproduced on Roborock. profiles/manager.py:631 `profiles = self.get_room_profiles()['profiles']` -> 225 merge_profile_dicts(built_in_profiles=get_default_room_profiles()) with no catalog -> room_profiles.py:191 the EUFY builtins (vacuum_deep = fan_speed 'Max'). The Roborock catalog IS passed to apply_room_profile_to_config (672-676) but only reaches normalize_room_profile, whose every field is `source.get(field, d.get(...))` (204-214) — the Eufy source declares all 9 keys, so normalize_defaults is never consulted. title: A mop room on a granite or concrete floor resolves water_level to the empty string and that empty string is written verbatim to the wire
area: AREA 2 — Payload building (queue/queue_engine.py build_room_clean_payload, queue/dispatch_engines.py, dispatch/manager.py, dispatch/zone_dispatch.py) and the profile-resolution inputs that feed it
observed_behavior: `_normalize_floor_type` (room_profiles.py:256-261) admits "granite" and "concrete", and both are user-selectable in the card's floor picker (`FLOOR_TYPE_OPTIONS`, src/renderers/setup.js:35-36). But NEITHER brand's `floor_type_water_defaults` has an entry for them — Eufy `FLOOR_TYPE_WATER_DEFAULTS` (room_profiles.py:140-147) and Roborock `FLOOR_TYPE_WATER_DEFAULTS` (adapters/roborock/vocabulary.py:167-174) both list only hardwood/laminate/tile/marble/carpet_*. Trace a granite room set to `vacuum_mop` whose stored `water_level` is "Off" (which is what every room gets — `_protected_room_config` stamps it, and a new room inherits it from `vacuum_quick`): in `resolve_room_profile_for_room` the carpet branch is skipped, the `elif "water_level" not in room_config` branch is skipped (the key IS present), and then the mop-safety guard at room_profiles.py:443-448 fires — `resolved_water_level.strip().lower() in ("", "off")` is True and not carpet — assigning `resolved_water_level = water_defaults.get("granite", "")` → `""`. The guard that exists to make mop mode valid is what produces the empty value. `apply_capability_gate` does `water_level = str(settings.get("water_level", "Off"))` — the key is present with `""`, so the "Off" default never fires; `clean_mode` is `vacuum_mop` so the vacuum-only branch is skipped; Eufy has `supports_water_control` True so `if not supports_water` is skipped. In `build_room_clean_payload`, `water_level = str(gated["water_level"])` → `""` (line 284), and `if supports_water and clean_mode in {"mop", "vacuum_mop"}` is True → `_write_room_field(payload_room, room_fields, "water_level", "")` (line 304). Eufy's `room_fields` declares `{"field_name": "water_level", "value_map": None}` (adapters/eufy/adapter.py:579), so `_write_room_field` takes the identity path (`value_map` falsy → `wire_value = canonical_value`) and emits `"water_level": ""` in the `rooms[]` entry of the `room_clean` send_command.
user_impact: A room the user configured to mop, on a granite or concrete floor, is dispatched to the Eufy with an empty water-level string — the robot either rejects the room_clean payload (the whole run silently fails to start) or mops with an undefined water setting. On Roborock the same empty value reaches `_run_global_pre_calls`, where `""` is not in the rank list; if it is the only room the loop hits `if best_index < 0: continue` (dispatch/manager.py:413) and the device-global mop intensity is LEFT AS-IS — potentially a HIGH level left over from a previous run, wet-mopping a room the user did not ask to be wet-mopped.
guards_checked: (1) `_protected_room_config` (profiles/manager.py:98-109) — only forces water "Off" for carpet or non-mop modes; a granite mop room passes through untouched. (2) `apply_capability_gate` (room_profiles.py:493-526) — all three branches that could rewrite `water_level` are proven inapplicable above. (3) `_write_room_field` (queue_engine.py:176-185) — performs no non-empty check and no vocabulary validation; `if value_map:` is falsy for Eufy so even a mapping miss cannot be detected. (4) `dispatch_zone_clean`-style defence-in-depth validation — exists for zones only, there is no equivalent validator on the room payload. (5) The mop-water guard at room_profiles.py:443-448 was itself recently fixed to be case-insensitive; that fix made it FIRE on more paths, which is what surfaces the missing granite/concrete defaults.

confirmations: Confirmed. _normalize_floor_type admits 'granite'/'concrete' (room_profiles.py:257-260) and both are user-selectable (src/i18n/en.js:1345-1346 setup.floor_granite/floor_concrete), but neither brand's FLOOR_TYPE_WATER_DEFAULTS has an entry (room_profiles.py:140-147; roborock/vocabulary.py:167-174). Traced: room_config always carries water_level (RoomConfig dataclass field, so the `elif 'water_level' not in room_config` branch at 435 cannot fire), the mop-safety guard at 443-448 fires for a mop room whose water is ''/'Off', and water_defaults.get('granite','') returns ''. apply_capability_gate cannot correct it (key present with '', clean_mode not 'vacuum', supports_water True). queue_engine.py:303-304 then writes it, and Eufy declares water_level with value_map None (adapter.py:579) so _write_room_field takes the identity path and emits water_level: '' on the wire. The reachability caveat is that the room's stored water must already be ''/'Off' while in mop mode — real but narrower than 'every room'.

Reproduced end-to-end on Eufy. 'granite' is admitted by _normalize_floor_type (room_profiles.py:257-260) and IS user-selectable (src/renderers/setup.js:35-36 FLOOR_TYPE_OPTIONS); neither brand's FLOOR_TYPE_WATER_DEFAULTS has granite/concrete (room_profiles.py:140-147, roborock/vocabulary.py:167-174). In resolve_room_profile_for_room the 435 elif is skipped (key present) and the mop-safety guard at 443-448 fires -> water_defaults.get('granite','') = ''. apply_capability_gate: settings.get('water_level','Off') returns '' (key present), clean_mode is vacuum_mop so 515 is skipped, Eufy supports_water True so 519 is skipped. build_room_clean_payload:284 -> ''; 303 is True -> _write_room_field with Eufy's {'field_name':'water_level','value_map':None} (adapter.py:579) takes the identity path -> the room_clean rooms[] entry carries "water_level": "". The guard that exists to make mop mode valid is what manufactures the empty value.

title: Zone-clean repeat cap defaults to 3 for Eufy while the framework's own room-clean cap for Eufy is 2, and the service schema has no upper bound
area: AREA 2 — Payload building (queue/queue_engine.py build_room_clean_payload, queue/dispatch_engines.py, dispatch/manager.py, dispatch/zone_dispatch.py) and the profile-resolution inputs that feed it
observed_behavior: `build_room_clean_payload` sets `passes_max: int = int(dispatch.get("passes_max", 2))` with the comment "# Eufy caps at 2 passes" (queue_engine.py:234) and clamps the wire value with `max(1, min(passes_max, clean_passes))` (line 294). The Eufy adapter's `dispatch` block (adapters/eufy/adapter.py:551-583) declares NEITHER `passes_max` NOR `zone_passes_max` — it relies on that default. `dispatch_zone_clean` uses a DIFFERENT default for the same brand: `_zone_repeat_max = int(cfg.get("zone_passes_max", cfg.get("passes_max", 3)) or 3)` then `repeat = max(1, min(int(clean_times), _zone_repeat_max))` (dispatch/manager.py:182-183), with a comment claiming the 3 "covers Eufy 1-2 and Roborock 1-3" — a default of 3 does not clamp an Eufy device to 2. The service schema imposes no ceiling either: `vol.Optional("clean_times", default=1): vol.All(vol.Coerce(int), vol.Range(min=1))` (services/job_control.py:130-132), with a comment asserting "the real per-brand ceiling is enforced against the adapter's zone-repeat capability at dispatch" — which, for Eufy, resolves to 3. `dispatch_zone_clean` then takes the non-`device_mm` branch (Eufy has no `zone_coords`) and sends `{"zones": zones, "clean_times": int(clean_times)}` — note this branch does not even use the clamped `repeat`; `_zone_repeat_max` is computed only inside the `device_mm` arm, so on Eufy the raw unbounded `clean_times` goes straight onto the wire.
user_impact: An Eufy zone clean called with clean_times=3 (or 10) dispatches that raw value to a device the framework itself documents as capping at 2 passes. The user draws a box, presses clean, and either gets a silently rejected command (nothing happens, no error surfaced) or an out-of-range pass count. The stated per-brand ceiling enforcement is a comment, not code, on the Eufy path.
guards_checked: (1) `_START_ZONE_CLEAN_SCHEMA` (services/job_control.py:117-134) — explicitly declines to bound clean_times, deferring to dispatch. (2) `dispatch_zone_clean`'s degenerate-rect check (dispatch/manager.py:112-118), `zone_max` count check (:131-135) and area bounds (:164-177) — all validate geometry, none validate the repeat count on the non-device_mm path. (3) `capabilities.zone_max` / `zone_min_area_m2` / `zone_max_area_m2` — Eufy declares zone side bounds but nothing about repeats. (4) `queue_engine.passes_max` default of 2 — never consulted by the zone path because it lives in the payload builder, not the dispatch config.

confirmations: Confirmed, and the mechanism paragraph is right even though the headline framing is not: the problem is not that the default is 3, it is that NO clamp runs on Eufy at all. _zone_repeat_max/repeat live only inside the `if cfg.get('zone_coords') == 'device_mm'` arm (dispatch/manager.py:182-183); I verified adapters/eufy/adapter.py declares no zone_coords, no passes_max and no zone_passes_max, so Eufy always reaches line 234 `{'zones': zones, 'clean_times': int(clean_times)}` with the raw caller value. services/job_control.py:129-132 is vol.Range(min=1) with a comment explicitly deferring the ceiling to dispatch. Exact duplicate of DQ-ZONE-1 at the same line — dedupe before assigning work.

Confirmed, and it is the same defect as DQ-ZONE-1 seen from the config-default angle. Verified by search: adapters/eufy/adapter.py declares neither passes_max nor zone_passes_max nor zone_coords (only roborock/adapter.py:338 declares passes_max). queue_engine.py:234 uses default 2 with the comment 'Eufy caps at 2 passes'; dispatch/manager.py:182 uses default 3 for the same brand. The finding's own closing sentence is the operative fact: _zone_repeat_max/repeat live INSIDE the device_mm arm, so Eufy (which takes the else at 195) never clamps at all — line 234 sends int(clean_times) raw. services/job_control.py:130-132 imposes Range(min=1) with a comment deferring the ceiling to dispatch. title: _write_room_field's value_map is fail-open: an unmapped canonical value is emitted raw, and the framework itself injects Eufy literals no adapter can declare a mapping for
area: AREA 2 — Payload building (queue/queue_engine.py build_room_clean_payload, queue/dispatch_engines.py, dispatch/manager.py, dispatch/zone_dispatch.py) and the profile-resolution inputs that feed it
observed_behavior: `_write_room_field` does `wire_value = value_map.get(str(canonical_value), canonical_value)` (queue_engine.py:182) — a lookup miss silently falls back to the RAW canonical value, with no log and no error. Nothing upstream guarantees the canonical value is one the adapter could have mapped, because `apply_capability_gate` injects hardcoded Eufy display literals that appear in no brand's declared vocabulary: `water_level = "Off"` at room_profiles.py:509 and again at :516, `path_type = "wide"` at :524, `clean_intensity` defaulting to `"Quick"` at :496. So a brand-3 adapter that correctly declares `value_map: {"off": 0, "low": 1, "medium": 2, "high": 3}` for its own lowercase canonical vocabulary still receives `"Off"` from the gate, misses the map, and emits the STRING `"Off"` into what the device expects to be an integer field. `DreameSegmentEngine` has the identical miss path at dispatch_engines.py:381-387 (`v = value_map.get(str(v), v)`), where the raw string lands inside a positional int array. The two shipped engines also disagree on what an ABSENT `room_fields` entry means: `_write_room_field` treats it as identity-rename-and-emit (queue_engine.py:176-177, "Absent canonical-name entry ... passes through unchanged"), while `DreameSegmentEngine` treats it as do-not-emit (`if cfg is None: continue`, dispatch_engines.py:376-377). A brand porting between templates gets opposite behaviour from the same config.
user_impact: Any brand whose wire vocabulary differs from the canonical one gets un-translatable framework literals on the wire for capability-gated fields — a malformed payload the device rejects, or a wrong setting applied — and the framework prints nothing. Not reachable on Eufy (declares `value_map: None` everywhere, so the identity path is taken) or Roborock (declares no `room_fields` and discards the Eufy-shaped payload), but it is a structural seam defect: the adapter config has no way to express a mapping for a value the framework invents after the adapter's vocabulary has been consulted.
guards_checked: (1) `adapters/config_schema.py` room_fields validation — validates shape, not that the declared value_map covers the values the gate can produce. (2) `apply_capability_gate`'s catalog-driven mop downgrade (room_profiles.py:505-512) — it correctly derives `path_type`/`clean_intensity` from the catalog's built-ins, proving the author knew literals were wrong here, but the three assignments at :509/:516/:524 were left hardcoded. (3) `_write_room_field`'s `if value_map:` truthiness (line 180) — an empty dict falls to identity, which is correct, but a NON-empty map with a missing key also falls to the raw value with no distinction. (4) There is no logging anywhere in `_write_room_field` or in the Dreame transpose loop.

confirmations: Confirmed. queue_engine.py:180-185 `wire_value = value_map.get(str(canonical_value), canonical_value)` is fail-open with no log, and apply_capability_gate genuinely injects display literals no adapter declared ('Off' at room_profiles.py:509/516/520, 'wide' at 524, 'Quick' at 496). DreameSegmentEngine repeats the miss at dispatch_engines.py:386. The engine-disagreement half is also real and is the sharper point: _write_room_field treats an absent room_fields entry as identity-emit (comment at 171-174) while DreameSegmentEngine treats it as do-not-emit (`if cfg is None: continue`, 376-377) — same config, opposite behaviour.

Code facts confirmed: queue_engine.py:182 `value_map.get(str(canonical_value), canonical_value)` is fail-open with no log, and apply_capability_gate injects 'Off'/'wide' literals (room_profiles.py:509/516/524) that no adapter vocabulary can declare a mapping for. Also confirmed the engine divergence: _write_room_field treats an absent room_fields entry as identity-emit (176-177) while DreameSegmentEngine treats it as do-not-emit (dispatch_engines.py:376-377). Not reachable on either shipped brand (Eufy declares value_map: None everywhere -> identity path; Roborock declares no room_fields and discards the payload). No concrete triggering install exists, so this is a seam observation rather than a reachable defect — MEDIUM overstates it against the campaign's shipped-brand rule.

title: _protected_room_config stamps the Eufy literal "Off" into every non-mop room's water_level regardless of brand, on the path into the payload builder
area: AREA 2 — Payload building (queue/queue_engine.py build_room_clean_payload, queue/dispatch_engines.py, dispatch/manager.py, dispatch/zone_dispatch.py) and the profile-resolution inputs that feed it
observed_behavior: `_protected_room_config` (profiles/manager.py:84-111) hardcodes `protected["water_level"] = "Off"` at line 104 (carpet) and line 108 (any non-mop mode), with no reference to the adapter's catalog or vocabulary. `core/manager.build_room_payload` runs it over EVERY room immediately before the payload builder — `managed_rooms = {room_id: self.protected_room_config(room_data) for ...}` (core/manager.py:2498-2501) — and `_finalize_room_update` (profiles/manager.py:186) runs it on every room save, so the capitalized value is also PERSISTED into the Roborock room store. Roborock's declared `water_level_options` are lowercase (`off/low/medium/high`, adapters/roborock/vocabulary.py:62-67), so the stored value is outside the brand's own vocabulary. Downstream, `resolve_room_profile_for_room`'s `elif "water_level" not in room_config` branch (room_profiles.py:435) can then never fire for any room, because the key is now always present. This is the same class of defect the fresh `room_defaults.py` change was written to eliminate (its docstring names exactly `"Max"` / `"Off"` / `"Quick"`), on a code path the change did not touch.
user_impact: On a mop-settable Roborock the room editor's water chip row (strict `===` against the lowercase option values) renders nothing as selected for any vacuum-mode room, so the room reads as unconfigured. The value survives only because `_run_global_pre_calls` happens to lowercase before ranking (dispatch/manager.py:409) — a coincidence, not a contract. Any consumer that compares strictly against the brand's declared vocabulary sees an unrecognised value.
guards_checked: (1) `resolve_profile_catalog` — `_protected_room_config` takes no vacuum_entity_id and no catalog argument at all, so it cannot consult the brand. (2) `rooms/room_defaults.resolve_new_room_defaults_for_vacuum` — writes the correct lowercase `"off"` at creation; `_protected_room_config` overwrites it on the first save. (3) `_run_global_pre_calls` rank matching at dispatch/manager.py:370 and :409 (`str(v).strip().lower()`) — case-insensitive, so it rescues the DISPATCH path only; it does not rescue the stored value or any strict-equality consumer. (4) `apply_capability_gate`'s `if not supports_water: water_level = "Off"` (room_profiles.py:519-520) — the same literal, so the gate cannot correct it either.

confirmations: Code fact confirmed: profiles/manager.py:104 and :108 hardcode 'Off' with no catalog/vacuum argument, and core/manager.py:2498-2501 runs protected_room_config over every room immediately before the payload builder while _finalize_room_update:188 persists it. But every consequence I could trace is absorbed: _run_global_pre_calls lowercases before ranking (dispatch/manager.py:409), GenericRoomIdsEngine discards the field, and the claimed card impact is a water chip row on a VACUUM-mode room, where water is not an actionable control. This is a genuine Eufy-ism leak in a storage path with no demonstrated user-visible wrong result — latent, not MEDIUM.

Mechanism confirmed: profiles/manager.py:104 and :108 assign protected['water_level'] = 'Off' with no catalog/vacuum argument, and the function runs on every save (_finalize_room_update:188) and over every room in build_room_payload (core/manager.py:2498-2501), so a Roborock room persists Eufy casing outside its own declared vocabulary (roborock/vocabulary.py:62-67). But the claimed user-visible impact does NOT reproduce: src/renderers/room-editor.js:260-262 documents and gates the water chip row to mop mode only (state.showWaterLevel()), and _protected_room_config only stamps 'Off' for NON-mop rooms — so the row is hidden in exactly the case that gets the bad value. The other named consumer, resolve_room_profile_for_room's `elif 'water_level' not in room_config` (435), is already unreachable for every brand because RoomConfig always emits the key. Vocabulary-purity defect with no demonstrable wrong outcome today.

title: clean_passes_field: null omits passes in two engines but produces a None dict key in build_room_clean_payload
area: AREA 2 — Payload building (queue/queue_engine.py build_room_clean_payload, queue/dispatch_engines.py, dispatch/manager.py, dispatch/zone_dispatch.py) and the profile-resolution inputs that feed it
observed_behavior: `GenericRoomIdsEngine`'s docstring documents the contract explicitly — "``clean_passes_field`` (default ``\"repeat\"``) — the batch scalar key; set to ``None`` to omit passes entirely" (dispatch_engines.py:167-168) — and both non-Eufy engines honour it (`if passes_field is not None:` at dispatch_engines.py:208 and :365). `build_room_clean_payload` does not: it reads `clean_passes_field: str = dispatch.get("clean_passes_field", "clean_times")` (line 233) and then unconditionally writes `payload_room = {room_id_field: room_id, clean_passes_field: max(1, min(passes_max, clean_passes))}` (lines 292-295). A declared `None` therefore produces a literal `None` KEY in each per-room dict. The same asymmetry applies to `map_id_field` at line 354 (`wire_payload[map_id_field] = cast_map_id` with no None check), whereas `map_id_TYPE` does get a dedicated omission path at lines 351-355. Note both flat-id engines call `build_room_clean_payload` internally to reuse profile resolution (dispatch_engines.py:188 and :251), so the malformed inner dict is built even for Roborock — it is only harmless because that payload is discarded.
user_impact: A brand whose room-clean command carries no per-room pass count cannot express that on the `eufy_room_clean` template: instead of omitting the field it gets a `{None: 1}` entry, which fails JSON serialisation or reaches the device as a garbage key. The adapter author follows a documented contract and gets a broken payload with no validation error.
guards_checked: (1) `adapters/config_schema.py` dispatch block validation — accepts the key; nothing asserts non-null for the eufy template. (2) `dispatch_engines._SinglePhaseMixin.build_phases` — passes kwargs straight through, adds no normalisation. (3) The `map_id_type == "int"` omission logic at queue_engine.py:351-355 — proves the author does handle field omission for map_id's TYPE mismatch, but it keys off the cast result, not off a null field name, so it does not cover this. (4) No shipped adapter declares null for either key today (Eufy: "clean_times"/"map_id"; Roborock: "repeat"), so this is latent.

confirmations: Confirmed. dispatch_engines.py:167-168 documents `clean_passes_field: None` as 'omit passes entirely' and both non-Eufy engines honour it (208, 271, 365), while queue_engine.py:292-295 writes `{room_id_field: room_id, clean_passes_field: max(1, min(...))}` unconditionally — a declared None becomes a literal None dict key. The map_id_field asymmetry at 351-355 is also real: map_id_TYPE gets an omission path, a null field NAME does not. Correctly rated LOW (no shipped adapter declares null).

Confirmed: dispatch_engines.py:208 and :365 both guard `if passes_field is not None`, and the GenericRoomIdsEngine docstring (167-168) documents null as 'omit passes entirely' — but queue_engine.py:292-295 writes {room_id_field: room_id, clean_passes_field: ...} unconditionally, producing a literal None dict key. Same asymmetry for map_id_field at 354 (the 351-355 omission path keys off the CAST result, not a null field name). Verified latent: Eufy declares 'clean_times', Roborock 'repeat'; no shipped adapter declares null. Note both flat-id engines call build_room_clean_payload internally (188, 251), so the malformed inner dict would be built even for a brand that discards it.

title: Strict-order per-room phases invert the live-id safety rule: an unresolvable slug dispatches the STALE stored segment id instead of being skipped
area: AREA 3 — Dispatch engines (queue/dispatch_engines.py): the DispatchEngine Protocol, _SinglePhaseMixin, EufyRoomCleanEngine, GenericRoomIdsEngine, RoborockSegmentEngine, DreameSegmentEngine, get_dispatch_engine / known_dispatch_templates — plus the seams where their output is consumed (planning/run_plan.py _build_dispatch_phases/_build_steps_phases, jobs/phase_runner.py _dispatch_active_phase, dispatch/manager.py _resolve_live_dispatch_payload/_dispatch_clean_payload, adapters/registry.py _validate_adapter).
user_impact: On a Roborock strict-order run (user toggles 'clean in order', or ANY stepped run — run_plan.py:1363-1370 hardcodes strict_order=True for a profile containing a charge_wait/wait/zone step), if a target room's name changed or the map was re-segmented since the ids were stored, the robot is commanded to clean a segment id that now belongs to a different room. It physically cleans the WRONG ROOM. The phase watchdog then makes it worse rather than better: `_await_phase_started` (phase_runner.py:929-965) confirms only on native current_room == the phase target, which never matches, so it re-dispatches the same stale id up to `phase_timing.max_attempts` (3, adapter.py:325) — up to three wrong-room cleans — then gives up leaving `_phase_dispatch_pending` set and the run stalled.
guards_checked: (1) `if not slug_to_live_id` early return (dispatch/manager.py:295-300) — different condition (live source empty/refresh failed), does not fire when the source is healthy and only THIS slug is missing. (2) `if rooms_field not in payload: return payload` (line 275) — passes, per-room phases do carry `segments`. (3) `if dropped:` warning (line 312) — log only, no caller inspects it and nothing aborts. (4) phase_runner._dispatch_active_phase (lines 1019-1027) — hands `wire_payload` straight to `_dispatch_clean_payload`, no emptiness/identity check between resolve and send. (5) `_dispatch_clean_payload` (dispatch/manager.py:45-84) — pure envelope shaping, no validation of the id list. (6) `_await_phase_started` (phase_runner.py:855-965) — detects the failure only AFTER the wrong room has been cleaned, and its response is to re-dispatch the same payload. (7) `get_start_status` / `build_start_blocker_from_lifecycle` (jobs/job_monitor.py:233-273) — preflight runs on the batch (non-strict) plan and only blocks on zero rooms; it never sees the per-phase ids.

confirmations: Confirmed and it is the sharpest finding in the set. _build_per_room_phases (dispatch_engines.py:266-281) emits phases with resolved_rooms=[room] and payload={segments:[id]}; phase_runner.py:1019-1027 passes that one-element list into _resolve_live_dispatch_payload and sends the result with no inspection. In dispatch/manager.py:302-322 a single-target phase makes `dropped` non-empty EQUIVALENT to `new_segments == []`, so the 'live source unavailable' fallback `return payload` fires for a target that was resolved and REJECTED — dispatching the stale stored id. I verified Roborock declares resolve_live_ids_by_slug: True (adapter.py:353) precisely because ids renumber. I also verified reachability is broad: run_plan.py:1363-1370 hardcodes strict_order=True for ANY stepped profile, and Roborock's honors_clean_order False (adapter.py:601) makes effective_strict True at run_plan.py:776. The comment at phase_runner.py:1028-1030 asserts the opposite behaviour.

Reproduced and it is the highest-value finding in the set. Concrete case: Roborock, stepped or strict_order run (run_plan.py:1363-1370 hardcodes strict_order=True for any charge_wait/wait/zone profile; _build_dispatch_phases:776 folds it to effective_strict=True because honors_clean_order is False, adapter.py:601). GenericRoomIdsEngine._build_per_room_phases (dispatch_engines.py:266-281) emits one phase with resolved_rooms=[room] and payload={'segments':[stored_id]}. phase_runner.py:1019-1027 passes that ONE-element list to _resolve_live_dispatch_payload. With a healthy live map that simply lacks this room's slug (renamed in the Roborock app), dropped=[slug] AND new_segments==[] necessarily — the two branches that are distinct for a 5-room batch collapse into one for a 1-room phase — so dispatch/manager.py:317-322 returns the STALE stored id. Roborock reuses low segment ids after a re-segment, so the device cleans a different physical room. _await_phase_started then never confirms (it matches on native current_room == the phase target), so the same stale id is re-dispatched up to phase_timing.max_attempts=3 (adapter.py:325). Callers inspect nothing between resolve and send.

title: _SinglePhaseMixin silently swallows strict_order and the seam cannot express refusal — while the caller hides the order advisory on the strength of the request alone
area: AREA 3 — Dispatch engines (queue/dispatch_engines.py): the DispatchEngine Protocol, _SinglePhaseMixin, EufyRoomCleanEngine, GenericRoomIdsEngine, RoborockSegmentEngine, DreameSegmentEngine, get_dispatch_engine / known_dispatch_templates — plus the seams where their output is consumed (planning/run_plan.py _build_dispatch_phases/_build_steps_phases, jobs/phase_runner.py _dispatch_active_phase, dispatch/manager.py _resolve_live_dispatch_payload/_dispatch_clean_payload, adapters/registry.py _validate_adapter).
observed_behavior: `_SinglePhaseMixin.build_phases(self, *, strict_order=False, **kwargs)` returns `[self.build_payload(**kwargs)]` — `strict_order` is accepted, dropped on the floor, and nothing in the return value records that it was refused. The Protocol blesses this ("Engines that can't honor it (atomic batch shapes) ignore the flag", lines 93-97). Only GenericRoomIdsEngine overrides it; EufyRoomCleanEngine and DreameSegmentEngine inherit the swallow. The caller then treats the REQUEST as proof of enforcement: planning/run_plan.py:1458-1464 computes `order_advisory = None if strict_order else self._order_advisory(...)` using the raw parameter, not `effective_strict` and not any engine feedback, with the comment "Suppressed when strict_order is active — order is then ENFORCED (the sequenced per-room dispatch), so the advisory would contradict." `_order_advisory` (run_plan.py:697-723) returns its text precisely when `capabilities.honors_clean_order` is False — the exact brand class for which `_build_dispatch_phases` sets `effective_strict = bool(strict_order) and not honors_order` = True and therefore the one where an atomic engine's silent swallow bites. There is no field on the returned phase list (no `job_model`, no `strict_order_honored`) for the framework to check, so this cannot be detected downstream; it is a gap in the Protocol itself, not a missing call.
user_impact: A brand that path-optimizes (honors_clean_order False) but whose payload shape is list-of-dicts or positional-arrays — i.e. anything on eufy_room_clean, dreame_room_clean, or a future engine built off _SinglePhaseMixin — gets ONE batch dispatch when the user asks for strict order. The rooms are cleaned in the device's optimized order, and the standing advisory that would have told the user 'this vacuum cleans in the order saved in its own app' is suppressed because they asked for strict order. The user is told order is enforced while it silently is not. Neither shipped brand hits this today (Eufy honors order so effective_strict folds to False and the advisory is None anyway; Roborock is on the overriding engine).
guards_checked: (1) `_build_dispatch_phases`'s `effective_strict = bool(strict_order) and not honors_order` (run_plan.py:771-776) — narrows WHEN the flag is passed but never checks whether the engine acted on it. (2) `capabilities.honors_clean_order` — an adapter-declared hint consumed only by run_plan, never by the engine. (3) The DispatchEngine Protocol's `job_model` attribute (dispatch_engines.py:62-63) — declared on the class, but nothing at the call site reads it; run_plan calls `build_phases` and takes the length of the result. (4) `_START_SELECTED_ROOMS_SCHEMA` (services/job_control.py:92, `vol.Optional("strict_order"): cv.boolean`) — accepts the flag for any brand with no capability check. (5) `advance_active_job_phase` / `start_selected_rooms`'s `phases if len(_phases) > 1 else None` (core/manager.py:5034) — a swallowed strict_order yields exactly 1 phase, so the job degrades to atomic with no error path.

confirmations: Confirmed. _SinglePhaseMixin.build_phases (dispatch_engines.py:110-114) accepts strict_order and drops it, the Protocol blesses the silence (93-97), and the returned envelope carries no field recording refusal. run_plan.py:1458-1461 computes order_advisory from the RAW strict_order parameter, not effective_strict and not any engine feedback, and _order_advisory (697-723) returns text exactly when honors_clean_order is False — the same brand class where effective_strict is True. Neither shipped brand hits it (Eufy folds to False and gets no advisory anyway; Roborock is on the overriding engine), so future-brand-only is correct. Structural seam gap, MEDIUM is right per rule 4.

Confirmed: _SinglePhaseMixin.build_phases (dispatch_engines.py:110-114) accepts and drops strict_order, the Protocol blesses it (93-97), and the returned envelope has no field recording refusal — so this genuinely cannot be detected downstream. run_plan.py:1458-1464 computes order_advisory from the RAW strict_order parameter, not effective_strict and not engine feedback, with a comment asserting order 'is then ENFORCED'. Verified not reachable today: Eufy honors order so effective_strict folds False (advisory is None anyway) and Roborock is on the overriding engine. Structural seam (a future path-optimizing brand on a list-of-dicts or positional-array shape is told order is enforced while it silently is not) — MEDIUM per the campaign's structural-seam rule.

title: DreameSegmentEngine's documented 'direct envelope (no command)' is unreachable — an omitted command defaults to Eufy's room_clean
area: AREA 3 — Dispatch engines (queue/dispatch_engines.py): the DispatchEngine Protocol, _SinglePhaseMixin, EufyRoomCleanEngine, GenericRoomIdsEngine, RoborockSegmentEngine, DreameSegmentEngine, get_dispatch_engine / known_dispatch_templates — plus the seams where their output is consumed (planning/run_plan.py _build_dispatch_phases/_build_steps_phases, jobs/phase_runner.py _dispatch_active_phase, dispatch/manager.py _resolve_live_dispatch_payload/_dispatch_clean_payload, adapters/registry.py _validate_adapter).
observed_behavior: The class docstring instructs the adapter author: "Direct envelope (no ``command``)", and the schema echoes it (adapters/config_schema.py:1007-1014, `command` required False, "Omit for templates that call the service directly"). The send site does not implement that: dispatch/manager.py:67 reads `command = command_override or cfg.get("command", "room_clean")` — the default is the EUFY verb, not None. Line 80-83 then branches on `if command:`, which is truthy for the string "room_clean", so the direct-merge branch `data = {"entity_id": ..., **payload}` is only reachable if the adapter explicitly writes `"command": None`. An adapter that follows the Dreame engine's own docstring and omits the key sends `vacuum_clean_segment` with `{entity_id, command: "room_clean", params: {segments:[...], suction_level:[...], repeats:[...]}}`. The Roborock adapter already carries the counter-knowledge as a hand-written comment ("`command` MUST be explicit — an absent key defaults to Eufy's `room_clean`", adapters/roborock/adapter.py:328-329), i.e. the trap was discovered once and documented per-adapter instead of being fixed or reflected in the engine that most needs it. The other two DreameSegmentEngine docstring claims are also unbacked: the module header (lines 48-53) presents Dreame as the `sequenced` job-model example, but the class mixes in `_SinglePhaseMixin` so `job_model == "atomic_batch"` and it never emits multiple phases.
user_impact: Whoever enables the shipped-but-unused dreame_room_clean template and follows the engine's own documentation produces a service call the device cannot execute — the clean never starts, and because `_dispatch_clean_payload` awaits `hass.services.async_call(..., blocking=True)` the failure surfaces as a raw HA service exception rather than anything that names the misconfiguration. Zero impact today (no Dreame adapter ships), but the engine is registered in `_DISPATCH_ENGINES` and therefore passes `_validate_adapter`'s template check, so it presents as ready.
guards_checked: (1) `_validate_adapter`'s dispatch block check (adapters/registry.py:432-441) — validates only that `template` names a registered engine; it does not cross-check `command` against the template, and its issues are warnings (registry.py:154-173) not rejections. (2) adapters/config_schema.py — a documentation/test dict only; nothing imports it for runtime validation (verified: the only importers are tests/integration/test_adapters.py and tests/adapters/test_adapter_contract.py). (3) `command_override` (dispatch/manager.py:51) — used only by the zone path (`dispatch_zone_clean`), never by the room path. (4) `params_as_list` (line 74-79) — orthogonal; it shapes params inside the wrapped envelope and is ignored on the direct-merge branch that is never taken.

confirmations: Confirmed. dispatch/manager.py:67 is `command = command_override or cfg.get('command', 'room_clean')` — the default is Eufy's verb, and line 80 `if command:` is truthy for that string, so the direct-merge branch at 83 is only reachable if an adapter writes an explicit `"command": None`. DreameSegmentEngine's docstring at dispatch_engines.py:316 says 'Direct envelope (no command)'. I also confirmed the secondary claim: the module header presents Dreame as the sequenced example while the class mixes in _SinglePhaseMixin, so job_model is 'atomic_batch'. The Roborock adapter's hand-written comment at 328-329 documents the trap per-adapter instead of fixing it.

Confirmed: dispatch/manager.py:67 `command = command_override or cfg.get('command', 'room_clean')` defaults to the Eufy verb, and 80-83 branches on truthiness, so the direct-merge arm is only reachable with an explicit "command": None. The DreameSegmentEngine docstring (316) and config_schema.py:1007-1014 both tell the author to OMIT the key. Also confirmed the second docstring error: DreameSegmentEngine mixes in _SinglePhaseMixin, so job_model is 'atomic_batch' despite the module header presenting Dreame as the 'sequenced' example. However the seam CAN express the intent ("command": None works, and roborock/adapter.py:328-329 documents it), so this is a doc/default mismatch on an engine no shipped adapter uses — not a structural inexpressibility. Zero installs affected.

title: An omitted dispatch.template silently resolves to the Eufy engine with no warning, and the claimed registration-time rejection does not exist
area: AREA 3 — Dispatch engines (queue/dispatch_engines.py): the DispatchEngine Protocol, _SinglePhaseMixin, EufyRoomCleanEngine, GenericRoomIdsEngine, RoborockSegmentEngine, DreameSegmentEngine, get_dispatch_engine / known_dispatch_templates — plus the seams where their output is consumed (planning/run_plan.py _build_dispatch_phases/_build_steps_phases, jobs/phase_runner.py _dispatch_active_phase, dispatch/manager.py _resolve_live_dispatch_payload/_dispatch_clean_payload, adapters/registry.py _validate_adapter).
observed_behavior: `get_dispatch_engine(name)` starts with `if not name: return _DISPATCH_ENGINES[_FALLBACK_TEMPLATE]` and the docstring states the silence is deliberate ("an absent name is normal legacy behavior and is not warned"). Nothing upstream restores that signal for a NEW adapter: (a) adapters/config_schema.py:982-996 marks `template` `required: True`, but the schema is documentation-only — no runtime code imports it; (b) `_validate_adapter` (adapters/registry.py:432-441) guards with `if template is not None`, so an ABSENT template is not even examined; (c) even for a present-but-unknown template the result is only `issues.append(...)`, and `register_adapter_config` (registry.py:154-173) logs each issue as a warning and registers the config anyway, raising only for a non-dict — which directly falsifies the comment at registry.py:428-431 ("is rejected at registration rather than silently falling back to the Eufy shape and cleaning wrong"); (d) `_warn_eufy_fallbacks` (registry.py:256-281), the mechanism written for exactly this failure class ("every permissive default in this framework resolves to a concrete EUFY answer, not to a refusal"), enumerates `_EUFY_FALLBACK_BLOCKS = {mapping, job_segmenter, room_attribution}` — dispatch, the only block that COMMANDS the robot, is not in the table. Net: a brand-3 adapter that declares `service_domain`/`service_name`/`command`/`rooms_field`/`clean_passes_field`/`room_fields` and forgets `template` gets EufyRoomCleanEngine, which emits `{<map_id_field>: X, <rooms_field>: [{<room_id_field>: 3, <clean_passes_field>: 1, ...}]}` — a list of DICTS under the brand's own field names — with no log line at any level.
user_impact: A future brand's clean command is built in the wrong structural shape and shipped to its service. The failure mode is either a hard service error at start (best case) or a partially-parsed command the device acts on. The framework's own audibility mechanism for this exact class of silent-Eufy-fallback covers three engine seams and omits the actuation seam; per the campaign's sibling-sweep finding this is the vocabulary-by-hand-copied-comment pattern reappearing at the most consequential block.
guards_checked: (1) `_validate_adapter` dispatch check (registry.py:432-441) — `template is not None` guard skips absent templates entirely; warning-only for unknown ones. (2) `register_adapter_config` (registry.py:142-179) — `raise TypeError` only on a non-dict config; every other issue proceeds to `self._registry[vacuum_entity_id] = config`. (3) `_warn_eufy_fallbacks` (registry.py:256-281) — read in full; `_EUFY_FALLBACK_BLOCKS` (lines 237-253) has no `dispatch` entry. (4) config_schema.py `required: True` on template — verified unenforced; grepped every importer of adapters.config_schema (tests only). (5) `known_dispatch_templates()` — correct and in sync with `_DISPATCH_ENGINES`, but only consulted on the `is not None` path. (6) Both shipped adapters DO declare template (eufy/adapter.py:555, roborock/adapter.py:332), so no live install is affected.

confirmations: Confirmed on every leg. get_dispatch_engine returns the Eufy engine for a falsy name with no log (dispatch_engines.py:421-422). registry.py:432-435 guards with `if template is not None`, so an ABSENT template is never examined; register_adapter_config (142-179) logs issues as warnings and raises only for a non-dict, which directly falsifies the comment at 428-431 claiming registration-time rejection. I read _EUFY_FALLBACK_BLOCKS in full (registry.py:237-253): mapping, job_segmenter, room_attribution — no dispatch entry, in the one block that actually commands the robot. Both shipped adapters do declare template (eufy:555, roborock:332), so no live install is affected.

Every claim verified in source. get_dispatch_engine (dispatch_engines.py:421-422) returns the Eufy engine for an absent name with no log. _validate_adapter (registry.py:432-441) guards with `if template is not None`, so an ABSENT template is never examined, and an unknown one only appends to `issues`. register_adapter_config (registry.py:154-170) logs issues as warnings and then registers anyway, raising TypeError only for a non-dict — which directly falsifies the comment at registry.py:428-431 ('rejected at registration'). _EUFY_FALLBACK_BLOCKS (registry.py:237-253) contains exactly mapping / job_segmenter / room_attribution — no 'dispatch' entry, so the framework's own silent-Eufy-fallback audibility mechanism omits the only block that COMMANDS the robot. Both shipped adapters declare template (eufy:555, roborock:332), so no live install is affected. Structural seam at the actuation block -> MEDIUM stands.

title: Engine phase envelopes omit queue_room_ids/queue_rooms, making the run-plan group-union computation dead code and emptying queue_rooms on every phase advance
area: AREA 3 — Dispatch engines (queue/dispatch_engines.py): the DispatchEngine Protocol, _SinglePhaseMixin, EufyRoomCleanEngine, GenericRoomIdsEngine, RoborockSegmentEngine, DreameSegmentEngine, get_dispatch_engine / known_dispatch_templates — plus the seams where their output is consumed (planning/run_plan.py _build_dispatch_phases/_build_steps_phases, jobs/phase_runner.py _dispatch_active_phase, dispatch/manager.py _resolve_live_dispatch_payload/_dispatch_clean_payload, adapters/registry.py _validate_adapter).
observed_behavior: Every engine return envelope — `build_payload` (lines 211-217, 390-396) and `_build_per_room_phases` (lines 273-280) — carries exactly `{vacuum_entity_id, map_id, payload, resolved_rooms, room_count}`. It never carries `queue_room_ids` or `queue_rooms`, yet both keys are part of the phase shape everywhere else: planning/run_plan.py hand-builds charge_wait / wait / zone phases with explicit `"queue_room_ids": [], "queue_rooms": []` (lines 851, 858, 877), and two consumers read them off phases. (a) run_plan.py:902 computes the collapse fallback's room set as `all_ids = [rid for p in collapsed for rid in p.get("queue_room_ids", [])]` then `queue_room_ids=all_ids or sorted(included_room_ids)` — because engine phases never set the key, `all_ids` is unconditionally `[]` and the `or` branch is the only reachable one, so the union-of-groups intent is dead code. (b) queue/queue_engine.py:465 `advanced["queue_rooms"] = list(next_phase.get("queue_rooms", []))` — every advance past phase 0 of a strict-order run therefore writes `queue_rooms: []` onto the active job, even though phase 0 inherited the full list from `queue_state` (queue_engine.py:406).
user_impact: No user-visible wrong result today, but both are unearned rescues rather than correct code. (a) is masked only because `included_room_ids` currently happens to equal the union of the groups' rooms — `apply_run_profile` disables every room then re-enables exactly the profile's room_group rooms (profiles/manager.py:1201-1242), and blocked rooms are already disabled out of `effective_rooms` (run_plan.py:1297-1298). Any future step type that scopes a subset of the enabled rooms silently widens the collapse to every included room. (b) is masked only by ordering: `_room_name_from_active_job` (jobs/active_job.py:619-627) scans `resolved_rooms` before `queue_rooms` and the current phase's room is always in the former, and learning/job_finalizer.py:298-300 re-reads `queue_live` when the snapshot's list is empty.
guards_checked: (1) run_plan.py:902 `all_ids or sorted(included_room_ids)` — the masking fallback; confirmed it is the only branch ever taken. (2) `build_room_clean_payload`'s `selected_ids = set(queue_room_ids or [])` plus `not selected_ids or ...` (queue_engine.py:213, 242) — an empty id list would widen to ALL enabled rooms, so the `sorted(included_room_ids)` fallback is load-bearing, not cosmetic. (3) jobs/active_job.py:319 `normalized.setdefault("queue_rooms", [])` — normalizes shape, does not repopulate.
