title: Cancel is defeated by the phase watchdog: _cancel_in_flight is checked once, before two multi-second awaits, then the clean is dispatched unconditionally
area: AREA 4 — ACTUATION: dispatch/manager.py (_dispatch_clean_payload, dispatch_zone_clean, _resolve_live_dispatch_payload, _run_global_pre_calls) plus its two production send-sites (core/manager.py start_selected_rooms, jobs/phase_runner.py _dispatch_active_phase/_run_advanced_phase) and dispatch/zone_dispatch.py
observed_behavior:
_run_advanced_phase checks the cancel flag at line 536-549 and then calls `await self._dispatch_active_phase(...)` (552-555). Inside _dispatch_active_phase there are three awaits before the send and NO re-check of `_cancel_in_flight`:
```
await self._manager._run_global_pre_calls(...)                 # blocking=True select.select_option to the device
await ...apply_per_room_live_settings_awaited(...)             # blocking=True vacuum.set_fan_speed
wire_payload = await self._manager._resolve_live_dispatch_payload(...)  # -> async_refresh_room_source -> roborock.get_maps, blocking=True, network
await self._manager._dispatch_clean_payload(...)               # fires regardless
```
Meanwhile jobs/active_job.py:2198-2215 sets `_cancel_in_flight = True` and `_phase_dispatch_pending = False` synchronously and then awaits `vacuum.return_to_base`. Its comment claims the flag "stops [the watchdog] before it can re-dispatch during the return-to-base window" — that is true only if the flag is re-read after each await, and it never is. A cancel landing anywhere inside the ~1-4 s pre-call + get_maps window is therefore followed by an app_segment_clean. This is a genuine cross-await interleaving (a blocking service call and a network refresh), not a mid-synchronous-block race. user_impact: User presses Cancel Run. The robot heads for the dock, then turns around and cleans the next room. The integration has already finalized and discarded the job, so nothing tracks or will stop the run; the user must cancel again (or from the vendor app). title: A raising dispatch kills the phase watchdog task and wedges the run in 'started' forever
area: AREA 4 — ACTUATION: dispatch/manager.py (_dispatch_clean_payload, dispatch_zone_clean, _resolve_live_dispatch_payload, _run_global_pre_calls) plus its two production send-sites (core/manager.py start_selected_rooms, jobs/phase_runner.py _dispatch_active_phase/_run_advanced_phase) and dispatch/zone_dispatch.py
observed_behavior:
_run_advanced_phase's retry loop is:
```

        await self._dispatch_active_phase(...)   # no try/except
    if await self._await_phase_started(...):
```

_dispatch_active_phase can raise from three places: `_dispatch_clean_payload` -> hass.services.async_call(blocking=True) raises HomeAssistantError when the vacuum entity is unavailable or the brand integration rejects the command; `apply_per_room_live_settings_awaited` -> vacuum.set_fan_speed likewise; and on a zone phase `dispatch_zone_clean` raises ValueError by design for every cap violation (zone_max, degenerate rect, zone_min/max_area_m2, zone_min/max_side_m, unconvertible projection — dispatch/manager.py:109/118/122/131/151/158/169/173/223/228). _run_advanced_phase is only ever started via `hass.async_create_task(...)` (core/manager.py:5072, phase_runner.py:193) with no wrapper, so the exception ends the task. title: The mixed-batch water SAFETY pre-call is best-effort — if it fails the clean still dispatches and the robot wet-mops the vacuum-only rooms
area: AREA 4 — ACTUATION: dispatch/manager.py (_dispatch_clean_payload, dispatch_zone_clean, _resolve_live_dispatch_payload, _run_global_pre_calls) plus its two production send-sites (core/manager.py start_selected_rooms, jobs/phase_runner.py _dispatch_active_phase/_run_advanced_phase) and dispatch/zone_dispatch.py
observed_behavior:
_run_global_pre_calls ends every entry with:
```

    await self._manager.hass.services.async_call(domain, service_name, {"entity_id": target_entity, value_key: wire_value}, blocking=True)
except Exception:
    _LOGGER.exception("global pre-call %s.%s failed for %s", ...)
```
and the caller then dispatches the clean regardless (core/manager.py:5005-5023; phase_runner.py:1010-1027). For a plain fan pre-call "best-effort" is defensible. For the `mixed_mode_water_policy: "safest"` entry it is not: that entry IS the safety mechanism. The docstring states the contract — "a device-GLOBAL water/mop-intensity select can't be zeroed per-room, so a mixed mop + vacuum-only batch that max-wins to the strongest water would WET-MOP the dry (vacuum-only) rooms" — and the whole mitigation is the one select_option call at 436. title: Per-zone SIZE bounds are enforced by coordinate-space branch, not by which bound the adapter declared — the other combination is silently ignored
area: AREA 5 — ZONE CLEAN (dispatch/manager.py::dispatch_zone_clean + all of dispatch/zone_dispatch.py)
observed_behavior: The two size checks are hard-wired to opposite branches of the coordinate-space `if`. title: Eufy per-side bound check is skipped entirely when live-map dims are unreadable, while the mm branch REFUSES on the same missing input

title: Every break/zone phase flips transit_capture_valid to False, so a stepped run's per-room learning silently degrades to an even split of the run's wall time — charge/wait dock time included
area: AREA 6 — Phases and the lifecycle handoff (queue/queue_engine.py build_active_job_state / advance_active_job_phase / TypedDicts, and the seam into jobs/phase_runner.py, jobs/active_job.py, learning/history_store.py)
observed_behavior: phase_runner._capture_finishing_phase_timing DELIBERATELY writes an empty timing for non-cleaning phases: `phases[idx]["room_timing"] = []` at line 256 (charge_wait/wait, via is_dock_polled_phase) and line 270 (zone). history_store then reads that same key as a captured/not-captured flag: `_every_phase_captured = isinstance(_phases, list) and bool(_phases)` (983-985), then `for _p in _phases: _rt = _p.get("room_timing"); if _rt: _phase_room_timings.extend(_rt) else: _every_phase_captured = False` (986-992), then `transit_capture_valid = _every_phase_captured` (996). An empty list is falsy, so any charge_wait / wait / zone phase forces False. run_plan._build_steps_phases GUARANTEES at least one such phase survives in any multi-phase list: lines 898-908 collapse the list back to a single atomic dispatch phase whenever `not any(p.get("phase_type") in _BREAKS or == "zone")`, and manager.py:5034 only attaches `phases` when `len(_phases) > 1`. So transit_capture_valid is False for EVERY stepped run, without exception. Downstream, stats_rebuilder.py:440 gates the entire per-room capture on it — `if _safe_bool(job_info.get("transit_capture_valid"), False): for _rt in job_info.get("room_timings")... captured[_rid] = (area_m2, cleaning_wall_seconds/60)`. With it False, `captured` stays empty and every room falls back to `per_room_duration = total_duration / room_count` (stats_rebuilder.py:413, 431). And `total_duration` is `job.duration_minutes`, computed at history_store.py:848-855 as `wall_clock - paused_duration_seconds - recharge_seconds_accumulated` — the PLANNED charge/wait hold is in none of those subtrahends, because active_job.update_active_job_recharge_observation returns early for a dock-polled phase (active_job.py:427-435) precisely so the planned dock is not counted as a recharge. A 20-min vacuum + 90-min charge + 20-min mop run therefore teaches every room 130/N minutes.
user_impact: Every run that uses the charge_wait / wait / zone step feature writes corrupted per-room baselines: the exact per-room area and wall-minutes that were captured are thrown away, and each room instead learns an even share of the whole run including the charging hold. Room time estimates, the water/battery estimator and the preflight 'expected minutes' inflate run after run, with no error or warning anywhere.
guards_checked: job_finalizer._apply_idle_wall_hold (691-696) — I expected this to exclude break-phase runs from learning and rescue the corpus; it does the OPPOSITE, `_run_had_break_phase(active_job_state)` is passed as `had_break_phase` specifically to EXEMPT these runs from the extreme_idle_wall hold, so `used_for_learning` stays True and the poisoned even-split is ingested. outcome.learning_blockers is untouched by transit_capture_valid. phase_runner.py:314-325 (`area_source: learned_fallback`) repairs area INSIDE room_timing, but room_timings is discarded wholesale by the gate. history_store.py:997-1007 (_build_transit_blocks legacy path) is not reached — `_phase_room_timings` is non-empty whenever any room phase captured, so the else branch never runs for a stepped job.

title: A multi-room room_group phase is recorded as ONE room — the group's whole cleaning time, area and battery are attributed to its first room and every other room in the group vanishes from the record
area: AREA 6 — Phases and the lifecycle handoff (queue/queue_engine.py build_active_job_state / advance_active_job_phase / TypedDicts, and the seam into jobs/phase_runner.py, jobs/active_job.py, learning/history_store.py)
observed_behavior: _capture_finishing_phase_timing hardcodes one-room-per-phase: `queue_ids = [_safe_int(r,-1) for r in (active_job.get("queue_room_ids") or []) if > 0]` then `rid = queue_ids[0]` (297-301), then `room_timings = [self._phase_room_timing(rid, slug_by_id.get(rid), slice_samples)] if rid is not None and len(usable) >= 2 else []` (310-313) — a single-element list, always. _phase_room_timing's own docstring states the assumption: 'One strict-order phase = one room' (430). But a phase is NOT always one room. run_plan._build_dispatch_phases computes `effective_strict = bool(strict_order) and not honors_order` (776); Eufy declares `honors_clean_order: True` (adapters/eufy/adapter.py, capabilities), so effective_strict is False even though _build_effective_start_plan passes strict_order=True for a stepped run (run_plan.py:1363-1370). effective_strict False routes to _SinglePhaseMixin.build_phases (dispatch_engines.py:110-114), which returns ONE phase containing ALL of the group's rooms. So a Eufy step list [room_group{Kitchen,Hallway}, charge_wait, room_group{Dining}] produces phase 0 with resolved_rooms = [Kitchen, Hallway] and room_count 2, and _phase_room_timing computes cleaning_seconds / area_m2 / battery_delta as last−first over the phase's whole counter slice — both rooms — and stamps it with Kitchen's room_id. Hallway gets no room_timing entry at all. history_store.py:986-994 concatenates these per-phase lists straight into the record's `job.room_timings`.
user_impact: On a Eufy stepped run, the run review / history shows 'Kitchen — 34 min, 61 m²' (the combined figure for Kitchen AND Hallway) and shows nothing for Hallway. Any consumer of room_timings sees one room where two cleaned. If DQ-PH-1 is fixed without fixing this, that fabricated figure becomes Kitchen's learned baseline.
guards_checked: phase_runner.py:306-313 — the `len(usable) >= 2` guard only suppresses a timing when the slice has no counter samples; it does not bound the room count. phase_runner.py:290-295 builds slug_by_id over ALL of the phase's resolved_rooms, proving the code already knows the phase can hold more than one room, yet only queue_ids[0] is used. phase_runner.py:314-325's learned-area fallback iterates `for rt in room_timings` — a list that can never exceed length 1. history_store.py:986-992 does not de-duplicate or validate room_timings length against room_count. run_plan.py:842-846 (`phases.extend(self._build_dispatch_phases(...))`) is the site that would have split the group, but only when effective_strict is True.

confirmations: Confirmed. phase_runner.py:297-313 takes `rid = queue_ids[0]` and builds a single-element room_timings list, while lines 290-295 build slug_by_id over ALL of the phase's resolved_rooms — the code already knows a phase can hold more than one room. The multi-room-phase premise checks out for Eufy: run_plan.py:771-776 sets effective_strict = strict_order and not honors_order, honors_clean_order defaults True and Eufy does not declare it, so a stepped Eufy run routes to _SinglePhaseMixin.build_phases (dispatch_engines.py:110-114) and each room_group becomes ONE phase containing all its rooms. history_store.py:986-992 concatenates without validating length against room_count.

Reproduced on Eufy. run_plan.py:776 effective_strict = strict_order and not honors_order; Eufy declares honors_clean_order True, so a stepped run (which forces strict_order=True at 1369) still routes to _SinglePhaseMixin.build_phases (dispatch_engines.py:110-114) and each room_group becomes ONE phase holding all its rooms. phase_runner.py:297-301 then takes rid = queue_ids[0] and 310-313 builds a single-element room_timings list whose cleaning_seconds/area_m2/battery_delta are last-minus-first over the phase's WHOLE counter slice — both rooms — stamped with the first room's id. _phase_room_timing's own docstring (430) states the 'one phase = one room' assumption. slug_by_id is built over ALL of the phase's resolved_rooms (290-295), proving the code knows a phase can hold several. history_store.py:986-992 concatenates the result into job.room_timings with no length check, so the run review shows one room carrying two rooms' figures and the other room absent.

title: QueueEntry / PayloadItem / ActiveJobSnapshot describe a shape the module has never emitted, and disagree with build_active_job_state on the fields it does write
area: AREA 6 — Phases and the lifecycle handoff (queue/queue_engine.py build_active_job_state / advance_active_job_phase / TypedDicts, and the seam into jobs/phase_runner.py, jobs/active_job.py, learning/history_store.py)
observed_behavior: ActiveJobSnapshot (62-78) declares `queue_entries: dict`, `payload_items: dict`, `frozen_at: float`, `job_id: str`, `started_at: float`, `ended_at: Optional[float]` and `status: "running"|"paused"|"completed"|"cancelled"`. build_active_job_state (401-427) writes NONE of queue_entries / payload_items / frozen_at / job_id / ended_at, writes `"status": "started"` — a value absent from the declared union — and every timestamp the manager attaches is an ISO string, not a float (`active_job["started_at"] = started_at` where `started_at = _iso_now()`, manager.py:4997/5038). Conversely, the ~12 keys the builder actually writes (queue_rooms, payload, resolved_rooms, room_count, paused_at, paused_duration_seconds, completed_room_ids, completed_rooms, current_room_id, current_room_started_at, current_room_paused_seconds) plus the three phase keys (phases / current_phase_index / phase_count) are undeclared. PayloadItem declares `stable_key` and `map_id` per room, which build_room_clean_payload never emits, and `clean_passes`, which it emits under the adapter's `clean_passes_field` (default 'clean_times'). All three are total=False and unreferenced, so nothing validates against them.
user_impact: No runtime effect — these are documentation only. But they are the first thing a reader (or a future brand adapter author) opens to learn the snapshot contract, and they describe a different system. The module comment at 19-24 admits this, which makes them knowingly-stale rather than accidentally-stale; the real contract lives implicitly in jobs/active_job.py:253-292 (_default_active_job) and is not cross-referenced.
guards_checked: Verified they are unused: no `ActiveJobSnapshot(`, `QueueEntry(` or `PayloadItem(` construction or isinstance/annotation use anywhere in custom_components; total=False means even a type checker would not flag the missing keys. jobs/active_job._normalize_active_job (314-356) is the de-facto shape enforcer and setdefaults a completely different key set (counter_samples, state_transitions, observed_mop_wash_cycles, has_observed_active_lifecycle, ...) that no TypedDict here mentions.

confirmations: Confirmed the drift is real and precisely as described — build_active_job_state (queue_engine.py:401-427) writes status 'started' (absent from the declared union), omits queue_entries/payload_items/frozen_at/job_id/ended_at, and the ~12 keys it does write are undeclared; the classes are total=False and I found no construction or annotation use. However the module carries an explicit NOTE at lines 19-24 labelling all three 'legacy / aspirational' and stating they do not reflect what the module emits, which the finding itself acknowledges. Documented-stale documentation, not a hidden trap. LOW is correct and I would rank it last.

Verified accurate: ActiveJobSnapshot (queue_engine.py:62-78) declares queue_entries/payload_items/frozen_at/job_id/ended_at and a status union of running|paused|completed|cancelled, while build_active_job_state (401-427) writes none of those and sets status 'started'; the manager attaches ISO-string timestamps (core/manager.py:4997/5038) against declared floats. PayloadItem declares stable_key and per-room map_id that build_room_clean_payload never emits. Confirmed unused — no construction or isinstance/annotation use anywhere in custom_components, and total=False means a type checker would not flag the gaps. The module's own NOTE at 19-24 already admits this, so it is knowingly-stale documentation rather than a latent bug; correctly filed LOW.

title: advance_active_job_phase resets every per-phase pointer except _native_current_room_id, leaving a latent cross-phase carry-over that only the phases-gate currently hides
area: AREA 6 — Phases and the lifecycle handoff (queue/queue_engine.py build_active_job_state / advance_active_job_phase / TypedDicts, and the seam into jobs/phase_runner.py, jobs/active_job.py, learning/history_store.py)
observed_behavior: The 'Reset per-phase progress' block (466-484) clears completed_room_ids, completed_rooms, current_room_id, current_room_started_at, current_room_paused_seconds, status, has_observed_active_lifecycle and _phase_dispatch_pending, but not `_native_current_room_id`, which active_job.py:1221 and 1299 are the only writers of and which nothing anywhere clears (grep: 4 hits total, all in active_job.py). If the native-signal rollover ever ran on a phased job, `confirmed = _safe_int(active_job.get("_native_current_room_id", -1), -1)` (1206) would still hold the PREVIOUS phase's room when the new phase's room is first signalled, and the `confirmed >= 0` branch (1239-1246) would fire _set_native_current_room with `complete_room_id=confirmed` — re-completing the previous phase's room into the freshly-emptied completed list and firing a second EVENT_ROOM_FINISHED for it with the new phase's elapsed minutes.
user_impact: None today. It is a tripwire under the phases-gate: relaxing active_job.py:937 (which is the natural fix for DQ-PH-2/DQ-PH-3, since a multi-room group phase genuinely needs intra-phase rollover) immediately activates duplicate room-finished events and phantom completions on every phase boundary.
guards_checked: active_job.py:937-938 `if active_job.get("phases"): return active_job` — this is the only thing preventing it, and it sits above BOTH the native branch (951-952) and the timing branch, so it is a whole-mode kill switch rather than a targeted guard. Roborock's `rooms_unique_per_job: False` (adapters/roborock/adapter.py:589) would additionally force `complete_room_id=None` at 1244, so Roborock is doubly covered; Eufy declares `rooms_unique_per_job: True` (adapters/eufy/adapter.py:822) and so would be exposed the moment the gate moves — though Eufy also sets `native_transition_source: False` (adapter.py:753), a third independent gate.

confirmations: Confirmed. The reset block at queue_engine.py:466-484 clears eight keys and omits _native_current_room_id; I grepped the component and found only four references, all in active_job.py, with no clearing site anywhere. Correctly framed as a tripwire rather than a live bug: the `if active_job.get('phases'): return active_job` gate at active_job.py:936-938 is the only thing suppressing it, and that gate is precisely what a fix for DQ-PH-2/DQ-PH-3 would have to relax. I also confirmed the secondary gates the finder cited — Roborock's rooms_unique_per_job False (adapter.py:589) and Eufy's native_transition_source False — so the exposure really is Eufy-on-relaxation only.

Confirmed: the reset block at queue_engine.py:466-484 clears eight per-phase keys and omits _native_current_room_id, and a repo-wide grep returns exactly four hits, all in active_job.py (1180 docstring, 1206 read, 1221 and 1299 writes) — nothing anywhere clears it. title: clean_intensity is re-materialized as the Eufy literal "Quick" for Roborock rooms that deliberately carry no such key, and is written to the wire with no capability gate
area: AREA 2 — Payload building (queue/queue_engine.py build_room_clean_payload, queue/dispatch_engines.py, dispatch/manager.py, dispatch/zone_dispatch.py) and the profile-resolution inputs that feed it
observed_behavior: The fresh `rooms/room_defaults.py` change correctly omits `clean_intensity` for Roborock (`if field in profile`, room_defaults.py:81-83; Roborock's `ROOM_PROFILES` declare no such key, vocabulary.py:110-151). But the key does not stay absent. `resolve_room_profile_for_room` reads `room_config.get("clean_intensity", resolved_profile.get("clean_intensity", ""))` (room_profiles.py:416-418) — the room has no key, so it falls to `resolved_profile`, and `resolved_profile` came from `get_room_profile`, which returns `normalize_room_profile(profile, catalog)` (room_profiles.py:291). `normalize_room_profile` line 209 is `normalize_clean_intensity(source.get("clean_intensity", d.get("clean_intensity", "Quick")))` — `source` is Roborock's `vacuum_quick` (no key) and `d` is Roborock's `normalize_defaults` = `CUSTOM_ROOM_PROFILE` (also no key, vocabulary.py:153-162), so the hardcoded Eufy literal `"Quick"` is used. `apply_capability_gate` independently repeats the same literal at room_profiles.py:496. `build_room_clean_payload` then does `clean_intensity = str(gated["clean_intensity"])` (line 284), writes it UNCONDITIONALLY via `_write_room_field(..., "clean_intensity", ...)` at line 301 — note water_level, edge_mopping and path_type all sit behind capability gates at lines 303/306/309, but clean_intensity has none — and stamps it into `resolved_rooms[i]["clean_intensity"]` at line 329, which is frozen into the active-job snapshot (`build_active_job_state`, line 388) and consumed by learning/history.
user_impact: Every Roborock room reports a phantom `clean_intensity: "Quick"` it does not have and cannot act on, in the job snapshot, run history and learning records — the brand declares no `clean_intensity_options` at all. The value is discarded before the Roborock wire only because `RoborockSegmentEngine` throws the whole Eufy-shaped payload away; a future brand on the `eufy_room_clean` template that simply omits `clean_intensity` from its `room_fields` gets the literal "Quick" on the device wire (absent `room_fields` entry means identity rename + identity value, queue_engine.py:176-177).
guards_checked: (1) `rooms/room_defaults.NEW_ROOM_SETTING_FIELDS` + the `if field in profile` test — correct, and correctly leaves the key off the stored room; it is defeated one layer down. (2) Roborock's `room_profiles.normalize_defaults` (adapter.py:683 → `CUSTOM_ROOM_PROFILE`) — also omits the key, which is exactly why `normalize_room_profile` falls through to its hardcoded "Quick" rather than to a brand value. (3) `normalize_clean_intensity` (room_profiles.py:118-120) — only folds "standard"/"normal" to "Quick"; it passes "Quick" through and has no notion of "this brand has no intensity axis". (4) The capability gates in `build_room_clean_payload` at lines 303/306/309 — there is no `supports_clean_intensity` flag and no gate on line 301, so nothing suppresses the field. (5) `_write_room_field` field_name=None suppression — requires the adapter to declare the field explicitly as null; an adapter that just omits the entry gets it emitted.

killed_by: REFUTED at the premise. The finding requires the stored Roborock room to have NO clean_intensity key so resolve_room_profile_for_room falls through to the profile's 'Quick'. It always has the key. Both room-creation writers build through the RoomConfig dataclass and emit asdict() — rooms/room_manager.py:91-116 (`clean_intensity=str(_default('clean_intensity',''))`) and maps/map_manager.py:176-199 (`clean_intensity=str(_prev_or_brand('clean_intensity',''))`) — and models/models.py:208 declares `clean_intensity: str = ''`. room_defaults correctly omits the field, so the RoomConfig default '' is used and STORED. Therefore room_profiles.py:416-418 returns '' (room wins), apply_capability_gate's `settings.get('clean_intensity','Quick')` finds '' present, and the payload/resolved_rooms carry '' — not 'Quick'. The stated user impact ('every Roborock room reports a phantom clean_intensity Quick' in job snapshot / history / learning) does not occur. The residual true fact — that queue_engine.py:301 writes clean_intensity with no capability gate while water/edge/path have one — is a much smaller latent issue and is already covered structurally by DQ-PAY-5.

title: A zone-first phased run dispatches an EMPTY clean command instead of the zone; the zone is only sent ~90 s later on the watchdog retry
area: AREA 4 — ACTUATION: dispatch/manager.py (_dispatch_clean_payload, dispatch_zone_clean, _resolve_live_dispatch_payload, _run_global_pre_calls) plus its two production send-sites (core/manager.py start_selected_rooms, jobs/phase_runner.py _dispatch_active_phase/_run_advanced_phase) and dispatch/zone_dispatch.py
observed_behavior:
start_selected_rooms takes `payload = payload_state.get("payload", {})` where `payload_state = phases[0]` (planning/run_plan.py:1379) and sends it unconditionally at 5015-5023, with no phase_type branch (grep for phase_type in core/manager.py finds only snapshot/timeline uses). A zone phase is built as `{"phase_type": "zone", "zones": rects, ..., "payload": {}, "room_count": 0}` (run_plan.py:873-879), so:
- `_run_global_pre_calls(resolved_rooms=[])` -> no-op
- `_resolve_live_dispatch_payload(payload={})` -> `rooms_field not in payload` -> returns `{}`
- `_dispatch_clean_payload(payload={})` -> Roborock: `{entity_id, command: "app_segment_clean", params: [{}]}`; Eufy: `{entity_id, command: "room_clean", params: {}}`
The drawn zone rects are simply discarded. _build_steps_phases' own docstring asserts "Leading/trailing/duplicate charge phases (nothing to bracket) are dropped so phase 0 is always a real clean the initial dispatch can send" — but the strip loops at run_plan.py:884-887 test `phase_type in _BREAKS` where `_BREAKS = ("charge_wait", "wait")`, so a leading ZONE is never stripped and is not a payload the initial dispatch can send.
Two reachable routes to a zone at index 0: (a) a saved run profile whose steps list begins with a zone — ProfileManager.normalize_run_profile_steps (profiles/manager.py:751-809) validates shape only and imposes no ordering, and start_run_profile stashes the list verbatim into _pending_run_steps (profiles/manager.py:1311-1316); (b) any well-formed `[room_group, zone, room_group]` profile whose FIRST group's rooms are all disabled or blocked — `if not group_ids: continue` (run_plan.py:828-829) drops the group and promotes the zone to index 0.
Recovery is slow by design: `_run_advanced_phase(phase_index=0, initial=True)` deliberately skips the dispatch on attempt 1 ("phase 0 was already dispatched by start_selected_rooms", 552), so the real zone command is not sent until _await_phase_started burns its no-progress budget (verify_seconds = 90 s on Roborock) and attempt 2 calls _dispatch_active_phase, which DOES branch on the zone type (phase_runner.py:996-1008).
user_impact: The user starts a zone-first run profile. A malformed segment/room clean goes to the robot (device error at best; on Eufy the fork's room_clean handler receives no map_id/rooms at all). Nothing cleans for ~90 s, then the zone finally starts. If the brand integration raises on the empty command, the exception propagates out of start_selected_rooms — no active job is ever created, the run silently never happens, and the popped run-profile steps are already gone (see DQ-ACT-6).
guards_checked: add_queue_zone clamps `after = max(1, min(after_index, room_count))` (core/manager.py:1749) and set_queue_breaks clamps identically (1843-1844) — these DO prevent a leading zone from the ad-hoc queue path, and are exactly why this looked safe; they do not cover the run-profile stash path, which bypasses queue_breaks entirely. normalize_run_profile_steps: shape-only, no ordering. The leading/trailing strip loops (run_plan.py:884-887) and the collapse loop (888-894) test only _BREAKS. maybe_advance_phase DOES route by phase_type (phase_runner.py:182-199) and _dispatch_active_phase DOES handle zone — the initial phase-0 send is the single path that does not.

killed_by: REFUTED by the preflight the finder listed as 'not a guard here'. start_selected_rooms calls get_start_status FIRST (core/manager.py:4938) and returns early on blocked (4943). get_start_status builds the SAME plan via _build_effective_start_plan (2765-2770, peek mode — it still sees the stashed steps and still builds phases through _build_steps_phases) and passes int(payload_state.get('room_count',0)) to build_start_blocker_from_lifecycle (2857). A zone phase is constructed with room_count 0 (run_plan.py:878), so job_monitor.py:268-273 returns invalid_payload/blocked and the run never reaches line 5021. This holds for BOTH stated routes — an authored zone-first profile and a [room_group, zone, room_group] whose first group is fully blocked — because either way phases[0] is the zone phase with room_count 0. The empty room_clean is never dispatched. The real defect at this seam is DQ-Q-3 (the run is permanently unstartable with a misleading 'payload is missing or invalid' message).

title: max_residual_mm returns 0.0 for NaN coefficients, so the refuse-gate passes and the dispatch dies on int(round(nan)) instead
area: AREA 5 — ZONE CLEAN (dispatch/manager.py::dispatch_zone_clean + all of dispatch/zone_dispatch.py)
observed_behavior: _solve3_two:36 tests `if abs(d) < 1e-9: return None`; for d = NaN that comparison is False, so a NaN determinant is NOT treated as singular and the solver returns NaN coefficients. max_residual_mm:89-99 then accumulates `worst = max(worst, abs(px - mx), abs(py - my))` — every comparison against NaN is False, so Python's max() keeps the incumbent and `worst` stays 0.0. normalized_rects_to_mm:119 `if max_residual_mm(...) > validate_tol_mm: return None` therefore does not fire, and the NaN rects are returned to the caller as if validated. Verified by direct execution against the real module: appending a single (nan, 0.5, 0.0, 0.0) correspondence to a clean 8-point set yields coeffs (nan,)*6 and resid 0.0. The dispatch then fails at dispatch/manager.py:186 `int(round(x0))`, which raises ValueError('cannot convert float NaN to integer').
user_impact: No wrong dispatch — it fails closed by accident, at the wrong layer. The user gets 'Failed to start zone clean: cannot convert float NaN to integer' instead of the designed 'could not place the drawn zone on the device coordinate frame ... refusing to dispatch', which is the message that tells them to re-open the map. The documented safety contract ('the fit ... is then round-trip VALIDATED ... returns None and the caller MUST refuse', zone_dispatch.py:11-15) is not the thing that stopped it.
guards_checked: (1) _solve3_two:36 singularity check — verified non-firing for NaN. title: A run whose first phase is a zone dispatches an empty room_clean command to the robot, because start_selected_rooms always sends phases[0]['payload'] and a zone phase's payload is {}
area: AREA 6 — Phases and the lifecycle handoff (queue/queue_engine.py build_active_job_state / advance_active_job_phase / TypedDicts, and the seam into jobs/phase_runner.py, jobs/active_job.py, learning/history_store.py)
observed_behavior: run_plan._build_effective_start_plan sets `payload_state = phases[0]` unconditionally (1379). run_plan._build_steps_phases drops only leading BREAKS — `_BREAKS = ("charge_wait", "wait")` and `while phases and phases[0].get("phase_type") in _BREAKS: phases.pop(0)` (883-885) — a `zone` phase is explicitly excluded from _BREAKS ('A zone is a real clean phase', 895-897) and therefore survives in position 0. A zone phase is constructed at 873-879 with `"payload": {}, "room_count": 0, "resolved_rooms": []`. start_selected_rooms then does `payload = payload_state.get("payload", {})` (4986) → {}, passes it through _resolve_live_dispatch_payload (which returns it unchanged because `rooms_field not in payload`, dispatch/manager.py:275-276), and calls `await self._dispatch_clean_payload(vacuum_entity_id=..., payload=wire_payload)` (5021-5023) with no room-count check. DispatchManager._dispatch_clean_payload builds `data = {"entity_id": ..., "command": "room_clean", "params": {}}` (or `params=[{}]` for Roborock's `params_as_list`) and awaits `hass.services.async_call(..., blocking=True)` (dispatch/manager.py:79-84). The real zone dispatch is then deliberately skipped on the first watchdog attempt: _run_advanced_phase does `if not (initial and attempt == 1): await self._dispatch_active_phase(...)` (phase_runner.py:552-555), on the stated assumption that 'phase 0 was already dispatched by start_selected_rooms' (504-505) — which is false for a zone. The zone only actually goes out on retry attempt 2, after verify_seconds. Note that the docstring of _build_steps_phases claims 'phase 0 is always a real clean the initial dispatch can send' (807-808) — the initial dispatch can only send a ROOM clean, so that comment asserts a guarantee the code does not provide.
user_impact: A run profile whose first step is a zone either raises out of the start service (the empty send_command is awaited blocking and untried, and the active_job is not built until line 5029, so the run never starts and no job record exists) or pushes a malformed room_clean to the device; either way the zone itself is delayed by a full verify window. guards_checked: manager.add_queue_zone:1749 `after = max(1, min(_safe_int(after_index, 1), room_count))` DOES prevent a leading zone from the ad-hoc queue path, and its comment says 'It does not lead' — but profiles.normalize_run_profile_steps (751-809) applies no such ordering rule to a saved profile's steps, it only validates each step's shape, so steps=[{type:zone},{type:room_group}] normalizes cleanly and reaches _build_steps_phases. get_start_status is not a guard here — the queue has rooms, only phase 0 is roomless. _run_global_pre_calls at 5005-5008 is also fed payload_state's empty resolved_rooms, so the global fan/water pre-call is skipped for the whole run.

title: water_level and carpet fan_speed use a DIFFERENT precedence than every sibling field (floor default OVERRIDES the profile), so applying a built-in mop profile immediately re-labels the room "custom"
area: AREA 1 — THE RESOLUTION CORE (profiles/room_profiles.py: resolve_room_profile_for_room, resolve_profile_name_for_constraints, get_room_profile, normalize_clean_intensity)
observed_behavior: Every sibling field resolves as `room value (if key present) else profile value`. water_level does not: after line 423 sets it from the profile, lines 432-436 overwrite it — `if floor_type.startswith("carpet"): resolved_fan_speed = fan_defaults.get(...); resolved_water_level = water_defaults.get(...)` / `elif "water_level" not in room_config: resolved_water_level = water_defaults.get(floor_type, "")`. So for a room_config that omits water_level the FLOOR default wins over the profile, and on carpet the floor default wins over the profile for fan_speed too. Executed: resolve_room_profile_for_room({'profile_name':'vacuum_mop_quick','floor_type':'hardwood'})['water_level'] == 'Low' although vacuum_mop_quick declares 'Medium'; resolve_room_profile_for_room({'profile_name':'vacuum_quick','floor_type':'carpet_low_pile'})['fan_speed'] == 'Max' although vacuum_quick declares 'Standard'. That asymmetry breaks the profile round-trip. ProfileManager._match_profile_from_fields (profiles/manager.py:153-177) builds each candidate as a bare `{"profile_name": name, "floor_type": ...}` — no water_level key — so the candidate gets the FLOOR default, while the real room (written by apply_room_profile_to_config, room_profiles.py:565, which stores the PROFILE's water_level) carries the PROFILE value. I replayed the exact protect->resolve->protect->compare pipeline over all four built-ins x five floors: vacuum_mop_quick and vacuum_mop_deep match on 'tile' ONLY (where the floor default 'Medium' coincidentally equals the profile value) and fail to match on hardwood, laminate, marble, granite, concrete and carpet; vacuum_quick fails to match on carpet_low_pile (fan Standard vs carpet default Max). _finalize_room_update (manager.py:196) then does `result["profile_name"] = matched if matched else "custom"`, and it runs on BOTH apply_room_profile (manager.py:671) and every update_room_settings save (core/manager.py:1369).
user_impact: The user picks the built-in "Quick" or "Deep" mop profile for a hardwood/laminate/marble room; the save stores profile_name="custom" and the chip they just clicked deselects. Same for a plain vacuum room on low-pile carpet. Renaming a room, or changing any unrelated setting, also silently drops its profile label to "custom". The comment at manager.py:138-147 explicitly CLAIMS this asymmetry was closed by resolving the candidate under the room's floor_type — it was closed for vacuum rooms only, and the comment asserts a guard that does not cover mop rooms.
guards_checked: _normalize_profile_match_value (profiles/manager.py:113-135) — lowercases and folds "off", so 'Medium' vs 'Low' is a genuine mismatch, not a casing artefact. _protected_room_config (manager.py:84-111) — forces water_level "Off" only for non-mop modes, so it masks the asymmetry for vacuum profiles and leaves it exposed for mop profiles. The mop-with-no-water correction (room_profiles.py:443-448) — does not fire, because the candidate's floor default is non-empty on hardwood ('Low'). apply_room_profile_to_config (room_profiles.py:565) — writes the profile's water_level verbatim, with no floor-default reconciliation. RoomConfig.as_dict/asdict (models/models.py:237) — confirms real rooms always carry the water_level key, so only the CANDIDATE side takes the floor-default branch, which is what creates the asymmetry.

confirmations: CONFIRMED by execution against the shipped code. resolve_room_profile_for_room({'profile_name':'vacuum_mop_quick','floor_type':'hardwood'})['water_level'] == 'Low' (profile declares 'Medium'); ({'profile_name':'vacuum_quick','floor_type':'carpet_low_pile'})['fan_speed'] == 'Max' (profile declares 'Standard'). I then replayed the real apply_room_profile_to_config -> _protected_room_config -> _match_profile_from_fields pipeline over all 4 built-ins x 8 floors: vacuum_mop_quick/vacuum_mop_deep match ONLY on tile; hardwood/laminate/marble/granite/concrete all return None -> 'custom'. carpet_low_pile+vacuum_quick also returns None, and carpet_low_pile+vacuum_mop_deep mis-attributes to vacuum_deep. RoomConfig.as_dict (asdict, models.py:237) confirms real rooms always carry water_level, so only the candidate side takes the floor-default branch — the asymmetry is exactly as described. Overlaps A3-PP-CRUD-2 and A6-PP-EST-DSP-1 (same root, three framings).

Reproduced by executing the real apply_room_profile_to_config -> _protected_room_config -> _match_profile_from_fields pipeline over all 4 built-ins x 8 floor types. vacuum_mop_quick and vacuum_mop_deep fail to match on hardwood/laminate/marble/granite/concrete (match only on tile, where FLOOR_TYPE_WATER_DEFAULTS 'Medium' coincidentally equals the profiles' declared water) -> profile_name='custom'. vacuum_quick on carpet_low_pile also -> 'custom' (fan 'Standard' vs carpet default 'Max'), and vacuum_mop_deep on carpet_low_pile MIS-attributes to 'vacuum_deep'. Root cause confirmed in source: room_profiles.py:435 `elif "water_level" not in room_config` fires only for the bare candidate dict, never for a real room (RoomConfig.as_dict always materialises the key). HIGH stands: user-visible, no error, and the chip they just clicked deselects. Same defect as A3-PP-CRUD-2.

title: path_type resolves to the literal string "None" for any room backfilled by the startup migration, and that string reaches the Eufy wire payload
area: AREA 1 — THE RESOLUTION CORE (profiles/room_profiles.py: resolve_room_profile_for_room, resolve_profile_name_for_constraints, get_room_profile, normalize_clean_intensity)
observed_behavior: `resolved_path_type = str(room_config.get("path_type", resolved_profile.get("path_type", "wide")))`. The precedence is key-presence, but path_type is the one setting field whose RoomConfig default is None rather than a string (models/models.py:213, `path_type: Optional[str] = None`), and core/manager.py:424 stamps `_room.setdefault("path_type", None)` into every stored room at manager construction as an "add fields added after initial release" backfill. Present-with-None means the profile fallback is skipped and `str(None)` yields the four-character string 'None'. Executed: resolve_room_profile_for_room(room_config={...,'path_type':None})['path_type'] == 'None'. Nothing downstream sanitizes it: apply_capability_gate line 497 `path_type = str(settings.get("path_type", "wide"))` (key present, default unused), queue/queue_engine.py:285 `path_type = str(gated["path_type"])`, then line 309-310 `if supports_path: _write_room_field(..., "path_type", path_type)` with Eufy's identity rename map (adapters/eufy/adapter.py:581, `{"field_name": "path_type", "value_map": None}` — _write_room_field:180-185 passes the value through untouched). supports_path_control is True for the x10/x8 families (adapters/eufy/adapter.py:226). The value is also self-perpetuating: build_managed_rooms._default (rooms/room_manager.py:87-89) and rebuild_map_bucket._prev_or_brand (maps/map_manager.py:173-175) both return the existing value when `key in existing`, and None IS present, so the brand default 'wide' never gets a chance to replace it on any re-save.
user_impact: An Eufy X10/X8 room-clean payload carries path_type:"None" instead of "wide"/"narrow" — an out-of-vocabulary enum the device did not ask for, on every run of any room that predates the path_type field. planning/run_plan.py:370 (`str(room.get("path_type","")).strip() or None`) also reads the raw room dict and produces the string 'None', so the run plan displays a path type of "None".
guards_checked: apply_capability_gate line 524 `if not supports_path: path_type = "wide"` — only rescues brands WITHOUT path control (Roborock), which never puts path_type on the wire anyway; the Eufy X10/X8 that does support it is exactly the case left unguarded. _write_room_field (queue_engine.py:155-185) — no validation, no options check (unlike the per_room_live_settings options_key filter in jobs/active_job.py:1385-1393, which would have caught it). resolve_new_room_defaults (rooms/room_defaults.py:81-83) — supplies path_type for both brands' default profiles, so only pre-existing/backfilled rooms are affected. apply_room_profile_to_config line 569 — writes a real string, so a room repaired by applying a profile stops being affected.

confirmations: CONFIRMED. core/manager.py:424 does `_room.setdefault('path_type', None)` in the post-release backfill loop; models.py:213 declares `path_type: Optional[str] = None` and as_dict is asdict, so the key is always PRESENT. Executed: resolve_room_profile_for_room(room_config={...,'path_type':None})['path_type'] == 'None' (the 4-char string). apply_capability_gate line 497 uses `settings.get('path_type','wide')` — key present, default unused — and the only gate call site (queue_engine.py:271) always supplies the resolver output. adapters/eufy/adapter.py:581 declares path_type as an identity rename with value_map None, and supports_path_control is True for x10/x8 (adapter.py:226 capability_hints), so the string reaches the wire. _finalize_room_update (manager.py:194) re-stamps it, and build_managed_rooms/_prev_or_brand return the existing None on every re-save, so it self-perpetuates. Legacy/backfilled Eufy rooms only.

Executed: resolve_room_profile_for_room({'path_type': None}) returns the four-character string 'None'. Confirmed core/manager.py:424 `_room.setdefault("path_type", None)` backfill, models/models.py path_type: Optional[str] = None, apply_capability_gate:497 key-present so the 'wide' default is unused, queue_engine.py:309 writes it under Eufy's identity rename map, supports_path_control True for x10/x8. Worse than reported: _finalize_room_update:194 writes `result["path_type"] = _resolved.get("path_type")`, so the string 'None' is PERSISTED on the next room save rather than repaired. Downgraded to MEDIUM because reachability is narrower than stated: rooms/room_defaults.py supplies path_type from both shipped brands' default profiles, so only rooms predating the field (legacy installs) are affected — a fresh install cannot hit it.

title: "granite" and "concrete" are user-selectable floor types with no entry in either brand's FLOOR_TYPE_WATER_DEFAULTS, so the mop-with-no-water correction corrects to empty string
area: AREA 1 — THE RESOLUTION CORE (profiles/room_profiles.py: resolve_room_profile_for_room, resolve_profile_name_for_constraints, get_room_profile, normalize_clean_intensity)
observed_behavior: _normalize_floor_type (line 257-261) admits "granite" and "concrete" into the allow-list, and entity_helpers.py:120-121 gives them user-facing labels ("Granite / Natural Stone", "Concrete"), so they are pickable. Neither FLOOR_TYPE_WATER_DEFAULTS (room_profiles.py:140-147) nor the Roborock override (adapters/roborock/vocabulary.py:167-174) declares them. The correction at 443-448 exists precisely to rescue "mop mode with no water" — on granite/concrete it re-assigns the same empty value it just tested for, so the guard is a no-op on exactly the floors it is needed for. confirmations: CONFIRMED by execution: resolve_room_profile_for_room({'profile_name':'vacuum_mop_quick','floor_type':'granite'})['water_level'] == ''. _normalize_floor_type (line 257) admits granite/concrete; neither FLOOR_TYPE_WATER_DEFAULTS (line 140) nor the Roborock override (vocabulary.py:167) declares them, so `water_defaults.get(floor_type,'')` at both line 436 and the repair at line 448 returns ''. title: get_available_profile_names hardcodes the four Eufy built-in keys, so get_available_profiles silently drops every user-saved custom profile and would return {} for a brand with different catalog keys
area: AREA 1 — THE RESOLUTION CORE (profiles/room_profiles.py: resolve_room_profile_for_room, resolve_profile_name_for_constraints, get_room_profile, normalize_clean_intensity)
observed_behavior: get_available_profile_names takes only `capabilities` — no `catalog`, no `stored_profiles` — and returns one of two literal lists of the framework's own built-in keys (lines 306-317). get_available_profiles then merges builtins + stored profiles (lines 327-331) and immediately filters with `if name in allowed_names` (line 338). A user-saved profile is keyed `user_<timestamp>` (_generate_room_profile_id, profiles/manager.py:73) or `user_1` (manager.py:305), none of which is in the literal list, so every custom profile the merge just added is discarded. The `stored_profiles=` argument is accepted and then made inert. Structurally the same hole applies to a brand: the catalog reaches merge_profile_dicts but never the allow-list, so a future adapter declaring `builtins` under its own key names resolves to an empty dict.
user_impact: sensor/profile.py:63-70 passes the user's stored profiles in and publishes `profile_count` / `profiles` / `profile_labels` from the result, so the "available room profiles" sensor always reports 2 or 4 and never lists a profile the user created — an automation reading that attribute cannot see custom profiles at all. No error is raised; the count simply looks plausible.
guards_checked: merge_profile_dicts (line 217-233) — correctly merges stored over built-ins; the loss happens after it. sensor/profile.py:40-70 — no compensating merge, it renders the filtered dict verbatim. profiles/manager.py get_room_profiles (line 220-232) — the websocket/card path uses merge_profile_dicts directly and is NOT filtered, which is why the card still shows custom profiles and the defect is confined to the sensor. capabilities gating itself (supports_mop_features / supports_water_control) is correct for the built-ins.

confirmations: CONFIRMED from source. get_available_profile_names (line 294-317) takes only `capabilities` and returns one of two hardcoded lists of the four in-code keys; get_available_profiles merges stored profiles at line 327 then filters them all out at line 338 with `if name in allowed_names`. A stored key is `user_<timestamp>` (manager.py:73) or `user_1` (manager.py:305), never one of the four — so the stored_profiles argument is inert on every call. Verified the single production consumer: sensor/profile.py:63-70 passes its stored profiles in and renders the filtered dict verbatim as profile_count/profiles/profile_labels. The card is unaffected because it uses the UNfiltered ProfileManager.get_room_profiles (manager.py:220), which is why this stayed invisible. Executed: get_available_profiles(capabilities=mop+water, stored_profiles={'user_20260101T000000': {...}}) returns exactly the 4 built-in keys — the stored profile is merged in at line 327 and filtered out at 338. Confirmed the only production consumer, sensor/profile.py:63-70, reads its own custom-profile store, passes it in, and publishes profile_count/profiles/profile_labels from the filtered result, so the sensor can only ever report 2 or 4. get_room_profiles (manager.py:220) is unfiltered, which is why the card is unaffected. title: normalize_room_profile injects the Eufy literal "Quick" whenever the brand's normalize_defaults omits clean_intensity, and apply_room_profile_to_config PERSISTS it into Roborock room storage
area: AREA 1 — THE RESOLUTION CORE (profiles/room_profiles.py: resolve_room_profile_for_room, resolve_profile_name_for_constraints, get_room_profile, normalize_clean_intensity)
observed_behavior: Extends DQ-Q-4 past the read path. `"clean_intensity": normalize_clean_intensity(source.get("clean_intensity", d.get("clean_intensity", "Quick")))` — `d` is the catalog's normalize_defaults, which for Roborock is CUSTOM_ROOM_PROFILE (adapters/roborock/adapter.py:683), and adapters/roborock/vocabulary.py:153-162 deliberately omits clean_intensity ("OMITTED from every profile on purpose — Roborock exposes no intensity axis"). The `d.get(..., "Quick")` third-level literal defeats the omission. Verified: get_room_profile(profile_name='vacuum_quick', catalog=<roborock>) returns clean_intensity 'Quick'. Because every built-in is run through normalize_room_profile (get_room_profile line 291, merge_profile_dicts line 231), the injected value is not confined to display: apply_room_profile_to_config line 566 does `updated["clean_intensity"] = normalized["clean_intensity"]`, and ProfileManager.apply_room_profile (profiles/manager.py:671-678) writes that dict back to the room store. title: normalize_room_profile's third-level literals are the one fallback a brand CANNOT override — the more deliberately a brand omits an axis, the more certainly it gets the Eufy literal for it
area: AREA 2 — the capability gate (profiles/room_profiles.py: apply_capability_gate, apply_room_profile_to_config, merge_profile_dicts, normalize_room_profile, plus resolve_profile_catalog / get_available_profile_names and the queue_engine + active_job + dispatch/manager consumers that make each defect land or not)
observed_behavior: Full enumeration of literals `normalize_room_profile` can inject (lines 204-214), each as the THIRD arm of `source.get(k, d.get(k, LITERAL))` where `d` is the brand's `normalize_defaults`: label→"User Profile 1"; clean_mode→"vacuum"; fan_speed→"Max" (Eufy); water_level→"Off" (Eufy); clean_intensity→"Quick" (Eufy); path_type→"wide"; clean_passes→1; edge_mopping→False; mop_required→False. Of these, "wide"/1/False are framework-canonical (both shipped catalogs use them) and "vacuum" is the canonical mode; "Max", "Off" and "Quick" are Eufy DISPLAY vocabulary. Tracing each against the shipped Roborock catalog: `CUSTOM_ROOM_PROFILE` (adapters/roborock/vocabulary.py:153-162) declares 8 of the 9 keys, so "Max" and "Off" are shadowed — but it deliberately omits `clean_intensity` (documented at vocabulary.py:107-109: "An omitted key means the room stores nothing for it, rather than an inert 'Quick' nobody can act on"). Because the brand's own `normalize_defaults` is silent on the key, the literal `"Quick"` is what `d.get("clean_intensity", "Quick")` returns. The catalog is the mechanism a brand has for saying "I do not have this axis", and the only way it can say it is by omission — which is precisely the input that routes to the hardcoded Eufy literal. title: get_available_profile_names hardcodes the four Eufy catalog KEYS and takes no catalog — get_available_profiles merges every user-created profile in and then filters all of them back out
area: AREA 2 — the capability gate (profiles/room_profiles.py: apply_capability_gate, apply_room_profile_to_config, merge_profile_dicts, normalize_room_profile, plus resolve_profile_catalog / get_available_profile_names and the queue_engine + active_job + dispatch/manager consumers that make each defect land or not)
observed_behavior: `get_available_profile_names` (lines 294-317) takes only `capabilities` — no `catalog` — and returns a hardcoded list of the four in-code Eufy built-in keys. `get_available_profiles` (lines 320-339) then does `allowed_names = set(get_available_profile_names(capabilities=capabilities))` and returns `{name: ... for name, profile in all_profiles.items() if name in allowed_names}`, where `all_profiles` came from `merge_profile_dicts(..., stored_profiles=stored_profiles, ...)`. Any stored profile key ("user_1", "user_2", any "Save as New" name) is by construction not one of the four literals, so it is merged in on line 327 and discarded on line 338 — the `stored_profiles` argument is dead weight on every call. Separately, `catalog` IS accepted by `get_available_profiles` and threaded into the merge, but the filter it is then subjected to is catalog-blind: a brand whose `room_profiles.builtins` uses any other key set gets an EMPTY dict back, and a brand adding a fifth built-in has it silently hidden. Both shipped brands happen to use identical keys (adapters/roborock/vocabulary.py:110-151 mirrors BUILT_IN_ROOM_PROFILES exactly, by explicit design comment), which is why nothing has broken yet — the seam is held together by two hand-matched key lists, the exact pattern [[feedback_centralize_question_not_vocabulary]] names.
user_impact: The 'Available cleaning profiles' diagnostic sensor (sensor/profile.py:63-70) reads its own custom-profile store, passes it in, and reports a count that can only ever be 2 or 4 — a user with five saved custom room profiles sees '4' and finds none of them in `extra_state_attributes["profiles"]` / `profile_labels`. For brand 3, the same call returns `{}` and the sensor reports '0 profiles available' for a fully-configured vacuum.
guards_checked: sensor/profile.py:63-70 (the only production consumer — passes stored_profiles and consumes the filtered result directly, no re-merge); merge_profile_dicts (line 327 — the merge that is immediately undone); get_room_profiles (manager.py:220-232 — the UNfiltered sibling the card actually uses, which is why the card's profile picker still shows custom profiles and this stayed invisible); resolve_profile_catalog (line 156-173 — supplies `builtins` but nothing consults it for the allowed-name set).

confirmations: CONFIRMED from source and consumer. get_available_profile_names (lines 294-317) takes no catalog and returns hardcoded framework keys; get_available_profiles merges stored profiles (line 327) and immediately filters them out (line 338). title: apply_capability_gate hardcodes the Eufy literal "Off" in three places for the framework's own 'no water' concept
area: AREA 2 — the capability gate (profiles/room_profiles.py: apply_capability_gate, apply_room_profile_to_config, merge_profile_dicts, normalize_room_profile, plus resolve_profile_catalog / get_available_profile_names and the queue_engine + active_job + dispatch/manager consumers that make each defect land or not)
observed_behavior: `water_level = "Off"` appears at line 509 (mop unsupported → downgrade), line 516 (clean_mode == "vacuum") and line 520 (not supports_water). All three write Eufy display casing. user_impact: Contained today. `dispatch/manager.py:409` ranks with `str(room.get(field) or "").strip().lower()`, so the mop-intensity pre-call on a settable-mop Roborock still resolves "Off"→"off" correctly; and queue_engine.py:303 skips the water field entirely for vacuum-mode rooms, so it never reaches the wire. title: resolve_profile_catalog uses `or` for every key, so a brand that explicitly declares an EMPTY block silently gets Eufy's
area: AREA 2 — the capability gate (profiles/room_profiles.py: apply_capability_gate, apply_room_profile_to_config, merge_profile_dicts, normalize_room_profile, plus resolve_profile_catalog / get_available_profile_names and the queue_engine + active_job + dispatch/manager consumers that make each defect land or not)
observed_behavior: All seven keys use the falsy-or idiom: `"builtins": block.get("builtins") or BUILT_IN_ROOM_PROFILES` (166), and identically for custom_template, legacy_aliases, default_profile, floor_type_water_defaults, floor_type_fan_defaults, normalize_defaults (167-172). `{}` and `""` are falsy, so `{"builtins": {}}` — a brand stating it has no built-in profiles — is indistinguishable from not declaring the key, and resolves to Eufy's four. adapters/config_schema.py validates only that each of these is a dict when set (documented at docs/dev/21-adapter-system.md:66), so `{}` passes validation and is then silently replaced. Same for `"default_profile": ""`. This is the mirror image of the `_hint_wins` problem core/capabilities.py:302-310 was written to solve — 'a hardcoded default here is unreachable by any adapter' — one layer over.
user_impact: No shipped brand declares an empty sub-block, so nothing is broken today. A brand-3 author who writes `"floor_type_water_defaults": {}` meaning 'this device has no water, do not apply surface defaults' gets Eufy's Low/Medium/Off table applied to its rooms with no warning, and the only diagnosis is reading resolve_profile_catalog.
guards_checked: adapters/config_schema.py room_profiles rules (dict-when-set only — verified it does not reject or warn on empty); resolve_profile_catalog lines 164-173 (all seven keys, all `or`); tests/unit/test_profile_catalog.py [PC-1..PC-5] (verified every case passes either None or a non-empty override — the empty-dict case is untested); rooms/room_defaults.py:73 (`resolve_profile_catalog(catalog if isinstance(catalog, dict) else None)` — an isinstance check, not an emptiness one).

confirmations: CONFIRMED by execution — resolve_profile_catalog({'builtins':{}, 'floor_type_water_defaults':{}}) returns the in-code Eufy constants by identity. All seven keys use the falsy-`or` idiom (lines 166-172); adapters/config_schema.py validates dict-when-set and neither rejects nor warns on {}. No shipped brand declares an empty sub-block, so this is future-brand-only. Same defect as A1-PP-RES-8, which additionally surfaces the bare-deref KeyError at line 289 and is therefore the more complete write-up of the two.

Confirmed identical to A1-PP-RES-8 — same seven `or` fallbacks at room_profiles.py:166-172, same schema gap in adapters/config_schema.py. Raised to MEDIUM only for consistency with RES-8 and methodology rule 4 (a structural seam a third brand categorically cannot express is worth MEDIUM on its own). title: apply_room_profile writes Eufy vocabulary onto Roborock rooms — the catalog it resolves is inert
observed_behavior: `apply_room_profile` picks the profile DICT from `self.get_room_profiles()["profiles"]` (manager.py:631). `get_room_profiles` (manager.py:220-232) calls `get_default_room_profiles()` and `merge_profile_dicts(...)` with NO catalog and takes no `vacuum_entity_id` — so `merged` is always the in-code EUFY `BUILT_IN_ROOM_PROFILES`. Sixteen lines later the method DOES resolve the right catalog (`catalog = resolve_profile_catalog((get_adapter_config(vacuum_entity_id) or {}).get("room_profiles"))`, manager.py:658-662) and threads it into `apply_room_profile_to_config(..., catalog=catalog)`. That thread is INERT: `apply_room_profile_to_config` only uses the catalog via `normalize_room_profile(profile, catalog=catalog)`, whose every line is `str(source.get(k, d.get(k, ...)))` (room_profiles.py:204-214) — `d` (the brand's `normalize_defaults`) is consulted ONLY for keys MISSING from `source`, and the Eufy built-in declares all 9. Verified by executing the real functions with the real Roborock catalog: applying `vacuum_deep` to a Roborock room yields `fan_speed='Max'`, `water_level='Off'`, `clean_intensity='Deep'`, where the brand's own `ROOM_PROFILES['vacuum_deep']` (adapters/roborock/vocabulary.py:121-130) declares `fan_speed='max'`, `water_level='off'`, and NO clean_intensity key at all. The stored room field then WINS at dispatch (`resolve_room_profile_for_room` does `room_config.get("fan_speed", ...)`), so queue_engine passing the correct catalog cannot rescue it.
user_impact: On Roborock, selecting any room profile from the card silently poisons the room. `jobs/active_job.py:1385-1393` filters `per_room_live_settings` values against `fan_speed_options` = {gentle,quiet,balanced,turbo,max} with a strict `str(wire_value) not in valid` — 'Max' and 'Standard' both fail, so the `vacuum.set_fan_speed` call for that room is DROPPED entirely and the robot cleans it at whatever suction was last on the device. The room editor's chip rows compare with strict `===` (src/renderers/room-editor.js:250, :275), so suction and water render with nothing selected right after the user picked a profile. A meaningless `clean_intensity` is stamped onto a brand that deliberately has no intensity axis.
guards_checked: (1) The catalog resolution at manager.py:658-662 — resolves correctly but reaches only `normalize_room_profile`'s missing-key path, which never fires for a fully-populated Eufy built-in. (2) `normalize_room_profile` room_profiles.py:204-214 — read line by line; `source.get(k, d.get(k))` means the brand default is a FALLBACK, not an override. (3) `merge_profile_dicts` room_profiles.py:217-233 — accepts a catalog but `get_room_profiles` passes none. (4) `queue/queue_engine.py:265-275` — DOES pass `catalog=_catalog` to both `resolve_room_profile_for_room` and `apply_capability_gate`, but the room's own stored field takes precedence over the profile, so the poisoned stored value survives. (5) `dispatch/manager.py:325-410` `_run_global_pre_calls` — its `rank` comparison lowercases (`str(room.get(field) or "").strip().lower()`), which DOES rescue Eufy-cased water_level; fan_speed on the S6 has no global_pre_call, it rides the strict per-room-live filter, so it is not rescued. (6) `_finalize_room_update` manager.py:181-197 — takes no catalog either, so it cannot correct the values.

confirmations: CONFIRMED. Same mechanism as A2-PP-CAP-1, verified independently: get_room_profiles (manager.py:220-232) takes neither catalog nor vacuum_entity_id, so apply_room_profile's `profile` is always a fully-populated Eufy built-in; the catalog resolved sixteen lines later (manager.py:658-662) reaches only normalize_room_profile's missing-key path (lines 204-214) and is therefore a no-op. I executed the resolver with the shipped Roborock catalog and confirmed the brand's own vacuum_deep declares fan_speed 'max' / water_level 'off' and no clean_intensity, while the Eufy built-in writes 'Max' / 'Off' / 'Deep'. Downstream is not rescued: the stored room field wins in resolve_room_profile_for_room, and jobs/active_job.py:1385-1393 with roborock/adapter.py:374 options_key='fan_speed_options' silently DROPS the set_fan_speed call for an out-of-vocabulary value. Duplicate of A2-PP-CAP-1 — dedupe before assigning work.

Same defect as A2-PP-CAP-1, independently confirmed. get_room_profiles has no catalog parameter at all (manager.py:220-232), so the profile dict handed to apply_room_profile_to_config is always the Eufy built-in; the catalog resolved 16 lines later (manager.py:658-662) reaches only normalize_room_profile's missing-key path, which cannot fire for a 9-key source. Verified the downstream drop at jobs/active_job.py:1385-1393 (strict `not in valid` against Roborock's fan_speed_options) and that the poisoned STORED field wins at dispatch even though queue_engine does pass the correct catalog (room_config.get beats profile.get at room_profiles.py:422). HIGH stands.

title: Applying a mop room profile instantly rewrites the room's profile_name to "custom" — the profile the user just picked does not stay selected
observed_behavior: `apply_room_profile` → `_finalize_room_update` (manager.py:671) → `_match_profile_from_fields` (manager.py:195). The match builds each candidate as `candidate_config = {"profile_name": name}` plus floor_type (manager.py:154-156) and resolves it via `resolve_room_profile_for_room` (manager.py:157-162). That candidate dict has NO `water_level` key, so `resolve_room_profile_for_room`'s `elif "water_level" not in room_config: resolved_water_level = water_defaults.get(floor_type, "")` (room_profiles.py:435-436) REPLACES the profile's declared water_level with the floor-type default. The ROOM side, however, carries the profile's DECLARED water_level, because `apply_room_profile_to_config` wrote `updated["water_level"] = normalized["water_level"]` (room_profiles.py:565) and `_protected_room_config` leaves it alone for mop modes (`is_mop_mode` True → the `if not is_mop_mode` clamp at manager.py:107 is skipped). So the comparison at manager.py:168-169 is profile-declared 'Medium' vs floor-default 'Low' → no match → `result["profile_name"] = "custom"` (manager.py:196). Executed against the real `apply_room_profile_to_config` + `resolve_room_profile_for_room` with the shipped Eufy catalog: hardwood/laminate/marble/granite × {vacuum_mop_quick, vacuum_mop_deep} → all 8 land on "custom"; tile matches only because FLOOR_TYPE_WATER_DEFAULTS['tile'] == 'Medium' happens to equal the profiles' declared water. Carpet has the same defect on the FAN axis: applying `vacuum_quick` to carpet gives "custom" (candidate picks up FLOOR_TYPE_FAN_DEFAULTS carpet 'Max', room stores the profile's 'Standard'), and applying `vacuum_mop_deep` to carpet MIS-ATTRIBUTES to `vacuum_deep`.
user_impact: On Eufy — the primary shipped brand — a user taps the "Deep" or "Quick" mop profile chip on any hardwood, laminate, marble, granite or concrete room and the card immediately re-renders with the "Custom" chip highlighted instead (src/renderers/room-editor.js:144-148, :158). No error, no toast. The settings applied are correct; only the association is destroyed, so the room can never be recognised as being on a preset and the same tap fails every time. The same `_match_profile_from_fields` stamp runs in planning/run_plan.py:1310-1311, so the run-plan preview also reports "custom" for those rooms.
guards_checked: (1) `_protected_room_config` manager.py:84-111 — its `if not is_mop_mode: protected["water_level"] = "Off"` clamp is what rescues the VACUUM profiles (both sides get forced to 'Off'); it deliberately does not fire for mop modes, which is exactly why only mop profiles break. (2) The `room_floor_type` conditional at manager.py:155-156 — it was added to close the earlier asymmetry and does pass floor_type through, but passing floor_type is what ACTIVATES the floor water default on the candidate. (3) The mop-with-no-water guard at room_profiles.py:443-448 — does not fire ('low' is not in ('', 'off')). (4) `_normalize_profile_match_value` manager.py:113-135 — lowercases and folds 'off', so casing is not the cause; 'medium' vs 'low' is a genuine value difference. (5) Existing tests tests/integration/test_profiles_manager.py:343 (PM-10) and :370 (PM-10b) — PM-10 builds its room by calling `resolve_room_profile_for_room({"profile_name": "vacuum_mop_quick"})` with no floor_type, so the room it asserts on ALREADY carries the hardwood default 'Low'; it never exercises the profile's declared 'Medium' that `apply_room_profile` actually writes. Both tests pass while the shipped path is broken.

confirmations: CONFIRMED by executing the real apply_room_profile_to_config -> _protected_room_config -> _match_profile_from_fields pipeline over all four built-ins x eight floor types. hardwood/laminate/marble/granite/concrete x {vacuum_mop_quick, vacuum_mop_deep} all return None -> profile_name='custom'; tile matches only because FLOOR_TYPE_WATER_DEFAULTS['tile']=='Medium' coincides with the profiles' declared water. The carpet variants are also broken as claimed: carpet_low_pile+vacuum_quick -> None, carpet_low_pile+vacuum_mop_deep -> mis-attributed to vacuum_deep, carpet_high_pile+vacuum_deep -> None. The root is the candidate/room precedence asymmetry at room_profiles.py:435-436 (candidate has no water_level key so the floor default overrides the profile), and _protected_room_config's non-mop water clamp is exactly why vacuum profiles are rescued and mop profiles are not. _finalize_room_update:196 then stamps 'custom'. Same root as A1-PP-RES-2 and A6-PP-EST-DSP-1.

Same defect as A1-PP-RES-2, reproduced by executing the real pipeline: all 8 mop-profile/hard-floor combinations except tile land on 'custom'; carpet_low_pile + vacuum_quick -> 'custom'; carpet_low_pile + vacuum_mop_deep -> mis-attributed to 'vacuum_deep'. Confirmed the asymmetry source (candidate dict has no water_level key, so room_profiles.py:435 fires for it and never for the real room) and that _protected_room_config's non-mop clamp is exactly why only mop profiles break. HIGH stands.

title: rename_room_profile changes the store key and silently orphans every room referencing it — no migration, no reference check, no warning
observed_behavior: `rename_room_profile` ends with `if target_name != normalized_name: del stored_profiles[normalized_name]` then `stored_profiles[target_name] = updated_profile` (manager.py:587-589). Nothing walks `data["maps"][*][*]["rooms"]` to rewrite the rooms whose `profile_name` is the OLD key, and the success payload carries no room count. `delete_room_profile` (manager.py:615-616) is identical — a bare `del` with no reference check. A room left pointing at a vanished key resolves silently: `get_room_profile` does `profile = merged.get(normalized_name)` → None → `normalized_name = catalog default_profile` → returns 'vacuum_quick' with NO error and NO flag (room_profiles.py:282-291). This is not a YAML-only path: the card's rename flow pre-computes a NEW key from the new label (`makeRoomProfileName`, src/state/room-profiles.js:98-123 → `custom_<slug>`) and pre-fills it as the prompt default (src/bindings/room-editor.js:244-248), then sends it as `new_profile_name` whenever it differs from the current key (src/bindings/room-editor.js:252-258). So editing a custom profile's LABEL renames its KEY by default. The card re-applies the profile to exactly one room — `if (currentProfileName === targetProfileName)` (src/bindings/room-editor.js:274-276), the room open in the editor. Every other room that used that profile is left dangling.
user_impact: A user renames a custom room profile from "Kitchen Deep" to "Kitchen Deep Clean" and every OTHER room using it loses its profile association. Those rooms' chip rows show nothing selected (strict `===` against the library keys, src/renderers/room-editor.js:158), `get_effective_room_details` reports `selected_profile_name='vacuum_quick'` / `resolved_profile_label='Vacuum Only Quick'` — a profile the user never chose — and the next field edit on any of them snaps `profile_name` to "custom" via `_finalize_room_update`, making the loss permanent. No error is shown at any point; the service returns `{"renamed": True}`.
guards_checked: (1) rename's own guards, manager.py:543-574 — protected-name refusal, `profile_name_exists` collision check, `missing_label`: all three interrogate the PROFILE STORE only; none of them looks at rooms. (2) `_get_editable_room_profile` manager.py:209-218 — validates the source profile exists and is not built-in; nothing about consumers. (3) `get_room_profile`'s `if profile is None` fallback chain, room_profiles.py:284-289 — read in full: it substitutes the default profile and returns normally, so the dangling reference produces no exception, no log line and no error field anywhere in the stack. (4) `_normalize_profile_name` / LEGACY_PROFILE_ALIASES room_profiles.py:236-244 — an alias map exists for the two Eufy legacy keys but nothing writes a rename into it. (5) The card's post-rename repair at src/bindings/room-editor.js:270-277 — only fires for the single room currently in the editor. (6) `delete_room_profile` manager.py:598-620 — same shape, same absence of a reference check.

confirmations: CONFIRMED on both halves. Backend: rename_room_profile ends at manager.py:587-589 with `del stored_profiles[normalized_name]` + reassignment, delete_room_profile at 615-616 with a bare `del`; I read all guards (543-574, 601-613) and every one interrogates the profile store only — nothing enumerates map rooms, and the return payload carries no referrer count. get_room_profile lines 284-289 then swallow the dangling reference with no exception, log or error field. title: Protected-profile-name set is frozen from the Eufy in-code catalog, so a brand's own built-ins are unprotected and can be shadowed by a user profile
observed_behavior: `_PROTECTED_ROOM_PROFILE_NAMES: frozenset[str] = frozenset(BUILT_IN_ROOM_PROFILES.keys())` (manager.py:47) is computed once at import from the EUFY in-code constants and is never derived from a catalog. Meanwhile `merge_profile_dicts` lets a STORED profile overwrite a built-in of the same key (`merged[profile_key] = normalize_room_profile(profile, ...)`, room_profiles.py:231), and that merge is the one queue_engine performs WITH the brand catalog. title: start_run_profile mutates and persists every room's selection and settings BEFORE the start is allowed, and never reverts when the start refuses
area: AREA 4 — Run-profile CRUD and step normalization (custom_components/eufy_vacuum/profiles/manager.py: normalize_run_profile_steps, run_profile_steps, get_saved_run_profiles, save_run_profile, set_run_profile_steps, overwrite_run_profile, rename_run_profile, delete_run_profile, apply_run_profile, start_run_profile)
observed_behavior:
start_run_profile calls apply_run_profile first (line 1283), unconditionally. apply_run_profile disables every room on the map (lines 1201-1204: `rooms[room_key] = {**room_data, "enabled": False}`), then rewrites the profile rooms' enabled/order/clean_mode/fan_speed/water_level/clean_intensity/clean_passes/edge_mopping through _finalize_room_update, and commits with `map_bucket["rooms"] = rooms` + _refresh_room_derived_state + _notify_rooms_updated.

Only AFTER all of that does it await start_selected_rooms, which has three early returns that never reach dispatch (core/manager.py:4943 `start_status["blocked"]`, 4953 `requires_confirmation` without a valid confirm_token, 4988 `vacuum_missing`). start_run_profile handles exactly one consequence of those returns — popping the leaked `_pending_run_steps` stash (lines 1340-1343) — and does nothing about the room mutation. The persistence is what makes it permanent: button.py:286-298 awaits start_run_profile, IGNORES the returned dict entirely, and then calls `await self._manager.async_save()`, writing the clobbered map to .storage regardless of whether the run started. start_run_profile itself is only ever passed `confirm_reduced_run=False` and `confirm_token=None` from that button (button.py:293-297), so a reduced run always takes the confirmation_required branch on the first press.

There is no undo. For the confirmation flow specifically, the user is being asked "are you sure?" about a run whose side effects have already been applied and persisted, so answering "no" is not a no-op.
