title: apply_run_profile leaves no backend record that the applied profile is stepped, so a plain Start runs it flat — or inherits the map's unrelated leftover breaks
area: AREA 4 — Run-profile CRUD and step normalization (custom_components/eufy_vacuum/profiles/manager.py: normalize_run_profile_steps, run_profile_steps, get_saved_run_profiles, save_run_profile, set_run_profile_steps, overwrite_run_profile, rename_run_profile, delete_run_profile, apply_run_profile, start_run_profile)
observed_behavior:
apply_run_profile writes only `map_bucket["rooms"]` and `map_bucket["summary"]` (lines 1244-1245). It never writes `map_bucket["queue_breaks"]` and never populates `data["_pending_run_steps"]` — start_run_profile's own comment at lines 1301-1306 states this outright ("apply_run_profile, which never writes queue_breaks"). Only start_run_profile stashes the steps (1314-1316).

So after a bare apply, planning/run_plan._build_effective_start_plan takes the fallback branch at lines 1339-1351: `_pending_run_steps` is empty, so it derives the plan from `get_queue_steps(...)`, whose breaks come from `self._map_queue_breaks(map_bucket)` (core/manager.py:1602) — the map's OWN stored breaks, which have nothing to do with the profile just applied. If the map has none, the applied profile's charge/wait/zone steps are silently dropped and the whole thing dispatches as one atomic clean. If the map has stale breaks left from an earlier ad-hoc composition, those are applied to the profile's rooms at their own `after_index` positions.

The only thing that keeps this correct today is browser-session memory: src/bindings/run-profiles.js:74 sets `setAppliedRunProfile(profileId)` and src/bindings/rooms.js:139-145 reroutes the primary Start button to startRunProfile when `pendingStepRunProfileId()` is truthy. That state lives in `this._runProfilesState` (src/state/run-profiles.js:123-138) — plain in-memory card state with no persistence. A page reload, a second dashboard/tab, a different user's browser, or an automation calling apply_run_profile followed by start_cleaning all bypass it.
user_impact: User presses "Apply" on a stepped profile, walks away, comes back to a reloaded dashboard (or starts it from a second tab / a phone), presses Start — and the run silently loses its structure: the charge-to-90% break never happens so the robot dies mid-run, a wait step is skipped, and a zone step is never cleaned at all. Same for any automation that does `apply_run_profile` then `start_cleaning`, which the service descriptions give no reason to think is wrong. Worse, if the map still carries queue_breaks from an earlier composition, the charge break lands after an arbitrary room of the profile's run.
guards_checked: Read apply_run_profile (1170-1263) — no write to queue_breaks and no _pending_run_steps stash. Read start_run_profile (1301-1316) — the stash is written only there, keyed on step_requires_stepped_execution. Read planning/run_plan._build_effective_start_plan (1330-1355) — the fallback to get_queue_steps and the (charge_wait/wait/zone) gate. Read core/manager._map_queue_breaks (1602-1614) — reads map_bucket["queue_breaks"], entirely independent of any applied profile. Read core/manager._clear_room_selections_after_start (771-772) — it drains queue_breaks only after a SUCCESSFUL start, so stale breaks can survive any refused/abandoned run. Read src/state/run-profiles.js pendingStepRunProfileId (221-227) and _ensureRunProfilesState (123-138) — confirmed the applied-profile id is ephemeral card state, never sent to the backend.

title: Run-profile ids are generated at one-second resolution and assigned without a collision check, so two saves in the same second silently overwrite each other
area: AREA 4 — Run-profile CRUD and step normalization (custom_components/eufy_vacuum/profiles/manager.py: normalize_run_profile_steps, run_profile_steps, get_saved_run_profiles, save_run_profile, set_run_profile_steps, overwrite_run_profile, rename_run_profile, delete_run_profile, apply_run_profile, start_run_profile)
observed_behavior:
_generate_run_profile_id returns `f"rp_{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%dT%H%M%S')}"` — no counter, no uuid, no randomness, and local naive time. save_run_profile then does a blind assignment:

    profile_id = self._generate_run_profile_id()
    ...
    library[profile_id] = { ... }

with no `while profile_id in library` check and no membership test anywhere in the function (lines 955-975). Because the whole method is synchronous with no await before the write, two save_run_profile calls that land in the same wall-clock second produce the identical key and the second dict replaces the first outright. The service handler (services/run_profiles.py:97-105) reports `saved: True` both times and returns the same profile_id, so the caller sees two successes and one profile.

The same generator shape is used for room profiles (_generate_room_profile_id, line 73).
user_impact: A script or automation that saves two run profiles back to back ("Quick" then "Deep" for the same map) ends up with one — the first is destroyed with no error, and the response even hands back the colliding id as if it were new. Under a DST fall-back the same second recurs an hour later, which can also collide a new save with an existing profile saved a year ago at that timestamp.
guards_checked: Read _generate_run_profile_id (75-77) and _get_saved_run_profile_store (707-718) — the store is a plain dict keyed by id with no uniqueness enforcement. Read save_run_profile (924-997) in full: the only guards are `missing_name` and `no_rooms_selected`; the assignment at 962 is unconditional. Checked that no await separates generation from assignment (methodology rule 1 — this is not an interleaving claim; a single caller issuing two sequential service calls in the same second is enough). Checked _handle_save_run_profile (services/run_profiles.py:97-105) — it awaits async_save() after each call but never inspects for collisions.

confirmations: CONFIRMED — same defect as A3-PP-CRUD-8, run-profile side. _generate_run_profile_id (manager.py:75-77) is `rp_` + naive local `%Y%m%dT%H%M%S` with no counter or uniqueness source; save_run_profile (924-997) has only missing_name and no_rooms_selected guards and assigns `library[profile_id] = {...}` unconditionally at 962, with no await between generation and write (so this is not an interleaving claim — two sequential service calls in the same second suffice). services/run_profiles.py:97-105 reports saved:True and hands back the colliding id both times. Dedupe with A3-PP-CRUD-8; one fix (a uniquify loop in both generators) closes both.

Confirmed _generate_run_profile_id (manager.py:77) is second-resolution naive local time and save_run_profile:962 assigns `library[profile_id] = {...}` with no membership test (read the whole method: only missing_name and no_rooms_selected guard). Downgraded to LOW to match A3-PP-CRUD-8, which is the same defect one generator over: it needs a script issuing two saves inside one wall-clock second, and the card derives its own keys, so no interactive user path reaches it.

title: normalize_run_profile_steps passes arbitrary per-room fields through untouched, and the run-plan overlay treats them as authoritative settings — the one dispatch path that skips _protected_room_config
area: AREA 4 — Run-profile CRUD and step normalization (custom_components/eufy_vacuum/profiles/manager.py: normalize_run_profile_steps, run_profile_steps, get_saved_run_profiles, save_run_profile, set_run_profile_steps, overwrite_run_profile, rename_run_profile, delete_run_profile, apply_run_profile, start_run_profile)
observed_behavior:
normalize_run_profile_steps coerces only the id and keeps everything else: `clean_rooms.append({**r, "room_id": room_id})` (line 779). Its docstring calls this "shape-only" discipline, which is accurate about its own intent — but the consumer does not treat those extra keys as inert. planning/run_plan._build_steps_phases (835-841) overlays every non-room_id key onto the effective room used to build the phase:

    for field, value in r.items():
        if field != "room_id":
            merged[field] = value

and merged goes straight to _build_dispatch_phases -> build_room_clean_payload. That path DOES run resolve_room_profile_for_room + apply_capability_gate (queue/queue_engine.py:265-276), but it does NOT run _protected_room_config — and resolve_room_profile_for_room lets an explicit per-room clean_mode win unconditionally (profiles/room_profiles.py:415), with the carpet arm at 432-434 only touching fan/water. So a step room carrying `clean_mode: "mop"` for a room whose floor_type is carpet reaches the payload as mop; queue_engine.py:302 then writes water_level because clean_mode is in {"mop","vacuum_mop"}.

The card is a real producer of these fields: src/state/steps-order.js roomsToGroupStep (135-148) captures clean_mode / fan_speed / water_level / clean_intensity / clean_passes / edge_mopping into each group room, and sanitizeStepsForSave (157-158) passes `[...step.rooms]` through verbatim. set_run_profile_steps then stores them (line 1018) with the service schema validating nothing beyond `steps: list` (services/run_profiles.py:85).

So the stored room says "vacuum", the card renders "vacuum", and the phase payload says "mop".
user_impact: A user captures a room group while a room is hardwood and set to mop, then later marks that room as carpet (rug moved in). Every other path in the system now refuses to mop it — the card shows Vacuum, and apply_run_profile rewrites the stored room to Vacuum — but the stepped run still dispatches clean_mode=mop for that room, dragging the mop plate across carpet. The UI never shows the value the robot was actually sent. The same overlay lets a hand-written set_run_profile_steps call inject any per-room setting straight into a dispatch payload without the protection pass.
guards_checked: Read normalize_run_profile_steps (750-809): the room_group arm validates only room_id; no field whitelist, no protection call. Read _build_dispatch_phases (749-790) and build_room_clean_payload (188-340): resolve_room_profile_for_room and apply_capability_gate run, _protected_room_config does not. confirmations: CONFIRMED, and this is the one place the carpet protection genuinely IS bypassed (unlike A1-PP-RES-1). normalize_run_profile_steps line 779 keeps arbitrary per-room keys; _build_steps_phases:834-841 overlays every non-room_id key onto the effective room AFTER run_plan.py:1309 already protected it, and the merged dict goes straight to _build_dispatch_phases -> build_room_clean_payload, which runs resolve_room_profile_for_room + apply_capability_gate but NOT _protected_room_config. Confirmed normalize_run_profile_steps:779 keeps arbitrary per-room keys (`{**r, "room_id": room_id}`), _build_steps_phases:838-841 overlays every non-room_id key onto the already-protected effective_rooms, and the resulting merged dict goes to build_room_clean_payload, which runs resolve_room_profile_for_room + apply_capability_gate but NOT _protected_room_config; resolve gives an explicit room clean_mode unconditional precedence (room_profiles.py:415) and the carpet arm touches only fan/water. title: Applying a profile whose rooms no longer exist silently deselects and persists every room on the map, and reports the failure as "profile_not_found"

title: A multi-room_group plan with no charge/wait/zone is silently flattened to ONE atomic dispatch — the card routes it as sequenced
observed_behavior:
Three independent gates all ask "does the plan contain a BREAK?", never "does the plan contain more than one room_group?":

(1) run_plan.py:1352 — `if _run_steps and any(isinstance(s, dict) and s.get("type") in ("charge_wait", "wait", "zone") for s in _run_steps):` … `else: phases = self._build_dispatch_phases(... queue_room_ids=queue_state.get("queue_room_ids", []) ...)`. A steps list of `[room_group, room_group]` fails the gate and takes the flat atomic branch, so `_build_steps_phases` is never called and the second group is never a phase.

(2) Even if it were stashed, run_plan.py:898-908 would re-flatten it: `if not any(p.get("phase_type") in _BREAKS or p.get("phase_type") == "zone" for p in collapsed): ... return self._build_dispatch_phases(managed_rooms=effective_rooms, queue_room_ids=all_ids or sorted(included_room_ids), ...)`. Two adjacent room_group dispatch phases carry NO `phase_type` key at all (the engines return `{vacuum_entity_id, map_id, payload, resolved_rooms, room_count}` — queue/dispatch_engines.py:211-217, 273-280), so the condition is True and both phases are replaced by a single dispatch built from `effective_rooms` — the per-group `group_managed` overlay (run_plan.py:834-841) is discarded.

(3) profiles/manager.py:1311 `if any(step_requires_stepped_execution(s) for s in _prof_steps)` — same break-only vocabulary, so `_pending_run_steps` is never stashed.

The card disagrees on purpose: profiles/manager.py:852 `"has_stops": (plan_requires_stepped_execution(steps) or len(_room_group_steps) > 1)` and src/state/run-profiles.js:221-226 `pendingStepRunProfileId` — "Gates on has_stops (NOT charge-only has_charge_steps) so a WAIT-only or multi-group profile still routes through the stepped path". src/state/steps-order.js:135-148 `roomsToGroupStep` writes real per-room `clean_mode/fan_speed/water_level/clean_intensity/clean_passes/edge_mopping` into each group, and src/state/run-profiles.js:351 `captureCurrentRoomsAsDraftGroup` appends a second group with one click.

user_impact: The canonical two-pass profile — "vacuum every room, then mop the kitchen and bath" — is saved, displayed as a multi-step sequenced run in the card's stepped preview, and then executed as ONE flat clean: rooms that appear in both groups are cleaned once with the SECOND group's settings (the vacuum pass is silently deleted), rooms only in the first group keep first-group settings. No warning, no log line, and the card keeps showing the two-phase plan it thought it dispatched.

title: Any plan whose FIRST surviving phase is a zone is refused with "Room-clean payload is missing or invalid" — and a live blocker rule can push a plan into that state
observed_behavior:
run_plan.py:873-879 builds a zone phase with `"payload": {}, "room_count": 0`. The leading trim at 884-885 is `_BREAKS = ("charge_wait", "wait")` only, so a zone at the head survives (intentionally — step_types.py:23-25). Then line 1379 `payload_state = phases[0]` makes that empty zone envelope the plan's payload_state, and get_start_status (core/manager.py:2857-2864) feeds `payload_room_count=int(payload_state.get("room_count", 0))` into build_start_blocker_from_lifecycle, whose jobs/job_monitor.py:268-273 arm is `if int(payload_room_count or 0) <= 0: return {"reason": "invalid_payload", "message": "Room-clean payload is missing or invalid.", "blocked": True}`.

Beyond the known static zone-first case, this is REACHABLE DYNAMICALLY with ordinary authoring. Steps `[room_group(A), zone(Z), room_group(B)]`: when a blocker rule matches every room of the FIRST group, run_plan.py:827-829 `group_ids = [...]; if not group_ids: continue` drops that group, leaving `phases = [zone, dispatch(B)]`. `queue_room_ids` is still `[B]` (non-empty, so the `no_rooms_selected` arm at job_monitor.py:261 passes) and preflight reports `included_room_ids=[B]`, `reason="rooms_blocked"` — but payload_room_count is 0 and the start is blocked as an invalid payload.
user_impact: A saved run that worked yesterday becomes unstartable the moment a door/occupancy sensor blocks the rooms in its first group — with an error that blames a corrupt payload rather than naming the blocked room. The rest of the plan (room group B and the zone) is perfectly runnable and preflight says so. There is no way for the user to recover except editing the profile.
guards_checked: the leading/trailing trim (run_plan.py:884-887 — `_BREAKS` deliberately excludes "zone", documented at step_types.py:23-25, so it cannot rescue this); the collapse fallback (run_plan.py:898-901 — explicitly keeps a zone-containing list multi-phase, so phases[0] stays the zone); phase_runner._dispatch_active_phase (jobs/phase_runner.py:996-1008 — DOES handle a zone phase via dispatch_zone_clean, but it is only reached for phases attached to an active job, and start_selected_rooms never gets that far); the `len(_phases) > 1` guard at core/manager.py:5034 (irrelevant — start is blocked before dispatch); normalize_run_profile_steps (profiles/manager.py:798-808 — no positional constraint on a zone step); add_queue_zone's `after = max(1, min(_safe_int(after_index, 1), room_count))` (core/manager.py:1749 — prevents a leading zone in the AD-HOC queue only, not in a saved profile, and does not help once the leading group is dropped at plan time).

confirmations: CONFIRMED including the dynamic reachability, which is what lifts it past known-soft-spot DQ-Q-3. A zone phase is built with room_count 0 (run_plan.py:873-879); the leading trim at 884-885 uses _BREAKS = ('charge_wait','wait') only, deliberately excluding zone per step_types.py:23-25, so a head zone survives; line 1379 makes it payload_state; core/manager.py get_start_status passes `payload_room_count=int(payload_state.get('room_count',0))` into build_start_blocker_from_lifecycle, and I read jobs/job_monitor.py:250-273 — `queue_count <= 0` is checked FIRST (passes, since queue_room_ids is still [B]) and then `payload_room_count <= 0` returns invalid_payload / 'Room-clean payload is missing or invalid.' with blocked True. The dynamic path is real: run_plan.py:828-829 drops a fully-blocked leading group, leaving phases=[zone, dispatch(B)] while preflight still reports included_room_ids=[B] and reason='rooms_blocked'. Error names the wrong cause and the user cannot recover without editing the profile.

Mechanism confirmed end to end: the leading trim's _BREAKS tuple (run_plan.py:883) deliberately excludes 'zone' (step_types.py:23-25 documents why), so a zone at the head survives to become phases[0]; that phase carries room_count 0 (run_plan.py:873-879); get_start_status passes it as payload_room_count and jobs/job_monitor.py:268-273 returns 'invalid_payload' / 'Room-clean payload is missing or invalid.' with queue_room_ids still non-empty so the no_rooms_selected arm at :261 passes. The dynamic path is also confirmed: `if not group_ids: continue` at run_plan.py:828-829 drops a fully-blocked first group. Downgraded to MEDIUM: it needs a zone step in the plan AND a blocker rule taking out every room of the preceding group — the always-reachable static case is the already-known DQ-Q-3 lead.

title: _build_steps_phases can return an empty list; `phases[0]` then raises IndexError inside get_start_status, killing the whole dashboard snapshot (Roborock)
observed_behavior:
run_plan.py:1363-1370 hardcodes `strict_order=True` for every stepped plan. On a brand with `capabilities.honors_clean_order = False` (adapters/roborock/adapter.py:601) `_build_dispatch_phases` computes `effective_strict = bool(strict_order) and not honors_order` = True (run_plan.py:776) and routes to GenericRoomIdsEngine._build_per_room_phases, which returns `phases = []` when `resolved` is empty (queue/dispatch_engines.py:266-281 — the loop simply never appends).

When every room_group step is skipped (`if not group_ids: continue`, run_plan.py:828-829) the only phases left are breaks, the leading trim at 884-885 pops them all, `collapsed == []`, and `not any(...)` over an empty list is True, so the fallback at 902-908 runs with `all_ids or sorted(included_room_ids)` == `[]` → the Roborock engine returns `[]` → line 1379 `payload_state = phases[0]` raises IndexError.

Reachable state: a stepped queue (a persisted `queue_breaks` entry) plus zero includable rooms — e.g. every enabled room matched by a blocker rule (all set `enabled: False` in effective_rooms at line 1298), or all rooms disabled while breaks persist (`_map_queue_breaks` keeps any entry with `after >= 1` regardless of the current room count, core/manager.py:1602-1614, and `get_queue_steps` drains the orphaned break as a trailing step at 1661-1663). `_build_effective_start_plan` is called at the TOP of get_start_status (core/manager.py:2765), before the `all_selected_rooms_blocked` guard at 2834 that was written for exactly this state — so the guard is unreachable and the exception propagates out of get_start_status, get_job_control_state (core/manager.py:3841) and get_dashboard_snapshot (3913).
user_impact: For a Roborock user, turning on a blocker (e.g. the sensor behind a "don't clean while the baby naps" rule) while a charge/wait break sits in the queue makes the integration's dashboard snapshot service raise instead of returning "All selected rooms are blocked" — the card cannot render start status or job controls at all until the rule clears. Eufy is immune: the atomic engine always returns exactly one phase, so the same state reports the intended blocked message.
guards_checked: get_start_status's `all_selected_rooms_blocked` arm (core/manager.py:2834-2855 — correct, but sequenced AFTER the plan build that throws); build_start_blocker_from_lifecycle `no_rooms_selected` / `invalid_payload` arms (jobs/job_monitor.py:261-273 — same, never reached); _SinglePhaseMixin.build_phases (queue/dispatch_engines.py:110-114 — always returns one phase, which is why Eufy is safe); `if not group_ids: continue` (run_plan.py:828 — this is the code that empties the list); the fallback's `all_ids or sorted(included_room_ids)` (run_plan.py:906 — evaluates to [] here, and queue_engine.py:242 `not selected_ids` then means "no filter", but every room in effective_rooms is enabled=False so nothing resolves); set_queue_breaks' `room_count < 2 -> clear` (core/manager.py:1809-1810 — only fires when the card explicitly rewrites the break list, not when rooms are disabled or blocked).

confirmations: CONFIRMED, traced line by line. With every room_group skipped (run_plan.py:828-829), only break phases remain; the leading/trailing trims at 884-887 empty the list; `not any(...)` over an empty collapsed is True, so the fallback at 902-908 runs with `all_ids or sorted(included_room_ids)` == [] and strict_order=True (hardcoded at 1369). _build_dispatch_phases folds effective_strict = True for Roborock (honors_clean_order False, adapter.py:601) and routes to GenericRoomIdsEngine._build_per_room_phases (dispatch_engines.py:239-281), whose loop over an empty `resolved` returns [] — then run_plan.py:1379 `phases[0]` raises IndexError. Eufy is immune because _SinglePhaseMixin.build_phases always returns exactly one phase. Critically, I confirmed the ordering: core/manager.get_start_status calls _build_effective_start_plan at line 2765, BEFORE the all_selected_rooms_blocked guard at 2834 — so that guard is unreachable and the exception escapes get_start_status / get_job_control_state / get_dashboard_snapshot.

Every link verified in source. GenericRoomIdsEngine._build_per_room_phases (dispatch_engines.py:266-281) returns [] when resolved is empty — the loop simply never appends — while _SinglePhaseMixin.build_phases (110-114) always returns one phase, which is exactly why Eufy is immune. Roborock declares honors_clean_order False (adapter.py:601) and run_plan.py:1363-1370 hardcodes strict_order=True for stepped plans, so effective_strict is True. With every room_group skipped, phases holds only breaks, the 884-885 trim empties it, `not any(...)` over [] is True, and the fallback runs with `[] or sorted(included_room_ids)` == [] against an effective_rooms where every room is enabled=False -> [] -> `payload_state = phases[0]` raises IndexError. Confirmed get_start_status calls _build_effective_start_plan at its very top (core/manager.py:2765), before the all_selected_rooms_blocked guard at 2834 that exists for this exact state. HIGH stands.

title: The collapse fallback's `all_ids` is provably always [] — and the unit test manufactures the very key the real engines never emit
observed_behavior:
`all_ids = [rid for p in collapsed for rid in p.get("queue_room_ids", [])]` reads `queue_room_ids` off dispatch phases. No engine writes that key: EufyRoomCleanEngine → build_room_clean_payload returns `{vacuum_entity_id, map_id, payload, resolved_rooms, room_count}` (queue_engine.py:357-363); GenericRoomIdsEngine.build_payload returns the same five keys (dispatch_engines.py:211-217); _build_per_room_phases the same (273-280). Only the framework's OWN break/zone phases carry `"queue_room_ids": []` (run_plan.py:851-852, 858-859, 877-878) — and the fallback only runs when NO break or zone phase survives. So `all_ids` is always `[]` and the expression is always `sorted(included_room_ids)`.

Why it survived seven audits: tests/integration/test_charge_wait_phase.py:245-248 monkeypatches `_build_dispatch_phases` with `lambda **kw: [{"ids": ..., "queue_room_ids": list(kw["queue_room_ids"])}]` — the fake injects the exact key the production engines omit, so CW-8/CW-9 exercise the live branch and never the dead one.

Consequence today is bounded (the union of room_group rooms is always a superset of `included_room_ids`, because both step sources derive from the same enabled set: apply_run_profile disables every non-profile room at profiles/manager.py:1201-1204, and get_queue_steps builds its groups from `_enabled_room_ids_in_order`), so the SET is right by accident. What is lost is real: the fallback rebuilds from `effective_rooms`, discarding the `group_managed` per-group overlay built at run_plan.py:834-841, and merges every surviving group into one dispatch.
user_impact: A stepped plan whose breaks are all trimmed (leading and/or trailing) runs as one flat clean using each room's GLOBAL stored settings instead of the per-group settings the card wrote into the step — e.g. `[room_group(kitchen: vacuum), room_group(kitchen: mop), charge_wait]` cleans the kitchen once, with whatever the room's persisted settings happen to be. The dead `all_ids` also means any future fix that assumes step-order is preserved here will silently not work.
guards_checked: queue_engine.build_room_clean_payload return dict (357-363 — no queue_room_ids); dispatch_engines._SinglePhaseMixin/GenericRoomIdsEngine/DreameSegmentEngine return dicts (114, 211-217, 273-280, 390-396 — none emit it); the three framework phase literals in run_plan.py (851, 858, 877 — the only writers, all excluded by the enclosing condition); tests/integration/test_charge_wait_phase.py `_steps_phases` helper (245-248 — the fake that keeps the branch green).

confirmations: CONFIRMED. I checked every engine return dict: EufyRoomCleanEngine delegates to build_room_clean_payload (queue_engine.py:357-363), GenericRoomIdsEngine.build_payload (211-217) and _build_per_room_phases (273-280), and DreameSegmentEngine (390-396) — none emits a queue_room_ids key. Only the framework's own break/zone phases carry `"queue_room_ids": []` (run_plan.py:851, 858, 877), and the fallback at 902 runs only when no such phase survives. So `all_ids` is provably always [] and the expression always degrades to sorted(included_room_ids). The 'why it survived' claim also checks out: tests/integration/test_charge_wait_phase.py:247 (and 289) monkeypatch _build_dispatch_phases with `lambda **kw: [{'ids': ..., 'queue_room_ids': list(kw['queue_room_ids'])}]` — the fake manufactures the exact key production omits. Consequence is bounded (the id SET is right by accident) but the per-group `group_managed` overlay built at 834-841 is discarded.

The dead-code claim is proven: I read every engine's return dict — build_room_clean_payload (queue_engine.py:357-363), GenericRoomIdsEngine.build_payload (dispatch_engines.py:211-217) and _build_per_room_phases (273-280) all return {vacuum_entity_id, map_id, payload, resolved_rooms, room_count} and none emits queue_room_ids; only the framework's own break/zone phases carry it, and those are excluded by the enclosing condition. So `all_ids` is always [] and the expression is always sorted(included_room_ids). Downgraded to LOW: it is dead code today (the set is right by accident, as the finder concedes), and the one behavioural consequence — losing the per-group overlay — only materialises when the trim in A5-PP-RP-5 fires, which is where that impact is already counted.

title: A user-authored leading or trailing charge/wait step is silently deleted at dispatch while the card still shows it and stamps has_charge_steps
observed_behavior:
`while phases and phases[0].get("phase_type") in _BREAKS: phases.pop(0)` / `while phases and phases[-1].get("phase_type") in _BREAKS: phases.pop()` (run_plan.py:884-887). The stated rationale — "A break with no clean to bracket is pointless" (880-882) — is false for a LEADING break: `[charge_wait(95), room_group(...)]` has a clean immediately after it, and "charge to 95%, then clean" is a coherent plan; the same holds for a trailing "top up to 100% after the run".

Both orderings are one click away in the shipped editor: `addDraftChargeStep`/`addDraftWaitStep` append at `steps.length` (src/state/run-profiles.js:320-330) and `captureCurrentRoomsAsDraftGroup` appends a group at the end (351-358) — so "add a charge step, then capture the rooms" yields a LEADING charge, and the more natural "capture the rooms, then add the charge" yields a TRAILING one. `moveDraftStep` (344-347 → moveStep, steps-order.js:59-67) can put any step at index 0. Nothing rejects either: set_run_profile_steps only requires one room_group (profiles/manager.py:1015), and _enrich_saved_run_profile still reports `has_charge_steps: any(s.get("type") == "charge_wait" for s in steps)` (profiles/manager.py:844) so the card renders the charge chip.

The drop is also what pushes a single-group plan into the PP-RP-4 collapse: after the trim, `collapsed` holds only room_group dispatch phases and the fallback replaces them.
user_impact: A profile the user built as "wait 30 minutes, then clean" or "charge to 95%, then clean" starts cleaning immediately, at whatever battery level the robot is sitting at; "clean, then charge to 100%" never charges. The step remains visible in the profile editor and the stepped preview, and nothing is logged, so the user has no way to learn the step is inert.
guards_checked: normalize_run_profile_steps (profiles/manager.py:786-797 — clamps values only, no positional rule); set_run_profile_steps (1015 — one room_group required, position irrelevant); sanitizeStepsForSave (src/state/steps-order.js:154-180 — no positional rule); clampIndex in insertChargeStep/insertWaitStep (steps-order.js:52-56, 70-78, 104-109 — allows index 0); add_queue_break's `after = max(1, min(_safe_int(after_index, 1), room_count - 1))` (core/manager.py:1707 — DOES prevent a leading break, but only on the ad-hoc live queue, not in a saved run profile); tests/integration/test_charge_wait_phase.py:263-266 CW-8 — asserts the drop as intended behaviour, i.e. the trim is deliberate and no caller compensates.

confirmations: CONFIRMED. run_plan.py:884-887 pops leading and trailing phases whose phase_type is in ('charge_wait','wait'), and the justifying comment at 880-882 ('a break with no clean to bracket is pointless') is false for a leading break — 'charge to 95%, then clean' has a clean immediately after it. Both orderings are one click away: src/state/run-profiles.js:320-330 addDraftChargeStep/addDraftWaitStep insert at steps.length and captureCurrentRoomsAsDraftGroup (351-358) also appends, so charge-then-capture yields a leading break and capture-then-charge a trailing one; moveDraftStep can put anything at index 0. Nothing rejects either — normalize_run_profile_steps clamps values only, set_run_profile_steps:1015 requires only one room_group, and _enrich_saved_run_profile:844 still reports has_charge_steps so the card renders the chip. core/manager.py add_queue_break DOES clamp after_index for the ad-hoc queue, which is precisely why saved profiles are the unguarded case.

Confirmed the unconditional leading/trailing pops at run_plan.py:884-887 and that the stated rationale ('a break with no clean to bracket') does not hold for a leading break. Confirmed both orderings are authorable in the shipped editor: addDraftChargeStep/addDraftWaitStep splice at steps.length (src/state/run-profiles.js:320-330), moveDraftStep -> moveStep (steps-order.js:59-67) allows index 0, clampIndex in insertChargeStep/insertWaitStep permits 0, and neither normalize_run_profile_steps nor set_run_profile_steps:1015 imposes a positional rule. Confirmed core/manager.py:1707 DOES prevent a leading break — but only on the ad-hoc live queue, not in a saved profile. The step stays visible and has_charge_steps still True, so nothing tells the user it is inert. MEDIUM is right.

title: A stepped Roborock run enforces clean order but still tells the user the order is advisory
observed_behavior: The advisory is suppressed off the METHOD PARAMETER: `order_advisory = (None if strict_order else self._order_advisory(...))` (run_plan.py:1458-1464), whose comment says "Suppressed when strict_order is active — order is then ENFORCED ... so the advisory would contradict". But the stepped branch does not use the parameter: run_plan.py:1363-1370 calls `_build_steps_phases(..., strict_order=True)` unconditionally, and `_build_dispatch_phases` then computes `effective_strict = bool(strict_order) and not honors_order` = True for Roborock (`honors_clean_order: False`, adapters/roborock/adapter.py:601), producing one single-segment phase per room (dispatch_engines.py:239-281). Meanwhile `strict_order` (the parameter) is still False, so `_order_advisory` runs and returns its text whenever `len(included_room_ids) >= 2`.
user_impact: Every stepped Roborock run with two or more rooms displays "Cleaning order shown here is advisory: this vacuum cleans rooms in the order saved in its own app (set a cleaning Sequence there to enforce it) or optimizes the path itself" — on precisely the runs where the integration IS enforcing the order room-by-room. The user is told to go configure a Sequence in the Roborock app to fix a problem that does not exist on this run.
guards_checked: _order_advisory itself (run_plan.py:697-723 — correctly gates on `honors_clean_order` and `len(included_room_ids) < 2`; it has no way to know the plan turned out stepped); _build_dispatch_phases' fold (run_plan.py:770-777 — correct, and the reason Eufy is unaffected: honors_order True → effective_strict False → advisory already None); the stepped-branch comment at 1356-1362 which documents the hardcoded True.

confirmations: CONFIRMED but cosmetic — downgraded. run_plan.py:1458-1464 suppresses the advisory off the METHOD PARAMETER strict_order, which is False for get_start_status's default call, while the stepped branch at 1363-1370 passes strict_order=True into _build_steps_phases; _build_dispatch_phases:770-777 then computes effective_strict = True for Roborock (honors_clean_order False, adapter.py:601) and emits one single-segment phase per room. Confirmed the two variables are different: run_plan.py:1458-1464 suppresses the advisory off the METHOD PARAMETER strict_order (False from get_start_status), while the stepped branch at 1363-1370 hardcodes strict_order=True into _build_steps_phases, where Roborock's honors_clean_order False makes effective_strict True and produces one single-segment phase per room. Downgraded to LOW: the run is dispatched correctly and in the right order — only an advisory sentence is wrong, telling the user to configure a Sequence they do not need. Cosmetic.

title: _settings_profile_display hardcodes the Eufy-era built-in profile-name set and takes no vacuum_entity_id, so a brand with its own profile keys renders every room as "Custom"
observed_behavior:
`is_custom = selected_normalized in {"", "custom", "user_1"} or (selected_normalized != resolved_normalized and selected_normalized not in {"vacuum_quick", "vacuum_deep", "vacuum_mop_quick", "vacuum_mop_deep"})` (run_plan.py:125-128), with the same four names plus `custom`/`user_1` hardcoded again in `_profile_name_label`'s `explicit` map (81-95). The function signature (98-110) is keyword-only display values — no `vacuum_entity_id`, no `catalog` — so it structurally cannot consult `resolve_profile_catalog((get_adapter_config(vid) or {}).get("room_profiles"))`, the seam every other resolution site now threads (queue_engine.py:222-224, room_profiles.resolve_room_profile_for_room's `catalog` argument). This is the same brand-blind shape as DQ-Q-2's `_match_profile_from_fields`, one layer up in presentation.

Both shipped brands happen to reuse the framework keys — adapters/roborock/adapter.py:679-689 declares `room_profiles` with "Same profile KEYS as the framework catalog ... only the VALUES are Roborock's" — so there is no impact today; the defect is that the seam cannot express a brand that names its profiles differently.
user_impact: A future adapter that declares its own `room_profiles.builtins` keys (the block is adapter-owned and free-form) gets `is_custom = True` for every room whose profile resolves cleanly, so the pre-run plan, the water-estimate room list and the job snapshot all label real presets as "<Room> Custom <Mode>", and `is_custom_profile` — which the card uses to decide whether to show the preset chip — is wrong for every room.
guards_checked: resolve_profile_catalog / get_room_profile / resolve_profile_name_for_constraints (profiles/room_profiles.py:342-409 — all accept a `catalog` and are correctly brand-parameterised; the display layer is the only site that isn't); adapters/roborock/adapter.py:679-689 (declares the same keys, which is what masks this today); the call sites (run_plan.py:422-435 in estimate_job_water_usage — has `vacuum_entity_id` in scope and could pass it, but the callee has no parameter to receive it).

confirmations: CONFIRMED. _settings_profile_display's signature (run_plan.py:98-110) is keyword-only display values with no vacuum_entity_id and no catalog, so it structurally cannot reach resolve_profile_catalog; the four framework keys are hardcoded in the is_custom test at 125-128 and again in _profile_name_label's explicit map at 87-94. Verified the call site at 422-435 does have vacuum_entity_id in scope and simply has no parameter to pass it to, and that roborock/adapter.py:679-689 deliberately reuses the framework KEYS ('Same profile KEYS as the framework catalog ... only the VALUES are Roborock's'), which is exactly what masks this today. title: Mid-job path-block report walks reachability over the QUEUE only, so any queued room whose access parent is not in the queue is reported blocked — and can cancel the job
area: AREA 6 — Estimates and what the user is told (planning/run_plan.py: estimate_job_water_usage, get_runtime_path_block_report, _settings_profile_display; profiles/room_profiles.py TypedDicts)
user_impact: Running a subset of rooms (the normal case) plus any door/motion blocker rule: the first time that blocker entity changes state mid-run, rooms that the start plan judged perfectly accessible are declared blocked. With cancel_and_event the run is cancelled and the robot returns to the dock mid-job (job data finalized as incomplete); with pause_and_event the robot stops; with the default event_only the user gets a false "N rooms blocked" event naming rooms that are fine and will still be cleaned.
guards_checked: Read and none rescue it: `active_job.get("status") not in {"started","paused"}` (1529) only limits to live jobs; `_structural_access_graph_issues(validation)` (1537) returns non-empty only for self_reference/duplicate_edge/cycle_detected/multiple_inbound/multiple_dock_rooms (access_graph.py:836-844) — a well-formed tree passes; `if not queue_room_ids` (1545) and `if not remaining_room_ids` (1556) are both non-empty mid-run; the `blocker_rules_present and not any(grants_access_to ...)` early return (1608-1613) does NOT fire because an access graph exists in this scenario (that is the precondition); the sha1 signature dedupe (1691) only suppresses REPEATS of the same false report; `_room_rule_matches` (1584) guards only `direct_blocked`; `listeners/path_blockers.py:116` only filters no-op state changes.

confirmations: CONFIRMED — and this is the strongest genuinely-new finding in the set. get_runtime_path_block_report seeds `accessible_room_ids` from queue_room_ids only (run_plan.py:1615-1619) and filters parents to queue_room_id_set in the fixpoint (1628-1632) and again in the affected-rooms loop (1650-1654), while its declared sibling _build_effective_start_plan walks all_rooms_by_id with unfiltered parents (1132-1146). I verified rooms/access_graph.py:251-274 builds requires_map over EVERY managed room and setdefaults [] for parentless ones, so a queued room with an unqueued parent is neither seeded nor reachable and falls straight into the access_dependency arm at 1642-1672 — which, unlike direct_blocked, is NOT gated on _room_rule_matches, so it fires on any watched-entity change including a blocker turning OFF. listeners/path_blockers.py:116 only skips no-op transitions, then applies path_block_action at 139-157. I checked every early return the finder names (1529, 1537, 1545, 1556, 1608) and none rescues a well-formed graph with a partial queue. Downgraded one notch only because the destructive arms (cancel_and_event / pause_and_event) are opt-in; the default event_only still fires a false 'N rooms blocked' naming rooms that are fine.

The asymmetry is real and I verified both sides: _build_effective_start_plan seeds accessible_room_ids from ALL rooms and follows unfiltered parents (run_plan.py:1132-1136, 1145), while get_runtime_path_block_report seeds from queue_room_ids only and filters parents to queue_room_id_set (1615-1632). rooms/access_graph.py:251-274 builds requires_map over every managed room, so a queued room whose single access parent is not queued can never enter the set: not seeded (requires_map non-empty) and `if parent_ids and any(...)` is False because parent_ids filters to []. Confirmed the access-dependency arm is NOT gated on _room_rule_matches (only the direct arm at 1584 is), and confirmed listeners/path_blockers.py fires on any watched blocker-entity transition (including OFF) and applies path_block_action, with cancel_and_event calling async_cancel_active_job + EVENT_JOB_FINISHED. Downgraded to HIGH: on the SHIPPED DEFAULT (event_only, jobs/active_job.py:289) the outcome is a false 'N rooms blocked' event naming rooms that are fine — user-visible and wrong with no error. The physical cancel/pause outcomes require the user to have explicitly selected the non-default path_block_action, so CRITICAL overstates the default configuration.

title: A room stamped profile_name="custom" is re-labelled as the brand's DEFAULT preset ("Vacuum Quick") with is_custom_profile=False — proven for any mop room on hardwood
area: AREA 6 — Estimates and what the user is told (planning/run_plan.py: estimate_job_water_usage, get_runtime_path_block_report, _settings_profile_display; profiles/room_profiles.py TypedDicts)
observed_behavior:
Three verified steps:

(1) `_build_effective_start_plan` (run_plan.py:1310-1311) re-derives the name on every start:

    matched_profile = self._manager._match_profile_from_fields(updated_room)
    updated_room["profile_name"] = matched_profile if matched_profile else "custom"

`_match_profile_from_fields` (profiles/manager.py:137-179) builds its candidate from a bare `{profile_name, floor_type}` with NO water_level key, so `resolve_room_profile_for_room`'s `elif "water_level" not in room_config:` (room_profiles.py:435-436) FIRES and overwrites the profile's own water with the floor default, while the real room (a full RoomConfig dict, models.py:207) always carries the key so that branch never fires for it. I executed the pipeline: applying the built-in `vacuum_mop_quick` ("Quick", water "Medium") to a **hardwood** room stores "Medium", the candidate resolves to "Low", and the match returns **None** → "custom". Same for laminate/marble/granite/concrete; only `tile` ("Medium") matches. `carpet_low_pile` + `vacuum_quick` also fails (fan forced to "Max" by floor_type_fan_defaults vs stored "Standard").

(2) `get_room_profile` (room_profiles.py:284-289) then substitutes the DEFAULT profile's IDENTITY for the unknown name:

    if profile is None:
        normalized_name = (catalog or {}).get("default_profile") or DEFAULT_ROOM_PROFILE_NAME
        profile = merged.get(normalized_name)

Executed: `resolve_room_profile_for_room` on `{profile_name:"custom", clean_mode:"vacuum_mop", water_level:"Medium", ...}` returns `selected_profile_name: 'vacuum_quick'`, `resolved_profile_name: 'vacuum_quick'`, `selected_profile_label: 'Vacuum Only Quick'` — while clean_mode stays `vacuum_mop`. Downstream cannot distinguish "no profile" from "the default profile".

(3) `_settings_profile_display` (run_plan.py:123-136) then computes `is_custom` False (selected==resolved=='vacuum_quick', neither in {"","custom","user_1"}) and emits `profile_label = f"{room_label} Vacuum Quick"`, `is_custom_profile: False`. It is fed by `queue_engine.build_room_clean_payload`'s resolved_rooms, which stores only the NAMES (queue_engine.py:319-320) and discards the resolver's `selected_profile_label`, so the label is re-derived from a hardcoded 4-entry map (`_profile_name_label`, run_plan.py:87-94). Both display sites are affected: `core/manager.py:2562` (get_payload_state, service-exposed) and `run_plan.py:423` (water-estimate rooms).
user_impact: A kitchen the user set to the built-in "Quick" vacuum+mop profile is shown in the run plan / payload panel as "Kitchen Vacuum Quick", flagged as a stock preset rather than custom. Any user-saved profile is worse: its store key is `user_<timestamp>` (profiles/manager.py:73), so `_profile_name_label` renders it "User 20260730t142530" instead of the label the user typed. The card mirrors the same logic (src/renderers/metrics.js `_localizedProfile`, src/state/review.js:188), so it does not correct it.
guards_checked: Read and none rescue it: `get_room_profile`'s second fallback (room_profiles.py:287-289) only re-defaults again; `_normalize_profile_name` maps only LEGACY_PROFILE_ALIASES, not "custom"; `merge_profile_dicts` merges stored profiles but there is no store key "custom"; `_settings_profile_display`'s first is_custom disjunct checks `selected_normalized in {"","custom","user_1"}` — by the time it runs the name has ALREADY been replaced with "vacuum_quick", so the check is looking for a value that can no longer arrive; card-side `src/renderers/rooms.js:1588` derives isCustomProfile from the ROOM entity's profile_name, which is a different object and does not fix the plan/payload rows.

confirmations: CONFIRMED at all three steps by execution. (1) I replayed the real apply -> protect -> match pipeline and reproduced 'custom' for vacuum_mop_quick/deep on hardwood/laminate/marble/granite/concrete and for vacuum_quick on carpet_low_pile — and run_plan.py:1310-1311 re-derives profile_name on every start, so the stamp is not a one-off. (2) Executed resolve_room_profile_for_room on a room whose profile_name is 'custom': it returns selected_profile_name 'vacuum_quick' and selected_profile_label 'Vacuum Only Quick' via get_room_profile's silent default substitution at lines 284-289 — the identity of 'no profile' is destroyed. (3) _settings_profile_display then computes is_custom False (selected == resolved == 'vacuum_quick', neither in the sentinel set) and emits profile_label '<Room> Vacuum Quick' / is_custom_profile False. Verified queue_engine.py:319-320 stores only the NAMES and discards the resolver's selected_profile_label, so the label is re-derived from the hardcoded 4-entry map. Both display sites (core/manager.py:2562, run_plan.py:423) inherit it. The user_<timestamp> rendering is a real second symptom.

All three steps verified. Step 1 reproduced by executing the real apply -> protect -> match pipeline (mop profile on hardwood/laminate/marble/granite/concrete -> 'custom'; run_plan.py:1310-1311 re-derives it on every start). title: The gate's absent-key defaults cannot see the new empty-string convention: gating an already-empty field yields "", gating an absent one yields an Eufy literal, and neither is flagged
area: AREA 2 — the capability gate (profiles/room_profiles.py: apply_capability_gate, apply_room_profile_to_config, merge_profile_dicts, normalize_room_profile, plus resolve_profile_catalog / get_available_profile_names and the queue_engine + active_job + dispatch/manager consumers that make each defect land or not)
observed_behavior: Every value the gate reads uses an absent-key default: `fan_speed = str(settings.get("fan_speed", "Max"))` (494), `water_level = str(settings.get("water_level", "Off"))` (495), `clean_intensity = normalize_clean_intensity(settings.get("clean_intensity", "Quick"))` (496), `path_type = str(settings.get("path_type", "wide"))` (497). `dict.get` rescues a MISSING key, never an EMPTY value — and the recent change made "" the framework's canonical 'nobody said' (models/models.py:188-190, rooms/room_manager.py:101-103, room_profiles.py:411-414). title: Cancel is defeated ACROSS _dispatch_active_phase's awaits — the watchdog re-sends a clean after return_to_base, then the run is finalized while the robot keeps cleaning
area: WD — the watchdog and retry (jobs/phase_runner.py: _await_phase_started, _dispatch_active_phase, _run_advanced_phase retry/max_attempts)
observed_behavior: _run_advanced_phase checks job['_cancel_in_flight'] exactly ONCE per attempt (lines 531-549), then enters `await self._dispatch_active_phase(...)` which performs FOUR sequential awaits with no re-check: _run_global_pre_calls (Roborock: vacuum.set_fan_speed + a mop-intensity select, blocking=True cloud calls), apply_per_room_live_settings_awaited, _resolve_live_dispatch_payload (which does `await async_refresh_room_source(...)` — a full get_maps network refresh) and finally _dispatch_clean_payload. That is a multi-second-to-tens-of-seconds gap ACROSS awaits, not an intra-sync-block interleave. async_cancel_active_job (jobs/active_job.py:2203-2215) sets _cancel_in_flight synchronously and THEN awaits vacuum.return_to_base. If the user cancels inside the dispatch chain, the watchdog resumes and sends app_segment_clean / room_clean anyway — the robot turns around and starts cleaning. async_cancel_active_job's terminal-state confirm loop (line 2223) polls 30s for docked/idle, never sees it, logs only a WARNING (line 2240) and finalizes anyway; mark_active_job_finalized clears the slot. The watchdog's own _await_phase_started then sees status != 'started' and returns True, so nothing ever undoes the send.
user_impact: The user presses Cancel Run, the robot returns to base, then immediately drives back out and cleans the phase's room. The job record is written as cancelled/completed and the active-job slot is cleared, so the ongoing clean is untracked, unrecorded, and no longer cancellable from the card — the user has to cancel again (or use the vacuum's own app). The window overlaps exactly the moment a user is most likely to hit Cancel: the between-room dock pause.
guards_checked: phase_runner.py:531-549 (the single per-attempt _cancel_in_flight/status/phase guard — it is BEFORE the dispatch, not inside it); _dispatch_active_phase 968-1036 (no job re-read, no cancel check on any of its 4 await boundaries); dispatch/manager.py:45-84 _dispatch_clean_payload (fires the service unconditionally, no active-job inspection); dispatch/manager.py:247-323 _resolve_live_dispatch_payload (awaits async_refresh_room_source, no cancel awareness); jobs/active_job.py:2188-2247 async_cancel_active_job (sets the flag up front — correct — but its 30s non-confirmation path only WARNs and proceeds to finalize); phase_runner.py:894-904 _await_phase_started's per-poll cancel re-check (correct, but it runs AFTER the dispatch has already gone out).

confirmations: CONFIRMED from source. phase_runner.py:536-541 reads _cancel_in_flight once per attempt, then :552-555 awaits _dispatch_active_phase, which (:1010-1027) performs _run_global_pre_calls -> apply_per_room_live_settings_awaited -> _resolve_live_dispatch_payload (await async_refresh_room_source) -> _dispatch_clean_payload (async_call blocking=True) with NO job re-read at any boundary. active_job.py:2203-2215 writes _cancel_in_flight synchronously then awaits return_to_base, so the flag IS visible — nothing reads it. This is a genuine cross-await gap, not an intra-sync-block interleave, so the single-loop rule does not rescue it. _await_phase_started's per-poll cancel check (:898-904) returns True AFTER the send, and the 30s confirm loop (:2223-2247) only WARNs then finalizes. Window is seconds (blocking cloud calls), once per phase, at the between-room dock — exactly when a user cancels. NOTE: identical to A2-CAN-1; dedupe.

CONFIRMED mechanically. phase_runner.py:536-541 reads _cancel_in_flight once per attempt; :553 then enters _dispatch_active_phase (:968-1036) which has four sequential awaits and never re-reads the job. active_job.py:2203-2208 sets the flag synchronously then awaits return_to_base. _run_global_pre_calls (dispatch/manager.py:434-446) and apply_per_room_live_settings_awaited (active_job.py:1449-1460) confirmed to swallow but they still AWAIT blocking=True service calls, and _resolve_live_dispatch_payload (dispatch/manager.py:281) awaits async_refresh_room_source. So the window across awaits is real, not an intra-sync interleave. Concrete case: Roborock, phases [room_group kitchen, room_group hall]; hall phase dispatch attempt 2 begins at t=0; set_fan_speed + mop_intensity + get_maps refresh occupy t=0..6s; user presses Cancel Run at t=2s -> flag set, return_to_base sent; at t=6s _dispatch_clean_payload fires app_segment_clean and the robot turns around. SEVERITY DOWNGRADE: the trigger window is the few seconds inside the dispatch chain, entered once per attempt (the settle sleep at :529 is BEFORE the guard, and _await_phase_started re-checks cancel every poll), so this is a narrow race, not the CRITICAL 'run is unrecoverable / data destroyed' bar. Robot does the wrong thing but a second Cancel recovers it.

title: Every abnormal exit from the watchdog leaves _phase_dispatch_pending set, and that state is UN-REAPABLE BY DESIGN — the run wedges in 'started' forever and blocks all future starts
area: WD — the watchdog and retry (jobs/phase_runner.py: _await_phase_started, _dispatch_active_phase, _run_advanced_phase retry/max_attempts)
observed_behavior: Enumerating every exit from _run_advanced_phase: (a) confirmed start -> _clear_phase_dispatch_pending, clean; (b) job advanced/finalized/paused/cancelled -> returns, guard owned elsewhere, clean; (c) attempts exhausted (line 572) -> guard LEFT SET; (d) an exception anywhere in the dispatch chain -> guard LEFT SET, task dies. For (d) the raisers are real and unguarded: _dispatch_clean_payload's `hass.services.async_call(..., blocking=True)` raises HomeAssistantError when the vacuum integration is unreachable/re-authing mid-run; _resolve_live_dispatch_payload's async_refresh_room_source can raise; dispatch_zone_clean raises ValueError on five distinct paths (no zone_command, no live map, projection validation failure, zone count cap, per-zone size bounds — dispatch/manager.py:108-172) and a zone phase's ONLY dispatch site is this task. There is no try/except anywhere in _run_advanced_phase or _dispatch_active_phase. The NEW part beyond DQ-ACT-3 is what the left-set guard costs: job_monitor.is_stranded_started (line 359) returns False the instant phase_dispatch_pending is True, so the stranded-job reaper is explicitly disabled; listeners/lifecycle.py:297 sets should_finalize_completed = False on the same flag, so the completion gate is disabled; and advance_active_job_phase (queue_engine.py:476) had already reset has_observed_active_lifecycle to False, which is a SECOND independent block on both the completion gate (lifecycle.py:269) and the reaper (job_monitor.py:357). The job therefore sits status='started' permanently, and evaluate_job_lifecycle then returns 'active_job_running' -> build_start_blocker_from_lifecycle blocks EVERY subsequent start.
user_impact: One transient service failure (or a zone phase whose live map isn't loaded) permanently kills the run AND every future run: the card shows a job forever 'in progress' on a parked robot, scheduled/automated starts are blocked with 'A room-clean job is currently active', and nothing recovers it — not the reaper, not the completion gate, not an HA restart's normal path. Only a manual Cancel Run clears it. On Roborock nothing surfaces the stall at all (see guards), so the user's only symptom is that cleaning silently stopped happening.
guards_checked: phase_runner.py:486-576 (no try/except on the loop or the dispatch); phase_runner.py:837-856 _clear_phase_dispatch_pending (only reachable on the success path); jobs/job_monitor.py:355-369 is_stranded_started (phase_dispatch_pending AND has_observed_active_lifecycle are both hard early-outs); listeners/lifecycle.py:263-298 (has_observed_active_lifecycle + _phase_dispatch_pending both gate should_finalize_completed); listeners/lifecycle.py:196-209 (the flag can only re-arm when lifecycle_state is active AND, for Roborock, is_job_active is ON — false for a parked robot); jobs/active_job.py:736 / core/manager.py:3264-3268 detect_run_anomalies (stall/EVENT_STALL_DETECTED is hard-disabled when capabilities.honors_clean_order is False — i.e. Roborock, the primary strict-order brand — and on Eufy needs awaiting_bounds_exit plus 2x the room estimate); dispatch/manager.py:435-446 and jobs/active_job.py:1449-1460 (verified _run_global_pre_calls and apply_per_room_live_settings_awaited DO swallow, so they are not the raisers — the raisers are the two dispatch calls).

confirmations: Core mechanism CONFIRMED: _run_advanced_phase (:530-576) has no try/except and only clears _phase_dispatch_pending inside the confirmed-start branch (:561); the exhaustion path (:572) and any raise leave it set. _dispatch_clean_payload's async_call(blocking=True) and _resolve_live_dispatch_payload's async_refresh_room_source are unguarded raisers (verified the pre-calls and per-room settings DO swallow, so the finder correctly identified the real raisers); dispatch_zone_clean raises ValueError on 5 paths (dispatch/manager.py:108-172, read). job_monitor.py:359 and lifecycle.py:297 both treat the flag as an unconditional veto; queue_engine.py:476 resets has_observed_active_lifecycle. BUT the 'blocks EVERY subsequent start' half is PARTLY REFUTED: for a parked robot evaluate_job_lifecycle needs active_cleaning_target OR an active task_status OR an active vacuum_state (job_monitor.py:197-201) — on Eufy the target reads a clear sentinel and task_status/vacuum_state are idle, so it returns 'ready', and get_start_status (manager.py:2784) blocks only on status=='paused'. It holds only on Roborock, whose current_room reverts to the dock ROOM NAME (non-empty). Recovery via Cancel Run also exists, so 'unrecoverable' is overstated. Downgrading to HIGH. Overlaps A5-STR-3.

title: has_native gates on the DECLARED entity-id string (always truthy on both shipped brands), so the coarse fallback is dead code and Eufy verifies phases against a signal its own adapter declares unusable as a live current-room source
area: WD — the watchdog and retry (jobs/phase_runner.py: _await_phase_started, _dispatch_active_phase, _run_advanced_phase retry/max_attempts)
observed_behavior: `has_native = bool(cfg.get('entities', {}).get('active_cleaning_target'))` tests whether the adapter DECLARED an entity id, not whether that entity exists or whether the signal is a trustworthy live current-room source. Both shipped adapters unconditionally build the string (adapters/eufy/adapter.py:247, adapters/roborock/adapter.py:197), so has_native is always True and the `elif self._vacuum_started_cleaning(...)` fallback at line 949 — which the docstring at 885-887 advertises for 'brands with no native current-room signal' — is unreachable on Eufy and Roborock. The right question already exists elsewhere in the codebase: live_transition.native_transition_source, which Roborock sets True (adapter.py:474) and Eufy explicitly sets False (adapter.py:753). jobs/active_job.py:951 uses that flag to decide whether to trust the same resolver; the watchdog does not. docs/dev/design/eufy-native-transition.md:34-39 states outright that Eufy's active_cleaning_target is a completion SENTINEL of the wrong shape and that a 'name-surfacing + slug-reconciliation shim' is a PREREQUISITE that has not been built. So on Eufy, native_current_room_target_id (active_job.py:1120-1166) slug-matches a target-set descriptor (core/manager.py:3527-3528 documents it reads e.g. "N zone" for a whole zone) against individual room slugs; for any multi-room room_group phase it cannot match, so `signal` is None on every poll, `progressed` never becomes True, idle reaches verify_seconds (90s) with cleaning_in_target == 0, and _await_phase_started returns False -> re-dispatch. Same failure on Roborock whenever sensor.<id>_current_room is missing/unavailable (a cloud-poll blip; the entity's existence is never checked — hass.states.get returning None yields signal None, indistinguishable from 'not in the room'). Eufy sequenced jobs are reachable today: planning/run_plan.py:1352-1370 builds phases for ANY brand whenever the run steps contain charge_wait / wait / zone, and only INTRA-group strict order is gated on honors_clean_order.
user_impact: On a Eufy 'vacuum -> charge to 80% -> mop' profile, the mop phase is re-dispatched up to 3 times, 90 seconds apart, while the robot is already mopping — each room_clean restarts the clean, so the robot repeatedly abandons and restarts the same rooms. title: An HA restart during a room_group or zone phase's un-confirmed window strands the run — the re-arm covers ONLY dock phases and the comment's claimed recovery path cannot fire
area: WD — the watchdog and retry (jobs/phase_runner.py: _await_phase_started, _dispatch_active_phase, _run_advanced_phase retry/max_attempts)
observed_behavior: core/manager.py:332-336 force-clears _phase_dispatch_pending on every loaded job, then core/manager.py:473-480 re-arms via rearm_dock_phase_if_needed, which returns False at line 125 for anything that is not is_dock_polled_phase_type (i.e. everything except charge_wait/wait). The comment at manager.py:325-326 claims 'a ROOM-group run then advances via the normal completion path (or Cancel Run)' — that is a claim the code does not have. A persisted _phase_dispatch_pending == True means precisely that the watchdog had NOT yet confirmed the phase started, i.e. the robot is parked in the settle window (10s, or 45s for a dock-room target) or in a verify window where the dispatch was ignored. advance_active_job_phase already reset has_observed_active_lifecycle to False (queue_engine.py:476), and listeners/lifecycle.py:269 requires it for should_finalize_completed while lifecycle.py:200-202 can only re-arm it when the lifecycle reads active (and, on Roborock, when is_job_active is ON). user_impact: Restart HA (or reload the integration) while a phased run is between rooms, and the run stops dead: the robot never leaves the dock, the card shows the job still 'started' forever, no error and no log line is emitted, the reaper never fires, and every future start is blocked with 'A room-clean job is currently active' until the user manually cancels.

I checked whether the completion path the comment claims can rescue it: has_observed_active_lifecycle was reset to False by the advance and can only re-arm when lifecycle is in {active_job_running, mid_job_service} (lifecycle.py:48-51, 200-202) — for a parked robot Eufy reads 'ready' (target is a sentinel) and Roborock additionally requires is_job_active strict 'on', which is OFF on the dock. So neither brand re-arms; the gate stays shut and the reaper is blocked by has_observed_active_lifecycle (job_monitor.py:357). Narrowing caveat the finder missed: the wedge needs the restart to land in the window AND the device to have actually ignored the dispatch — if the robot IS cleaning, the flag re-arms and the comment's claim holds. Given the docstring's own '~1 room in 4 actually fired', that compound is not rare, so HIGH stands.

The genuine failure needs the restart to land while the phase was NOT actually running: the 10s settle (45s for a dock-room target) before the first send, or a verify window where the device ignored the dispatch. That is a ~10-90s window per phase, so MEDIUM, not HIGH.

title: Adapter-declared phase_timing overrides are applied with no clamping — poll_seconds: 0 pins the event loop in a hot loop, max_attempts: 0 dispatches nothing and wedges the phase
area: WD — the watchdog and retry (jobs/phase_runner.py: _await_phase_started, _dispatch_active_phase, _run_advanced_phase retry/max_attempts)
observed_behavior: core/manager.py:4904-4912 merges dispatch.phase_timing straight over the defaults with only a type coercion (`type(pt[key])(declared[key])`) and no range check; adapters/config_schema.py:969-973 declares phase_timing as an unvalidated free-form dict. phase_runner.py:891 then does `_poll = float(pt['poll_seconds'])` and phase_runner.py:966 does `await asyncio.sleep(_poll)`. With poll_seconds: 0 the loop yields but never advances its accounting — cleaning_in_target and idle both increment by 0.0, so neither `>= confirm_seconds` nor `>= verify_seconds` can ever be reached and _await_phase_started spins the event loop indefinitely at full CPU with no exit. With max_attempts: 0 (or negative) `range(1, 1)` is empty, so _run_advanced_phase performs ZERO dispatches and falls straight through to the give-up log at 572, leaving _phase_dispatch_pending set — the WD-2 permanent wedge, reached without a single command being sent. A negative verify_seconds makes every attempt fail on the first poll, burning all three re-dispatches immediately.
user_impact: A future brand adapter (the seam exists precisely so a third path-optimizing brand can declare its own profile) that ships a typo or a deliberate 0 either freezes Home Assistant's event loop for every integration on the box, or silently disables phase dispatch entirely. Neither shipped adapter trips it today — Eufy declares no phase_timing block and Roborock's values are sane — so this is a seam defect, not a live bug.
guards_checked: core/manager.py:4889-4913 _phase_timing (the only resolver — type coercion in a try/except, no min/max, no positivity check); adapters/config_schema.py:969-973 (phase_timing is typed only as 'dict', its sub-keys are not in the schema at all); phase_runner.py:890-966 (_poll and pt['confirm_seconds']/pt['verify_seconds'] are consumed raw, no defensive floor); phase_runner.py:515/530/565 (settle_seconds, max_attempts consumed raw in _run_advanced_phase); adapters/roborock/adapter.py:314-326 (the only live override — all values sane, which is why nothing catches this today).

Neither shipped adapter trips it (Eufy declares no block; Roborock's values at adapter.py:314-326 are sane), so future_brand_only/MEDIUM is right. One overstatement: asyncio.sleep(0) still yields, so it burns CPU rather than literally freezing the loop for other integrations.

Neither shipped adapter trips it (Eufy declares no phase_timing block; adapters/roborock/adapter.py:314-326 declares sane values), so this is future-brand-only.
