title: Cancel is LOST across _dispatch_active_phase's awaits — the watchdog re-sends a clean AFTER return_to_base and the robot is left cleaning with no job record
observed_behavior: _run_advanced_phase reads `job` and checks `_cancel_in_flight` ONCE at the top of each attempt (phase_runner.py:531-541), then calls `await self._dispatch_active_phase(...)` at :553. _dispatch_active_phase (:968-1036) never re-reads the job and contains FOUR sequential awaits before the clean actually goes out: `_run_global_pre_calls` (dispatch/manager.py:434-439 — one `blocking=True` service call per declared global pre-call; Roborock declares fan_speed + mop_intensity), `apply_per_room_live_settings_awaited` (active_job.py:1449-1455 — another blocking call per per-room setting), `_resolve_live_dispatch_payload`, then `_dispatch_clean_payload`. Each blocking service call is a real device round-trip, so the window from the guard check to the wire send is seconds. `async_cancel_active_job` sets `_cancel_in_flight=True` synchronously (active_job.py:2203-2208) and then awaits `vacuum.return_to_base` — but nothing between the watchdog's guard check and `_dispatch_clean_payload` re-reads that flag. The segment-clean therefore lands AFTER the return-to-base and the robot resumes cleaning. The cancel's terminal-confirm poll (:2223-2237) then never sees docked/idle, logs a warning at :2240 and finalizes anyway; `mark_active_job_finalized` sets status='completed', so the lifecycle listener's `status not in {started, paused}` filter (listeners/lifecycle.py:137) stops tracking the still-running robot entirely.
user_impact: The user presses Cancel Run, the card reports the job cancelled and cleared — and the vacuum keeps cleaning the room it was told to cancel, now completely untracked. No error is surfaced anywhere; the only trace is a WARNING in the log. This is the DQ-ACT-2 lead extended to its actual consequence: the loss is not merely 'cancel is delayed', it is 'cancel is undone and the robot physically keeps running'.
guards_checked: phase_runner.py:536-541 attempt-loop guard (status/phase-index/_cancel_in_flight) — checked once, BEFORE the dispatch, never again; phase_runner.py:898-904 `_await_phase_started`'s per-poll cancel check — runs only AFTER the dispatch has already gone on the wire, so it cannot prevent it; phase_runner.py:849-856 `_clear_phase_dispatch_pending` — no-op during cancel because the cancel already cleared the flag, and it is not a dispatch gate; active_job.py:2203-2208 the `_cancel_in_flight` write itself — it IS synchronous and IS visible in `manager.data`, the defect is purely that no re-read happens; active_job.py:2223-2247 the 30 s terminal-confirm poll — it only WARNS on non-confirmation and finalizes regardless, so it does not rescue; dispatch/manager.py:433-445 the per-call try/except — swallows failures, does not abort.

confirmations: CONFIRMED — same defect as A1-WD-1, independently verified against source (phase_runner.py:536-555, :968-1036; active_job.py:2203-2215, :2223-2247; dispatch/manager.py:433-445 confirmed to SWALLOW, so the finder correctly located the four real awaits). The added claim that lifecycle.py:137's status filter drops the still-running robot once mark_active_job_finalized sets status='completed' is also correct. DUPLICATE of A1-WD-1 — one work item, not two.

CONFIRMED — this is the same defect as A1-WD-1, verified independently and reported by a second area. Everything checks out in source: the guard at phase_runner.py:536-541 is per-attempt and pre-dispatch; _dispatch_active_phase never re-reads the record; active_job.py:2203-2208 writes _cancel_in_flight synchronously before awaiting return_to_base; the non-confirmation path at :2239-2247 only WARNs and finalizes anyway; mark_active_job_finalized (:2034) sets status='completed' so listeners/lifecycle.py:137 stops tracking the still-running robot. CAN-1 adds one correct detail WD-1 omits: dispatch/manager.py:433-445's per-call try/except swallows failures rather than aborting the chain, so nothing short-circuits the dispatch after a cancel. SEVERITY DOWNGRADE for the same reason as WD-1: a several-second race window entered once per attempt, and a second Cancel recovers.

title: Cancelling a sequenced run reports the WRONG missed rooms — per-phase reset of queue_room_ids/completed_room_ids feeds the incomplete-run log and trouble-rooms counters
observed_behavior: `advance_active_job_phase` REPLACES `queue_room_ids` with only the next phase's rooms and RESETS `completed_room_ids`/`completed_rooms` to [] on every advance (queue/queue_engine.py:463, 467-468). `async_cancel_active_job` finalizes with `forced_outcome_status='cancelled'`, and the finalizer reads the LIVE record (`active_job_state = manager.get_active_job(...)`, learning/job_finalizer.py:469-472). `_write_incomplete_run_log` then computes `missed_room_ids = set(queued_room_ids) - set(active_completed)` from exactly those two per-phase fields (job_finalizer.py:1505-1522), and `_update_trouble_rooms_log` does the same (:1603-1622). The rescue at job_finalizer.py:752-761 that synthesizes the full queue applies ONLY to `outcome_status == 'completed'`, explicitly not to cancelled. Two distinct wrong outcomes: (a) cancel during a room_group phase N>0 -> `queued_room_ids` is only phase N's room(s), so every room in phases N+1..end that was never cleaned is silently ABSENT from the missed list; (b) cancel during a charge_wait/wait/zone phase -> that phase carries `queue_room_ids: []` (planning/run_plan.py:851, 858, 878), which triggers the fallback at job_finalizer.py:332-333 to the LIVE map queue (the full original selection) while `completed_room_ids` is still [], so EVERY room in the run is reported missed including the ones phase 0 actually cleaned. Case (b) is the documented path: `_run_charge_wait_phase`'s docstring (phase_runner.py:596-597) claims the timeout 'finalize[s] like a cancel, so the un-cleaned remaining rooms are reported missed' — a comment asserting behaviour the code does not have.
user_impact: After cancelling a stepped run the card's incomplete-run banner and the EVENT_RUN_INCOMPLETE automation payload name the wrong rooms — under-reporting (rooms silently never retried by a `retry_missed_rooms` automation) or over-reporting (already-clean rooms re-run). The chronic trouble-rooms detector is poisoned in the same motion: case (b) records a miss against every room of the run, so rooms that clean perfectly get flagged as chronic problem rooms.
guards_checked: learning/job_finalizer.py:752-761 the completed-outcome queue synthesis — gated on `outcome_status == 'completed'`, so it never fires for a cancel; job_finalizer.py:332-333 the `queue_live` fallback — present, but it fires only when the active record's queue is EMPTY, which is precisely what turns case (b) into over-reporting rather than rescuing it; job_finalizer.py:1497-1503 the outcome-status gate — cancelled/failed/interrupted all take the broken branch; listeners/_common.py:265-275 `run_incomplete_event_data` — passes `missed_room_ids` straight through with no cross-check against the run's phases; queue_engine.py:458 `advanced = dict(active_job)` — the `phases` list (which DOES hold the full room set) survives on the record, so the information is present and simply never consulted by either log writer.

confirmations: CONFIRMED end to end. queue_engine.py:463-476 replaces queue_room_ids with the next phase's rooms (derived from that phase's resolved_rooms — [] for charge_wait/wait/zone, verified at run_plan.py:851/858/877) and resets completed_room_ids/completed_rooms to []. job_finalizer.py:752-761's queue synthesis is gated on outcome_status=='completed', so a cancel never gets it; :1497-1522 computes missed = set(queued) - set(active_completed) from exactly those per-phase fields; :332-333's queue_live fallback fires only when the active queue is EMPTY, which is what converts case (b) into over-reporting rather than rescuing it. Case (a) is reinforced by A3-REC-3: completed_room_ids is ALWAYS [] on a phased job, so even a mid-group cancel reports the whole current phase missed and silently omits every later phase.

CONFIRMED, both cases, walked in source. queue_engine.py:463/467-468 replaces queue_room_ids with the next phase's rooms and resets completed_room_ids/completed_rooms to [] on every advance. job_finalizer.py:1505-1522 computes missed_room_ids = set(queued_room_ids) - set(active_completed) from exactly those fields, and the completed-outcome queue synthesis at :752-761 is gated on `outcome_status == 'completed'` so it never fires for a cancel (:1497-1503 routes cancelled/failed/interrupted into the broken branch). Case (a): Eufy profile [group A(kitchen,hall), wait 30m, group B(bed1,bed2)], user cancels during group B -> queued_room_ids = [bed1,bed2] only, so nothing from group A is even eligible and any later phase is invisible. Case (b) verified sharper: a charge_wait/wait/zone phase carries queue_room_ids: [] (run_plan.py:851, 858, 878), which trips the queue_live fallback at job_finalizer.py:332-333 to the FULL original selection while completed_room_ids is [], so every room in the run is reported missed including the ones phase 0 actually cleaned. The docstring claim at phase_runner.py:596-597 ('remaining rooms reported missed') is indeed behaviour the code does not have. Trouble-rooms poisoning at :1603-1622 uses the same two fields.

title: Cancel OPENS the completion gate it is about to wait for — it clears _phase_dispatch_pending before return_to_base, and neither the gate nor maybe_advance_phase checks _cancel_in_flight
observed_behavior: `async_cancel_active_job` sets `_phase_dispatch_pending = False` (active_job.py:2205) BEFORE issuing return_to_base, then spends up to 30 s awaiting the device to reach docked/idle/task_status=completed (:2210-2237). That flag is the ONLY thing stopping the lifecycle completion gate from acting on a between-phase dock (listeners/lifecycle.py:297-298). The job's status stays 'started' for the whole window, so the listener's filter at lifecycle.py:137 admits it, and `should_finalize_completed` (lifecycle.py:263-284) is evaluated as a LEVEL check on the exact signals the cancel is driving the robot toward. Neither lifecycle.py:300-312 nor `PhaseRunner.maybe_advance_phase` (phase_runner.py:141-200) checks `_cancel_in_flight` at all. Consequences: (a) mid-sequence -> `advance_active_job_phase` runs, incrementing `current_phase_index` and wiping `completed_room_ids`/`completed_rooms` (feeding CAN-2); (b) on the LAST phase, and for every ATOMIC job, `maybe_advance_phase` returns False and the listener calls `finalize_learning_for_active_job` with NO forced status (lifecycle.py:316-321) — it takes the exactly-once claim first, so the run is written as a normal COMPLETED run with used_for_learning=True and the cancel's own forced 'cancelled' finalize gets 'already_finalized'/'finalize_in_flight'. The heuristic cancel detector cannot rescue (b): `_detect_cancel_likely_run` bails with 'not_single_room' unless `len(resolved_rooms) == 1` (job_finalizer.py:1326-1328). Worst reachability is Roborock: `completion.task_status_value` is 'charging' (adapters/roborock/adapter.py:263), so during a charge_wait phase the robot is LITERALLY sitting in the completion state — and the charge-timeout auto-cancel at phase_runner.py:696 routes through this same function, clearing the guard while the robot charges on the dock.
user_impact: A cancelled or charge-timed-out run is recorded as a successful full completion and fed into the learning set, so a truncated run's room timings/areas/battery deltas become the learned baseline. The user gets no cancelled record, no incomplete-run banner and no EVENT_RUN_INCOMPLETE, and the active-job snapshot's finalize_summary is then blanked to all-None when the cancel's own `mark_active_job_finalized` runs with the rejected result.
guards_checked: listeners/lifecycle.py:137 status filter — 'started' is admitted for the entire cancel window; lifecycle.py:281-284 `is_job_active` recharge guard — Eufy declares no `entities.job_active` so it returns False (listeners/_common.py:134-136), and on Roborock the binary is OFF once the robot is charging; lifecycle.py:269 `has_observed_active_lifecycle` — True mid-run, only reset by an advance; lifecycle.py:297-298 `_phase_dispatch_pending` — the one real guard, and the cancel is what clears it; phase_runner.py:141-200 `maybe_advance_phase` — no status check and no `_cancel_in_flight` check anywhere; learning/manager.py:690-741 the exactly-once claim — it correctly prevents TWO records, but it does not decide WHICH writer wins, so it cements the wrong (uncancelled) outcome; job_finalizer.py:1326-1328 `_detect_cancel_likely_run` — single-room-only, so a multi-room atomic run is never reclassified.

confirmations: CONFIRMED for the room_group case. active_job.py:2204-2205 sets _cancel_in_flight AND clears _phase_dispatch_pending before return_to_base, then holds status='started' for up to 30s (:2218-2237). lifecycle.py:263-298 (read in full) has no _cancel_in_flight check anywhere, and phase_runner.py:141-200 maybe_advance_phase has neither a status nor a cancel check before it mutates storage and returns True. On Roborock, cancelling mid-room-group: has_observed_active_lifecycle is True, task_status hits 'charging' (= completion value) on dock, secondary is bypassed by require_job_active_clear, job_active clears -> gate opens -> advance or (last phase) a NORMAL completed finalize that wins the exactly-once claim (learning/manager.py:702-716, verified). TWO CORRECTIONS: (1) 'every ATOMIC job' is wrong — active_job.py:2203 gates the whole block on job.get('phases'), so an atomic job's gate state is unchanged by cancel; (2) the claimed 'worst reachability, charge_wait' does NOT hold — advance resets has_observed_active_lifecycle to False and Roborock cannot re-arm it while docked (needs is_job_active strict 'on'), so the gate is shut during a charge phase.

CONFIRMED for phased jobs, with one factual correction. Verified: active_job.py:2203-2205 clears _phase_dispatch_pending BEFORE return_to_base and before the 30s poll (:2218-2237), status stays 'started' throughout; listeners/lifecycle.py:263-298 has no _cancel_in_flight check anywhere, and phase_runner.py:141-200 maybe_advance_phase has neither a status nor a cancel check. On the LAST phase maybe_advance_phase returns False and lifecycle.py:316-321 finalizes with NO forced status -> the run is written as a normal completed run and the cancel's own forced-'cancelled' finalize loses the exactly-once claim. Roborock reachability is real: adapters/roborock/adapter.py:263 sets completion.task_status_value='charging', so the cancel drives the robot into its own completion state, and the charge-timeout auto-cancel at phase_runner.py:696 routes through the same function. CORRECTION: the claim 'and for every ATOMIC job' is wrong — active_job.py:2203 gates the whole block on `if active_job.get('phases')`, so an atomic job never had the guard set and the cancel opens nothing; the atomic-job completion race pre-exists and is not caused by cancel. Severity stays HIGH on the phased path alone (a cancelled run recorded as a successful completion and fed to learning).

title: Pause+resume permanently kills the phase watchdog for room_group and zone phases — resume re-arms ONLY dock phases and never restores the dispatch guard
observed_behavior: `pause_active_job` flips status to 'paused' and clears `_phase_dispatch_pending` (active_job.py:1900-1906). On the next poll the live watchdog `_run_advanced_phase` sees `status != 'started'` and RETURNS permanently (phase_runner.py:536-549) — likewise `_await_phase_started` returns True and exits (phase_runner.py:898-904). `async_resume_active_job` restores only status/paused_at/paused_duration (active_job.py:1941-1943) and then calls `rearm_dock_phase_if_needed` (:2155), which bails at phase_runner.py:125 via `is_dock_polled_phase_type` — DOCK_POLLED_PHASE_TYPES is {'charge_wait','wait'} only, deliberately excluding 'zone' and never containing 'room_group' (step_types.py:41). So for a room_group or zone phase, resume re-arms NOTHING and does not restore the guard. The phase is left with no driver, no retry budget and no gate suppression. This matters because the watchdog's whole purpose is re-sending an `app_segment_clean` the device IGNORED (phase_runner.py:7-12): if the pause lands inside the settle/verify window — up to `settle 10 s` (or `dock_settle 45 s`) plus 3 x `verify 90 s` ~= 4.5 min of every phase (core/manager.py:74-99) — the room may never have started, and after resume nothing will ever re-dispatch it. `vacuum.start` (active_job.py:2136-2141) resumes the device's own last command, not our segment target. With `_phase_dispatch_pending` now False, the robot's dock state satisfies the completion gate and `maybe_advance_phase` walks straight past the un-started phase. For a ZONE phase this is sharper still: a zone is dispatched ONLY by `_dispatch_active_phase`'s zone branch (phase_runner.py:996-1008), so the whole zone clean is skipped.
user_impact: A pause+resume during a stepped run silently skips a room or an entire saved-zone step, and the run then finalizes as a normal successful completion (the guard that would have stalled it is gone). The user sees a clean 'completed' record for a run that never touched one of its rooms. The in-code comment at active_job.py:2146-2148 asserts the opposite — 'a ROOM-group phase resumes guard-free and the completion gate advances normally' — which is true only when the robot actually IS cleaning that room, exactly the condition the watchdog exists to verify.
guards_checked: phase_runner.py:101-139 `rearm_dock_phase_if_needed` — read in full; the `is_dock_polled_phase_type` early return at :125 is what excludes room_group and zone; step_types.py:41 DOCK_POLLED_PHASE_TYPES and its docstring — confirms 'zone' is excluded ON PURPOSE for the poller, but no compensating re-arm exists for it; phase_runner.py:77-99 `_spawn_dock_poller` — the double-spawn guard is correct but is only reachable for dock phases; active_job.py:1902-1906 pause's guard-clear and its comment; active_job.py:1913-1948 `resume_active_job` — restores status/paused_at/paused_duration_seconds and nothing else; phase_runner.py:849-856 `_clear_phase_dispatch_pending` — irrelevant, the guard is already False; listeners/lifecycle.py:297 — the gate is unsuppressed once the flag is False; core/manager.py:5070-5079 — the only other `_run_advanced_phase` spawn site is job start, never re-entered on resume.

confirmations: Mechanism CONFIRMED: pause_active_job (:1900-1906) flips status and clears the guard; the watchdog (:536-549) and _await_phase_started (:898-904) both permanently exit on status != 'started'; resume (:1941-1948) restores only status/paused_at/paused_duration and then calls rearm_dock_phase_if_needed, which bails at phase_runner.py:125 for anything outside {charge_wait, wait} (step_types.py:42). Nothing re-spawns _run_advanced_phase (verified the only other spawn site is manager.py:5070-5079, job start). Downgrading to MEDIUM: the harm requires the pause to land in the un-confirmed window AND the device to have ignored the dispatch. If the robot had actually started (the common case, including every already-dispatched zone), vacuum.start resumes it and the completion gate advances normally, which is precisely what the comment at :2146-2148 claims. What is genuinely lost is the retry budget, not the dispatch itself.

CONFIRMED mechanically, with the stated OUTCOME corrected. Verified: pause_active_job clears _phase_dispatch_pending (active_job.py:1906); _run_advanced_phase returns permanently on status != 'started' (phase_runner.py:536-549); resume_active_job restores only status/paused_at/paused_duration (:1941-1943) and async_resume_active_job's only re-arm is rearm_dock_phase_if_needed (:2155), which bails at phase_runner.py:125 for room_group and zone (DOCK_POLLED_PHASE_TYPES = {charge_wait, wait}, step_types.py:42). core/manager.py:5070-5079 is the only other _run_advanced_phase spawn site and is never re-entered. So a pause landing in the settle window (10s, or 45s dock-room) or a verify window where the device ignored the send leaves the phase with no driver and no retry budget, permanently. CORRECTION to the impact: it does NOT 'finalize as a normal successful completion' — advance_active_job_phase already set has_observed_active_lifecycle=False (queue_engine.py:476) and a parked robot cannot re-arm it (lifecycle.py:200-208), so the completion gate stays shut and the run WEDGES in 'started' with the reaper equally blind (job_monitor.py:357). Bad, but a wedge, not a silent skip-and-complete. SEVERITY DOWNGRADE: needs the pause to land inside a window where the device had not actually started the phase; a pause during genuine cleaning resumes correctly (vacuum.start restarts the device's own command and the lifecycle re-arms).

title: Pause has NO in-flight flag at all — a dispatch already inside _dispatch_active_phase lands after vacuum.pause and the robot cleans while the record says 'paused'
observed_behavior: `async_pause_active_job` awaits `vacuum.pause` with `blocking=True` (active_job.py:2101-2106) and only AFTERWARDS flips status via `pause_active_job` (:2107). There is no pause analogue of `_cancel_in_flight` — the sole signal to the watchdog is the status field, written at the very end. So two windows exist where the phase watchdog still sees status=='started': (1) the whole duration of the `vacuum.pause` service round-trip, and (2) any `_dispatch_active_phase` call already past its guard check (phase_runner.py:536-553), which as in CAN-1 has four sequential blocking awaits before the segment reaches the wire and never re-reads the record. In either case the `app_segment_clean` lands after the pause and un-pauses the device. title: A multi-room room_group phase records ONLY queue_room_ids[0] — the group's whole time/area lands on one room, the other N-1 rooms produce no timing at all, and the run is still flagged high-confidence

Per-metric attribution for an N-room group: cleaning_seconds = the group's whole cleaning_time delta -> room[0]; area_m2 = the group's whole cleaning_area delta -> room[0]; cleaning_wall_seconds = the entire phase wall clock -> room[0]; battery_delta -> room[0] (always None, see REC-5); passes/clean_mode are not per-room recorded at all (they ride the phase payload). Rooms 1..N-1 get NO room_timing entry. learning/history_store.py:988-996 then concatenates the per-phase room_timing lists into the run's `room_timings` AND sets transit_capture_valid = _every_phase_captured, which stays True because each phase DID produce a (single) non-empty timing. learning/stats_rebuilder.py:441-449 gates on exactly that flag, so room[0] gets a 'captured' (highest-trust) minutes+area sample worth the whole group while the remaining rooms silently fall back to per_room_duration = total/room_count.
user_impact: On any Eufy stepped run (a run profile or queue with a wait / charge / zone stop, e.g. 'vacuum kitchen+hall+living, wait 30 min, mop kitchen+hall+living'), the first room of each group permanently learns ~N x its true cleaning minutes and ~N x its true area, while the other rooms never accumulate a real observation. title: Phase 0's timing is attributed to the whole-run queue's first room, which need not be a room of phase 0 at all
observed_behavior: _capture_finishing_phase_timing reads the room id from `active_job.get('queue_room_ids')`, not from the phase's own `resolved_rooms`. For phases 1+ that is safe: advance_active_job_phase (queue/queue_engine.py:463) rewrites queue_room_ids to the NEXT PHASE's rooms. Phase 0 is never narrowed — queue/queue_engine.py:389 builds the initial active job with `queue_room_ids = list(queue_state.get('queue_room_ids', []))`, i.e. the FULL run queue (all enabled rooms sorted by their configured `order`, build_queue_from_managed_rooms), while `resolved_rooms` comes from payload_state = phases[0] and IS phase-scoped. A run profile's step order is independent of room `order`, so queue_room_ids[0] can be a room that belongs to a LATER step. Example: rooms Kitchen(order 1), Bathroom(order 2); profile steps = [room_group(mop: Bathroom), wait, room_group(vacuum: Kitchen, Bathroom)]. queue_room_ids = [Kitchen, Bathroom]; phase 0 = Bathroom only; rid = Kitchen. The Bathroom mop's cleaning_seconds / area_m2 / cleaning_wall_seconds are recorded against KITCHEN. The slug lookup even disagrees — slug_by_id is built from the PHASE's resolved_rooms (:290-295), so slug_by_id.get(rid) returns None for the foreign id — and nothing compares the two.
user_impact: The first clean of a stepped run teaches the wrong room. A mop pass on the bathroom is learned as a kitchen vacuum sample (and ingested as high-confidence — see REC-1's transit_capture_valid path), so the kitchen's estimate drifts toward a room it never cleaned and the room that actually ran learns nothing. title: Every counter sample carries battery=None — last_battery_percent is read but never written by anything, so per-room battery attribution is dead on both recording paths
observed_behavior: record_counter_sample stamps each sample with `'battery': job.get('last_battery_percent')`. A repo-wide grep finds `last_battery_percent` in exactly three places: this read, and two test fixtures that pre-seed it by hand. No production code writes it. The only writer of active-job sensor keys is listeners/job_metrics.py, whose watch_map (:87-124) subscribes to precisely three entities — cleaning_time -> last_cleaning_time_seconds, cleaning_area -> last_cleaning_area_m2, water_level -> last_station_water_percent. The battery entity (declared by BOTH adapters: adapters/eufy/adapter.py:252, adapters/roborock/adapter.py:201) is never added. So every sample's battery is None on both brands, which zeroes out both downstream consumers: counter_segmentation.py:388-390 leaves battery_delta None for every segment of an atomic run, and phase_runner.py:453 (`bat_delta = int(bats[0]-bats[-1]) if len(bats) >= 2`) leaves it None for every strict-order phase. docs/dev/06-job-lifecycle.md:242 and :687 both assert the job-metrics listener writes last_battery_percent — a documentation claim the code does not honour.
user_impact: Per-room battery drain is never observed on either brand: every completed_job record's room_timings[].battery_delta is null, so the only per-room battery figure available anywhere is the even split total_battery_used / room_count (stats_rebuilder.py:433). title: Mid-job recharge NEVER ends: the recharge-end branch is unreachable dead code, so recharge_seconds_accumulated is always 0 and every recharging run is silently held from learning
observed_behavior: `update_active_job_recharge_observation` returns early at line 462 (`if not self._is_charging(vacuum_entity_id): ...persist...; return active_job`). Everything after 462 therefore runs with `_is_charging == True`. Line 470 enters the 'recharge already in progress' branch and line 472 asks `if not self._is_charging(vacuum_entity_id):` — the SAME pure `hass.states` read, in the SAME synchronous block, with no await between. It can never be True. Lines 473-484 are dead: `recharge_seconds_accumulated` is never incremented, `observed_mid_job_recharge` is never reset to False, and `tracker.resume_sampling()` is never called (grep confirms active_job.py:484 is its ONLY call site outside `tracker.end_job`). The branch is doubly unreachable: line 496 sets `pending_mid_job_recharge_return = False` when a recharge starts, and while the robot is charging `_is_low_battery_return_state` is False, so subsequent ticks bail even earlier at line 456. Consequences: (a) `recharge_seconds_accumulated` is permanently 0, so `history_store.build_completed_job_payload` (learning/history_store.py:848-856) subtracts nothing and `duration_minutes` includes the entire charge; (b) `learning/utils.evaluate_idle_wall_hold` — whose own docstring asserts 'duration_minutes is already paused/recharge-adjusted' — then sees `idle_gap = duration - cleaning` ≈ the whole charge (60-180 min) with no exemption, because `_run_had_break_phase` (learning/job_finalizer.py:148) only exempts COMMANDED charge_wait/wait phases and an unplanned recharge has none; idle_gap >= 20 → hold=True → `used_for_learning=False`, blocker `extreme_idle_wall`; (c) `compute_overhead_observed` reports `recharge_minutes: 0.0` while dumping the charge into `total_overhead_minutes`; (d) `observed_mid_job_recharge_count` sticks at 1 — a second recharge in the same run is never counted; (e) mapping-tracker sampling stays paused for the rest of the run. PROOF the branch is untestable in production: tests/integration/test_jobs_active_job.py:261 monkeypatches `_is_charging` with `MagicMock(side_effect=[True, False])` and comments 'First charging check (gate) True; second (recharge-ended check) False' — the test is green only because it forces one pure state read to return two different values.
user_impact: Any run where the robot returns to dock to recharge mid-job (the common case for large multi-room Eufy jobs) is silently excluded from learning with an `extreme_idle_wall` blocker, and its stored duration is inflated by the full charge time. The user sees runs quietly not improving their estimates, with no error. A second recharge in one run is never recorded at all.

title: The two sample recorders still use the repudiated `started_at and not ended_at` predicate and write into EVERY map bucket, so a finished or stranded job silently absorbs another run's counters
observed_behavior: `record_active_job_sensor_value` (line 1676) and `record_counter_sample` (line 1709) both gate on `job.get('started_at') and not job.get('ended_at')` and both loop over `data['active_jobs'][vacuum_entity_id].values()` — every map bucket. This module's OWN docstring (lines 139-157) documents that predicate as wrong: 'nothing in this integration ever writes ended_at onto an active-job record ... Callers using it treat a finished job as in-flight', and explicitly names these two functions as the reason `run_is_in_flight` exists ('Do NOT reuse this for the sample recorders (record_counter_sample, record_active_job_sensor_value) ... That is a different question with its own answer — run_is_in_flight below'). Two sibling call sites were converted — core/error_tracker.py:1030-1038 and battery/manager.py:459-463, whose comments record the exact damage ('on multi-map installs the first finalized bucket permanently shadowed the live one') — but these two, the ones the helper was written for, were never migrated. `record_pose_sample` (line 1775) partially migrated (it adds a status check) but kept the same dead conjunction. Reachability of two simultaneously-matching buckets: `mark_active_job_finalized` (line 2034) sets status='completed' and leaves `started_at` in place; nothing ever writes `ended_at` (grep-confirmed). The start gate cannot block it — `evaluate_job_lifecycle`'s `active_job_exists` is computed from the SELECTED map's job only (core/manager.py:2648), and a stranded/completed bucket on another map leaves the robot docked/idle with a clear target, so lifecycle reads 'ready'. The job-metrics listener (listeners/job_metrics.py:172-181) calls both recorders unconditionally on every cleaning_time/cleaning_area state change with no status gate of its own. Result: while map B runs, map A's stale bucket has `last_cleaning_time_seconds` / `last_cleaning_area_m2` / `last_battery_percent` overwritten with map B's live values and map B's counter samples appended to its `counter_samples`. `learning/job_finalizer.py:552-558` reads exactly those `last_*` fields from the active-job state at finalize.
user_impact: On a multi-map install, a run stranded as `started` on map A (the exact condition `poll_stranded_started_job` exists for) absorbs map B's live cleaning time and area while B runs; when the stranded reaper finalizes A as `interrupted` after the 5-minute grace, that record carries map B's numbers and is Restore-able into learning by the user, poisoning map A's room baselines. Even without a strand, every finalized bucket keeps accumulating foreign counter samples and re-persisting them to .storage.
guards_checked: Read and confirmed non-rescuing: `dispatched_job_is_in_flight` / `run_is_in_flight` (lines 139-184) exist and are correct but are not called from either recorder; `_default_active_job_state` / `_normalize_active_job` never set `ended_at`; grepped for any writer of `ended_at` on an active-job record — none exists; `mark_active_job_finalized` (2020-2082) sets status/finalized/paused_at/has_observed_active_lifecycle/_phase_dispatch_pending but not `ended_at`; `clear_active_job` (1862) resets the slot but is only reached via the explicit service or external-run teardown; the `_MAX_COUNTER_SAMPLES` cap bounds size, not correctness; `maybe_handle_external_run` (learning/external_run.py:87-96) correctly blocks external capture when any map holds started/paused, but says nothing about `completed` buckets and does not gate the metrics listener.

title: Cancel clears `_phase_dispatch_pending` up front, so the return-to-base dock is read as phase completion and the job advances to the next phase during the 30 s cancel window
observed_behavior: `async_cancel_active_job` sets `_cancel_in_flight = True` AND `_phase_dispatch_pending = False` (lines 2204-2205) on the stored record, then awaits `vacuum.return_to_base` and polls for a terminal state for up to `_CANCEL_CONFIRM_TIMEOUT_S = 30` s (lines 2210-2237) before finalizing at 2272. The status stays `started` for that whole window. The completion gate in listeners/lifecycle.py evaluates on every watched state change and its ONLY strict-order suppressor is `if should_finalize_completed and active_job.get('_phase_dispatch_pending')` (line 297) — the flag the cancel just cleared. It has NO `_cancel_in_flight` check. The other conditions are all satisfied by the cancel's own return-to-base: `task_status == completion.task_status_value` (Roborock 'charging', reached the moment it docks; Eufy 'completed'), `completion_secondary_satisfied` (job_active clears on RTB), `has_observed_active_lifecycle` True, and the `is_job_active` recharge guard (line 281) does not fire because job_active just cleared. So `should_finalize_completed` becomes True and the listener calls `maybe_advance_phase` (phase_runner.py:141), which ALSO has no `_cancel_in_flight` and no status check: it runs `_capture_finishing_phase_timing`, calls `advance_active_job_phase`, and overwrites the stored record (phase_runner.py:167-169) with the next phase — `current_phase_index` incremented, `queue_room_ids` / `resolved_rooms` / `payload` / `room_count` swapped to the NEXT (never-cleaned) phase, `completed_room_ids` and `completed_rooms` reset to `[]`, `has_observed_active_lifecycle` reset to False. `async_cancel_active_job` then finalizes THAT record. The cancel's own comment at lines 2198-2202 justifies clearing the guard by reasoning about the watchdog ('it guards on _cancel_in_flight') — true of `_run_advanced_phase` (phase_runner.py:536-541, which does bail, so the robot is not re-dispatched) and of the dock pollers (`_still_ours`, phase_runner.py:625-631/760-766) — but the COMPLETION GATE was never given that check, and it is the one the cleared flag was guarding.
user_impact: Cancelling a multi-phase run (e.g. vacuum → charge-to-X% → mop) produces a cancellation record attributed to the phase that never ran: zero completed rooms and the wrong room set / room_count, so the run-incomplete 'missed rooms' report and the learning record both describe rooms the robot never touched. No error is surfaced — the cancel reports `cancelled: True`.
guards_checked: Read and confirmed non-rescuing: listeners/lifecycle.py:263-298 — the full `should_finalize_completed` chain, including the `is_job_active` recharge guard (281) and the `_phase_dispatch_pending` guard (297), with no `_cancel_in_flight` anywhere; phase_runner.py:141-200 `maybe_advance_phase` — no status and no `_cancel_in_flight` check before mutating storage and returning True; queue/queue_engine.py:430-485 `advance_active_job_phase` — gates only on `len(phases) >= 2` and `idx < len-1`, and `dict(active_job)` carries `_cancel_in_flight` forward but nothing reads it there; phase_runner.py:536-541 `_run_advanced_phase` — DOES check `_cancel_in_flight`, which prevents the robot from physically re-cleaning but does not undo the advance already written at phase_runner.py:169; phase_runner.py:625-631 and 760-766 `_still_ours` — same, they bail after the advance; active_job.py:2272 `mark_active_job_finalized` — runs AFTER, stamping `completed` onto the already-advanced record; the atomic-job path is unaffected (the block at 2203 is `if active_job.get('phases')`).

confirmations: CONFIRMED — same root as A2-CAN-3 (dedupe), verified independently. The cancel clears the one guard the completion gate honours (active_job.py:2205 vs lifecycle.py:297) and neither lifecycle.py:263-312 nor phase_runner.py:141-200 checks _cancel_in_flight; advance_active_job_phase (queue_engine.py:430-485) gates only on phase count/index and happily carries _cancel_in_flight forward unread. CONFIRMED, and the cleanest statement of the cancel/completion-gate collision. Verified: active_job.py:2204-2205 sets _cancel_in_flight AND clears _phase_dispatch_pending, then awaits return_to_base and polls up to 30s (:2210-2237) with status still 'started'; listeners/lifecycle.py:263-298 has no _cancel_in_flight check and its only strict-order suppressor is the flag the cancel just cleared; the is_job_active recharge guard at :281 does not fire because job_active clears on RTB. maybe_advance_phase (phase_runner.py:141-200) then runs with no status and no cancel check, and queue_engine.py:458-485 overwrites the record: current_phase_index incremented, queue_room_ids/resolved_rooms/payload/room_count swapped to the never-cleaned next phase, completed_room_ids and completed_rooms reset to [], has_observed_active_lifecycle reset to False. async_cancel then finalizes THAT record at :2272. title: Strand exclusion consults only task_status against a narrower vocabulary — an Eufy dock service cycle reaps a healthy mid-run job as `interrupted`
observed_behavior: `poll_stranded_started_job` calls `completed_finalize_signals()` (active_job.py:2370), which returns FOUR signals including `dock_status` — then reads only `signals["task_status"]` at line 2379 and passes `is_mid_run_status=task_status_n in mid_run_set`. `dock_status` is fetched and DISCARDED. The mid-run set is the adapter's `external_mid_run_statuses` (eufy/adapter.py:355) = exactly six task_status strings: 'Returning to Wash', 'Washing Mop', 'Returning to Empty', 'Emptying Dust', 'Returning to Charge', 'Charging (Resume)'. The SAME adapter separately declares the dock-service vocabulary `blocked_dock_status_states = ["Washing", "Recycling waste water"]` (adapter.py:375) and `HARD_SERVICE_STATES` (eufy/vocabulary.py:19) = {washing, washing mop, recycling waste water, recycling wastewater, emptying dust, emptying dust bin, dust emptying}. 'Recycling waste water' / 'recycling wastewater' / bare 'Washing' / 'Emptying dust bin' / 'Dust emptying' appear in the dock-service vocabulary and have NO counterpart in `external_mid_run_statuses` — so the strand exclusion cannot fire for those cycles on EITHER entity. `evaluate_job_lifecycle` in the same subsystem proves the codebase knows the value can arrive on either entity: it checks `dock_status_n in hard_service_states or task_status_n in hard_service_states` (job_monitor.py:180). The reaper checks one entity against the narrower list. Third ignored signal: the job record `poll_stranded_started_job` already has in hand carries `observed_mid_job_recharge=True` for the whole duration of an unplanned mid-run recharge dock (set at active_job.py:490, cleared only when charging stops) — the subsystem's own authoritative 'parked mid-run, will resume' state — and `is_stranded_started` never reads it. On Eufy every rescue is therefore absent: `job_active_on` is permanently False (Eufy declares no `entities.job_active`, so `is_job_active` returns False at _common.py:135-136), `secondary_satisfied` is True the moment `active_cleaning_target` clears (the robot is parked, not cleaning a segment), `vacuum_state` reads 'docked', `_phase_dispatch_pending` is False for an atomic Eufy job. A dock waste-water recycle / wash cycle runs several minutes; STRANDED_REAP_GRACE_MINUTES is 5.0 with a 1-minute tick, so 5-6 consecutive ticks inside one dock cycle is routine.
user_impact: A healthy Eufy vacuum+mop run parked at the dock for a service cycle is finalized as `interrupted` mid-run. `mark_active_job_finalized` sets status='completed' and clears the slot; the robot then resumes and cleans the remaining rooms with NO active job, so that work is recorded nowhere (and `maybe_handle_external_run` will treat the resumed half as an app-started run needing manual review). Worse, the reaper fires EVENT_RUN_INCOMPLETE listing the not-yet-cleaned rooms (pause_timeout.py:142), so a documented `retry_missed_rooms` automation dispatches a NEW clean of those rooms while the robot is still mid-run on them.
guards_checked: is_stranded_started() every early return (job_monitor.py:355-368): status!='started', has_observed_active_lifecycle, phase_dispatch_pending/job_active_on/is_mid_run_status, vacuum_state not in (docked,idle), secondary_satisfied, task_status==completion value — none covers a dock-status-only service state. is_job_active(unavailable_is_active=True) at _common.py:110-143 — returns False when the adapter declares no job_active entity, which is Eufy. completion_secondary_satisfied (_common.py:178) — Eufy takes the default branch, satisfied by a cleared active_cleaning_target. The stranded_since stamp/clear cycle (active_job.py:2400-2413) — it only requires the strand to hold on ~6 consecutive 1-minute ticks, well inside one dock cycle. update_active_job_recharge_observation (active_job.py:410) — writes observed_mid_job_recharge but nothing in the strand path reads it. The dock-phase exclusion via is_dock_polled_phase (active_job.py:433) — only covers COMMANDED charge_wait/wait phases, not an unplanned dock cycle.

confirmations: Code asymmetry CONFIRMED, user impact NOT. Verified: completed_finalize_signals returns dock_status (_common.py:170-175) and poll_stranded_started_job reads only signals['task_status'] (:2379), while its sibling evaluate_job_lifecycle checks BOTH entities against hard_service_states (job_monitor.py:180) — a real, verified divergence. Also verified is_stranded_started's early returns, is_job_active returning False for Eufy (no entities.job_active, _common.py:135-136), and that blocked_dock_status_states is dead config (grep: consumed by nothing outside config_schema descriptions). title: async_finalize_stranded_job calls the finalizer unguarded — one raising finalize kills the entire reaper tick for every vacuum, every minute, forever
observed_behavior: `async_finalize_stranded_job` awaits `self._manager.finalize_learning_for_active_job(...)` with no try/except, then calls `mark_active_job_finalized`. `finalize_learning_for_active_job` (core/manager.py:4619) does not swallow exceptions — it awaits `learning.async_finalize_completed_job` and `_ingest_completed_job_into_room_history` bare. Its SIBLING `async_cancel_active_job` wraps the identical call in try/except with a comment naming a PROVEN raiser: 'A finalizer that raises (e.g. a run ending on a zone, which it can't attribute) previously killed the cancel before mark_active_job_finalized ran, leaving the job stranded started and only clearable via Dev Tools' (active_job.py:2249-2271). That fix was never applied to the stranded twin. Compounding it, the reaper loop in listeners/pause_timeout.py:66-153 has no per-vacuum/per-map error isolation: `_process()` iterates `for vacuum_entity_id ... for map_id ...` with the cancel and strand calls inline, so a raise aborts the whole tick — every remaining vacuum and map is skipped, and `await manager_local.async_save()` at line 153 never runs. The same raise recurs on the next tick because `mark_active_job_finalized` never ran, `stranded_since` is still stamped and still past the grace. `async_cancel_active_job` is the other raiser on this loop: its `hass.services.async_call('vacuum','return_to_base', blocking=True)` at line 2210 is unguarded, and the pause-timeout reap fires precisely at a device that has been sitting untouched (frequently offline/unavailable).

title: _phase_dispatch_pending is a permanent strand exclusion — a watchdog that gives up wedges the run AND blinds the reaper that exists to recover it
observed_behavior: `_run_advanced_phase` exits its `for attempt in range(1, max_attempts+1)` loop without ever clearing `_phase_dispatch_pending`: the only clear is `_clear_phase_dispatch_pending()` inside the success branch at phase_runner.py:561, reached only when `_await_phase_started` returns True. On retry exhaustion the code logs 'run stalled — Cancel Run to recover' (line 572-576) and returns with the flag still True. Same outcome if the coroutine raises — it is a bare `hass.async_create_task(self._run_advanced_phase(...))` (phase_runner.py:193 and core/manager.py:5072) with no exception handling, so a raising `_dispatch_active_phase` kills the task with the flag set. `is_stranded_started` treats that flag as an unconditional exclusion (`if phase_dispatch_pending or job_active_on or is_mid_run_status: return False`, job_monitor.py:359), and the completion gate treats it the same way (listeners/lifecycle.py:297). The flag was designed as a TRANSIENT 'we are mid-dispatch' marker but has no timeout, no age check and no expiry anywhere; both consumers use it as a permanent veto. Nothing clears it without a user action: pause_active_job:1906, async_cancel_active_job:2205 and mark_active_job_finalized:2041 all require the user to intervene; `async_initialize` (core/manager.py:335) clears it only on a full HA restart. Sequenced jobs are NOT Roborock-only: planning/run_plan.py:1352-1370 builds multi-phase jobs for any run with a charge_wait/wait/zone stop and the comment at 1359-1362 states group boundaries are enforced by the phase structure regardless of honors_clean_order — so an Eufy stepped run (vac -> charge -> mop, the shipped v1.7.0 feature) carries phases and the flag too.
user_impact: A run whose next phase the device ignores three times (or whose dispatch raises) sits at status='started' indefinitely with both automatic recovery paths disabled. The card shows a job running forever, external-run capture stays suppressed, and the stranded reaper — the sole automatic escape — is structurally unable to see it. Only a manual Cancel Run or an HA restart clears it, and nothing tells the user that.

title: A dispatched run the device never started can never be reaped, then the NEXT run's completion signals finalize the stale slot with the wrong run's data
observed_behavior: `is_stranded_started` requires `has_observed_active_lifecycle` (line 357-358). That flag is armed in exactly one place — listeners/lifecycle.py:200-208 — and only when `evaluate_job_lifecycle` returns a state in `_ACTIVE_LIFECYCLE_STATES`. For a docked Eufy whose `app_segment_clean` the device silently ignored (the DQ-DE-1 stale-slug dispatch, an empty resolved segment list, a rejected wire payload), `evaluate_job_lifecycle` sees active_cleaning_target empty, task_status 'Standby'/'Charging' (not in ACTIVE_RUN_TASK_STATES) and vacuum_state 'docked' (not in the HA active set), so it falls through to 'ready' at job_monitor.py:225 and the flag never arms. The job is therefore permanently outside the strand definition. Nothing else clears the slot: an atomic job has no phases and no watchdog, and `get_paused_job_timeout_report` only handles status=='paused' (active_job.py:2297). Second-order damage: `maybe_handle_external_run` refuses to open a capture slot while ANY map holds status started/paused (external_run.py:87-96), so the stale slot suppresses external capture. When the user next starts a run from the app, the lifecycle listener arms `has_observed_active_lifecycle` on the STALE record (active_job exists + vacuum cleaning -> 'active_job_running'), and that run's completion signals then satisfy the gate at lifecycle.py:263-270 and finalize the STALE job — its queue rooms, its started_at — using the new run's counters.
user_impact: A dispatch the robot never acted on leaves a phantom 'running' job that no automatic path can clear, and the next app-started run is silently recorded against it: wrong rooms, wrong duration, wrong start time, fed into learning as a completed run. This is exactly the FN-1 mis-attribution the stranded reaper was built to prevent, and the reaper's own arming precondition excludes the case.

title: async_finalize_stranded_job reports success regardless of the finalizer's answer — a refused finalize still marks the slot 'completed' and fires a bogus EVENT_JOB_FINISHED
observed_behavior: `async_finalize_stranded_job` never inspects `finalize_result`. It passes whatever came back to `mark_active_job_finalized` and unconditionally returns `{"finalized": True, ...}`. Three refusal shapes reach it: `{"finalized": False, "reason": "finalize_in_flight"}` and `{... "already_finalized"}` from the exactly-once claim (learning/manager.py:704-716), and plain `None` when `_get_learning_manager()` is None (core/manager.py:4634-4635) or `{... "missing_started_at"}` (4645-4651). `mark_active_job_finalized` then sets status='completed', finalized=True and a finalize_summary of all-None (active_job.py:2034-2076) — labelling an unrecorded interrupted run 'completed'. The listener at pause_timeout.py:124 checks only `result.get("finalized")`, so it fires EVENT_JOB_FINISHED, and `job_finished_event_data` DEFAULTS the payload status to 'completed' when the outcome dict is empty (_common.py:229). The `finalize_in_flight` refusal is reachable because the reaper tick has no overlap guard: `async_track_time_interval(..., timedelta(minutes=1))` re-enters `hass.async_create_task(_process())` (pause_timeout.py:155-161) whether or not the previous `_process` finished, and `_process` can exceed 60s — `async_cancel_active_job` alone holds a hard 30s terminal-confirm poll (`_CANCEL_CONFIRM_TIMEOUT_S`, active_job.py:2218-2237) per paused job, before a `rebuild_stats=True` finalize, iterated over every vacuum and every map id.
user_impact: On an overlapping tick the user gets two EVENT_JOB_FINISHED events for one run — one carrying real data, one claiming status 'completed' with job_id None for a run that was actually interrupted and, in the None/missing_started_at case, never written to disk at all. Automations that count runs or key off the finished status double-fire and mis-report; the run's real record can be silently absent while the slot reads 'completed'.

title: The vacuum-state busy branch is unreachable for every HA-standard vacuum state — an errored or externally-cleaning robot classifies as "ready" and Start dispatches at it
observed_behavior: The final busy check is `if vacuum_state_n not in {"", "docked", "idle", "paused"} and vacuum_state_n not in active_vacuum_states`. `active_vacuum_states` defaults to `_HA_ACTIVE_VACUUM_STATES` = {cleaning, returning, paused, error} (job_monitor.py:10-15). The HA vacuum platform's activity enum has exactly six values — cleaning, docked, idle, paused, returning, error — and `_norm()` folds unavailable/unknown to "". The union of the two exemption sets therefore covers EVERY state the entity can report, so this branch can never fire in production; the same set is used at line 200 as EVIDENCE OF ACTIVITY and at line 217 as an EXEMPTION FROM BUSY, meaning the exact states it exists to catch are the ones it lets through. Because line 197's `active_cleaning_target` / active-state test is gated behind `active_job_exists`, the only remaining defence for an UNTRACKED run is line 209 (`task_status_n in active_run_task_states`). Roborock's `ACTIVE_RUN_TASK_STATES` (adapters/roborock/vocabulary.py:16-26) contains no "error", "paused" or "idle", and that module's own docstring records `error` (plus `bumper_stuck` / `wheels_suspended`) as live-observed `sensor.ivy_status` values. So: robot stuck mid-floor after an app-started run -> vacuum.ivy="error", sensor.ivy_status="error", no framework-tracked job -> line 180/188 skipped (Roborock declares hard_service_states=[] and drying_states=[]), line 197 skipped (no active job), line 209 skipped, line 217 exempted -> returns lifecycle_state="ready", message "Ready to start cleaning.", blocking=False. The same falls out for vacuum_state="paused" on either brand ("paused" sits in BOTH exemption sets, and Eufy's ACTIVE_RUN_TASK_STATES has no "paused").
user_impact: The card shows "Ready to start cleaning." and an enabled Start button while the robot is sitting on the floor in an error/stuck state or paused mid-run. Pressing Start passes the only start gate and dispatches a real clean command (app_segment_clean / room clean) at a robot that is faulted or already mid-run, on top of a run the framework is not tracking.

title: invalid_payload uses phase 0's room count as the whole run's room count — a saved run profile whose first step is a zone is accepted on save but can never start
observed_behavior: `if int(payload_room_count or 0) <= 0: return {"reason": "invalid_payload", ...}`. The caller passes `payload_room_count=int(payload_state.get("room_count", 0))` (core/manager.py:2863) where `payload_state = start_plan["payload_state"]`, and for a STEPPED run `_build_effective_start_plan` sets `payload_state = phases[0]` (planning/run_plan.py:1379). `_build_steps_phases` pops leading/trailing break phases, but `_BREAKS = ("charge_wait", "wait")` only (planning/run_plan.py:883-887) — a `zone` phase is deliberately NOT a break ("A zone is a real clean phase", line 895) and is emitted with `"payload": {}, "room_count": 0` (line 873-879). So for a profile whose steps are [zone, room_group], phases[0] is the zone phase, payload_room_count == 0, and build_start_blocker_from_lifecycle returns blocked=True / "Room-clean payload is missing or invalid." before it ever looks at the lifecycle state. `set_run_profile_steps` accepts this profile: its only structural guard is `if not any(s.get("type") == "room_group" for s in normalized)` (profiles/manager.py:1015) — it requires a room_group to EXIST, not to come first, and `normalize_run_profile_steps` (profiles/manager.py:798-808) accepts a zone step in any position. The phase runner explicitly expects this shape: `_snapshot_zone_timing`'s docstring says the start is "the run start for a leading zone" (jobs/phase_runner.py:341). start_run_profile then deletes the stashed steps because the run did not start (profiles/manager.py:1341-1345), so the next plain Start is a flat clean.
user_impact: A user saves a run profile like "clean the hallway zone first, then the bedrooms", presses its exposed button, and gets "Room-clean payload is missing or invalid." every time, with rooms visibly selected and a valid queue. Nothing names the real cause (the step ordering); the profile is permanently unstartable and the only fix is reordering steps the UI never said were order-constrained.

title: _phase_room_timing computes a naive last-minus-first over a slice whose leading samples belong to the previous phase, and silently clamps the garbage to zero
observed_behavior: _phase_room_timing derives the phase figures as `area = max(0.0, cas[-1]-cas[0])` and `secs = int(max(0.0, cts[-1]-cts[0]))`, justified by a docstring claiming cleaning_time/cleaning_area are 'CUMULATIVE across the run'. counter_segmentation.py:151-158 contradicts that for the same data — it explicitly windows samples 'after the LAST cleaning_time reset to 0, dropping any stale pre-reset sample carried over from the previous job', i.e. the counters DO reset when a new clean is dispatched, and each phase is a separate device clean. The phase path does no reset detection at all. Compounding it, the slice boundary is `s['t'] > start_t` where start_t is the previous phase's _timing_end_t, stamped at the completion hook — but listeners/job_metrics.py's own header documents that the counter sensors land on a DIFFERENT DPS packet that can arrive after the completion packet. So the finishing room's final counter values routinely land in the NEXT phase's slice as a high leading value, after which the reset to 0 makes cas[-1]-cas[0] and cts[-1]-cts[0] negative. Both are clamped to 0 rather than detected: cleaning_seconds is recorded as 0, and area_m2 falls to 0 and then to the learned-area fabrication of REC-6. cleaning_wall_seconds (from the timestamps) survives, which is why the corruption is not obvious.
user_impact: A phase whose slice starts with a stale pre-reset sample records cleaning_seconds = 0 and a fabricated area for that room, and the phase before it loses the tail of its own cleaning rise — with transit_capture_valid still True, so the record presents as fully and validly captured. The failure is order-of-arrival dependent, so the same run can be recorded correctly one day and zeroed the next with nothing distinguishing them.
guards_checked: the max(0.0, ...) clamps at :451-452 (they convert a detectable negative into a plausible zero — the opposite of a guard); the `usable >= 2` gate (:306-313, counts samples carrying a counter, not whether they belong to this phase); the area fallback (:316-325, masks the area but leaves cleaning_seconds at 0); _wall_seconds (:415-425, timestamp-based so unaffected — which is what hides the problem); counter_segmentation's _Window reset handling (:151-158, the correct treatment, deliberately not reused here); lexical slice compare `str(s['t']) > start_t` (safe — timestamp_utils.utc_now_iso is fixed-width, microsecond=0, Z-suffixed).

confirmations: CONFIRMED as a real contradiction with a real trigger. phase_runner.py:451-452 computes `max(0.0, cas[-1]-cas[0])` and `int(max(0.0, cts[-1]-cts[0]))` on the docstring's claim (:430-434) that the counters are 'CUMULATIVE across the run'. counter_segmentation.py:151-158 contradicts that for the same stream — it explicitly windows to `norm[reset_i:]` after the LAST cleaning_time reset to 0, 'dropping any stale pre-reset sample carried over from the previous job' — and the phase path does no reset detection at all. The slice-boundary race is documented in the producer: listeners/job_metrics.py:1-8 states outright that the counter sensors ride a separate DPS packet that 'may arrive before the sensor values have landed', i.e. the finishing room's final counter values can land after the completion packet and therefore after _timing_end_t, seeding the NEXT phase's slice with a high pre-reset value. The clamps then convert a detectable negative into a plausible zero: cleaning_seconds records 0 and area falls to 0 and on into REC-6's fabrication, while _wall_seconds (:416-425, timestamp-based) survives and hides it. MEDIUM is right — order-of-arrival dependent, non-deterministic, silently degrading rather than user-visible.
killed_by: KILLED — the load-bearing premise is not established from source. The corruption requires cleaning_time/cleaning_area to RESET at a PHASE boundary; the finder's sole evidence is counter_segmentation._prepare_window, which I read (:150-158): its comment and code window after the last reset 'carried over from the PREVIOUS JOB', i.e. a job-to-job reset, not a phase boundary. Nothing in the phase path, the adapters, or the listener establishes that a re-dispatched app_segment_clean/room_clean within one run zeroes the counters — and _phase_room_timing's docstring asserting they are run-cumulative is therefore not contradicted by the cited code. Without a per-phase reset the boundary slip the finder describes is benign: a stale leading sample only makes the next phase's last-minus-first slightly small and the previous phase's slightly short, with no negative to clamp and no zeroed cleaning_seconds. Also note the knock-on claim ('area falls to 0 and then to the learned-area fabrication of REC-6') fails independently — that fallback is dead code (see REC-6).

title: slugify_room_name has no uniqueness guarantee and nothing enforces one — two rooms can share a slug, and on Roborock the second one dispatches to the FIRST one's segment id
area: ID- (Area 1: room identity across namespaces — slugify, room_discovery, room_id/slug/stored-key)
observed_behavior: slugify_room_name (rooms/utils.py:35) deletes ' and ", maps & -> "and", and space -> "_". I executed it on real inputs: 'Bedroom'/'Bedroom' -> 'bedroom'; 'Bed & Bath'/'Bed and Bath' -> 'bed_and_bath'; 'Kids Room'/'Kids_Room' -> 'kids_room'; "Cat's Room"/'Cats Room' -> 'cats_room'; '"Guest" Room'/'Guest Room' -> 'guest_room'. The docstring at rooms/utils.py:16-18 CLAIMS the invariant 'distinct names must yield distinct slugs' — the code does not have it, and no caller enforces it. discover_rooms_for_vacuum dedupes ONLY by numeric room_id (seen_room_ids, room_discovery.py:223/240) and then stamps 'slug': slugify_room_name(name) at :254 with no collision check, so both rooms are emitted with the same slug. Two consequences, both silent: (1) WRONG PHYSICAL ROOM on Roborock — dispatch/manager.py:285-291 builds slug_to_live_id first-wins ('if not slug or slug in slug_to_live_id: continue'), so the colliding room's live id is never registered; at :306 the second room's target slug resolves to the FIRST room's live segment id, is appended to new_segments, and dispatched. The 'dropped' warning path at :310 is NOT reached because the lookup succeeds, so there is no log line at all. Selecting both rooms yields new_segments=[16,16]. (2) STORED DATA DESTROYED on both brands — plan_migration (reconciliation.py:178-179, 210) builds existing_by_slug with setdefault (first-wins); on a confirmed migrate both discovered rooms resolve to the SAME source dict and both get carried with identical durable settings (profile, floor_type, grants_access_to, rules, color), while the second stored room's config is overwritten and is NOT reported in 'dropped' (dropped is derived from existing_by_slug at :247-251, which never contained it). Room attribution during a run is also first-wins by slug (jobs/active_job.py:1158-1164).
user_impact: A user with two rooms whose names collide under slugify (two 'Bedroom's, or 'Bed & Bath' vs 'Bed and Bath') selects room B and the robot cleans room A instead, with no warning in the log and no error in the UI. On a confirmed re-map, room B's per-room settings, access grants and rules are permanently replaced by room A's and never listed as dropped.
guards_checked: rooms/utils.py:35 slugify (no disambiguation, no uniqueness); room_discovery.py:223+240 seen_room_ids (int room_id only, never slug); room_discovery.py:245-248 name non-empty check (does not check slug uniqueness); room_manager.build_managed_rooms:57-116 (keys by room_id, no slug check); reconciliation.py:84 and :179 existing_by_slug.setdefault (first-wins, silent); reconciliation.py:91-95 discovered_slugs guard (guards the renamed/id_changed contradiction only, not collisions); dispatch/manager.py:288 (first-wins) and :312-316 dropped-warning (not reached on a collision); maps/map_manager.rebuild_map_bucket:176-180 (slug=room.get('slug'), no check). title: discover_rooms_for_vacuum's single-map fallback serves ANOTHER map's room list and relabels it with the REQUESTED map_id, defeating the map_id filter at both room writers
area: ID- (Area 1: room identity across namespaces — slugify, room_discovery, room_id/slug/stored-key)
observed_behavior: For service_response brands (Roborock), room_discovery.py:174-180 does 'segments = per_map.get(str(resolved_map_id))' and, when that misses, 'if segments is None and len(per_map) == 1: segments = next(iter(per_map.values()))' — it takes whatever single map is cached WITHOUT checking that it is the map that was asked for. Every room built from those segments is then stamped '"map_id": str(resolved_map_id)' at :251 — the REQUESTED id, not the source cache key. That relabelling defeats the only guard the write path has: room_crud.save_managed_rooms:239-241 and rebuild_map:418-420 filter 'str(room.get("map_id")) == str(map_id)', which can never fail because the label was applied from the request. save_managed_rooms:261 then does 'map_bucket["rooms"] = managed_rooms' — a wholesale replacement of the real map's stored rooms with the other map's rooms. Reaching len(per_map)==1 with two real maps is concrete: source_refresh.flatten_maps_response:205 writes 'out[map_name] = seg_list', so two maps that resolve to the SAME key (both unnamed with the same 'flag', or both renamed to the same name in the app) collapse to one entry with no warning; and async_refresh_room_source:249-254/264-272 swallows every failure and leaves the PREVIOUS cache in place, so a cache captured when the user had one map survives after a second map is added. The same mislabelled list also feeds dispatch/manager.py:282-291, where slug_to_live_id is then built from the wrong floor's segments.
user_impact: On a multi-map (multi-floor) Roborock, importing or re-saving one floor writes the OTHER floor's rooms into that floor's bucket, destroying its stored per-room settings; and a live-id dispatch resolves 'bedroom' to the other floor's segment id, so the robot cleans the wrong floor's room. No error is surfaced — the map_id on every room looks correct because it was stamped from the request.
guards_checked: room_crud.save_managed_rooms:239-241 map_id filter and rebuild_map:418-420 map_id filter (both defeated by the :251 relabel); room_crud.reconcile_room:145-154 'no_discovery' guard (only protects against an EMPTY discovery, not a wrong-map one); source_refresh.flatten_maps_response:183-188 map-name fallback (only special-cases len(maps)==1, does not prevent key collapse at :205); source_refresh.async_refresh_room_source:249-254 unavailable-skip and :264-272 exception swallow (both leave the stale cache); room_discovery.py:181-187 'not isinstance(segments, list)' check (passes — the substituted list is a valid list); dispatch/manager.py:295-300 no-live-source fallback (not reached, slug_to_live_id is non-empty).

confirmations: Mechanism CONFIRMED in source: room_discovery.py:176-180 takes `next(iter(per_map.values()))` with no check that the single cached key is the requested map, and :252 stamps `"map_id": str(resolved_map_id)` from the REQUEST — which does defeat the only guards on the write path (room_crud.py:239-241 and :418-420 both compare str(room['map_id']) == str(map_id)). save_managed_rooms:261 is an unconditional wholesale assignment, verified. title: remove_map leaves the map's saved run-profile library, queue state and onboarding state behind; re-importing the same map_id resurrects run profiles holding room ids from the deleted segmentation
observed_behavior: The docstring claims remove_map removes "one imported map and all associated integration data", but the body (lines 359-388) touches exactly five buckets: maps, discovery, room_history, room_rule_status, active_jobs. At least three other per-vacuum/per-map stores survive: `data["run_profiles"][vac][map_id]` (profiles/manager.py:714-717), `data["queue"][vac][map_id]` (core/manager.py:1479-1481) and `data["onboarding"][vac][map_id]` (onboarding/manager.py:63-74). Map ids are stable for a given physical map on both brands, so the natural remediation flow — delete the badly-segmented map, re-import it — reuses the same map_id and the orphaned run-profile library reappears intact. Each saved run profile stores a room snapshot of `{room_id, name, profile_name, ...}` (profiles/manager.py:720-733) with NO slug, and `get_saved_run_profiles` renders the label from the profile's OWN stored names (profiles/manager.py:735-749, 881-921) — never cross-checked against the current room set. `apply_run_profile` (profiles/manager.py:1200-1243) then disables all rooms and re-enables strictly by stored `room_id`; an id that still exists is silently accepted, only a wholly absent id lands in `missing_room_ids`, and the method proceeds either way.
user_impact: The user deletes a map precisely to discard its stale room identities, re-imports, and their saved run profiles are still listed showing the old room NAMES ("Kitchen, Den") while the ids underneath now address whatever rooms occupy those segment numbers after re-segmentation. Starting the profile enables and dispatches the wrong physical rooms, and additionally overwrites those rooms' fan speed, water level, passes and order with the dead room's settings. title: No in-flight coalescing or lock on the refresh: triggers spawn unbounded concurrent get_maps cloud calls, and an older response landing last becomes the resident cached snapshot — including one that started before a map switch and lands after it
observed_behavior: There is no lock, no in-flight future, and no debounce anywhere in this module (grepped: no Lock/asyncio primitives). listeners/discovery.py:80-93 fires `hass.async_create_task(_do())` per trigger with no coalescing, and Roborock declares three triggers (adapter.py:453-457) plus a 6h periodic default; vacuum_docked and active_map_changed routinely fire together when a robot docks and the map reloads. dispatch/manager.py:281 adds a fourth concurrent caller. Each task independently awaits `roborock.get_maps` — a cloud call — so N triggers make N cloud calls, and a rate-limited/timed-out call is precisely the input that produces SRC-1's silent stale serve. Separately, because line 280's write is unconditional last-writer-wins, a refresh that STARTED earlier and finishes later overwrites a newer snapshot; that older snapshot then stays resident until the next trigger. The map-switch variant is worse than a plain revert: `_active_map_id_from_config` is evaluated at line 278, i.e. AFTER the await returns, so a refresh whose get_maps response was captured BEFORE a map switch is keyed using the POST-switch active map name in the len(maps)==1 branch (line 183) — the old map's rooms are cached under the new map's name.
user_impact: Redundant cloud calls raise the probability of the get_maps failure that triggers SRC-1's wrong-room dispatch. When a pre-switch response wins the race, the cache holds the previous map's segment ids under the current map's key, which a later dispatch resolves as live.

title: The room-source cache is never invalidated — not on config-entry unload/reload, not on map switch, not when a vacuum is unmanaged — and it keeps hass.data[DOMAIN] alive so the unload cleanup never fires
observed_behavior: set_cached_room_source writes into hass.data[DOMAIN]['room_source_cache'][entity_id] and nothing ever removes it. __init__.py:465-546 async_unload_entry pops mapping_tracker, DATA_BATTERY, DATA_ERROR_TRACKER, DATA_ADAPTER_COORDINATOR, DATA_RUNTIME, DATA_LEARNING and the panel lists — DATA_ROOM_SOURCE_CACHE is not among them. Two consequences. (1) The cache survives every reload, so at the exact moment the user changes configuration and reloads, discovery starts from an arbitrarily old snapshot; the reload-time refresh (config_entry_reload -> async_at_started, listeners/discovery.py:106-114) is precisely the one most likely to hit the unavailable-entity skip at source_refresh.py:249, because the Roborock integration is often still materialising its entities — and per SRC-1 that skip is indistinguishable from success, so the stale snapshot is served as live. (2) The lingering key makes `domain_data` non-empty, so `if not domain_data: hass.data.pop(DOMAIN, None)` at __init__.py:545-546 never executes — the DOMAIN slot leaks past unload, along with segment data for vacuums no longer managed or since renamed. There is also no invalidation on active-map change: the listener triggers a REFRESH but nothing clears the prior entry first, so a failed post-switch refresh leaves the pre-switch map's segments resident and readable.
user_impact: Right after a reload — the moment the user is most likely to be reconfiguring rooms — discovery and dispatch can resolve against a snapshot from before the reload with no indication of its age. Stale entries for removed/renamed vacuums persist for the life of the HA process and defeat the DOMAIN-slot cleanup.

title: Mid-run reachability is queue-scoped while preflight is graph-scoped — a run that omits the dock room reports EVERY remaining room as access_blocked and can cancel the job
observed_behavior:
rooms/access_graph.py exports the EDGES (_build_room_access_views, :236-276) but never the reachability ANSWER, so each consumer re-implements traversal and they disagree.

Preflight (run_plan.py:1132-1148) computes accessibility over ALL managed rooms: seeds = {rid in all_rooms_by_id if not requires_map.get(rid)} then a fixpoint over requires_map with no membership filter. A room reachable only through an UNSELECTED transit room is therefore correctly accessible.

The mid-run sibling (run_plan.py:1615-1637) restricts the same computation to the queue: the seed comprehension iterates queue_room_ids only, and the propagation step filters parent_ids to `parent_id in queue_room_id_set` (:1628-1632). Critically the seed TEST still uses the GLOBAL requires_map (:1618), so a queued room whose parent is outside the queue is neither a seed nor reachable by propagation — it can never become accessible.

In a graph the validator calls valid, every non-dock room has exactly one inbound edge (access_graph.py:767-778 raises missing_dependency otherwise), so the ONLY room that can seed at :1615 is the dock room. Consequence: if the dock room is not enabled for this run, accessible_room_ids is empty and every remaining room falls into affected_remaining_rooms with reason 'access_blocked' and blocked_by_room_id=None (:1650-1672).

Worse, this fires with no blocker rule matching. The direct_blocked scan at :1570-1582 also walks queue_room_ids only, so blocker_rules_present stays False when the only blocker rule lives on an unqueued transit room — which disarms the bail-out at :1608-1613. listeners/path_blockers.py:196 subscribes to that rule's entity regardless, so any state change on it (:116 only rejects old_state == new_state) invokes the report.

Walked concretely: valid tree Dock(1)->Hall(2)->Bed(3), Dock flagged is_dock_room, a blocker rule on Hall watching binary_sensor.door. User enables only Bed. Preflight: seeds {1}, propagates to {1,2,3}, Bed included, job starts with queue_room_ids=[3]. Door sensor changes state (to ANY value). Runtime report: no structural issues, queue=[3], remaining=[3], direct_blocked={} (Hall not walked), blocker_rules_present=False, seeds={} because requires_map[3]==[2], propagation filters parent 2 out of the queue set -> accessible={} -> Bed reported access_blocked. listeners/path_blockers.py:143-157 then applies path_block_action verbatim: pause_and_event pauses the job, cancel_and_event cancels it and fires EVENT_JOB_FINISHED + EVENT_RUN_INCOMPLETE.
user_impact: A perfectly valid access graph plus a normal partial run (user cleans the bedroom, not the entryway the dock sits in) turns any watched blocker entity's state change into a spurious 'path blocked' verdict on every unfinished room. With path_block_action=cancel_and_event the run is aborted mid-clean and the rooms are never cleaned; with pause_and_event the robot stops until the pause timeout. The event names no blocking room (blocked_by_room_id=None), so the user cannot diagnose it. On event_only it still fires a false EVENT_PATH_BLOCKED that user automations act on.
guards_checked: run_plan.py:1536-1538 — the _structural_access_graph_issues early return only covers self_reference/duplicate_edge/cycle_detected/multiple_inbound/multiple_dock_rooms (access_graph.py:836-844); the scenario graph is fully VALID so nothing is returned. run_plan.py:1608-1613 — the 'blocker rules but no grants' bail needs blocker_rules_present, which :1570-1582 only sets from QUEUE rooms, so it is False here; even when True, grants exist so the `not any(...)` half is False. run_plan.py:1545-1546 and 1556-1558 — queue and remaining are both non-empty. run_plan.py:1691-1692 — the sha1 signature dedupe only suppresses REPEATS of the identical bogus report, not the first one. access_graph.py:266-274 — _build_room_access_views does requires_map.setdefault(room_id, []) for every valid room, so requires_map.get() returns [] (falsy) only for true graph roots; a queued non-root is never seeded. listeners/path_blockers.py:114-118 — entity_id membership and old_state==new_state are the only pre-filters; a genuine state change passes. listeners/path_blockers.py:143-157 — pause/cancel act on the report with no re-verification against the preflight answer. core/manager.py:4943 start gate is irrelevant, the job already started legitimately.

confirmations: CONFIRMED line by line — the sharpest finding in this batch. Preflight (run_plan.py ~1553) seeds from all_rooms_by_id with an unfiltered requires_map. get_runtime_path_block_report seeds from queue_room_ids while still testing the GLOBAL requires_map, and its propagation filters parent_ids to `parent_id in queue_room_id_set` — so a queued room whose parent is outside the queue is neither seeded nor reachable, permanently. _validate_room_access_graph raises missing_dependency for every non-dock room with no inbound edge, so in any graph the validator calls valid only the dock room can seed. I verified the bail-out at :1608-1613 is disarmed exactly as claimed: blocker_rules_present is set only while walking queue_room_ids, so a rule on an unqueued transit room leaves it False. And I read listeners/path_blockers.register: watch_map is built from every room on every map regardless of enabled/queue state, so the rule entity IS subscribed. blocked_by_room_id is None because parent_ids is empty after the queue filter. pause/cancel act on the report with no re-verification.

Reproduced line by line. Preflight (run_plan.py:1132-1148) seeds from all_rooms_by_id over the global requires_map; the mid-run sibling (:1615-1637) seeds from queue_room_ids while still testing the GLOBAL requires_map and filters propagation parents to queue_room_id_set, so a queued room whose only parent is unqueued can never become accessible. In any graph the validator accepts, every non-dock room has exactly one inbound edge (:767-778), so only the dock room can seed — with Dock(1)->Hall(2)->Bed(3) and only Bed queued, accessible={} and Bed is reported access_blocked with blocked_by_room_id=None.
