title: _access_graph_state fails OPEN to 'blank', so a numeric-slot rebuild that wipes the access graph, dock flag and blocker rules leaves the next run silently unconstrained
observed_behavior:
_access_graph_state's first branch is `if not has_dock and not has_grants: return 'blank'` (:864-873), and 'blank' is the ALLOW state — run_plan.py:983-994 only blocks blank when rules also exist (`graph_state == 'blank' and any_rules`). The state is therefore indistinguishable between 'user never configured a graph' and 'the graph was just erased', and the fallback is permissive.

Erasure is reachable through the shipped rebuild_map service. rebuild_map_bucket (maps/map_manager.py:144-199) matches previous settings by NUMERIC SLOT only: `previous = existing_rooms.get(room_id_key, {})` (:148), then :192-195 take is_dock_room, grants_access_to and rules from that `previous`. When a re-segment renumbers ids — the shipped Roborock identity behaviour, where segment ids renumber and identity is the name slug — every discovered id misses its previous entry, so every room is rebuilt with is_dock_room=False, grants_access_to=[] and rules=[] at once. has_dock and has_grants both go False, _access_graph_state returns 'blank', any_rules is also False (the rules went with them), and the next run proceeds with no access constraints and no blocker rules, with no warning anywhere.

The integration already has the correct implementation for this exact situation and does not use it here: rooms/reconciliation.py::plan_migration matches by slug with an id-collision guard (:186-215) and explicitly rewrites grants_access_to through the old->new id remap, dropping only targets that no longer resolve (:230-245). rooms/room_crud.py exposes both — reconcile_room (:81-215) uses plan_migration, rebuild_map (:403-428) uses the numeric-slot rebuild_map_bucket — so which of the two the user happens to invoke decides whether their access graph and blocker rules survive.
user_impact: A Roborock user who re-segments and then uses Rebuild map (rather than the reconcile/re-map flow) loses the dock room, every access link and every blocker rule in one silent step, and the very next run cleans everything selected with none of those gates applied — including a room the user had gated behind a blocker rule such as 'do not enter while the baby is asleep'. Nothing reports the loss: the graph simply reads as never-configured. Eufy is exposed on the narrower case where a re-map merges or drops rooms and frees their ids.
guards_checked: access_graph.py:874-876 — the only other branch requires `validation is not None`; the blank return at :873 short-circuits before validation is ever consulted, so a wiped graph is never validated. run_plan.py:989-994 — the blank+rules block is the sole guard on blank, and rebuild wipes rules in the same pass (map_manager.py:167 `_prev_rules = previous.get('rules')` with previous={}), so it cannot fire. maps/map_manager.py:154-165 — the comment there explains the approval-flag divergence and asserts the RoomConfig build keeps writers in sync, but says nothing about and does nothing for graph edges; the code carries them by slot regardless. rooms/room_crud.py:411-420 — rebuild_map filters discovery by map_id only; no slug matching and no id_remap is computed on this path. rooms/reconciliation.py:230-245 — verified correct, and verified NOT reachable from rebuild_map. core/manager.py:1374-1379 — update_room_fields validation only guards writes made through that method; the rebuild writes map_bucket['rooms'] directly.

confirmations: The fail-open half is confirmed: _access_graph_state returns 'blank' before validation is ever consulted (access_graph.py:864-873) and blank is the ALLOW state unless rules exist (run_plan.py:983-994), and rebuild_map_bucket does carry is_dock_room/grants_access_to/rules by numeric slot only (map_manager.py:148, 192-195) so a full renumber erases all three at once. But the stated trigger does not exist: rebuild_map has NO service registration and no card caller — I grepped services/*.py, services.yaml and src/ — which the sibling finding A3-CRUD-6 itself concedes. The reachable equivalent is save_managed_rooms invoked without enabled_room_ids after a renumber, where the same id-keyed lookup in build_managed_rooms (room_manager.py:64, 107-110) yields grants=[]/rules=[]/dock=False for every room and drops the graph to 'blank'. Real with a corrected trigger; conditions are narrow. MEDIUM.
killed_by: REFUTED on reachability. The finding's stated trigger — 'reachable through the shipped rebuild_map service' — does not exist. I enumerated every key in custom_components/eufy_vacuum/services.yaml and grepped the whole tree: there is no rebuild_map service, no repair flow and no card action; rebuild_map_bucket's only caller is RoomMapManager.rebuild_map, whose only caller is EufyVacuumManager.rebuild_map, which nothing invokes. observed_behavior: Every in-memory read the coordinator performs for the Eufy backend locates its data with `_msr.eufy_inmem_candidates(self._manager.hass, mem_cfg)` — a function whose ONLY inputs are `hass` and `{hass_data_domain: 'robovac_mqtt', mapdata_attrs: [...]}`. It returns (map_source_runtime.py:839-858) `('hass_data', 'robovac_mqtt', hass.data['robovac_mqtt'])` FIRST, then each config entry's runtime_data. `eufy_mapdata_obj_from_candidates` (runtime:957-968) then runs `_walk(root, _holds_mapdata)` — a bounded BFS whose predicate (runtime:949-955) is 'any object exposing `_map_data` whose `room_pixels` is bytes' — and returns the FIRST hit. hass.data['robovac_mqtt'] is the WHOLE domain bucket; per this repo's own adapter comment (adapters/eufy/adapter.py:650) it is `{<entry>: {'coordinators': [EufyCleanCoordinator, ...]}}`, a LIST of robots. Five coordinator entry points inherit this: `_refresh_eufy_map_source` (line 397 -> static rooms + image_size + hazards), `_read_inmem_pose` (line 461 -> robot/dock/trail), `get_live_mapdata_obj` (line 361), `async_get_map_render_data` (line 645 -> the raster the card DRAWS), `async_get_map_data_dict` (line 689 -> the raster `zone_membership`/`current_room_for_pixel` consume). title: Sticky last-known-good hold re-serves a frozen current_room/robot_anchor as `present: True`; the `stale` flag it sets has NO consumer, so a docked Roborock reports a phantom room for up to 6 hours
observed_behavior: `_commit_result` lines 105-134: when a new result is absent and the reason is not in `_MAP_SOURCE_HARD_CLEAR_REASONS`, it re-publishes the previous result as `held = dict(cached_res)` with `stale=True/stale_since/stale_reason` added — but `held['present']` stays True and every moving field (`current_room`, `robot_anchor`, `dock_anchor`, `path`, `robot_heading`) is carried over verbatim, frozen. For Roborock this is the NORMAL docked state, not an edge case: per .claude/notes/reference_map_source_lifecycle.md the parsed MapData lives only in HA memory and is nulled when the vacuum idles/docks, so `roborock_result_from_candidates` emits `no_parsed_map` — deliberately excluded from the hard-clear set (coordinator:50-55) so it ALWAYS holds. title: The storage-path mtime cache early-return omits the `map_id` check its sibling `_commit_result` performs, so map A's geometry is returned as map B's answer with `present: True`
observed_behavior: `_refresh_storage_map_source` lines 257-266 reuses the cached result when `mtime` and `present_gate` match, and returns `cached['result']` directly. It never compares `cached.get('map_id')` to the `map_id` it was called with, and it never re-commits — so the cache entry keeps whatever map_id was stamped last. That is precisely the check `_commit_result` performs 140 lines earlier at line 117, annotated `# never serve another map's geometry`. The bypass is reachable because nothing in the Eufy source is map-scoped: `eufy_store_path` resolves ONE file per DEVICE (`.storage/robovac_mqtt.<serial>`) holding whatever map is current, and the presence gate `camera.{object_id}_map` (adapters/eufy/adapter.py:618) contains no {map_slug}, so `present` is identical across maps. The store lags by the fork's save-throttle — documented in this repo at adapters/eufy/adapter.py:645-648 ('The .storage robot position ... lags the fork's save-throttle'). So after a map switch the active-map select flips to B immediately while the store file is still map A with an UNCHANGED mtime: `mtime is not None and cached['mtime'] == mtime and cached['present_gate'] == present` all hold, and map A's rooms are returned as the answer for map B with `present: True` and no `stale` marker. Neither consumer can detect it: core/manager.py:4197 and sensor/map_overlays.py:52 both read `entry['result']` and never look at `entry['map_id']`.
user_impact: For the window between a map switch and the fork's next store write, the card's room bboxes, the map-tap room resolution (`deviceRoomIdAtContentPct`) and the map_overlays sensor all describe the PREVIOUS floor's rooms while the backdrop shows the new one — a tap resolves to the old map's room number and dispatches a clean of the wrong room, with no error and no staleness indication. Narrower than LC-1: for Eufy this branch is only the fallback (`_refresh_eufy_map_source` is memory-primary and its `_mem_rooms_cache` is keyed by a content sha1, which IS correct), so it is reachable on installs whose fork exposes no in-memory `_map_data` (legacy builds, other forks, post-#136 attr drift) or during the startup window before the coordinator populates it.
guards_checked: `_commit_result` line 117 — the sibling map_id guard that exists and is bypassed here. `present_gate` (line 263) — real, but map-independent for Eufy since the camera pattern has no {map_slug}, so it never differs between maps. `store_version` (line 269) guards the wrapper schema, not the map. `_compute_map_frame_gate` (core/manager.py:4275-4336) does NOT rescue this: it gates zone-draw/map-tap on the ROBOT re-localizing, its docstring explicitly assumes 'the raster + room list update immediately' (the exact assumption that fails here), and it is surfaced only through `_resolve_map_switcher`, which returns None when the fork's `*_map_select` entity is absent. Consumers core/manager.py:4197 and sensor/map_overlays.py:50-55 read the result with no map_id comparison.

confirmations: CONFIRMED. _refresh_storage_map_source:260-266 returns cached['result'] on mtime+present_gate match and never compares cached['map_id'] to the map_id argument, nor re-commits — bypassing the guard _commit_result:117 applies with the comment 'never serve another map's geometry'. The bypass is genuinely reachable: eufy_store_path resolves ONE file per DEVICE, and the Eufy live_map_image_entity_pattern is 'camera.{object_id}_map' (adapter.py:618) with no {map_slug}, so present_gate is identical across maps. title: The same mtime early-return skips `_apply_inmem_pose_to_result`, freezing the robot/dock/current_room/path overlays for as long as the store file is unchanged
observed_behavior: On a full read `_refresh_storage_map_source` calls `_apply_inmem_pose_to_result` at line 285 to make the fork's fresh in-memory pose AUTHORITATIVE over the moving fields (`apply_live_pose_override` clears stale current_room/path first). The mtime early-return at line 266 returns `cached['result']` and never calls it — so the moving overlays are served frozen at the timestamp of the last full parse. Because the store is save-throttled, an unchanged mtime is the COMMON case, not the rare one: the cache hit is the design goal ('an unchanged map costs one stat, not a 200 KB parse'), and it silently drags the pose along with the static segmentation. The memory branch demonstrates the correct pattern in the same file: `_refresh_eufy_map_source` caches only the STATIC scan (`_mem_rooms_cache`), shallow-copies it (line 440) and re-layers a fresh pose every call (line 441) — 'the pose changes every refresh; the static rooms scan does not'. The storage branch caches the whole result including the moving fields. `live_pose` and `memory` are independent adapter blocks, so an install where the fork exposes `_robot_pixel` but not `_map_data` gets the storage branch with a working live pose that is applied only on the rare ticks where the file changed.
user_impact: The map_overlays sensor's state (current room) and its `robot_anchor`/`dock_anchor`/`robot_heading` attributes stop advancing while the robot is cleaning — they only step forward when the fork happens to flush its Store — so the recorded room-over-time history for these installs shows the robot jumping between rooms at save-throttle granularity instead of tracking the run. Not user-visible on the card, which is rescued by the separate ~2s `get_map_live_pose` poll that `mapOverlayData()` (src/state/map.js:1055-1070) folds over the snapshot; the sensor has no such rescue because it reads only `_map_state_source_cache`.

title: `_commit_result` is blind last-writer-wins across the storage path's two executor awaits — a refresh started before a map switch can commit after a newer one
observed_behavior: Two independent triggers call `async_refresh_map_state_source` for the same vacuum with no serialization: the sensor platform's 60s timer (sensor/__init__.py:457) and EVERY dashboard-snapshot service call (services/snapshots.py:62). The memory-hit path is safe — `_refresh_eufy_map_source` contains no `await` between locating the MapData and `_commit_result`, so under HA's single event loop it is atomic. The storage path is not: `_refresh_storage_map_source` awaits `async_add_executor_job(_stat_mtime)` (line 251) and `async_add_executor_job(load_store_json)` (line 268), and `async_get_map_data_dict`/`async_get_map_render_data` await the same load. Across those gaps another refresh can complete end-to-end. `_commit_result`'s present branch (line 136) then overwrites unconditionally — there is no sequence number, generation token or per-vacuum lock, and the only map guard (line 117) sits on the ABSENT branch. So refresh#1 (map A, stat -> load -> slow) can commit AFTER refresh#2 (map B) finished, leaving the cache holding map A's result stamped map_id='A' while the active map is B.
user_impact: Until the next tick (up to 60s, sooner if the card is polling), the snapshot and the map_overlays sensor serve the previous map's rooms/anchors under the new map — and since neither consumer compares `entry['map_id']` to the map they are rendering, nothing flags it. Self-correcting: the next stat sees the newer mtime, mismatches the committed one, and re-reads. Rated LOW because the window is one executor round-trip and the wrong state is transient, but it is a real gap ACROSS an await, not a synchronous-block false positive.
guards_checked: Verified `_refresh_eufy_map_source`'s memory-hit path is await-free (lines 395-451: eufy_inmem_candidates, eufy_mapdata_obj_from_candidates, mapdata_dict_from_obj, eufy_result_from_mapdata, _apply_inmem_pose_to_result, _commit_result are all sync) so no finding is claimed there. `_commit_result` (78-137) has no lock, no generation counter, and its map_id comparison is only on the `not result.get('present')` branch. No asyncio.Lock or in-flight set exists anywhere in the coordinator or on the manager for this cache. Both call sites confirmed: sensor/__init__.py:433-471 (`async_track_time_interval`, 60s, plus an initial `hass.async_create_task`) and services/snapshots.py:54-68.

I re-read _refresh_eufy_map_source:395-451 and confirm the memory-hit path is await-free, so the finder correctly claims nothing there. Self-correcting on the next tick; LOW is right.

title: Live-pose room lookup projects a MEMORY-frame robot pixel through STORAGE-frame geometry (no memory fallback, no store_version guard) — feeds room attribution at 2 s
observed_behavior:
async_get_map_live_pose() reads the robot pixel from the fork's IN-MEMORY coordinator (_read_inmem_pose -> _robot_pixel, computed by the fork as (cur_pose - in-memory origin)/res) but resolves the geometry it normalizes against from _load_live_pose_geom(), which is .storage-ONLY (map_source_coordinator.py:476-498). Every other Eufy reader in this coordinator is memory-PRIMARY with a storage fallback (_refresh_eufy_map_source:397-435, async_get_map_data_dict:687-705, async_get_map_render_data:643-653); this one path is storage-only with no memory attempt. The pixel is then fed to current_room_for_pixel(map_data=STORAGE, px=MEMORY-frame) which subtracts the STORAGE ro_dx/ro_dy and indexes the STORAGE raster.

ARITHMETIC (real device numbers from .claude/notes/reference_eufy_intersession_coord_drift.md: origin=(-1367,-987), grid 360x300, res 5, outline origin +105 cells): stored map_data gives ro_dx = round((-842 - (-1367))/5) = 105. The device extends the map 1 m to the left; the fork's in-memory origin_x becomes -1467 while room_outline_origin_x stays -842, so the fork now computes px' = (pose + 1467)/5 = px + 20 and the correct offset is ro_dx' = round((-842 + 1467)/5) = 125, giving rx = px + 20 - 125 = rx_true. Using the LAGGED storage value the code computes rx = px + 20 - 105 = rx_true + 20 -> it reads the raster 20 cells = 20 x 5 cm = 1.00 m to the right of where the robot actually is, and returns the neighbouring room's id. 20 cells is far inside the raster, so the 0 <= rx < ro_w bound never fires.

Second failure mode on the same line: when the store file is missing/unreadable, _load_live_pose_geom returns None and the service returns {'present': False, 'reason': 'no_geom'}; pose_sampler.py:201 then returns None and SKIPS the tick — for the whole run — even though the in-memory map is fully usable and the card's snapshot path is serving it.

_load_live_pose_geom also never applies source_cfg['store_version'], unlike eufy_result_from_store (map_source_runtime.py:128), so after a fork schema bump the pre-warm hard-clears on store_version_mismatch while this path keeps reading and normalizing against whatever map_data shape is in the file.
user_impact: listeners/pose_sampler.py:197 is the per-tick (~2 s) sampler that produces `current_room` for per-room attribution. A wrong room id here is written into the run's room timeline and into learned history: the user sees 'cleaned the Living Room for 8 minutes' when the robot was in the Kitchen, with no error anywhere. In the missing-store case the run produces no per-room attribution at all while the map renders normally, so nothing signals that attribution silently stopped.
guards_checked: _load_live_pose_geom (map_source_coordinator.py:476-498) — only `isinstance(map_data, dict)`; the cache key is mtime alone; no version check and no memory attempt. async_get_map_live_pose (500-528) — `if not map_data: return no_geom` is a presence check only, nothing compares frames. current_room_for_pixel's `0 <= rx < ro_w and 0 <= ry < ro_h` bound (map_source.py:422) — a 20-cell error lands well inside a 300-cell raster, so it passes. _apply_inmem_pose_to_result (292-328) DOES hand the correct in-memory map_data on the snapshot path (_refresh_eufy_map_source:441-443) — the pose-sampler path bypasses it entirely. compare_map_data / `normalization_safe` (map_source.py:737-788) exists precisely to detect memory-vs-storage divergence but is reachable ONLY from the diagnostic compare service (grepped: manager.py:4403, mapping_services.py:2306) and is never consulted by any runtime decision. _is_parked (pose_sampler.py:203) only nulls the sample while docked. eufy_result_from_store's expected_version guard is on a different call path.

confirmations: CONFIRMED. async_get_map_live_pose:514-527 takes the robot pixel from _read_inmem_pose (the fork's in-memory _robot_pixel) but resolves geometry from _load_live_pose_geom:476-498, which is .storage-ONLY with no memory attempt — while _refresh_eufy_map_source:397, async_get_map_data_dict:687 and async_get_map_render_data:643 are all memory-PRIMARY. I verified in the fork that _pose_to_pixel (coordinator.py:541-550) computes px=round((x_cm - self._map_data.origin_x)/res) against the CURRENT in-memory map, so the pixel and the geometry genuinely come from different frames whenever the store lags a geometry change. current_room_for_pixel's 0<=rx<ro_w bound cannot catch an in-range offset error. Second failure mode also confirmed: no_geom -> pose.present False -> pose_sampler._read_live_pose_sample returns None and skips the tick (listeners/pose_sampler.py:197-202), silently ending per-room attribution while the card still renders. Duplicate of A5-POSE-1.

CONFIRMED, and it is the only asymmetric reader in the file. _read_inmem_pose (453-474) reads the fork's in-memory _robot_pixel, which the fork computes as round((x_cm - self._map_data.origin_x)/res) against the CURRENT in-memory map (robovac_mqtt/coordinator.py:546). _load_live_pose_geom (476-498) resolves eufy_store_path and returns the .storage map_data with NO memory attempt and NO store_version guard, while _refresh_eufy_map_source (397-443), async_get_map_render_data (643-653) and async_get_map_data_dict (687-705) are all memory-PRIMARY. live_pose_overlay then normalizes a memory-frame pixel against storage-frame width/height and indexes the storage raster via storage ro_dx/ro_dy. current_room_for_pixel's bound (map_source.py:422) only catches errors large enough to leave the raster. Consumer confirmed: listeners/pose_sampler.py:197 _read_live_pose_sample buffers pose['current_room'] per ~2s tick for run attribution. The 'no_geom -> skip the whole run' second mode is also real (coordinator 521-523).

title: zone_membership scans the entire room_outline raster with a per-cell normalize_rendered before the bbox reject, synchronously on the event loop — measured ~0.10 s per zone, ~1.0 s per dashboard read
observed_behavior:
The filing loop iterates all ro_h x ro_w cells and calls normalize_rendered(rx+ro_dx, ry+ro_dy, _w, _h) for EVERY cell (line 387) before applying the cheap bbox reject (line 388). normalize_rendered does two divisions, two clamps and two round(x,5) calls per cell. The zone's bbox is known up front (bx0..by1 at line 353) and could be inverted once to a pixel sub-rectangle, so the full scan is unnecessary.

Measured on this machine with the real device grid (360x300 = 108,000 cells, from the live X10 map in .claude/notes/reference_eufy_intersession_coord_drift.md): 0.1036 s per full scan, excluding the point_in_polygon ray-casts on cells that survive the bbox test.

Both callers are async service handlers running on the HA event loop with no executor hop: _handle_create_saved_zone (mapping_services.py:2506) does one scan per create, and _backfill_saved_zone_area (mapping_services.py:1458-1469, reached from the dashboard read at mapping_services.py:1276) loops over EVERY zone whose area_m2 is None. Eufy caps saved zones at 10, so the first dashboard read after an upgrade/import that leaves zones unsized costs 10 x 0.104 s ~= 1.0 s of blocked loop.
user_impact: On the first card load after zones exist without a stored area_m2, the whole Home Assistant event loop stalls for roughly a second — every other integration's updates, websocket pushes and service calls freeze with it. Drawing a new zone stalls it for ~0.1 s. Nothing logs; the user just sees the UI hitch.
guards_checked: _backfill_saved_zone_area's active-map guard (mapping_services.py:1447) only skips zones on a non-active map, it does not bound the scan. The `pending` filter (1433) returns early once every zone is sized, but the first read after zones are created/imported has them all pending. zone_membership's own bbox reject (line 388) runs AFTER the per-cell normalize_rendered, so it removes none of the cost. `_outline_geometry` returning None (line 370) short-circuits only when width/height/ro dims are missing. Eufy's capabilities.zone_max=10 bounds the loop at 10 iterations but does not avoid them. Neither caller wraps the call in hass.async_add_executor_job.

confirmations: Mechanism and measurement CONFIRMED. map_source.py:387 calls normalize_rendered for every one of ro_h*ro_w cells BEFORE the bbox reject at 388, and the zone bbox (353) is known up front. I reproduced the benchmark on this machine against the real live grid from Z:/.storage/robovac_mqtt.AFC96X0F33201054 (256x244=62,464 cells): 0.068 s per scan; at the finder's 360x300 it is 0.114 s — their 0.1036 s figure is accurate. Both callers verified on-loop with no executor hop (mapping_services.py:2506 create; :1460 backfill, reached from the dashboard read at :1277). DOWNGRADED to LOW: this is a bounded one-time ~0.7 s loop stall (backfill only runs while zones lack area_m2, and create-time sizing fills it), producing no wrong result — it does not meet this audit's MEDIUM bar of a user-visible wrong answer.

CONFIRMED AND MEASURED. I ran zone_membership against a synthetic 360x300 outline raster with the live device's geometry: 0.1053 s for one call on this machine. The loop at map_source.py:381-395 calls normalize_rendered for every one of ro_h*ro_w cells BEFORE the bbox reject at 388, so the reject removes none of the cost. On the user's real map (256x244 = 62,464 cells) it is ~0.06 s per zone; on a Pi-class HA host materially worse. Blocking-loop performance defect, not a wrongness defect — MEDIUM is right.

title: normalize_rendered CLAMPS out-of-grid pixels onto the map border instead of rejecting them, so off-grid raster cells and bad poses fold onto an edge rather than disappearing — diverging from the card's own decoder, which drops them
observed_behavior:
normalize_rendered applies _clamp01 to both axes and always returns a valid pair; there is no way for a caller to distinguish 'this point is at the left edge' from 'this point is 25 cells off the map'. Three in-scope callers feed it unvalidated pixel coordinates:

(a) rooms_from_room_pixels (line 302-303) and zone_membership (line 387) map outline cell (rx, ry) to main grid (rx+ro_dx, ry+ro_dy) with NO bounds check against width/height. With the live device's ro_dx = 105 (origin -1367, outline origin -842, res 5) and an outline raster 300 cells wide, cell rx=280 lands at px=385 on a 360-wide grid: _clamp01(385/360) = _clamp01(1.0694) = 1.0. Every such cell collapses onto nx = 1.0. In zone_membership that means all of them pass the bbox reject for any zone drawn to the right edge (bx1 = 1.0) and are then counted in the >=90% dominance vote; in rooms_from_room_pixels the affected room's bbox is stretched to exactly 1.0.

(b) vacuum_to_normalized (line 217) projects hazard layers with px = (vx - origin_x)/res and no plausibility gate. The fork demonstrably carries TWO coordinate frames (map/biz frame spanning X[-1367,433] vs the raw DPS-179 telemetry frame at ~16000 — proven in reference_eufy_intersession_coord_drift.md). If a schema shift delivers the raw frame, px = (16000+1367)/5 = 3473 on a 360-wide grid -> _clamp01(9.65) = 1.0. hazards_from_mapdata then emits a valid-looking polygon squashed flat against the right edge, because _normalize_vacuum_point returns a truthy list and the `if p0 and p1` / `if len(pts) >= 3` tests (lines 511, 521) all pass.

(c) live_pose_overlay (line 582) pins an out-of-frame robot pixel to a map corner instead of omitting robot_anchor.

The card's own decoder does NOT do this: src/bindings/map.js:281-284 iterates px over [0, W) and `continue`s when rx/ry fall outside the raster, so out-of-grid cells are simply never drawn. Python folds them onto the border; JS drops them. The two decoders of the same raster disagree.
user_impact: A room whose segmentation extends past the main grid gets a tap-region and label box pinned to the map edge. A saved zone drawn against the right edge can be filed to the wrong room because off-grid cells were swept into its dominance vote. A hazard layer read in the wrong frame renders as a plausible-looking stripe glued to the map border rather than not rendering at all — the failure looks like data instead of like an error.
guards_checked: normalize_rendered's only guard is `if width <= 0 or height <= 0: return [0.0, 0.0]` (line 189-190) — a dimension check, not a range check on px/py. _outline_geometry (220-245) validates that width/height/ro_w/ro_h are non-zero but never checks ro_w + ro_dx <= width or ro_h + ro_dy <= height. rooms_from_room_pixels' `0 < rid < _CATCH_ALL_RID` filter (line 286) filters room IDs, not coordinates. zone_membership's bbox reject (line 388) compares the ALREADY-clamped value, so it cannot reject on that basis. vacuum_to_normalized's type/dims guards (lines 205-214) reject non-numeric input and missing dims but nothing out-of-range. _numeric_pair (175-180) checks shape only. The card-side bounds check at src/bindings/map.js:281-284 and src/state/map.js:960 confirms the correct behaviour exists on the JS side and is absent here.

confirmations: Code property CONFIRMED: normalize_rendered:189-193 clamps with _clamp01 and always returns a valid pair; rooms_from_room_pixels:288/302-303 and zone_membership:387 map outline cells to the main grid with no bounds check; the card's decoder does the inverse direction and skips out-of-range cells (src/bindings/map.js:281-284, verified), so Python folds where JS drops. DOWNGRADED to LOW: no reachable trigger today. The live store has room_outline_origin == origin and room_outline_width/height == width/height (256x244, verified), so ro_dx=ro_dy=0 and no cell can leave the grid; sub-claim (a) is gated on the same nonzero-offset precondition as EXT-4. Sub-claim (b) (hazards delivered in the raw DPS-179 frame) is speculative — no shipped path produces it. Sub-claim (c) is reachable only via the memory/storage frame divergence already reported as POSE-7.

The code property is real — normalize_rendered (183-193) clamps rather than rejecting, and the card's decoders bounds-REJECT instead (src/bindings/map.js:281-284 `continue`; src/state/map.js:958-961 return null), so the two decoders of the same raster genuinely disagree. title: correspondences_from_mapdata's docstring claims clamped corners are skipped; _mapdata_projector silently clamps with no detection, leaving the affine round-trip check as the only guard
observed_behavior:
The docstring at line 534-535 states 'bad/clamped corners are simply skipped (the converter's round-trip check guards the rest)'. `proj` (lines 461-468) returns `[_clamp01(p.x / img_w), _clamp01(p.y / img_h)]` — it returns None only when the library transform RAISES. There is no clamp detection anywhere: a corner projecting outside the image silently becomes exactly 0.0 or 1.0 and is appended as a genuine correspondence at line 555, corrupting the least-squares fit that dispatch/zone_dispatch.py uses to place the drawn zone in device millimetres.

I proved this is NOT reachable under the shipped configuration and so it is latent, not live. homeassistant/components/roborock/__init__.py:94 builds MapParserConfig(map_scale=MAP_SCALE) with MAP_SCALE=4 (const.py:59) and no rotate and no trim, so vacuum_map_parser_base ImageConfig gives scale=4, rotation=0, trim=0. With those: ImageDimensions.to_img returns ((x/50 - L)*4, (H - (y/50 - T) - 1)*4) and the PIL image is (W*4, H*4). Room corners come from _image_to_map(room_px + image_left) (vacuum_map_parser_roborock/map_data_parser.py:244-247), so nx = room_img_x*4/(W*4) which is at most (W-1)/W < 1, and ny = (H - room_y - 1)*4/(H*4) which is at most (H-1)/H < 1. Both axes are strictly inside [0,1) — no clamp can fire. Non-zero rotation or trim would break that, and neither is reachable from HA today.

The surviving guard is max_residual_mm (zone_dispatch.py:85-99) at a 50 mm tolerance, computed over the SAME points that were fitted — a clamped outlier does perturb the fit enough to trip it, so the 'refuse rather than mis-dispatch' contract holds. The defect is the false docstring, not a live mis-dispatch.

Same `proj` is used by overlays_from_mapdata for user-drawn no-go areas, virtual walls and zones (lines 673-681), which CAN legitimately be authored beyond the trimmed map bounds; those clamp into distorted polygons on the overlay.
user_impact: No live mis-dispatch today. The risk is that the docstring reads as an implemented safety guard, so a future change to the projector, the trim/rotate config, or the residual tolerance would remove the only real protection without anyone noticing the claimed one was never there. Overlay-side, a no-go zone drawn past the map edge renders with its outside vertices collapsed onto the border.
guards_checked: _mapdata_projector's guards (map_source_runtime.py:451-458): dims/data presence, `img_w <= 0 or img_h <= 0`, and a bare `except Exception -> None` inside proj — none of which detect a clamp. correspondences_from_mapdata's own filters (lines 549, 553-557) reject only None coords and non-float-castable mm values. fit_normalized_to_mm's `len(pts) < 3` and _solve3_two's `abs(d) < 1e-9` singularity test (zone_dispatch.py:60, 36) reject too-few/collinear points, not clamped ones. max_residual_mm at validate_tol_mm=50.0 (zone_dispatch.py:106,119) is the only thing that would actually catch a clamped corner, and it is fitted on the same corrupted set. dispatch/manager.py:155-161 correctly refuses on a None return.

confirmations: CONFIRMED, and the finder's own refutation work is correct. correspondences_from_mapdata's docstring (map_source_runtime.py:534-535) claims clamped corners are skipped; proj (461-468) returns [_clamp01(x/img_w), _clamp01(y/img_h)] and returns None only when the library transform raises, so a clamped corner is appended at 555 as a genuine correspondence. I independently verified the latency claim: homeassistant/components/roborock/__init__.py:85-95 builds MapParserConfig(map_scale=MAP_SCALE) with MAP_SCALE=4 (const.py:59) and no rotate/trim, and ImageDimensions.to_img (vacuum_map_parser_base/map_data.py:98-104) is ((x-left)*scale, (height-(y-top)-1)*scale) over an image sized width*scale — so normalized corners are strictly inside [0,1) and no clamp can fire. Correctly rated LOW as a false-docstring defect, not a live mis-dispatch. Duplicate of A4-RB-8.

CONFIRMED. correspondences_from_mapdata's docstring (map_source_runtime.py:534-535) claims 'bad/clamped corners are simply skipped'; proj (461-468) returns [_clamp01(p.x/img_w), _clamp01(p.y/img_h)] and returns None only when the library transform raises, so a clamped point is appended at 555 as a genuine correspondence. title: A room's normalized bbox excludes its last pixel row/column while width_m/height_m on the same dict include it (+1) — the two size descriptors disagree by exactly one cell, and Roborock's equivalent omits the +1
observed_behavior:
normalize_rendered returns the TOP-LEFT corner of a pixel's normalized band, so the bbox built at lines 302-304 spans [min_px/W, max_px/W] — the half-open extent, one column short of the room's real footprint. width_m at line 314 uses (max_px - min_px + 1) * res / 100 — the inclusive extent.

ARITHMETIC (live device grid W=360, res=5 cm): a room occupying main-grid columns 100..139 (40 cells). bbox x0 = 100/360 = 0.27778, x1 = 139/360 = 0.38611, span 0.10833. De-normalized with this module's own formula (zone_membership line 361: span * width * res / 100) that is 0.10833 * 360 * 5 / 100 = 1.950 m. width_m reports (139-100+1)*5/100 = 2.000 m. The two fields describe the same room and differ by exactly one cell (5 cm). For a 10-cell room (0.50 m) the bbox reports 0.45 m against width_m's 0.50 m — a 10% disagreement.

Cross-brand: rooms_from_mapdata (map_source_runtime.py:520) computes width_m = abs(x1-x0)/1000 from the parser's mm corners, which are themselves the exclusive extent (max_img_x - min_img_x) * 50 mm — NO +1. So the same physical geometry yields the inclusive metre value on Eufy and the exclusive one on Roborock.
user_impact: resolve_furnished_render ships per-room art placement transforms while the card places art inside the room's bbox and sizes to width_m/height_m — furnished art is scaled ~2.5% too large in a 2 m room and ~10% too large in a 0.5 m room, and the error grows as rooms get smaller. Room labels (src/renderers/map.js:566) and the bbox tap-target (src/state/map.js deviceRoomIdAtContentPct) are biased half a cell toward the top-left, so the last row/column of a room is not tappable.
guards_checked: rooms_from_room_pixels applies min/max re-ordering at line 304, which fixes corner ordering but not the half-open span. normalize_rendered's clamp (line 191-192) does not affect this. The card does not compensate: src/state/map.js roomIdAtContentPct inverts with px = floor(nx*W) and pyN = (H-1) - ny*H, which is the exact inverse of the same half-open convention, so the card faithfully reproduces the one-cell shortfall rather than correcting it. No caller reconciles bbox against width_m/height_m.

confirmations: Arithmetic CONFIRMED. normalize_rendered returns a pixel's top-left normalized corner, so the bbox built at map_source.py:302-304 spans (max_px-min_px)/W while width_m at :314 is (max_px-min_px+1)*res/100 — de-normalizing the bbox span with this module's own factor (width*res, zone_membership:361) gives exactly one cell (res cm) less. Cross-brand inconsistency also confirmed: rooms_from_mapdata:520 uses abs(x1-x0)/1000 from the parser's exclusive mm corners, no +1. Card inverse verified (src/state/map.js:948-951 px=floor(nx*W)), which does reproduce the half-open convention rather than correcting it, so the last row/column is genuinely outside the bbox hit-target. LOW is right.

CONFIRMED by arithmetic in the source. rooms_from_room_pixels builds the bbox from normalize_rendered(min_px)/normalize_rendered(max_px) = [min_px/W, max_px/W] (half-open, one column short) at 302-304, while width_m at 314 uses (max_px - min_px + 1) * res / 100 (inclusive). For a 40-cell room on W=360: bbox span 0.10833 -> de-normalized by this module's own formula (line 361) = 1.950 m vs width_m 2.000 m. Roborock's rooms_from_mapdata:520 uses abs(x1-x0)/1000 with no +1, but its inputs are mm corners not cell indices, so that half of the cross-brand claim is weaker than stated. One-cell (5 cm) descriptor disagreement — cosmetic.

title: zone_membership's docstring says the dominance vote counts cells 'whose centre falls inside the zone polygon'; the code tests the cell's top-left corner
observed_behavior:
The docstring (line 334-336) explicitly promises centre-based membership. Line 387 computes the test point as normalize_rendered(rx + ro_dx, ry + ro_dy, _w, _h), which by that function's own convention is the TOP-LEFT corner of the cell's normalized band, not its centre. That point is what feeds both the bbox reject (line 388) and point_in_polygon (line 390).

ARITHMETIC (live grid W=360, H=300, res=5 cm): cell px occupies normalized x [px/360, (px+1)/360]; its centre is (px+0.5)/360. The code tests px/360, i.e. centre - 0.5/360 = centre - 0.00139 normalized. Converted back with the module's own de-normalization that is 0.00139 * 360 * 5 = 2.5 cm, half a cell, and the same on Y. Equivalently the effective sampling window is shifted half a cell toward +x/-y: cells enter the vote when their LEFT edge is inside the zone rather than their centre.
user_impact: The >=90% floor-dominance filing of a saved zone is computed over a cell set biased by half a cell on each boundary. For the Eufy minimum 0.5 m zone (10 cells across) that is a ~5% shift in the counted set per edge, enough to flip a borderline vote and file a zone under the neighbouring room (or leave it Unassigned). Filing only — it never affects dispatch, per the docstring, which I confirmed: room_number is written to the zone record at mapping_services.py:2507 and never read by the dispatch path.
guards_checked: point_in_polygon (mapping/boundary.py:12-40) is a standard ray-cast with no tolerance or half-cell allowance; it takes the point it is given. The bbox pre-reject at line 388 uses the same corner point, so it cannot compensate. The >=0.90 threshold (line 398) is a ratio over the biased set, not a robustness guard against sampling offset. The area_m2 branch (lines 356-363) is offset-independent as documented and is unaffected.

confirmations: CONFIRMED. The docstring at map_source.py:334-336 explicitly promises cells 'whose centre falls inside the zone polygon'; line 387 tests normalize_rendered(rx+ro_dx, ry+ro_dy, _w, _h), which by that function's own convention is the cell's top-left/low-edge normalized corner, and that same point feeds both the bbox reject (388) and point_in_polygon (390). Offset is exactly half a cell on each axis (0.5/W in x, 0.5/H in the flipped y). point_in_polygon (mapping/boundary.py) is a plain ray-cast with no tolerance, and the >=0.90 threshold is a ratio over the biased set, so neither compensates. Filing-only impact confirmed (room_number written at mapping_services.py:2507, never read by dispatch). LOW is right.

CONFIRMED. The docstring at map_source.py:333-336 promises cells 'whose centre falls inside the zone polygon'; line 387 tests normalize_rendered(rx+ro_dx, ry+ro_dy) which by that function's own convention (nx = px/W, ny = (H-1-py)/H) is the cell's top-left corner of its normalized band, not its centre. Half-cell (2.5 cm at res=5) bias on both axes, applied identically to the bbox pre-reject and to point_in_polygon. Filing-only, never dispatch — verified room_number is written at mapping_services.py:2507 and not read by dispatch.

title: Eufy in-memory map/pose source has NO device selection — every vacuum gets coordinators[0]'s map
observed_behavior: `eufy_inmem_candidates(hass, source_cfg)` takes NO device/serial argument. It returns `hass.data['robovac_mqtt']` (and every entry's runtime_data) wholesale. `eufy_mapdata_obj_from_candidates` then BFS-walks that root with `_holds_mapdata` and returns the FIRST object exposing `_map_data` with a bytes `room_pixels`, and `eufy_live_pose_from_candidates` does the same for `_robot_pixel`/`_dock_pixel`. Verified against the SHIPPED fork: `robovac_mqtt/__init__.py:130-246` builds `coordinators = []` one per device (`is_multi_device = len(all_devices) > 1`) and stores `hass.data[DOMAIN][entry.entry_id] = {'coordinators': coordinators}`; `robovac_mqtt/coordinator.py:85,155,156,158` shows each EufyCleanCoordinator carries `self.device_id`, `self._map_data`, `self._robot_pixel`, `self._dock_pixel`. `_walk` is a deque-popleft BFS over insertion order: root dict (d0) -> per-entry dict (d1) -> the `coordinators` list (d2) -> `coordinators[0]` (d3, inside max_depth=5). So `coordinators[0]` matches the predicate first, deterministically, for EVERY vacuum_entity_id. `device_identifier_value`/`eufy_store_path` DO key correctly by serial — but only for the `.storage` path, which is the FALLBACK; `async_refresh_map_state_source` (map_source_coordinator.py:187) routes to the memory-PRIMARY `_refresh_eufy_map_source` whenever the adapter declares a `memory` block, which the Eufy adapter always does. `.device_id` — the exact field needed to filter — exists on the coordinator and is never read.
user_impact: With two or more Eufy robots, the second (and third...) vacuum's entire map identity is the first robot's: room numbers, room names, bboxes, the room-id raster, current_room, robot/dock anchors and the trail. `async_get_map_data_dict` hands robot B vacuum A's raster, so `zone_membership` files saved zones against the wrong home and `current_room_for_pixel` attributes B's run to A's rooms (poisoning learned per-room history). `async_get_map_render_data` renders A's floor plan on B's card. Tapping a room region on B dispatches the room NUMBER carried by A's bbox — B cleans the wrong room. Nothing logs an error; the diagnostics breadcrumb reports a confident `pose_at`/`mapdata_at`.
guards_checked: `_WALK_SKIP_ATTRS` denylist and `max_depth=5` in `_walk` (map_source_runtime.py:224-271) — neither filters by device, and the coordinator sits at depth 3 so it IS reached; `_holds_mapdata` (line 949) matches any coordinator with a bytes raster; `_mem_rooms_cache` is keyed by vacuum_entity_id (map_source_coordinator.py:420) so the two vacuums get SEPARATE cache slots — both filled from the same coordinator, which hides rather than fixes the collision; `_commit_result`'s `cached.get('map_id') == str(map_id)` guard (map_source_coordinator.py:117) only protects the stale-hold path, not source selection; `device_identifier_value`/`eufy_store_path` (lines 50-96) do key by serial but only feed the `.storage` fallback; the design doc `docs/dev/design/map-state-source.md` explicitly specified `locate: <how to find the coordinator for this vacuum>` for the memory backend — that contract was never implemented on the Eufy side.

confirmations: CONFIRMED — same defect as A1-LC-1, independently verified against the shipped fork. eufy_inmem_candidates takes no device argument; _walk returns the first _holds_mapdata / _is_pose_holder hit; the fork's hass.data[DOMAIN][entry_id]['coordinators'] is a per-device LIST whose members each carry .device_id (never read). The adapter's memory/live_pose blocks declare only hass_data_domain + attr names, no locate/identity key, while the sibling roborock_candidates:1020-1023 DOES accept and prioritise a per-vacuum image entity — the asymmetry the finder cites is real. _mem_rooms_cache is keyed per vacuum but filled from the unfiltered locator, so it hides rather than fixes the collision.

CONFIRMED — same defect as A1-LC-1, verified independently against the fork source (robovac_mqtt/__init__.py:130-246 builds one coordinator per device, is_multi_device = len(all_devices) > 1, stores {'coordinators': coordinators}; coordinator.py:154-158 carries device_id, _map_data, _robot_pixel, _dock_pixel). eufy_inmem_candidates (map_source_runtime.py:839-858) takes no device argument; _holds_mapdata (949-955) matches on attribute presence only; _walk is FIFO so coordinators[0] wins deterministically at depth 3, inside max_depth=5. title: Content version hashes ONLY the room raster, but the cache it gates holds the grid geometry the fork mutates independently
observed_behavior: `eufy_mapdata_obj_from_candidates` computes `version = hashlib.sha1(bytes(rp)).hexdigest()[:12]` over the `room_pixels` bytes ALONE. `_refresh_eufy_map_source` (map_source_coordinator.py:419-435) uses that version as the sole cache key for `_mem_rooms_cache`, and the cached entry holds BOTH the normalized room result AND the converted `map_data` dict, which is then handed to `_apply_inmem_pose_to_result` -> `live_pose_overlay` -> `normalize_rendered(px, py, width, height)` and `current_room_for_pixel` (which derives ro_dx/ro_dy from origin_x/room_outline_origin_x). The fork GUARANTEES the raster stays byte-identical while that geometry changes: `robovac_mqtt/coordinator.py:526-535` — on a plain `Map` frame (`map_data.room_pixels is None`, the frame type that arrives during cleaning) it copies `room_pixels`, `room_outline_width/height`, `room_outline_origin_x/y`, `room_names` and the hazard layers forward from the previous MapData, but `width`, `height`, `origin_x`, `origin_y` and `resolution` come from the NEW frame (`try_extract_map_data`, map_stream.py:509-524, reads `map_msg.info.width/height/origin` every frame). ARITHMETIC using the live device's real values (width=256, height=244, origin_x=-852 cm, res=5): the robot explores west, the new frame reports origin_x=-1052 and width=296. Robot physically at x=-52 cm. The fork computes `_robot_pixel` with the NEW origin (`_pose_to_pixel`, coordinator.py:546): px = round((-52 - (-1052))/5) = 200. VA normalizes it against the CACHED width: nx = 200/256 = 0.781, while the truth on the new grid is 200/296 = 0.676 — a 0.105 error = 31 px = 155 cm. For the room lookup, the correct outline offset on the new grid is round((room_outline_origin_x(-852) - origin_x(-1052))/5) = +40, but the cached map_data yields round((-852 - (-852))/5) = 0, so `current_room_for_pixel` reads outline cell 200 instead of 160 — 40 cells = 2 metres into a different room. The same defect is in `eufy_version_of` (map_source.py:621-628), which hashes only `room_pixels` and is what the card caches its whole render (including width/height/ro_dx/ro_dy) by. The cache is never invalidated by anything else — no TTL, no map_id key, no geometry check.
user_impact: During and after any run in which the map grows, or across any session where Eufy re-localizes its coordinate origin (a documented behaviour of this device), the robot dot lands metres from where the robot is, the room bboxes/tap-regions are scaled against a dead grid, and `current_room` resolves to the WRONG room. Because current_room is the input to live rollover and per-room attribution, cleaning time and coverage are written into the wrong room's learned history — stored room data silently corrupted, with no error and no absent marker (the result is `present: True`, so `_commit_result`'s stale-hold logic never engages). It self-heals only when a full MapBackup frame delivers a different raster.
guards_checked: `_stat_mtime` + the `cached.get('mtime') == mtime` reuse in `_refresh_storage_map_source` (map_source_coordinator.py:250-266) — storage path only, never reached on the memory-primary branch; `_live_pose_geom_cache` (line 486) is a separate mtime-keyed cache used only by `async_get_map_live_pose`; `_commit_result`'s hold/TTL/`_MAP_SOURCE_HARD_CLEAR_REASONS` logic (lines 105-134) fires only on an ABSENT result, so a stale-but-present result is committed unconditionally; `present_gate` gates presence, not content; the `image_size` extra in `eufy_result_from_mapdata` (map_source_runtime.py:177-180) is read from the SAME cached map_data, so the card's letterbox correction inherits the stale ratio rather than correcting it; `mapdata_dict_from_obj` is only re-run on a cache MISS (map_source_coordinator.py:426), so the fresh geometry is never even read.

confirmations: CONFIRMED, including the load-bearing external claim. So the raster bytes — the ONLY input to eufy_mapdata_obj_from_candidates' sha1 version (map_source_runtime.py:966) — stay identical while the grid geometry changes. _refresh_eufy_map_source:419-435 then reuses cache['map_data'] (the STALE converted dict) and hands it to _apply_inmem_pose_to_result -> live_pose_overlay -> normalize_rendered/current_room_for_pixel, while the fork's _robot_pixel (coordinator.py:481/546) was computed against the NEW origin. mapdata_dict_from_obj is only re-run on a version MISS, so the fresh geometry is never read. eufy_version_of (map_source.py:621-628) has the same raster-only hash and is the card's render cache key (:654). So the fork guarantees a byte-identical raster while the grid geometry changes underneath — a permanent cache hit serving dead width/height/origin to normalize_rendered and to current_room_for_pixel's ro_dx derivation, while _robot_pixel is computed against the NEW origin (coordinator.py:546). title: A dropped/renamed upstream geometry field degrades to a confidently WRONG map, not a loud absent one
observed_behavior: `mapdata_dict_from_obj` copies fields with `v = _attr(name); if v is not None: out[name] = v` — a renamed or removed attribute is silently OMITTED from the dict; only a missing `room_pixels` returns None. Downstream, `_outline_geometry` (map_source.py:239-245) hard-requires only four fields — `if not (width and height and ro_w and ro_h): return None` — while `origin_x`, `origin_y`, `room_outline_origin_x`, `room_outline_origin_y` fall through `_as_int(value, default)`, which returns the default with NO logging. Arithmetic with the live device's values: if the fork renames `origin_x` across the pending #136 merge, ox becomes 0 while `room_outline_origin_x` is still -852, so ro_dx = round((-852 - 0)/5) = -170 on a 256-pixel-wide grid — every room slides 66% of the map width off-grid and `normalize_rendered` clamps the wreckage to [0,1] without complaint. Symmetrically, losing `room_outline_origin_x` makes it default to ox, forcing ro_dx=0. The asymmetry is the defect: losing `width` degrades loudly to `no_segmentation`, losing `origin_x` degrades to a plausible-looking wrong map. `_refresh_eufy_map_source` (map_source_coordinator.py:426-431) also falls back to `.storage` ONLY when `mapdata_dict_from_obj` returns None; a dict that converts but scans to zero rooms is cached under the version and served forever with a working store file sitting on disk untouched.
user_impact: After an upstream fork schema change, room regions, current-room and the robot anchor are all displaced by a large fixed offset with no warning in the log and no `unavailable` state — the card looks live and is wrong. In the zero-rooms variant the map vanishes permanently (until HA restart or a re-map) even though the `.storage` fallback holds a perfectly good copy.
guards_checked: `_outline_geometry`'s four-field truthiness gate (map_source.py:239) — verified it does NOT cover any of the four origin fields; `_as_int` (line 162) swallows TypeError/ValueError and returns the default silently, by explicit design comment; `mapdata_dict_from_obj`'s `except Exception -> None` (line 712) only catches raises, not omissions; the adapter's `field_attrs` remap hook exists (adapters/eufy/adapter.py `memory` block) but is inert until a human notices and edits it; `compare_map_data` (map_source.py:737-788) WOULD surface the mismatch via `normalization_safe` but it is only reachable through the manual `compare_map_sources` diagnostic service, never on the refresh path; the `store_version` guard (map_source_runtime.py:128) catches a bumped Store wrapper version but the in-memory object has no version at all.

confirmations: Code behaviour CONFIRMED and the required degradation path IS shown (not bare speculation). mapdata_dict_from_obj:707-710 omits any attr that is None; _outline_geometry:239 hard-requires only width/height/ro_w/ro_h while origin_x/origin_y/room_outline_origin_x/y fall through _as_int(value, default) which swallows TypeError/ValueError silently by design (:162-172); losing width degrades loudly to no_segmentation, losing origin_x degrades to a plausible wrong offset with no log. The .storage fallback is confirmed to fire only when mapdata_dict_from_obj returns None (coordinator:426-431), and compare_map_data/normalization_safe is confirmed reachable only from the manual compare service. DOWNGRADED to LOW: the trigger is a hypothetical upstream rename with no shipped path today, which by this audit's own rule 4 ranks below reachable defects. (Worth noting a more plausible sibling the finder did not raise: a RoomOutline proto whose origin field defaults to 0 while origin_x is negative would silently produce ro_dx=170 on the live 256-wide grid.)

The asymmetry is real: mapdata_dict_from_obj (map_source.py:695-711) copies with `if v is not None` so a renamed/removed attr is silently OMITTED, and _outline_geometry (239-245) hard-requires only width/height/ro_w/ro_h while the four origin fields fall through _as_int(value, default) with no logging — losing `width` degrades loudly to no_segmentation, losing `origin_x` degrades to a plausible wrong map. title: Room-outline offset is the exact NEGATION of the fork renderer's — overlays desync from the live backdrop whenever the outline origin differs from the map origin
observed_behavior: VA computes `ro_dx = round((room_outline_origin_x - origin_x) / res)` and indexes with `rx = px - ro_dx` (`current_room_for_pixel`:418) / `px = rx + ro_dx` (`rooms_from_room_pixels`:288). The shipped fork computes the SAME quantity with the opposite sign in BOTH of its own transforms: `render_map_png` (robovac_mqtt/api/map_stream.py:233) `_ro_dx = round((map_data.origin_x - map_data.room_outline_origin_x) / res)` then `rx = px_x - _ro_dx`, and `room_id_at_normalized` (map_stream.py:135) identically. Derivation from the fork's own grid convention (`_pose_to_pixel`, coordinator.py:546: `px = round((x_cm - origin_x)/res)`, i.e. world = origin + index*res): world(outline cell rx) = ro_ox + rx*res, world(main px) = ox + px*res, so rx = px + (ox - ro_ox)/res — which is VA's sign, NOT the fork's. So VA is arithmetically right and the fork's renderer is wrong, but the card overlays VA's normalized geometry on the fork's rendered PNG. Arithmetic on the X10 map VA's own docstring cites (outline origin +105 cells from the map origin): VA places outline cell 0 at main pixel +105; the fork's renderer paints it at -105 — a 210-cell separation. Verified this is zero on the live device (`.storage/robovac_mqtt.AFC96X0F33201054`: origin_x=-852, room_outline_origin_x=-852; origin_y=-987, room_outline_origin_y=-987, res=5, so ro_dx=ro_dy=0), which is why nothing has been seen yet. The docstring's 'sign is VERIFIED against the fork's rendered map ... ~93%' claim does not survive reading the fork: that verification can only have been against the `raw_pixels` floor mask (which lives in the main grid with no offset at all), not against the fork's room colouring.
user_impact: On any Eufy map whose room-outline origin differs from the map origin (VA's own notes record an X10 map at +105 cells), the card's room tap-regions, room labels, current-room highlight and robot dot sit displaced by twice the offset relative to the live fork camera backdrop they are drawn over — a visibly mis-registered map with no error. The VA-rendered backdrop is unaffected (it consumes VA's own `ro_dx`/`ro_dy` from `render_data_from_storage`, so it is self-consistent), which makes the defect appear and disappear with the backdrop toggle and look like a card bug.
guards_checked: Read the fork's two consumers of the offset (`render_map_png` map_stream.py:230-243 and `room_id_at_normalized` map_stream.py:123-141) rather than trusting the VA docstring, per the 'a comment asserting a guard is a CLAIM' rule; confirmed the grid convention from `_pose_to_pixel` (coordinator.py:541-550) and `normalized_rects_to_quads_cm` (coordinator.py:552+); confirmed the live store carries ro_origin == origin so ro_dx is 0 today; `render_data_from_storage` (map_source.py:655-671) exports ro_dx/ro_dy to the card so the VA canvas stays self-consistent; the unit tests (tests/unit/test_map_source.py:164-165, 324-325) hard-code VA's sign as the expected value, so they can never catch the divergence; the card's `isLiveImageDisplayed()` gate (docs/dev/design/map-state-source.md, Wave 3c) is what makes the fork PNG the backdrop and therefore makes this reachable.

confirmations: Sign divergence CONFIRMED by reading both sources, exactly as the finder demanded of itself. VA: _outline_geometry:243 ro_dx = round((room_outline_origin_x - origin_x)/res), used as rx = px - ro_dx (:418) / px = rx + ro_dx (:288). Fork: render_map_png (eufy-clean map_stream.py:233) _ro_dx = round((origin_x - room_outline_origin_x)/res) then rx = px_x - _ro_dx, and room_id_at_normalized (map_stream.py:135-138) is identical — the exact negation. I redid the derivation from the fork's own grid convention (_pose_to_pixel: world = origin + index*res): rx = px + (ox - ro_ox)/res = px - (ro_ox - ox)/res, which is VA's sign, so the fork's renderer is the one that disagrees with the convention. I also confirmed from the live store that origin_x == room_outline_origin_x (-852/-852, -987/-987), so ro_dx = 0 today and nothing is visible on this device. Reachable on any map with a nonzero outline origin (VA's own docstring records +105 cells). ONE correction to the impact text: robot_anchor is normalize_rendered(px,py,width,height) with no ro_dx, so the robot DOT is not displaced — only room bboxes/labels/tap-regions and the current-room highlight are.

CONFIRMED by reading the fork, and the arithmetic favours VA. Fork api/map_stream.py:135 and :233 both compute `_ro_dx = round((origin_x - room_outline_origin_x)/res)` then `rx = px - _ro_dx`; VA's _outline_geometry (map_source.py:243) computes `ro_dx = round((room_outline_origin_x - origin_x)/res)` then `rx = px - ro_dx` (map_source.py:418). Derivation from the fork's own grid convention (_pose_to_pixel, coordinator.py:546: world = origin + index*res) gives rx = px + (origin_x - ro_origin_x)/res, i.e. VA's sign. The fork's renderer is the one that is wrong, and the card overlays VA geometry on the fork's PNG. The live store confirms this is ZERO today (origin_x = room_outline_origin_x = -852, origin_y = room_outline_origin_y = -987), so nothing is visible yet — it is reachable only on a map whose outline origin differs from the map origin. The docstring's 'VERIFIED against the fork's rendered map ... ~93%' claim does not survive reading the fork's room colouring. Rendering-only misregistration, currently dormant.

title: Two room extractors disagree on the input coordinate frame and the dead one is the one under test
observed_behavior: `rooms_from_parsed_map` has no production caller — a repo-wide grep finds it only in its own definition and in tests/unit/test_map_source.py:127,135,212. The shipped Roborock extractor is `rooms_from_mapdata` (map_source_runtime.py:478). They disagree on the fundamental question of what `Room.x0..y1` MEANS: `rooms_from_parsed_map`'s docstring says 'Coords are in image pixels; we normalize by the image dims' and divides by image_width/height directly, while `rooms_from_mapdata` treats the same fields as VACUUM millimetres and projects them through the parser's own `ImageDimensions.to_img` (`_mapdata_projector`, line 438) — `_rb_area_m2` divides by 1,000,000 confirming the mm reading. They also emit different shapes: the shipped one adds `area_m2`/`width_m`/`height_m`, the dead one omits them. `rooms_from_parsed_map` additionally carries an admitted-unverified `flip_y` hypothesis in its own docstring. `find_roomlike_collection` (map_source_runtime.py:274) is likewise dead — `find_mapdata` superseded it, per its own comment about `no_go_areas` false matches.
user_impact: No user impact today (dead code). The trap is for the next brand adapter: the extractor that LOOKS canonical (it lives in the pure module, it has the descriptive name, it is the one with unit tests) divides raw device coordinates by image dimensions, which for any parser handing back millimetres yields bboxes clamped to a corner of the map. Test coverage on the unused function also inflates confidence in the extraction layer that ships.
guards_checked: Grepped the whole repo for `rooms_from_parsed_map` and `find_roomlike_collection` — only definitions plus tests; traced `roborock_result_from_candidates` (map_source_runtime.py:739) to confirm it calls `rooms_from_mapdata`, not `rooms_from_parsed_map`; confirmed `_rb_area_m2` (line 473) documents 'coords are vacuum units (1 unit = 1 mm)', contradicting the dead function's 'image pixels' docstring; checked that neither dead function is re-exported from mapping/__init__ or mapping_services.

confirmations: CONFIRMED dead and CONFIRMED contradictory. Repo-wide grep for rooms_from_parsed_map returns only its definition (map_source.py:808) and tests/unit/test_map_source.py:127/135/212; find_roomlike_collection only its definition (:274) and tests/unit/test_map_source_runtime.py:456-478. roborock_result_from_candidates:739 calls rooms_from_mapdata, not the dead one. The frame contradiction is real: rooms_from_parsed_map's docstring says 'Coords are in image pixels' and divides by image dims, while rooms_from_mapdata treats the identical Room.x0..y1 as vacuum mm and projects through the parser's ImageDimensions.to_img, with _rb_area_m2 dividing by 1e6 to confirm the mm reading. CONFIRMED dead. A repo-wide grep for rooms_from_parsed_map and find_roomlike_collection returns only their definitions plus tests/unit/test_map_source.py:127,135,212 and tests/unit/test_map_source_runtime.py:456,466,478 — no production caller. title: Roborock MapData lookup never binds the found map to the requested map_id — a multi-map (multi-floor) device converts drawn zones in the wrong floor's coordinate frame
observed_behavior: find_mapdata(root, max_depth=6) is a bounded BFS whose predicate _is_mapdata (line 364) is `getattr(o,'image',None) is not None and getattr(o,'rooms',None) is not None`. It returns the SHALLOWEST match and takes no map identity argument — there is no map flag, map name, or map_id parameter anywhere in the Roborock extraction path. map_id IS threaded into both callers (map_source_coordinator.py:144 async_refresh_map_state_source, :330 get_live_mapdata_obj) but is used ONLY to resolve the presence-gate image entity (_resolve_live_map_image_entity, manager.py:4349, which is an existence check on `image.{object_id}_{map_slug}`) — it never reaches the walk. The repo's own test model of the graph is flag-keyed: tests/unit/test_map_source_runtime.py:284 builds `_Coordinator(maps={0: md})`, i.e. `coordinator.maps` is a dict keyed by map flag holding one map per floor. BFS over a dict enumerates insertion order (map_source_runtime.py:256), so the FIRST map (flag 0) wins regardless of which map_id was asked for. The per-map image entity IS the correct root and is candidate 0 (roborock_candidates:1021-1023), but the image entity itself carries no MapData — the walk must descend through its `coordinator` attribute (not in _WALK_SKIP_ATTRS, line 224) into the SHARED coordinator, at which point the per-map scoping is gone. The second mechanism is the switch lag: `_home_trait._map_content.map_data` (the path recorded in .claude/notes/reference_map_source_lifecycle.md) holds only the CURRENTLY loaded map, refreshed on the roborock IMAGE_CACHE_INTERVAL (~30 s per docs/dev/29-roborock-adapter.md), while VA's active map_id flips as soon as `select.{id}_selected_map` changes — so for up to a refresh interval after a floor switch the walk returns the previous floor's MapData under the new map_id. Consequence chain: dispatch/manager.py:145-160 (adapters/roborock/adapter.py:305 `zone_coords: device_mm`) calls get_live_mapdata_obj(map_id=...) -> correspondences_from_mapdata(map_source_runtime.py:527) -> zone_dispatch.normalized_rects_to_mm. The correspondences are the WRONG map's own room-bbox corners, so they are perfectly self-consistent: fit_normalized_to_mm returns an exact affine and max_residual_mm is ~0, far under the 50 mm validate_tol_mm. The refuse-gate passes and `app_zoned_clean` is sent with millimetre coordinates computed in a different floor's frame.
user_impact: On a Roborock with more than one saved map (a two-storey home — the exact case the adapter's `active_map = select.{id}_selected_map` block exists for), the user draws a zone box on the upstairs map and the robot vacuums the corresponding rectangle of the downstairs map. No error, no warning: the 'refuse rather than mis-dispatch' safety gate is satisfied because it only checks that the affine reproduces the correspondences it was fitted from. The same wrong-map geometry is also committed to _map_state_source_cache under the requested map_id (map_source_coordinator.py:101), so room bboxes, tap-to-select hit-testing and the m² chips all show the other floor's rooms.
guards_checked: _is_mapdata (map_source_runtime.py:364) — two attribute-name checks, no map identity; find_mapdata (:373) — no map argument, returns first BFS hit and never resumes; roborock_candidates (:1005) — collects roots, no map filter; image_entity_object (:760) — returns the per-map entity OBJECT but nothing reads its map_flag before the walk descends into the shared coordinator; _resolve_live_map_image_entity (core/manager.py:4349-4385) — hass.states.get() existence check only, so it passes for an `unavailable` entity and does not prove the in-memory map matches; _commit_result (map_source_coordinator.py:113-118) — its `cached.get('map_id') == str(map_id)` test only stops a CACHED other-map result being served, it does not validate freshly-extracted geometry; zone_dispatch.normalized_rects_to_mm / max_residual_mm (dispatch/zone_dispatch.py:85-120) — validates the affine against the SAME correspondences it was fitted from, so a wrong-but-self-consistent map fits at ~0 mm residual and passes; the per-zone zone_min_area_m2 / zone_max_area_m2 bounds (dispatch/manager.py:165-178) — area is frame-relative and survives a wrong-frame conversion unchanged when the two maps have similar scale.

confirmations: Mechanism CONFIRMED and STRONGER than the finder could show — but downgraded on certainty of the wrong-map landing. Verified in VA source: find_mapdata (map_source_runtime.py:373) takes no map argument, _is_mapdata (:364) is a two-attribute test, and map_id is threaded into async_refresh_map_state_source/get_live_mapdata_obj ONLY to resolve the presence-gate image entity — it never reaches the walk. I then checked the INSTALLED HA-core roborock integration rather than relying on the repo's test fixture: image.py:86-88 shows self._home_trait.home_map_content is a dict[map_flag, MapContent] and sensor.py:632 shows _home_trait.current_map_data — i.e. MULTIPLE maps' MapData genuinely coexist in one shared home trait, and the per-map RoborockMap entity's own map_flag is never consulted by the walk. The refuse-gate cannot catch it: normalized_rects_to_mm/max_residual_mm (dispatch/zone_dispatch.py:85-120) validates the affine against the same correspondences it was fitted from, so a wrong-but-self-consistent map fits at ~0 mm. DOWNGRADED to HIGH: the ABSENCE of any map binding is proven, and the switch-lag path is real, but which node BFS lands on is HA-version dependent (current_map_data would coincidentally be right in steady state), so a wrong-floor dispatch is proven-possible rather than proven-certain on today's shipped graph.

CONFIRMED, and I verified the multi-map container against the installed HA core rather than the repo's fixture. homeassistant/components/roborock/image.py:85-88: `self._home_trait.home_map_content.get(self.map_flag)` — home_map_content is a dict keyed by map flag holding one MapContent per map, and each MapContent carries `.map_data` (the parsed MapData) plus `raw_api_response`. find_mapdata (map_source_runtime.py:373) takes no map argument and _walk is FIFO BFS, so starting from the per-map image entity it descends image_entity -> _home_trait -> home_map_content dict -> MapContent values (ALL flags, insertion order) -> .map_data, and returns the FIRST MapData regardless of which flag was requested. The entity's own `map_flag` and its `_map_content` property — the exact per-map selector — are never consulted. map_id IS threaded to both callers (coordinator.py:144, :330) but only reaches _resolve_live_map_image_entity, an existence check. Consequence chain to app_zoned_clean is as described, and max_residual_mm cannot catch it because the affine is fitted on the wrong map's own corners (residual ~0). Reachable on any two-storey Roborock.

title: No device scoping anywhere in the Roborock candidate walk — on a two-vacuum Roborock account the card's rendered raster and the diagnostics drift report come from an arbitrary robot
observed_behavior: roborock_candidates() appends `entry.runtime_data` for EVERY config entry of the `roborock` domain (:1029-1032) plus `hass.data['roborock']` (:1033-1035) with no duid/device filter, and its docstring explicitly declines to filter ('we don't over-filter here'). A Roborock config entry is per ACCOUNT and its runtime_data holds the per-device coordinators, so these roots cover every robot on the account. The only per-vacuum root is the image entity (:1021-1023), and two of the four call sites do not supply it: map_source_coordinator.py:627 calls `roborock_candidates(hass, source_cfg)` with no image_entity_id (the comment at :620 states this is deliberate — 'No map_id / image entity needed'), and diagnostics.py:502 does the same. Both then take the FIRST BFS hit — roborock_render_data_from_candidates (:396, loop at :404) returns the first MapContent's decoded raster, roborock_geometry_drift_from_candidates (:416) the first MapData/MapContent pair. Meanwhile the map_state_source path (map_source_coordinator.py:208-210) DOES pass the image entity, so the room bboxes and pose overlays resolve to the correct robot. The two halves of the same card view therefore come from different robots, and map_source_coordinator.py:629 stamps THIS vacuum's stored room names (_roborock_render_room_names, keyed by segment id) onto the other robot's raster. The declared `identifier_domain: 'roborock'` (adapters/roborock/adapter.py:511) and the existing device_identifier_value() helper (:50, documented 'Roborock by its duid') are never called on the Roborock path — device_identifier_value is used only by eufy_store_path.
user_impact: A household with two Roborock vacuums: the VA-rendered map backdrop for robot B shows robot A's floor plan, painted with robot B's room names. Because src/state/map.js gates zone drawing on `isVaRenderActive()` (canDrawZone = supportsZoneClean() && (isLiveBackdropActive() || isVaRenderActive())), the user draws a zone on that wrong floor plan; the normalized rect is then converted by get_live_mapdata_obj's (correct-robot) projector and dispatched — a wrong-area clean the refuse-gate cannot see, since the affine it validates is self-consistent. Diagnostics for robot B likewise report robot A's geometry drift, and diagnostics._self_check:169-170 reads `roborock_geometry_drift.present` as 'this vacuum's map is available', so a robot with no usable map is reported healthy.
guards_checked: roborock_candidates (:1005-1036) — no duid/device predicate, confirmed by reading every append; image_entity_object (:760) — the only per-device root, not passed at map_source_coordinator.py:627 or diagnostics.py:502; roborock_render_data_from_candidates (:404-413) — takes the first MapContent, no identity check; roborock_geometry_drift_from_candidates (:425-435) — same; device_identifier_value (:50) — exists and is documented for exactly this, grepped every caller: only eufy_store_path (:88); adapters/roborock/adapter.py map_state_source block (:496-514) — declares identifier_domain and hass_data_domain but nothing consumes identifier_domain; roborock_result_from_candidates diagnostics `mapdata_at` (:738) — records the access path but nothing compares it to the vacuum.

title: roborock_result_from_candidates hard-returns on the first duck-typed MapData match, so one false positive permanently blanks the Roborock map source — and the stale-hold masks it for six hours
observed_behavior: The function is written as a multi-candidate search (`for origin, key, root in candidates`, :734) but the body cannot reach a second candidate once ANY candidate yields a MapData-ish object: on `if not rooms:` it RETURNS `no_room_geometry` (:743-744) instead of `continue`. find_mapdata (:373) matches on _is_mapdata (:364) = only `.image is not None` and `.rooms is not None`, and _walk is breadth-first (:236-271) so the SHALLOWEST object bearing those two very common attribute names wins and the walk never resumes past a rejected hit. The docstring on find_mapdata claims it 'Targets MapData specifically ... NOT a generic x0/y0/x1/y1 collection' — that claim is a two-attribute name test, not a type or shape test: nothing verifies `.rooms` values are Room-like or that `.image` has `.dimensions`/`.data`. HA core's own per-map record carries both names (`rooms` = dict[int,str] of segment id -> name, `image` = rendered PNG bytes), and it sits on `coordinator.maps` — the exact dict the repo's test fixture models at tests/unit/test_map_source_runtime.py:284, i.e. SHALLOWER than the real MapData nested inside it. Hijacked that way, _mapdata_projector (:438) does `getattr(bytes_image, 'dimensions', None)` -> None -> returns None -> rooms_from_mapdata returns [] (:492-493) -> the early return fires. Note the sibling function roborock_render_data_from_candidates (:404-412) does exactly the right thing in the same situation (`continue` on a failed decode), which makes the asymmetry a defect rather than a design choice. The failure is then hidden: `no_room_geometry` is deliberately excluded from _MAP_SOURCE_HARD_CLEAR_REASONS (map_source_coordinator.py:50-55), so _commit_result holds the last-known-good map for up to _STALE_MAP_TTL_SECONDS = 6 h (:45), and .claude/notes/reference_map_source_lifecycle.md records that the frontend staleness badge is still unbuilt.
user_impact: A change in the HA core roborock integration's in-memory shape (or any provider object that happens to expose `.rooms` and `.image`) silently kills the entire Roborock map source: rooms, current room, robot/dock anchors, no-go/wall/path overlays, tap-to-select and zone drawing all stop. The user sees a normal-looking six-hour-old map with a frozen robot and no badge, then the map vanishes with reason `no_room_geometry` — while a fully valid MapData is present on the next, untried candidate root.
guards_checked: _is_mapdata (:364-370) — the trailing `hasattr(o,'rooms') and hasattr(o,'image')` clauses are redundant with the getattr checks and add no specificity; _walk (:236-271) — BFS, first predicate hit returns immediately, no resume-after-reject; _mapdata_diag (:691-713) — records room_count 0 into diagnostics but the caller does not act on it; roborock_result_from_candidates :734-747 — read line by line, the only `continue` is on `map_data is None`; roborock_render_data_from_candidates :404-412 — the correct continue-on-failure sibling; _MAP_SOURCE_HARD_CLEAR_REASONS (map_source_coordinator.py:50-55) — `no_room_geometry` deliberately absent, so the hold applies; _commit_result (:105-134) — holds and stamps stale/stale_since, and the note file confirms nothing consumes those flags yet.

DOWNGRADED to MEDIUM: the specific decoy the finder posits is unconfirmed — I checked the installed HA-core roborock integration and home_map_info entries carry .rooms but I could not confirm any shallower object carrying BOTH .rooms and .image, and in practice every candidate root converges on the same home trait, so 'a valid MapData on the next untried candidate' is not demonstrated. The robustness defect is real; the HIGH impact story is not established.

The code defect is real — roborock_result_from_candidates:743-744 RETURNS no_room_geometry where its sibling roborock_render_data_from_candidates:404-412 correctly `continue`s, and _walk never resumes past a rejected hit, so one duck-type false positive permanently blanks the source while a valid MapData sits on the next root.
