title: rooms_from_mapdata publishes the live segment number as the room's only identity and synthesizes the name, so after a Roborock re-map a tap on room A selects room B
observed_behavior: rooms_from_mapdata emits `{'number': getattr(r,'number',None), 'name': str(name) if name else f'Room {num}'}` (:509-514). Its own docstring states 'The parser leaves Room.name None, so names fall back to Room {number}' — verified by tests/unit/test_map_source_runtime.py:190 which asserts `r['name'] == 'Room 16'` with the comment 'Roborock leaves name None'. So for Roborock every map_state_source room carries a SYNTHETIC name and the live segment number as its only key. docs/dev/29-roborock-adapter.md states segment ids 'renumber on every re-map' and that is why dispatch declares `resolve_live_ids_by_slug: True` (adapters/roborock/adapter.py:353). The card matches by exact id equality with no slug and no map-version check: src/renderers/map.js:559 `managed.find((m) => String(m.id) === String(r.number))` for labels, and src/state/map.js:991 `best = r.number` in deviceRoomIdAtContentPct, whose comment asserts 'the device room NUMBER (== managed room id)'. Stored managed ids are the get_maps `segment_id` (adapters/roborock/adapter.py discovery `room_id_key: 'segment_id'`), i.e. the ids captured at the LAST discovery. After a re-map the live numbers shift (e.g. Kitchen 17 -> 27) while stored ids do not. Concretely: stored {17: Kitchen, 27: Bathroom}; after re-map the live Kitchen is number 27. rooms_from_mapdata publishes bbox=<kitchen geometry>, number=27, name='Room 27'. The card labels the kitchen's bbox 'Bathroom' and a tap inside it returns 27, selecting the managed Bathroom. Dispatch's resolve_live_ids_by_slug then faithfully resolves the Bathroom slug to its current live id and cleans the bathroom. The one identity signal that would survive a re-map — the segment-id -> name map HA core holds alongside the parsed map — is available in the same object graph the walk already traverses and is plumbed for the RENDER path (map_source_coordinator.py:574 _roborock_render_room_names) but rooms_from_mapdata takes no names argument at all.
user_impact: After the robot re-maps (an app-initiated re-scan, or the automatic re-map some models do after a large layout change), the live map's room labels and tap targets are shifted onto the wrong rooms with no visible error. The user taps the Kitchen on the card and the robot cleans the Bathroom. The map still looks right — the bboxes are correct geometry — only the identity attached to them is wrong.

title: roborock_geometry_drift_from_candidates pairs a MapData and a MapContent found by two independent BFS walks with no check they are the same map, and reports present:True regardless of the verdict
observed_behavior: Lines 427-428 run two separate bounded BFS walks over the same root with different predicates — `md, _ = find_mapdata(root)` (predicate: `.rooms` + `.image`) and `mc, _ = find_map_content(root)` (predicate: bytes `.raw_api_response` + non-None `.map_data`). Each returns its own shallowest hit, and nothing asserts `mc.map_data is md`. The predicates are loose enough that this is not theoretical: _is_map_content (:382-386) accepts ANY non-None `.map_data` — the repo's own fixture sets it to `object()` (tests/unit/test_roborock_raw_map.py:180). When the root covers more than one map or more than one device (see RB-2: diagnostics.py:502 passes account-wide roots with no image entity), the parser bboxes and the raster can come from different maps. geometry_drift then reports a room-id set mismatch and low IoU as decode 'drift' — the report has no field that distinguishes 'the decode is miscalibrated' from 'these are two different maps'. Separately, the wrapper returns `{'present': True, **geometry_drift(...)}` (:434) whenever a pair is found and decodes, independent of the `aligned` verdict; diagnostics._self_check:169-170 consumes exactly that (`has_decoded_map = bool(drift.get('present'))`) as the brand-agnostic 'map available' signal.
user_impact: The on-device decode validator — the tool the notes record as having turned Roborock calibration 'from eyeball to data' — can report a bogus systematic drift that sends the maintainer hunting a flip/trim bug that does not exist, or conversely mark a device 'map available' in self_check when the geometry it validated belongs to a different robot or floor.

title: image_entity_object silently drops the only per-vacuum candidate root on any HA-internals change, while the presence gate still reports the map as present
observed_behavior: image_entity_object reaches into a private HA internal — `hass.data.get('entity_components').get('image').get_entity(entity_id)` (:770-772) — behind a bare `except Exception: return None` (:773-774) with no logging, and returns None on three separate silent paths: the `entity_components` key missing, no `image` component registered, or `get_entity` absent. There is no public by-id entity-object API, so the docstring's 'best-effort + defensive' is accurate about the mechanism but the DEGRADATION is the problem: roborock_candidates (:1021-1023) does `ent = image_entity_object(...); if ent is not None: out.append(...)` — a None simply omits the candidate, with no log and no marker. The result is not a loud failure but a QUIETER WRONG ANSWER: the walk falls through to the account-wide runtime_data / hass.data roots (RB-2) and returns some robot's map. Meanwhile the presence gate is independent — _resolve_live_map_image_entity (core/manager.py:4370/4383) only calls `hass.states.get(candidate) is not None`, so `present` stays True and roborock_result_from_candidates proceeds as if all is well. The `diag['candidates']` breadcrumb (:729) is the only trace, and it records an ABSENCE (the `image_entity:...` label simply not being in the list) — the one shape of evidence an operator scanning a log for an error will not notice.
user_impact: An HA core refactor of the entity-component registry (or an image platform load order change) turns the per-vacuum map lookup into an account-wide guess with no error, no warning log, and a presence gate that still says the map is available. On a single-vacuum install this happens to keep working, which is why it would ship unnoticed; on a multi-vacuum install it silently produces another robot's map (see RB-2).
guards_checked: image_entity_object (:760-775) — bare except with no _LOGGER call, three silent None paths; roborock_candidates (:1019-1023) — `if ent is not None` append, no else, no log; map_source_coordinator.async_refresh_map_state_source (:167-173) — computes `present` from _resolve_live_map_image_entity and passes live_img on, but never checks whether the entity OBJECT resolved; _resolve_live_map_image_entity (core/manager.py:4349-4385) — hass.states existence only, documented in the notes as passing even for an `unavailable` entity; roborock_result_from_candidates diagnostics (:729, :738) — records candidate labels and mapdata_at, but an omitted candidate is an absence rather than a signal; tests/unit/test_map_source_collectors.py:293-334 — five tests pin that each failure path returns None, i.e. the silent degradation is asserted as the intended contract.

confirmations: CONFIRMED. image_entity_object:769-775 reaches a private HA internal behind a bare except with no logging and three silent None paths; roborock_candidates:1020-1023 appends it only 'if ent is not None' with no else and no marker, so the failure degrades to the account-wide roots rather than to an error. The presence gate is genuinely independent — _resolve_live_map_image_entity is a hass.states existence check, documented in the repo's own note as passing even for an unavailable entity. DOWNGRADED to LOW: the trigger is a hypothetical HA-core registry refactor, the single-vacuum case is unaffected, and the multi-vacuum consequence is already reported as RB-2. The finder's own citation that five tests pin these None paths as the intended contract also argues this is a design-observability gap, not a defect.

CONFIRMED. image_entity_object (:769-775) reaches into hass.data['entity_components']['image'].get_entity behind a bare `except Exception: return None` with no _LOGGER call and three silent None paths, and roborock_candidates (:1021-1023) simply omits the candidate with no else and no marker. The degradation is a quieter wrong answer (fall through to account-wide roots) rather than a loud failure, while _resolve_live_map_image_entity keeps present=True off a states existence check. Correctly rated LOW: latent, triggered only by an HA-internals change, and benign on a single-vacuum install.

title: _walk and _structure_tree can only descend objects exposing __dict__, so a slotted/C-extension node is both an undiscoverable dead end and an uninformative diagnostic
observed_behavior: _walk's object branch is `attrs = getattr(obj, '__dict__', None); if isinstance(attrs, dict): children = [...]` (:260-266) — an object defined with `__slots__` (or an attrs `@define` class, or a C-extension/pydantic-private object) yields no `__dict__`, so children is [] and the subtree below it is invisible. _structure_tree has the identical branch (:317-333) and falls through to `return tname` (:334), i.e. it prints a bare type name. The whole Roborock backend is explicitly designed as 'deploy-and-discover' — the module docstring (:9-13) says 'The exact attribute path is NOT knowable offline, so this is a DEFENSIVE introspector that ... ALWAYS attaches a diagnostics breadcrumb — the live deploy is what confirms/tunes the path'. That contract fails exactly where it is needed: a slotted node produces `no_parsed_map` (:756), which is byte-for-byte the same result as 'the data genuinely is not there', and the structure dump shows only the class name with no hint that traversal was blocked. Note the code already has the vocabulary for this — `show_skipped` (:288, :326-329) marks denylisted attrs as '(skipped)' so an operator can tell 'exists but not traversed' from 'absent' — but the same distinction is not made for un-traversable objects.
user_impact: When a python-roborock or HA core release moves the map behind a slotted container, the Roborock map source goes absent with reason `no_parsed_map` and a diagnostics dump that gives the maintainer nothing to tune — the failure looks like 'the vacuum has no map' rather than 'the introspector could not walk here'.
guards_checked: _walk (:236-271) — read in full: dict / list-tuple / __dict__ are the only three child sources, no __slots__ handling, no dir()/getattr fallback; _structure_tree (:287-334) — same three branches, returns a bare tname otherwise; show_skipped (:288, :326-329) — exists and solves the analogous denylist case, proving the distinction was considered but not extended; roborock_result_from_candidates (:749-757) — attaches the structure tree but has no way to flag an untraversable node; _WALK_SKIP_ATTRS (:224-228) — a name denylist, unrelated to this.

confirmations: CONFIRMED as written. _walk:260-266 sources children only from dict / list-tuple / obj.__dict__, so a __slots__ / attrs / C-extension node yields no children and its subtree is invisible; _structure_tree:317-334 has the identical branch and falls through to a bare type name. The resulting no_parsed_map (:756) is byte-identical to 'the data genuinely is not there', and show_skipped (:288, 326-329) proves the exists-but-not-traversed distinction was already considered for the denylist and simply not extended. Purely latent; LOW is correct. (Note this also bounds RB-1/RB-3: if the roborock traits expose their maps as properties rather than __dict__ fields, this walk reaches none of them.)

CONFIRMED by reading _walk (:254-266) and _structure_tree (:317-334): dict / list-tuple / __dict__ are the only three child sources, so a __slots__, attrs-@define, C-extension or pydantic-private node yields no children and the subtree is invisible, while the diagnostic dump prints a bare type name. The observation that show_skipped (:288, :326-329) already solves the analogous denylist case — proving the 'exists but not traversed' distinction was considered and not extended — is a fair reading. Latent diagnosability gap, no current failure.

title: correspondences_from_mapdata's docstring claims clamped corners are skipped; the code feeds them into the least-squares fit, turning a rare edge case into an unexplained zone refusal
observed_behavior: The docstring states 'bad/clamped corners are simply skipped (the converter's round-trip check guards the rest)' (:534-535). The code has no such guard: proj (map_source_runtime.py:461-468) returns `[_clamp01(p.x/img_w), _clamp01(p.y/img_h)]`, and _clamp01 (map_source.py:158-159) is `min(max(v,0.0),1.0)` — it returns a perfectly valid pair for an out-of-range input, so `if p:` at :553 is always true for a numeric projection and the clamped point is appended as if it were an exact correspondence. Since correspondences_from_mapdata feeds an unweighted least-squares fit (zone_dispatch.fit_normalized_to_mm:47-77), a clamped corner is an outlier that biases the whole affine, and max_residual_mm then measures the fit against that same corrupted point set. Arithmetic: a corner whose true normalized x is 1.004 on a 1024 px raster at 50 mm/px clamps to 1.0, a 0.004 x 1024 x 50 = 205 mm error — four times validate_tol_mm (50 mm), so normalized_rects_to_mm returns None and dispatch/manager.py:158-163 raises 'could not place the drawn zone on the device coordinate frame'. The safety outcome is correct (refuse, not mis-dispatch) — but the docstring's claimed mechanism does not exist, so the failure mode is a hard refusal instead of the documented graceful skip.
user_impact: If any room bbox corner projects outside the rendered image (rotation/trim edge cases), zone cleaning refuses with 'map projection failed validation' for the whole vacuum and no diagnostic points at the single bad corner — where the documented behaviour would have dropped that corner and fitted on the rest.
guards_checked: correspondences_from_mapdata (:527-558) — read in full: the only skips are `None in (x0,y0,x1,y1)` (:549) and the float() TypeError/ValueError (:554-557); neither detects a clamp; _mapdata_projector.proj (:461-468) — clamps rather than rejecting, and its own docstring says proj 'returns None on any per-point failure (incl. None coords)' which does not cover an out-of-range value; _clamp01 (map_source.py:158) — unconditional min/max, no sentinel; fit_normalized_to_mm (dispatch/zone_dispatch.py:47-77) — unweighted normal equations, no outlier rejection; max_residual_mm / normalized_rects_to_mm (:85-120) — validate_tol_mm 50.0 catches the corrupted fit, which is why this is LOW rather than a wrong-place bug.

confirmations: CONFIRMED — same docstring/code mismatch as A2-GEO-4, verified independently. The claim at map_source_runtime.py:534-535 that clamped corners are skipped has no implementation: proj:461-468 clamps and returns a valid pair, so 'if p:' at :553 is always true and the clamped point enters the unweighted least-squares fit (dispatch/zone_dispatch.py:47-77), which max_residual_mm then measures against the same corrupted set. The safety OUTCOME is correct (refuse at 50 mm tolerance, dispatch/manager.py refuses on None), which is why LOW is right. Duplicate of A2-GEO-4; GEO-4 additionally proves it is unreachable under the shipped MapParserConfig (scale 4, no rotate/trim).

CONFIRMED, same false docstring as A2-GEO-4 (map_source_runtime.py:534-535 vs proj at :461-468, where _clamp01 always yields a valid pair so `if p:` at :553 is always true). The two reports differ only in which downstream consequence they emphasise; RB-8's 'hard refusal instead of the documented graceful skip' is the correct characterisation given max_residual_mm at validate_tol_mm=50.0 does catch the corrupted fit. Duplicate finding — count it once.

title: Live pose is normalized and room-looked-up against .storage geometry while the map it is drawn on is memory-PRIMARY — the one reader never repointed
observed_behavior: Every other Eufy reader in this subsystem was repointed to the fork's in-memory `_map_data` (P2 repoint): `_refresh_eufy_map_source` (L397-443) builds rooms from `mapdata_dict_from_obj(mem['obj'])` and then calls `_apply_inmem_pose_to_result(result, map_data=<that same in-memory dict>)`; `async_get_map_render_data` (L643-653) returns `render_data_from_storage(mem['map_data'])`; `async_get_map_data_dict` (L688-695) is memory-primary. `_load_live_pose_geom` (L476-498) is the sole survivor: it resolves `eufy_store_path` and returns `(store_json['data'])['map_data']` from the .storage FILE. `async_get_map_live_pose` (L520-527) then feeds that .storage map_data into `live_pose_overlay`, which uses it for BOTH `normalize_rendered(px,py,width,height)` and `current_room_for_pixel(map_data, px, py)` — while the robot pixel it is normalizing (`_robot_pixel`) was computed by the fork against the IN-MEMORY map's origin/res. The two map_data dicts are byte-identical in steady state (the P1 compare probe proved that), but they diverge whenever the in-memory map changes ahead of the fork's throttled store save: a re-segmentation or grid expansion changes width/height/origin_x/origin_y/room_outline_origin_*. This same device is documented to have gone from a room_outline offset of +105 cells (map_source.py:230 docstring) to 0 offset after a re-segmentation. Arithmetic with those two observed geometries and a live robot pixel (200,150) in the NEW frame: correct raster index rx=200-0=200; the .storage path computes rx=200-105=95 — a lookup 105 cells = 5.25 m to the left, returning a different room's id (or None). If the grid also resized (360x300 -> 420x340) the anchor moves too: nx=200/360=0.5556 served vs 200/420=0.4762 correct (8% of map width), ny=(300-1-150)/300=0.4967 vs (340-1-150)/340=0.5559 (6%). The live `path` (`normalize_trail`) rides the same dims. This is NOT display-only: listeners/pose_sampler.py:197 calls `async_get_map_live_pose` every ~2 s during a run and buffers `pose.get('current_room')` into `pose_samples`, which learning/external_ingest.py `_attribute` / `_apply_pose_identity` (L737, L768) consume to decide which rooms an external run cleaned and to stamp segment room identity.
user_impact: During the window between a map re-segmentation/expansion and the fork's next throttled store save, the card draws the robot dot and live trail in a different coordinate frame than the map underneath it, the current-room highlight lands on the wrong room, and — silently, with no error — every pose sample buffered for room attribution carries the wrong room id, so an external run's learned per-room history is written against rooms the robot never entered.
guards_checked: `_live_pose_geom_cache` mtime check (L487) — caches the storage read, never reconciles frames. `_apply_inmem_pose_to_result` (L292-328) — this IS the correct pattern (pose normalized against the same map_data that produced the rooms, on both the memory and the storage-fallback branch), which is what proves the asymmetry. `current_room_for_pixel`'s bounds check `0 <= rx < ro_w and 0 <= ry < ro_h` (map_source.py:422) — only rescues when the mismatched index falls off the raster entirely; an in-range wrong index returns a wrong room with no signal. `_CATCH_ALL_RID` filter (map_source.py:432) — id-value filter only. `compare_map_data` / `async_compare_map_sources` (L530-572) — a manual diagnostic service; `normalization_safe` is never consulted at runtime. `_commit_result`'s map_id guard (L117) — the pose service never touches that cache. pose_sampler `_is_parked` / `_read_live_pose_sample` (pose_sampler.py:108-209) — nulls current_room only when task_status says parked; a wrong-but-non-null room while actively cleaning passes straight into the buffer.

Every other Eufy reader in the coordinator is memory-primary (_refresh_eufy_map_source:397-443, async_get_map_render_data:643-653, async_get_map_data_dict:687-695); _load_live_pose_geom:476-498 is the sole survivor reading .storage only, and its output feeds BOTH normalize_rendered and current_room_for_pixel inside live_pose_overlay while the pixel came from the fork's in-memory frame. _apply_inmem_pose_to_result:292-328 IS the correct pattern (pose normalized against the map_data that produced the rooms) and the pose service bypasses it. title: `stale` / `stale_since` / `stale_reason` are written by the hold path and read by nothing — the docstring's "the card dims/badges it" is false
observed_behavior: `_commit_result` holds a last-known-good PRESENT result through a transient dropout and stamps `held['stale']=True`, `held['stale_since']`, `held['stale_reason']` (L127-129), keeping `present: True` and — by design, per its own docstring — freezing the whole prior pose (`robot_anchor`, `dock_anchor`, `current_room`, `path`) with it, for up to `_STALE_MAP_TTL_SECONDS = 6*3600` (L45). The docstring asserts "the last-good map is kept and flagged `stale` (the card dims/badges it and freezes the pose)". Only the freeze half is real. A repo-wide search for `stale` / `stale_since` / `stale_reason` across src/ and custom_components/ returns exactly the three WRITE sites in this function and zero readers: the card's `mapStateSource()` / `mapOverlayData()` (src/state/map.js:1055-1077) never inspects the flag, and `sensor/map_overlays.py` copies a fixed key list into attrs (`dock_anchor`, `robot_anchor`, `robot_heading`, `no_go`, `no_mop`, `walls`, `zones`, `obstacles` — L105-110) that excludes all three, so the flag is not even exposed to templates/automations. `native_value` (map_overlays.py:72-84) branches only on `res.get('present')`, which a held result still satisfies, and returns the FROZEN `current_room`'s room name as the sensor STATE — the recorded value (only attributes are in `_unrecorded_attributes`).
user_impact: When the map source drops out transiently — the documented Roborock case is the cloud map entity going unavailable as the vacuum idles/docks, reason `no_parsed_map` — the map-overlays sensor keeps reporting the last room the robot was seen in as its live state, writing it into the recorder's room-over-time history for up to six hours, and the card keeps drawing the frozen robot/dock/trail as live. Nothing anywhere tells the user, an automation, or a template that the data is held rather than current.
guards_checked: `_MAP_SOURCE_HARD_CLEAR_REASONS` (L50-55) — only clears on structural reasons (`live_map_absent`, `store_version_mismatch`, `not_configured`, `no_device`); `no_parsed_map` / `no_room_geometry` / `refresh_error` are explicitly the held cases. The `cached.get('map_id') == str(map_id)` guard (L117) — prevents cross-map serving, not staleness disclosure. The TTL fall-through (L134) — bounds the hold at 6 h but says nothing during it. `sensor/map_overlays.py` `_UNRECORDED` (L29-32) and the `if not res.get('present')` early return (L97-99) — the absent branch surfaces `reason`, but a held result is `present: True` and never reaches it. src/state/map.js `mapOverlayData` (L1055) and `mapImageSize` (L1082) — read `present`, `image_size`, `current_room`, `path`, never `stale`.

confirmations: CONFIRMED — same defect as A1-LC-2, verified by the same grep: three write sites in _commit_result, zero readers anywhere in src/ or custom_components/. The sensor half is the part not covered by the repo's own 'card badge approved, not built' note: sensor/map_overlays.py native_value returns the frozen room NAME as the recorded state (only attributes are in _unrecorded_attributes) and the three stale keys are not exposed as attributes at all, so no template or automation can detect the hold either. _MAP_SOURCE_HARD_CLEAR_REASONS deliberately excludes the transient reasons, so the documented Roborock dock dropout always takes this path.

CONFIRMED — duplicate of A1-LC-2, verified by the same exact-key grep: stale/stale_since/stale_reason appear ONLY at map_source_coordinator.py:119,127,128,129 and nowhere in src/ or any other Python module. sensor/map_overlays.py attrs (105-110) do not include them, so they are not even template/automation-visible, and native_value (72-84) branches only on `present`, returning the frozen room name as the RECORDED state (only attributes are in _unrecorded_attributes). The docstring's 'the card dims/badges it' is false about the current code.

title: The pose-geometry .storage read skips the `store_version` guard that every other reader of the same file applies
observed_behavior: Both other readers of the fork's Store file version-guard it before trusting `data.map_data`: `eufy_result_from_store` (map_source_runtime.py:128-131) returns `store_version_mismatch` — a HARD-CLEAR reason (`_MAP_SOURCE_HARD_CLEAR_REASONS`, L50-55) that also raises a WARNING at L274-279 — and `eufy_render_data_from_store` (map_source_runtime.py:198-199) does the same. `_load_live_pose_geom` reads the identical file through the identical `load_store_json` and pulls `(store_json.get('data') or {}).get('map_data')` (L491-492) with no version comparison at all, even though `source_cfg` (which carries `store_version`) is right there in its signature. Because the Eufy path is memory-PRIMARY, a fork schema bump never surfaces: `_refresh_eufy_map_source` reads the in-memory MapData and never calls `eufy_result_from_store`, so the map renders correctly and the mismatch WARNING is never logged — while the pose service silently normalizes the robot pixel and does the room raster lookup against a map_data dict from a schema the adapter has explicitly declared it does not understand. The codebase anticipates exactly this event throughout ("the fork may bump it at the pending #136 merge", adapter.py:633-634; `field_attrs` drift remapping; `_as_int` type coercion).
user_impact: After a fork store-schema bump, the map keeps rendering correctly from memory while the robot dot, the live trail and the current-room highlight are computed from stale-schema geometry — and the one designed signal for that condition (the `store_version_mismatch` warning) never fires, so the wrongness is undetectable from the logs.
guards_checked: `eufy_result_from_store` version guard (map_source_runtime.py:128) and `eufy_render_data_from_store` version guard (map_source_runtime.py:198) — both bypassed on this path. `_LOGGER.warning` on mismatch (L273-279) — only reachable via `_refresh_storage_map_source`, which the shipped memory-primary Eufy config only enters on a memory miss. `isinstance(map_data, dict)` (L493) — a shape check, not a schema check. `_load_live_pose_geom`'s `if not map_data: return None` in the caller (L521) — only catches a missing block, not a reshaped one.

confirmations: Inconsistency CONFIRMED. eufy_result_from_store:128-131 and eufy_render_data_from_store:198-199 both version-guard the same Store file (and store_version_mismatch is a hard-clear reason that also logs a WARNING at coordinator:273-279), while _load_live_pose_geom:489-493 reads the identical file through the identical load_store_json and pulls data.map_data with no version comparison, despite source_cfg being in its signature. Memory-primary means _refresh_eufy_map_source never calls eufy_result_from_store on the shipped Eufy path, so the designed warning would indeed never fire. DOWNGRADED to LOW: the trigger is a fork Store-schema bump that has not happened (the live store is version 1, matching the adapter's declared store_version 1), so this is a latent guard-parity gap rather than a reachable wrong result.

CONFIRMED as an asymmetry: eufy_result_from_store (map_source_runtime.py:128-131) and eufy_render_data_from_store (:198-199) both version-guard the same file and the first raises a WARNING (coordinator.py:273-279), while _load_live_pose_geom (:491-492) pulls data.map_data with no version comparison despite source_cfg being in its signature. The observation that memory-primary means the mismatch WARNING never fires is a genuinely sharp catch. But the trigger is a future fork store-schema bump that has not happened — latent robustness gap, not a live wrong result.

title: The live pose carries no freshness stamp, so a frozen `_robot_pixel` is reported as `present: True` forever — and the fork's own `_last_robot_render` timestamp is ignored
observed_behavior: `eufy_live_pose_from_candidates` (map_source_runtime.py:910-917) returns `{present, robot_pixel, dock_pixel, robot_heading, trail_pixels, diagnostics}` — no timestamp, no sequence number. `_read_inmem_pose` (L453-474) adds none, and `async_get_map_live_pose` returns `{'present': True, **overlay, 'diagnostics': ...}` (L528) — also none. `present` is computed purely as `robot is not None or dock is not None`, i.e. from ATTRIBUTE EXISTENCE, so a `_robot_pixel` the fork stopped updating is indistinguishable from a live one. This is observed behaviour, not hypothesis: pose_sampler.py:114-120 documents that the pose "sat reporting the robot 'in' the dock room for ~13 min after a `Completed` dock, so 100 dock-sitting ticks were recorded as that room". The freshness signal exists and is unread — the confirmed live structure dump of the fork's EufyCleanCoordinator lists `_last_robot_render` (a float) alongside `_robot_pixel`/`_dock_pixel`/`_robot_trail`, and the adapter's `live_pose` block (adapter.py:659-665) declares `robot_pixel_attrs`/`dock_pixel_attrs`/`trail_pixel_attrs`/`heading_attrs` but no timestamp attr. Separately, the pose is read synchronously at L514 and then an `await` (L520, an executor stat plus possibly a ~200 KB JSON read) precedes the return, while the card polls on a bare `setInterval(tick, 2000)` with no in-flight guard (src/cards/vacuum-map-host.js:180-199) and `setLivePose` unconditionally assigns (src/state/map.js:1036) — with no stamp on the payload, an overlapping slow/fast pair of polls silently lets an older pose overwrite a newer one.
user_impact: When the fork's map/pose channel stalls while the state channel keeps flowing, the card shows a confident live robot dot parked at a position the robot left long ago, and the pose sampler records that same wrong room every tick into the run's attribution buffer — with no staleness indicator anywhere and no way for a consumer to tell a stationary robot from a dead feed.
guards_checked: pose_sampler `_is_parked` (pose_sampler.py:108-129) — rescues the sampler only when the adapter declares `entities.task_status` AND its state is readable and non-unknown; its documented fallback is `bool(pose.get('robot_docked'))`, the very flag the same comment says "can stay False through a real dock". `_POSE_STALL_COALESCE_TICKS` / `_POSE_STALL_ANCHOR_EPS` / `_POSE_STALL_AREA_EPS_M2` (jobs/active_job.py:116-128) — collapses a static tail only when `cleaning_area` is ALSO flat, so a stalled pose channel while the DPS cleaning_area counter keeps climbing is explicitly not coalesced. `_commit_result`'s stale-hold/TTL machinery (L105-135) — applies to the map_state_source cache only; `async_get_map_live_pose` never consults it. src/cards/vacuum-map-host.js:187 `if (resp == null) return` — handles a WS drop, not a stale-but-valid payload.

confirmations: CONFIRMED, including the unread-signal claim which I checked in the fork: eufy-clean coordinator.py:160 does carry self._last_robot_render (a float) alongside _robot_pixel/_dock_pixel/_robot_trail, and the adapter's live_pose block declares no timestamp attr, so the freshness signal exists and is genuinely unread. eufy_live_pose_from_candidates:910-917 returns no timestamp or sequence number, and _read_inmem_pose / async_get_map_live_pose add none. The observed 13-minute post-dock ghost is documented in the repo's own pose_sampler comment (:114-120). Card-side overlap risk confirmed: the poll is a bare setInterval with setLivePose assigning unconditionally (src/state/map.js:1036). ONE nit: present is value-derived (robot/dock resolved to a numeric pair), not purely attribute-existence — only the HOLDER match is existence-based; the substance (a frozen-but-valid pixel is indistinguishable from a live one) stands.

CONFIRMED as code: eufy_live_pose_from_candidates (:910-917) returns no timestamp and computes `present` as `robot is not None or dock is not None` — pure attribute existence — and the fork's `_last_robot_render` float does exist (robovac_mqtt/coordinator.py:499) and is not declared in the adapter's live_pose block. The card's bare setInterval with no in-flight guard is also real. But the headline symptom (the documented 13-minute dock ghost) is already mitigated by pose_sampler._is_parked's MQTT task_status primary, and no current failure is demonstrated for a moving robot — the concern is a stalled map/pose channel, which is hypothesised rather than observed. Latent.

title: `_refresh_storage_map_source`'s mtime early-return bypasses the live-pose override entirely, re-serving the frozen pose it exists to kill
observed_behavior: The live-pose override is applied at L285-287, AFTER the mtime cache check at L260-266. When the Store file is unchanged and the presence gate matches, the method does a bare `return cached['result']` — it never calls `_apply_inmem_pose_to_result`, and it never reaches `_commit_result`. The returned result therefore carries the `robot_anchor` / `current_room` / `path` that were layered on whenever the file last changed, not the fresh in-memory pose. This is the exact "stale in the kitchen ghost" the feature was built to eliminate (map_source.py:568-570), reintroduced by the caching layer above it. Reachable on any install whose adapter declares `live_pose` without a `memory` block (the branch the code itself labels "legacy / other forks", L192-196), and on the shipped Eufy adapter whenever the in-memory MapData misses twice in a row and `_refresh_eufy_map_source` falls through to this method (L414-417, L428-431) — the fork's store save is throttled, so between saves the mtime is stable while the robot moves. The same early return also omits the `cached.get('map_id') == str(map_id)` check that `_commit_result` applies four lines away with the comment "never serve another map's geometry" (L117), so an active-map change that has not yet reached the store file serves the previous map's rooms and pose under the new map_id.
user_impact: On the storage backend the dashboard snapshot and the map-overlays sensor report the robot at a position and in a room it left minutes ago, with no error and no staleness marker — and the sensor's recorded room-over-time history inherits the frozen value.
guards_checked: `_commit_result` (L78-137) — never invoked on this branch, so neither its map_id guard nor its stale stamping runs. `cached.get('present_gate') == present` (L262) — covers the live-map artifact appearing/disappearing, not pose movement. `mtime is not None` (L261) — only forces a re-read when the stat failed. `_apply_inmem_pose_to_result` (L285) — correct, but unreachable past the early return. `_refresh_eufy_map_source`'s `_commit_result(..., present_gate=present)` with no mtime (L449-451) — stores `mtime: None`, which does prevent a memory-path commit from being served by this cache, but does nothing once two storage reads run back to back.

confirmations: CONFIRMED — same code path as A1-LC-4, verified directly: the bare 'return cached["result"]' at line 266 precedes _apply_inmem_pose_to_result at 285 and never reaches _commit_result, so neither the fresh pose nor the map_id guard at 117 nor the stale stamping runs on that branch. Reachability confirmed on the legacy/other-fork branch (coordinator:192-196, live_pose without a memory block) and on the shipped Eufy adapter whenever the in-memory MapData misses (414-417, 428-431). I also confirmed the memory path commits with mtime=None (449-451), which correctly prevents a memory-path commit from satisfying this cache — so the early return only fires between two consecutive storage reads, exactly as described.

CONFIRMED as code — duplicate of A1-LC-4, same line-266 early return skipping both _apply_inmem_pose_to_result (285) and _commit_result's map_id guard (117). Same reachability limitation applies: on the shipped Eufy adapter this branch runs only after an in-memory MapData miss, and no shipped adapter declares live_pose without memory. Real on a fallback path.

title: `resolve_furnished_render` passes a stored placement transform through with no map-geometry stamp, so a re-mapped floor plan silently misaligns the art
observed_behavior: `resolve_furnished_render` returns `home_art.transform` and each room's `transform` / `viewport` exactly as stored ("Transforms/viewports are stored resolution-independent (pct floats) and passed through untouched", L94-96). The stored value is `{tx, ty, scale, rotation}` in percent of the natural map frame (mapping_services.py:1975-1986; src/state/map.js:449-459 "pct, natural frame"), and the card paints it over the map backdrop, whose extent is the raw device grid (`width` x `height` from map_data). Resolution independence protects against a display-size change; it does NOT protect against the FRAME changing shape. When the device re-segments or expands the grid — the same device is documented going 360x300 with a +105-cell outline offset to 360x300 with none — the physical home occupies a different fraction of, and sits at a different offset within, the normalized frame, while tx/ty/scale stay fixed. A 360x300 to 420x340 expansion leaves the same house covering 360/420 = 86% of the frame width, so art authored to fill the old frame overhangs by ~14% of frame width (about 3 m on an 18 m map) plus the origin-shift offset. Nothing in the codebase stamps stored user geometry with a map version: `eufy_version_of` (L621-628) exists and produces exactly the content hash needed, but a repo-wide search shows its only consumer is `render_data_from_storage` (L654) for client-side cache-busting — no layout, no `home_art`, no `art_placement_transform` and no `viewport` records which map geometry it was authored against, and `resolve_furnished_render` has no staleness output to return.
user_impact: After the vacuum re-maps or expands its floor plan, the furnished digital-twin art keeps rendering at its old placement over a map that has moved and rescaled underneath it — off by metres — with nothing in the payload, the log, or the UI indicating the saved placement no longer matches the map it was aligned to.
guards_checked: `segmentation_mode == 'custom'` gate (L103) and the active-layout resolution (L105-109) — select WHICH layout is projected, not whether it still fits the map. `_furnished_art_url` (L69-83) — validates only that the variant resolves to a browser_url. `_FURNISHED_FIELDS` presence filter (L115-121) — an existence test. `layout.get('render_mode') or 'live'` (L141) — a mode default. `eufy_version_of` (L621) — the available signal, confirmed unused outside `render_data_from_storage`. `set_furnished_art_placement` (mapping_services.py:1968-1990) — clamps scale to [0.05, 20] and stamps `updated_at`, but records no map geometry.

confirmations: CONFIRMED. resolve_furnished_render:139-144 returns home_art.transform and each room's transform/viewport untouched, and its own docstring states they are passed through resolution-independent — which protects against a display-size change but not against the map FRAME changing extent or origin. I verified the missing stamp by grep: eufy_version_of exists and produces exactly the content hash needed, and its ONLY consumer in the entire component is render_data_from_storage:654 for client-side cache-busting — no layout, home_art, art_placement_transform or viewport record which map geometry they were authored against, and set_furnished_art_placement (mapping_services.py:1968-1990) stamps only updated_at. resolve_furnished_render has no staleness output to return even if a caller wanted one. MEDIUM is fair: user-visible misalignment after a re-map with nothing indicating why.

CONFIRMED as a code property: resolve_furnished_render (map_source.py:86-144) passes home_art.transform and per-room transform/viewport through untouched with no map-geometry stamp, and eufy_version_of (:621-628) — the available content hash — is consumed only by render_data_from_storage (:654), so no stored placement records which map geometry it was authored against. The pct-in-natural-frame storage protects against display-size changes but not against the frame itself changing shape. However this is a known-open design item (the memory index records the furnished-twin 're-align open') and the impact is user-authored decorative art rendering out of place — no robot behaviour, no data destroyed, and visibly obvious to the user rather than silent.

title: An off-grid robot pixel is clamped onto the map edge and reported as a confident anchor — "off the map" is indistinguishable from "at the edge"
observed_behavior: `live_pose_overlay` validates the pixel with `_numeric_pair` (L579), which is a TYPE check only — it enforces a 2-element sequence of non-bool numbers and imposes no range. The value then goes to `normalize_rendered` (L183-193), whose `_clamp01` silently pins any out-of-grid coordinate to 0.0 or 1.0. With the live 360x300 grid and a robot pixel of (500, 120): nx = _clamp01(500/360 = 1.389) = 1.0, ny = (300-1-120)/300 = 0.5967, so `robot_anchor` is emitted as [1.0, 0.597] — the right-hand map edge — with no marker distinguishing it from a robot genuinely there. The companion lookup does detect the condition: `current_room_for_pixel` computes rx = 500 - ro_dx and rejects it via `0 <= rx < ro_w` (L422), returning None, so `current_room` is omitted; `apply_live_pose_override` then POPS the previous `current_room` (L615-616). The two halves therefore disagree by construction — the payload asserts a precise robot position while simultaneously reporting no room — and the caller has no way to tell that from a legitimately off-raster transit pose. The same clamp makes a zero/uninitialised pixel (0, 0) render as [0.0, 0.9999], the bottom-left corner, rather than as unknown. A pixel can leave the grid whenever the pose and the map geometry are momentarily out of step — the fork computes `_robot_pixel` as (pose - origin)/res against the current map, so any of the geometry-divergence conditions in POSE-1 or POSE-3 produce one.
user_impact: A robot whose reported pixel falls outside the map grid is drawn pinned to the map border as if that were its real position, and the live trail accumulates that clamped point (src/state/map.js:1032 `accumulateTrail`), so a genuine "position unknown" renders as a confident wrong position instead of hiding the marker.
guards_checked: `_numeric_pair` (L175-180) — type/arity only, no bounds. `_clamp01` (L158-159) — the clamp itself, silent. `current_room_for_pixel`'s `0 <= rx < ro_w and 0 <= ry < ro_h` (L422) and its `idx >= len(raster)` check (L429) — correctly return None, but only affect `current_room`, never the anchor. `live_pose_overlay`'s `if not (width and height): return out` (L577-578) — guards missing dims, not out-of-range pixels. `apply_live_pose_override`'s `_LIVE_POSE_OWNED_KEYS` pop (L615) — clears the stale room, which is what makes the anchor/room disagreement visible rather than resolving it. `_first_attr_pair` (map_source_runtime.py:796-802) — reuses the same `_xy_pair` type test with no range check.

confirmations: CONFIRMED as a code property with a real (if secondary) trigger. live_pose_overlay:579-582 validates the pixel with _numeric_pair (type/arity only) and normalize_rendered's _clamp01 pins any out-of-grid value to 0.0/1.0, while the companion current_room_for_pixel correctly rejects it via 0<=rx<ro_w and apply_live_pose_override pops the stale current_room — so the payload asserts a precise anchor while reporting no room, by construction. On reachability: the fork's _pose_to_pixel guarantees the pixel is in-grid against the MEMORY map, so an off-grid value arises specifically when the storage geometry the anchor is normalized against is smaller/shifted — i.e. via the POSE-1/EXT-2 frame divergence, which the finder correctly identifies. LOW is right.

The code property is real: live_pose_overlay (map_source.py:579-582) validates the pixel with _numeric_pair (type/arity only) and normalize_rendered's _clamp01 pins any out-of-grid value to 0.0/1.0, while current_room_for_pixel's bound correctly returns None — so the payload asserts a precise anchor while reporting no room, and the caller cannot distinguish that from a legitimate off-raster transit. The finder's own arithmetic (px 500 on W=360 -> nx 1.0) is correct. But I found the guard the finder missed: the fork's _pose_to_pixel (robovac_mqtt/coordinator.py:547-550) returns None unless `0 <= px < width and 0 <= py < height`, so _robot_pixel is never off-grid w.r.t. the CURRENT in-memory map. This is reachable only as a corollary of POSE-1/EXT-2's frame mismatch, which is where the fix belongs. LOW confirmed.

title: end_job has only ONE caller (successful finalize) — every cancel/abort/strand path leaves the tracker permanently stuck on the finished job's map and rooms
observed_behavior: `_active_job[vac]` is cleared in exactly two places: `end_job` (tracker.py:322) and `unregister_vacuum` (tracker.py:272). A repo-wide grep for `end_job` finds exactly one production caller: the `finally` block of the successful-completion branch in listeners/lifecycle.py:335-344. But the job record is cleared by `mark_active_job_finalized` from three other reachable paths that never touch the tracker: jobs/active_job.py:2272 (`async_cancel_active_job`, reached from services/job_control.py:212 user service, listeners/path_blockers.py:153, listeners/pause_timeout.py:78, jobs/phase_runner.py:696) and jobs/active_job.py:2459 (`async_finalize_stranded_job`, reached from listeners/pause_timeout.py:119). After any of these, `tracker._active_job[vac]` still holds the dead job's `{map_id, rooms}`. title: resume_sampling is provably unreachable — _sampling_paused is a one-way latch, so all room attribution stops permanently at the first mid-job recharge
observed_behavior: `_sampling_paused` gates the entire confidence path at tracker.py:382 (`if vacuum_entity_id not in self._sampling_paused`). It is cleared by `resume_sampling` (tracker.py:316), `end_job` (tracker.py:323) and `unregister_vacuum` (tracker.py:275). `resume_sampling` has exactly one production caller: jobs/active_job.py:484. That call sits behind two consecutive `self._is_charging(vacuum_entity_id)` tests inside ONE synchronous method (`update_active_job_recharge_observation`, a plain `def` at jobs/active_job.py:410 with no `await` anywhere in the body). Line 462 reads `if not self._is_charging(vacuum_entity_id): ... return active_job` — so control only reaches line 470 when `_is_charging` is True. Line 472 then reads `if not self._is_charging(vacuum_entity_id):` and gates the `resume_sampling` call at line 484 on it. `_is_charging` (jobs/active_job.py:382-384) is a pure synchronous read of `hass.states`; HA runs a single event loop, so within one synchronous block with no await, nothing can mutate `hass.states` between line 462 and line 472. Both calls provably return the same value, so line 472's condition is always False and line 484 is dead code. The existing test only passes because it manufactures an impossible input: tests/integration/test_jobs_active_job.py:261-262 monkeypatches `_is_charging` with `MagicMock(side_effect=[True, False])` and its own comment names the two call sites ("First charging check (gate) True; second (recharge-ended check) False"), forcing two different answers from a call that cannot differ in production. user_impact: As soon as a run docks for an unplanned low-battery recharge, live per-room attribution dies for the whole rest of the run: no further `eufy_vacuum_room_completed` events, no dwell accrual, and the card's ETA timeline stops reanchoring — silently, with the job still shown as running. title: The HOLD path keeps ACCRUING dwell and movement for a room the robot has already left, inflating duration_seconds and forcing confidence to 1.0
observed_behavior: `_detect_current_room` returns None for three distinct situations (tracker.py:405-425): a blank/sentinel signal, a room flagged `is_transition`, and any room name not present in this job's `rooms` dict. `_update_confidence` treats all three identically as HOLD, and at tracker.py:448-451 does NOT merely hold the room id — it calls `conf_state.update(vx, vy)`, which keeps incrementing `movement_count` and recomputes `time_in_room_seconds` as `(now - entered_at).total_seconds()` (tracker.py:91-105). So wall-clock time and movement samples accumulated while the robot is physically somewhere else are credited to the room it last matched. Arithmetic: robot enters Kitchen at t=0; at t=20s it has logged 3 movement samples, so confidence = min(20/30, 1.0) * min(3/10, 1.0) = 0.6667 * 0.3 = 0.2000 — well under the 0.85 threshold. It then crosses a hallway flagged `is_transition` for 600s, which HOLDs Kitchen on every tick. At t=620s: time_factor = min(620/30, 1.0) = 1.0, movement_count has long passed 10 so move_factor = 1.0, confidence = round(1.0 * 1.0, 4) = 1.0. On entering the Bedroom, tracker.py:456-471 fires room_completed for Kitchen with confidence=1.0 and duration_seconds=round(620.0, 1)=620.0 — for a room the robot occupied for 20 seconds at confidence 0.2. Holding the room ID across a momentary blank is the documented and correct intent (the comment at tracker.py:442-445 says so); continuing to bank NEW dwell credit during the hold is the defect. Freezing the counters during a hold would preserve the true 20s/0.2.
user_impact: src/controllers/learning-controller.js:154-164 reads `duration_seconds`, records it as the room's `actual_duration_minutes` (620/60 = 10.3 min instead of 0.3 min), adds it to `_jobProgress.completedRoomMinutes`, and calls `_reanchorTimeline()`. Every room that precedes a transition room, a dock pass, or any window where the device's native current-room reads blank is reported with a wildly inflated dwell and a fabricated confidence of 1.0, skewing the card's live remaining-time estimate for the rest of the run. Rooms that were barely touched are reported as confidently completed.
guards_checked: Read `_RoomConfidenceState.update` (tracker.py:87-105) and confirmed `time_in_room_seconds` is recomputed from `entered_at` on every call — there is no pause/freeze accumulator. Read `reset_room` (tracker.py:68-75) and confirmed `entered_at` is only re-stamped on an actual room CHANGE, never during a hold. Confirmed the `CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD` gate at tracker.py:458 is applied to the inflated value, so it is not a rescue. Confirmed the `is_transition` skip at tracker.py:418-419 is what routes hallway ticks into the HOLD path rather than into a room change. Confirmed `MOVEMENT_DELTA_THRESHOLD` (10.0 units) does not rescue this: a robot crossing a hallway is moving, so samples clear the threshold easily. Checked the X/Y dedup at tracker.py:386-389 — it only drops exactly-repeated coordinates, so a moving robot is unaffected.

title: _norm_room_name normalises differently from slugify_room_name — it merges room identities that rooms/ keeps distinct, and lacks the NFC canonicalisation slugify was given specifically to prevent this
observed_behavior: Two independent resolvers map the device's native current-room NAME to a room id. `listeners/pose_sampler.py:149-183` uses `slugify_room_name` (rooms/utils.py:11-44): strip, lower, drop `'` and `\"`, `&`->`and`, ` `->`_`, then Unicode NFC. The tracker uses `_norm_room_name` (tracker.py:47-49): strip, lower, then `re.sub(r'[\s_-]+', ' ', ...)`. Two concrete divergences. (a) SEPARATOR MERGE: rooms named "Guest-Room" and "Guest Room" slugify to "guest-room" and "guest_room" — distinct identities that rooms/ and the learning baselines key durable data on separately. `_norm_room_name` maps BOTH the slug and the name of BOTH rooms to the single string "guest room". `_detect_current_room` (tracker.py:417-424) iterates `rooms.items()` and returns the FIRST match, so whichever room happens to come first in dict order absorbs the attribution regardless of which room the device actually named. Note the direction: this is the tracker collapsing identities that rooms/ deliberately keeps apart, which is the opposite of the rooms/ slug-collision defect and is not fixed by fixing rooms/. (b) NO NFC: `slugify_room_name`'s docstring states the NFC step exists precisely because "a brand returning NFD on one firmware and NFC on another" would otherwise derive different keys for the same room. `_norm_room_name` does no Unicode canonicalisation, so a non-ASCII room name arriving decomposed (e.g. Cyrillic U+0418 + U+0306) while `room_data['name']`/`['slug']` are stored precomposed (U+0419) compares byte-unequal on both branches at tracker.py:421-422. pose_sampler matches it; the tracker returns None.
user_impact: Case (a): live dwell is attributed to the wrong room id whenever two rooms' names differ only in a separator character, and the card's reanchored timeline marks the wrong room complete. Case (b): for non-ASCII room names in a decomposed form the tracker never matches, so `_detect_current_room` returns None every tick and — per TRK-3 — the entire run's dwell is credited to whatever room matched last, or nothing is ever attributed if none ever matched. The integration ships 18 language packs, so non-ASCII room names are an expected configuration. In both cases the tracker's answer disagrees with the pose sampler's answer for the same device signal, with no error surfaced.
guards_checked: Read `slugify_room_name` (rooms/utils.py:11-44) in full and compared each transform step against `_norm_room_name` (tracker.py:47-49). Read `_resolve_managed_room_id` (listeners/pose_sampler.py:149-183) and confirmed it is the parallel resolver reading the SAME entity (`entities.active_cleaning_target`) via a different normalisation. Confirmed the tracker's two-branch compare at tracker.py:420-423 (slug OR name) IS a genuine rescue for the apostrophe and `&` cases — verified by hand: name "Kid's Room"/slug "kids_room" matches on the name branch, and "Kitchen and Dining" matches on the slug branch — so I am not reporting those. Confirmed `is_blank_state` (entity_helpers.py:28-41) short-circuits only the five blank sentinels and does not affect these cases. Confirmed `_detect_current_room` returns on first match with no ambiguity detection or tie-break.

confirmations: CONFIRMED by reading both normalizers. slugify_room_name (rooms/utils.py:34-44) does strip/lower, drops ' and ", maps & to 'and', maps space to '_', then NFC — it PRESERVES hyphens, so 'Guest-Room' -> 'guest-room' and 'Guest Room' -> 'guest_room' are distinct durable identities. _norm_room_name (tracker.py:47-49) collapses [\s_-]+ to a single space, mapping both slugs AND both names to 'guest room', and _detect_current_room (:417-425) returns the FIRST dict-order match with no ambiguity detection — so the tracker collapses identities rooms/ deliberately keeps apart. The NFC gap is also real: slugify's docstring states the step exists precisely to survive NFD/NFC firmware differences, _norm_room_name has no unicodedata call, and listeners/pose_sampler.py:167 resolves the SAME entity through slugify_room_name — so the two resolvers genuinely disagree on the same signal. The finder correctly declined to report the apostrophe/& cases, which the name-OR-slug two-branch compare does rescue.

CONFIRMED by reading both normalizers. slugify_room_name (rooms/utils.py:35-44): strip, lower, drop ' and ", &->and, space->_, then unicodedata.normalize('NFC'), with a docstring stating the NFC step exists exactly to stop a brand's NFD/NFC firmware difference deriving different keys. _norm_room_name (tracker.py:47-49): strip, lower, re.sub(r'[\s_-]+', ' ') — no NFC, and it collapses '-' and '_' and space to one character class, so 'Guest-Room' (slug guest-room) and 'Guest Room' (slug guest_room) both normalize to 'guest room' and _detect_current_room (417-425) returns the FIRST dict-order match with no ambiguity detection. Both divergences are real. Downgrading: each requires a specific room-naming configuration (two rooms differing only by separator, or a decomposed non-ASCII name stored precomposed), and the two-branch slug-OR-name compare genuinely rescues the apostrophe/& cases the finder correctly declined to report.

title: Dock-drift append rewrites the entire log file on every reading, and a failed write silently forfeits that drift event via the already-committed _last_dock_pos
observed_behavior: Two issues in the dock-drift path. (1) WRITE AMPLIFICATION: `_append_dock_drift` (tracker.py:173-223) is an append that is implemented as a full read-modify-write — `path.read_text().splitlines()` at line 198 loads the whole file, one record is appended, the list is roll-off trimmed to `DOCK_DRIFT_MAX_LINES = 5000`, then the ENTIRE list is re-serialised and rewritten via `tmp.write_text(...)` at line 218. Once the log saturates at 5001 lines (~90 bytes each, ~450 KB), every single logged reading costs a ~450 KB read plus a ~450 KB write and a rename. This is O(n) per append and O(n²) over the log's life, for a file described in its own comment as "Passive: append-only" — an append that never rewrites would be O(1). (2) LOST EVENT ON FAILURE: `_maybe_log_dock_drift` commits `self._last_dock_pos[vacuum_entity_id] = (vx, vy)` at tracker.py:165 BEFORE dispatching the write to the executor at line 168. If `_append_dock_drift` raises, the in-memory state already claims that position was logged, so the dedup at line 163 suppresses every subsequent identical reading and that drift event is never recoverable. The failure itself is not silent (`_LOGGER.exception` at line 221), but the data loss is unannounced and the `dx`/`dy` chain in the file becomes discontinuous — the next successful record's delta is computed against a position that was never written.
user_impact: On an SD-card or eMMC HA install the rewrite amplification is real flash wear for a purely diagnostic log; the cost scales with how often the reported docked position jitters, which is exactly what the log exists to measure. Separately, the drift timeline the log is meant to provide can contain silent gaps and misleading dx/dy deltas after any transient write error, undermining its diagnostic purpose at the moment it matters.
guards_checked: Confirmed the work runs off the event loop via `hass.async_add_executor_job` (tracker.py:168), so this is NOT blocking I/O on the loop — I am not claiming that. Confirmed `_dock_drift_lock` (tracker.py:135, held at line 184) correctly serialises concurrent executor appends within the instance, and that `tmp.write_text` + `tmp.replace(path)` (tracker.py:217-219) is a correct atomic-rename publish that cannot truncate the log on a crash — neither guard addresses the amplification or the pre-committed dedup state. Confirmed the roll-off logic at tracker.py:210-216 correctly preserves the `_meta` header line while trimming the body, so the cap itself works. Confirmed the dedup at tracker.py:162-164 and the docked/charging state gate at tracker.py:159-161 do bound the write rate to distinct positions only. Confirmed `except Exception` at line 220 uses `_LOGGER.exception`, so the failure is logged rather than swallowed.

confirmations: CONFIRMED, and correctly scoped. _append_dock_drift:196-219 is a full read_text().splitlines() -> append -> roll-off -> tmp.write_text -> replace on EVERY reading, i.e. O(n) per append against a 5000-line cap. The lost-event half is also real: _maybe_log_dock_drift commits self._last_dock_pos at :165 BEFORE dispatching the write at :168, so a raising _append_dock_drift leaves the dedup at :162-164 suppressing every subsequent identical reading and the next record's dx/dy computed against a position never written. The finder correctly does NOT claim loop-blocking (the work is on the executor) and correctly credits _dock_drift_lock and the atomic tmp+replace as real but orthogonal guards. LOW is right for a passive diagnostic log.

CONFIRMED both halves. _append_dock_drift (173-223) implements an append as a full read_text().splitlines() -> append -> roll-off -> tmp.write_text() -> replace, so at the 5000-line cap every logged reading costs a full read plus a full rewrite — O(n) per append for a file its own comment calls 'append-only'. And _maybe_log_dock_drift commits self._last_dock_pos[vid] = (vx, vy) at line 165 BEFORE dispatching the write at 168, so a write failure (logged at 221 but not compensated) leaves the dedup at 162-164 suppressing that reading forever and the next record's dx/dy computed against a position never written. The finder correctly declined to claim blocking-I/O (it is on the executor) and correctly credited the lock and the atomic tmp-rename. Diagnostic-only.

title: start_job/end_job are dispatched to an executor thread on the strength of a comment describing disk I/O that start_job does not perform
observed_behavior: listeners/lifecycle.py:226-237 wraps `tracker.start_job` in `hass.async_add_executor_job` justified by the comment "start_job is sync and performs disk I/O (`_load_samples_from_disk` / `_delete_samples_tmp_file`). Run it on the executor to avoid both the not-awaitable TypeError and the blocking-I/O warning." Neither method exists on `MappingTracker` — I read the class in full and grepped the file; there is no base class. `start_job` (tracker.py:286-310) does exactly three things: pop `_last_recorded_pos`, call `reset_job()`, and assign `_active_job[vac]`. Zero I/O. `end_job` (tracker.py:320-325) is likewise pure dict mutation and is dispatched the same way at listeners/lifecycle.py:339-344 with the comment "kept on the executor to stay off the loop." The comment describes behaviour the code does not have. The consequence is that `_active_job`, `_confidence` and `_last_recorded_pos` — dicts otherwise mutated exclusively from the event loop by the `@callback` `_handle_position_update` (tracker.py:368) — are written from an executor thread. `start_job` in particular calls `reset_job()` before assigning `_active_job`, so a position callback landing between those two statements sees a zeroed confidence state with no job and routes into the dock-drift branch instead of the confidence branch.
user_impact: No user-visible failure proven: the individual dict operations are GIL-atomic and the interleaving window is a handful of bytecodes, so at worst one position sample is misrouted at job start. The real cost is that a false comment currently justifies threading loop-owned mutable state, which is the kind of claim a future change would build on — and it defeats the single-event-loop reasoning that makes the rest of this state machine analysable.
guards_checked: Read `MappingTracker` in full (tracker.py:112-509) and confirmed no `_load_samples_from_disk` or `_delete_samples_tmp_file` member and no base class that could supply one. Confirmed `_handle_position_update` is decorated `@callback` (tracker.py:368), i.e. it runs on the event loop, establishing the cross-thread contact. Confirmed no lock protects `_active_job` or `_confidence` (only `_dock_drift_lock` exists, and it covers the JSONL write alone).

title: current_room_for_pixel truncates toward zero with int() instead of flooring, so a slightly negative pixel resolves to grid cell 0 rather than being rejected as off-map
observed_behavior:
Lines 418-419 do `rx = int(px) - ro_dx` / `ry = int(py) - ro_dy`. Python's int() truncates toward zero, so int(-0.4) = 0 and int(-0.9) = 0, whereas floor gives -1. For px in (-1, 0) the function therefore behaves as if the robot were at main-grid column 0 instead of one column off the grid.

ARITHMETIC: with ro_dx = 0 (the default when room_outline_origin_x is absent, since _outline_geometry line 243 defaults it to origin_x), px = -0.4 gives rx = 0, which passes the `0 <= rx < ro_w` bound at line 422 and returns whatever room id sits at raster cell 0 — a real room id for a pose that is off the map. Flooring would give rx = -1 and correctly return None. The asymmetry also means the truncation direction flips with sign: a pose at px = +0.4 rounds down to cell 0 (correct) while px = -0.4 rounds UP to cell 0 (wrong).

Separately, the anchor passed to normalize_rendered at line 582 of live_pose_overlay is NOT truncated, so the drawn robot dot and the resolved current_room can be derived from sub-pixel-different positions for the same anchor.
user_impact: Narrow: requires a sub-pixel negative robot/trail coordinate, which the fork's integer _robot_pixel does not normally produce. When it does occur the robot is attributed to whichever room owns the raster's first cell instead of reporting 'not in a room', and that id flows into the same attribution stream as GEO-1.
guards_checked: The `except (TypeError, ValueError)` around the conversion (line 420-421) catches non-numeric input only, not sign. The `0 <= rx < ro_w and 0 <= ry < ro_h` bound at line 422 is exactly what the truncation defeats, since it compares the already-truncated value. `idx >= len(raster)` (line 429) only catches a short raster. `0 < rid < _CATCH_ALL_RID` (line 432) filters background/catch-all ids but cell 0 commonly holds a real room. current_room_from_storage (line 443) passes trail[-1] through unvalidated beyond _numeric_pair.

confirmations: The code property is real: map_source.py:418-419 uses int() (truncation toward zero) so int(-0.4) == 0 passes the `0 <= rx < ro_w` bound at 422 and returns cell 0's room instead of None, and the sign asymmetry is genuine. But I found a rescue the finder did not: the fork's _pose_to_pixel (robovac_mqtt/coordinator.py:541-550) returns integers and returns None unless `0 <= px < width and 0 <= py < height`, so _robot_pixel and _robot_trail entries are never negative or fractional. The trigger is therefore essentially unreachable except as a corollary of GEO-1/POSE-1's frame mismatch. LOW confirmed and, if anything, generous.
killed_by: REFUTED — unreachable. int() vs floor only differs for a negative fractional px, and no caller can produce one. I grepped every caller of current_room_for_pixel: only map_source.py:443 (current_room_from_storage, trail[-1]) and :583 (live_pose_overlay, robot_pixel or dock_pixel). All of those originate in the fork's _pose_to_pixel (eufy-clean coordinator.py:541-550), which returns px=round(...) and RETURNS None unless 0<=px<width and 0<=py<height — so every pixel that ever reaches this function is a non-negative integer inside the grid. _dock_pixel is a previously captured _robot_pixel (coordinator.py:358-363) and _robot_trail entries are the same tuples; the .storage copies are those ints re-serialised (coordinator.py:993-995). For every reachable input int(px)==floor(px), and the sub-pixel-disagreement corollary is vacuous for integers. The finder itself concedes 'the fork's integer _robot_pixel does not normally produce' it — there is no path at all, not merely an unusual one.

title: dock_events treats any arrival at a trigger value as a NEW dock cycle — a startup, an entity re-add, or an `unavailable` blip mid-cycle re-records the event and increments the durable counter
observed_behavior: `_handle_dock_event` dedupes only on `new_val == old_val` (line 74), with `old_val = str(old_state.state)... if old_state else ""` (line 72). It never requires that the PREVIOUS value was a real, non-trigger dock state. Three reachable event shapes therefore all read as 'a new cycle started': (a) `old_state is None` — the first state_changed after the dock_status entity is added. The watched entity is NOT ours: adapters/eufy/adapter.py:191 builds `dock_status` from the vacuum entity id, so it belongs to the eufy-clean/robovac_mqtt integration, and manifest.json declares no dependency/after_dependency on it, so eufy_vacuum can register this listener before that entity exists on every HA start. (b) `unknown -> drying` — the brand sensor comes up `unknown` then publishes the in-progress cycle. (c) `unavailable -> drying` / `unavailable -> washing` — an MQTT/cloud blip during a cycle, exactly the transition class HA guarantees will happen. In every case the loop at line 91 matches the trigger set (adapters/eufy/vocabulary.py:78 DOCK_EVENT_TRIGGERS: drying/drying mop/mop drying, washing/washing mop, emptying dust...) and calls `record_dock_event`, which at dock/manager.py:383 unconditionally overwrites `dock_events[vid][event_type] = now` and at :420-424 increments `mop_wash_count`/`dust_empty_count`/`dry_start_count`. The eufy adapter declares `debounce_seconds` for `last_mop_wash` ONLY (adapters/eufy/adapter.py:479-481), so `last_dry_start` and `last_dust_empty` have `debounce = 0.0` -> `should_count = True` with no suppression at all; and even for mop wash the debounce is checked AFTER the timestamp write, so `last_mop_wash` is still reset to the blip time. An X10 Pro Omni dry cycle runs 2-4 hours, so the window for a restart or a blip to land inside one is large and daily. This is the module that diverges: the sibling in listeners/discovery.py:127-131 filters precisely this class ('Only fire on transition INTO docked — filter out ... unknown -> docked startup noise'); dock_events, the only listener of the eight that WRITES durable counters from a raw state arrival, has no such filter.
user_impact: Maintenance data drifts upward silently and permanently: dry-start / dust-empty / mop-wash counts inflate by one per HA restart or connectivity blip that lands inside a dock cycle, and the 'last washed / last dried / last emptied' timestamps shown on the Base Station tab are reset to the moment of the blip rather than the moment of the real cycle. mop_wash_count also feeds the post-job water amendment's `mop_wash_count_at_finalization`, so inflated wash counts propagate into the completed-job water actuals. No error is surfaced anywhere.
guards_checked: listeners/dock_events.py:68 `if new_state is None: return` — only covers entity REMOVAL, not addition. listeners/dock_events.py:74 `if new_val == old_val: return` — defeated because old_val is "" (old_state None) or "unknown"/"unavailable", never equal to the trigger value. listeners/dock_events.py:77 `watched.get(entity_id)` — resolves fine. dock/manager.py:394-419 debounce — declared only for `last_mop_wash`; `_debounce_cfg.get(event_type, 0)` yields 0.0 for dry/empty so `should_count` stays True; and the timestamp write at :383 precedes the debounce block, so even a debounced wash still corrupts the timestamp. adapters/eufy/adapter.py:465-489 dock_events block — confirms triggers are declared and only mop-wash is debounced. custom_components/eufy_vacuum/manifest.json — no dependency on the brand integration, so setup order is arbitrary. tests/integration/test_listeners_state_driven.py:157 covers only the same-value guard; no test exercises old_state=None or unavailable->trigger.

confirmations: CONFIRMED at the code level. dock_events.py:72 maps old_state=None to "" and the only suppression is new_val==old_val (:74), so old_state=None (entity add) and unavailable->drying/washing both reach the trigger loop. dock/manager.py:381-383 writes vacuum_events[event_type]=now BEFORE the debounce block at :394-424, and adapters/eufy/adapter.py:479-481 declares debounce_seconds for last_mop_wash ONLY, so float(_debounce_cfg.get(event_type,0) or 0)==0 for last_dry_start/last_dust_empty and `if debounce > 0` skips the whole check -> should_count stays True. discovery.py:127-131 does carry the sibling filter, so the divergence claim holds. ONE SUB-CLAIM IS WRONG: the finder says inflated mop_wash_count propagates into the post-job water amendment's mop_wash_count_at_finalization. It does not — lifecycle.py:399 reads _water['actual_mop_wash_count'], which learning/job_finalizer.py:204 sets from observed_mop_wash_count (the inline lifecycle detector, i.e. A2-LIFE-3's target), NOT from dock/manager.py's mop_wash_count. Removing that propagation leaves durable maintenance counters + Base Station timestamps as the harm, which is MEDIUM not HIGH. Same defect as A6-GUARD-3 — merge them.

Walked the real code. dock_events.py:72 sets old_val="" when old_state is None and the ONLY suppression is new_val==old_val (:74). Concrete sequence: HA restarts at 02:10 while the X10 Pro Omni is 40 min into a 3 h dry. eufy-clean adds sensor.<vac>_dock_status with old_state=None, new_state="Drying Mop". Handler: new_val="drying mop", old_val="" -> not equal -> proceeds; _triggers from the eufy adapter (adapter.py:465-489, sourced from vocabulary.DOCK_EVENT_TRIGGERS) matches last_dry_start -> record_dock_event. Verified dock/manager.py:381-383 writes vacuum_events["last_dry_start"]=now BEFORE the debounce block, and :394 reads _debounce_cfg which the Eufy adapter populates for last_mop_wash ONLY (adapter.py:479-481) -> debounce=0.0 -> `if debounce > 0` skipped -> should_count stays True -> dry_start_count += 1. Same for unavailable->drying. Confirmed the sibling filter exists in discovery.py:127-131 and is absent here. Severity corrected: the damage is maintenance metadata (counters + last-* timestamps on the Base Station tab, plus mop_wash_count feeding water actuals), not a run outcome or robot action — narrower blast radius than HIGH. Same defect as A6-GUARD-3, aligned to MEDIUM.

title: lifecycle registers a state listener + timer (post-job water amendment) whose unsubs are function-local and unreachable from lifecycle.remove()/async_unload_entry — the only unsub leak among the eight modules
observed_behavior: Inside the lifecycle handler, `_register_post_job_water_amendment(hass, ...)` (lifecycle.py:390) calls core/water_amendment.py, which at lines 243-246 registers `async_track_state_change_event(hass, [dock_status_entity], _on_dock_change)` plus `async_call_later(hass, timeout_seconds, _on_timeout)` and stores both unsubs in the FUNCTION-LOCAL lists `unsub_listener` / `unsub_timeout` (lines 110-111). Nothing writes them into `hass.data[DOMAIN]`, and `lifecycle.remove()` (lifecycle.py:62-71) pops and cancels only `_job_lifecycle_unsubs` — the single `async_track_state_change_event` from `register()`. So `async_unload_entry`'s `lifecycle.remove(hass)` (__init__.py:480) does not cancel them. The only paths that cancel are `_commit()` firing on the adapter's commit_state or the timeout expiring (default `timeout_seconds=180`, lifecycle.py:388). Every one of the other seven modules stores 100% of what it registers in its hass.data unsub list (discovery even stores the `async_at_started` handle), so this is a single-module asymmetry, not a house style. Reachable window: any mop job finalizes, then within 180 s the config entry is unloaded/reloaded (an options change, a HACS update, `_async_update_listener` firing) or the vacuum is deleted via `_teardown_vacuum`. During that window the orphaned callback keeps consuming dock_status state_changed events against a torn-down entry, and `_on_timeout -> _commit -> hass.async_create_task(_flush_amendment())` performs an executor `os.replace` over the completed-job JSON at `job_path` after the integration has been unloaded. Related: `hass.data[DOMAIN]['_water_amendment_jobs']` (water_amendment.py:71) is never popped by `async_unload_entry`, so the `if not domain_data: hass.data.pop(DOMAIN, None)` at __init__.py:545 can never fire once any mop job has been amended.
user_impact: An unloaded/reloaded integration keeps a live state subscription and a pending timer for up to 180 s and rewrites a completed-job learning file after teardown. Because the leaked `_commit` reads the live water_level entity at fire time, a reload mid-window can stamp `water_amended_at` / `actual_*` water figures derived from post-teardown state onto a finished job record; the user sees no error and no indication the write came from a dead entry.
guards_checked: listeners/lifecycle.py:62-71 remove() — pops only `_JOB_LIFECYCLE_UNSUBS`; nothing else. custom_components/eufy_vacuum/__init__.py:480-487 — calls remove() on all eight modules; none of them knows about the amendment. core/water_amendment.py:74-76 job_id idempotency set — prevents duplicate registration for one job, does NOT bound lifetime. core/water_amendment.py:113-125 `_cancel_all()` — exists but is only invoked from `_commit`, i.e. only on commit_state or timeout. core/water_amendment.py:85-91 and :100-107 early-return paths — they `registered_jobs.discard(job_id)` and return BEFORE registering, so a Roborock (no `entities.dock_status`, no `post_job_wash_amendment` block) never reaches the registration and is unaffected. adapters/roborock/adapter.py:668 confirms post_job_wash_amendment is omitted for Roborock (note `_amendment_enabled` in lifecycle.py:373 defaults to True, so the guard that actually saves Roborock is the missing dock_status entity, not the enable flag).

confirmations: CONFIRMED. core/water_amendment.py:110-111 declares unsub_listener/unsub_timeout as FUNCTION-LOCAL lists, :243-246 appends async_track_state_change_event + async_call_later into them, and nothing writes them into hass.data. lifecycle.remove() (lifecycle.py:62-71) pops only _JOB_LIFECYCLE_UNSUBS; I read __init__.py:465-550 async_unload_entry in full and it calls remove() on all eight modules, stops mapping_tracker/battery/error_tracker/coordinator, and cancels nothing else. Also confirmed hass.data[DOMAIN]['_water_amendment_jobs'] (:70-71) is never popped on unload, so __init__.py:545 `if not domain_data` can never fire after any mop job. Roborock is genuinely unaffected — the dock_status early return at :85-91 fires before registration.
