title: Per-vacuum teardown never re-registers listeners, and the documented 'a subscription to a now-deleted entity is inert' invariant is false — discovery keeps running passes for the deleted vacuum and re-creates its setup_progress bucket
observed_behavior: `_teardown_vacuum` (__init__.py:576-631) deliberately does not touch the listeners, resting on the invariant stated at core/manager.py:1051-1053: 'the global listeners self-correct on the next reload/restart — a subscription to a now-deleted entity is inert.' That premise is wrong: the watched entities are built from the vacuum entity id and belong to the BRAND integration (adapters/eufy/adapter.py:190-194), so deleting our device deletes none of them and the subscriptions keep delivering. Four of the eight modules re-derive the vacuum set live from `manager.get_known_vacuum_ids()` on every fire (lifecycle.py:105, pause_timeout.py:68, job_progress.py:64, pose_sampler.py:312) and are genuinely self-correcting; four snapshot it at register() (discovery's `_make_run_pass(vid)` closure at discovery.py:80-96, dock_events' `watched` map at dock_events.py:51-55, job_metrics' `watch_map` at job_metrics.py:77-124, path_blockers' `watch_map` at path_blockers.py:68-91). Three of the four snapshot modules are rescued by accident rather than design — dock_events by `unregister_adapter_config` in `_teardown_vacuum` making `get_adapter_value(...,'dock_events','triggers')` return `{}`; job_metrics because `record_active_job_sensor_value` (jobs/active_job.py:1669) uses `.get()` not `setdefault`. discovery is NOT rescued: its periodic ticker (discovery.py:163-175, adapter-configured interval) and its docked/active-map triggers keep calling `_do()` for the deleted vid, which runs `async_refresh_room_source(hass, vid)` (for Roborock, a `get_maps` service call against a vacuum the user deleted) and `run_discovery_pass` -> `update_drift_history` -> `_get_progress_record` (setup/drift.py:152-159), which unconditionally `setdefault`s `data['setup_progress'][<deleted vid>]` back into storage, then `await manager.async_save()` (discovery.py:88) persists it — silently undoing part of what `remove_vacuum_record` just deleted.
user_impact: After deleting one vacuum from a multi-vacuum install, an orphaned `setup_progress` entry for it is written back to .storage and survives restarts, and a background discovery pass (including a brand service call on Roborock) keeps firing for the removed vacuum until the entry is reloaded or HA restarts. Nothing is user-visible today because the resurrected bucket is empty and `get_known_vacuum_ids()` (manager.py:2966-2969) unions only vacuums/maps/active_jobs — but the invariant the design leans on is not actually held by the code, so any future writer reached from a snapshot-based listener resurrects real data.
guards_checked: core/manager.py:1062-1078 remove_vacuum_record — pops every top-level bucket, but runs once, before these writes, and is never re-run. custom_components/eufy_vacuum/__init__.py:616-621 `unregister_adapter_config(vacuum_entity_id)` — this is what actually neuters dock_events (triggers become {}) and mostly neuters discover_rooms_for_vacuum, but it does not stop `_get_progress_record` from setdefaulting. setup/drift.py:292 `update_drift_history` — calls `_get_progress_record` before any emptiness check, so an empty discovered set still creates the record. listeners/lifecycle.py:104-110 — re-derives matched vacuums per event, confirmed inert for a removed vacuum. jobs/active_job.py:1669 — `.get()` not `setdefault`, confirmed no active_jobs resurrection.

confirmations: CONFIRMED. __init__.py:576-631 _teardown_vacuum never touches the listeners and its docstring states the 'subscription to a now-deleted entity is inert' premise verbatim; core/manager.py:1051-1053 repeats it. discovery.py:80-96 binds vid+manager at register time and its vacuum_docked subscription is on the BRAND's vacuum entity (not deleted) while the periodic ticker (:163-175) is not entity-bound at all. setup/drift.py:144-158 _get_progress_record does root.setdefault(vacuum_entity_id, {...}) unconditionally, update_drift_history (:292+) calls it before any emptiness check, and discovery.py:88 awaits manager.async_save() — so the popped setup_progress bucket is resurrected and persisted. title: dock_events.register() never reads the adapter's `dock_events.enabled` flag — a brand that declares enabled:False but inherits triggers still records dock events
observed_behavior: adapters/config_schema.py:647-654 documents `dock_events.enabled` as 'Whether to record dock events (wash, empty, dry). Set False for brands with no dock actions. Default: False.' The eufy adapter sets it True (adapters/eufy/adapter.py:468). But `dock_events.register()`/`_handle_dock_event` read only `entities.dock_status` (line 53) and `dock_events.triggers` (line 85-91) — `enabled` is never consulted. The only reader anywhere in the component is core/manager.py:3995, where it gates the `supports_base_station` capability flag for the UI. Recording is therefore gated purely on 'a dock_status entity is declared AND a non-empty triggers dict exists'. Both shipped brands happen to be self-consistent (Eufy: enabled + triggers; Roborock: neither block, so `get_adapter_value(..., fallback={})` yields {} and nothing fires), so this is latent today.
user_impact: A future adapter that copies the Eufy dock_events block and flips `enabled: False` to opt out gets the opposite of what it declared: dock events are recorded and counters incremented, while the Base Station UI tab is hidden — so the data accumulates with no surface to inspect or correct it. Fails toward Eufy behaviour, silently, which is the recurring shape of this seam.
guards_checked: listeners/dock_events.py:42-59 register() — reads only `entities.dock_status`; no enabled check. listeners/dock_events.py:85-91 — reads only `dock_events.triggers`. title: The exactly-once claim's REFUSAL dict is consumed as a successful finalize — the duplicate EVENT_JOB_FINISHED survived the fix and now carries an all-null payload
observed_behavior: The shipped exactly-once claim (learning/manager.py:702-716) does not raise and does not return None on re-entry — it returns a REFUSAL DICT, {"vacuum_entity_id":..., "finalized": False, "reason": "finalize_in_flight"}. lifecycle.py never inspects `finalized` or `reason`. It logs "Auto-finalized job ... %s", calls mark_active_job_finalized(finalize_result=<refusal>) — which writes finalize_summary with job_id/job_path/used_for_learning/sanity_passed/sanity_flags/status ALL None and finalized_at None — and then fires EVENT_JOB_FINISHED because `finalize_result is not None` is true for a refusal. job_finished_event_data (_common.py:225-237) then defaults status to "completed" via outcome.get("status", "completed") while job_id, room_count, duration_minutes, actual_cleaning_minutes, used_for_learning, finalized_at and job_path are all None. Reachability of the second pass is not a lucky interleave: the claim writes only `finalize_claimed_at` into the stored job, it does NOT change active_job["status"], and mark_active_job_finalized (the sole writer of status="completed") runs only AFTER the heavy executor hop in _finalize_claimed. So a second _process task created by any watched-entity change during the finalize window re-reads status=="started", re-reads the same live completion signals, and passes the identical gate. At dock that is the normal case, not an edge: on Eufy the parser sets task_status="Completed" and clears active_cleaning_target in one pass (that pair IS the predicate) and then vacuum->docked and dock_status->drying follow, each now passing the full gate; on Roborock status->charging, binary_sensor cleaning->off and current_room->dock-room land together. HA's eager-start of async_create_task does not rescue this — eager-start only helps when the predicate is not yet satisfied. Ordering makes it worse: the refusal path suspends exactly once (the tracker.end_job executor hop at :339) while the real path is still inside finalize_from_inputs + _auto_record_accuracy, so the BOGUS event normally fires FIRST. This is the exact residual V1 listed as surviving F2 ("EVENT_JOB_FINISHED fires per task"), and it is the same defect shape already open at two SIBLING sites — A5-STR-5 (jobs/active_job.py:2464) and A2-CAN-6 (jobs/active_job.py:2189) — but not at this one, the primary every-run path.
user_impact: The documented public automation trigger `eufy_vacuum_job_finished` (docs/advanced/02-events.md; docs/dev/02-ha-integration.md:438 documents an 11-key contract) fires twice on a normal completed run, and the FIRST of the two claims status "completed" with every data field null. A user automation that notifies "{{ trigger.event.data.room_count }} rooms in {{ trigger.event.data.duration_minutes }} min" renders "None rooms in None min" or throws a template error, then is immediately followed by a second, correct notification. Nothing is logged as an error — the debug line asserts "Auto-finalized job". Additionally mark_active_job_finalized is invoked with the refusal, blanking the stored finalize_summary (all values None); the real finalize normally overwrites it a moment later, but the two paths race on separate executor hops, so on a slow/contended executor the card's post-run summary is left permanently blank — no outcome, no learning verdict, no sanity flags — which is the identical user-visible symptom already recorded for A2-CAN-6.
guards_checked: (1) learning/manager.py:695-719, the exactly-once claim — read in full: it guards the finalize BODY (`already_finalized` / `finalize_in_flight`) and is correct, but it deliberately returns a dict so the CALLER's post-finalize side-effects are unprotected; the release in the `finally` (:737-741) does not touch status either. (2) lifecycle.py:137 `if active_job.get("status") not in {"started","paused"}: continue` — read from a normalized COPY (jobs/active_job.py:1639 _normalize_active_job) before the awaits and never re-read; verified none of the three intervening `continue`/`return` paths re-checks it. (3) lifecycle.py:354 `if finalize_result is not None` — a refusal is a dict, so it passes; there is no `.get("finalized")` or `.get("reason")` check anywhere in lifecycle.py. (4) jobs/active_job.py:2020 mark_active_job_finalized — inspects finalize_result only to read fields out of it, never to decide whether to act. (5) sensor/__init__.py:410 `_finalized_ok = bool(job_path)` — a real guard, but it protects only the internal error-latch clear, not the public event or the other consumers. (6) sensor/lifecycle.py:162 `_on_job_finished` — filters on vacuum_entity_id/map_id only, no payload validity check. (7) Confirmed maybe_handle_external_run (learning/external_run.py:75-134) and maybe_advance_phase (jobs/phase_runner.py:141-200) are await-FREE coroutines, so they cannot be the interleave point — the only suspension before the claim is the tracker.start_job hop at :230, which does not run on a completion event.

confirmations: CONFIRMED end to end. learning/manager.py:702-716 returns a REFUSAL DICT ({'finalized': False, 'reason': 'already_finalized'|'finalize_in_flight'}) with no completed_job key, and the wrapper core/manager.py:4653-4660 explicitly documents that no claim lives there. lifecycle.py:354 tests only `finalize_result is not None`, so a refusal passes: it fires EVENT_JOB_FINISHED via job_finished_event_data, which at _common.py:229 defaults status to 'completed' while job_id/room_count/duration_minutes/used_for_learning/finalized_at/job_path are all None; and jobs/active_job.py:2020-2076 mark_active_job_finalized writes finalized_at=None plus an all-None finalize_summary. Reachability verified: the claim writes only finalize_claimed_at into the stored dict — it does NOT set status — and mark_active_job_finalized (the sole writer of status='completed') runs only after the executor hops, so a second _process created by another watched-entity change during the finalize window re-reads status=='started' and re-passes the identical gate (lifecycle.py:137 reads a normalized copy once and never re-checks). No in-flight flag exists anywhere in lifecycle.py. Same root cause as A6-GUARD-2 and the already-open A5-STR-5 / A2-CAN-6 — one fix (inspect finalize_result['finalized']) closes all four.

Confirmed end to end. learning/manager.py:702-716 returns a refusal DICT ({"finalized": False, "reason": "already_finalized"|"finalize_in_flight"}) rather than raising or returning None, and core/manager.py:4619-4694 (the wrapper) has no await before that claim, so the refusal path suspends nowhere. lifecycle.py:354 tests only `finalize_result is not None`. Concrete Roborock dock sequence, one coordinator update writing three states synchronously: (1) sensor.<vac>_status -> "charging": T1 created, gate passes task_status+secondary(require_job_active_clear=True)+has_observed, then is_job_active(unavailable_is_active=True) reads binary_sensor.<vac>_cleaning still "on" -> suppressed. (2) binary_sensor.<vac>_cleaning -> "off": T2 created, gate passes, T2 writes finalize_claimed_at and suspends on the finalize executor hop. (3) sensor.<vac>_current_room -> "Living Room" (dock room): T3 created, re-reads active_job.status which is STILL "started" (verified mark_active_job_finalized at jobs/active_job.py:2034 is the sole writer of status and runs only after T2's awaits), gate passes again, finalize returns the refusal synchronously. T3 then calls mark_active_job_finalized(finalize_result=<refusal>) -> jobs/active_job.py:2042-2076 writes finalized_at=None and a finalize_summary with job_id/job_path/status/used_for_learning/sanity_passed/sanity_flags all None, and fires EVENT_JOB_FINISHED whose payload via _common.job_finished_event_data:229 defaults status to "completed" with every other field None. HIGH stands: the documented public trigger fires twice per normal run, the first with a null payload and a "completed" status. Note the finder's ordering claim is inverted — the refusal task normally finishes FIRST, so the real finalize usually overwrites the blanked summary; the durable, always-present defect is the duplicate null-payload event, not the permanently blank summary.

title: _process tasks are untracked — remove() drops only the subscription, so a config-entry reload orphans an in-flight finalize bound to the dead manager
observed_behavior: `hass.async_create_task(_process())` creates a task owned by `hass`, not by the config entry, and nothing holds a reference to it. `remove(hass)` (:62-71) pops and calls only the `async_track_state_change_event` unsub — it cannot and does not cancel tasks already spawned. `manager_local` is resolved once from hass.data at :100, at EVENT time, and the `manager_local is None` early return at :101-102 therefore cannot catch a reload that happens later, during the multi-hundred-millisecond await chain (finalize executor hop, accuracy executor hop, tracker.end_job hop, async_save). async_unload_entry (__init__.py:480-487) calls remove() on all eight listeners and tears down the mapping tracker, battery manager, error tracker and adapter coordinator, but cancels no listener tasks. An orphan therefore completes against the torn-down manager: it calls mark_active_job_finalized on the DEAD manager's `data` dict, fires EVENT_JOB_FINISHED, and finally `await manager_local.async_save()` — writing the dead manager's snapshot into the Store the freshly-constructed manager also owns. The new manager loaded active_jobs from that Store during setup and still holds the run as status="started", with no `finalize_claimed_at` and no `finalized` flag, so its own lifecycle listener will re-finalize the same run on the next watched change, or the stranded reaper will later book it as `interrupted`. This is the exact mechanism the audit's F1 confirmed for PhaseRunner tasks; the fix landed as a PhaseRunner concern and this sibling spawn site was not covered. phase_runner.py has an ownership check (`_still_ours`); lifecycle.py has no equivalent.
user_impact: Reload the integration (Configure -> options change, HACS update, Dev-Tools reload) in the seconds after a run docks and the run's finalization lands in a manager that is no longer authoritative: the live manager still shows the job as `started`, so the card keeps displaying an in-progress run, manual start stays blocked, and the run is subsequently either finalized a second time or reaped and recorded as `interrupted` rather than `completed` — which changes whether it feeds learning. No error is surfaced on either side.
guards_checked: remove() at :62-71 (pops `_JOB_LIFECYCLE_UNSUBS` and calls the unsub — subscription only, no task set); register() at :74-76 (calls remove() first, so the subscription itself is correctly non-duplicating); the `manager_local is None` check at :100-102 (evaluated synchronously at event time, before every await, so it cannot detect a mid-flight teardown); __init__.py:465-534 async_unload_entry read in full — it stops battery_manager, error_tracker, mapping_tracker and the adapter coordinator, and cancels no tasks for any listener module; jobs/phase_runner.py `_still_ours` — the ownership pattern exists in the codebase but is not applied here.

confirmations: CONFIRMED. lifecycle.py:409 hass.async_create_task(_process()) keeps no handle; remove() at :62-71 pops and calls only the state-change unsub. Checked the reviewer trap: __init__.py:465-534 async_unload_entry cancels no listener tasks and there is no entry.async_on_unload covering this spawn. manager_local is resolved once at :100 at EVENT time, so the None check cannot detect a teardown that happens during the multi-hop await chain (finalize executor hop, accuracy, tracker.end_job hop, async_save). The orphan then calls mark_active_job_finalized on the dead manager's data dict and awaits manager_local.async_save(), overwriting the Store the freshly-constructed manager owns — while that new manager still holds the run as status='started'. jobs/phase_runner.py's _still_ours ownership pattern exists in-repo and is not applied here, confirming this is an unpatched sibling of the same F1 defect.

Mechanism verified: lifecycle.py:409 hass.async_create_task(_process()) keeps no handle; remove() (:62-71) cancels only the state subscription; __init__.py:465-534 async_unload_entry cancels no listener tasks; manager_local is bound at :100 before every await so the :101 None-check cannot see a mid-flight teardown. Concrete: Alfred docks at T, T2 enters finalize_learning_for_active_job and suspends on the executor hop; at T+150 ms the user saves an option -> _async_update_listener -> unload+setup; the new manager loads active_jobs from the Store with the run still status="started"; the orphan resumes, calls mark_active_job_finalized on the DEAD manager's data dict, fires EVENT_JOB_FINISHED, and awaits the dead manager's async_save(). The live manager keeps showing the run in flight and later re-finalizes it or the stranded reaper books it `interrupted`. Severity corrected to LOW: the window is the sub-second finalize await chain and requires a reload landing inside it. The already-verified A2-LIFE-1 shows the far more reachable consequence of the same untracked-task design.

title: The inline mop-wash detector diverges from the dedicated dock_events listener: hard-coded Eufy wash vocabulary as a fallback, and no same-state guard against attribute-only re-triggers
observed_behavior: Two divergences from listeners/dock_events.py, which watches the same entity for the same transition. (a) VOCABULARY: `_wash_triggers = frozenset(...adapter dock_events.triggers.last_mop_wash...) or frozenset({"washing", "washing mop"})`. The `or` fires not only when the adapter declares nothing but also when it declares an EMPTY list — the honest way for an adapter to say "this dock has no wash cycle" — and substitutes Eufy's literal dock vocabulary. dock_events.py:85-89 does the same lookup with `fallback={}` and consequently records nothing for an undeclared brand, so the two consumers of one declaration answer opposite ways; this is the adapter-seam failure mode audit #4 characterised (an unapplied edge failing toward Eufy silently). (b) SAME-STATE: `async_track_state_change_event` fires on ANY State-object change including an attribute-only change where `state` is identical. dock_events.py:74 guards this explicitly (`if new_val == old_val: return`); lifecycle.py:170 tests only `_new_state_n in _wash_triggers`, i.e. the LEVEL of new_state, and re-enters update_active_job_mop_wash_observation on every such event while dock_status remains "washing". The only backstop is that method's own cooldown (jobs/active_job.py:533, adapter `dock_events.debounce_seconds.last_mop_wash` = DOCK_EVENT_MOP_WASH_DEBOUNCE_SECONDS = 60 s), which collapses re-entries only within 60 s of the last COUNTED wash — an Eufy X10 Omni wash cycle runs longer than that, so an attribute tick (or a dock_status flap out and back) more than 60 s into one physical wash is counted as a second wash. Note Roborock declares no `entities.dock_status`, so `_dock_status_entity` is falsy and the whole block is skipped there — this is Eufy-reachable and future-brand-reachable only.
user_impact: `observed_mop_wash_count` on the active job is inflated. That value is written into the completed-job record as `actual_mop_wash_count` and is handed to register_post_job_water_amendment at lifecycle.py:398 as `mop_wash_count_at_finalization`, which is the baseline the post-job amendment compares against to decide whether a further wash happened after finalization. An over-count therefore both overstates the run's water usage in the learning record and can suppress the legitimate post-job water amendment, with no error shown. For a future brand that declares an empty last_mop_wash trigger list, mop washes are counted against Eufy's words on a dock that has none.
guards_checked: lifecycle.py:162 `if _dock_status_entity and entity_id == _dock_status_entity` (entity filter only — no state-delta filter); lifecycle.py:170 `_new_state_n in _wash_triggers` (level test, not edge test); jobs/active_job.py:507-569 update_active_job_mop_wash_observation read in full — the status gate (`started`/`paused`) and the 60 s cooldown are the only guards, and the cooldown is keyed off the last COUNTED wash so it does not bound a long-running level; listeners/dock_events.py:42-127 read in full — it is the sibling that DOES carry both guards (`fallback={}` at :88 and `new_val == old_val` at :74), which is what makes this a divergence rather than a shared gap; adapters/eufy/adapter.py dock_events block (triggers sourced from vocabulary.py DOCK_EVENT_TRIGGERS, debounce_seconds.last_mop_wash = 60) confirms the declaration exists and is non-empty on Eufy today, so (a) is latent and (b) is live; adapters/roborock/adapter.py:195-209 confirms no dock_status entity is declared, so Roborock is unaffected.

confirmations: CONFIRMED both halves. (a) lifecycle.py:164-169: `frozenset(...) or frozenset({'washing','washing mop'})` — an adapter declaring an EMPTY last_mop_wash list gets Eufy's literal dock vocabulary, while listeners/dock_events.py:88 does the same lookup with fallback={} and records nothing. Two consumers of one declaration answer opposite ways; latent today. (b) lifecycle.py:162-170 filters on entity identity plus a LEVEL test only — I re-read the handler and there is no new_state==old_state guard anywhere in lifecycle.py (unlike dock_events.py:74). jobs/active_job.py:507-569 read in full: the only backstops are the started/paused status gate and a cooldown keyed off observed_mop_wash_last_at (the last COUNTED wash, adapter value 60 s), so a dock_status flap out and back more than 60 s into one physical wash counts a second wash. Impact chain verified: job_finalizer.py:204 sets actual_mop_wash_count from observed_mop_wash_count and lifecycle.py:398-400 feeds that to mop_wash_count_at_finalization — so this, not A1-REG-1, is the finding that genuinely reaches the water amendment. Roborock unaffected (no entities.dock_status).

Both halves verified in source. (a) lifecycle.py:164-169 — `frozenset(...adapter dock_events.triggers.last_mop_wash...) or frozenset({"washing", "washing mop"})`; an adapter declaring `"last_mop_wash": []` yields an empty frozenset, which is falsy, so Eufy's literal dock vocabulary is substituted. The sibling at dock_events.py:88 uses fallback={} and records nothing in the same situation — a real divergence at the adapter seam. (b) lifecycle.py:162 filters on entity identity only and :170 tests `_new_state_n in _wash_triggers` (a LEVEL test); dock_events.py:74 carries the `new_val == old_val` edge guard and lifecycle does not. Concrete live case on Eufy: dock_status "Washing Mop" at T, MQTT blip -> "unavailable" at T+80 s, back to "Washing Mop" at T+95 s. Read jobs/active_job.py:507-569 in full: the only backstop is the 60 s cooldown keyed off observed_mop_wash_last_at (the last COUNTED wash, adapter debounce DOCK_EVENT_MOP_WASH_DEBOUNCE_SECONDS = 60), so at 95 s the re-entry counts a SECOND wash inside one physical cycle. observed_mop_wash_count then lands in the record as actual_mop_wash_count and is passed as mop_wash_count_at_finalization at lifecycle.py:398. title: is_job_active() treats a NOT-YET-ADDED / removed job_active entity as "no job running", defeating the Roborock mid-recharge completion guard
observed_behavior: is_job_active() resolves entities.job_active from the adapter registry, then does `state = hass.states.get(entity_id); if state is None: return False` (lines 138-139) BEFORE the unavailable/unknown handling on line 141. The `unavailable_is_active=True` mode — whose docstring (lines 125-130) says an indeterminate binary must be read as STILL ACTIVE so "a blip during a mid-recharge dock lets the completion gate finalize the job early and record a truncated learning sample" — is therefore bypassed entirely for the one indeterminate case that lasts longest: the entity is not in the state machine at all. Roborock's entity IDs are pure string derivation (adapters/roborock/entities.py:52 `f"{domain}.{object_id}{suffix}"`, SUFFIX_JOB_ACTIVE="_cleaning"), so `entities.job_active` is ALWAYS declared regardless of whether the HA roborock integration has created binary_sensor.{id}_cleaning yet. The gate this defeats: listeners/lifecycle.py:281-284 is the ONLY suppression of finalization during a mid-job recharge. Roborock's completion.task_status_value is "charging" (adapters/roborock/adapter.py:263) — i.e. the robot's own mid-job recharge dock state IS its completion terminal — and completion_secondary_satisfied() returns True unconditionally for Roborock (require_job_active_clear, _common.py:198-201). has_observed_active_lifecycle is persisted on the active_job record (jobs/active_job.py:1629; never reset at startup). So with the job_active entity absent, the gate reduces to: task_status=="charging" AND True AND True -> finalize. Reachable window: our listeners register during our own async_setup_entry (custom_components/eufy_vacuum/__init__.py:398, BEFORE async_forward_entry_setups) using entity IDs derived from stored vacuum records, so at an HA restart taken while a Roborock run is parked mid-recharge, the roborock integration's sensor.{id}_status is added with state "charging" and fires a watched state_changed (job_active and task_status are both in get_lifecycle_watch_entities, _common.py:97-103) while binary_sensor.{id}_cleaning has not yet been added by its own platform — HA guarantees no ordering across entities/platforms. The deferred `_process()` task then reads hass.states.get(binary_sensor...) -> None -> False. The same hole opens on a roborock config-entry reload (entities removed then re-added; removal itself fires the watched event) and on any capability-gated removal of that binary sensor.
user_impact: A Roborock run that docked mid-job to recharge is auto-finalized while the robot is still going to resume. No error is surfaced: the user sees a "completed" job whose duration/room set covers only the first half. mark_active_job_finalized clears the active_job slot, so the resumed second half has no dispatched job to attribute to (it becomes an orphan/external run). Worse, the truncated record is written to the learning history as a normal completed job and feeds the per-room minute estimates, durably skewing every subsequent time estimate for those rooms.
guards_checked: listeners/lifecycle.py:281-284 (the recharge guard — this IS the guard, and it is the only one); listeners/lifecycle.py:297-298 `_phase_dispatch_pending` (only set on a sequenced phase advance, queue/queue_engine.advance_active_job_phase — no-op for atomic/batch jobs); listeners/lifecycle.py:269 has_observed_active_lifecycle (persisted True from before the restart, jobs/active_job.py:1629, only cleared at 2037/queue_engine.py:476); _common.completion_secondary_satisfied lines 198-201 (returns True for Roborock, adds nothing); _common.py:141 `unavailable_is_active` branch (unreachable — the None return on 139 precedes it); adapters/registry.py has NO validation touching job_active (grepped: zero hits for job_active/require_job_active_clear); jobs/job_monitor.is_stranded_started (a different path, and it correctly bails at the vacuum_state docked/idle + task_status==completion-value checks); listeners/lifecycle.py:96-98 confirms the handler does NOT early-return on new_state/old_state being None.

confirmations: CONFIRMED. _common.py:137-139 returns False on state is None BEFORE the unavailable_is_active branch at :141, so the mode the docstring says exists to survive an indeterminate binary is bypassed for the longest-lived indeterminate case. Verified the gate this defeats is the only one: Roborock declares completion.task_status_value='charging' (adapters/roborock/adapter.py:264) and require_job_active_clear=True (:272), so completion_secondary_satisfied returns True unconditionally (_common.py:198-201) and the recharge suppression at lifecycle.py:281-284 is the sole remaining brake. Tried to refute on reachability and found the mechanism is BROADER than the finder's restart case: lifecycle.py:96-98 does NOT early-return on new_state being None, so the REMOVAL of binary_sensor.<id>_cleaning during a roborock config-entry reload is itself a watched event that runs the handler while sensor.<id>_status still reads 'charging' — a routine operation, not a startup race. has_observed_active_lifecycle is persisted and survives the restart. entities.job_active is always declared for Roborock (pure string derivation), so no adapter-side guard intervenes; adapters/registry.py has zero references to job_active.

Confirmed by reading _common.py:133-143: `if not entity_id: return False` then `state = hass.states.get(entity_id); if state is None: return False` — both precede the unavailable_is_active branch at :141, so an absent entity can never take the 'treat as still ACTIVE' path the docstring at :125-130 exists for. Concrete Roborock timeline: Ivy is 20 min into a whole-house run, drops to 19%, docks to recharge; active_job status="started", has_observed_active_lifecycle=True (verified persisted on the stored record at jobs/active_job.py:1629 and cleared only at :2037 / queue_engine.py:476 — nothing resets it at startup). HA is restarted. Our async_setup_entry registers lifecycle.register(hass) at __init__.py:398 from stored vacuum records, and roborock's entity IDs are pure string derivation (adapters/roborock/entities.py, SUFFIX_JOB_ACTIVE="_cleaning"), so entities.job_active is declared whether or not the entity exists. The roborock sensor platform adds sensor.<vac>_status = "charging" (a watched entity per _common.py:97-103) before its binary_sensor platform adds binary_sensor.<vac>_cleaning. _process runs: task_status "charging" == completion.task_status_value (adapters/roborock/adapter.py:263) ✓; completion_secondary_satisfied returns True unconditionally via require_job_active_clear (_common.py:198-201, adapter.py:272) ✓; has_observed_active_lifecycle True ✓; the recharge guard at lifecycle.py:281-284 calls is_job_active -> hass.states.get(binary_sensor...) is None -> False -> guard does NOT suppress; _phase_dispatch_pending unset for an atomic/batch job. The run is finalized mid-recharge, the learning record covers only the first half, and mark_active_job_finalized clears the slot so the resumed half becomes an orphan/external run. Also verified the competing stranded reaper cannot pre-empt this: is_stranded_started (jobs/job_monitor.py:366) returns False because task_status already equals the completion value. HIGH stands — durable, silently truncated learning sample feeding per-room estimates.

title: completion_secondary_satisfied() returns True from a config FLAG without verifying the entity it delegates to exists; the "Invariant" asserted in the caller is never validated
observed_behavior: completion_secondary_satisfied() reads completion.require_job_active_clear and, when truthy, returns True with no further check (lines 198-201). Its own docstring says the real signal is "enforced by the separate is_job_active guard in the lifecycle handler" — but it never confirms that guard has anything to enforce with. listeners/lifecycle.py:191-193 states this as an invariant in a comment: "a brand that sets require_job_active_clear must also declare entities.job_active (true for Roborock) — otherwise is_job_active is always False and the flag would never arm." That claim is verified nowhere: adapters/registry.py's registration path (_warn_eufy_fallbacks / the validation helper at line ~228+) warns about absent mapping / job_segmenter / room_attribution blocks and says nothing about job_active or require_job_active_clear (grep for both over registry.py returns zero hits). An adapter declaring require_job_active_clear=True without entities.job_active gets: secondary_satisfied -> always True (bypassed), is_job_active -> always False (no suppression), and the arming gate at lifecycle.py:200-202 -> `_needs_active_proof and is_job_active(...)` -> never arms. title: completed_finalize_signals() docstring claims it returns "" for unavailable entities; it actually returns the literal "unavailable"/"unknown"
observed_behavior: The docstring (lines 154-155) says "Returns empty strings for absent or unavailable entities". The implementation's `_state()` only returns "" when the entity id is falsy or `hass.states.get()` returns None (lines 163-167); an entity that exists and reads `unavailable`/`unknown` is a real State object whose `.state` is the string "unavailable", so line 168 returns "unavailable". Both brands survive this only by coincidence: Eufy's declared completion.secondary_clear_sentinels happens to list "unavailable" and "unknown" explicitly (adapters/eufy/adapter.py:435-437), and Roborock bypasses the sentinel check via require_job_active_clear. A brand-3 author who trusts the docstring and declares `secondary_clear_sentinels: ["", "none"]` (a reasonable reading of "unavailable is normalized to empty") would find the secondary never satisfied when the target sensor drops to unavailable. Separately, the genuine "" case (entity id declared but the entity does not exist) IS in every default sentinel set, so a mis-named or not-yet-created active_cleaning_target silently auto-satisfies the Eufy secondary rather than refusing.
user_impact: No wrong result on either shipped brand today. Latent: it is a false description of behaviour in the one place a new adapter author reads to choose their sentinel vocabulary, and it makes 'entity does not exist' indistinguishable from 'entity says the run is over'.

title: get_adapter_value() is a second, independent implementation of the identical lookup already shipped in adapters/registry.py
observed_behavior: _common.get_adapter_value() (lines 52-76) walks a nested path with a fallback. adapters/registry.py:535-552 and the coordinator method at registry.py:202-216 implement the same traversal with the same semantics (non-dict intermediate -> fallback, None value -> fallback). Every listener imports the _common copy; jobs/active_job.py also imports the _common copy while the registry module itself exports the other. A shared quirk lives in both: a key whose declared value is literally `None` is indistinguishable from an absent key, so an adapter cannot declare a null override.
user_impact: No behavioural difference today. title: Sampler cadence collapses to min() across all vacuums while the attribution engine multiplies tick counts by each vacuum's OWN declared interval_s — Roborock is sampled at 2.0s but its ticks are valued at 5.0s
observed_behavior: register() builds ONE ticker for ALL vacuums at `interval_s = min(intervals)` (line 309), where `intervals` is every vacuum's declared `room_attribution.tuning.interval_s`. Eufy declares 2.0 (adapters/eufy/adapter.py:740), Roborock declares 5.0 (adapters/roborock/adapter.py:564). On a mixed install the ticker runs at 2.0s and `_handle_pose_tick` (line 311-313) samples EVERY vacuum on every tick, so the Roborock buffers ~2.5x more samples than its declared cadence. The consumer never learns this: `external_ingest._attribute` re-reads the ADAPTER's tuning per vacuum (`result["interval_s"] = _safe_float(tuning.get("interval_s"), 2.0)`, external_ingest.py:423) and `EufyAnchorWindingAttributor._resolve` merges the same adapter block (room_attribution_engines.py:279), so the engine converts Roborock ticks to seconds at 5.0 s/tick. The in-file comment at lines 299-302 states this limitation is 'Unreachable while only Eufy declares attribution' — that comment is STALE: adapters/roborock/adapter.py:539-566 declares a full room_attribution block with source native_current_room. This is a single-config-entry integration (config_flow.py:44-51 sets unique_id=DOMAIN and aborts duplicates), so both vacuums provably share one manager and one ticker.
user_impact: On an install with both shipped brands (the maintainer's own Alfred/Eufy + Ivy/Roborock setup), every Roborock app-started run writes per-room durations 2.5x too long: external_ingest.build_pose_only_record:649 computes `active_s = int(round(entry["n"] * interval_s))` from the inflated tick count, and that `time_active_s` lands in the durable learning record feeding per-room time estimates. `per_room[rid]["dwell_s"]` (room_attribution_engines.py:148) is inflated identically. Separately, the 3000-sample buffer cap (_MAX_POSE_SAMPLES) was sized for the declared cadence — at the real 2.0s cadence it holds ~100 min instead of ~250 min, so a long Roborock whole-house run silently del-oldest-evicts its earliest rooms and those rooms drop out of the attributed set entirely. title: The sampling timer is fire-and-forget: a tick slower than interval_s overlaps the next tick, double-recording samples and stamping stale pose content with a fresh timestamp
observed_behavior: `async_track_time_interval` builds a `_TrackTimeInterval` whose `_interval_listener` (homeassistant/helpers/event.py:1638-1643) calls `self._schedule_timer()` FIRST and then `hass.async_run_hass_job(self._run_job, ..., background=True)` — it never awaits the coroutine. `_handle_pose_tick` (pose_sampler.py:311) is a coroutine that awaits per-vacuum, and on the live_pose path each vacuum's `_read_live_pose_sample` awaits `manager.async_get_map_live_pose`, which does an executor `_stat_mtime` round trip and, whenever mtime changed, a full `load_store_json` of the fork's .storage map file including its base64 raster (mapping/map_source_coordinator.py:476-498). During an active run the fork rewrites map_data continuously, so the mtime cache misses on most ticks. With interval_s at 2.0s (Eufy's declared cadence, and the effective cadence for every vacuum per POSE-1), a tick whose disk read and JSON parse exceed 2.0s produces two concurrent `_handle_pose_tick` tasks. Nothing serializes them — there is no in-flight flag, no lock, and `record_pose_sample` (jobs/active_job.py:1744) appends unconditionally once its status guard passes.
user_impact: On a slower host or with a large map raster, an external run buffers more samples than ticks elapsed, and `active_s = round(entry["n"] * interval_s)` (external_ingest.py:649) turns the surplus into over-reported per-room cleaning durations in the learning record. Because `record_pose_sample` stamps `t` at APPEND time rather than read time, a sample whose pose was read one interval earlier is written with the later timestamp, so `_dominant_room` window matching (external_ingest.py:427) can mis-assign a counter segment near a room boundary by up to one interval. The buffer also fills faster, bringing the 3000-sample eviction of the run's start forward. Non-deterministic and entirely silent.
guards_checked: Read HA's `_TrackTimeInterval` in the installed homeassistant/helpers/event.py (lines 1600-1651) — confirmed `_schedule_timer()` precedes the job dispatch and the job is run with `background=True`, i.e. not awaited. `remove()`/`register()` (pose_sampler.py:276-289) only cancel/create the timer handle; no re-entrancy guard exists. `_sample_vacuum_once` (line 235) has no per-vacuum guard. `record_pose_sample`'s guards (status in ('external','started') and started_at/not ended_at) both pass for two concurrent ticks of the same live run. `_pose_sample_is_static` coalescing does NOT suppress the duplicate: the two overlapping ticks read different poses (the robot moved), so `_pose_stall_run` resets to 0 and both append. The mtime cache in `_load_live_pose_geom` does not help while the fork is actively rewriting the file.

confirmations: HA mechanism personally verified in the installed source: homeassistant/helpers/event.py:1637-1643 _interval_listener calls self._schedule_timer() first and then async_run_hass_job(..., background=True) — the coroutine is not awaited, so overlap is structurally possible, and pose_sampler.py:276-316 has no in-flight flag or lock. Downgraded to LOW because the harm is unproven and narrower than stated: only the live_pose path has a suspension point at all (_read_native_current_room_sample is fully synchronous, so a Roborock-only install cannot overlap), and no measurement shows a stat+load_store_json tick exceeding 2.0 s. Real as a hardening gap, not a demonstrated wrong result.

The structural half is verified from source: pose_sampler.py:315 uses async_track_time_interval with a coroutine handler and there is no in-flight flag, lock, or task handle anywhere in the module (remove()/register() at :276-289 touch only the timer unsub), and record_pose_sample appends unconditionally once its status guard passes. But the finder's concrete trigger does not hold up. I read mapping/map_source_coordinator.py:475-528: async_get_map_live_pose reads the pose from the fork's IN-MEMORY entity attributes (_read_inmem_pose), and the only disk work is _load_live_pose_geom, which is mtime-cached and does a full load_store_json only when the .storage mtime actually changes — HA Store writes are delay-debounced, so that is far less frequent than every 2 s, and live_pose_overlay is geometry math, not a raster decode. So 'the mtime cache misses on most ticks' is not supported and no tick exceeding 2.0 s is demonstrated from source. Severity corrected to LOW: a genuine missing re-entrancy guard with no proven triggering timeline, latent until some future tick body actually blocks.

title: _is_parked has no working fallback on the native_current_room path — when task_status is unreadable it returns 'not parked', the opposite of what its own docstring claims
observed_behavior: `_is_parked`'s final line is `return bool(pose.get("robot_docked"))` (line 129). `_read_native_current_room_sample` calls it as `_is_parked(hass, cfg, {})` (line 223) — an empty dict, because the native path decodes no pose. So the documented fallback ('We fall back to the pose flag only when task_status can't be read (no declared entity / unavailable state / no vocab — e.g. a future non-Eufy brand)', lines 119-120) is structurally dead on exactly the path the docstring names: it always evaluates to False, i.e. 'the robot is actively cleaning'. The fallback is reached whenever the `if active and ts_id` guard (line 124) fails or the state reads unavailable/unknown (line 127): a brand declaring `room_attribution.source: native_current_room` but no `vocabulary.active_run_task_states`, or a declared task_status entity that momentarily reads unavailable/unknown. `_can_sample` (line 95-105) gates the native path on `entities.active_cleaning_target` ONLY — it never requires task_status or the active-run vocabulary, so a brand can pass the sampling gate with no parked signal at all.

Consequence chain: `manager.maybe_pulse_live_room_refresh` (core/manager.py:4915 → live_refresh/manager.py:112) has exactly ONE caller in the entire package — this ticker (verified by grep). Lever B's stated job is "keep the brand's live current-room/map data fresh so the native per-room rollover... tracks the adapter's interval instead of the device's slower native map cadence" (live_refresh/manager.py:113-115). title: `_duration_state_to_seconds` silently treats any unrecognized unit as seconds, and re-resolves the unit per event with no mid-run consistency check
observed_behavior: The function handles only ms/min/h aliases; every other unit string — including HA's `UnitOfTime.DAYS` ("d"), `WEEKS` ("w"), `MICROSECONDS`, `NANOSECONDS`, and any localized or misspelled unit — falls through to `return int(round(value))`, i.e. is assumed to already be seconds, with no log line. The sibling area path deliberately documents this policy (`cleaning_area_to_m2`, learning/utils.py:44-55: "An unknown or absent unit is assumed to ALREADY be m² ... we never guess a factor"), but for duration the silent default is the unsafe direction: an unhandled larger unit is under-read by its whole factor rather than merely unscaled. Separately, the unit is resolved fresh on every event (job_metrics.py:153-157) and the resulting seconds value is appended to `counter_samples` as an absolute — nothing compares the unit used for sample N against sample N-1. If the entity's `unit_of_measurement` ever changes or appears/disappears mid-run (e.g. a restored state that lacks the attribute until the first live update, with an adapter `cleaning_time_unit` hint present), the buffered series silently mixes two scales, and `counter_segmentation._prepare_window` would read the scale change as a huge increment or a reset. No shipped brand is known to hit this today.
user_impact: Latent. On the two shipped brands the resolved units are "s" (Eufy, absent → seconds) and the adapter hint "min" (Roborock, bare number), both handled correctly and test-covered, so no wrong value reaches a user today. title: A blocker sensor going `unavailable` satisfies every negating rule operator, so a Zigbee/cloud dropout pauses or CANCELS a live run (return_to_base)
observed_behavior: `_handle_path_blocker_change` filters only two things: `new_state_obj is None` (entity removal) and `old_state == new_state` (attribute-only tick). A transition `open -> unavailable` passes both — `unavailable` is a real State whose `.state` string differs — so `_process()` runs and calls `get_runtime_path_block_report`, which evaluates every blocker rule on the queued rooms through `AccessGraphManager._room_rule_matches` (rooms/access_graph.py:907). That function does NO availability check: it fetches the State (non-None for `unavailable`), normalizes the literal string "unavailable" via `_normalize_rule_operand`, and compares. For `not_equals` it returns `"unavailable" != <target>` = True; `not_in` likewise True; `missing` is True the moment the entity is dropped. The rule therefore MATCHES, the room enters `direct_blocked`, and path_blockers.py:139-157 applies `path_block_action`: `cancel_and_event` calls `async_cancel_active_job`, which issues `vacuum.return_to_base` (jobs/active_job.py:2210) and finalizes the run as `cancelled` with an incomplete_run_log. `pause_and_event` pauses instead — and the paused run is then reaped and cancelled by pause_timeout.py once `pause_timeout_minutes` elapses, so both actions end in an aborted run. All three operators (`not_equals`, `not_in`, `missing`) are first-class options in the card's rule editor (src/state/room-rules.js:25-27, 516-532) and `cancel_and_event` is a first-class `path_block_action` (services/job_control.py:83).
user_impact: A battery-powered contact/occupancy sensor dropping off the mesh for one poll — routine on Zigbee/Z-Wave and on Eufy's push-only MQTT — physically aborts a clean in progress: the robot stops mid-room and drives home. The run is recorded as `cancelled`, its rooms land in the incomplete_run_log, and the learning sample is discarded. The user sees a path-blocked event naming a door that never actually opened.

title: path_blockers spawns unbounded concurrent `_process` tasks; a second blocker event inside the 30s cancel-confirm window double-cancels and the loser deterministically nulls the run's finalize_summary
observed_behavior: `hass.async_create_task(_process())` is called for EVERY qualifying state change with no in-flight guard and no task handle kept. `async_cancel_active_job` does not mark the job before it awaits: it checks `status in {started, paused}` (jobs/active_job.py:2189), then awaits `return_to_base` and polls for a terminal state for up to `_CANCEL_CONFIRM_TIMEOUT_S = 30` seconds (line 2218) before `mark_active_job_finalized` runs. Throughout that whole window the stored status is unchanged, so a second `_process` — a different blocker entity changing, or the SAME sensor bouncing (the clearing pass pops `last_path_block_signature` at run_plan.py:1675, so the re-trigger is not deduped) — passes the same guard and starts a SECOND cancel: a second `vacuum.return_to_base` and a second 30s poll. Both then call `finalize_learning_for_active_job`. The exactly-once claim (learning/manager.py:690-719) protects the learning record: the second call returns `{"finalized": False, "reason": "already_finalized"|"finalize_in_flight"}` with NO `completed_job` key. But `async_cancel_active_job` still runs `mark_active_job_finalized` unconditionally (line 2272) with that refusal dict, and jobs/active_job.py:2042-2076 then writes `finalized_at = None` and a `finalize_summary` whose `job_id`, `job_path`, `status`, `used_for_learning`, `sanity_passed`, `sanity_flags` are all None. The refused task is by construction the one that reached finalize LAST, so the null summary is always the last write. It also returns `cancelled: True`, so path_blockers.py:159 fires a second EVENT_JOB_FINISHED built by `_common.job_finished_event_data`, which defaults `status` to `"completed"` when `completed_job` is absent.
user_impact: A cancelled run reports itself as completed. `sensor` lifecycle (sensor/lifecycle.py:199-202) returns "finalized" instead of "cancelled"; the card summary (jobs/active_job.py:1558-1568) reads "Job completed" instead of "Job cancelled"; the stored pointer to the learning record (job_id/job_path/finalized_at) is nulled, so the run is no longer navigable from the active-job record. Any automation triggering on eufy_vacuum_job_finished with `status == completed` fires for a run the robot never finished — and it fires twice.

No `_cancel_in_flight`-style flag is consulted here (jobs/active_job.py:2204 sets one, but only the strict-order phase watchdog reads it).

title: dock_events treats a first-sighting (old_state=None) and an unavailable-recovery as a fresh dock cycle, inflating maintenance counters and resetting last_dry_start
observed_behavior: `old_val = str(old_state.state).strip().lower() if old_state else ""` deliberately maps a None old_state to the empty string, and the only suppression is `new_val == old_val` (line 74). So the FIRST state_changed event for the dock_status entity — old_state is None on entity add, which happens on every HA restart and on every reload of the brand integration (eufy-clean), whose load order relative to ours is not guaranteed — is treated as a transition INTO whatever the dock is currently doing. Same for a recovery: `drying -> unavailable` records nothing ("unavailable" is in no trigger set), then `unavailable -> drying` records a full new event. `record_dock_event` (dock/manager.py:370-427) then overwrites `dock_events[vid]["last_dry_start"]` with now and increments `dry_start_count`. The debounce that exists for exactly this noise is wired for ONE event type only — the Eufy adapter declares `debounce_seconds: {"last_mop_wash": 60}` (adapters/eufy/adapter.py:479-481), so `last_dust_empty` and `last_dry_start` get `debounce = 0` and `should_count` is unconditionally True. `last_dry_start` is the worst case because an Eufy dry cycle runs for hours, giving the largest window for a restart or an MQTT staleness blip to land inside it; the 60s mop-wash cooldown would not cover a restart anyway.
user_impact: Maintenance counters drift upward with no user action — every HA restart during a dry or wash cycle adds a phantom cycle. The Base Station tab shows the dry as having started at the restart time rather than the real start, and consumable/maintenance advice derived from mop_wash_count / dust_empty_count / dry_start_count is silently wrong. The counters are persisted, so the error is durable and only correctable via `set_dock_event_count`.

title: The 1-minute reap ticker has no in-flight guard while each reap blocks up to ~35s, so two reapable slots guarantee overlapping ticks and a duplicate cancel
observed_behavior: `_handle_pause_timeout_tick` fires every 60s and unconditionally does `hass.async_create_task(_process())` — no flag, no handle, no check that the previous tick's task finished. `_process` walks every (vacuum, map) SEQUENTIALLY and each paused-timeout reap awaits `async_cancel_active_job`, which is a blocking `return_to_base` service call plus a poll loop bounded by `_CANCEL_CONFIRM_TIMEOUT_S = 30` (jobs/active_job.py:2218-2237). With two reapable slots (two managed vacuums whose paused jobs time out on the same tick — the normal outcome after a power event or an HA outage), one pass takes ~70s and the next tick fires while it is still inside the second slot's poll. `get_paused_job_timeout_report` (jobs/active_job.py:2286-2329) re-reads the stored job, which still says `status: paused` with the original `paused_at` (nothing is written until the cancel completes), so it returns a report again and a SECOND `async_cancel_active_job` starts for the same slot. From there the damage is identical to GUARD-2: a second return_to_base, a finalize refused by the exactly-once claim, and `mark_active_job_finalized` writing a null `finalize_summary` + `finalized_at: None` last, plus a duplicate EVENT_JOB_FINISHED whose `status` defaults to "completed". A single slot can also exceed 60s on its own if `hass.services.async_call(..., blocking=True)` stalls against an unreachable cloud vacuum.
user_impact: After a multi-vacuum outage the auto-cancelled runs report as "completed"/"finalized" instead of "cancelled", lose their job_id/job_path pointer, and fire duplicate job-finished events — so a `retry_missed_rooms`-style automation sees an extra completed run for a job that was reaped.

The stranded reap is not implicated in the overlap (poll_stranded_started_job requires `started` and `async_finalize_stranded_job` does not poll), and `_clear_stranded_stamp` correctly drops the stamp on any non-started status.

title: A discovery pass on the active map is scored against configured rooms across ALL maps, so switching maps makes the other map's rooms accrue "removed" strikes
observed_behavior: Both adapters declare `active_map_changed` and `vacuum_docked` (adapters/eufy/adapter.py:525-529, adapters/roborock/adapter.py:453-457). `_on_active_map` fires `_run_pass()` on any active_map value change, which calls `run_discovery_pass` -> `discover_rooms_for_vacuum` (rooms/room_discovery.py:168) with `map_id=None`, so it resolves and reads only the ACTIVE map's room list. It then hands that set to `update_drift_history`, which compares it against `_list_configured_room_ids` (setup/drift.py:224-247) — a union over `manager.data["maps"][vid]` of EVERY map's configured rooms. Every configured room id that exists on another map but not on the newly active one takes `missing_passes += 1` and has `seen_passes` reset (setup/drift.py:323-329). With Eufy's `removal_confirmation_passes` of 3, three passes on the new map (a map switch plus two dock events or the 6-hour periodic net) push those rooms over the threshold and `compute_room_drift` reports them as removed. Overlapping room ids across maps (Eufy reuses ids 1-11) partially mask this, so the rooms actually flagged are the ones whose id exists only on the non-active map.
user_impact: On a multi-floor/multi-map setup, switching maps makes the setup tab report rooms as removed from the vacuum and flips setup_complete out of sync (setup/status.py:193-218), prompting the user to delete room configuration — including its learning history — for rooms that still exist and are simply on the other map.
guards_checked: discovery.py:150-153 — the handler filters None/unknown/unavailable and no-change, so the pass it fires is a legitimate map switch, not noise. setup/drift.py:296-302 — `rejected_rooms` is subtracted but there is no map scoping. setup/drift.py:112-140 `get_discovery_cadence` — `removal_confirmation_passes` clamps to >=1 and defaults to 3; it slows the flag but does not prevent it. rooms/room_discovery.py:168 — `map_id or get_active_map_id(...)`, and `run_discovery_pass` never passes a map_id. setup/status.py:193 — consumes `in_sync` for the setup gate; I found no run-blocking use, which is why this is not rated higher.

title: Discovery triggers survive per-vacuum deletion and re-create a setup_progress record for the deleted vacuum — the "subscription to a deleted entity is inert" comment is false
observed_behavior: `_teardown_vacuum` (__init__.py:576-631) deliberately does NOT re-register the global listeners, and `remove_vacuum_record`'s docstring (core/manager.py:1051-1053) justifies it with "the global listeners self-correct on the next reload/restart — a subscription to a now-deleted entity is inert". For discovery.py that premise is wrong twice over: the `vacuum_docked` subscription is on the BRAND's vacuum entity, which is not deleted (only our own device/entities are), and the periodic `async_track_time_interval` (line 171) is not entity-bound at all. Both closures hold `vid` and the `manager` captured at register time, so the next dock — or the next 6-hour tick — runs `run_discovery_pass(hass, manager, vid)` for the deleted vacuum. `update_drift_history` calls `_get_progress_record`, whose `root.setdefault(vacuum_entity_id, {...})` (setup/drift.py:150-158) RE-CREATES the `setup_progress[vid]` bucket that `remove_vacuum_record` just popped, and discovery.py:88 then `await manager.async_save()` persists it.
user_impact: Deleting a vacuum's device leaves a resurrected setup_progress skeleton in storage that survives restarts and shows up in diagnostics. Cosmetic today because `vacuums` stays deleted so the card and `get_known_vacuum_ids` ignore it — but it silently violates the documented "delete is complete and cannot resurrect" contract that _teardown_vacuum was written to guarantee.
guards_checked: __init__.py:576-631 `_teardown_vacuum` — unregisters the adapter config, mapping/battery/error trackers and the panel; it never calls `discovery.register/remove`. discovery.py:41-49 remove() — only reachable from async_unload_entry, not from device deletion. discovery.py:80-94 `_make_run_pass` — the try/except swallows exceptions but the setdefault write happens inside `run_discovery_pass` before anything can raise. rooms/source_refresh.py:227-230 — bails early once the adapter config is gone, so the get_maps call is skipped, but `run_discovery_pass` on line 87 still executes. rooms/room_discovery.py:153-166 — returns [] for a missing adapter, which is precisely the empty-set path that still creates the record.

title: get_manager() is re-fetched after a device-length await, so a config-entry reload mid-dispatch loses the just-started job record (or raises a bare KeyError)
area: WIRE — registration, teardown and the shared spine (services/__init__.py, services/_common.py, services/debug.py, registration survey across all 13 domain modules)
observed_behavior: `_common.get_manager(hass)` is a bare subscript: `hass.data[DOMAIN][DATA_RUNTIME]` (_common.py:35). Five job_control handlers call it TWICE with a real await in between — e.g. `_handle_start_selected_rooms`: line 152 `payload = await get_manager(hass).start_selected_rooms(...)`, then line 156 `await get_manager(hass).async_save()`. This is a gap ACROSS an await, not a synchronous claim. The awaited call is long: core/manager.py:4921 `start_selected_rooms` awaits `_run_global_pre_calls`, `_resolve_live_dispatch_payload`, `_dispatch_clean_payload` and an executor job — it physically commands the robot — and it writes the new job into `self.data['active_jobs'][vac][map_id]` IN MEMORY ONLY (verified: no async_save inside; the handler's line 156 is the only persist). If the config entry reloads during that window (`__init__.py:462` `_async_update_listener` on any options change; the Reload button; or `services/setup.py:165` `setup_add_vacuum`, which explicitly does `hass.async_create_task(hass.config_entries.async_reload(...))`), then either (a) DATA_RUNTIME has been popped (__init__.py:542; `hass.data[DOMAIN]` itself is popped at :546) and line 156 raises an unhandled KeyError, or (b) setup has already re-run and line 156 returns the NEW manager, whose `async_save()` writes storage-loaded data — silently overwriting the storage without the active-job record. Same shape at lines 162/166, 189/193, 200/204, 212/234. `hass.services.async_remove` does not cancel or await in-flight handlers, so the handler outlives the unload.
user_impact: The robot is cleaning but the integration has no active-job record: the card shows no run in progress, no per-room progress or attribution, no learning sample, and no finalization. In path (b) nothing is logged at all — a clean success response with the job silently gone. In path (a) the user gets a raw `KeyError` traceback in the log because line 156 sits OUTSIDE the handler's try/except (lines 151-154).
guards_checked: `_handle_start_selected_rooms`'s try/except (job_control.py:151-154) wraps ONLY the start call — the save at 156 is outside it, so neither path is converted to a HomeAssistantError. `_common.get_manager` (line 35-37) has no `.get()` fallback and no None handling, unlike the sibling pattern in services/setup.py and services/errors.py which use `hass.data.get(DOMAIN, {}).get(DATA_RUNTIME)` and return a graceful shape. `async_unload_entry` (__init__.py:492 then :542) removes services BEFORE popping DATA_RUNTIME, which is correct ordering for NEW calls but does nothing for an already-running handler. `entry.runtime_data = manager` exists (__init__.py:317) as the idiomatic per-entry handle but no handler uses it. core/manager.py:4921 read in full to confirm start_selected_rooms never persists itself.

confirmations: Confirmed: _common.get_manager is a bare hass.data[DOMAIN][DATA_RUNTIME] subscript (no .get), and job_control.py:152/156, 162/166, 189/193, 200/204, 212/234 each call it twice with a real device-length await in between; core/manager.start_selected_rooms writes active_jobs in memory only and never persists itself. __init__.py:542-546 pops DATA_RUNTIME then DOMAIN, and async_remove does not cancel in-flight handlers, so both the KeyError and the wrong-manager-save paths are reachable. Downgraded because the trigger is a config-entry reload landing inside one dispatch window — real but narrow, and the same class of hazard exists for any long await in HA. The genuinely actionable part is the deviation: rooms.py:181/198 and snapshots.py:56 DO capture `manager = get_manager(hass)` once, job_control/queue/run_profiles/room_profiles do not.

Mechanism verified. _common.get_manager (line 35) is a bare hass.data[DOMAIN][DATA_RUNTIME]. job_control handlers call it twice with a real device-length await between (152 -> 156, 162 -> 166, 189/193, 200/204, 212/234). core/manager.py:5060-5062 writes active_jobs in memory only — no async_save inside start_selected_rooms (read 4921-5149 in full). __init__.py:542-546 pops DATA_RUNTIME and then DOMAIN, and async_remove does not await in-flight handlers. setup.py:165 genuinely schedules async_reload from inside a service. title: resolved_call_data's docstring claims an unresolvable map_id always raises; discover_rooms is the one consumer that silently falls through and persists the payload under an empty-string map key
area: WIRE — registration, teardown and the shared spine (services/__init__.py, services/_common.py, services/debug.py, registration survey across all 13 domain modules)
observed_behavior: `resolved_call_data` (_common.py:40-76) documents: "active_map entity missing or sentinel-valued -> returned unchanged; the manager method will raise its own clear error on the missing kwarg, which is the desired behavior (silent fallback to a wrong map would be worse)." That is a CLAIM about 46 downstream manager entry points. I enumerated every method reached via `**resolved_call_data(...)` and checked each signature: all declare `map_id` as a required keyword-only arg (so a missing map_id does raise TypeError, caught and surfaced) EXCEPT two — `dispatch_zone_clean` (core/manager.py:4828, `map_id: str | None = None`, deliberate and documented at job_control.py:120) and `discover_rooms` (rooms/room_crud.py:41, `map_id: str | None = None`), which is NOT deliberate. When the adapter's `active_map` entity exists in the state machine but reads `unknown`/`unavailable`, `get_active_map_id` returns None early (rooms/room_discovery.py:69-74 via `is_blank_state`, entity_helpers.py:39-41 — the blank set includes "unknown" and "unavailable") and never reaches the `_implicit_attribute_map_id` fallback. `resolved_call_data` then returns the data with no map_id key. `room_crud.discover_rooms` proceeds anyway: `discover_rooms_payload` returns `active_map_id: None` (room_discovery.py:268-283), and line 61 computes `_disc_map_id = str(payload.get('active_map_id') or map_id or '')` = `""`, then line 74 writes `data['discovery'][vac][''] = payload`. The rooms are cached under `""` while every reader (room_crud.py:132/233/365/412, setup/drift.py) keys by the real map id, so the setup panel shows zero discovered rooms with no error, and a stale `discovery[""]` bucket is persisted permanently.
guards_checked: `_DISCOVER_ROOMS_SCHEMA` (services/rooms.py:64-69) declares `map_id` Optional, so voluptuous does not reject the omission. `resolved_call_data`'s early return at _common.py:74-76 returns data unchanged rather than raising. `_handle_discover_rooms`'s try/except (rooms.py:139-142) only catches exceptions — there are none on this path. The `run_discovery_pass` call is separately wrapped in a best-effort except (rooms.py:147-152). `get_active_map_id`'s registry fallback (room_discovery.py:79-90) is only reached when the entity is ABSENT from the state machine, not when it is present-but-blank. None rescue it.

confirmations: Confirmed end to end. rooms/room_discovery.get_active_map_id returns None on a present-but-blank active_map state (is_blank_state) before ever reaching _implicit_attribute_map_id; discover_rooms_payload then returns active_map_id=None; room_crud.py:56 computes _disc_map_id = str(payload.get('active_map_id') or map_id or '') = '' and line 74 writes data['discovery'][vac][''] = payload; services/rooms.py:154 persists it. room_crud.discover_rooms really does declare map_id: str | None = None, so resolved_call_data's docstring claim ('the manager method will raise its own clear error') is false for this one consumer. _DISCOVER_ROOMS_SCHEMA marks map_id Optional and nothing raises, so the handler's try/except never fires.

title: The debug-capture auto-stop timer is not cancelled on unload, so an orphaned timer from before a reload kills a capture started after it
area: WIRE — registration, teardown and the shared spine (services/__init__.py, services/_common.py, services/debug.py, registration survey across all 13 domain modules)
observed_behavior: `register_debug_services` builds a closure-local `autostop = {'cancel': None}` (line 483) and stores an `async_call_later` handle in it (line 510) when the caller passes `max_minutes`. `services/debug.py:31` calls `register_debug_services` on every `register(hass)`, i.e. on every config-entry setup — so a reload creates a FRESH `autostop` dict, and `_cancel_autostop` (line 485) can only ever see the new one. Nothing cancels the pending timer: it is not registered via `entry.async_on_unload`, and `async_unload_entry` (__init__.py:496-499) calls `get_capture().stop()` but never touches the timer. `DebugCapture` is a process-wide singleton (`get_capture`, line 404), so when the orphaned timer fires it calls `stop()` on whatever capture is live at that moment.
user_impact: User starts a capture with `max_minutes: 60`, reloads the integration, starts a new capture — the new capture silently stops at the old timer's deadline, logged only as 'debug capture auto-stopped after 60 min'. Diagnostic tooling only; no user data affected.
guards_checked: `_cancel_autostop` (debug_capture.py:485-488) reads only the current closure's dict. `services/debug.py` has no `remove()`/teardown entry point at all — `services/__init__.py:66-71` only calls `hass.services.async_remove` per name, so a module cannot run any other cleanup on unload. `DebugCapture.stop()` (line 249-271) is idempotent, so the double-stop itself is safe; the loss is the ACTIVE capture, not corruption.

title: start_selected_rooms discards every refusal — no supports_response, no exception, DEBUG log only; docs promise a response it cannot return

title: Break schemas do not enforce the break_type→parameter dependency, and the two sibling schemas disagree on which break types exist
area: JOB — job control and queue services (services/job_control.py, services/queue.py)
observed_behavior: `_ADD_QUEUE_BREAK_SCHEMA` requires `break_type` in `["charge_wait", "wait"]` but leaves BOTH `target_battery_percent` and `wait_minutes` `vol.Optional` with no cross-field rule; `_QUEUE_BREAK_ENTRY_SCHEMA` (line 51, used by set_queue_breaks) does the same and additionally leaves `zone_ids` Optional. Same for `charge_wait` with no `target_battery_percent` (normalize line 788), and for a `zone` entry with no `zone_ids` in set_queue_breaks (normalize line 800 → `continue`, entry silently dropped from the wholesale replace, while the response still says `"set": True`). title: get_queue_steps returns `breaks` in a shape set_queue_breaks rejects — the documented read-modify-write round trip fails validation

observed_behavior: `get_queue_steps` returns `breaks` as `[{"after_index": int, "step": {"type": ..., ...}}]` (core/manager.py:1672), documented at 1670-1671 as being there "so the card can reconstruct the combined rooms+breaks reorder list". `_SET_QUEUE_BREAKS_SCHEMA` requires each entry to match `_QUEUE_BREAK_ENTRY_SCHEMA`: `{after_index, break_type, target_battery_percent?, wait_minutes?, zone_ids?}`. `vol.Schema` defaults to `extra=PREVENT_EXTRA`, so an entry carrying `step` is rejected outright, and `break_type` is missing (it is nested one level down as `step.type`). title: async_save() sits after the try/except in every job_control handler — a raise after dispatch leaves a running job in memory only

observed_behavior: All seven mutating job_control handlers use the same shape: `try: payload = await manager.X(...) except Exception as err: raise HomeAssistantError(...) from err` and THEN `await get_manager(hass).async_save()` (lines 156, 166, 193, 204, 234, 245). In start_selected_rooms the writes to `data["queue"]`, `data["payloads"]` and `data["active_jobs"]` land at core/manager.py 4979-4984 and 5060-5062, and `_dispatch_clean_payload` (5021) has already sent the clean command to the robot, before code that can still raise: `get_planned_job_estimate` (5054), `apply_per_room_live_settings` (5102), `_clear_room_selections_after_start` (5112). user_impact: The robot is cleaning, the user sees a red "Failed to start cleaning: …" error, and the active job exists only in RAM. A restart or reload before the next unrelated save orphans the run: it is never finalized, never learned from, and the card shows no job while the vacuum is mid-clean. title: resolved_call_data's docstring claims a "clear error" on unresolvable map_id; the actual failure is a bare TypeError, and no service in either module raises ServiceValidationError
area: JOB — job control and queue services (services/job_control.py, services/queue.py)
observed_behavior: The docstring at lines 58-60 states: "active_map entity missing or sentinel-valued -> returned unchanged; the manager method will raise its own clear error on the missing kwarg, which is the desired behavior". What actually happens is `TypeError: get_queue_state() missing 1 required keyword-only argument: 'map_id'` from the `**resolved_call_data(...)` splat. In queue.py (no try/except) that surfaces as a raw traceback logged as an integration error; in job_control.py it is caught and re-wrapped as `HomeAssistantError("Failed to start cleaning: start_selected_rooms() missing 1 required keyword-only argument: 'map_id'")` — a Python signature error shown to the user as a start failure. Separately, neither module ever raises `ServiceValidationError`, so every user-input error in these 23 services is classified by HA as an integration fault rather than a bad call, and gets a full traceback in the log.
user_impact: A user on an adapter that declares no `active_map` entity (scalar/Tuya Eufy, or any brand-3 adapter) who omits `map_id` — which every schema marks Optional and every services.yaml field describes as "Leave blank to use the current active map" — gets a Python TypeError instead of "this vacuum needs an explicit map_id". The docstring is the reason no one added the check.
guards_checked: _common.py resolved_call_data 40-76 (three pass-through branches; the third returns data with map_id absent and no raise of its own); every schema in job_control.py and queue.py (`vol.Optional("map_id")` — nothing makes it conditionally required); core/manager.py get_queue_state 1541, build_queue 1458, get_start_status 2751, start_selected_rooms 4921 (all keyword-only `map_id: str` with no default, so the splat is the failure point); grep for ServiceValidationError across custom_components/eufy_vacuum/services/ — zero hits.

confirmations: Confirmed: the manager entry points (get_queue_state, build_queue, get_start_status, start_selected_rooms) all declare `map_id: str` keyword-only with no default, so the **resolved_call_data splat raises a bare TypeError, not the 'clear error' the _common.py:57-60 docstring promises. Grep confirms zero ServiceValidationError references anywhere in job_control.py or queue.py. Overlaps A3-ROOMS-11, A5-RUNPROF-7 and A6-DIAG-7 — this is one docstring-vs-code defect surfacing in four areas, and should be deduplicated to a single fix at _common.resolved_call_data.

The docstring at _common.py:57-60 claiming 'the manager method will raise its own clear error' is false: core/manager.py get_queue_state:1541, build_queue:1458, get_start_status:2751 and start_selected_rooms:4921 all declare map_id as a non-defaulted keyword-only str, so the ** splat fails with a bare TypeError. In queue.py (no try/except anywhere) that surfaces as an unhandled traceback; in job_control.py it is re-wrapped as HomeAssistantError with a Python signature as the user-facing text. grep for ServiceValidationError across services/job_control.py and services/queue.py returns zero hits.

title: save_managed_rooms silently wipes a map's entire saved room configuration when the discovery cache for that map is empty
area: ROOMS — room and profile mutation (services/rooms.py, services/room_profiles.py, services/access_graph.py)
observed_behavior: `_handle_save_managed_rooms` forwards `resolved_call_data(...)` straight into `manager.save_managed_rooms(**...)` with no precondition. Downstream (rooms/room_crud.py:232-237) the manager reads `data['discovery'][vacuum][str(map_id)]` and takes `.get('rooms', [])`. When that vacuum/map has no cached discovery the list is `[]`, `build_managed_rooms` returns `{}` (rooms/room_manager.py:57 — the loop body never runs), and line 261 does `map_bucket['rooms'] = managed_rooms`, i.e. an unconditional REPLACE with `{}`. Every room's enabled flag, order, floor_type, clean_mode/fan_speed/water_level/clean_intensity/clean_passes/edge_mopping, per-room `color`, `grants_access_to`, `rules`, `is_dock_room`, `is_transition` and `configured_at` are gone. `if managed_rooms:` at line 273 is False so nothing is re-stamped, and the handler then calls `await manager.async_save()` (services/rooms.py:164), persisting the empty bucket to .storage. The discovery cache is keyed by the ACTIVE map (`_disc_map_id = str(payload.get('active_map_id') or map_id or '')`, room_crud.py:56/74), so a two-map household that calls this service against the non-active map ALWAYS hits the empty branch. The identical hazard is explicitly guarded in the sibling method in the same class — reconcile_room, room_crud.py:145-154, `if not discovered_rooms: return {... 'skipped': 'no_discovery'}` with the comment "Never migrate against an empty discovery — a stale/offline discovery would otherwise rebuild the map to nothing and wipe saved rooms." That guard was never copied to save_managed_rooms.
user_impact: An automation or script calling eufy_vacuum.save_managed_rooms against a map it has not just re-discovered permanently destroys all of that map's room configuration. The service is registered WITHOUT supports_response and the handler returns None (services/rooms.py:236-237, 251-254), so the caller receives no error, no response, and no room_count — nothing at all. The user discovers it when the room entities vanish and the next Start finds an empty queue.
guards_checked: _SAVE_MANAGED_ROOMS_SCHEMA (services/rooms.py:79-88) — types only, no discovery precondition. resolved_call_data (services/_common.py:40-76) — fills map_id from the adapter's active_map entity but does not verify a discovery exists for it; a caller-supplied map_id is passed through untouched.
