The UI path setup_save_rooms (services/setup.py:208-226) calls the SAME manager method with the same absence of a guard.

confirmations: Confirmed as the strongest finding in the set. rooms/room_crud.save_managed_rooms:232-241 sources its room list ONLY from data['discovery'][vac][str(map_id)]['rooms'] and never re-discovers; rooms/room_manager.build_managed_rooms:57 iterates that list so an empty list yields {} (existing_rooms is consulted only per-room INSIDE the discovered loop at line 64, so it cannot re-add anything); room_crud.py:261 does an unconditional map_bucket['rooms'] = managed_rooms; services/rooms.py:164 persists it. The sibling guard is verbatim where the finder said — room_crud.py:145-154, `if not discovered_rooms: return {... 'skipped': 'no_discovery'}` with the comment 'would otherwise rebuild the map to nothing and wipe saved rooms'. That guard is absent here. No supports_response, so the caller gets nothing back.

Reproduced. Call: eufy_vacuum.save_managed_rooms {vacuum_entity_id: vacuum.x, map_id: '1'} on an install where data['discovery'][vac]['1'] is absent or stale. rooms/room_crud.py:232-241 sources rooms ONLY from that snapshot; an empty list gives filtered_rooms = [], room_manager.py:57's loop never runs, and line 261 does the unconditional map_bucket['rooms'] = {} — destroying enabled, order, floor_type, per-room clean settings, color, grants_access_to, rules, is_dock_room, is_transition and configured_at. title: enabled_room_ids: null coerces to [] and wipes every managed room — the exact opposite of omitting the key
area: ROOMS — room and profile mutation (services/rooms.py, services/room_profiles.py, services/access_graph.py)
observed_behavior: `vol.Optional('enabled_room_ids'): vol.All(cv.ensure_list, [vol.Coerce(int)])`. I ran HA's `cv.ensure_list` against the installed core: `ensure_list(None) -> []` (it starts `if value is None: return []`). Validating `{'vacuum_entity_id': 'vacuum.x', 'enabled_room_ids': None}` through the real schema returns `{'enabled_room_ids': []}` — verified by execution. Downstream, build_managed_rooms goes to explicit trouble to distinguish the two cases: line 53 `has_explicit_enabled_ids = enabled_room_ids is not None`, and line 61 `if has_explicit_enabled_ids and room_id not in explicit_enabled_ids: continue`. But `_normalize_enabled_room_ids` (room_manager.py:10-13) collapses `[]` to `set()` via `if not enabled_room_ids: return set()`, so with `[]` the flag is True and the set is empty — every discovered room is skipped, `managed = {}`, and `map_bucket['rooms'] = {}` (room_crud.py:261) destroys the map exactly as in ROOMS-1. The None/[] distinction the manager relies on has already been destroyed one layer up, at the schema boundary.
user_impact: A YAML author who writes `enabled_room_ids:` with a blank value (a key with no value is None in YAML — the single most common YAML slip) gets total destruction of that map's room configuration, while the DOCUMENTED behaviour for that field (docs/advanced/03-services.md:255, 'Omit to keep all rooms enabled') is the opposite. No error, no response (the service has no supports_response). Same for an explicit `enabled_room_ids: []`, which no documentation covers.
guards_checked: The vol.Coerce(int) item validator never runs on an empty list. `_normalize_enabled_room_ids` (room_manager.py:10-23) — its `if not enabled_room_ids: return set()` is the collapse, not a guard. There is no minimum-length check (contrast `_SETUP_REJECT_ROOMS_SCHEMA`, services/setup.py:114, which at least makes room_ids Required). `_handle_save_managed_rooms` (rooms.py:157-164) inspects nothing. services.yaml marks enabled_room_ids `required: true` (line ~62) but that is a UI hint only — HA does not enforce services.yaml requiredness, the voluptuous schema does, and there it is vol.Optional.

confirmations: Confirmed by reading HA's installed cv.ensure_list (config_validation.py:354-357): `if value is None: return []`. So {'enabled_room_ids': None} validates to []. Downstream, room_manager.py:53 sets has_explicit_enabled_ids = (enabled_room_ids is not None) — True for [] — while _normalize_enabled_room_ids collapses [] to set(), so line 61 skips every discovered room and line 261 replaces the map's rooms with {}. The None-vs-[] distinction the manager deliberately relies on is destroyed at the schema boundary one layer up. A bare `enabled_room_ids:` key in YAML is the most common possible slip, and docs:255 documents the opposite behaviour for omission.

title: save_managed_rooms stamps every room's floor type as user-confirmed while its schema makes it structurally impossible to supply one
area: ROOMS — room and profile mutation (services/rooms.py, services/room_profiles.py, services/access_graph.py)
observed_behavior: `_SAVE_MANAGED_ROOMS_SCHEMA` declares only vacuum_entity_id / map_id / enabled_room_ids. The manager method it calls accepts a fourth kwarg, `floor_types: dict[int, str] | None` (rooms/room_crud.py:227), and the sibling UI service setup_save_rooms DOES expose it (`vol.Optional('floor_types'): vol.Schema({cv.string: cv.string})`, services/setup.py:100, passed at setup.py:217). Because voluptuous defaults to PREVENT_EXTRA, passing floor_types to save_managed_rooms is rejected outright — I verified: `extra keys not allowed @ data['floor_types']`. So every room this service creates falls to `str(existing.get('floor_type', 'hardwood'))` (room_manager.py:71). It then calls `self._manager.confirm_floor_type(...)` for EVERY managed room unconditionally (room_crud.py:278-283), marking that guessed 'hardwood' as explicitly user-confirmed in the onboarding store. That defeats the start gate at core/manager.py:2805-2825 (`if not onboarding['floor_types_complete'] -> blocked, reason='onboarding_required'`), which exists precisely to force the carpet question before the first clean.
user_impact: A carpeted room created through this service is recorded as hardwood and confirmed, so the user is never asked. The carpet invariants in _protected_room_config (profiles/manager.py:98-105 — force water 'Off', edge_mopping False, downgrade mop modes) key off floor_type and therefore never fire for it. When the user subsequently applies a mop profile to the map (apply_room_profile with vacuum_mop_deep), that room gets water 'Medium' + edge mopping from FLOOR_TYPE_WATER_DEFAULTS['hardwood']='Low'/profile water and the robot wet-mops carpet, with the readiness gate showing green.
guards_checked: PREVENT_EXTRA confirmed by executing the exact schema. `_handle_save_managed_rooms` (rooms.py:157-164) passes `**resolved_call_data` so it cannot inject floor_types either. confirm_floor_type (onboarding/manager.py:148-160) is a bare setter with no 'was this actually asked' flag. build_managed_rooms's floor_type precedence (room_manager.py:68-72) preserves an EXISTING floor_type, so this only bites rooms newly admitted by this service — but that is exactly the population the onboarding gate is for. reconcile_room takes the opposite care, calling onboarding.remap_confirmed_floor_types explicitly (room_crud.py:193-197).

confirmations: Confirmed both halves. _SAVE_MANAGED_ROOMS_SCHEMA declares only three keys under default PREVENT_EXTRA, so floor_types is rejected — while the sibling _SETUP_SAVE_ROOMS_SCHEMA (setup.py:100) DOES declare it and setup.py:217 passes it. Meanwhile room_crud.py:273-283 calls confirm_floor_type for EVERY managed room unconditionally, and onboarding/manager.confirm_floor_type is a bare setter that writes floor_types_confirmed[room_id] = True with no 'was this actually asked' flag. So rooms newly admitted through this service get the 'hardwood' fallback from room_manager.py:68-72 stamped as user-confirmed, defeating the onboarding gate for exactly the population it exists to protect.

Both halves verified. _SAVE_MANAGED_ROOMS_SCHEMA (rooms.py:79-88) has no floor_types key and voluptuous PREVENT_EXTRA rejects it (executed: extra keys not allowed), while the manager accepts floor_types (room_crud.py:227) and setup.py:100/217 does pass it. room_manager.py:68-72 then falls back to str(existing.get('floor_type','hardwood')), and room_crud.py:278-283 calls confirm_floor_type for EVERY managed room unconditionally; onboarding/manager.py:148-161 is a bare setter with no 'was this asked' flag, so the onboarding gate is satisfied for a guessed value. Downgraded to MEDIUM: it only bites rooms newly admitted through this YAML-only service (existing floor types are preserved), and the wet-mop-on-carpet outcome needs a second user action (applying a mop profile) to materialise.

title: apply_room_profile silently no-ops on unknown room ids and returns a success-shaped response with no way to tell
area: ROOMS — room and profile mutation (services/rooms.py, services/room_profiles.py, services/access_graph.py)
observed_behavior: `_handle_apply_room_profile` returns the manager payload verbatim without inspecting it. In ProfileManager.apply_room_profile (profiles/manager.py:664-681) the per-room loop does `room = rooms.get(room_key); if room is None: continue` — an id that is not on the map is dropped with no record. The success return (profiles/manager.py:695-701) is `{vacuum_entity_id, map_id, profile_name, updated_room_ids: [...], room_count: N}`. With every requested id unknown that is `updated_room_ids: []`, `room_count: 0` and NO error key — structurally identical to a legitimate success. The only failure the service reports is profile_not_found, which returns a DIFFERENT shape (`error` present, `room_count` absent, profiles/manager.py:635-641), so a caller branching on `error` sees nothing wrong. Two direct siblings do report this same condition: core/manager.update_room_fields returns `{'ok': False, 'error': 'room_not_found', 'reason_detail': 'The selected room was not found on this map.'}` (core/manager.py:1313-1323) for exactly one bad room_id, and ProfileManager.apply_run_profile returns an explicit `missing_room_ids` list (profiles/manager.py:1224, 1262). apply_room_profile has neither. Additionally `_safe_int(r, -1) >= 0` (line 652) silently discards any non-numeric entry, and it admits room_id 0 while _normalize_grants_access_to and normalize_run_profile_steps both require `> 0`.
user_impact: An automation that applies a named profile to rooms after a re-segment renumbered them (Roborock does this routinely) reports success while changing nothing — the rooms clean at their old settings and the user has no signal. supports_response=True is declared (room_profiles.py:230-233), so the card DOES receive the payload; there is simply nothing in it to branch on. This is the same 'failure returns the success shape' seam the card audit flagged one layer up.
guards_checked: _APPLY_ROOM_PROFILE_SCHEMA (room_profiles.py:103-110) validates shape only — cv.ensure_list + Coerce(int) accepts any integer including ids that exist on no map, and accepts an empty list. resolved_call_data (services/_common.py:40-76) resolves map_id but never validates it against the stored maps. ensure_map_bucket (profiles/manager.py:643, maps/map_manager.py:10-28) CREATES a durable empty bucket for an unknown map_id rather than rejecting it, so a typo'd map_id both silently no-ops and adds a phantom map that then appears in get_vacuum_maps. `_handle_apply_room_profile` does `await get_manager(hass).async_save()` unconditionally (room_profiles.py:172), persisting the phantom bucket.

confirmations: Confirmed: profiles/manager.apply_room_profile's per-room loop does `room = rooms.get(room_key); if room is None: continue` with no record, and the success return carries no error key while profile_not_found returns a structurally different shape — so a caller branching on `error` sees nothing. The sibling contrast is real: apply_run_profile returns an explicit missing_room_ids list and update_room_fields returns {'ok': False, 'error': 'room_not_found'}. Downgraded because the returned room_count IS a usable discriminator (0 vs len(room_ids)), which weakens the 'structurally identical to success' claim — the defect is the missing missing_room_ids field, not a total absence of signal.

Confirmed at profiles/manager.py:665-669 (`room = rooms.get(room_key); if room is None: continue` — no record kept) and 695-701 (the success return has no error key). The contrast is real: core/manager.py:1313-1323 update_room_fields returns room_not_found with a reason_detail, and apply_run_profile returns an explicit missing_room_ids list (1224/1262). ensure_map_bucket at 643 also durably creates a bucket for a typo'd map_id, and room_profiles.py:172 async_saves it. Downgraded to MEDIUM: the response is not truly indistinguishable — room_count: 0 with updated_room_ids: [] is a checkable signal — and nothing stored is destroyed.

title: update_room_fields accepts any clean_mode string; a casing/spelling variant keeps water in storage and in the UI but silently drops it from the wire payload
area: ROOMS — room and profile mutation (services/rooms.py, services/room_profiles.py, services/access_graph.py)
observed_behavior: `vol.Optional('clean_mode'): cv.string` — no vocabulary check, and services.yaml offers a bare `text: {}` selector with no enumeration (services.yaml:163-166), and docs/advanced/03-services.md's update_room_fields table lists clean_mode with an empty Notes cell. The value is stored verbatim: core/manager.py:1330-1331 does `updates['clean_mode'] = str(clean_mode)` and _protected_room_config only lowercases into a LOCAL variable for its tests (`clean_mode = str(protected.get('clean_mode','')).lower()`, profiles/manager.py:95) — `protected['clean_mode']` is only reassigned inside the carpet branch, so the stored casing survives. title: set_run_profile_steps accepts a bare `list` and silently drops or clamps every malformed step; only 'at least one room_group survived' is enforced
observed_behavior: `_RUN_PROFILE_STEPS_SCHEMA` declares `vol.Required("steps"): list` — a type check with no element schema, so any list contents pass validation. `ProfileManager.normalize_run_profile_steps` (profiles/manager.py:750-809) then drops, without any diagnostic, every step whose `type` is not one of room_group/charge_wait/wait/zone (a typo'd `charge`, `charge_to`, `dry`), every charge_wait whose `target_battery_percent` is not int-coercible, every room_group whose rooms all fail `room_id > 0`, and it silently CLAMPS `target_battery_percent` to 1..100 and `wait_minutes` to 1..1440. title: acknowledge_error returns the same {"acknowledged": true} whether the latch was deleted, merely MARKED, or was never there — and both docstrings still describe the pre-audit delete semantics
observed_behavior: `ErrorTracker.acknowledge` (core/error_tracker.py:957-1008) has three materially different outcomes and one return type: (a) mid-run with a dict latch and `run_is_in_flight(...)` true, it MARKS — `latch["acknowledged"] = True; latch["current_message"] = ""; latch["recovered"] = True` — and KEEPS the latch so the finalizer can still harvest its evidence; (b) otherwise it DELETES via `record["active_run_error"] = None`; (c) it returns True whenever `vacuum_entity_id in root` even if both latches were already None. All three return the bare `True` that the handler wraps as `{"acknowledged": bool(ok), "vacuum_entity_id": ..., "scope": ...}`. There is no field naming which branch ran and no field saying whether anything was actually latched. The handler docstring (services/errors.py:55-63) still says "Clear the active-run / last-device error latch(es)" and "The next rising edge re-creates whichever latch the upstream condition triggers" — describing behaviour the code no longer has for the in-flight case, where the latch is retained and later collected by the post-finalize auto-clear. The module docstring (line 4) repeats "clear ... latch(es)". Separately, the failure branch is inconsistent: `tracker is None` returns `{"acknowledged": False, "reason": "tracker_not_loaded"}` with only two keys, while an unknown/typo'd `vacuum_entity_id` returns `{"acknowledged": False, "vacuum_entity_id": ..., "scope": ...}` with NO `reason` at all.
user_impact: A caller (card or automation) that wants to confirm the alert was cleared cannot: `acknowledged: true` is returned for a vacuum with no error at all, and the mid-run case reports the same success while the latch is deliberately still present. A caller checking `reason` to explain a failure gets a KeyError-shaped absence for the most likely real failure (wrong entity id) and a value only for the least likely one (tracker not loaded). Anyone reading services/errors.py to understand acknowledge semantics is told the latch is deleted, which is exactly the behaviour audit #5 removed.

title: Mutate-then-save is not atomic in all three write services: a save failure surfaces an error while the change has already taken effect in memory

title: async_initialize spawns loop-lifetime work with no teardown — after a config-entry reload the PREVIOUS manager writes its stale self.data over the live store
observed_behavior: async_initialize (306) ends by spawning background work that outlives the config entry: the re-arm loop at 473-480 calls phase_runner.rearm_dock_phase_if_needed -> _spawn_dock_poller -> hass.async_create_task (jobs/phase_runner.py:98), and the external-run path arms hass.helpers async_call_later timers (learning/external_run.py:119 and :203, EXTERNAL_FINALIZE_GRACE_S=300s re-armed up to EXTERNAL_GRACE_MAX_RECHECKS=8, i.e. up to ~45 min of live timers). The manager exposes NO shutdown method (grep for 'def shutdown/async_shutdown/stop(' over core/manager.py, jobs/phase_runner.py, learning/external_run.py, live_refresh/ returns nothing) and registers nothing with the entry (grep 'async_on_unload' over those files returns nothing). async_unload_entry (custom_components/eufy_vacuum/__init__.py:465-546) removes listeners, trackers, services, panels and pops DATA_RUNTIME, but never cancels those tasks/timers. On reload, async_setup_entry builds a SECOND EufyVacuumManager (__init__.py:234) with its own EufyVacuumStorage/Store over the SAME STORAGE_KEY. The orphaned callbacks hold self._manager = the OLD manager and end in a full-dict write: learning/external_run.py:213 'await self._manager.async_save()' and jobs/phase_runner.py:856 'self._manager.hass.async_create_task(self._manager._async_save_logged())'. core/manager.py:803 async_save is a bare 'await self.storage.async_save(self.data)' — it writes the WHOLE root dict, so the old manager's pre-reload snapshot replaces everything the new manager has persisted since. No interleaving argument is needed: the stale write is a single scheduled callback, not a race across an await.
user_impact: Every change persisted after a reload can be silently reverted. Concrete: user runs setup_add_vacuum, which saves the new vacuum then schedules a reload (services/setup.py:166); 2-5 minutes later the pre-reload manager's external-run grace timer fires, calls _finalize_external_run and async_save, and the store goes back to the snapshot without vacuum #2. The UI keeps showing the new vacuum (the live manager's in-memory dict) until the next HA restart, when it is gone — along with any rooms, profiles, themes, queue edits or job state saved in the same window. Same shape via Options-flow reload and the integration page Reload button. The orphaned charge/wait poller can also still call maybe_advance_phase and dispatch the next room, so a second manager and a dead one can both drive the same physical run.

title: Room-history preload overwrites the persisted cache with {} whenever the rebuild throws, and marks the cache ready so it never retries
observed_behavior: async_initialize seeds data['room_history'] from storage (line 316) and it is persisted by async_save like any other root key. _load_room_history_cache_sync (2206) wraps the ENTIRE rebuild — LearningHistoryStore construction, load_jobs_index, load_all_completed_jobs and every ingest — in one 'except Exception' (2252) that logs and falls through to 'return temp_root.get(vacuum_key, {})', i.e. an EMPTY dict on any failure (ensure_dirs/os.makedirs OSError on a read-only or relocated config dir, permission error, an ingest raising on a malformed record). async_preload_room_history_cache then does an unconditional REPLACE — 'self.data.setdefault("room_history", {})[vacuum_key] = vacuum_history' (2275) — with no emptiness or sentinel check, and immediately adds the vacuum to _room_history_cache_ready (2276), so _ensure_room_history_cache (2195) will never schedule another rebuild for the life of the process. The preload is not opportunistic: sensor/__init__.py:227 fires it for every vacuum at platform setup on every startup, and rooms/room_crud.py:201/:268 and profiles/manager.py:689 discard the ready flag to force a rebuild after a room renumber/delete. The empty dict is then written to the store by the next unrelated async_save. Partial failure is worse than total: the try wraps the whole loop, so a throw on job file 7 of 30 keeps the first 6 and silently rolls every other room's last_cleaned_at back to an older value.
user_impact: Every room's cleaning-history sensor and the card's last-cleaned/last-mopped chips read 'never cleaned' for the rest of the HA run, with nothing shown to the user (the only signal is a log line). The blank state is then persisted. It also silently weakens a destructive-action guard: setup/protection.py:63-72 derives the 'has_learning_data' protection reason from data['room_history'][vac][map] being non-empty, so a map that does have history drops a reason and can fall from 'high' (typed confirmation) to a lower protection level for map deletion.
guards_checked: _ensure_room_history_cache (2195) — only guards against a concurrent/duplicate load, never against a failed one; _room_history_cache_loading is discarded in the finally (2286) but ready is set before it, so no retry; the 'or ["unknown"]' at 2279 only affects which map the update callback names, it does not detect the empty result; get_room_cleaning_history (2421) calls _ensure_room_history_cache but reads whatever is in data with no fallback to the pre-replace value; LearningHistoryStore.read_json (learning/history_store.py:157) swallows its own errors and returns None, so the outer except only fires for errors read_json does not cover — which is exactly the path-level ones.

confirmations: Mechanism confirmed: _load_room_history_cache_sync (manager.py:2206-2256) wraps LearningHistoryStore construction, load_jobs_index, load_all_completed_jobs and every ingest in ONE `except Exception` and falls through to `return temp_root.get(vacuum_key, {})` — {} on any throw. async_preload_room_history_cache then does an unconditional replace at 2275 with no emptiness check and adds to _room_history_cache_ready at 2276, and _ensure_room_history_cache (2195-2204) early-returns forever after. room_history IS a persisted root key (core/storage.py saves the whole dict), so the empty value is written by the next async_save. setup/protection.py:63-72 does derive has_learning_data from data['room_history'][vac][map] being truthy, so the protection-reason claim holds. Severity corrected DOWN: I traced every raise site and read_json (history_store.py:157-177) swallows JSONDecodeError AND bare Exception, _safe_int/parse_timestamp guard the ingest, so the only realistic throw is a path-level OSError from ensure_dirs' four mkdir calls or list_job_files — a read-only/relocated/permission-broken config dir. That is narrow conditions, i.e. MEDIUM, not HIGH.

Mechanism CONFIRMED at manager.py:2206-2286. _load_room_history_cache_sync wraps the entire rebuild in one 'except Exception' (2252) and falls through to 'return temp_root.get(vacuum_key, {})' — an empty dict on any failure. async_preload_room_history_cache then does an unconditional REPLACE at 2275 with no emptiness/sentinel check and adds the vacuum to _room_history_cache_ready at 2276, after which _ensure_room_history_cache (2198-2199) early-returns forever for this process. data['room_history'] is a persisted top-level key (seeded at 316, written by the whole-dict async_save), so the blank subtree is durable. LearningHistoryStore.read_json swallows its own errors, so the outer except only fires on path-level failures (read-only/relocated config dir, permission error) or an ingest raising on a malformed record — none of which is a routine condition — and the ready flag is per-process, so a plain HA restart retries the rebuild. title: Startup re-seed of the bundled theme library resurrects themes the user deleted, and re-points default_theme_id
observed_behavior: async_initialize constructs ThemeManager(self.data) at 347, whose __init__ (themes/manager.py:55-68) calls ensure_preloaded_theme_library (themes/preloaded.py:514). That seeder walks PRELOADED_THEME_SPECS and re-creates any spec id that is not currently in data['theme']['library'] (:525-542) — it has no record of user DELETIONS, only a 'don't clobber what exists' rule. The delete side has no matching guard: ThemeManager.delete_theme (themes/manager.py:379-397) does a plain 'del theme["library"][theme_id]' with no source=='core' check, and the card renders the delete control for every preset except the current default (src/renderers/theme.js:511-518, wired at src/bindings/theme.js:1220). Sibling asymmetry: save/import stamp source='core'/user provenance and the seeder even backfills source='core' onto existing bundled entries (:534), so it KNOWS which entries are its own — it just never asks whether the user removed one on purpose. The seeder also re-stamps data['theme']['default_theme_id'] = 'theme_follow_ha' whenever the stored default is empty or names a missing theme (:544-546), which is exactly the state delete_theme leaves behind when the deleted theme was the default (:388-389).
user_impact: A user who curates the theme library — deleting the bundled themes they do not want, with a confirm dialog implying it stuck — finds all of them back in the picker after the next HA restart, silently and with no error. If the deleted theme was the global default, the default is silently re-pointed at theme_follow_ha, changing the rendered theme for every vacuum that is not individually pinned.
guards_checked: ensure_preloaded_theme_library's 'if theme_id in library: continue' (:527) protects EDITS to a bundled theme but not deletion; delete_theme (themes/manager.py:379) read in full — the only precondition is 'theme_id in library'; the card's delete button is suppressed only for state.defaultThemeId (src/renderers/theme.js:511), not for core-sourced presets; no tombstone/'deleted_preloaded' key exists anywhere in data['theme'] (the sub-tree seeded at themes/manager.py:64-67 is library/default_theme_id/vacuums only).

confirmations: Confirmed end to end. ThemeManager.__init__ (themes/manager.py:55-68) calls ensure_preloaded_theme_library, which at preloaded.py:525-542 re-creates any PRELOADED_THEME_SPECS id not currently in library (the `if theme_id in library: continue` at :527 only protects EDITS, and :534 backfills source='core' on survivors — so the seeder demonstrably knows which entries are its own). delete_theme (themes/manager.py:379-397) read in full: its only precondition is `theme_id not in library`, then a plain `del theme['library'][theme_id]`, and :388-389 sets default_theme_id = None when the deleted theme was the default — exactly the state :544-546 re-stamps to 'theme_follow_ha'. No tombstone key exists anywhere in the theme sub-tree (only library/default_theme_id/vacuums are seeded). The card renders the delete control for every preset except state.defaultThemeId (src/renderers/theme.js:511-518) with no source check, and the path is service-backed (themes/services.py:202-206, SERVICE_DELETE_THEME).

CONFIRMED. themes/manager.py:55-68 calls ensure_preloaded_theme_library on EVERY ThemeManager construction (i.e. every async_initialize, every restart AND every reload), and themes/preloaded.py:514-546 re-creates any PRELOADED_THEME_SPECS id not currently in library — the only guard is 'if theme_id in library: continue' (:527), which protects edits, not deletions. There is no tombstone key anywhere in data['theme'] (the sub-tree is library/default_theme_id/vacuums only, manager.py:64-67). delete_theme (themes/manager.py:379-397) read in full: its only precondition is 'theme_id in library' — no source=='core' check — and it sets default_theme_id=None when the deleted theme was the default (:388-389), which is precisely the state the seeder re-points to 'theme_follow_ha' at :544-546. Card side verified: src/renderers/theme.js:511-518 renders the delete control for every preset except state.defaultThemeId, so bundled themes are deletable from the UI. SEVERITY DOWNGRADED to MEDIUM: no durable user data is destroyed (user themes are untouched; the resurrection ADDS entries), and the consequence is a presentation-layer surprise — deleted presets reappear, and the global default silently re-points. Recurring and silent, but cosmetic in effect, so MEDIUM rather than HIGH.

title: The startup backfill and setup_progress migration hard-code Eufy vocabulary and structurally cannot consult the adapter
observed_behavior: The backfill block (417-439) stamps _room.setdefault('floor_type', 'hardwood') and _room.setdefault('profile_name', 'vacuum_quick') into every stored room. rooms/room_defaults.py exists specifically to be THE single answer to 'what settings does a room start with', resolved from the brand's room_profiles.default_profile, and its module docstring enumerates the four hand-maintained copies of exactly these literals that it replaced; this block is a fifth copy that the refactor missed. It cannot be fixed in place by calling the adapter either: the whole block runs inside async_initialize, before register_brand_adapter (__init__.py:307), so _get_adapter_config would return None here. The same pattern sits in _migrate_setup_progress (551-561), which hard-codes completed_steps = ['add_vacuum','import_active_map','save_rooms'] — its own docstring calls them 'the three legacy Eufy steps' — rather than the adapter-declared list that the reader uses (setup/status.py:75 get_adapter_setup_steps). Today both shipped brands declare exactly those three ids (adapters/eufy/adapter.py:546, adapters/roborock/adapter.py:430), so nothing diverges yet.
user_impact: No divergence on the two shipped brands today. A third brand whose room_profiles.default_profile is not 'vacuum_quick' would have any legacy room missing profile_name stamped with another brand's profile key at startup (get_room_profile falls back to the catalog default for an unknown name, so it degrades rather than crashes); a brand declaring a different setup-step vocabulary would have a pre-state-machine install stamped complete against step ids it does not declare, leaving its real first step showing as incomplete forever.
guards_checked: profiles/room_profiles.py:243-261 normalize_floor_type coerces anything outside the allowed set back to 'hardwood', and get_room_profile (:264-291) falls back to the catalog default then DEFAULT_ROOM_PROFILE_NAME, so neither stamped value can crash a reader — this is a vocabulary/ownership defect, not a crash; setdefault means rooms written by current code (which always emit both fields via RoomConfig) are untouched, so only pre-release stored rooms are reachable; is_step_completed (setup/drift.py:171) is plain list membership, so extra stamped ids are inert.

confirmations: Confirmed by reading manager.py:417-439 and 528-561. The backfill stamps `_room.setdefault('floor_type','hardwood')` and `_room.setdefault('profile_name','vacuum_quick')`, and _migrate_setup_progress hard-codes completed_steps ['add_vacuum','import_active_map','save_rooms'] with its own docstring calling them 'the three legacy Eufy steps'. rooms/room_defaults.resolve_new_room_defaults_for_vacuum is the extracted brand-resolved answer (save_managed_rooms uses it at room_crud.py:253-255, and build_managed_rooms makes new_room_defaults a REQUIRED arg precisely to stop this pattern), so this block is an unmigrated copy. The 'cannot consult the adapter here' point is also confirmed — the block runs before register_brand_adapter. Correctly scoped future_brand_only/LOW: both shipped adapters declare exactly those three step ids and normalize_floor_type/get_room_profile coerce unknown values, so nothing diverges today.

CONFIRMED as a vocabulary/ownership defect with no shipped-brand divergence. manager.py:429-430 stamps _room.setdefault('floor_type','hardwood') and _room.setdefault('profile_name','vacuum_quick'), and rooms/room_defaults.py's module docstring explicitly names itself THE single answer to 'what settings does a fresh room start with', enumerating the four hand-maintained copies it replaced — this backfill block is a fifth the refactor missed, and it is structurally unfixable in place because it runs inside async_initialize, before register_brand_adapter (__init__.py:307), so the adapter cannot be consulted. Verified the contrast: RoomMapManager.save_managed_rooms (rooms/room_crud.py:255) DOES route through resolve_new_room_defaults_for_vacuum. _migrate_setup_progress (manager.py:551-561) hard-codes the same three Eufy step ids, and both shipped adapters declare exactly those, so nothing diverges today. Impact is future-brand-only and degrades rather than crashes (normalize_floor_type / get_room_profile both fall back), so LOW is correct.

title: Room-update fan-out identifies "stale" entities by unique_id PREFIX, so a room edit on one vacuum permanently deletes a sibling vacuum's entities from the entity registry
observed_behavior:
`_notify_rooms_updated(vacuum_entity_id, map_id)` (core/manager.py:622) carries the identity of the changed map as a TUPLE, but every entity-syncing subscriber throws that tuple away and re-derives ownership by string prefix. switch.py:71, number.py:101 and sensor/__init__.py:255 + :312 all compute `prefix = f"{vacuum_entity_id.replace('.', '_')}_{map_id}_"` and then classify every unique_id in their in-memory `entity_map` that `startswith(prefix)` and is not in `desired` as STALE — deleting it with `hass.async_create_task(stale.async_remove())` AND `_registry.async_remove(entity_id)` (switch.py:77-83).

The unique_id is built by `entity_helpers.make_room_unique_id` (entity_helpers.py:63-72) as `f"{vacuum_key}_{map_id}_{room_id}_{suffix}"` where `vacuum_key = vacuum_entity_id.replace('.', '_')`. Both the vacuum key and the map id are variable-length, unquoted, and joined by the same `_` separator, so `<keyA>_<mapA>_` is a valid PREFIX of `<keyB>_...` whenever `keyB == keyA + "_" + mapA`.

That is exactly what Home Assistant produces for two identical robots: vacuum A = `vacuum.robovac` (key `vacuum_robovac`), vacuum B = `vacuum.robovac_2` (key `vacuum_robovac_2`). A's map "2" prefix is `vacuum_robovac_2_` — which every single one of B's room unique_ids begins with, on EVERY one of B's maps.

Nothing downstream re-checks ownership: `entity_map` is keyed by unique_id alone and stores no (vacuum, map) tuple; `_registry.async_get_entity_id("switch", DOMAIN, uid)` resolves the id without validating who owns it; and the room entities DO carry `_vacuum_entity_id` / `_map_id` attributes (room_entities.py) that the sweep never consults. The manager's fan-out then swallows nothing here because nothing raises — the deletion is the success path.

The sibling that got this right proves the shape: button.py:169 builds `f"{vacuum_key}_{map_id}_run_profile_"`, and the trailing literal segment makes a bleed impossible (B's map id would have to literally be `run_profile`). Only the four room-entity prefixes end on a bare `_`.
user_impact: On any multi-vacuum install where one vacuum's entity_id is another's plus a numeric suffix (HA's own default for a second identical robot), the first room edit — toggling a room switch, applying a room profile, saving rooms, reordering the queue — on vacuum A's map "2" silently deletes ALL of vacuum B's room switches, room number entities, room-history sensors and rule-status sensors from the entity registry. Registry deletion is durable and takes the user's customizations with it: renamed entity_ids, custom names, icons and area assignments are gone, and every automation, script and dashboard card referencing those entity_ids breaks. No error is surfaced anywhere — the sweep logs nothing and `_notify_rooms_updated`'s try/except never fires because this is not an exception path. The entities reappear (as fresh, un-customized registry entries) only after a config-entry reload or HA restart.
guards_checked: (1) `_notify_rooms_updated` core/manager.py:622-637 — passes vacuum_entity_id and map_id as separate kwargs; the loss of that separation is entirely on the consumer side, so the notifier offers no rescue. (2) `sort_room_items` (entity_helpers.py:75) — filters unconfigured rooms only; performs no vacuum/map scoping. (3) `desired` in every sweep is built exclusively from the notified vacuum/map's rooms, so a foreign entity can never be rescued by appearing in it. (4) `_registry.async_get_entity_id("switch", DOMAIN, uid)` — a pure unique_id lookup, no ownership assertion. (5) The `EufyVacuumRoomEntity` base (room_entities.py:41) stores `_vacuum_entity_id` and `_map_id` on each entity — a correct check is available and is not used. (6) button.py:166-169 — the only prefix builder with a trailing literal segment, and the only one immune; confirms the guard is absent rather than unnecessary. (7) config_flow.py:45-51 — single-instance domain, so this is not mitigated by per-vacuum config entries; __init__.py comments (line 579-586) confirm the design is explicitly "one entry manages many vacuums".

confirmations: Strongest finding in the set; confirmed line by line and I specifically tried to kill it on the scoping question. entity_map in switch.py:30 is built by iterating `manager.data['maps']` over ALL vacuums and ALL maps (switch.py:32-45) — it is ONE dict for the whole entry, not per-vacuum, so a foreign vacuum's unique_ids are genuinely present in the dict the sweep scans. The prefix is `f"{vacuum_entity_id.replace('.','_')}_{map_id}_"` at switch.py:71, number.py:101 and sensor/__init__.py:255/285/312/341, while make_room_unique_id (entity_helpers.py:63-72) emits `{vacuum_key}_{map_id}_{room_id}_{suffix}` — both variable-length fields joined by the same separator, so vacuum.robovac + map '2' yields prefix `vacuum_robovac_2_`, which prefixes EVERY unique_id of vacuum.robovac_2 on every one of its maps. `desired` is built only from the notified vacuum/map, `entity_map` stores no ownership tuple, and `_registry.async_get_entity_id('switch', DOMAIN, uid)` performs no ownership check, so the foreign entities are removed from the entity registry (switch.py:77-83) — durable, taking renamed entity_ids/areas/customizations with it. The control case holds: button.py:166-169 is the only prefix builder ending in a literal segment ('..._run_profile_') and is the only one immune.

Mechanism CONFIRMED. entity_helpers.make_room_unique_id (entity_helpers.py:63-72) builds '{vacuum_key}_{map_id}_{room_id}_{suffix}' with both variable-length fields joined by the same '_' and no quoting. switch.py:71-83 (and identically number.py:101-104, sensor/__init__.py:255/285/312/341, setup/delete.py:136) classifies stale purely by uid.startswith(f"{vac_key}_{map_id}_") and then does BOTH stale.async_remove() and _registry.async_remove(entity_id). Critically, entity_map is built across ALL vacuums (switch.py:32-45 iterates manager.data['maps'] for every vacuum), so a foreign vacuum's entities ARE in the sweep's search space; nothing re-checks ownership even though EufyVacuumRoomEntity carries _vacuum_entity_id/_map_id, and 'desired' is built only from the notified vacuum so it can never rescue them. Concrete case walked: vacuum.robovac (key vacuum_robovac) with a map id '2' yields prefix 'vacuum_robovac_2_', which every unique_id of vacuum.robovac_2 begins with on every one of its maps — and 'vacuum.robovac_2' is exactly what HA generates for a second identical robot. Verified the immune sibling: button.py:169 appends a trailing literal segment ('_run_profile_'), confirming the guard is absent rather than unnecessary. SEVERITY DOWNGRADED to HIGH: it does destroy durable registry data (custom entity_ids, names, icons, area assignments) silently, but the trigger requires a specific naming coincidence — a multi-vacuum install where one entity_id is another's plus a separator and a matching map id — and the entities themselves are re-created on the next reload, so the loss is the customizations rather than the room configuration. HIGH rather than CRITICAL.

title: async_preload_room_history_cache replaces the whole per-vacuum room_history subtree AFTER an executor await, silently discarding any room-history written during that await
observed_behavior:
`async_preload_room_history_cache` (manager.py:2258) awaits `hass.async_add_executor_job(self._load_room_history_cache_sync, vacuum_key)` — a full disk read of the vacuum's completed-job files via `LearningHistoryStore.load_all_completed_jobs` — and then, at line 2275, does a WHOLESALE assignment:

    self.data.setdefault("room_history", {})[vacuum_key] = vacuum_history

This is a replace, not a merge. The executor result was snapshotted from disk before the await resolved, so any write to `self.data["room_history"][vacuum_key]` that landed on the loop DURING the await is destroyed.

A concrete writer exists on exactly that path: `async_finalize_learning_job` (manager.py:4618) awaits `learning.async_finalize_completed_job(...)` and then calls `_ingest_completed_job_into_room_history(vacuum_entity_id=..., completed_job=...)` with `_history_root` defaulting to None, which manager.py:2380-2385 resolves to `self.data.setdefault("room_history", {})` and mutates in place (`last_cleaned_at`, `last_vacuumed_at`, `last_mopped_at` per room), then fires `_notify_room_history_updated`. This is a gap ACROSS an await, not a synchronous-block claim: both coroutines suspend at real I/O.

After the clobber, line 2276 adds the vacuum to `_room_history_cache_ready`, so `_ensure_room_history_cache` (manager.py:2195-2204) will never schedule another rebuild, and lines 2277-2284 then fan out `_notify_room_history_updated` — actively pushing the stale values to the sensors. The next `manager.async_save()` persists the regressed subtree.
user_impact: A run that finishes while a room-history rebuild is in flight has its per-room "last cleaned / last vacuumed / last mopped" timestamps reverted to the previous run's values on every room-history sensor, and the wrong values are then persisted. Nothing is logged. The condition is not self-correcting within the process — the ready-flag suppresses further rebuilds — so it persists until an HA restart or an explicit invalidation (save_managed_rooms / reconcile_room / apply_room_profile all `discard` the ready flag). The rebuild is scheduled at every platform setup (sensor/__init__.py:227) and after each of those invalidations, so the window overlaps the single most common event in the integration: a run ending.
guards_checked: (1) manager.py:2264-2269 — the `_room_history_cache_ready` / `_room_history_cache_loading` checks plus `.add()` are all synchronous before the first await, so they correctly prevent a DOUBLE preload; they do not and cannot guard a concurrent non-preload writer. (2) The `finally` at manager.py:2285-2286 only discards the loading flag; it performs no re-read or merge. (3) `_ingest_completed_job_into_room_history` manager.py:2380-2383 — the `_history_root` parameter exists precisely so the executor path writes to a temp dict, confirming the authors knew the loop copy was live; the loop-side call at manager.py:4686 deliberately omits it. (4) `_load_room_history_cache_sync` manager.py:2206-2256 — builds into `temp_root` and returns it; it never merges against `self.data`, so the merge would have to happen at line 2275 and does not. (5) rooms/room_crud.py:201 and :268 `_room_history_cache_ready.discard(...)` — invalidation only; an in-flight preload is not cancelled or re-run, so an invalidation raised mid-flight is also swallowed by the same assignment.

title: The manager's four own callback registries append without a duplicate check while the theme registry they delegate to dedupes, and unregister removes only one copy
observed_behavior:
Five register/unregister pairs sit next to each other at manager.py:577-619 and are not written to the same contract. The four manager-owned ones (`register_room_update_callback`, `register_run_profile_update_callback`, `register_room_history_update_callback`, `register_room_rule_status_update_callback`) do a bare `self._<x>_callbacks.append(callback)`. The fifth, `register_theme_update_callback` (manager.py:613), delegates to `ThemeManager.register_update_callback` (themes/manager.py:75-78) which guards with `if callback not in self._update_callbacks`.

The unregister side is symmetric-looking but is not idempotent against a double register: `if callback in list: list.remove(callback)` removes exactly ONE occurrence, so N registrations require N unregistrations. A subscriber registered twice therefore stays subscribed after its single `entry.async_on_unload` lambda runs, and fires twice on every notification in the meantime — doing its full stale-sweep and add-entities pass twice per event.

No caller registers twice today, which is why this is latent rather than active: button.py:108, number.py:127, switch.py:97 and sensor/__init__.py:346-380 each register exactly once per platform setup, and listeners/path_blockers.py:98 is preceded by an unconditional `remove(hass)` at line 61 that unregisters first. But the facade advertises five identically-shaped entry points with two different contracts, and the four unguarded ones are the ones whose subscribers perform destructive entity-registry sweeps (see CB-1).
user_impact: Latent today. If any future caller registers a room-update callback twice — or if the path_blockers `remove()`/`register()` pairing is ever broken so its `remove` no-ops — that subscriber survives config-entry unload and keeps firing against torn-down entities, and its stale-entity sweep runs twice per room change. The behavioural difference between the theme pair and the other four is invisible at the call site.

title: Three of the four fan-out subscribers call async_write_ha_state() unguarded while the fourth routes through a hass-is-None guard, so one bad entity aborts the rest of that subscriber's sync silently
observed_behavior:
sensor/__init__.py:62-76 defines `_request_entity_state_write(entity)`, which explicitly checks `hass = getattr(entity, "hass", None); if hass is None: return` before scheduling the write, and routes all seven of the sensor platform's callback-driven refreshes through it. The three sibling subscribers on the same fan-out do not: switch.py:89, number.py:119 and button.py:100 each call `existing.async_write_ha_state()` directly inside the `for uid, entity in desired.items()` loop.

`Entity.async_write_ha_state()` raises when `self.hass` is None (an entity handed to `async_add_entities` but whose add task has not yet run) or when the entity has already been removed from its platform. Because that call sits mid-loop, a single raise aborts the remainder of the subscriber's pass: the not-yet-processed entries in `desired` are never appended to `new_entities`, and the terminal `if new_entities: async_add_entities(new_entities)` never runs. The manager's fan-out (`_notify_rooms_updated`, manager.py:629-637) catches the exception per-subscriber, so later subscribers are unaffected — but the aborted subscriber's missing entities are reported only as one ERROR log line and are never retried.

The asymmetry is the finding: the sensor platform documents and applies the guard; the three siblings performing the identical operation on the identical notification do not.
user_impact: When it triggers, some of a map's room switches or number entities silently fail to appear after a room change, with only an "Room update callback failed for ... map ..." ERROR in the log and no user-facing signal. They appear on the next room update or after a reload. The trigger requires a second notification for the same vacuum/map before the previous `async_add_entities` task has drained (or a write against an already-removed entity), so it is narrow — but the guard that would make it impossible already exists one platform over.
guards_checked: (1) sensor/__init__.py:62-76 `_request_entity_state_write` — the guarded sibling, with a docstring stating why the funnel exists; used at lines 275, 288, 331, 344, 375, 424, 462. (3) manager.py:629-637 / 646-654 — the per-subscriber try/except in the fan-out, which isolates other subscribers but converts this into a silent partial failure rather than preventing it. (4) `_notify_rooms_updated` is only ever invoked from loop context (all call sites are sync manager/profile/room_crud methods), so `_request_entity_state_write`'s `call_soon_threadsafe` docstring claim about worker threads is not load-bearing — the `hass is None` check is the part that matters and is the part the siblings lack.

title: mop_active collapses "tank sensor unreadable" into a definite False, so the card confidently reports "Vacuuming" and hides the water-level control on Roborock
observed_behavior:
The snapshot builder declares mop_active as a TRI-STATE (`mop_active: bool | None`, comment at 3936-3940: "None when the adapter declares no tank sensor"), but the code only ever produces None when the ADAPTER omits the entity id:

```python
_mop_active_entity = (_adapter_cfg.get("entities", {}) or {}).get("mop_active")
mop_active: bool | None = None
if _mop_active_entity:
    _mop_state = self.hass.states.get(_mop_active_entity)
    mop_active = bool(_mop_state is not None and str(_mop_state.state).strip().lower() == "on")
```

The `_mop_state is not None` test sits INSIDE `bool(...)`, so "entity declared but not in the state machine" and "state is `unavailable`/`unknown`" both evaluate to a hard `False` — indistinguishable from "tank confirmed detached". Roborock declares `entities.mop_active = binary_sensor.<obj>_water_box_attached` unconditionally for every model (adapters/roborock/adapter.py:208), and that binary_sensor goes `unavailable` whenever the S6 is asleep/offline, and is absent entirely during the window where eufy_vacuum has set up but the Roborock integration has not.

This is the odd one out among its own siblings in the SAME builder: `setting_entities` (4046-4050), `scene_select` (4057-4062) and `_resolve_live_map_image_entity` (4370, 4383) all existence-check with `hass.states.get(...) is not None` and degrade to omitted/None. No error, no "unknown" state, no way for the user to tell it is a sensor dropout rather than a real reading. If the binary_sensor is disabled-by-default in the entity registry on some HA/Roborock versions, the wrong answer is permanent rather than transient.

title: get_dashboard_snapshot composes get_job_progress_snapshot TWICE, so job_progress and job_control in the same payload can describe different rooms — and every side effect in the progress composer fires twice per card poll

title: The snapshot has no read of the exactly-once finalize claim, so across the finalize await it reports a finished run as actively cleaning and offers Pause / Cancel on it
observed_behavior:
`LearningManager.async_finalize_completed_job` (learning/manager.py:690-741) writes `finalize_claimed_at` into the stored job SYNCHRONOUSLY, then awaits the finalize body — whose core is `await hass.async_add_executor_job(finalizer.finalize_from_inputs, ...)` (773), a disk write plus a full learning-stats rebuild. `status` stays `"started"` and `finalized` stays absent for that whole window; only `mark_active_job_finalized` (jobs/active_job.py:2034) flips them, and it runs AFTER the await returns.

The dashboard snapshot is a separate service the card polls on a timer, so it lands inside that window across a real await (not a synchronous-block claim). It reads only `status` and `finalized`:

```python
status = str(active_job.get("status", "idle")).strip().lower()
finalized = bool(active_job.get("finalized"))
can_pause = status == "started"
can_cancel = status in {"started", "paused"}
```

Nothing in `get_job_control_state` (3833-3895), `get_job_progress_snapshot`'s `terminal` (3335) or `live_queue.active` (3437) consults `finalize_claimed_at`. So the payload says the job is running, non-terminal, pausable and cancellable while the job subsystem has already claimed it as finished and is writing its completed record.
user_impact: For the duration of the finalize (a stats rebuild over a long history is easily seconds), the card shows "Cleaning <room>" with a live queue and enabled Pause / Cancel buttons for a run that is already over and being written to disk. Pressing Pause sends a real pause command to a robot that has already docked; pressing Cancel sends a stop/return_to_base to a docked robot, then reaches the finalize chokepoint, is refused with `reason: "finalize_in_flight"` (learning/manager.py:710-716), and `mark_active_job_finalized` is then called with that refusal as the finalize_result — so the user's Cancel is silently swallowed and the resulting `finalize_summary.status` is None.
guards_checked: (1) `mark_active_job_finalized` (jobs/active_job.py:2034-2035) sets status="completed"/finalized=True only after the await returns — it cannot cover the window. (2) The claim IS written before the first await (learning/manager.py:719) so it is atomic and readable — the snapshot simply never looks at it. (3) `get_job_control_state`'s `finalized` read at 3845 only feeds `can_clear`, not `can_pause`/`can_cancel`/`terminal`. (4) `_job_status_summary` (jobs/active_job.py:1548-1557) branches on status alone and returns "Cleaning <room>". (5) `async_pause_active_job` (jobs/active_job.py:2092) rejects only `status != "started"` — status IS "started" here, so it proceeds. (6) `_clear_orphaned_finalize_claims` (manager.py:484-508) only runs at startup and so does not bound the live window.

confirmations: Confirmed. learning/manager.py:696-719 writes finalize_claimed_at into the STORED job synchronously before the first await, then awaits _finalize_claimed whose core is `await self.hass.async_add_executor_job(finalize_from_inputs...)` (learning/manager.py:770-785) — a disk write plus stats rebuild. So the payload advertises a live, pausable, cancellable run for a job already claimed as finished, and a Cancel that reaches the chokepoint is refused with 'finalize_in_flight' (710-716). Real across-await window, narrow duration — MEDIUM.

title: zone_max invents Eufy's device limit (10) for any brand that declares none, while the dispatch gate enforces no cap at all when the key is absent
observed_behavior: The snapshot hardcodes an Eufy-shaped fallback into the brand-agnostic composer: `zone_max = int(_caps_cfg.get("zone_max", 10) or 10)`. The server-side enforcement asks the SAME question and answers it differently — `dispatch/manager.py:130-135` does `_zone_max = _zone_caps.get("zone_max")` and only raises `if _zone_max is not None`, i.e. an undeclared brand gets NO cap. The sibling `zone_bounds` block immediately below (4024-4034) gets this right: it emits only the keys the adapter actually declares and never substitutes a default. Note the same builder does the same thing for the tri-state it gets right elsewhere — `supports_water_control`/`supports_edge_mopping` (3977-3978) default True, which is Eufy's answer, not a neutral one.
user_impact: A future adapter that declares no `zone_max` gets a card that silently stops the zone draw at 10 boxes with no explanation, while the backend would happily have dispatched more — a limit the user is shown but that the device and the server do not have. Zero impact today: both shipped adapters declare `zone_max` explicitly (eufy 10 at adapters/eufy/adapter.py:807, roborock 5 at adapters/roborock/adapter.py:612).

title: get_start_status validates PHASE 0's room count as if it were the whole job — a stepped run whose first phase is a zone is refused with a false "invalid payload" error
observed_behavior: `_build_effective_start_plan` returns `payload_state = phases[0]` (planning/run_plan.py:1379) — phase 0 only, NOT the whole job. `get_start_status` then feeds that into the blocker builder as `payload_room_count=int(payload_state.get("room_count", 0))` (core/manager.py:2863), and `build_start_blocker_from_lifecycle` blocks on `payload_room_count <= 0` with reason `invalid_payload` (jobs/job_monitor.py:268-273). A zone phase legitimately carries `"room_count": 0, "payload": {}` (run_plan.py:873-879) because it dispatches saved-zone rects, not segments. So whenever phase 0 is a zone the run is refused. Two reachable ways to get a leading zone phase: (a) a saved run profile whose `steps` list opens with a zone — `normalize_run_profile_steps` (profiles/manager.py:751-809) applies NO ordering rule, it accepts a leading zone verbatim, and `start_run_profile` stashes those steps into `_pending_run_steps` which the plan builder materializes via `_build_steps_phases`; (b) an ordinary rooms+zone queue where the FIRST room group is entirely rule-blocked at start time — `_build_steps_phases` does `if not group_ids: continue` (run_plan.py:828-829), dropping the leading room_group and promoting the zone to phase 0. The leading-break strip that would have saved this only removes charge/wait: `_BREAKS = ("charge_wait", "wait")` (run_plan.py:883-885) deliberately excludes `zone`.
user_impact: A run profile like "clean the entryway zone, then the kitchen", or any rooms+zone queue whose first room happens to be blocked by a room rule that moment, refuses to start and reports "Room-clean payload is missing or invalid." The rooms and the zone are all perfectly runnable; the message points the user at a payload problem that does not exist, and there is no way to act on it from the card. Saved Zones (v1.6.0) ship on both brands, so this is live today.
guards_checked: Read every earlier return in get_start_status that could have caught this first and none do: the `active_job.status == "paused"` early return (2785), `onboarding["floor_types_complete"]` (2805), and the `all_selected_rooms_blocked` test (2834) which requires `included_room_count == 0` — with a leading zone the remaining rooms are still included, so it does not fire. `preflight["blocked"]` (2889) is not set for this case: the plan is valid, only phase 0 has no rooms. Verified `queue_count <= 0` (job_monitor.py:261) does not pre-empt it either — `queue_state["queue_room_ids"]` is built from `effective_rooms` and still lists the non-blocked rooms. Checked add_queue_zone's clamp (manager.py:1749 `after = max(1, min(...))`) and `_map_queue_breaks`'s `if after >= 1` filter (manager.py:1611) — those DO prevent a leading zone from the ad-hoc queue backing, which is why route (b) needs a blocked first group; route (a) bypasses them entirely. Checked tests/integration/test_zone_phase.py: every case ([ZN-1], [ZN-2]) places the zone BETWEEN room groups; a leading zone is untested.

confirmations: Confirmed and the block is unavoidable. planning/run_plan.py:1383 is `payload_state = phases[0]`; a zone phase is emitted with `"payload": {}, "room_count": 0` (run_plan.py:872-879); manager.py:2863 passes `payload_room_count=int(payload_state.get('room_count', 0))` into build_start_blocker_from_lifecycle, which at jobs/job_monitor.py:268-273 returns reason 'invalid_payload' / 'Room-clean payload is missing or invalid.' blocked=True. Both routes to a leading zone check out: normalize_run_profile_steps (profiles/manager.py:751-809) applies no ordering rule and appends a zone step verbatim wherever it appears, and _build_steps_phases does `if not group_ids: continue` (run_plan.py:828-829) so a fully rule-blocked first room group promotes the zone to phase 0. The leading-break strip is literally `_BREAKS = ('charge_wait','wait')` (run_plan.py:883-887) — zone is deliberately excluded. I checked every earlier return in get_start_status (paused 2785, onboarding 2805, all_selected_rooms_blocked 2834 which needs included_room_count==0) and none pre-empts it, and queue_count is non-zero because the remaining rooms are still queued.

CONFIRMED, reachable today. planning/run_plan.py:1379 sets payload_state = phases[0] (phase 0 only), and core/manager.py:2863 passes 'payload_room_count=int(payload_state.get("room_count", 0))' to build_start_blocker_from_lifecycle, which blocks with reason 'invalid_payload' / 'Room-clean payload is missing or invalid.' at jobs/job_monitor.py:268-273. A zone phase legitimately carries room_count 0 and payload {} (run_plan.py:872-879). Both routes verified: (a) ProfileManager.normalize_run_profile_steps (profiles/manager.py:750-808) read in full — it applies NO ordering rule at all and appends a leading {'type':'zone'} step verbatim, so a saved run profile can genuinely open with a zone; (b) _build_steps_phases does 'if not group_ids: continue' at run_plan.py:828-829, dropping a fully rule-blocked leading room_group and promoting the zone to phase 0. The leading-break strip cannot rescue either: _BREAKS is literally ('charge_wait','wait') at run_plan.py:883, deliberately excluding zone. Verified no earlier return pre-empts it: the all_selected_rooms_blocked test at manager.py:2834 needs included_room_count == 0, which is false when other rooms remain, and queue_count is built from effective_rooms so it is > 0. title: start_selected_rooms dispatches phase 0 with no phase_type branch, unlike its phase_runner sibling — and _build_steps_phases' docstring claims a guard that does not exist
observed_behavior: `jobs/phase_runner.py:996-1006` explicitly branches on the phase type before dispatching: `if str(_phase.get("phase_type")) == "zone"` it routes to `dispatch_zone_clean(zones=...)` and skips the global pre-calls, the per-room live settings, and the segment payload entirely. `start_selected_rooms` — which dispatches phase 0 of the very same phase list — has NO such branch: it unconditionally runs `_run_global_pre_calls` (5005), `_resolve_live_dispatch_payload` (5015), then `_dispatch_clean_payload(payload=wire_payload)` (5021). For a zone phase that payload is `{}`, and `_dispatch_clean_payload` (dispatch/manager.py:45-84) has no empty-payload guard at all — it would send `vacuum.send_command` with `command="room_clean"` / `app_segment_clean` and `params={}` or `[{}]`. Its own sibling `dispatch_zone_clean` DOES validate its target list (`if not zones: raise ValueError`, dispatch/manager.py:108). Compounding this, `_build_steps_phases`' docstring (run_plan.py:806-808) asserts "Leading/trailing/duplicate charge phases (nothing to bracket) are dropped so phase 0 is always a real clean the initial dispatch can send" — the code behind it only strips `_BREAKS = ("charge_wait", "wait")`, so the stated invariant is false for a zone.
user_impact: Latent today: the only thing stopping a segment-clean command with an empty room list from reaching the robot is the accidental `payload_room_count <= 0` block described in START-1, which is a side effect of the zone phase having no rooms rather than an intentional guard. If START-1 is fixed by relaxing that block (the obvious fix), the robot receives a room_clean/app_segment_clean with no segments — on Roborock a params list with no `segments` key, which the device may interpret as a full-house clean. The docstring reads as a guarantee and will lead whoever fixes START-1 to assume phase 0 is safe to dispatch.
guards_checked: Read _dispatch_clean_payload end to end (dispatch/manager.py:45-84) — no empty/None payload check, no phase_type awareness, it shapes and sends whatever it is handed. Read _resolve_live_dispatch_payload's delegation (manager.py:4841-4858) — it re-resolves slugs and cannot manufacture a guard. Confirmed the phase_runner zone branch is reached for phases 1+ only (phase_runner.py:987 comment: "the phase-0 pre-call fires in start_selected_rooms, phases 1+ fire here"), so phase 0 has no zone handling anywhere. Confirmed `_BREAKS` at run_plan.py:883 is the literal tuple ("charge_wait", "wait") and the two `while phases and phases[0/-1].get("phase_type") in _BREAKS` strips at 884-887 are the only leading/trailing filters.

confirmations: Confirmed: phase_runner.py:991-1006 explicitly branches `if str(_phase.get('phase_type')) == 'zone'` and routes to dispatch_zone_clean, while start_selected_rooms (manager.py:5005-5022) unconditionally runs _run_global_pre_calls, _resolve_live_dispatch_payload and _dispatch_clean_payload with `payload = payload_state.get('payload', {})`. _dispatch_clean_payload (dispatch/manager.py:45-84) read end to end — no empty/None payload check and no phase_type awareness, whereas its sibling dispatch_zone_clean does validate (`if not zones: raise ValueError`, :108). The docstring at run_plan.py:806-808 does claim phase 0 is always dispatchable. Severity corrected DOWN to LOW: this is unreachable today because start_selected_rooms returns early on start_status['blocked'] (manager.py:4943-4951) and START-1's invalid_payload always fires first. It is a real trap for whoever fixes START-1, but by the stated rubric an unreachable defect is latent.

Mechanism CONFIRMED. start_selected_rooms (manager.py:5005-5023) runs _run_global_pre_calls -> _resolve_live_dispatch_payload -> _dispatch_clean_payload unconditionally, with no phase_type branch, while the sibling that dispatches phases 1+ (phase_runner.py:996-1006) explicitly routes a zone phase to dispatch_zone_clean and skips the pre-calls, per-room settings and segment payload — and phase_runner.py's own comment at :987 confirms 'the phase-0 pre-call fires in start_selected_rooms, phases 1+ fire here', so phase 0 has no zone handling anywhere. Verified _dispatch_clean_payload (dispatch/manager.py:45-84) has no empty-payload guard while its sibling dispatch_zone_clean validates its target list at :108. The docstring claim at run_plan.py:806-808 ('phase 0 is always a real clean the initial dispatch can send') is FALSE for a zone — confirmed the code behind it strips only _BREAKS. SEVERITY DOWNGRADED to LOW: the finder's own analysis is right that this is unreachable today because START-1's payload_room_count<=0 block fires first, so nothing wrong reaches the wire. title: get_start_status can never surface a non-blocking lifecycle warning message — preflight's "ready" text shadows it, making dock-drying starts show warning=True with the message "Ready to start cleaning."
observed_behavior: The non-blocked return computes `"reason": water_reason or preflight.get("reason") or result["reason"]` and `"message": water_message or preflight.get("message") or result["message"]` (2941-2943). `preflight` ALWAYS carries a non-empty reason and message: the initializer sets `"reason": "ready", "message": "Ready to start cleaning."` (run_plan.py:951-952) and the final `preflight.update` re-sets both unconditionally (run_plan.py:1470-1471). So the `or result[...]` fallbacks are dead code — `result["reason"]`/`result["message"]` are unreachable on this branch. But `"warning"` at 2945 DOES include `result.get("warning", False)`. The one lifecycle state that returns `blocked=False, warning=True` is `dock_drying` (jobs/job_monitor.py:296-302), whose message is "Dock is currently drying pads, but start is allowed." That message is discarded while its warning flag survives. `start_selected_rooms` then copies the shadowed text straight into the started result: `"warning_message": start_status["message"] if start_status.get("warning") else None` (5143-5146).
user_impact: Every start attempt during the post-mop dock-drying window — which follows every mop run on both brands — returns a warning flag whose explanatory text says "Ready to start cleaning." and whose reason is "ready". The card raises a caution the user cannot interpret, and the actual reason (the dock is mid-dry) is never shown. The same shadowing silently discards any future non-blocking lifecycle state added to build_start_blocker_from_lifecycle.

title: save_managed_rooms facade wipes every stored room for a map when the discovery cache is empty — the precondition its sibling reconcile_room has
area: FACADE — the delegation surface of core/manager.py (~40 thin delegating methods compared against each other)
observed_behavior: The facade `save_managed_rooms` (core/manager.py:1434) is a bare `return self.room_map.save_managed_rooms(**kwargs)` — it adds no precondition. The delegate reads `data["discovery"][vac][map_id]["rooms"]`, filters to `str(room["map_id"]) == str(map_id)`, feeds the result to `build_managed_rooms(...)` and then unconditionally assigns `map_bucket["rooms"] = managed_rooms`. With an empty or missing discovery entry that assignment is `{}` — a total replacement, not a merge. Its SIBLING on the same class, `reconcile_room` (facade at core/manager.py:1430), guards exactly this case with an explicit early return (`if not discovered_rooms: ... "skipped": "no_discovery"`) whose comment reads 'Never migrate against an empty discovery — a stale/offline discovery would otherwise rebuild the map to nothing and wipe saved rooms.' The third entrance, `setup/workflow._import_active_map`, also guards (`if not rooms: return _result("blocked", ...)`). Two of three entrances into the same destructive write have the precondition; the facade does not, and both service entrances that reach it — `eufy_vacuum.save_managed_rooms` and `eufy_vacuum.setup_save_rooms` (the card's Setup > room editor Save button, the ONLY way to set a room's floor_type, since update_room_fields cannot write floor_type) — call `await manager.async_save()` afterwards, so the wipe is durable. Empirically confirmed by driving the real RoomMapManager: seeded 2 rooms with floor_type=carpet_high_pile and color=#ff0000, emptied the discovery entry, re-called save_managed_rooms -> room_count 0, stored rooms {}; the same sequence through reconcile_room returned skipped=no_discovery and kept both rooms. Deleting the discovery KEY entirely gives the same wipe.
user_impact: Every per-room setting for that map is permanently destroyed and persisted: floor types, per-room map fill colours, clean mode/fan/water/intensity/passes/edge-mopping overrides, room order, enabled state, is_dock_room / is_transition flags, the whole grants_access_to access graph and all per-room rules. The room switch/number/sensor entities for that map disappear. The user sees no error — the setup room editor they just saved from was populated from the SAVED rooms (setup_get_map_rooms -> get_managed_rooms), not from the discovery cache the save actually rebuilds from, so the UI showed the rooms right up to the moment they were deleted. Recovery requires re-doing the entire room configuration by hand.
guards_checked: Read and confirmed NOT rescuing: (a) `RoomMapManager.save_managed_rooms` has no empty/short-discovery test of any kind (rooms/room_crud.py:221-296); (b) `build_managed_rooms` (rooms/room_manager.py:26-118) iterates `discovered_rooms` and returns `{}` for an empty list — no 'refuse to shrink' rule; (c) `ensure_map_bucket` (maps/map_manager.py:10) only creates a default bucket, it does not protect existing rooms; (d) service handler `_handle_save_managed_rooms` (services/rooms.py:157-164) has no precondition and saves unconditionally; (e) `setup_save_rooms` (services/setup.py:208-226) has no precondition and calls `_record_setup_step` + `async_save()` regardless of room_count; (f) the setup 'protection' path I checked — `setup_delete_map`/`_delete_map` requires a confirmation_token, but nothing equivalent gates this write; (g) `_migrate_setup_progress` / the async_initialize backfill (core/manager.py:415-453) do not restore rooms. The only guard that DOES fire is in the siblings, not here.

confirmations: Confirmed, and the sibling asymmetry is exactly as described. RoomMapManager.save_managed_rooms (rooms/room_crud.py:221-296) reads data['discovery'][vac][map_id]['rooms'], filters by map_id, and does an unconditional `map_bucket['rooms'] = managed_rooms` at :261 with no empty/short-discovery test anywhere; build_managed_rooms (rooms/room_manager.py:26-58) iterates discovered_rooms and returns {} for an empty list. reconcile_room, on the same class, DOES guard — rooms/room_crud.py:142-154, with the comment 'Never migrate against an empty discovery — a stale/offline discovery would otherwise rebuild the map to nothing and wipe saved rooms' — and setup/workflow._import_active_map guards with `if not rooms: return _result('blocked', ...)` (workflow.py:193-202). The facade (manager.py:1434) adds nothing. Both service entrances persist the result: services/rooms.py:157-164 and services/setup.py:208-226 both `await manager.async_save()` unconditionally. Two of three entrances have the precondition and the destructive one does not — this is precisely the audit-#13 shape.

title: Dock-action gate is blind to app-started (external) runs — every dock action reports "Ready" and fires while the robot is mid-run at the dock
area: VAC — vacuum records, capabilities and dock actions
observed_behavior: `get_dock_action_status` (reached via the facade `EufyVacuumManager.get_dock_action_status`, core/manager.py:981) computes `active_job_running = active_job.get("status") in {"started", "paused"}` — a hand-copied literal set. The codebase already owns the answer to this exact question: `jobs/active_job.py:136` defines `_RUN_IN_FLIGHT_STATUSES = _DISPATCHED_IN_FLIGHT_STATUSES + ("external",)` and `run_is_in_flight()`, whose docstring says verbatim to ask it "when the question is about the ROBOT rather than the queue: is it out on the floor right now?". Dock actions are exactly that question, and the dock gate does not use it. An app-started run is captured into a slot with `status="external"` (jobs/active_job.py:1856), so `active_job_running` is False for the whole capture. The only remaining gate is `docked = vacuum_state == "docked"` — but the external lifecycle EXPLICITLY expects the robot to be docked mid-run: `learning/external_run.py:113` comments "the robot may be docking mid-run (mop prewash, recharge) and about to resume" and holds the slot open through a grace window of `EXTERNAL_FINALIZE_GRACE_S = 300` s re-armed up to `EXTERNAL_GRACE_MAX_RECHECKS = 8` times (~40 min) whenever task_status is one of the Eufy adapter's `external_mid_run_statuses` (adapters/eufy/adapter.py:355: "Returning to Wash", "Washing Mop", "Returning to Empty", "Emptying Dust", "Returning to Charge", "Charging (Resume)"). Throughout that window every action returns `allowed: true, reason: "ready"`, and `_async_run_dock_action` (line 300) presses the button. The gate's own message — "Finish, pause, or cancel the tracked job before using dock actions" — is the guard that is silently absent.
user_impact: The user starts a clean from the Eufy app. The robot returns to the dock to recharge ("Charging (Resume)") or wash the pad mid-run. The card's Base Station tab shows Wash Mop / Dry Mop / Empty Dust as Ready. Tapping Dry Mop starts a multi-hour dock dry cycle on a robot that is about to resume cleaning; tapping Empty Dust / Wash Mop injects an extra dock cycle. There is no error and no warning. Secondarily, the resulting dock_status transition is recorded by listeners/dock_events.py -> `record_dock_event`, bumping `mop_wash_count`, which is what `core/water_amendment.py` consumes as `mop_wash_count_at_finalization` — so the captured external run is finalized with wrong water actuals that then feed learning.
guards_checked: dock/manager.py:154 (the only job-state gate; literal set, no "external"); dock/manager.py:158 `docked` (satisfied — mid-run docking is the documented normal case); dock/manager.py:181-215 `build_action_status` (the remaining gates are `supported`, `action_entity is None`, per-action dock_status vocabulary and `_hard_service_states` — none of which reference run state); dock/manager.py:300-315 `_async_run_dock_action` (re-reads the same status, adds no run check); jobs/active_job.py:139-184 `dispatched_job_is_in_flight` / `run_is_in_flight` (the correct predicate exists and is used by core/error_tracker.py:997,1037 — never by dock); learning/external_run.py:75-200 (confirms the slot stays status="external" while docked and that the vacuum entity reads "docked"/"idle" in that window). The synchronous claim is atomic — the whole gate runs before the first await — so this is a missing predicate, not an interleaving race.

The correct predicate exists at jobs/active_job.py:136/160-186: _RUN_IN_FLIGHT_STATUSES = dispatched + ('external',) and run_is_in_flight, whose docstring says verbatim to ask it 'when the question is about the ROBOT rather than the queue: is it out on the floor right now'.
