title: refresh_vacuum_capabilities does NOT reproduce startup's detect_capabilities inputs — it silently drops the dock-button entity candidates, contradicting the comment above it
area: VAC — vacuum records, capabilities and dock actions
observed_behavior: The comment at core/manager.py:1120-1123 claims the refresh "uses the same entity candidates and model hints as startup", and 1129-1134 claims it "reproduces the SAME detect_capabilities inputs as startup". The hints half is true; the candidates half is not. Startup passes the adapter's `entity_candidates` dict (adapters/eufy/adapter.py:186-208), which contains the probe-only keys `wash_mop_button`, `dry_mop_button`, `empty_dust_button` (each with TWO firmware naming variants) alongside the sensor keys. The refresh instead rebuilds candidates from `_adapter_cfg.get("entities", {})` (line 1125-1128) — the RESOLVED entity map written at adapters/eufy/adapter.py:243-295, which contains no `*_button` keys at all (they were probe inputs, never stored). So on refresh `core/capabilities.py:252-254 _any_present("wash_mop_button"...)` reads an empty candidate list and returns False, and `supports_mop_wash = bool(_hints.get(...)) or False`. The refreshed payload is then written straight over the persisted snapshot at core/manager.py:1163 and returned. For x10/x8 the model hint is True so the loss is masked; for any Eufy whose model_family is not x10/x8 (an unrecognised model code resolves to "generic", including a new omni-dock model not yet in adapters/eufy/model_catalog.py) the hints are False and the flags flip True -> False. This is not only user-triggered: `get_vacuum_capabilities` self-heals on a model_family mismatch (core/manager.py:1205-1211), so a boot where `_get_registry_model_code` returns nothing and the family resolves to "generic" fires the refresh automatically.
user_impact: On an Eufy model outside the x10/x8 hint families that nevertheless exposes wash/dry/empty dock buttons, running the `eufy_vacuum.get_vacuum_capabilities` service (schema default refresh=True, and it async_save()s the result — services/adapter_config.py:195-204) or hitting the model_family self-heal permanently rewrites the stored snapshot with supports_mop_wash/mop_dry/empty_dust False. The Base Station dock controls then report "This vacuum does not support that dock action" for a device that demonstrably does, with no indication that a refresh caused it.
guards_checked: core/manager.py:1120-1163 (the whole input-assembly block — nothing re-supplies the *_button keys); core/manager.py:1129-1147 (the hints branch, which IS faithful and is what masks the bug on x10); core/capabilities.py:211-224 (`_cands.get(key, [])` returns [] for a missing key — a miss is indistinguishable from "absent", exactly the silent shape KNOWN_CAPABILITY_HINTS' docstring warns about for hints); adapters/eufy/adapter.py:186-208 vs 243-295 (candidates vs stored entities — the *_button keys exist only in the former); core/manager.py:1205-1211 (self-heal — a refresh TRIGGER, not a rescue); core/manager.py:1163 (unconditional overwrite of the stored snapshot, no merge, no compare).

confirmations: Confirmed, including the comment-vs-code gap the methodology warns about. manager.py:1120-1123 claims the refresh 'uses the same entity candidates and model hints as startup', but 1124-1128 rebuilds candidates from `_adapter_cfg.get('entities', {})`. I diffed the two blocks in adapters/eufy/adapter.py: entity_candidates (190-208) contains wash_mop_button/dry_mop_button/empty_dust_button with two firmware variants each, while the STORED entities dict (243-295) contains no *_button keys at all. core/capabilities.py:252-254 then reads `_cands.get(key, [])` -> [] and 292-294 computes supports_mop_wash/dry/empty_dust as `bool(_hints.get(...)) or <entity present>`. The hints branch is faithful — adapters/eufy/adapter.py:318 stores capability_hints, and 221-228 sets the mop-wash/dry hints True only for x10/x8 — so on any other family the flags flip True->False and manager.py:1163 overwrites the stored snapshot with no merge. The self-heal at 1205-1211 is a genuine automatic trigger, not just a manual one.

CONFIRMED, including the false comment. manager.py:1120-1123 claims the refresh 'uses the same entity candidates and model hints as startup' and 1129-1134 claims it 'reproduces the SAME detect_capabilities inputs as startup'. Verified only the hints half is true: line 1125-1128 rebuilds _entity_candidates from _adapter_cfg['entities'], and I diffed the two adapter dicts — adapters/eufy/adapter.py:204-206 puts wash_mop_button / dry_mop_button / empty_dust_button (two firmware variants each) in entity_candidates ONLY, while the stored 'entities' map built at :243-295 contains no *_button key at all. So on refresh core/capabilities.py:252-254 _any_present('wash_mop_button') reads an empty list and returns False, and supports_mop_wash collapses to the hint alone — which adapters/eufy/adapter.py:223 defines as model_family in {'x10','x8'}. Line 1163 then overwrites the persisted snapshot with no merge or compare. The x10/x8 hint masks it; a Eufy resolving to 'generic' that nevertheless exposes the dock buttons flips True -> False permanently, and the self-heal at 1205-1211 can fire the refresh without any user action. title: remove_vacuum_record drops data["room_history"][vacuum] but leaves the _room_history_cache_ready marker — three sibling call sites invalidate it, the one that DELETES the data does not
area: VAC — vacuum records, capabilities and dock actions
observed_behavior: `remove_vacuum_record` is storage-only by design and its docstring hands in-memory teardown to the caller. The caller `_teardown_vacuum` (__init__.py:592-631) unwinds the mapping tracker, battery manager, error tracker, adapter registry and sidebar panel — but nothing clears the MANAGER's own per-vacuum in-memory state: `self.runtime[vacuum_entity_id]`, `self._room_history_cache_ready` / `_room_history_cache_loading`, `self._map_state_source_cache[vacuum_entity_id]`, `self._map_frame_gate[vacuum_entity_id]`. The room-history one is a proven inconsistency rather than a judgement call: three other mutators that merely CHANGE stored rooms all call `self._manager._room_history_cache_ready.discard(vacuum_entity_id)` (rooms/room_crud.py:201, rooms/room_crud.py:268, profiles/manager.py:689) precisely so the cache re-ingests; the one that deletes `data["room_history"][vacuum]` outright does not. `_ensure_room_history_cache` (core/manager.py:2195-2204) returns immediately when the id is in `_room_history_cache_ready`, so the bucket is never rebuilt. This survives removal because a non-configured vacuum's removal does NOT reload the entry: `async_remove_config_entry_device` (__init__.py:715-723) only schedules `_schedule_clear_configured_vacuum` — which is what triggers a reload — when the removed vacuum equals CONF_VACUUM_ENTITY_ID, and the hook's own docstring states one entry can manage many vacuums.
user_impact: On a multi-vacuum config entry, a user who deletes vacuum B's device and then re-adds the same vacuum entity (import map / save rooms) sees an empty Room Cleaning History panel for it — no history rows, no error, no way to force a rebuild — until HA is restarted. `ensure_runtime` likewise hands back vacuum B's pre-removal VacuumRuntimeState (stale selected_map_id / selected_room_ids / active_map_id) instead of a fresh one.
guards_checked: core/manager.py:1035-1079 (the removal itself — top-level bucket scan plus theme/battery nested buckets; storage coverage is genuinely complete, the gap is in-memory); __init__.py:592-631 `_teardown_vacuum` (the four in-memory teardowns it does perform — none touch the manager's caches); __init__.py:715-723 (the reload is conditional on the removed vacuum being the configured one); core/manager.py:2195-2204 `_ensure_room_history_cache` (the early return that makes the stale marker permanent); core/manager.py:2258-2280 `async_preload_room_history_cache` (guarded by the same `ready` set, so it will not re-run either); rooms/room_crud.py:201,268 and profiles/manager.py:689 (the siblings that do discard).

confirmations: Confirmed. remove_vacuum_record (manager.py:1035-1078) pops data['room_history'][vac] via the top-level scan but touches no manager in-memory state, and _teardown_vacuum (__init__.py:592-631) unwinds the mapping tracker, battery manager, error tracker, adapter registry and panel — never _room_history_cache_ready / _room_history_cache_loading / runtime / _map_state_source_cache / _map_frame_gate. The asymmetry is verified: rooms/room_crud.py:270 (inside save_managed_rooms), rooms/room_crud.py:201 and profiles/manager.py:689 all call `_room_history_cache_ready.discard(...)` for far less destructive changes. _ensure_room_history_cache (2195-2204) and async_preload_room_history_cache (2264-2266) both early-return on the ready flag, so the empty bucket is never rebuilt, and the removal path does not reload the entry unless the removed vacuum is the configured one (__init__.py:715-723). Multi-vacuum + delete + re-add in the same HA run is genuinely narrow — MEDIUM fits.

CONFIRMED as a proven inconsistency rather than a judgement call. remove_vacuum_record (manager.py:1035-1078) pops data['room_history'][vacuum] but never touches _room_history_cache_ready, while three sibling mutators that merely CHANGE stored rooms all discard it (rooms/room_crud.py:201, rooms/room_crud.py:268, profiles/manager.py:689). _teardown_vacuum (__init__.py:576-631) was read in full: it unwinds the mapping tracker, battery manager, error tracker, adapter registry and sidebar panel, and touches none of the manager's own per-vacuum caches (_room_history_cache_ready / _room_history_cache_loading / self.runtime / _map_state_source_cache / _map_frame_gate). _ensure_room_history_cache (2198-2199) early-returns on the stale marker so the bucket is never rebuilt, and async_preload_room_history_cache is gated by the same set. Confirmed this survives removal because async_remove_config_entry_device (__init__.py:713-722) only schedules the reload-triggering _schedule_clear_configured_vacuum when the removed vacuum equals CONF_VACUUM_ENTITY_ID. MEDIUM holds: on a multi-vacuum entry, delete-then-re-add leaves an empty Room Cleaning History and a stale VacuumRuntimeState with no error and no recovery short of a restart.

title: get_managed_vacuums reads data["capabilities"] raw and reports supports_* as None when no snapshot exists, unlike its sibling get_vacuum_capabilities which detects on demand
area: VAC — vacuum records, capabilities and dock actions
observed_behavior: `get_vacuum_capabilities` (line 1166) guarantees a snapshot — `if refresh or stored is None: return self.refresh_vacuum_capabilities(...)` — so every other reader in the integration is handed real booleans even on a cold record. `get_managed_vacuums` (line 1080) instead does `capabilities = self.data.get("capabilities", {}).get(vacuum_entity_id, {})` and emits `capabilities.get("supports_rooms")` etc., which is `None` for a vacuum that has an `ensure_vacuum_record` entry but has never had capabilities detected (e.g. a record created by `rooms/room_crud.py:48` or `__init__.py:252` before any capability read). Same facade, same question, two different answers — and the None is a third value the boolean-shaped field is not documented to carry.
user_impact: Latent today: the only consumer, setup/status.py:171, reads just `vacuum_entity_id` from the returned items. Any future consumer of the four supports_* fields (or a diagnostics dump) would read `null` and treat it as "unsupported" rather than "not yet detected".
guards_checked: core/manager.py:1080-1102 (no ensure/detect call, no default for the four flags); core/manager.py:1166-1218 (the sibling that does guarantee a snapshot — including the documented refresh=False detection path, which I verified behaves as its docstring claims); setup/status.py:171-200 (the sole caller — consumes only vacuum_entity_id, which is why this is latent).

confirmations: Confirmed by reading both siblings. get_managed_vacuums (manager.py:1080-1102) does `capabilities = self.data.get('capabilities', {}).get(vacuum_entity_id, {})` and emits capabilities.get('supports_rooms') etc. with no default, yielding None on a record that has never been detected; get_vacuum_capabilities (1166-1218) guarantees a snapshot via `if refresh or stored is None: return self.refresh_vacuum_capabilities(...)`. Verified the sole consumer setup/status.py:171 reads only vacuum_entity_id, so it is latent — LOW is correct.

CONFIRMED. get_managed_vacuums (manager.py:1080-1102) reads self.data['capabilities'].get(vacuum_entity_id, {}) raw and emits capabilities.get('supports_rooms') etc., which is None for a record created by ensure_vacuum_record before any detection — whereas the sibling get_vacuum_capabilities (1166-1217) guarantees a snapshot via 'if refresh or stored is None: return self.refresh_vacuum_capabilities(...)'. title: Dock-phase re-arm runs INSIDE async_initialize (eager task start), so its brand lookups resolve before register_brand_adapter — Roborock gets Eufy phase timing and a battery read with no declared battery entity
observed_behavior: The re-arm loop (473-480) is the last real statement of async_initialize and reaches hass.async_create_task(coro) at jobs/phase_runner.py:98. manifest.json requires HA >= 2025.6.0 (hacs.json), and since HA 2024.6 hass.async_create_task defaults to eager_start=True — the coroutine runs SYNCHRONOUSLY up to its first true suspension, i.e. inside async_initialize, not at the next loop yield. _run_charge_wait_phase awaits _run_charge_wait_phase_impl inline (phase_runner.py:604); that body is synchronous through get_active_job, the _still_ours check and get_battery_level, so on the common restart case 'battery already >= target' it goes straight into 'await self.maybe_advance_phase(...)' (phase_runner.py:645), which is also synchronous through _capture_finishing_phase_timing (a def, not async) and advance_active_job_phase, and then spawns _run_advanced_phase with another eager async_create_task (:192). _run_advanced_phase's FIRST statement is 'pt = self._manager._phase_timing(vacuum_entity_id)' (:515) and only then does it await asyncio.sleep. Meanwhile async_setup_entry has not returned from 'await manager.async_initialize()' (__init__.py:236), so load_stored_adapter_configs (:295) and register_brand_adapter (:307-314) have not run and hass.data[DOMAIN][DATA_RUNTIME] (:316) / DATA_LEARNING (:318) are unset. core/manager.py:4904 therefore resolves _get_adapter_config(...) to None and pt falls back to the in-core _PHASE_* defaults; the Roborock adapter declares confirm_seconds: 15 precisely because the core default of 45 is wrong for the S6 (adapters/roborock/adapter.py:314-326). Same window: core/charging.py:50 loses the adapter's declared entities.battery and falls back to the vacuum entity's battery_level attribute (0 when absent). Note the ordering is safe WITHOUT eager start — there is no await between __init__.py:236 and :314 — so this defect exists only because the task starts eagerly.
user_impact: After an HA restart during a charge_wait/wait phase, the first phase of the resumed run is driven with the wrong brand's watchdog timing for its entire duration (pt is read once). On Roborock the phase needs 45s of sustained cleaning-of-target to confirm instead of the declared 15s, so a normal short room never confirms inside the 90s verify window: the same room is re-dispatched up to max_attempts=3 times and the run can be left stalled ('recoverable via Cancel Run') even though the robot cleaned it. The adapter-less battery read can also report 0 and send the robot back to the dock for a charge it does not need.
guards_checked: Traced every call between the re-arm and the adapter lookup for a suspension point — _still_ours, get_battery_level, _capture_finishing_phase_timing and advance_active_job_phase are all synchronous; _spawn_dock_poller's _dock_poller_active guard (phase_runner.py:85-88) prevents a double spawn but not early execution; _phase_timing (4896-4913) has no 'adapter not registered yet' branch, its try/except only covers int() coercion of declared values; get_adapter_config returning None is handled as 'brand declared nothing' rather than 'brand not loaded yet'; there is no await in async_setup_entry between line 236 and line 314 that would otherwise let the task run at a safe point.

confirmations: The MECHANISM is confirmed, the claimed impact is not. Verified in the installed HA (2026.5.3): `HomeAssistant.async_create_task(target, name=None, eager_start=True)` — eager by default, so _spawn_dock_poller (phase_runner.py:98) starts the coroutine inside async_initialize. Verified there is NO await in __init__.py between `await manager.async_initialize()` (236) and register_brand_adapter (307-314), so _get_adapter_config returns None during that window; _phase_timing (manager.py:4889-4913) has no not-yet-registered branch and silently falls back to the in-core _PHASE_* defaults, and core/charging.py:50 loses entities.battery. So an eagerly-started poller genuinely resolves brand config before the brand exists. Severity corrected DOWN to LOW: the specific harm chain is self-defeating. Reaching _run_advanced_phase's `pt = _phase_timing(...)` requires the `get_battery_level(...) >= target` shortcut (phase_runner.py:645) — but with the adapter absent that read falls back to the vacuum entity's deprecated battery_level attribute and, per the finder's own second claim, typically yields 0, which takes the OTHER branch. I also read _run_wait_phase_impl (748-830): it suspends on `return_to_base` before any advance, so the second dock-phase type cannot reach the early pt read at all. What is actually reachable is a redundant return_to_base issued during setup and one 30s poll before the adapter is live — latent, not a run-length mistiming.
killed_by: The eager-start observation is CORRECT — hacs.json pins HA >= 2025.6.0, hass.async_create_task defaults to eager_start=True, and I confirmed there is NO await in async_setup_entry between 'await manager.async_initialize()' (__init__.py:236) and register_brand_adapter (:307-314), so a task spawned from the re-arm loop does begin executing before the adapter exists. But BOTH claimed wrong outcomes are refuted by the code. (1) Phase timing: _run_advanced_phase's stale 'pt' is only used for settle_seconds, dock_settle_seconds and max_attempts — and adapters/roborock/adapter.py:314-326 declares settle 10 / dock_settle 45 / verify 90 / poll 5 / max_attempts 3, byte-identical to the core defaults at core/manager.py:74-99. The ONLY divergent key is confirm_seconds (15 vs 45), and _await_phase_started RE-READS its own 'pt = self._manager._phase_timing(vacuum_entity_id)' at phase_runner.py:889 — which runs after 'await asyncio.sleep(settle)', by which time async_setup_entry has completed and the adapter IS registered. So confirm_seconds is never taken from the stale read; there is no divergence on either shipped brand. The claimed stall is doubly refuted: _await_phase_started's terminal branch (phase_runner.py:960-965) returns 'cleaning_in_target > 0', a weak-confirm that explicitly treats a room finishing under confirm_seconds as confirmed rather than a no-show, so no re-dispatch and no stall. (2) Battery: with no adapter, get_battery_level (core/charging.py:50-63) falls back to the vacuum attribute or 0; target defaults to 100 (_safe_int(phase.get('target_battery_percent'), 100)), so a 0 read FAILS the '>= target' test and simply enters the poll loop, which re-reads correctly 30s later with the adapter registered. The interim return_to_base is a documented no-op on an already-docked robot ('a no-op if it is already docked + charging', phase_runner.py:669). No concrete triggering case produces the stated wrong outcome; the residual is a latent future-brand concern only.

title: The device is commanded before the job exists in memory at all — the await inside _dispatch_clean_payload opens a window where the robot is cleaning with no dispatched job on any map, which is exactly the condition the external-run capture treats as an app-started run
observed_behavior: Ordering in start_selected_rooms is: `_run_global_pre_calls` (5005) -> `_resolve_live_dispatch_payload` (5015) -> `_dispatch_clean_payload` (5021, DEVICE COMMANDED) -> `self.data["active_jobs"][vac][map] = active_job` (5060-5062) -> executor round-trip for the learning snapshot (5121) -> caller's `async_save()`. Confirming audit #13's WIRE-1: the record is written after the command and persisted only by the caller. The EXTENSION is that this is not only a crash window. `_dispatch_clean_payload` ends in `await hass.services.async_call(domain, name, data, blocking=True)` (dispatch/manager.py:84), so the event loop yields with the robot already commanded and NO active job on ANY map. `learning/external_run.py:75-96` documents its precondition as "Internal starts are blocked while a run is in progress, so a vacuum that is cleaning with NO dispatched job (status started/paused on any map) is an external run" and opens a `status="external"` capture slot when it sees `vacuum_state == "cleaning"` and `dispatched` is False. That precondition is violated for the duration of the blocking service call — if the provider flips the vacuum entity to `cleaning` inside its own handler, the lifecycle listener (listeners/lifecycle.py:117-125) runs during that await and opens an external slot for a run the integration itself just dispatched. Separately, `_run_global_pre_calls` at 5005 permanently pushes global fan/water settings to the device (Roborock) before any record exists; if the dispatch then raises, the service handler re-raises as HomeAssistantError (services/job_control.py:151-154) and `async_save()` is skipped, so the device setting change is neither recorded nor restored.
user_impact: Two failure shapes. (1) External-run cross-talk: a spurious `status="external"` capture opens for an internally dispatched run; it self-heals only because `start_external_capture` keys on `resolve_active_map_id` and line 5062 overwrites that same map key moments later — a coincidence, not a guard, and it breaks the moment the two map-id spellings diverge. (2) Roborock's global fan/water are changed on the device with no job record and no restore when the dispatch fails, leaving the vacuum silently on a different fan/water setting for the next app-started run.
guards_checked: Confirmed nothing between 5024 and 5062 awaits, so the record write is atomic once the dispatch returns — the exposure is strictly the await at dispatch/manager.py:84, not a synchronous interleave. Confirmed no asyncio.Lock or semaphore exists anywhere in the integration (grepped the whole custom_components tree) and that HA does not serialize concurrent calls to the same service. Confirmed there is no periodic whole-store autosave: every async_save/_async_save_logged call site is event-driven (services/, listeners/, jobs/active_job.py:1106/1319, jobs/phase_runner.py:856). Verified the success-path callers all DO save (services/job_control.py:156, learning/services.py:735, services/job_control.py:166 for the profile path, button.py:298) — the gap is the raise path, where the HomeAssistantError wrapper skips the save while `self.data["queue"]`, `self.data["payloads"]` and the popped `_pending_run_steps` entry have already been mutated in memory. Read _external_grace_finalize (external_run.py:183-190) and confirmed its `slot.get("status") != "external"` re-check is what limits the blast radius.

confirmations: The ordering is confirmed — manager.py:5021 dispatches to the device, manager.py:5060-5062 writes the active job, and dispatch/manager.py:84 ends in `await hass.services.async_call(..., blocking=True)`, so the loop genuinely yields with the robot commanded and no dispatched job on any map. learning/external_run.py:75-96 does document exactly that state as its external-run precondition, and listeners/lifecycle.py:117-125 calls maybe_handle_external_run from the state-change processing path. But severity is corrected DOWN to LOW because neither claimed harm survives scrutiny as a wrong outcome: the finder itself concedes the spurious external slot self-heals (line 5062 overwrites the same resolve_active_map_id key), and the 'global pre-calls not restored on dispatch failure' complaint is not failure-specific — _run_global_pre_calls never restores the device setting on the SUCCESS path either, so the raise path is not a divergence. What remains is a real but latent ordering hazard already characterized by audit #13's WIRE-1.
killed_by: The ordering observation is accurate — _dispatch_clean_payload at manager.py:5021 commands the device, the record lands at 5060-5062, and dispatch/manager.py:84 ends in an awaited blocking service call — but that is the already-known WIRE-1 lead, and neither NEW claimed outcome survives verification. (1) External cross-talk: this requires the vacuum entity to flip to 'cleaning' INSIDE the blocking service call. For both shipped brands the state change arrives asynchronously well afterwards (eufy-clean via an MQTT push; Roborock via the next coordinator poll), so I cannot construct a concrete trigger — and the finder itself concedes the case self-heals because line 5062 overwrites the very map key start_external_capture keys on (resolve_active_map_id). (2) Roborock pre-call not restored on a dispatch failure: the global fan/water is left changed on the SUCCESS path too, by design (that is what a global pre-call is), so the failure path is not a delta; and the failure is not silent — services/job_control.py:151-154 re-raises as HomeAssistantError, which HA surfaces to the user. title: Panels registered outside async_setup_entry are never tracked, so unload can't remove them and setup silently re-adds the "no vacuum configured" fallback panel
observed_behavior: async_setup_entry tracks panels ONLY by what its own loop registers: `panel_url = await async_register_vacuum_panel(...)` / `if panel_url: registered_panels.append(panel_url)` (415-421), stored at 450 as hass.data[DOMAIN][f"_panels_{entry.entry_id}"], and async_unload_entry (471-478) removes exactly that list. `async_register_vacuum_panel` (panels.py:80-89) returns None when the url is already registered — HA's frontend.async_register_built_in_panel raises ValueError on a duplicate (verified in installed HA 2026.5, frontend/__init__.py:387-388) and panels.py swallows it at DEBUG. A grep proves nothing else ever appends to `_panels_<entry_id>`, yet setup/workflow.py:106 (add_vacuum, reached from the panel's own onboarding service) registers a per-vacuum panel outside setup. services/setup.py:161-167 then schedules a config-entry reload immediately after a successful add, so the bad interleaving is automatic, not hypothetical: (1) add_vacuum registers `eufy-vacuum-<obj>` untracked; (2) the auto-reload's unload pops the tracked list — which holds only the fallback `eufy-vacuum` — and leaves `eufy-vacuum-<obj>` registered in hass.data[DATA_PANELS]; (3) the new setup's loop hits ValueError for that vacuum, gets None, so `registered_panels` stays empty and the vacuum's panel remains untracked forever; (4) because `registered_panels` is empty the `if not registered_panels:` branch (428) fires and re-registers the fallback setup-placeholder panel. The state is self-perpetuating across every subsequent reload because step 3 repeats; only a full HA restart (which clears the in-memory panel dict) resets it. Note also that the re-used registration keeps the OLD `js_url` mtime cache-buster from _frontend_url.py, so the documented "a config entry reload re-registers the panel so browsers pick up a new bundle" contract silently does not hold for these vacuums.
user_impact: Right after onboarding a vacuum through the panel (the documented primary path — the config flow's vacuum field is optional and the default notes text tells the user to add the vacuum from the sidebar panel), the sidebar shows a duplicate "Vacuum Agent" entry that renders the "no vacuum configured, go to Settings -> Configure" placeholder, and it comes back on every reload. The real vacuum panel is never removed when the integration is unloaded, disabled or deleted, so it lingers in the sidebar pointing at a dead backend until HA is restarted. Every second and later vacuum is affected unconditionally, since the config entry can carry only one vacuum_entity_id and all others must be added through add_vacuum. No error is shown — the duplicate-registration ValueError is logged at DEBUG.
guards_checked: panels.py:79-89 (ValueError caught, returns None — the only signal, and the caller treats None as "nothing to track"); the `if panel_url:` guard at 420 (it is what drops the url); the fallback-panel try/except ValueError at 447-448 (catches its own duplicate, does not repair the list); _remove_panel_for_vacuum (562-573) and _teardown_vacuum (624) — they do remove an untracked panel, but only on device deletion, not on unload; grep for `_panels_` across the repo — only __init__.py touches it, so setup/workflow.py:106 and services/setup.py:307 (rename, replace=True) never register their urls; services/setup.py:161-167 confirms the reload that triggers the interleaving; tests/integration/test_init_setup.py:66-70 patches panel_custom.async_register_panel with an AsyncMock that never raises ValueError, so no test covers this path.

confirmations: CONFIRMED from source. Verified each link: (1) HA frontend/__init__.py async_register_built_in_panel raises ValueError("Overwriting panel ...") when frontend_url_path is already in hass.data[DATA_PANELS] and update=False; panel_custom.async_register_panel calls it WITHOUT update=, so the default False applies. (2) panels.py:89-91 catches that ValueError and returns None. (3) __init__.py:420 `if panel_url:` drops the None, so nothing is appended. (4) grep -rn '_panels_' across the package returns exactly 4 hits, all in __init__.py (450 write, 471 pop, 569/572 the _remove_panel_for_vacuum scan) — setup/workflow.py:104-110 (add_vacuum) registers a per-vacuum panel and appends to nothing. (5) services/setup.py setup_add_vacuum does `hass.async_create_task(hass.config_entries.async_reload(entries[0].entry_id))` on a success result, so the reload is automatic, not hypothetical. (6) I walked the single-vacuum steady state: unload pops ['eufy-vacuum'] (the fallback, the only tracked url) and removes it; the untracked 'eufy-vacuum-<obj>' survives in DATA_PANELS; the new setup's loop gets None for it, so registered_panels==[] and the `if not registered_panels:` branch at 428 re-registers the fallback placeholder. This repeats on every reload — self-perpetuating until an HA restart clears the in-memory panel dict. Confirmed the test blind spot too: tests/integration/test_init_setup.py _patch_frontend() patches homeassistant.components.panel_custom.async_register_panel with an AsyncMock, so the duplicate-url ValueError never fires under test. Minor overreach that does not change the verdict: services/setup.py:307 (setup_set_panel_title) uses replace=True on the SAME url, which is already in the tracked list, so that call site is harmless — workflow.py:106 is the only untracked registrar.

MECHANISM VERIFIED, ONE SUB-CLAIM OVER-STATED, SEVERITY OVER-RATED.

Verified from source: __init__.py:412-421 builds `registered_panels` only from what its own loop registers; :450 stores it as `_panels_<entry_id>`; async_unload_entry:471 pops exactly that list. panels.py:89-91 swallows ValueError and returns None. HA 2026.5.3 confirmed: frontend/__init__.py:386-387 `if not update and panel.frontend_url_path in panels: raise ValueError(...)`, and panel_custom/__init__.py:123-131 calls async_register_built_in_panel WITHOUT `update=`, so it defaults False -> duplicate url raises. setup/workflow.py:105-110 registers a per-vacuum panel and appends nowhere; services/setup.py:161-167 schedules `hass.async_create_task(hass.config_entries.async_reload(...))` right after a successful add. grep confirms only __init__.py ever touches `_panels_`. Test claim confirmed: tests/integration/test_init_setup.py:65-70 patches panel_custom.async_register_panel with AsyncMock (never raises), and grep for `_panels_` across tests/ returns nothing.

CONCRETE REPRODUCER (I re-derived it and it only works from a BLANK install): install with the vacuum picker left blank (config_flow.py:62 makes it Optional and the default notes string at :64-67 literally instructs the user to add it from the sidebar panel) -> get_known_vacuum_ids() empty -> `registered_panels == []` -> fallback 'eufy-vacuum' registered AND tracked. User adds the vacuum from that panel -> workflow.add_vacuum registers 'eufy-vacuum-<obj>' untracked -> services/setup.py auto-reload fires -> unload pops ['eufy-vacuum'] and removes only the fallback -> new setup registers 'eufy-vacuum-<obj>' -> already present -> ValueError -> None -> NOT appended -> `registered_panels` empty -> the `if not registered_panels:` branch at :428 re-registers the fallback placeholder. Steady state: TWO sidebar 'Vacuum Agent' entries, one rendering 'no vacuum configured'. Repeats on every reload; only a full HA restart clears hass.data[DATA_PANELS].

CORRECTION to the mechanism text: the claim 'every second and later vacuum is affected unconditionally' by the FALLBACK symptom is wrong. With vacuum A already tracked and B added via the panel, unload removes A, setup re-registers A successfully, `registered_panels` is NON-empty, and the fallback branch does not fire. For 2+ vacuums the only symptom is B's panel being permanently untracked (survives unload/disable/delete until restart) — which is exactly what A4-RELOAD-1 claims. The duplicate-fallback loop is specific to the all-vacuums-untracked case, i.e. the first vacuum added via the panel.

SEVERITY: not HIGH. Nothing durable is destroyed, the robot is unaffected, and an HA restart fully self-heals it. It is a persistent, unexplained sidebar-presentation defect on the documented onboarding path -> MEDIUM. (The `js_url` cache-buster sub-claim is also correct — the stale registration keeps its old `?v=` — but that is a cosmetic consequence, not independent severity.)

title: async_setup_entry has no failure unwind, and HA never calls async_unload_entry for an entry that failed setup — a mid-setup raise orphans every subsystem registered so far and the next reload builds a second live copy
observed_behavior: Setup registers roughly 20 long-lived things (see the inventory table) but attaches exactly ONE of them to the entry's unwind hook — `entry.async_on_unload(entry.add_update_listener(...))` at 265. There is no try/except or try/finally around the assembly, and only the per-vacuum loops (307-314, 327-333, 371-388) and the entity-registry cleanup (274-290) are individually guarded; `battery_manager.start()` (336), `error_tracker.start()` (344), the four `await async_register_*_services` calls (390-393) and the eight `*.register(hass)` calls (398-405) are unguarded. In installed HA 2026.5, an exception out of async_setup_entry is caught at config_entries.py:882-886, the state is set to SETUP_ERROR, and `_async_process_on_unload` runs only the entry.async_on_unload callbacks — our async_unload_entry is NOT called. Worse, a later reload also skips it: ConfigEntry.async_unload returns early at config_entries.py:1007-1010 whenever the state is not LOADED. So everything registered before the raise stays subscribed for the rest of the HA session, and the user's natural response (Reload) runs async_setup_entry again, producing a SECOND BatteryHealthManager, ErrorTracker, MappingTracker, manager and adapter coordinator while the first set's state listeners are still live. The first ErrorTracker's handlers write into the OLD manager's self.data and fire-and-forget `self._manager.async_save()` (core/error_tracker.py:1061-1070), which writes that stale blob over the store — the same clobber mechanism already verified as CRITICAL in audit #14, reached here by a different trigger. This is a cross-await gap, not a synchronous-block claim.
user_impact: After any setup failure (a corrupt/hand-edited storage block reaching an unguarded ensure_record, an ImportError in a lazily-imported listener module after an update, an exception in any service registration), the integration is left half-built with no cleanup, and reloading — the obvious user action, and what the options flow does automatically — duplicates every state listener and timer. The duplicated old subsystems keep writing an increasingly stale copy of the whole storage blob over the live one, so room/job/learning edits made after the reload silently disappear. Nothing surfaces this beyond the single "Error setting up entry" traceback from the original failure.
guards_checked: entry.async_on_unload at 265 — the only unwind hook, covers just the update listener; the per-vacuum try/except blocks at 307-314, 327-333, 371-388 and the registry-cleanup try/except at 274-290 — none of them wrap the registration steps themselves; the ConfigEntryNotReady at 237-240 — it is raised before anything but the coordinator exists, so the retry path itself is harmless and is NOT the concern; listeners/*.register() each call remove() first (verified in lifecycle.py:76, discovery.py:55, pause_timeout.py:52, pose_sampler.py:289, job_progress.py:55) so listener re-registration is idempotent — but BatteryHealthManager/ErrorTracker/MappingTracker/EufyVacuumManager are fresh INSTANCES whose per-instance idempotency guards (battery/manager.py:393, core/error_tracker.py:381) cannot see the previous instance's subscriptions; HA source verified at config_entries.py:882-886 and 1007-1010.

confirmations: CONFIRMED, including both HA claims which I read directly. config_entries.py: the broad `except SystemExit, Exception` around async_setup_entry logs 'Error setting up entry %s for %s' and the `finally:` runs only `await self._async_process_on_unload(hass)` — our async_unload_entry is never called. And ConfigEntry.async_unload early-returns True with `if self.state is not ConfigEntryState.LOADED:` after async_cancel_retry_setup, so a later user-triggered Reload also skips async_unload_entry. On our side I confirmed entry.async_on_unload appears EXACTLY ONCE in the whole entry setup (__init__.py:265, the update listener); battery_manager.start() (336), error_tracker.start() (344), the four service registrations (390-393), the eight listener register() calls (398-405) and async_forward_entry_setups (407) are all unguarded with no try/finally around the assembly. The stale-write consequence is real: core/error_tracker.py _persist_and_notify does `self._hass.loop.call_soon_threadsafe(self._hass.async_create_task, self._manager.async_save())` — an orphaned tracker holding the OLD manager writes that whole stale blob over the store, the audit #14 mechanism reached by a different trigger. Weakness I probed and am recording rather than refuting on: no concretely reachable raise is demonstrated (the two guarded hazards — manager init and ensure_vacuum_record — are both already wrapped), so the trigger is structural rather than proven. That is what keeps it MEDIUM and not higher; the ABSENCE of any unwind path is itself a genuine defect in an assembly script and is squarely inside this audit's failure-path scope, so I am not killing it as hypothetical.

STRUCTURAL MECHANISM FULLY VERIFIED AGAINST HA SOURCE; TRIGGER IS A FAULT CONDITION, NOT A USER ACTION.

Verified in HA 2026.5.3: config_entries.py:886-893 — a raise out of async_setup_entry is caught, and the `finally:` block runs only `await self._async_process_on_unload(hass)` (i.e. only entry.async_on_unload callbacks); our async_unload_entry is NOT called. config_entries.py:1007-1010 confirmed verbatim: `if self.state is not ConfigEntryState.LOADED: self.async_cancel_retry_setup(); self._async_set_state(hass, NOT_LOADED); return True` — so a subsequent Reload ALSO skips async_unload_entry. Both HA claims are exactly right.

Verified in-repo: __init__.py:265 is the ONLY entry.async_on_unload in the whole entry setup. battery_manager.start (336), error_tracker.start (344), the four service registrars (390-393) and the eight listener register() calls (398-405) are unguarded, with no try/finally around the assembly. The duplication consequence is real: core/error_tracker.py:218 holds `self._vacuum_unsubs` PER INSTANCE, and :382 `if vacuum_entity_id in self._vacuum_unsubs: return` is a per-instance guard a second instance cannot see. The clobber is real and I confirmed the exact line: core/error_tracker.py:1069-1071 `self._hass.loop.call_soon_threadsafe(self._hass.async_create_task, self._manager.async_save())` against the OLD manager, and core/manager.py:803-805 `async_save` = `await self.storage.async_save(self.data)` — an unconditional whole-blob write. Same clobber shape as audit #14, reached by a different door.

WHERE I DISAGREE: the proposed triggers are weaker than claimed. I checked each. 'Corrupt storage reaching an unguarded ensure_record' — manager.async_initialize is already wrapped in ConfigEntryNotReady (237-240) and load_stored_adapter_configs (adapters/config_loader.py:36-62) type-checks and try/excepts every row. 'ImportError in a lazily-imported listener module' — listeners/ and services/ are imported at MODULE top level (services/__init__.py:22-35), so an ImportError fails the integration import outright rather than mid-setup. The strongest surviving trigger is line 407 `async_forward_entry_setups` -> `integration.async_get_platforms(platforms)` (config_entries.py:2724-2727), which DOES propagate ImportError if a platform module fails to import (a partial/corrupt HACS deploy) — and by that point every subsystem is live. Note that platform-BODY exceptions do NOT reach it (entity_platform.py:518-525 swallows and returns False), so the window is narrower than implied.

MEDIUM is correct and I leave it: narrow, fault-only trigger, but the outcome when it fires is durable-store clobber.

title: Five learning services registered during setup are missing from async_unregister_learning_services, so they survive unload as ghost services
observed_behavior: async_setup_entry line 391 awaits async_register_learning_services, which registers 21 services (learning/services.py:735-815). async_unregister_learning_services (901-918), called from async_unload_entry line 490, removes only 16. An AST diff of async_register/async_remove call arguments in that file shows exactly five registered-but-never-removed: SERVICE_SET_LEARNING_PROCESSING, SERVICE_PROCESS_PENDING_RUNS, SERVICE_CONFIRM_EXTERNAL_RUN, SERVICE_GET_EXTERNAL_PENDING_RUNS, SERVICE_DISCARD_EXTERNAL_RUN. The unregister function is a hand-maintained flat list of async_remove calls with no shared tuple, unlike services/__init__.py (which walks each submodule's SERVICES tuple), mapping_services.py (ALL_MAPPING_SERVICES) and themes/services.py (inline loop) — all three of which I AST-verified as symmetric.
user_impact: After the integration is unloaded, disabled or deleted, those five eufy_vacuum.* services stay listed and callable in Developer Tools and in automations. Calling one raises an unhandled KeyError from `hass.data[DOMAIN]["runtime"]` (learning/services.py:252-254) instead of HA's clean "service not found", so an automation that touches process_pending_runs or confirm_external_run fails with a traceback rather than a comprehensible error. No data is lost — every one of the five handlers resolves the core manager before doing any work.
guards_checked: async_unload_entry lines 489-493 (the four unregister calls plus battery_rebaseline — no catch-all sweep of DOMAIN services); services/__init__.py:66-71 (walks SERVICES tuples — the pattern this file does not use); the five handlers at learning/services.py:300, 365 and their siblings — each calls _get_core_manager(hass) first, which is what keeps this LOW rather than a data-mutation path; _get_learning_manager (257-263) will lazily re-create hass.data[DOMAIN]["learning"] post-unload, but it is never reached first.

confirmations: CONFIRMED by my own independent AST pass over learning/services.py (I did not take the finder's count on trust): async_register_learning_services issues 21 hass.services.async_register calls; async_unregister_learning_services issues 16 async_remove calls. The set difference is exactly the five named: SERVICE_SET_LEARNING_PROCESSING (registered :773), SERVICE_PROCESS_PENDING_RUNS (:780), SERVICE_CONFIRM_EXTERNAL_RUN (:787), SERVICE_GET_EXTERNAL_PENDING_RUNS (:794), SERVICE_DISCARD_EXTERNAL_RUN (:801). Also confirmed the severity-limiting claim: _get_core_manager (learning/services.py:252-254) is `return hass.data[DOMAIN]['runtime']` — a bare subscript, so confirm/get_external_pending/discard raise KeyError before touching data, while handle_set_learning_processing (:455) and handle_process_pending_runs (:461) use hass.data.get(DOMAIN, {}).get(DATA_RUNTIME) and return {'error':'manager_unavailable'}. No data mutation is reachable post-unload, so LOW is the right call.

CONFIRMED BY MACHINE CHECK. I ran an independent AST diff over learning/services.py: async_register_learning_services registers 21 services, async_unregister_learning_services removes 16, MISSING = exactly {SERVICE_SET_LEARNING_PROCESSING, SERVICE_PROCESS_PENDING_RUNS, SERVICE_CONFIRM_EXTERNAL_RUN, SERVICE_GET_EXTERNAL_PENDING_RUNS, SERVICE_DISCARD_EXTERNAL_RUN}, EXTRA = {} — the finder's list is exact.

Handler behaviour verified line by line: _get_core_manager (learning/services.py:252-254) is `return hass.data[DOMAIN]['runtime']` — a bare subscript, no .get. handle_confirm_external_run (:270), handle_get_external_pending_runs (:301) and handle_discard_external_run (:366) each call it first, so post-unload they raise KeyError (on 'runtime', or on DOMAIN itself when __init__.py:545-546 popped the whole dict). handle_set_learning_processing (:455) and handle_process_pending_runs (:461) use `hass.data.get(DOMAIN, {}).get(DATA_RUNTIME)` and return {'error':'manager_unavailable'} — exactly as claimed. The asymmetry-vs-siblings claim also holds: services/__init__.py:66-71 walks each submodule's SERVICES tuple; learning/ has no such tuple and is hand-listed.

Trigger: disable or delete the integration, then call eufy_vacuum.confirm_external_run from Developer Tools or an automation -> raw KeyError traceback instead of 'service not found'. No data touched (every handler resolves the manager before doing work). LOW is the right call and the other two finders over-rated it.

title: Panels registered outside async_setup_entry are never tracked, so unload cannot remove them — and setup then re-adds the "no vacuum configured" fallback panel next to the working one
area: DOWN — teardown and symmetry (async_unload_entry / async_remove_entry / _teardown_vacuum / _remove_panel_for_vacuum / _schedule_clear_configured_vacuum / async_remove_config_entry_device)
observed_behavior: async_unload_entry (line 471) removes ONLY the panel urls recorded in hass.data[DOMAIN][f"_panels_{entry.entry_id}"], and that list is built exclusively inside async_setup_entry (lines 412-450). Two other call sites register per-vacuum panels and append to nothing: setup/workflow.py:106 (add_vacuum — the primary onboarding action, invoked from the card) and services/setup.py:307 (setup_set_panel_title, replace=True). panels.async_register_vacuum_panel swallows the duplicate-url ValueError and returns None (panels.py:89-91), and __init__.py:420 drops a None silently — so a panel that is already registered is never re-recorded either. Concrete sequence, all of it the documented onboarding path (the config flow's vacuum picker is optional; the entry's own default notes string says "Open the Vacuum Agent panel in the sidebar to add your vacuum"): (1) install with a blank CONF_VACUUM_ENTITY_ID -> get_known_vacuum_ids() is empty -> registered_panels == [] -> fallback panel "eufy-vacuum" registered and tracked; (2) user adds the vacuum from that panel -> workflow.add_vacuum registers "eufy-vacuum-<object_id>" and does not track it; (3) any reload (options save, HACS update, homeassistant.reload_config_entry) -> unload pops ["eufy-vacuum"] and removes only the fallback; the per-vacuum panel survives because it was never in the list; (4) setup re-runs, async_register_vacuum_panel hits the still-live duplicate, returns None, registered_panels stays EMPTY, so the `if not registered_panels:` branch at line 428 concludes "no managed vacuums yet" and re-registers the fallback setup-placeholder panel. Steady state after every reload until a full HA restart: a duplicate sidebar entry, one of which renders the "you haven't set up a vacuum yet" placeholder for an install that HAS a managed vacuum. Same untracked panel also survives disabling or deleting the integration entirely (frontend panels live in memory until restart), leaving a sidebar entry whose service calls no longer exist.
user_impact: After adding a vacuum through the panel (the advertised onboarding path), the sidebar shows two "Vacuum Agent" entries and one of them tells the user the integration is not set up yet — with no error or log warning above debug level. Disabling or removing the integration leaves a dead sidebar entry behind until Home Assistant is restarted.
guards_checked: panels.async_register_vacuum_panel — the `except ValueError: return None` at panels.py:89-91 is the swallow, not a rescue; __init__.py:420 `if panel_url:` — this is the drop, not a guard. __init__.py:447 `except ValueError` on the fallback registration only protects the fallback itself. _remove_panel_for_vacuum (line 562) DOES scan every `_panels_*` list, but it is only reached from _teardown_vacuum (device deletion), never from unload, and its scan cannot find a url that was never appended. hass.data pop at line 471 defaults to [] so no KeyError masks it. Checked tests/: grep for `_panels_` across the whole test tree returns nothing — no test covers the tracking list. Full HA restart does mask it (panels are re-registered into a fresh registry and tracked), which is why it reads as intermittent.

confirmations: CONFIRMED — same defect and same verified chain as A1-UP-1 (duplicate finding; the two finders reached it independently and the mechanisms agree). I re-checked the parts DOWN-1 states differently: __init__.py:471 pops with a [] default so no KeyError masks anything; _remove_panel_for_vacuum (562-573) does scan every _panels_* list, but it is reached only from _teardown_vacuum via async_remove_config_entry_device (device deletion), never from unload, and its scan cannot find a url that was never appended; a full HA restart does mask it because DATA_PANELS is in-memory. One inaccuracy that does not change the verdict: DOWN-1 names services/setup.py:307 (setup_set_panel_title) as a second untracked registrar — it uses replace=True on a url that is already in the tracked list, so it is not a leak site. workflow.py:106 alone is sufficient.

DUPLICATE of A1-UP-1 (same file, same line, same mechanism) — and this write-up states the reproducer MORE accurately: it correctly starts from a blank-vacuum install, which is the only ordering in which the `if not registered_panels:` fallback branch at __init__.py:428 actually fires. I re-derived and confirmed that sequence step by step; see my A1-UP-1 verdict for the full source verification (panels.py:89-91 swallow, HA frontend/__init__.py:386-387 ValueError, panel_custom passing no `update=`, setup/workflow.py:105-110 untracked registration, services/setup.py:161-167 auto-reload).

One correction: the claim that the untracked panel 'also survives disabling or deleting the integration entirely' is true, but async_remove_config_entry_device -> _teardown_vacuum -> _remove_panel_for_vacuum (__init__.py:562-573) DOES remove it by computed url on the device-deletion path — so deleting the DEVICE cleans it up; deleting/disabling the ENTRY does not. Worth keeping straight when fixing.

SEVERITY: not HIGH. Presentation-layer only, no durable data lost, no wrong robot action, fully cleared by an HA restart -> MEDIUM.

title: async_unregister_learning_services removes 16 of the 21 services async_register_learning_services registers — 5 survive unload and 3 raise a bare KeyError when called
area: DOWN — teardown and symmetry (async_unload_entry / async_remove_entry / _teardown_vacuum / _remove_panel_for_vacuum / _schedule_clear_configured_vacuum / async_remove_config_entry_device)
observed_behavior: AST-verified count: async_register_learning_services registers 21 services on LEARNING_DOMAIN (== DOMAIN, learning/services.py:39); async_unregister_learning_services (line 901) hand-lists 16 hass.services.async_remove calls. title: Unload stops the debug capture but never cancels its auto-stop timer, which then kills a later capture
area: AREA 4 — reload path and platform forwarding (RELOAD-)
observed_behavior: debug_capture.register_debug_services creates a closure-local ledger `autostop = {'cancel': None}` (debug_capture.py:483) and arms `autostop['cancel'] = async_call_later(hass, minutes * 60, _auto_stop)` when debug_capture_start is called with max_minutes (:510). The only cancel path is the closure-private _cancel_autostop (:485-488), called from the start and stop service handlers; register_debug_services returns SERVICE_NAMES only (:545), so the cancel handle is not reachable from outside. async_unload_entry:497-499 calls get_capture().stop() — which restores the logger but does not touch the pending timer — and nothing is registered with entry.async_on_unload. Because a reload runs register_debug_services again, the new closure gets a FRESH empty autostop dict, so the old handle is unreachable forever. _auto_stop calls get_capture().stop() on the process-wide singleton (debug_capture.py:401-409), which is shared across reloads.
user_impact: Reload the integration while a timed debug capture is armed (max_minutes), then start a new capture: the orphaned timer fires at the ORIGINAL deadline and silently stops the new capture, logging 'debug capture auto-stopped after N min' for an N the user never set on that capture. The user loses the diagnostic trace they were collecting, with no error.
guards_checked: async_unload_entry:496-499 — the comment there claims the stop() call makes reload safe ('so a reload doesn't inherit a propagate=False / DEBUG logger (idempotent)'); it addresses the logger state only, not the timer. DebugCapture.stop (debug_capture.py:249-...) is idempotent but has no reference to the timer. services/debug.py:26-32 registers via register_debug_services and exposes only SERVICES = SERVICE_NAMES, so services/__init__.py's unregister walk removes the four services but cannot cancel the timer. No entry.async_on_unload registration anywhere in debug_capture.py.

confirmations: CONFIRMED, and this one is unique to this finder — no sibling caught it. debug_capture.py:483 creates the closure-local `autostop: dict[str, Any] = {'cancel': None}`; the arm at :510 is `autostop['cancel'] = async_call_later(hass, minutes * 60, _auto_stop)`; the only cancel path is the closure-private _cancel_autostop (:485-488), invoked solely from the start and stop service handlers. register_debug_services returns SERVICE_NAMES (:545) — the handle is unreachable from outside. async_unload_entry:497-499 calls get_capture().stop(), and I verified get_capture (:404-409) is the PROCESS-WIDE singleton ('logging is process-global'), so the auto-stop closure acts on state shared across reloads. stop() restores the logger but holds no reference to the timer. Because a reload runs register_debug_services again with a fresh empty autostop dict, the old handle is permanently unreachable, and trap (b) applies: HA does not cancel a bare async_call_later on entry unload. The comment at __init__.py:496 claiming reload safety is exactly the kind of guard-by-assertion methodology rule 4 warns about — it addresses logger state only. Outcome (an orphaned timer silently stopping a later capture at a deadline the user never set for it) is correctly rated LOW.

VERIFIED IN FULL — this is the sharpest reproducer of the set.

debug_capture.py:483 `autostop: dict[str, Any] = {'cancel': None}` is closure-local to register_debug_services; :485-488 _cancel_autostop is closure-private; :510 `autostop['cancel'] = async_call_later(hass, minutes * 60, _auto_stop)`; :545 returns SERVICE_NAMES only, so the handle is unreachable from outside. __init__.py:497-499 calls `get_capture().stop()` and nothing else — and the comment there is, exactly as the finder says, a claim about LOGGER state ('so a reload doesn't inherit a propagate=False / DEBUG logger') that does not cover the timer. _CAPTURE is a module-global singleton (debug_capture.py:401-409), so the orphaned _auto_stop reaches across the reload into the NEW capture. On reload, register_debug_services runs again and builds a FRESH `{'cancel': None}`, so the new closure's _cancel_autostop finds nothing to cancel and the old handle is permanently unreachable.

Trigger: debug_capture_start with max_minutes -> reload the integration -> start a new capture -> at the ORIGINAL deadline the orphaned timer fires and silently stops the new capture, logging an auto-stop for an N the user never set on it. Diagnostic data lost, no error surfaced.

LOW is correct: narrow, developer-facing, no durable data destroyed. Good catch on ErrorTracker.stop cancelling its own async_call_later timers — the pattern exists in-repo and simply was not applied here.

title: Post-job water-amendment state listener and 180s timeout are never cancelled by unload
area: AREA 4 — reload path and platform forwarding (RELOAD-)
observed_behavior: register_post_job_water_amendment creates an async_track_state_change_event subscription on the dock_status entity (:243-245) and an async_call_later timeout (:246), both held only in closure-local lists cancelled by the closure-private _cancel_all (:113-125), which runs only from _commit. It is invoked from the job-finalization lifecycle handler — i.e. from work that async_setup_entry started — but nothing registers _cancel_all with entry.async_on_unload and async_unload_entry (__init__.py:465-548) never touches it. Its dedup ledger `hass.data[DOMAIN]['_water_amendment_jobs']` (:70-72) is also never popped, so the `if not domain_data: hass.data.pop(DOMAIN, None)` cleanup at __init__.py:545-546 can never fire once any job has finalized with a water amendment.
user_impact: For up to timeout_seconds (default 180s) after a job finalizes, an unloaded/removed integration still holds a live state subscription and a pending timer, and can still spawn a task that rewrites the job JSON file on disk (via hass.async_create_task at :222) after the user has disabled or deleted the integration. The written data is correct, so there is no wrong result — the defect is the uncancelled loop-lifetime work and the permanently retained hass.data[DOMAIN] dict.
guards_checked: async_unload_entry:480-546 — listeners/*.remove(), the four service-unregister awaits, mapping_tracker.unregister_all(), battery_manager.stop(), error_tracker.stop(), coordinator.shutdown(); none reach water_amendment. ErrorTracker.stop (core/error_tracker.py:336-352) DOES cancel its own async_call_later grace timers, showing the pattern exists elsewhere and was simply not applied here. The job_id dedup set (:73-75) prevents a duplicate registration across the reload but does not cancel the existing one.

confirmations: CONFIRMED — same defect as A2-DOWN-3(a), verified independently at source: closure-local unsub_listener/unsub_timeout (water_amendment.py:243-246), _cancel_all reachable only from _commit, sole registration path listeners/lifecycle.py:390, and no row for it anywhere in async_unload_entry (465-548). RELOAD-4 adds a corroborating detail I checked and confirmed: ErrorTracker.stop (core/error_tracker.py:336-352) DOES iterate self._grace_cancels and cancel its own async_call_later timers, so the teardown pattern exists in this codebase and was simply not applied to water_amendment — that strengthens the finding rather than weakening it. Also confirmed the job_id dedup set (:70-76) only dedupes within a job id and cancels nothing. LOW is correct: the amendment it writes is correct data, so the defect is the uncancelled loop-lifetime work plus the permanently retained hass.data[DOMAIN].

DUPLICATE of A2-DOWN-3, same file and line, and independently confirmed: core/water_amendment.py:243-246 stores both unsubs in closure-local lists; _cancel_all (:113-125) is closure-private and only reached from _commit (:202); the sole caller is listeners/lifecycle.py:390; nothing is registered with entry.async_on_unload and async_unload_entry (__init__.py:465-548) has no row for it. The `_water_amendment_jobs` key (:70-72) is popped nowhere (grep confirms), so __init__.py:545-546's `if not domain_data: hass.data.pop(DOMAIN, None)` cannot fire once any mop job has finalized.

The finder is admirably precise about what this does NOT prove: the data written by _write_amendment is correct, so there is no wrong result — only uncancelled loop-lifetime work and a permanently retained hass.data[DOMAIN]. The ErrorTracker.stop comparison is a good in-repo precedent for the fix. LOW is correct.

title: _async_update_listener reloads the entry on ANY entry mutation — including renaming the entry and the two "advanced" preference toggles, none of which the runtime reads
area: FLOW — config flow, options flow, and the entry update listener
observed_behavior: Line 265 registers `entry.add_update_listener(_async_update_listener)`, and the listener body is an unconditional `await hass.config_entries.async_reload(entry.entry_id)` with no comparison of what actually changed. I read HA's dispatcher at site-packages/homeassistant/config_entries.py:2540-2601: `_async_update_entry` sets `changed = True` for a change to ANY of unique_id, discovery_keys, minor_version, pref_disable_new_entities, pref_disable_polling, title, version, data, options or subentries, and then `_async_save_and_notify` (2603-2609) fires EVERY update listener. It is not options-specific. So all of these trigger a full unload+setup of this entry: (a) the user renaming the integration entry in Settings -> Devices & Services (a title-only change); (b) toggling "Enable newly added entities" (pref_disable_new_entities); (c) toggling "Enable polling for updates" (pref_disable_polling); (d) saving the options form after editing ONLY the notes field. I grepped the whole package for CONF_NOTES and CONF_TESTED_MODEL: neither is read by any runtime code path — the only consumers are config_flow.py itself and diagnostics.py:542, which reads `entry.data`/`entry.options` live and redacts them. So a notes edit changes nothing the running integration can observe, and title/pref changes are handled by HA itself; every one of these reloads is pure waste. This matters beyond wasted work because audit #14 proved a reload is precisely the event that orphans the manager's loop-lifetime work, after which the OLD manager's `self.data` is written over the live store.
user_impact: Renaming the entry to something friendlier, or flicking an entity-preference toggle, or fixing a typo in the free-text Notes field, silently bounces every entity of every managed vacuum (all 6 platforms), drops and re-registers every sidebar panel, and — per the already-logged audit #14 defect — hands an orphaned callback the chance to overwrite the live store with stale data. Nothing in the UI suggests renaming an entry could cost stored data.
guards_checked: No guard exists. The listener has no early return, no diff of entry.data/entry.options against a captured snapshot, and no `entry.async_on_state_change`-style filter. I checked the config flow's `_abort_if_unique_id_configured(reload_on_update=False)` (config_flow.py:51) — its comment is accurate but only suppresses the FLOW-side reload (and cannot fire at all here, since no `updates` dict is passed: HA config_entries.py:3087 requires `updates is not None`); it does nothing about the listener. I checked that HA does NOT fire listeners on a no-op write (`if not changed: return False`, config_entries.py:2595), so re-saving identical options is safe — that is the only case that is already rescued. I also checked the only in-repo caller of `async_update_entry` (__init__.py:653, `_schedule_clear_configured_vacuum`), whose reload IS wanted, so the fix must be a change-aware listener rather than removing the listener.

confirmations:
HA MECHANISM VERIFIED EXACTLY; SEVERITY BADLY OVER-RATED.

Confirmed in HA 2026.5.3 config_entries.py:2511-2601: _async_update_entry sets `changed = True` for unique_id, and for each of discovery_keys / minor_version / pref_disable_new_entities / pref_disable_polling / title / version, plus data / options / subentries — then :2603-2609 `_async_save_and_notify` fires EVERY entry.update_listeners. It is not options-scoped. And :2595 `if not changed: return False` confirms the finder's own caveat that a no-op re-save is already safe. __init__.py:462 is an unconditional `await hass.config_entries.async_reload(entry.entry_id)` with no diff. I also confirmed CONF_NOTES and CONF_TESTED_MODEL are read by nothing outside config_flow.py (grep: only config_flow.py:21,22,63,64,99,110,120) — so a notes edit genuinely changes nothing the runtime observes yet costs a full reload. Reproducer is concrete: rename the entry in Settings -> Devices & Services -> all 6 platforms bounce and every panel is dropped/re-registered.

SEVERITY: HIGH is wrong. On its own the proven outcome is a spurious reload — brief entity unavailability, nothing wrong, nothing lost. Crucially this is the HA-DOCUMENTED idiom (`entry.add_update_listener(...)` -> reload) used by a large fraction of core integrations, so it is an over-broad default rather than a defect with a wrong result. Its danger is entirely BORROWED from two other findings — audit #14's uncancelled manager work and the panel-tracking bug above — and severity must not be double-counted onto the trigger. LOW (latent; real but consequence-free in isolation). The finder's fix framing (a change-aware listener, not removing the listener) is right, and the note that __init__.py:653 is an in-repo caller whose reload IS wanted is correct.
killed_by: REFUTED as a defect, though every factual claim in it checks out. I read config_entries.py _async_update_entry: it does set changed=True for title, pref_disable_new_entities, pref_disable_polling, data, options, etc., and _async_save_and_notify fires every update listener; and `if not changed: return False` means an identical re-save is a no-op. So yes, renaming the entry or flipping an entity-preference toggle does run a full unload+setup. But that is the HA-idiomatic pattern — `entry.async_on_unload(entry.add_update_listener(...))` with an unconditional async_reload is what HA's own docs prescribe and what most integrations ship — and a reload is a contract HA treats as safe. Stripped of borrowed severity, the harm asserted here is 'wasted work': entities are briefly unavailable and panels are re-registered. The only concrete damage the finding points at is the audit #14 orphaned-manager store clobber, which the brief explicitly excludes from re-reporting; a change-aware listener is a mitigation for THAT defect, not an independent one. Under the calibration rule against reporting efficiency observations and style preferences as findings, this is an observation. Note it is also self-inconsistent as a HIGH: the finder's own guard section concedes the fix must keep the listener because _schedule_clear_configured_vacuum depends on the reload firing.
