title: Confidence breakpoint table has a dead band at 0.79–0.80; the best-learned rooms fall through it and render as LOW / red "error"
observed_behavior:
_BREAKPOINTS (lines 117-139) declares MEDIUM as max_score=0.79 and HIGH as min_score=0.80. _breakpoint_for_score uses an INCLUSIVE double-sided test `bp["min_score"] <= score <= bp["max_score"]`, so any score strictly between 0.79 and 0.80 matches NO bucket and hits the fall-through `return dict(_BREAKPOINTS[-1])` — which is the LOW entry (ui_rank 1, ui_variant "error").

That band is exactly where the best real rooms land. _score_room_confidence caps at base 0.55 + sample_bonus 0.25 = 0.80, and the variance penalty is min(cv/0.5,1.0)*0.25. So a room with >=10 samples and a coefficient of variation under 2% scores in (0.79, 0.80).

PROVEN (executed against the real constants): room with 12 timing samples, avg_minutes 10.0, minutes_stddev 0.15 (9 seconds of spread — an exceptionally consistent room), zero accuracy drift:
  cv = 0.15/10.0 = 0.015 ; variance_penalty = (0.015/0.5)*0.25 = 0.0075
  score = 0.55 + 0.25 - 0.0075 = 0.7925
  _breakpoint_for_score(0.7925): high 0.80<=0.7925 FALSE; medium 0.7925<=0.79 FALSE; low 0.7925<=0.49 FALSE -> fall-through -> LOW / ui_rank 1 / ui_variant "error".

The full sweep at 12 samples / avg 10.0:
  stddev 0.00 -> 0.8000 -> high/success
  stddev 0.05 -> 0.7975 -> LOW/error
  stddev 0.10 -> 0.7950 -> LOW/error
  stddev 0.15 -> 0.7925 -> LOW/error
  stddev 0.20 -> 0.7900 -> medium/warning
  stddev 0.50 -> 0.7750 -> medium/warning

The ordering is INVERTED: the noisier room (stddev 0.50) renders amber "warning" while the tighter room (stddev 0.15) renders red "error". Job confidence is min(room scores) (line 983), so one such room drags the WHOLE job estimate into the red band.

src/renderers/learning.js:534 reads `breakpoint.ui_variant` straight into the chip colour and src/renderers/rooms.js:742 / 1196 do the same, so the red chip reaches the user verbatim.
user_impact: The single most reliably-learned room in the house is badged red "Low confidence" on the card, and drags the whole job estimate to red with it — while a demonstrably worse-learned room next to it shows amber "Medium". Users are trained to distrust exactly the numbers they should trust, and the learning system appears not to be working after dozens of successful runs.
guards_checked: _confidence_result (line 172) clamps and rounds to 4 dp before the lookup — round(0.7925,4)=0.7925, so rounding does not rescue it. The fall-through at line 167 is the only safety net and it returns the WRONG end of the table (_BREAKPOINTS[-1] is LOW, not the nearest tier). The mirror gap at (0.49, 0.50) is harmless only by accident — it also falls through to LOW, which happens to be correct there. tests/unit/test_learning_estimator.py [LE-1] parametrises exactly 0.79 and 0.80 and never a value in between, so the band is untested. No caller re-derives the label from confidence_score; the card trusts confidence_label / ui_variant.

confirmations: Confirmed at source. _BREAKPOINTS (estimator.py:117-139) declares medium max_score=0.79 and high min_score=0.80; _breakpoint_for_score:165 uses an inclusive double-sided test, so (0.79, 0.80) matches nothing and line 167 returns _BREAKPOINTS[-1] = LOW/error, not the nearest tier. Redid the arithmetic against the real constants: sample_count 12 -> sample_bonus = min(12/10,1)*0.25 = 0.25 exactly; base 0.55; stddev 0.15/avg 10.0 -> cv 0.015 -> variance_penalty = min(0.015/0.5,1)*0.25 = 0.0075; score = 0.7925. round(0.7925,4) is unchanged, so _confidence_result does not rescue it. stddev 0.20 gives exactly 0.7900 -> medium/warning while stddev 0.15 gives LOW/error: the inversion is real. tests/unit/test_learning_estimator.py:60-61 parametrises 0.79 and 0.80 and nothing between, so the band is genuinely untested; src/renderers/learning.js:534 and rooms.js:742/1196 do read ui_variant straight into the chip. SEVERITY CORRECTED: the band is only 0.01 wide, and entering it requires ALL of >=10 samples, 0 < cv < 0.02, no intensity mismatch and drift_ratio exactly 0 (any recorded accuracy error pushes the score below 0.79 into medium). That is a narrow-conditions defect, not the 'best real rooms land exactly there' claim the finder makes.

Reproduced against the real constants. _BREAKPOINTS medium max_score=0.79, high min_score=0.80 (estimator.py:117-139) and _breakpoint_for_score uses the inclusive double-sided test at :165, so (0.79,0.80) matches nothing and falls through to _BREAKPOINTS[-1] = LOW/ui_rank 1/ui_variant 'error'. Confirmed the score is reachable: base 0.55 + min(12/10,1)*0.25 = 0.80; cv=0.15/10.0=0.015 -> penalty (0.015/0.5)*0.25=0.0075 -> 0.7925. round(0.7925,4) is unchanged by _confidence_result. Inversion confirmed: stddev 0.20 -> 0.7900 -> medium/warning; stddev 0.15 -> 0.7925 -> LOW/error. ui_variant does reach the card verbatim (src/renderers/learning.js:534, rooms.js:742-743, 1196). WRONG BADGE SHOWN, not a wrong number and not a wrong action - the ETA minutes are unaffected. Band is narrow (needs >=10 samples, cv<2%, and zero accuracy drift, which any previously-estimated room breaks).

title: App-started (external) runs contribute battery=0.0 samples; the estimator consumes a learned 0.0 as a real number and derives battery_warning / mid_job_recharge_risk = False from it
observed_behavior:
learning/external_ingest.py:1056-1105 (build_graduated_job) constructs the completed_job record with NO `battery` block at all — I read the whole literal; grep for "battery" in external_ingest.py returns zero hits. external_run.py:509 saves that record verbatim and immediately rebuilds stats. outcome.status is "completed" and used_for_learning is True (external_ingest.py:1084), so history_store.is_learning_job (line 414-428) admits it.

In the rebuilder, `total_battery_used = _safe_float(job.get("battery", {}).get("used"), 0.0)` -> 0.0, per_room_battery -> 0.0, and that 0.0 is accumulated into the SAME room_stats bucket as dispatched runs, diluting avg_battery_used toward zero.

The estimator then does `battery = _safe_float(match.get("avg_battery_used"), _DEFAULT_BATTERY_PER_ROOM)`. _safe_float (utils.py:20) only substitutes the default for None/""/"unknown"/"unavailable" — **0.0 is a valid float and passes straight through**. There is no zero-floor, no `area_sample_count`-style `battery_sample_count`, and no `source` marker distinguishing "learned 0%" from "no battery data".

PROVEN. Room bucket = 3 external samples (0.0 each) + 1 dispatched sample (8.0%): avg_battery_used = (0+0+0+8)/4 = 2.0. Five-room job, current_battery 25%, reserve 5%:
  total_battery_used            = 5 * 2.0 = 10.0   (truth ~5 * 8 = 40)
  required_start_battery        = 15.0
  battery_shortfall             = max(15-25, 0) = 0.0  -> battery_warning = False
  mid_job_recharge_needed       = max(10-25, 0) = 0.0  -> mid_job_recharge_risk = False
  remaining_battery_after_job   = 25 - 10 = +15%       (truth -15%)
  projected_recharge_overhead   = 10 * 0.05 = 0.5 min  (truth ~2.0 min)

With an all-external archive (the population external ingest exists to serve) avg_battery_used = 0.0 exactly: total_battery_used = 0.0, remaining_battery_after_job = current_battery, and the card asserts the job costs ZERO battery with battery_warning False at any charge level.

Critically, none of these outputs carry the confidence signal: confidence_score is computed from TIMING samples only (sample_count / minutes_stddev, lines 848-878). battery_warning and mid_job_recharge_risk are bare booleans presented as fact.
user_impact: The card tells the user a 5-room job will finish with 15% left and shows no battery warning and no mid-job-recharge risk, when the job actually needs 40% and the robot will strand and dock mid-run. A user who mostly starts runs from the vendor app — precisely the user external ingest was built for — gets a battery model that converges on "this job is free".
guards_checked: _safe_float's default only fires on None/blank/unknown/unavailable, not on 0.0 — verified in utils.py:20-27. is_learning_job does not gate on origin. The rebuilder has no battery-sample counter analogous to area_sample_count, so a zero is indistinguishable from an absence downstream. _DEFAULT_BATTERY_PER_ROOM=0.8 never fires because a match exists. estimate() has no floor on total_battery. can_run_now is intentionally always True (documented lines 1040-1043) so it is not a backstop. src/renderers/learning.js:203 and :868 render battery_warning; core/manager.py:3500 forwards mid_job_recharge_risk.

confirmations: Fully confirmed. grep for 'battery' across learning/external_ingest.py returns ZERO hits and I read build_graduated_job's record literal (external_ingest.py:1055-1105) — there is no 'battery' block, while outcome.status='completed' and used_for_learning=True, so history_store.is_learning_job:414-428 admits it. stats_rebuilder.py:414 is exactly `total_battery_used = _safe_float(job.get("battery", {}).get("used"), 0.0)` -> 0.0, and :432 per_room_battery = 0.0 is accumulated into total_estimated_battery_used (:520) with avg = total/sample_count (:648). estimator.py:844 uses _safe_float(match.get('avg_battery_used'), _DEFAULT_BATTERY_PER_ROOM); utils.py:20-27 confirms the default fires only on None/''/unknown/unavailable, so 0.0 passes through. Arithmetic re-verified: (0+0+0+8)/4 = 2.0; 5 rooms -> total_battery 10.0; required_start = 15.0; shortfall = max(15-25,0) = 0.0 -> battery_warning False (estimator.py:1045); mid_job_recharge_needed = max(10-25,0) = 0.0 -> risk False (:1036); remaining_battery_after_job = +15 (:1035); recharge overhead = 10*0.05 = 0.5. All correct. Confidence is scored from timing samples only, so these booleans carry no uncertainty signal.

Confirmed end to end. grep for 'battery' in learning/external_ingest.py returns ZERO hits and I read the build_graduated_job literal (lines ~1055-1105): the record has job/job_profile/resolved_rooms/outcome and NO battery block, with outcome.status='completed' and used_for_learning=True, so is_learning_job (history_store.py:414-428) admits it. stats_rebuilder.py:414 total_battery_used = _safe_float(job.get('battery',{}).get('used'), 0.0) -> {}.get('used') is None -> 0.0; :432 per_room_battery = 0.0; :520 accumulated into total_estimated_battery_used; :651 avg_battery_used = total/sample_count. estimator.py:844 _safe_float(match.get('avg_battery_used'), 0.8) - utils.py:20 only substitutes for None/''/'unknown'/'unavailable', so 0.0 passes through. Arithmetic checks: 3 external (0.0) + 1 dispatched (8.0) -> 2.0; 5 rooms -> total_battery_used 10.0 vs ~40 truth; required_start 15.0 vs current 25 -> battery_shortfall 0.0 -> battery_warning False; mid_job_recharge_needed max(10-25,0)=0 -> risk False; remaining_battery_after_job +15 vs -15 truth; recharge overhead 0.5 min vs 2.0. Confirmed this is a WRONG NUMBER SHOWN, not a wrong action - can_run_now is hard-coded True (estimator.py:1044) so nothing dispatches on it.

title: _find_room_match Pass 1 can NEVER match a Roborock room: it compares the raw "" intensity against the rebuilder's normalized "standard", so every Roborock room takes a permanent -0.15 intensity-mismatch penalty
observed_behavior:
Roborock declares no clean_intensity axis at all (adapters/roborock/vocabulary.py:107-109: "clean_intensity is OMITTED from every profile on purpose"; rooms/room_defaults.py:45-47 documents the same). So rooms/room_manager.py:103 stores `clean_intensity=str(_default("clean_intensity", ""))` -> the literal empty string on EVERY Roborock room.

The two sides then normalize that empty string DIFFERENTLY:
  learning/manager.py:2201 (estimator projection): `str(room.get("clean_intensity","standard")).strip().lower()` -> ""
  learning/stats_rebuilder.py:477-479 (stats key):   `str(room.get("clean_intensity","standard")).strip().lower() or "standard"` -> "standard"

_find_room_match._intensity (line 476) does `str(item.get("clean_intensity","standard")).strip().lower() == clean_intensity` -> "standard" == "" -> **False, always**. title: Estimate consumes avg_minutes with no outlier rejection and no band check, and a single poisoned sample scores MEDIUM confidence because stddev of one sample is 0 by construction

title: HIGH confidence is mathematically unreachable for any real room, yet _learning_velocity reports runs_to_high=0 at 10 samples and runs_to_medium=0 always
observed_behavior:
_score_room_confidence maxes at base 0.55 + sample_bonus 0.25 = 0.80, and the HIGH breakpoint min_score is 0.80. Reaching it requires sample_count >= 10 AND variance_penalty == 0 AND intensity_penalty == 0 AND accuracy_penalty == 0. variance_penalty is zero only when minutes_stddev <= 0 (line 306), and stats_rebuilder._stddev returns non-zero for any 10 wall-clock durations that are not byte-identical floats. accuracy_penalty is non-zero for any room that has ever been estimated and completed (any mean_abs_pct_error > 0 subtracts). So for a genuinely well-learned room the score asymptotes just BELOW 0.80 — which, per EST-1, is the dead band that renders red.

Meanwhile _SAMPLES_FOR_HIGH = ceil((0.80-0.55)/0.25*10) = ceil(10.0) = 10, and _learning_velocity returns `runs_to_high = max(10 - sample_count, 0)`. At sample_count=10 that is 0 — the card stops saying "N more runs" and implies the tier is reached — while current_tier is still "medium" (or red, per EST-1).

_SAMPLES_FOR_MEDIUM = ceil((0.50-0.55)/0.25*10) = ceil(-2.0) = -2, so `runs_to_medium = max(-2 - n, 0)` is **0 for every possible sample_count, including 0**. A brand-new unlearned room (source="default", score 0.20, tier LOW) is told it needs 0 more runs to reach MEDIUM.

The docstring at lines 142-144 concedes the targets are computed "assuming zero variance and no penalties" — but src/renderers/learning.js:615 and src/renderers/room-estimate.js:48 render runs_to_high as a user-facing promise, and the card falls silent once it hits 0.
user_impact: The card advertises a HIGH/green confidence tier that no room can ever reach, counts the user down to it over ten runs, then reports "0 runs remaining" while the badge stays amber or red. An unlearned room is simultaneously scored LOW and told it needs zero more runs to be reliable. The learning-velocity feature actively misinforms.
guards_checked: _learning_velocity clamps with max(...,0) but never cross-checks current_score against the tier it is counting toward — it returns current_tier alongside a contradictory runs_to_* of 0 with no reconciliation. Nothing recomputes the targets from the live penalties. tests/unit/test_learning_estimator.py [LE-8]/[LE-9] assert runs_to_high == 0 at saturation and > 0 at zero samples, which locks the behaviour in rather than catching it; no test asserts runs_to_medium.

confirmations: The arithmetic is exact and damning: _SAMPLES_FOR_MEDIUM = ceil((0.50-0.55)/0.25*10) = ceil(-2.0) = -2, so runs_to_medium = max(-2 - n, 0) is 0 for every n including 0 — a brand-new default-source room (score 0.20, LOW) is told it needs zero runs. _SAMPLES_FOR_HIGH = 10 and runs_to_high hits 0 at n=10 while HIGH needs score >= 0.80, which requires variance_penalty == 0 (i.e. minutes_stddev exactly 0). SEVERITY CORRECTED down: I refuted two of the finder's supporting claims. HIGH is NOT 'mathematically unreachable' — 0.80 is attainable when _stddev rounds to 0.0 with no drift/intensity penalty, so the claim is practical, not mathematical. And I grepped src/: runs_to_medium has NO renderer at all (only runs_to_high appears, at learning.js:615 and room-estimate.js:48, and only when > 0). So the always-zero runs_to_medium is latent payload junk, and the user-visible part is the card merely falling silent at n=10 — an absent promise, not a wrong number.

title: _find_room_match relaxed passes return the lexicographically-first bucket and ignore sample_count entirely — a 1-sample bucket beats a 30-sample one
observed_behavior:
Passes 2-5 iterate `room_stats` and `return item` on the FIRST structural match. room_stats arrives in stats_rebuilder order: `for key in sorted(room_stats.keys())` (line 623) where the key is `map_id::slug::mode::clean_times::is_carpet::clean_intensity::edge_mopping` — a plain lexicographic string sort. Neither sample_count nor timing_sample_count is consulted anywhere in _find_room_match, and there is no blending across the relaxed dimension.

Eufy intensities are "quick"/"narrow"/"deep" (adapters/eufy/adapter.py:421-425). Sorted: "deep" < "narrow" < "quick". So when Pass 1 misses, Pass 2 returns the DEEP bucket first — structurally the slowest setting.

PROVEN. Kitchen has 30 samples at intensity "narrow" (avg_minutes 9.0) and 1 sample at "deep" (avg_minutes 22.0). The user selects "quick" for the first time. Pass 1 finds no quick bucket. Pass 2 walks the sorted list and returns "deep":
  minutes = 22.0 (144% over the 9.0 the 30-sample bucket supports)
  sample_count = 1, minutes_stddev = 0.0 (n<2) -> variance_penalty 0
  score = 0.55 + 0.025 - 0.15 = 0.4250 -> LOW/error
The 30-sample evidence is never even examined.

The same mechanism applies to Pass 5 (ignore clean_passes): "1" sorts before "2" and "3", so a Roborock 3-pass request with no 3-pass bucket silently returns the 1-pass bucket — the FASTEST — and underestimates.
user_impact: Changing one room setting the user has not run before throws away every accumulated sample for that room and answers from whichever adjacent bucket happens to sort first, which is systematically the slowest bucket for intensity and the fastest for passes. The displayed room duration can be off by more than 2x while the room's real, well-supported history sits unread.
guards_checked: The intensity_mismatch penalty (-0.15) is applied, but it penalizes CONFIDENCE only — the duration and battery numbers still come from the arbitrary bucket. There is no tie-break on sample_count, no weighted average, and no fall-through to room_baselines (which carries the correctly-pooled per-room average and the by_clean_times / by_edge_mopping buckets, and which the estimator never reads at all except for ingress transit seconds).

title: estimate() runs ensure_dirs (four mkdir syscalls) three times per call on the event loop, even on full cache hits
observed_behavior:
estimate() calls load_room_stats (line 766), _load_accuracy_stats -> load_accuracy_stats (line 770), and _build_transit_indices -> load_job_stats (line 719). Each of those resolves its path via get_*_stats_path, and every one of those helpers calls `self.ensure_dirs(...)` (history_store.py:430-443, 548-563), which unconditionally executes four `Path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` syscalls (history_store.py:151-154) BEFORE the cache is consulted.

So one estimate performs 12 filesystem mkdir syscalls on the event loop. The comment at estimator.py:772-773 states the estimate "is computed on the event loop via the dashboard snapshot, so avoid a second read", and history_store.py:496-502 claims "caching keeps that off disk" — both claims cover the JSON read only. The directory-creation syscalls are outside the cache and run every time.

The user's HA config lives on an SMB share (Z:\ = \\192.168.4.104\config), where a mkdir round-trip is a network operation, not a local one.
user_impact: Recurring blocking filesystem I/O on the HA event loop on every dashboard snapshot. On a network-mounted config directory this can surface as HA's "blocking call inside the event loop" warning or as UI stutter, without any incorrect output.
guards_checked: The three read caches (_room_stats_cache / _accuracy_stats_cache / _job_stats_cache, history_store.py:496-513) are real and hass.data-scoped, and warm_estimate_caches (line 515) pre-populates them from an executor — so the read side is genuinely covered. What is not covered is path RESOLUTION: get_room_stats_path / get_accuracy_stats_path / get_job_stats_path all go through ensure_dirs rather than get_paths, so the mkdirs happen before the `if key in cache` check on every call. _build_transit_indices wraps its load in a broad `except Exception` (line 732) which would swallow an OSError from the mkdir and silently degrade global_inter_room to None.

title: A single transient read failure makes record_estimate_accuracy silently overwrite the entire accuracy history with one job's rooms
area: ACC — accuracy feedback and timeline (record_estimate_accuracy, next_room, reanchor_timeline)
observed_behavior: `existing = copy.deepcopy(self.store.load_accuracy_stats(...) or {})` cannot distinguish "no history yet" from "history exists but could not be read". history_store.read_json (157-178) catches `except Exception` on ANY failure — OSError on the SMB-mounted config share, permission error, partial read — logs it and returns None; load_accuracy_stats (565-579) maps that to None and caches the None. record_estimate_accuracy then builds `rooms_data = existing.get("rooms", {})` = {} and, at 655-664, UNCONDITIONALLY calls save_accuracy_stats with `{"rooms": rooms_data}` — write_json does an atomic os.replace, not a merge. The prior file is gone. The write side of exactly this hazard is reasoned about in this function's own comment ("a write_json failure (it re-raises, e.g. on an SMB hiccup)") and in write_json's docstring ("the failure mode that left `Extra data` trailing bytes on the SMB-mounted config share"); the read side is unguarded. Worse, the save happens even when `recorded` is empty — a failed read plus a job whose rooms carry no snapshot estimate writes `{"rooms": {}}`, a total wipe for zero gain.
user_impact: Concrete: store holds 14 room keys / 60 graded samples; one OSError while reading learned/accuracy_stats.json during a 2-room job's finalize rewrites the file with 2 keys at sample_count 1. The 12 lost keys had mean_abs_pct_error ~0.20+, which _score_room_confidence turns into the full -0.20 accuracy penalty; with the history gone _drift_ratio_for_room returns 0.0, so every one of those rooms' confidence JUMPS +0.20 on the very next estimate — e.g. 0.60 (MEDIUM/warning) to 0.80 (HIGH/success). The card presents a newly "high confidence" ETA whose entire supporting evidence was just destroyed, with no user-visible signal. Recoverable only if the user happens to run rebuild_accuracy_stats.
guards_checked: read_json 157-178 (blanket `except Exception` -> None, no absent-vs-unreadable distinction); load_accuracy_stats 565-579 (only `isinstance(payload, dict) else None`, and it CACHES the None); the `or {}` at 590; no path.exists() / loaded-shape check before the overwrite; no early return when `recorded` is empty; no sample-count regression guard; save_accuracy_stats 553-563 (unconditional write_json + cache replace, no merge, no backup); the finalize call site (learning/manager.py:812-819) gates only on used_for_learning, which does not help here; rebuild_accuracy_stats exists but is manual and never triggered by this path.

confirmations: Mechanism confirmed line by line. read_json:157-178 collapses JSONDecodeError and a blanket `except Exception` (any OSError on the SMB share) into None; load_accuracy_stats:565-579 maps that to None AND caches the None; estimator.py:589-592 does `copy.deepcopy(... or {})` then `existing.get("rooms", {})`; the save at :655-664 is unconditional — outside any `if recorded` check — and save_accuracy_stats -> write_json does an atomic os.replace, not a merge. So one failed read plus one job (or even zero gradable rooms) replaces the whole file. The confidence arithmetic checks out: _score_room_confidence:314-318 gives min(drift/0.20,1.0)*0.20, so a room at drift >= 0.20 jumps exactly +0.20 once its history is gone. SEVERITY CORRECTED from CRITICAL: the loss is NOT unrecoverable. learning/manager.rebuild_accuracy_stats replays the whole archive through the same _auto_record_accuracy extractor, and it is wired into the user-facing rebuild_learning_stats service via core/manager.async_rebuild_learning_accumulators (services.py:447 -> manager.py:4548). Destroyed-but-repairable-by-an-exposed-service is HIGH, not CRITICAL.

Mechanism fully confirmed. read_json (history_store.py:157-178) maps JSONDecodeError AND a bare `except Exception` (any OSError) to None, indistinguishable from the absent-file return at :161. load_accuracy_stats (:565-579) narrows to None and CACHES the None at :578. estimator.py:589-592 does `deepcopy(... or {})` then rooms_data = existing.get('rooms', {}) = {}, and :655-664 unconditionally saves {'rooms': rooms_data} through write_json's os.replace - no path.exists() check, no shape check, no early return when `recorded` is empty, no sample-count regression guard. Confirmed the write side of exactly this hazard is reasoned about in the same function's comment while the read side is not. Confidence arithmetic is right: with the history gone _drift_ratio_for_room returns 0.0, removing up to the full 0.20 accuracy penalty (:314-318), so 0.60 MEDIUM jumps to 0.80 HIGH on the next estimate. DOWNGRADING from CRITICAL: I verified learning/manager.py:1003 rebuild_accuracy_stats replays the whole jobs/ archive through the SAME _auto_record_accuracy extractor and is wired into core/manager.async_rebuild_learning_accumulators:4548, so this is recoverable data, not destroyed data - unlike A3-IO-2 (trouble_rooms), which has no rebuilder by explicit design. Recovery is also only as good as the archived estimated_minutes, so it can be partial.

title: reanchor_timeline ignores its own reanchor_at parameter — every ETA is anchored to job start plus the sum of room durations, so all wall-clock dead time is invisible and "Done at" times slide into the past
area: ACC — accuracy feedback and timeline (record_estimate_accuracy, next_room, reanchor_timeline)
observed_behavior: The docstring claims `reanchor_at: ISO timestamp to anchor remaining ETAs from. Defaults to now.` (1117-1118). It does not. `anchor_dt` (1122) is used for exactly one thing: echoing `result["reanchored_at"]` at 1223. Every per-room `eta_at` (1166, 1184) and the `job_eta_at` (1211) are computed as `job_start_dt + offset`, where job_start_dt comes from original_estimate["started_at"] (1138-1139) and offset is built purely from summed completed actuals plus remaining estimates. Nothing in the function reads the current wall clock into an offset. Room actual durations deliberately EXCLUDE paused time (jobs/active_job.py:373-380 subtracts current_room_paused_seconds), and the job-level `paused_duration_seconds` is never read here — so paused minutes vanish from the timeline entirely rather than pushing it out. The caller already supplies a live wall-clock anchor (core/manager.py:3188 passes `current_room_started_at or _iso_now()`) that would fix this; it is discarded.
user_impact: Concrete: 3 rooms at 10 min each, overhead 7.02, started 12:00. R1 completes at 12:10 with actual_duration 10.0. The user pauses the vacuum at 12:10 and resumes at 12:40. At 12:45 the card refreshes and reanchors with completed=[R1:10]: R2 eta_at = 12:00+20 = 12:20 (25 minutes in the PAST), R3 = 12:30, job_eta_at = 12:00+37.02 = 12:37 (8 minutes in the past). The live banner renders "Cleaning Kitchen — done at 12:20" at 12:45, and it never self-corrects: the timeline stays pinned to sum-of-actuals no matter how much real time elapses. title: Reanchoring drops inter-room transit from remaining rooms while keeping it in overhead — remaining ETAs jump earlier then later (oscillation) and the job ETA inflates by one transit leg per completed room on a run that is exactly on estimate
area: ACC — accuracy feedback and timeline (record_estimate_accuracy, next_room, reanchor_timeline)
observed_behavior: estimate() folds the learned transit leg into the cumulative per-room offsets (`cumulative_minutes += transit_before`, 900-904) AND into overhead.transition_minutes (`learned_transition_minutes=total_transit_minutes`, 973 -> 349-352) — counted once in the job total because the timeline offsets and the total are computed on different bases. reanchor_timeline rebuilds the remaining offsets from `minutes` ALONE (`remaining_cursor += estimated_minutes`, 1178) — `estimated_transit_minutes_before` survives on the entry (copied by `dict(room)` at 1155) but is never re-added — while reusing the ORIGINAL overhead wholesale (`overhead_minutes = original_estimate["overhead_minutes"]`, 1208-1210). Meanwhile a completed room's actual is completion-to-completion wall clock (current_room_started_at is set to the previous room's completed_at, jobs/active_job.py:2009), so it already CONTAINS the transit into that room. Net: transit is subtracted from every remaining room's ETA and added twice to the job total for every completed room.
user_impact: Concrete: 3 rooms × 10 min estimated, learned transit 2.0 min per boundary, overhead 7.02 (startup 1 + transitions 4 + recharge 0.12 + dust 0.9 + return 1), started 12:00. Original timeline: R2 eta 12:22, R3 eta 12:34, job eta 12:37.02. Every room then runs EXACTLY on estimate. After R1 (actual 10.0): R2 -> 12:20, R3 -> 12:30 (both jumped ~2-4 min EARLIER), job eta unchanged 12:37. After R2 (actual 12.0 = 2 transit + 10 clean): R3 -> 12:32 (jumped 2 min BACK OUT), job eta -> 12:39.02. So the user watches R3's "done at" go 12:34 -> 12:30 -> 12:32 with nothing having gone wrong. At completion the job eta reads 12:41.02 against a real finish of ~12:35. Scaled to an 8-room queue with a 2-min learned transit, the job ETA inflates by ~14 minutes over a perfectly on-schedule run.
guards_checked: no transit term in the remaining branch (1176-1192); `estimated_transit_minutes_before` is preserved on the entry but read by nobody; overhead is never recomputed on reanchor and `transition_minutes` is not reduced as rooms complete; the same defect exists on the cold-start path because _lookup_transit_minutes returns the 0.75 _TRANSITION_PER_ROOM constant and total_transit_minutes is still passed as learned_transition_minutes (967-975), so "no learned transit" does not rescue it; core/manager.py rebuilds the estimate fresh each snapshot and then reanchors, so the drift is recomputed identically on every refresh rather than accumulating in storage.

R3's 'done at' walks 12:34 -> 12:30 -> 12:32 on a run that is exactly on estimate, and the job total gains one transit leg per completed room after the first. Matches the finding exactly.

title: A skipped room can never be resolved: it holds "current" for the rest of the run, adds its full estimate to every later room's ETA, and permanently blocks all_completed
area: ACC — accuracy feedback and timeline (record_estimate_accuracy, next_room, reanchor_timeline)
observed_behavior: reanchor_timeline's only input for progress is `completed_rooms`. A skipped room is never completed, so it takes the else branch (1176-1192) forever — and line 1189 hard-writes `entry["skipped"] = False`, overwriting the field on every pass, so the timeline's skip flag is a constant. The tracker DOES have a first-class skip signal (jobs/active_job.py:821-851 computes skipped_room_ids and fires EVENT_ROOM_SKIPPED once per room per job) and reanchor_timeline has no parameter to receive it. Because the skipped room precedes the live room in queue order by the definition of the signal, it is the FIRST unresolved entry, so the marking loop at 1196-1206 assigns it `current=True`, and next_room() (1074-1088) returns the first non-completed entry — i.e. the skipped room.
user_impact: Concrete: queue Den(6 est) / Kitchen(10 est) / Hall(8 est); the robot skips Den and Kitchen completes with actual 10. Loop order: Den unresolved -> remaining_cursor 6, eta start+6; Kitchen completed -> actual_elapsed 10, eta start+10; Hall -> start 10+6 = 16, end 24, eta start+24 — 6 minutes later than the truth, for the whole rest of the run. next_room()/`current` point at Den, so get_next_room reports "Den, done at <past time>" while the robot is in Hall. rooms_remaining stays 2 and all_completed stays False, so the "All rooms complete / returning to dock" banner never fires for that job.
guards_checked: line 1189 `entry["skipped"] = False` (and 1172 on the completed branch) unconditionally clobbers any skip state; no `skipped_rooms` parameter on reanchor_timeline; the first-unresolved loop (1196-1206) has no skip predicate; next_room() checks only `completed`; core/manager.py:3203-3204 independently re-derives current_room_id from the active job, which rescues the CARD BANNER specifically (src/state/learning.js:919-931 prefers dashboardJobProgress().current_room_id) but not next_room(), the `current` flag, rooms_remaining, all_completed, or any downstream ETA.

confirmations: Confirmed. reanchor_timeline takes only completed_rooms — there is no skipped parameter — and both branches hard-write entry['skipped'] = False (:1171 and :1189), so the flag is a constant. A skipped room is never in completed_by_id/completed_by_slug, so it takes the else branch forever, contributes its full estimate to remaining_cursor, is picked up as the first unresolved entry by the marking loop (:1196-1206) and is what next_room() returns (:1074-1075, which checks only `completed`). remaining_count therefore never reaches 0, so all_completed stays False. The live skip signal does exist and is not plumbed in: active_job.py:821-851 computes skipped_room_ids and fires EVENT_ROOM_SKIPPED. core/manager.py:3196-3204 independently re-derives current_room_id, which rescues the banner only.

Confirmed. reanchor_timeline takes only completed_rooms - there is no skipped_rooms parameter - and line 1189 hard-writes entry['skipped'] = False on the unresolved branch (mirrored at :1171), so the timeline's skip flag is a constant. Verified the tracker does have a first-class signal that never reaches here: jobs/active_job.py:821-851 computes skipped_room_ids as queue-order predecessors of the current room that are not in completed_room_ids and fires EVENT_ROOM_SKIPPED once per room, but nothing adds them to completed_room_ids. Because a skipped room precedes the live room by that definition it is the first unresolved entry, so the marking loop at :1196-1206 (no skip predicate) assigns it current=True and next_room() (:1074-1088, checks only 'completed') returns it. Arithmetic reproduces: Den(6)/Kitchen(10)/Hall(8) with Den skipped and Kitchen actual 10 -> Hall start 16 / end 24, 6 minutes late for the rest of the run; rooms_remaining 2 and all_completed False permanently. Confirmed the partial rescue: core/manager.py:3200-3204 re-derives current_room_id from the active job for the banner, but next_room(), the timeline's `current` flag, rooms_remaining and all_completed are unrescued.

title: Completed-room slug matching is keyed on the literal string "none" — the documented slug fallback is dead, and a room with a null slug is marked complete before it is cleaned
area: ACC — accuracy feedback and timeline (record_estimate_accuracy, next_room, reanchor_timeline)
observed_behavior: Line 1130 does `slug = str(entry.get("slug", "")).strip().lower()`. The production writer hard-codes `"slug": None` on every completed-room entry (jobs/active_job.py:1993-1999), so the key EXISTS with value None and `str(None)` yields the literal "none" — which passes the `if slug:` truthiness test at 1133 and is stored as `completed_by_slug["none"]`. Two consequences. (a) The slug fallback documented at 1116 ("room_id OR slug") can never match a real slug for the production caller — it is dead code carrying a poison key. (b) The timeline side normalizes identically: estimate() line 820 does `str(room.get("slug", "")).strip().lower()`, and RoomConfig.slug is `str | None = None` (models/models.py:174) with queue_engine copying `room.get("slug")` straight through into resolved_rooms (queue_engine.py:318), so a room whose stored slug is null becomes the string "none" in the timeline and MATCHES the poison key at 1153. title: The "exact vs allocated" quality flag is recorded and never used — job-average actuals are blended into the same drift mean, permanently capping affected rooms below HIGH confidence while the card promises they will get there
area: ACC — accuracy feedback and timeline (record_estimate_accuracy, next_room, reanchor_timeline)
observed_behavior: record_estimate_accuracy stores `single_room_sample_count` (627, 637-638) and `mean_signed_error_minutes` (631, 643). A repo-wide grep finds NO reader for either — they appear only in this writer and in docs/dev/10-learning-system.md:503,507. The caller's comment asserts otherwise: "single_room=True means actual_minutes is exact, not allocated. The accuracy store uses this to weight high-quality observations" (learning/manager.py:949-951). It does not weight anything. _drift_ratio_for_room (554-565) reads only the blended `mean_abs_pct_error`, which mixes exact single-room actuals with the multi-room `actual_total / room_count` allocation. The only sanity filter on an incoming grade is `estimated <= 0 or actual <= 0` (607) — pct_error (615) is unbounded and enters a permanent running mean with no window, decay, or outlier rejection.
user_impact: Concrete: a 5-room job whose real per-room times are Bathroom 3 / Kitchen 15 / Living 20 / Hall 4 / Den 18 (60 min total) grades every room against actual_per_room = 12.0. Bathroom (estimated 3) records pct_error = |12-3|/3 = 3.00; Living (estimated 20) records 0.40. Bathroom's confidence ceiling becomes 0.55 base + 0.25 max sample bonus - 0.20 = 0.60 — it can never leave MEDIUM. Meanwhile _learning_velocity (258-273) computes runs_to_high purely from sample count and ignores penalties by construction, so after 10 runs the card reports runs_to_high = 0 while current_tier stays "medium": the "N more runs to a reliable estimate" promise silently never lands.

title: A non-dict `rooms` block crashes both accuracy readers — including estimate() on the event loop — while the sibling reader in the same subsystem explicitly tolerates it
area: ACC — accuracy feedback and timeline (record_estimate_accuracy, next_room, reanchor_timeline)
observed_behavior: `rooms_data: dict[str, Any] = existing.get("rooms", {})` (592) is annotated as a dict but never checked. If the payload's `rooms` is a list, `room_key not in rooms_data` succeeds (list membership) and the very next line `rooms_data[room_key] = {...}` (619) raises TypeError: list indices must be integers. If it is JSON null, `.get("rooms", {})` returns None and the same line raises TypeError. The read path is worse: _drift_ratio_for_room does `accuracy_stats.get("rooms", {}).get(room_key, {})` (564) which raises AttributeError on a list or None — and that call is inside estimate()'s per-room loop (857-860), which core/manager.get_job_progress_snapshot runs ON THE EVENT LOOP for every card refresh. The shape is treated as reachable elsewhere in this same subsystem: learning/manager.py:1191-1197 explicitly accepts both, commenting "Older or externally-produced payloads may use a list", and tests/integration/test_learning_services.py:1114 constructs the list form. The estimator is the only reader without the guard.
user_impact: A hand-edited or older accuracy_stats.json with a list-shaped `rooms` block takes down the entire job-progress snapshot on every card refresh (no estimate, no timeline, no live banner) rather than degrading to zero drift, and every finalize's accuracy fold raises out of _finalize_claimed after the archive write has already happened.
guards_checked: no isinstance check at 592 or 564; load_accuracy_stats (history_store.py:565-579) only guarantees the TOP-LEVEL object is a dict and says nothing about `rooms`; _load_accuracy_stats (549-552) likewise checks only the top level; the finalize call site (learning/manager.py:813-819) does not wrap the executor job in try/except; the sibling normalizer at learning/manager.py:1191-1197 proves the maintainers consider the shape live.

title: An empty room_timing on a charge/wait/zone phase is read as "capture failed", so every stepped run with a break or a zone is stripped of its accurate per-room timings and learns an even split instead
observed_behavior: build_completed_job_payload computes `_every_phase_captured` by truthiness: `_rt = _p.get("room_timing"); if _rt: extend else: _every_phase_captured = False` (lines 985-992), then `transit_capture_valid = _every_phase_captured` (line 996). But jobs/phase_runner.py:256 sets `phases[idx]["room_timing"] = []` for a dock-polled phase (charge_wait / wait, step_types.py:42) and line 270 sets `= []` for a ZONE phase — deliberately, so the finalizer's room path does not invent a phantom room. `[]` is falsy, so the two modules disagree on what the empty list means: phase_runner says "this phase legitimately cleaned no room", history_store reads "a phase was not captured". Result: transit_capture_valid=False for EVERY stepped run containing a charge break or a zone, even though every ROOM phase captured perfectly and its timings are written into the record. stats_rebuilder.py:440 gates the per-room capture on exactly that flag: `if _safe_bool(job_info.get("transit_capture_valid"), False): captured[_rid] = (area_m2, cleaning_wall_seconds/60)`. With it False, `captured` is empty, so line 486-489 takes the else branch: `room_area = None` (multi-room job) and `room_minutes = per_room_duration = total_duration / room_count`. ARITHMETIC: a v1.7.0 stepped run Kitchen(vacuum) -> charge_wait -> Hallway(mop) captures room_timings [{room_id 3, cleaning_wall_seconds 1800, area_m2 22.0}, {room_id 7, 900, 8.0}] — Kitchen 30.0 min, Hallway 15.0 min. duration_minutes excludes the recharge (recharge_seconds_accumulated is subtracted at line 848-856) = 45.0, room_count = 2, so per_room_duration = 22.5. Both rooms fold 22.5 min into room_stats/room_baselines (stats_rebuilder.py:519, :553): Kitchen learns 25% LOW, Hallway 50% HIGH, and because room_area is None neither room contributes an area sample at all — the exact 22.0 / 8.0 m2 figures sitting in the record are discarded. The estimator then serves those poisoned averages as a confident per-room ETA with no staleness or low-confidence marker.
user_impact: Using the flagship charge-break step (vac -> charge to X% -> mop) or queueing a saved zone alongside rooms silently downgrades that run's learning from exact per-room capture to an even time split, and contributes zero area. A Kitchen-only run afterwards is predicted at 22.5 min instead of 30 — the user sees a confident learned number that is 25% wrong, and the more they use stepped runs the worse the baselines get. Nothing surfaces that the run was not fully learned.
guards_checked: jobs/phase_runner.py:252-258 and :260-272 (the writers of the empty list — both intentional, neither sets any other marker history_store could distinguish); phase_runner.py:161 + comment at :160 confirms the FINAL phase is also captured, so this is not an off-by-one at the tail; step_types.py:38-42 confirms charge_wait/wait/zone all make a run stepped and that zone is excluded from DOCK_POLLED_PHASE_TYPES yet still gets room_timing=[] at phase_runner.py:270; stats_rebuilder.py:440 and :587 are the only consumers of transit_capture_valid and both hard-gate on it; stats_rebuilder.py:484-489 has no secondary fallback to room_timings when the flag is False; history_store.py:993 (`if _phase_room_timings:`) still publishes the accurate timings into the record, so the data is present but unusable.

confirmations: Confirmed on both sides of the disagreement. history_store.py:985-996 computes _every_phase_captured by truthiness (`if _rt: extend else: _every_phase_captured = False`) and assigns it to transit_capture_valid, while jobs/phase_runner.py:256 and :270 deliberately set phases[idx]['room_timing'] = [] for dock-polled and ZONE phases (the :265 comment says the empty list exists to keep the finalizer's ROOM path from misfiling a zone). stats_rebuilder.py:440 hard-gates the per-room capture on that flag, and :486-489 then falls to `room_area = None` + `room_minutes = per_room_duration` for a multi-room job. Arithmetic re-derived: duration_minutes already excludes the recharge (history_store.py:848-856 subtracts recharge_seconds_accumulated), so 45.0 / 2 = 22.5 is folded into BOTH rooms against captured truths of 30.0 and 15.0 — Kitchen 25% low, Hallway 50% high — and with room_area None neither contributes an area sample, so the 22.0/8.0 m2 figures sitting in the record are discarded. :993 confirms the accurate timings are still published into the record, i.e. present but unusable.

The semantic disagreement is real and I traced it end to end. jobs/phase_runner.py sets phases[idx]['room_timing'] = [] for a dock-polled phase (charge_wait/wait) and again for a zone phase, both with explicit comments saying the phase legitimately cleaned no room. history_store.py:985-996 tests truthiness (`if _rt: extend else: _every_phase_captured = False`) and assigns transit_capture_valid = _every_phase_captured, so an intentional empty list is read as a capture failure. stats_rebuilder.py:440 hard-gates the per-room capture on that flag; with it False `captured` is empty and :486-489 takes the else branch -> room_area = None (multi-room) and room_minutes = per_room_duration = total_duration / room_count. Confirmed the accurate timings are still written into the record at :993-994, so the data is present but unusable. Arithmetic checks out: Kitchen 1800s + Hallway 900s captured (30.0 / 15.0), duration_minutes 45.0 with recharge subtracted at :848-856, per_room_duration 22.5 -> Kitchen learns 25% low, Hallway 50% high, and neither contributes an area sample. Directly poisons the learned per-room averages that every ETA is built on, and the flagship vac->charge->mop step triggers it every run.

title: read_json turns a corrupt or unreadable file into None, and the trouble-rooms read-modify-write then overwrites the file with a one-job store — permanently destroying history that has no rebuilder by design
observed_behavior: read_json swallows BOTH failure classes into the same value the caller uses for "file absent": json.JSONDecodeError -> warning -> None (lines 169-175) and a bare `except Exception` -> None (176-178), which catches every OSError (EIO / ETIMEDOUT / EACCES / a dropped SMB mount). Nothing distinguishes "there is no history" from "I could not read the history". job_finalizer.py:1624 is a read-modify-write over that value on EVERY finalize: `existing = self.store.load_trouble_rooms(...) or {}` -> `rooms_data = existing.get("rooms", {})` -> the per-room counters are re-derived -> save_trouble_rooms (line 1657) write_json's the result, replacing the file. A single failed read therefore does not degrade gracefully, it ERASES. ARITHMETIC: trouble_rooms.json holds room 5 at run_count=40, miss_count=18 -> miss_rate 0.45, is_trouble=True (the card flags it), plus entries for 8 other rooms. One read fault during the next finalize (queue [5], room 5 missed) gives existing={} -> entry rebuilt from nothing: run_count = 0+1 = 1, miss_count = 0+1 = 1, miss_rate = round(1/1,3) = 1.0, is_trouble = (1 >= 2 and 1.0 >= 0.33) = FALSE. A chronically-missed room stops being flagged and needs two fresh misses to re-qualify; the other 8 rooms vanish from the file entirely. This is unrecoverable: core/manager.py:4528-4531 explicitly excludes trouble_rooms from async_rebuild_learning_accumulators ("A rebuilder for it would be dead weight"), so no service restores it. estimator.py:589 has the identical shape for accuracy_stats (`copy.deepcopy(self.store.load_accuracy_stats(...) or {})` -> save_accuracy_stats), which is repairable only because rebuild_accuracy_stats (manager.py:975) exists. The trigger is not hypothetical for this deployment: write_json's own docstring (lines 184-186) cites the observed `Extra data` trailing-byte corruption "on the SMB-mounted config share" that motivated the atomic write — every learned file written before that fix can still be sitting corrupt in the archive today, and the first finalize after it is read is the one that erases it.
user_impact: A transient network-share hiccup, or one legacy-corrupt file predating the atomic-write fix, silently wipes the chronic-trouble-room history: rooms the card has been correctly flagging as repeatedly missed stop being flagged, and dozens of runs of evidence are gone with no error shown and no service that can rebuild them. The only symptom is the warning line in the log next to a finalize that looks successful.
guards_checked: job_finalizer.py:1662 `except Exception` wraps the whole trouble-rooms update, but read_json never raises so it never fires — it only catches a write failure, i.e. the one case where the old data survives; job_finalizer.py:1626 `if not isinstance(rooms_data, dict): rooms_data = {}` re-seeds rather than aborts; history_store.py:325 (`return payload if isinstance(payload, dict) else None`) preserves the conflation instead of resolving it; save_trouble_rooms/write_json are unconditional — there is no "read failed, skip the write" path; core/manager.py:4528-4531 confirms no rebuilder exists; trouble_rooms is uncached (unlike room/job/accuracy stats), so every finalize re-reads from disk and every read is an independent chance to fail.

confirmations: Confirmed. read_json:169-178 returns None for both a JSONDecodeError and any OSError, indistinguishable from 'file absent'; job_finalizer.py:1624-1626 does `existing = self.store.load_trouble_rooms(...) or {}` and re-seeds rooms_data on a non-dict rather than aborting; the per-room counters are then rebuilt from nothing and save_trouble_rooms (:1657) write_json's the result unconditionally — there is no read-failed-skip-the-write path. The counter arithmetic checks out against :1629-1648: run_count 0+1 = 1, miss_count 0+1 = 1, miss_rate round(1/1,3) = 1.0, is_trouble = (1 >= 2 and ...) = False, and the other rooms' entries are simply gone. The unrecoverability claim is verified: core/manager.py:4528-4531 explicitly excludes trouble_rooms from async_rebuild_learning_accumulators, and services.py:878-898 registers no clear/repair service. The `except Exception` at job_finalizer.py:1662 only catches a write failure — read_json never raises. write_json's own docstring (:184-186) names the observed SMB 'Extra data' corruption, so the trigger is documented, not hypothetical.

Confirmed and this is the genuinely unrecoverable one. read_json collapses JSONDecodeError (:169-175) and any OSError (:176-178) into the same None the caller uses for absent. job_finalizer._update_trouble_rooms_log does `existing = self.store.load_trouble_rooms(...) or {}` then rebuilds per-room counters and unconditionally save_trouble_rooms -> write_json os.replace on EVERY finalize; the isinstance re-seed re-seeds rather than aborts, and the surrounding `except Exception` only catches a write failure (the case where the old data survives), never the read. Arithmetic verified against the writer: rebuilt from {} gives run_count 0+1 = 1, miss_count 0+1 = 1, miss_rate round(1/1,3) = 1.0, is_trouble = (1 >= 2 and ...) = False, and the other rooms' entries are gone. Unrecoverability confirmed at core/manager.py:4528-4531, which explicitly excludes trouble_rooms from async_rebuild_learning_accumulators, and services.py:878-898 registers no clear/repair service. Also confirmed trouble_rooms is uncached (unlike room/job/accuracy stats), so every finalize is an independent read attempt. The SMB corruption precedent is quoted verbatim in write_json's own docstring at :184-186.

title: A failed or absent read is cached as None for the life of the process, and load_*_stats has no bypass — so _reload_learning_stats_now's documented "guarantees the current on-disk stats" is false
observed_behavior: load_room_stats / load_accuracy_stats / load_job_stats memoize the read result in an hass.data-scoped dict keyed by str(path), and they cache the FAILURE value too: `payload = self.read_json(path); data = payload if isinstance(payload, dict) else None; cache[key] = data` (lines 534-537, mirrored at 576-579 and 491-494). The lookup is `if key in cache: return cache[key]` — membership, not truthiness — so a cached None is a permanent answer. The only writer that refreshes the cache is save_*_stats (454 / 466 / 562); there is no invalidate, no TTL and no force-reload argument. Concretely: __init__.py:327 calls warm_estimate_caches on the executor at setup; if that read hits a transient OSError or a corrupt file, read_json returns None (line 176/174), the cache pins None, and for the rest of the HA process every estimate sees no learned stats even though the file on disk is fine. manager.py:340-368 _reload_learning_stats_now exists precisely to escape this and its docstring claims "Unlike the passive preload helper, it guarantees that the returned payload reflects the current on-disk learned stats" — but its body is `self.store.load_room_stats(...)` / `self.estimator._load_accuracy_stats(...)`, which hit the same cache and return the same stale None. manager.py:370-381 _invalidate_learning_stats_cache pops only LearningManager's own per-vacuum dict, not the hass.data store cache, so the documented invalidation path does not reach the layer that is actually holding the value. Same for any out-of-band change to the files (restored backup, hand-edited learned/ dir): reads keep serving the in-memory copy until a save_* happens.
user_impact: One unlucky read at startup makes the card report no learned data / cold-start estimates for the whole HA session, and the two escape hatches a maintainer would reach for (the "reload now" helper and the cache invalidator) both silently fail to re-read disk. Recovery requires an HA restart or a full stats rebuild.
guards_checked: history_store.py:515-521 warm_estimate_caches is the intended pre-warm but it populates the poison rather than avoiding it; manager.py:383-419 async_preload_learning_stats also routes through store.load_room_stats, so the background reload returns the cached None too; manager.py:391 early-returns when both manager-level keys are present but that guard is upstream of the store cache; the isinstance(dict) re-checks at 492/535/577 normalize a non-dict to None, which is exactly what gets cached; no caller anywhere passes a bypass flag because none exists.

confirmations: Confirmed. load_room_stats:534-537, load_accuracy_stats:576-579 and load_job_stats:491-494 all cache the FAILURE value (`data = payload if isinstance(payload, dict) else None; cache[key] = data`) and the lookup is `if key in cache` — membership, not truthiness — so a cached None is permanent for the process. The only refresh is save_*_stats (:454/:466/:562); there is no invalidate, TTL or bypass argument. __init__.py:328 calls warm_estimate_caches at setup, so a transient failure there pins the None. I read learning/manager.py:340-368: _reload_learning_stats_now's docstring claims it 'guarantees that the returned payload reflects the current on-disk learned stats', but its body calls self.store.load_room_stats / estimator._load_accuracy_stats, which hit the same store cache — the claim is false. _invalidate_learning_stats_cache:370-381 pops only LearningManager's own dicts, never the hass.data store cache, so the documented escape hatch does not reach the layer holding the value.

Confirmed by reading all three loaders. load_room_stats (:523-537), load_accuracy_stats (:565-579) and load_job_stats (:480-494) each do `if key in cache: return cache[key]` - membership, not truthiness - and then cache[key] = data where data is None on any read failure or non-dict. Only save_*_stats (:454/:466/:562) refreshes; there is no invalidate, no TTL, no bypass argument. Confirmed the documented escape hatch is false: learning/manager.py:340-368 _reload_learning_stats_now claims it 'guarantees that the returned payload reflects the current on-disk learned stats' but its body calls self.store.load_room_stats and estimator._load_accuracy_stats, both of which hit the same store cache and return the pinned None. _invalidate_learning_stats_cache (:370-381) pops only LearningManager's own per-vacuum dicts, not the hass.data store cache. warm_estimate_caches (:515-521) is the intended pre-warm and is exactly what pins the poison at __init__ time. Recovery needs an HA restart or a save_*.

title: ensure_dirs runs inside every path getter, so the caches that exist to keep the loop-bound estimate off disk still issue ~32 blocking filesystem syscalls per dashboard snapshot
observed_behavior: get_job_stats_path (432), get_room_stats_path (437), get_accuracy_stats_path (550), get_live_snapshot_path (234), get_trouble_rooms_path (303) and list_job_files (223) all begin with `self.ensure_dirs(...)`, which unconditionally calls Path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) FOUR times (151-154). CPython's Path.mkdir issues os.mkdir every call and, on the EEXIST it always gets here, additionally calls self.is_dir() (another stat) before swallowing it — so ensure_dirs is up to 8 real filesystem syscalls, every time, whether or not the file is cached. The cache is checked only AFTER the path is resolved (load_room_stats line 529 resolves the path, line 530-532 checks the cache), so a cache HIT still pays the full mkdir storm. The _room_stats_cache docstring (496-502) states the purpose as "The dashboard-snapshot estimate reads room_stats on the event loop frequently — caching keeps that off disk": verified FALSE for the directory syscalls. The path is provably on the loop — services/snapshots.py:63-66 deliberately does NOT use async_add_executor_job ("Must NOT use async_add_executor_job here") and calls manager.get_dashboard_snapshot synchronously. That one call resolves four store paths: core/manager.py:4137 _learning_has_last_estimate -> load_job_stats; estimator.estimate line 766 -> load_room_stats; line 770 -> _load_accuracy_stats -> load_accuracy_stats; _build_transit_indices line 719 -> load_job_stats. 4 x 8 = up to 32 blocking syscalls per snapshot. src/main.js:547 schedules refreshDashboardSnapshot from `set hass` on a 500 ms debounce (main.js:722-729), so an open card drives up to ~64 loop-blocking syscalls per second, against the same SMB-mounted config share write_json's docstring (line 186) names.
user_impact: Sustained blocking filesystem I/O on the HA event loop whenever a card is open — measurable UI latency and HA's "Detected blocking call ... by custom integration 'eufy_vacuum'" warnings on a network-mounted config dir, despite a caching layer built and documented specifically to prevent it.
guards_checked: __init__.py:320-333 warms the caches off-loop, which removes the read_text but not the mkdir/stat calls; the hass.data caches at 496-513 are consulted after path resolution, never before; .claude/notes/reference_blocking_io_test_guard.md documents that the HA block_async_io test guard does not fire for this module (pathlib bypasses the patched builtins.open), so CI cannot catch it and prior sweeps would have missed it; ensure_dirs has no memo of "already ensured for this vacuum"; get_paths (136-146) is pure and would have sufficed for every read-only caller.

confirmations: Confirmed; same root defect as A1-EST-9, verified independently here. ensure_dirs:148-155 runs four Path.mkdir calls and is the first statement of get_job_stats_path:432, get_room_stats_path:437, get_accuracy_stats_path:550, get_live_snapshot_path:234, get_trouble_rooms_path:303 and list_job_files:223 — and the read caches at :496-513 are consulted only AFTER the path is resolved, so a cache hit still pays for them. The _room_stats_cache docstring's 'caching keeps that off disk' is therefore true for read_text and false for the directory syscalls. The loop-bound claim is verified at the source: services/snapshots.py:63-66 calls manager.get_dashboard_snapshot synchronously with an explicit 'Must NOT use async_add_executor_job here' comment, and that path resolves job_stats/room_stats/accuracy_stats/job_stats again via estimate() (:766, :770) and _build_transit_indices (:719). get_paths:136-146 is pure and would have sufficed for every read-only caller.

Verified in full. ensure_dirs (:148-155) issues four unconditional Path.mkdir calls and is the FIRST statement of get_job_stats_path (:432), get_room_stats_path (:437), get_accuracy_stats_path (:550), get_live_snapshot_path (:234), get_trouble_rooms_path (:303) and list_job_files (:223); CPython's Path.mkdir does os.mkdir plus an is_dir() stat on the EEXIST it always gets, so ~8 syscalls per call. The caches are consulted only AFTER path resolution (:529 then :530), so a cache HIT still pays the full storm - which directly falsifies the _room_stats_cache docstring at :496-502. Loop-bound path confirmed: services/snapshots.py:63-66 explicitly refuses async_add_executor_job because get_dashboard_snapshot fires bus events internally, and that one call resolves four store paths (core/manager.py:4137 load_job_stats, estimator.py:766 load_room_stats, :770 accuracy, :719 job_stats). Confirmed get_paths (:136-146) is pure and would serve every read-only caller. NOTE: A1-EST-9 is the same defect scoped to the estimate alone - one fix closes both.

title: get_completed_job_path interpolates an unvalidated job_id into a filesystem path, giving exclude/restore_learning_job an arbitrary *.json overwrite primitive — the exact hole the sibling module already hardened
observed_behavior: `return paths.jobs_dir / f"{job_id}.json"` with no validation of job_id. The two services that accept a caller-supplied id declare it as `vol.Required("job_id"): cv.string` (services.py:145 and :154) — cv.string coerces, it does not constrain — and pass call.data["job_id"] straight through (services.py:562, :579) to manager.exclude_learning_job / restore_learning_job, which do load_completed_job(job_id) then save_completed_job(job_id) (manager.py:2047+2079, 2108+2143). pathlib does not normalise "..", so job_id="../../../../custom_components/foo/manifest" resolves outside jobs_dir; read_json returns the parsed dict (the exclude path only requires it to BE a dict, manager.py:2051), the outcome block is injected, and write_json os.replace's the mutated payload over the target. write_json also does `path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` (line 188), so it will create directories along an arbitrary path as well. The `.json` suffix is appended, which limits targets to *.json files but does not close the primitive (integration data files, www/ assets, other custom components' configs) and does not limit arbitrary CREATION at all. title: write_json is rename-atomic but not durable — no fsync before os.replace, so a power loss can leave a zero-length learned file that read_json then reports as "no data"
observed_behavior: The temp file is written through os.fdopen and closed by the `with` block, which flushes to the OS but never calls os.fsync(fd); os.replace then renames. The rename is ordered but the DATA is not: after a power cut or a hard host reset the directory entry can be visible while the file's blocks are still unflushed, leaving a zero-length or short room_stats.json / trouble_rooms.json. read_json then hits `if not raw: return None` (line 163) or a JSONDecodeError, both of which return None — feeding IO-2's overwrite cascade and IO-3's negative cache. The docstring (181-187) claims the design means "a reader (or a restart mid-write) never sees a half-written or doubly-written file", which is true for a graceful restart and for a concurrent reader, but is not true for an ungraceful power loss — the claim is broader than what the code delivers.
user_impact: A power cut during a stats write can leave the learned file empty; on the next run the integration reports no learned history rather than an error, and the trouble-rooms accumulator then overwrites what remains (IO-2).
guards_checked: the `except BaseException` block (197-200) correctly unlinks the temp on a failed write, so no orphan is left on an in-process error, but it cannot help across a power loss; os.replace is atomic for the rename only; no os.fsync on the fd and no fsync of the parent directory; list_job_files' `.tmp` suffix filter (line 227) does correctly prevent an orphaned temp from being read as a job record.

title: The final room of EVERY non-completed run is recorded as "missed"; on a stranded run the documented retry automation re-dispatches the robot in an unbounded loop
area: STATE — incomplete-run / trouble-rooms / live-snapshot persisted states (learning/history_store.py + learning/services.py)
observed_behavior: `completed_room_ids` is only ever appended by a ROOM ROLLOVER, and both brands' rollovers structurally refuse to roll the last room: the Eufy/sequential path returns early at `jobs/active_job.py:970` (`if current_index >= len(unresolved_room_ids) - 1: return active_job`), and its counter-plateau branch carries the comment "expected_rooms caps boundaries at N-1, so this never rolls the final room"; the Roborock native path (`jobs/active_job.py:1238`) completes a room only when the device reports a DIFFERENT target, which never happens for the last one. The only compensation is `job_finalizer.py:752-761`, which synthesises `completed_room_ids = queued_ids` — but ONLY when `outcome_status == "completed"`. So for every cancelled / failed / interrupted / cancel-likely finalize, the last queued room is reported missed by construction. The stranded-run reaper (`listeners/pause_timeout.py:114-122` → `async_finalize_stranded_job`, `forced_outcome_status="interrupted"`) exists precisely for the case where the robot ALREADY finished and docked but no completion packet arrived (the documented Eufy MQTT push-only staleness) — the one case where the last room definitely WAS cleaned. That finalize writes `incomplete_run.json` naming it, and `listeners/_common.py:265-275` fires EVENT_RUN_INCOMPLETE from the same log. `handle_retry_missed_rooms` then accepts `log["missed_room_ids"]` with the single gate at line 689 (`if not log or not log.get("missed_room_ids")`) — no staleness check, no re-verification that the rooms are still dirty, no attempt counter, no loop guard — and calls `set_rooms_enabled_subset` + `build_queue` + `start_selected_rooms`. ARITHMETIC: queue [Kitchen=3, Hallway=5, Bedroom=7]. Rollovers fire for 3 and 5; the run strands. completed_room_ids=[3,5]; queued={3,5,7}; missed = {3,5,7}-{3,5} = [7]. The automation documented verbatim in this handler's own docstring (lines 657-668) fires retry_missed_rooms → the robot leaves the dock to re-clean the already-clean Bedroom. That retry is a SINGLE-room job, so NO rollover can fire at all: if it also strands (same firmware condition, same robot, same run shape), completed_room_ids=[], queued={7}, missed=[7] again → EVENT_RUN_INCOMPLETE fires again → the automation retries again. Nothing in the payload or the handler carries an attempt count, so the loop is unbounded.
user_impact: An unattended robot repeatedly leaves the dock to re-clean a room that is already clean, and each retry destroys the user's saved room selection (`set_rooms_enabled_subset` disables every other room on the map). Even without the automation, the card banner names an already-cleaned room as missed on every cancelled/interrupted run, and the one-click retry rewrites the user's selection to it.
guards_checked: `_write_incomplete_run_log` (job_finalizer.py:1496-1503) — only gates on outcome_status, never on whether the missed set is credible. The `outcome_status == "completed"` synthesis (job_finalizer.py:752-761) — deliberately NOT applied to interrupted, per its own comment ("we use the tracked state as-is"). `run_incomplete_event_data` (listeners/_common.py:267) — only checks the list is non-empty. `handle_retry_missed_rooms` line 689 — only checks the list is non-empty; `confirm_reduced_run` defaults to True so the reduced-run confirmation cannot block it. `poll_stranded_started_job`'s grace period delays but does not bound retries. `detect_run_anomalies`' `skipped_room_ids` (active_job.py:822-830) is a separate live signal and does not feed the incomplete log. No retry/attempt field exists anywhere in the incomplete_run payload (history_store.py:1541-1554 shows the full schema).

confirmations: Mechanism confirmed. jobs/active_job.py:970 is exactly `if current_index >= len(unresolved_room_ids) - 1: return active_job`, so the sequential rollover structurally cannot complete the last room, and the only compensation — job_finalizer.py:752-761 synthesising completed_room_ids from the queue — is gated on `outcome_status == "completed"`, with the comment explicitly declining to apply it to the other outcomes. _write_incomplete_run_log:1505-1520 then computes missed = queued - active_completed, and handle_retry_missed_rooms:689 gates only on the list being non-empty — no staleness check, no attempt counter, and I confirmed the incomplete_run payload schema (job_finalizer.py:1541-1554) carries no retry field. The single-room retry genuinely cannot roll over either (len 1 -> index 0 >= 0 -> immediate return). SEVERITY CORRECTED from CRITICAL: on a normal cancel the last room really was not cleaned, so the wrong-missed-room case is specifically the stranded-reaper path, and the 'unbounded loop' additionally requires the documented automation to be installed AND the retry to strand repeatedly. Robot-acts-wrongly under narrower-than-claimed conditions is HIGH here, not CRITICAL.

The structural half is fully confirmed. jobs/active_job.py:970 returns early when current_index >= len(unresolved_room_ids) - 1, so the sequential rollover cannot roll the final room, and the native Roborock path (:1238) completes a room only on a DIFFERENT reported target, which never arrives for the last. job_finalizer.py:752-761 synthesises completed_room_ids = queued_ids ONLY when outcome_status == 'completed', with a comment explicitly declining to do so for other outcomes. So for every cancelled/failed/interrupted finalize the last queued room is missed by construction - including the common case of cancelling during return-to-dock after the last room, and the stranded-run reaper case where the robot demonstrably finished. Arithmetic reproduces: queued {3,5,7}, rollovers for 3 and 5, missed = [7]. handle_retry_missed_rooms gates only on `if not log or not log.get('missed_room_ids')` at :689 - no staleness check, no re-verification, no attempt counter - and then calls set_rooms_enabled_subset + build_queue + start_selected_rooms. The single-room retry cannot roll over at all, so a repeat strand reproduces missed=[7] and re-fires EVENT_RUN_INCOMPLETE; I confirmed the incomplete_run payload (job_finalizer.py:1544-1556) carries no attempt field, so nothing bounds it. Holding CRITICAL: this drives a physical dispatch and destroys the saved room selection, and it makes the user act wrongly even without the automation - but note the fully unattended loop requires the automation documented in this handler's own docstring.

title: clear_incomplete_run's docstring claim "(full clean)" is false — ANY completed run erases the missed-room record, and it is unrecoverable because completed_room_ids is never persisted in the job archive
area: STATE — incomplete-run / trouble-rooms / live-snapshot persisted states (learning/history_store.py + learning/services.py)
observed_behavior: The docstring at lines 274-282 states it is "Called in two places: job_finalizer when a job completes without missed rooms (full clean)". Verified against the caller: `_write_incomplete_run_log` (job_finalizer.py:1499-1503) does `if outcome_status not in {"cancelled","failed","interrupted"}: self.store.clear_incomplete_run(...)`. That is ANY completed outcome, on ANY queue, of ANY size — there is no "full clean" test. Sequence: a 6-room whole-house run is cancelled after 2 rooms → incomplete_run.json records missed=[3 rooms]. The user then starts a 1-room Kitchen run; it completes; the log for the unrelated 4 missed rooms is unlinked. Nothing informs the user. Compounding this, `build_completed_job_payload` (this file, lines 1039-1119) writes `queue`, `outcome`, `room_timings` and `resolved_rooms` but NEVER writes `completed_room_ids` into the durable record — I checked the whole returned payload dict. `rebuild_all` reads only `jobs/*.json`, so once incomplete_run.json is gone the missed-room set for that job cannot be reconstructed by any rebuilder or service. user_impact: The user-facing "these rooms were missed" record — the only place the missed set exists — is silently and permanently destroyed by an unrelated later run, so rooms that were skipped are never retried and the user is never told.
guards_checked: `_write_incomplete_run_log`'s clear branch (job_finalizer.py:1499-1503) — no scope/room-overlap comparison against the existing log before clearing. `clear_incomplete_run`'s own body — no read-before-delete, no comparison, no logging on the success path (only a warning on unlink failure). `save_completed_job` / `build_completed_job_payload` — searched the full returned payload; `completed_room_ids` appears nowhere. `stats_rebuilder.rebuild_all` and `core/manager.async_rebuild_learning_accumulators` (manager.py:4509-4570) — neither reads nor rebuilds incomplete_run. confirmations: Confirmed. job_finalizer.py:1499-1503 is `if outcome_status not in {"cancelled","failed","interrupted"}: self.store.clear_incomplete_run(...)` — there is no full-clean test, no queue comparison and no room-overlap check, so any completed (or test) run of any size erases the log, contradicting clear_incomplete_run's own docstring at history_store.py:276-282. title: trouble_rooms.json is keyed by raw room_id and scoped per-vacuum, so its counters silently reattach to the wrong physical room after a re-segment or on a second map — the one id-keyed store reconcile-migrate forgets
area: STATE — incomplete-run / trouble-rooms / live-snapshot persisted states (learning/history_store.py + learning/services.py)
observed_behavior: `get_trouble_rooms_path` returns `live/trouble_rooms.json` — one file per VACUUM, no map component — and the payload is `{"rooms": {str(room_id): entry}}` (written at job_finalizer.py:1629-1655). Raw room_id is not stable identity anywhere else in this codebase: room_stats keys on `f"{map_id}::{slug}"` (`stats_rebuilder.py:67-69`), `save_access_graph_debug` (this file, line 357) is map-scoped, and `docs/dev/08-rooms-system.md:323` states "a re-segment renumbers many rooms at once". The migration path PROVES the repo knows this is a hazard: `rooms/room_crud.py:177-200` walks `plan["id_remap"]` and repairs every id-keyed durable store it knows about — it pops `room_rule_status` for BOTH old and new ids with the comment "a re-segment that frees an id ... would otherwise leave the dropped room's stale snapshot showing on the migrated room's sensor" — remaps confirmed floor types, and invalidates room_history. trouble_rooms.json is not in that list; nothing outside job_finalizer ever touches the file. ARITHMETIC: Kitchen=3 accrues miss_count=2, run_count=3 → miss_rate=round(2/3,3)=0.667, is_trouble = (2>=2 and 0.667>=0.33) = True. A re-segment renumbers Kitchen 3→4 and Hallway 5→3; the user confirms the migration. trouble_rooms.json still holds key "3" = {name:"Kitchen", miss_count:2, run_count:3, is_trouble:true}. The card reads `state.troubleRoomForRoom(normalizedRoom.id)` (src/renderers/rooms.js:1259) with the CURRENT map's id, so Hallway's tile renders "⚠ missed 2 of 3 runs (67%)". On the next finalize `entry["name"] = name_by_id.get(3)` = "Hallway", permanently relabelling Kitchen's misses onto Hallway. Recovery then needs 4 more clean Hallway runs (2/6=0.333 still >= 0.33; 2/7=0.286 clears). title: trouble_rooms is a raw-counter store with no rebuilder, no clear service and a denominator that only advances when the room is queued — the "decays on its own" justification for excluding it from repair does not hold
area: STATE — incomplete-run / trouble-rooms / live-snapshot persisted states (learning/history_store.py + learning/services.py)
observed_behavior: `core/manager.py:4528-4531` justifies leaving trouble_rooms out of `async_rebuild_learning_accumulators`: "It is a RATE over an always-incrementing denominator (is_trouble is recomputed on every finalize from miss_count / run_count), so a bad sample decays on its own within a few runs. Verified against the writer (job_finalizer.py:1629-1648): `run_count` is incremented ONLY inside `for room_id in queued_room_ids` — the denominator advances only when the room is in that run's queue. It is not "always-incrementing"; it is incrementing-while-queued. Once a room stops being queued the entry freezes at whatever rate it held. ARITHMETIC: Bedroom is missed on 3 consecutive whole-house runs (door shut) → miss_count=3, run_count=3, miss_rate=1.0, is_trouble=True. The user stops including Bedroom in runs (they clean it by hand, or via the vendor app — external/app-started runs graduate through `external_run.confirm_external_run`, which writes `jobs/ext-*.json` directly and never calls the finalizer, so they increment nothing). run_count stays 3 forever; the tile shows "⚠ missed 3 of 3 runs (100%)" permanently. Even for a room that IS re-queued, recovery is slow and unbounded from the user's side: from miss=2/run=2 it takes 5 further clean runs to fall under the 0.33 gate (2/6=0.333 still flags; 2/7=0.286 clears). There is no clear/reset/repair path: `exclude_learning_job` does not touch it, `rebuild_all` does not touch it, and `services.py:878-884` registers only `get_trouble_rooms_log` — no clear service exists. title: build_completed_job_payload's `queue` block prefers the LIVE queue over the job's own — a room switch flipped mid-run makes both the missed-rooms banner and trouble_rooms name a room that was never in the run

title: load_live_snapshot performs 4 mkdir syscalls plus an open()/read() on the Home Assistant event loop at every cold finalize
area: STATE — incomplete-run / trouble-rooms / live-snapshot persisted states (learning/history_store.py + learning/services.py)
observed_behavior: `get_live_snapshot_path` calls `ensure_dirs()` (line 148-155), which issues four `Path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` syscalls (jobs/, learned/, exports/, live/) before returning the path; `load_live_snapshot` then calls `read_json`, which does `path.exists()`, `path.is_file()` and `path.read_text()` — a real `open()`. The sole consumer is `_collect_finalization_inputs` (job_finalizer.py:455-459), whose cold path runs only when `_live_snapshot_cache` misses. In the production async path that function is called WITHOUT an executor: `learning/manager.py:762` invokes `self.finalizer._collect_finalization_inputs(...)` directly inside the coroutine, and only the subsequent `finalize_from_inputs` is wrapped in `async_add_executor_job` (773). So on the first finalize after every HA restart (cache empty, file present because it is never deleted — see STATE-8), the event loop blocks on 4 mkdirs plus a file read. That contradicts the docstring of the function performing it ("Does not perform heavy file I/O — only loads the tiny live snapshot from cache or disk") and the design intent stated in this file at lines 496-502 ("caching keeps that off disk"). The user's config directory is an SMB share (\\192.168.4.104\config), where each of those syscalls is a network round-trip, and HA's block_async_io patch on builtins.open will report the read as a blocking call. The repo already treats this class of defect as a bug — tests/integration/test_learning_services.py:1343 (`test_get_room_learning_estimates_cold_cache_no_blocking_reload`) exists specifically to assert a sibling loop path never block-reloads.
user_impact: The event loop stalls for the duration of a network filesystem mkdir×4 + read at the moment a job finishes, delaying every other entity update in Home Assistant, and HA logs a blocking-call warning.
