The card always forces re-analysis (src/bindings/map.js:1104 `analyzeMapImage(mapId, { force_reanalyze: true })`). Vertex-index reapplication confirmed at _adjust_polygon_pixel:740-748.

title: A failed or unavailable segmenter run overwrites the good cached segmentation with an empty available:False envelope and persists it
brands: Both. Eufy via engine_exception / missing optional CV libs; Roborock and any adapter without a registered segmenter engine hits it on the very first analyze call via noop_fallback.
observed_behavior: Line 1172-1175 does `result = await hass.async_add_executor_job(_run)` then unconditionally `map_bucket["image_segments"] = result` and `await manager.async_save()`. There is no check on `result.get("available")` and no rollback. The engine seam never raises: EufyCVSegmenter.segment_map_image wraps detect_room_segments in `except Exception` (segmenter_engines.py:280-291) and returns `_engine_unavailable(reason="engine_exception")`, and _engine_unavailable (segmenter_engines.py:429-440) returns a fully-formed dict with `available: False`, `image: None`, `segments: []`, `summary.segment_count: 0`. get_segmenter_engine(None) (segmenter_engines.py:391) also returns NoopSegmenter, which returns the same empty envelope for any adapter whose mapping block omits `segmenter_engine`. So every failure mode arrives as a well-formed EMPTY result that is written straight over the previously cached good segmentation and flushed to .storage.
reproduction: Eufy map with 9 cached CV segments plus links and adjustments. User uploads a replacement dark PNG; the card writes it to the SAME path (`map_<map_id>_dark.png`, line 896 — deterministic, no versioning, no backup) and then auto-calls analyze with force_reanalyze=true (src/bindings/map.js:1095-1104). detect_room_segments raises on the new image (or scipy/Pillow are absent — the integration declares requirements=[] and probes them at runtime via image_runtime_capabilities). The engine returns {available: False, reason: "engine_exception", segments: []}; line 1174 replaces the 9-segment store with it and line 1175 persists. Second path, no bad image needed: any adapter with no `segmenter_engine` declared (noop_fallback) — a single analyze_map_image call wipes image_segments to {segments: []} with reason "noop".
user_impact: All room polygons disappear from the map view (src/renderers/map.js:109 falls back to a placeholder when `!segmentsData.available`) and the cached segmentation is unrecoverable: the source PNG the segments were derived from was just overwritten at the same filename by the upload that triggered the analysis, so re-running analyze cannot reproduce the previous result. The user's `segment_room_links` and `image_segment_adjustments` survive as orphans and will be re-bound to whatever the next successful analysis produces (see IMAGE--1). The service returns the failure envelope, but the destruction has already been committed to .storage before the caller can react.
guards_checked: (a) `if not force_reanalyze and map_bucket.get("image_segments")` at 1100 — a cache-hit gate, not a write guard, and the card always passes force_reanalyze=true; (b) `if not image_path` at 1125 — the only pre-flight abort, and it returns before touching the bucket, which shows the write-guard shape was available and simply not applied to the engine result; (c) the executor call at 1172 — the engine's own try/except means no exception ever reaches this frame, so "an exception would have skipped the write" does not hold; (d) `_build_segments_response` at 1184 — read-side only; (e) manager.async_save() — persists whatever it is given, there is no prior snapshot.
doc_checked: docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md §2.12 ("Stored image_segments envelope") documents the success envelope and says _handle_analyze_map_image "then stamps analyzed_at"; it does not state that an unavailable result is also cached. docs/dev/03-data-model.md:150-157 calls image_segments "cached on the first analyze_map_image and treated as immutable from the UI" — an available:False overwrite contradicts that framing. docs/dev/22-adapter-config-reference.md:1125 describes the two call sites as consuming "the canonical SegmentationResult and cache it", again with no unavailable-result carve-out.

verdicts.reason: The engine seam genuinely never raises — both the CV engine's exception path and the noop engine return a fully-formed available:False envelope — and the handler assigns it over the cached segmentation and persists with no check on `available` and no snapshot. The 'an exception would have skipped the write' defence does not exist.
verdicts.evidence: mapping_services.py:1172-1175: result = await hass.async_add_executor_job(_run); result["analyzed_at"] = utc_now_iso(); map_bucket["image_segments"] = result; await manager.async_save() — no `if result.get("available")`. segmenter_engines.py:279-291: `try: raw = detect_room_segments(**kwargs) except Exception: _LOGGER.exception(...); return _engine_unavailable(engine=..., reason="engine_exception", ...)`. _engine_unavailable (segmenter_engines.py:416-440) returns {'available': False, 'reason': ..., 'image': None, 'segments': [], 'summary': {'segment_count': 0, ...}}. NoopSegmenter.segment_map_image (segmenter_engines.py:355-365) returns the same with reason 'noop'; get_segmenter_engine(None-or-unknown) (:386-403) returns it. adapters/roborock/adapter.py:482 declares "segmenter_engine": "noop_fallback". The only pre-flight abort is `if not image_path` at :1125, which returns before touching the bucket — proving the write-guard shape was available and not applied to the engine result.

verdicts.reason: Every engine failure arrives as a well-formed available:False envelope rather than an exception, and the handler writes it over the cached good segmentation and persists with no rollback or check.
verdicts.evidence: mapping_services.py:1172-1175 is unconditional: `result = await hass.async_add_executor_job(_run)` → `map_bucket["image_segments"] = result` → `await manager.async_save()`. No `result.get("available")` test exists in the handler. segmenter_engines.py:279-291: `try: raw = detect_room_segments(**kwargs) except Exception: _LOGGER.exception(...); return _engine_unavailable(engine=..., reason="engine_exception", ...)`, and _engine_unavailable (429-440) returns `{"available": False, "reason":..., "engine":..., "image": None, "segments": [], "summary": {"segment_count": 0, ...}, "engine_diagnostics": {...}}` — a complete dict, so the executor frame never sees an exception and the "an exception would have skipped the write" defence does not hold. get_segmenter_engine(None) returns NoopSegmenter (391-403). The image the segments came from was just overwritten at the same deterministic path (line 896, no versioning), so the prior result is unreproducible. Nuance: the finder's second path (Roborock/noop wiping on first analyze) requires an uploaded PNG to exist and prior CV segments to be present, which is unlikely on a noop_fallback adapter (adapters/roborock/adapter.py:482); the Eufy engine_exception / missing-optional-libs path is the solid one.

title: The analyze cache-hit gate tests truthiness, so a cached FAILURE envelope is served as a valid cache forever
observed_behavior: `if not force_reanalyze and map_bucket.get("image_segments"):` treats any non-empty dict as a valid cache. The failure envelope written by IMAGE--2 is a non-empty dict ({available: False, reason: ..., segments: [], summary: {...}}), so it is truthy and satisfies the gate. The gate never inspects `available`, `reason`, or `segments`. This is the codebase's documented 'absent is not zero / truthiness eats a legitimate state' pattern: 'no usable segmentation' and 'a valid cached segmentation' are indistinguishable here.
reproduction: scipy is missing at the time of the first analyze -> image_segments = {available: False, reason: "pipeline_unavailable", segments: []}. The user installs scipy and restarts HA. Any caller that invokes analyze_map_image without force_reanalyze (the default is False, ANALYZE_MAP_IMAGE_SCHEMA:355) — an automation, a script, Developer Tools, or any future card path — takes the cache branch at 1101 and returns the stale failure envelope with the old reason string. The segmenter is never retried; the only escape is knowing to pass force_reanalyze explicitly.
user_impact: Analysis appears permanently broken with a stale, now-incorrect reason ('you're missing scipy') after the cause has been fixed. The card is immune today because both of its call sites hard-code force_reanalyze:true, so this bites service/automation callers and any future UI path that trusts the documented default.

title: Re-uploading a map image does not invalidate image_segments, so a default analyze returns the previous image's segments
observed_behavior: _handle_upload_map_image's success block (926-958) writes the PNG, records/overwrites `image_variants[variant]`, optionally repoints a layout's backdrop/art variant, and saves. It never touches `image_segments`, `image_segment_adjustments`, or `segment_room_links`, and it stamps no marker that the analyzed image has changed. _handle_analyze_map_image's cache gate (1100) therefore still reports a hit for a segmentation computed from the REPLACED image, with the old `analyzed_at` and the old `image` dims.
reproduction: Call upload_map_image(map_id="5", variant="dark", image_base64=<new 1200x800 export>) — the file at eufy_vacuum/maps/<obj>/map_5_dark.png is overwritten and image_variants["dark"] now says 1200x800. Then call analyze_map_image(map_id="5") with no force_reanalyze (schema default False). Line 1100 returns the cached store from the OLD 600x400 image; get_map_segments then divides those polygons by the OLD store dims (1224-1226) and hands the card polygon_pct values describing rooms in an image that no longer exists on disk.
user_impact: An automation or script that uploads a refreshed map export and analyzes it gets the previous map's room geometry back with a success-shaped response and no staleness signal. The card path is immune (it always passes force_reanalyze:true), so this is an edge case confined to service callers — but the invalidation belongs on the write side, and its absence is exactly why the card had to hard-code the flag.
guards_checked: (a) the `if result["saved"]` block at 926 — updates only image_variants and layout pointers; (b) `analyzed_at` at 1173 — stamped only on a real run, so the stale response carries the old timestamp (detectable, but only by a caller that knows to compare); (c) _variant_path at 1109 — re-resolves the file path on a real run but is never reached on a cache hit; (d) no mtime/size/hash comparison between the stored envelope and the file.
doc_checked: docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md §6 / §6.1 describe upload_map_image as writing the PNG and recording variant metadata; docs/dev/03-data-model.md:604-620 (§3b) lists exactly the same effects. Neither doc claims upload invalidates the segmentation cache, and neither warns that it does not — the coupling is simply undocumented in both directions.

verdicts.reason: The upload success block writes only image_variants and (optionally) the layout art/backdrop pointers; image_segments, image_segment_adjustments and segment_room_links are untouched and no staleness marker is stamped. The truthiness cache gate then reports a hit for a segmentation computed from the replaced file.
verdicts.evidence: mapping_services.py:926-958 — the entire `if result["saved"]:` block: ensure_map_bucket, variants = map_bucket.setdefault("image_variants", {}), variants[variant] = {...}, then only the art_scope / layout_id branches writing layout['home_art']['art_variant'] / layout['rooms'][rid]['art_variant'] / layout['backdrop_variant'] and layout['updated_at'], then await manager.async_save(). No reference to image_segments in the function. Cache gate at :1100. get_map_segments divides by the stored envelope's own dims: :1224-1226 `store_img = raw.get("image") ...; img_w = store_img.get("width") or img_meta.get("width") or 1`.

verdicts.reason: The upload success block touches only image_variants and the layout's variant pointers; image_segments and its analyzed_at are left intact, so a default analyze after a replacement upload serves the previous image's geometry. Real, but the only shipped consumer bypasses it.
verdicts.evidence: mapping_services.py:926-958 — `variants[variant] = {variant, path, browser_url, width, height}`, then the art_scope branch writes home_art/rooms[*].art_variant, or the layout branch writes backdrop_variant, then `await manager.async_save()`. Grep of that block shows no reference to image_segments, image_segment_adjustments, segment_room_links, or any staleness marker. _handle_analyze_map_image:1100 therefore still reports a cache hit and returns the old envelope with the old `analyzed_at` and the old `image` dims; _handle_get_map_segments:1224-1226 then scales those polygons by `store_img.get("width")` from the stale store. Severity: the card is the only shipped caller and always passes force_reanalyze:true (src/bindings/map.js:1104), the stale read is non-destructive, and one explicit force_reanalyze fully repairs it — that is a LOW, not a MEDIUM.

title: Image filenames are built from an unsanitised free-form map_id, so one map's upload can silently overwrite another map's image
brands: Both; Roborock materially more exposed because get_active_map_id returns the user-authored map NAME verbatim.
observed_behavior: `suffix = "" if variant == "default" else f"_{variant}"` then `file_path = os.path.join(base_dir, f"map_{map_id}{suffix}.png")` (895-896), with `browser_url` built the same way (897) and _handle_delete_map_image reproducing the identical construction at 999-1000. `map_id` is `cv.string` — free-form, and on Roborock it is the map NAME reported verbatim by the active-map entity, so spaces and underscores are normal. The map_id and the variant are concatenated into one flat filename with an underscore separator and no escaping, quoting, length cap, or character filter. Storage keys stay distinct (ensure_map_bucket uses str(map_id) as a dict key), which is precisely why the collision is silent — the two buckets disagree with the filesystem, not with each other.
reproduction: Arithmetic on the name construction. Map A has map_id "Upstairs"; map B has map_id "Upstairs_dark" (a legal Roborock map name). upload_map_image(map_id="Upstairs", variant="dark") -> "map_Upstairs_dark.png". upload_map_image(map_id="Upstairs_dark", variant="default") -> "map_Upstairs_dark.png". Same path: the second upload overwrites the first map's dark segmenter input, and both buckets' image_variants records now advertise the same file with different recorded dims. delete_map_image(map_id="Upstairs", variant="dark") then removes map B's default backdrop while map B's bucket still lists it — after which analyze for map B either reports image_not_found or (if another variant exists) segments a different image than the one recorded. Second, cheaper failure: map_id "Main/2nd" makes file_path ".../map_Main/2nd.png", whose parent directory was never created (only base_dir is, line 900), so open(...,"wb") raises FileNotFoundError inside the executor and propagates out of the service — every other failure in this handler returns a structured {"saved": False, "reason": ...}, so the caller gets a traceback instead of a reason. On a POSIX host a map_id beginning "../" resolves outside base_dir entirely (components [.., maps, <obj>, "map_..", "..", "x.png"] collapse to .../maps/x.png), so the PNG lands outside the intended directory and delete_map_image will later os.remove that stored path.
user_impact: The user edits/uploads a backdrop for the map they named and it lands on a different map's file, with the storage records still claiming otherwise — a direct answer to 'does the edit land on the map it names?' being 'not guaranteed'. Requires an unfortunate but legal map name (a name ending in _dark/_light/_custom, or containing a path separator), so the common numeric-map_id Eufy path is unaffected; Roborock's name-as-map_id makes it reachable without any malicious intent.
guards_checked: (a) _image_variant (313-318) — constrains the VARIANT half of the filename only; there is no equivalent validator for map_id; (b) cv.string on map_id in all five schemas — type check only, no charset/normalisation; (c) ensure_map_bucket's str(map_id) keying — keeps STORAGE distinct, which is what makes the filesystem collision invisible; (d) os.makedirs(base_dir, exist_ok=True) at 900 — creates only the base dir, so a separator in map_id is a hard failure not a nested write; (e) no os.path.commonpath / basename / slugify anywhere in the module.
doc_checked: docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md §6.1 documents the path template `map_<map_id>[_<variant>].png` and explicitly claims "Variant names are normalised to lowercase, spaces and hyphens replaced by underscores" (line 517). No normalisation exists anywhere in the code — not for variants (the whitelist masks it) and not for map_id or the derived art keys `custom_<id>_room_<room_id>`, where a room id containing a space would produce a filename and a browser_url with a raw space. The doc's own examples assume a numeric map_id (map_6_dark.png).

verdicts.reason: The primary claim — that map_id and variant are concatenated into one flat filename with an underscore and no escaping, so map 'Upstairs' variant 'dark' and map 'Upstairs_dark' variant 'default' resolve to the identical path while their storage buckets stay distinct — is arithmetically exact and confirmed at both the write and delete sites. The documented normalisation does not exist. One sub-claim is REFUTED and should be struck before this reaches a fix: the POSIX '../' traversal does NOT resolve outside base_dir, because the first path component always carries the literal 'map_' prefix and POSIX resolves '..' only after resolving the preceding component, so the walk fails with ENOENT (I executed it; it raised FileNotFoundError). The separator case is therefore an unhandled OSError, not a write outside the directory.
verdicts.evidence: mapping_services.py:894-897 suffix = "" if variant == "default" else f"_{variant}"; file_path = os.path.join(base_dir, f"map_{map_id}{suffix}.png"); browser_url built identically at :897; _handle_delete_map_image reproduces it at :999-1000 (with entry.get("path") taking precedence). Collision arithmetic: ("Upstairs","dark") -> map_Upstairs_dark.png; ("Upstairs_dark","default") -> map_Upstairs_dark.png. Buckets stay distinct because ensure_map_bucket keys on str(map_id) (maps/map_manager.py:19). Roborock map_id is the free-text map NAME (adapters/roborock/adapter.py:190). Doc divergence confirmed: docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md:517 claims 'Variant names are normalised to lowercase, spaces and hyphens replaced by underscores' — grep for slugify|re.sub across mapping/ and maps/ returns only tracker.py:150 (unrelated). Traversal refutation: executed os.path.join(base, 'map_../../../../www/pwn.png') + open(...,'wb') -> FileNotFoundError [Errno 2]; os.path.normpath collapses lexically but open() does not.

verdicts.reason: The flat `map_{map_id}{_variant}.png` construction is genuinely ambiguous — two distinct map buckets can name the same file — and a map_id containing a separator produces an uncaught FileNotFoundError. The POSIX-traversal sub-claim in the reproduction is wrong, but it is not the finding's primary claim.
verdicts.evidence: Arithmetic on lines 895-897: map_id="Upstairs", variant="dark" → suffix "_dark" → "map_Upstairs_dark.png". map_id="Upstairs_dark", variant="default" → suffix "" → "map_Upstairs_dark.png". Identical path; ensure_map_bucket keys the two buckets separately by `str(map_id)` (maps/map_manager.py:17), so both records claim the same file with different recorded width/height, and _handle_delete_map_image:999-1000 reconstructs the same colliding path. `_image_variant` (313-318) constrains only the variant half; map_id is bare `cv.string` in all five schemas; no basename/slugify/commonpath call exists in the module (tracker.py:150 has the only re.sub in mapping-adjacent code). Separator case verified empirically: open() on `<base>/map_Main/2nd.png` raises FileNotFoundError because os.makedirs (line 900) creates only base_dir; the only try/except in _write_and_measure wraps the PIL measure (905-911), so the service raises instead of returning the {"saved": False, "reason": ...} shape. CORRECTION to the finding: the claim that a map_id beginning "../" "resolves outside base_dir entirely" is false on POSIX — I executed it and open() returns ENOENT because the literal `map_..` component does not exist; and the stated collapse target is off by one level (posixpath.normpath gives /config/eufy_vacuum/www/pwn.png, not /config/maps/x.png). Roborock exposure confirmed: adapters/roborock/adapter.py:190 documents active_map as the map NAME.

title: delete_map_image calls itself the mirror of upload but has no layout_id/art_scope sibling and sweeps no back-references
observed_behavior: The docstring at 965-974 calls this handler a "Mirror of _handle_upload_map_image". It is not. Upload is layout-aware in three ways: it accepts layout_id, derives the variant key (`custom_<layout_id>`, `custom_<id>_home_art`, `custom_<id>_room_<rid>`), verifies the layout exists before writing, and repoints `layout["backdrop_variant"]` / `layout["home_art"]["art_variant"]` / `layout["rooms"][rid]["art_variant"]` (846-875, 941-957). Delete accepts only (vacuum_entity_id, map_id, variant) — DELETE_MAP_IMAGE_SCHEMA:339-345 has no layout_id and no art_scope — and its whole mutation is `variants.pop(variant, None)` at 1014. No layout, art record, or `image_segments` reference to the removed variant is inspected or cleared. The reverse direction was implemented: _handle_delete_custom_layout (2392-2418) deliberately sweeps the layout's backdrop and art variants out of image_variants and off disk. Only this half of the pair is missing — the campaign's forgotten-override-sibling shape, with a permissive default (variant defaults to "default") making the omission silent.
reproduction: Create custom layout cl_A and upload its backdrop: upload_map_image(map_id="5", layout_id="cl_A", variant="custom") -> variant forced to "custom_cl_A", image_variants["custom_cl_A"] = {width: 1024, height: 768, ...}, layout.backdrop_variant = "custom_cl_A". Author segments against it. Now call delete_map_image(map_id="5", variant="custom_cl_A") — _image_variant accepts any custom_* key, so the schema permits it. Result: the PNG is gone and image_variants no longer has the key, but layout.backdrop_variant still reads "custom_cl_A". Next set_custom_segments for that layout does `backdrop = image_variants.get("custom_cl_A") or {}` -> `map_w = None` -> returns {"saved": False, "reason": "no_custom_backdrop"} (1669-1684) for a layout that still exists, still renders its previously authored polygons, and reports a backdrop_variant in the get_map_segments layouts_summary (1256). Same for home_art.art_variant / rooms[rid].art_variant, which no cleanup path other than layout deletion ever revisits.
user_impact: A layout survives its backdrop and becomes uneditable with a misleading reason ('no custom backdrop') while continuing to advertise one; get_map_segments silently substitutes the CV dark/default/light image metadata for the missing backdrop (1211-1217), so the layout's authored geometry is composed over a different picture than it was drawn on. Reachable only by a direct service call today (the card's variant list is dark/light/default only — src/renderers/map.js:76-80), which is why it rates MEDIUM rather than HIGH; the same asymmetry also means a per-layout backdrop or furnished-art PNG can never be removed through the card at all.
guards_checked: (a) `if not isinstance(entry, dict)` at 988 — only checks that the variant is recorded, never who references it; (b) _image_variant at 316 — actively ADMITS custom_* keys into the delete path, so the schema is not the guard; (c) the two-tap arm/confirm in the card (src/bindings/map.js:1129-1150) — a UI confirmation for the three CV variants only, absent for any service caller; (d) _handle_delete_custom_layout:2392-2418 — proves the reference sweep exists in the codebase, in the other direction only; (e) no reference count, no reverse index from variant -> layout.
doc_checked: docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md §6 line 510-511 documents that upload with layout_id/art_scope repoints backdrop_variant / home_art.art_variant / rooms[<rid>].art_variant; docs/dev/03-data-model.md:619-626 (§3b, 'Per-layout upload') documents the same repointing. Neither doc describes any delete-side counterpart. docs/dev/17-map-manager.md:358 states image_variants is "Written by upload_map_image, pruned by delete_map_image" — pruning the variant map is exactly all it does, so the doc is accurate about the mechanism and silent about the dangling reference it creates.

verdicts.reason: The asymmetry is exactly as described and the docstring's 'Mirror of _handle_upload_map_image' is falsified by the schemas: upload takes layout_id/art_scope/room_id and validates the layout before writing, delete takes none of them and its whole mutation is a variant pop. _image_variant actively admits custom_* keys into the delete path, so nothing stops a layout's backdrop being deleted out from under it. The reverse sweep exists in delete_custom_layout, proving the pattern was known.
verdicts.evidence: DELETE_MAP_IMAGE_SCHEMA mapping_services.py:339-345 — only vacuum_entity_id, map_id, variant (default "default"); no layout_id, no art_scope. Handler mutation is mapping_services.py:1014-1021: variants.pop(variant, None) then map_bucket["image_variants"] = variants (or {}). Upload's layout awareness at :846-875 (returns layout_not_found) and the repointing at :941-957. _image_variant:316 accepts `value.startswith("custom_")`. Downstream consequence confirmed: _handle_set_custom_segments:1668-1684 does `backdrop = (map_bucket.get("image_variants") or {}).get(variant) or {}` -> map_w None -> {"saved": False, "reason": "no_custom_backdrop"}, and _handle_get_map_segments:1211-1217 falls back through img_variants dark/default/light. The other half exists: _handle_delete_custom_layout:2392-2418 pops the backdrop variant plus every home_art / rooms[*] art_variant and os.removes their paths.

verdicts.reason: delete_map_image's schema has no layout_id/art_scope and its only mutation is a variant pop, while _image_variant explicitly admits custom_* keys — so a per-layout backdrop or art PNG can be deleted out from under a live layout that keeps advertising it. The reverse sweep exists on the layout-delete side, proving the asymmetry.
verdicts.evidence: DELETE_MAP_IMAGE_SCHEMA (339-345) = {vacuum_entity_id, map_id, variant} only. _handle_delete_map_image's whole mutation is `variants.pop(variant, None)` at 1014 plus the empty-dict normalisation; nothing scans custom_layouts. `_image_variant`:316 `value in ("default","dark","light","custom") or value.startswith("custom_")` — so variant="custom_cl_A" and "custom_cl_A_home_art" both pass the schema. Contrast _handle_upload_map_image:846-875 and 941-957, which require layout_id, return {"saved": False, "reason": "layout_not_found"} if it does not resolve, and repoint backdrop_variant / home_art.art_variant / rooms[rid].art_variant. Contrast _handle_delete_custom_layout:2392-2418, which explicitly pops the backdrop variant AND every home_art/rooms[*].art_variant and os.removes their files — the reference sweep exists in exactly one direction. After the delete, set_custom_segments line 1669 `backdrop = (map_bucket.get("image_variants") or {}).get("custom_cl_A") or {}` → map_w None → 1684 returns {"saved": False, "reason": "no_custom_backdrop"}, while get_map_segments:1256 still reports `backdrop_variant: "custom_cl_A"` in layouts_summary. Card reach is limited: src/bindings/map.js's delete-map-variant handler drives only the three CV variants.

title: delete_map_image drops the storage record and reports deleted:True even when the file removal failed, and analyze's filesystem probe then re-uses the orphan
observed_behavior: _remove_file (1002-1010) returns False on OSError after a warning log, and returns False on FileNotFoundError. The caller ignores the distinction: lines 1014-1022 pop the variant and save unconditionally, and the result at 1024-1031 reports `deleted: True` with the real outcome demoted to a secondary `file_removed` field. The card's caller checks only `result.deleted !== false` (src/bindings/map.js:1157-1161) and shows a success toast, so the failure is discarded end to end — the codebase's documented 'result-returning APIs whose failure is discarded' pattern. The orphaned PNG is then still live to the analyzer: _variant_path (1109-1113) falls back to `os.path.join(base_dir, f"map_{map_id}{suffix}.png")` whenever the variant is absent from image_variants, and 1118-1123 accepts it on `os.path.isfile`.
reproduction: delete_map_image(map_id="5", variant="dark") while map_5_dark.png cannot be unlinked (open handle / permission / read-only mount) -> os.remove raises PermissionError (an OSError) -> _remove_file returns False -> line 1014 still pops image_variants["dark"] and line 1022 persists. The card refetches segments, the IMAGE VARIANTS row for dark now renders 'not uploaded', and the user is toasted 'deleted'. The user then presses Analyse: _variant_path("dark") finds no variant record, rebuilds the conventional path, os.path.isfile returns True, and the segmenter re-analyzes the very image the user believed they deleted, stamping image_variant "dark" into the tuning and a fresh analyzed_at.
user_impact: The user is told a bad upload was removed, the UI agrees it is gone, and the segmenter keeps using it — the delete is neither honest nor effective. Also leaves an undeletable orphan: with no image_variants record, a second delete_map_image returns {"deleted": False, "reason": "not_found"} at 989 and never retries the unlink, so nothing in the integration can ever remove that file again. Requires the unlink to actually fail, which is uncommon on the usual Linux host, hence MEDIUM.
guards_checked: (a) `except FileNotFoundError: return False` at 1006 — deliberately makes the handler idempotent, and the docstring's 'safe to call multiple times' claim only covers that branch, not the OSError branch; (b) the `except OSError` warning log at 1008-1009 — logs and swallows; (c) the `file_removed` field in the response — present, and ignored by the only caller; (d) `remaining_variants` at 1030 — reports what the storage now says, not what is on disk; (e) analyze's `os.path.isfile` at 1120 — treats the filesystem as authoritative, which is the opposite of what the delete path assumed.
doc_checked: docs/dev/17-map-manager.md:358 says image_variants is "pruned by delete_map_image" — accurate for the storage half, silent on the file half. The handler docstring (965-975) states it "removes the PNG ... and drops the variant" and is "safe to call multiple times"; per rule 2 that is a claim, and the OSError branch falsifies the first half while leaving the second half (the storage pop) executed anyway. docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md §6.1 documents that the analyzer resolves images by the conventional path, confirming the orphan is reachable.

verdicts.reason: _remove_file returns False on OSError and the caller ignores the distinction, popping the variant and saving unconditionally while reporting deleted:True. The card checks only `deleted !== false`, so the failure is discarded end to end. The analyzer's filesystem probe then re-accepts the orphan, and a second delete returns not_found without retrying the unlink.
verdicts.evidence: mapping_services.py:1002-1022: `def _remove_file(): try: os.remove(file_path); return True; except FileNotFoundError: return False; except OSError as exc: _LOGGER.warning(...); return False` -> `file_removed = await hass.async_add_executor_job(_remove_file)` -> `variants.pop(variant, None)` ... `await manager.async_save()` with no branch on file_removed; result at :1024-1031 is {"deleted": True, "file_removed": file_removed, ...}. Card: src/bindings/map.js:1157-1161 `const ok = result && result.deleted !== false;` then a success toast. Orphan reachable: _variant_path (mapping_services.py:1109-1113) returns os.path.join(base_dir, f"map_{map_id}{suffix}.png") whenever the variant is absent from image_variants, and :1118-1123 accepts it on os.path.isfile. Second delete: :988-995 returns {"deleted": False, "reason": "not_found"} before reaching _remove_file.

verdicts.reason: The storage pop and the deleted:True response are unconditional on the unlink outcome, the real result is demoted to a secondary field the sole caller ignores, and the orphaned file remains reachable through analyze's filesystem fallback.
verdicts.evidence: _remove_file (1002-1010) returns False on both FileNotFoundError and OSError; the caller ignores the distinction — lines 1014-1022 pop and `await manager.async_save()` regardless, and 1024-1031 return `{"deleted": True, "file_removed": file_removed, ...}`. Caller verified: src/bindings/map.js:1157-1163 `const ok = result && result.deleted !== false;` → success toast; `file_removed` is never read anywhere in src/. Orphan reachability verified: _variant_path (1109-1113) `if v in variants and variants[v].get("path"): return ...` else rebuilds `os.path.join(base_dir, f"map_{map_id}{suffix}.png")`, and 1118-1123 accepts it on `os.path.isfile(p)` — so after the variant record is gone, analyze re-reads the file the user was told was deleted and stamps a fresh analyzed_at. A second delete_map_image returns {"deleted": False, "reason": "not_found"} at 989 without retrying the unlink, so nothing in the integration can remove it again. The docstring's "safe to call multiple times" covers only the FileNotFoundError branch.

title: min_area_pixels silently overrides the adapter's configured tuning because absent is coerced to 1200 before the is-not-None check
brands: Both; any adapter that tunes min_area_pixels away from 1200.
observed_behavior: The handler layers caller kwargs over the adapter's persisted `segmenter_tuning` (1147-1161). Three of the four knobs do this correctly: expected_room_count, max_segments and simplify_epsilon are read with a bare `call.data.get(...)` (1087-1090) and only written into `tuning` when not None, so an omitted field leaves the adapter's value standing. The fourth does not: `min_area_pixels: int = call.data.get("min_area_pixels", 1200)` at 1089 substitutes the literal 1200 for 'absent', after which `if min_area_pixels is not None` at 1152 is always true and `tuning["min_area_pixels"] = 1200` unconditionally clobbers whatever the adapter declared. ANALYZE_MAP_IMAGE_SCHEMA:353 deliberately gives this field NO voluptuous default (unlike the legacy GET_IMAGE_SEGMENT_SUGGESTIONS_SCHEMA:212, which does), so absence is representable at the schema layer and is discarded one line later. 1200 is also a hand-copied literal living in four places — here, segmenter_engines.py:273, adapters/eufy/adapter.py:600, and docs/dev/22-adapter-config-reference.md:1099.
reproduction: Adapter config declares mapping.segmenter_tuning = {"min_area_pixels": 400} (a documented knob for maps with small rooms). Call analyze_map_image(vacuum_entity_id=..., map_id="5") with no min_area_pixels. Line 1147 seeds tuning = {"min_area_pixels": 400}; line 1153 overwrites it with 1200; the engine receives 1200 (segmenter_engines.py:273) and every component between 400 and 1199 px is dropped as a tiny region. The adapter's configured value is unreachable from any caller that does not restate it, and no warning is logged.
user_impact: An adapter-level segmentation tuning knob that the adapter-config reference documents as configurable is silently inert for the omit-the-field case, so small rooms vanish from the segmentation with no diagnostic. Masked today because the only shipped adapter declares exactly 1200 — the bug is invisible until someone tunes it, which is precisely the forgotten-sibling shape (three knobs wired correctly, the fourth not, with a permissive default hiding it).
guards_checked: (a) `if min_area_pixels is not None` at 1152 — cannot fire, the .get default already removed the None; (b) EufyCVSegmenter.validate_tuning (segmenter_engines.py:218-226) — validates the value's type/range at registration, never that it survived to the engine; (c) segmenter_engines.py:273 `int(tuning.get("min_area_pixels", 1200))` — its own fallback would have handled the absent case correctly had the handler not injected one; (d) the sibling knobs at 1148/1150/1154 — inspected and correct, which is what isolates this line.
doc_checked: docs/dev/22-adapter-config-reference.md:1085-1125 documents segmenter_tuning as engine-owned knobs and states that _handle_analyze_map_image "layers caller kwargs over the adapter's segmenter_tuning" — min_area_pixels is not a caller kwarg here, so injecting it diverges from the documented precedence. The handler's own comment at 1136-1138 ("Tuning starts from the adapter's persisted defaults; call.data fields override them") makes the same claim and is falsified by the next 20 lines.

verdicts.reason: The line reads exactly as claimed and the is-not-None guard four dozen lines later is consequently dead. The three sibling knobs use a bare .get() and are correct, which isolates this one line, and the schema deliberately gives the field no voluptuous default so 'absent' was representable and was discarded. The handler's own comment about precedence is falsified by the next twenty lines.
verdicts.evidence: mapping_services.py:1089 `min_area_pixels: int = call.data.get("min_area_pixels", 1200)` versus the siblings at :1087 `expected_room_count = call.data.get("expected_room_count")`, :1088 `max_segments = call.data.get("max_segments")`, :1090 `simplify_epsilon = call.data.get("simplify_epsilon")`. Layering at :1147-1156: tuning = dict(adapter_tuning); `if expected_room_count is not None: ...`; `if max_segments is not None: ...`; `if min_area_pixels is not None: tuning["min_area_pixels"] = min_area_pixels` — always true. ANALYZE_MAP_IMAGE_SCHEMA:353 `vol.Optional("min_area_pixels"): vol.All(vol.Coerce(int), vol.Range(min=1))` — no default. The engine's own correct fallback exists at segmenter_engines.py:273 `int(tuning.get("min_area_pixels", 1200))`. Adapter declares the same literal at adapters/eufy/adapter.py:600 "min_area_pixels": 1200, which is what masks the bug today.

verdicts.reason: min_area_pixels is the one knob whose `.get` injects a literal default before the is-not-None test, so it unconditionally clobbers the adapter's persisted tuning. Confirmed, but the only shipped adapter declares exactly the injected value, so the runtime effect today is nil.

title: Upload persists width/height as None when Pillow is unavailable and still reports saved:True
brands: Both; depends on whether Pillow is importable on the host.
observed_behavior: _write_and_measure (899-922) measures the written PNG with Pillow and, on any exception (including ImportError), falls back to `declared_width`/`declared_height` from call.data. Those are Optional with no default (UPLOAD_MAP_IMAGE_SCHEMA:328-329) and the card never sends them — src/actions/map.js:231-243 forwards only {variant, layout_id, art_scope}. So with Pillow absent the record written at 934-940 is {"width": None, "height": None} and the handler still returns saved:True with no reason field. Pillow is an optional dependency by design here (manifest requirements are empty; segment_primitives.image_runtime_capabilities exists precisely to probe it).
reproduction: HA instance without Pillow. Upload a PNG backdrop for a custom layout: the bytes already start with the PNG magic so the conversion branch at 882-891 is skipped and the write succeeds; PIL.Image import fails at 906 so actual_width/height fall back to the absent declared values -> image_variants["custom_cl_A"] = {width: None, height: None}. set_custom_segments then evaluates `if not map_w or not map_h` (1673) as true for a backdrop that was uploaded successfully and, unless the caller separately supplies backdrop_width/height (src/actions/map.js:475 sends them only when the caller passes measured dims), returns {"saved": False, "reason": "no_custom_backdrop"}. The card's variant row also renders the raw values as "null × null" (src/renderers/map.js:1770).
user_impact: On a Pillow-less install a successful upload is recorded in a state that makes custom-segment authoring report a missing backdrop, and the variant row displays null dimensions. Confined to installs without Pillow, and the recorded dims are the only casualty (the PNG itself is correct), hence LOW.
guards_checked: (a) the try/except at 905-911 — deliberately degrades to declared dims, but nothing checks that declared dims exist; (b) the schema's Optional image_width/image_height — no defaults, no requirement that at least one source of dims be present; (c) `if result["saved"]` at 926 — saved is hard-coded True in _write_and_measure and never reflects the measurement outcome; (d) set_custom_segments' `no_custom_backdrop` return (1684) — catches it downstream with a reason that names the wrong cause.
doc_checked: docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md §6 line 510 states the recorded image_width/image_height "define the pixel space set_custom_segments rasterises that layout's authored polygons against"; docs/dev/03-data-model.md:604-618 (§3b) describes the VariantRecord as carrying width/height. Neither doc contemplates a record with null dims, and §2.11 documents Pillow as an optional, probed dependency — so the two statements are in tension.

verdicts.reason: The measurement fallback is to declared_width/declared_height, which have no schema default and which the card never sends — so with Pillow absent the recorded variant is {width: None, height: None} and saved is a hard-coded True. The downstream consequence names the wrong cause.
verdicts.evidence: mapping_services.py:899-922 _write_and_measure: `try: from PIL import Image as _PILImage; with _PILImage.open(file_path) as img: actual_width, actual_height = img.size; except Exception: actual_width = declared_width; actual_height = declared_height` and the returned dict hard-codes "saved": True. UPLOAD_MAP_IMAGE_SCHEMA:328-329 `vol.Optional("image_width"): vol.Coerce(int)` / image_height — no defaults. Card never supplies them: src/actions/map.js:231-244 uploadMapImage builds {vacuum_entity_id, map_id, image_base64, ...options}; both call sites pass only variant/layout_id/art_scope (src/bindings/map.js:1090-1095 `const opts = { variant }; ... opts.layout_id = lid;` and :2230-2234 {variant, layout_id, art_scope}). Record written at :933-940 with "width": result["actual_width"]. Downstream: :1673 `if not map_w or not map_h:` -> :1684 {"saved": False, "reason": "no_custom_backdrop"}.

verdicts.reason: With Pillow absent the measurement falls back to declared dims that no card path ever sends, so a successful upload records width/height None and still returns saved:True. Confirmed from source; whether Pillow is importable on a given host is not a source question.
verdicts.evidence: _write_and_measure (899-922): `try: from PIL import Image as _PILImage; with _PILImage.open(file_path) as img: actual_width, actual_height = img.size; except Exception: actual_width = declared_width; actual_height = declared_height` — the except catches ImportError, and `"saved": True` is a hard-coded literal in the returned dict, never reflecting the measurement. UPLOAD_MAP_IMAGE_SCHEMA:328-329 declares image_width/image_height as bare `vol.Optional` with no defaults. Card verified: src/actions/map.js:231-243 `uploadMapImage(mapId, imageBase64, options)` spreads only what callers pass, and both call sites — src/bindings/map.js:1095 (`opts = { variant }` plus optional layout_id) and 2230 ({variant, layout_id, art_scope}) — send no dimensions. So image_variants[variant] = {width: None, height: None}, and set_custom_segments:1673 `if not map_w or not map_h` then returns {"saved": False, "reason": "no_custom_backdrop"} for a backdrop that uploaded fine. manifest.json requirements=[] and segment_primitives.image_runtime_capabilities confirm Pillow is an optional, probed dependency.

title: Layout existence is validated before the executor write and re-checked afterwards only by a silent isinstance guard, so a concurrent layout delete orphans the upload
observed_behavior: For the layout-scoped branches the handler validates the layout at 863/874 (returning layout_not_found), then awaits the executor file write at 924 — a real suspension point in the single event loop, and a slow one for a multi-megabyte PNG. After resuming it re-fetches the layout at 945/954 and guards with `if isinstance(layout, dict)`, which silently skips the repointing when the layout has since disappeared. The file has already been written and image_variants[variant] is recorded unconditionally at 933-940, and the handler still returns saved:True with no indication that the layout link was not made.
reproduction: upload_map_image(map_id="5", layout_id="cl_A", art_scope="home") begins; while the executor writes the PNG, delete_custom_layout(layout_id="cl_A") runs on the loop and pops the layout plus its known art variants (2412-2420) — it cannot know about the art variant still in flight. The upload resumes: `layout` is None, the isinstance guard skips, image_variants["custom_cl_A_home_art"] is written and saved, and the PNG stays on disk. Result: a variant record and file referencing a layout that no longer exists, with the service reporting success. Nothing can clean it up — delete_custom_layout for cl_A already ran, and the card's delete UI covers only dark/light/default (IMAGE--6).
user_impact: A leaked PNG plus a phantom image_variants entry, and an upload the user believes attached to their layout that attached to nothing. Requires two service calls to overlap across a single await, so it is rare in practice; the missing part is that the post-await re-check has no failure reason and the earlier validation is never re-honoured.
guards_checked: (a) the pre-write layout_not_found checks at 849-875 — validated before the await, and the code correctly does not trust them afterwards; (b) `if isinstance(layout, dict)` at 946/955 — the re-check exists but its else branch is silence rather than a reason or a rollback of the just-written file; (c) delete_custom_layout's variant sweep (2392-2418) — runs before the in-flight variant is recorded, so it cannot cover it; (d) HA's single event loop — the interleaving here is genuinely across an await (async_add_executor_job), not two coroutines inside a synchronous block, so this is not a same-block false positive.
doc_checked: docs/dev/03-data-model.md:619-626 (§3b, 'Per-layout upload') documents the sequence as validate -> write PNG -> repoint backdrop_variant, i.e. the validation is described as governing the whole operation. docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md §6 line 510-511 describes the same contract. Neither doc addresses concurrency, so this is a gap rather than a divergence.

verdicts.reason: This is a genuine gap ACROSS an await, not an intra-block interleaving fantasy: the layout is validated before hass.async_add_executor_job and re-fetched after it, and the post-await re-check is a silent isinstance guard with no failure reason and no rollback of the file that was already written. The variant record is written unconditionally and saved:True is returned regardless.
verdicts.evidence: mapping_services.py:849-875 pre-write validation returning {"saved": False, "reason": "layout_not_found"}; :924 `result = await hass.async_add_executor_job(_write_and_measure)` — the suspension point; :933-940 variants[variant] = {...} written unconditionally; :945-946 and :954-955 `layout = (map_bucket.get("custom_layouts") or {}).get(layout_id)` / `if isinstance(layout, dict):` with no else. The concurrent deleter exists and cannot see the in-flight variant: _handle_delete_custom_layout:2392-2420 sweeps only the art variants already recorded on the layout. Result is returned at :959 as the same dict carrying "saved": True.

verdicts.reason: The layout is validated before a genuine await (the executor file write) and re-checked afterwards only by a silent isinstance guard, while the variant record and the file are written unconditionally and the response still says saved:True. The gap is across an await, not inside a synchronous block.
verdicts.evidence: mapping_services.py:846-875 validate and return {"saved": False, "reason": "layout_not_found"}; line 924 `result = await hass.async_add_executor_job(_write_and_measure)` is the suspension point (PNG write, up to a few MB); lines 933-940 write `variants[variant] = {...}` unconditionally; lines 945-957 re-fetch the layout and guard with `if isinstance(layout, dict):` whose else branch is silence — no reason, no rollback of the just-written file. _handle_delete_custom_layout:2412-2420 pops the layout and sweeps only the art variants it can see, so an in-flight variant is invisible to it. The response is the `result` dict with saved:True and no indication that the repoint did not happen. Card delete UI covers dark/light/default only, so the leaked custom_* PNG cannot be removed through the UI (see IMAGE--6). Requires two overlapping service calls, hence genuinely rare.

title: Four of the five services in this block have no services.yaml description, including the destructive delete_map_image
observed_behavior: All five handlers are registered with schemas and supports_response=True (2814-2833), but services.yaml declares only set_segmentation_mode (line 2419). upload_map_image, delete_map_image, analyze_map_image, get_map_segments and adjust_map_segment have no top-level entry at all, while their siblings registered in the same block (set_segment_room_link:2385, set_segmentation_mode:2419, set_custom_segments:2449, the whole saved-zone family:2773-2923) do. title: set_custom_segments is a REPLACE-ALL write that cannot name its target layout — it lands on whatever layout is active at call time, destroying another layout's authored geometry
brands: Both (Eufy + Roborock) — custom layouts are brand-independent map-bucket state.
observed_behavior: _handle_set_custom_segments takes only (vacuum_entity_id, map_id, segments[, backdrop_width/height]) — SET_CUSTOM_SEGMENTS_SCHEMA (line 378-397) and services.yaml both have NO layout_id field. The target is resolved server-side from global state at line 1667 (`layout = _ensure_default_layout(map_bucket)` -> `_active_custom_layout` -> `map_bucket['active_custom_layout_id']`), then line 1710 does `layout['custom_segments'] = {...}` — a full replace of that layout's authored polygons with no merge, no confirmation, no undo, and no prior-value capture. The card's compose-save (src/bindings/map.js:1382-1421) then loops `set_segment_room_link(mapId, seg.id, ...)` once per segment — also layout-less, also resolved through _resolve_active_scope at call time. Contrast the sibling writer _handle_upload_map_image (line 849-875), which REQUIRES layout_id and returns {'saved': false, 'reason': 'layout_not_found'} if it does not resolve: the identity guard exists in this file, but only on the non-destructive path.
reproduction: Two card instances on the same map (wall tablet + phone — normal HA usage). (1) Tablet is in custom mode on layout 'Upstairs' (active), user composes 6 shapes. (2) Phone user taps the layout picker for 'Downstairs' -> set_active_custom_layout -> map_bucket['active_custom_layout_id'] = downstairs_id. (3) Tablet taps Save. set_custom_segments resolves the active layout = Downstairs and overwrites Downstairs' custom_segments with the 6 Upstairs shapes; the following set_segment_room_link loop writes Upstairs' room links into Downstairs' links dict (and its 1:1 rule at line 1843-1846 POPS Downstairs' own links for each colliding room). Result: 'Upstairs' unchanged (the user believes it saved), 'Downstairs' authored geometry gone. Single-client variant: the Save button is disabled while busy (src/renderers/map.js:1527) but the layout-picker buttons are NOT — tapping another layout during the multi-await save (set_custom_segments, then N awaited set_segment_room_link calls, each awaiting manager.async_save()) splits one save across two layouts. That is a gap ACROSS awaits inside a single HA event loop, not an interleaving fantasy.
user_impact: Silent, unrecoverable loss of hand-authored map geometry plus its room links. The layout the user was editing is left untouched and the one they were not looking at is destroyed; the service returns {'saved': True, 'segment_count': N} either way, so nothing surfaces. Requires either two clients or an in-flight layout switch — the single-client, single-tab path is fine.
guards_checked: _ensure_default_layout (line 1596) — guarantees SOME layout exists, never that it is the intended one; the card's _composeLoadedFor/_composeKey (src/state/map.js:1418) — client-side only, keyed on the LAST fetched active_custom_layout_id, never re-validated before saving and never sent to the server; _handle_upload_map_image's layout_not_found validation — present, but only on the upload path; manager.async_save() — persists, no optimistic-concurrency token or version check anywhere in the bucket; the `if not res?.saved` check in the card binding — only catches no_custom_backdrop, not wrong-target.
doc_checked: docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md §10.2 + §10.4 ('rebuilds the **active layout's** custom_segments store from scratch each call (replace-all)') and docs/dev/03-data-model.md 'The active-scope seam' ('set_custom_segments targets the active layout'). The docs calmly DESCRIBE active-layout targeting; neither states that the client is unable to name the layout, and neither reconciles it with §10.3, which requires layout_id on the far less destructive upload path. services.yaml:2449-2457 is additionally stale — it says the call 'Rebuilds the map's custom segment set' (no mention of layouts at all) and 'Requires a custom backdrop image', which the live-dims path at line 1673-1682 has superseded.

verdicts.reason: The schema and the published contract both lack layout_id, the target is resolved from map-bucket global state at call time, and the write is a full replace with no merge, no prior-value capture and no concurrency token. The identity guard exists in the same file on the non-destructive upload path, which is the asymmetry the finding names. The in-flight-switch variant is a real gap across awaits (set_custom_segments, then N awaited set_segment_room_link calls each awaiting async_save).
verdicts.evidence: SET_CUSTOM_SEGMENTS_SCHEMA mapping_services.py:378-397 — vacuum_entity_id, map_id, segments, backdrop_width, backdrop_height; no layout_id. services.yaml set_custom_segments (2449-2478) declares vacuum_entity_id, map_id, segments only. Handler: :1666-1667 `_migrate_custom_layouts(map_bucket); layout = _ensure_default_layout(map_bucket)` -> _ensure_default_layout:1594-1600 -> _active_custom_layout:1477-1482 reading map_bucket['active_custom_layout_id']; :1710 `layout["custom_segments"] = {..."segments": built...}` — replace-all. title: In custom mode with no resolvable layout, _resolve_active_scope hands writers THROWAWAY dicts — set_companion_anchor / set_segment_room_link mutate a garbage-collected object and report saved: True
brands: Both (Eufy + Roborock). The card path additionally needs a live map source present (mss.present) for the dock-mascot fallback, which is the normal Eufy fork configuration.
observed_behavior: _resolve_active_scope's no-layout branch (lines 1550-1554) returns freshly-constructed `{}` literals for segments_store/links/anchors. They are not reachable from manager.data. _handle_set_companion_anchor (line 1890) binds `anchors = _resolve_active_scope(map_bucket)['anchors']`, writes `anchors[room_id] = {...}`, calls `await manager.async_save()` (which serialises manager.data — the anchor is not in it), and returns `{'saved': True, 'action': 'set', 'companion_anchors': {<the anchor>}}`. _handle_set_segment_room_link (line 1834) does the same for links. The third writer through the same seam, _handle_set_custom_segments, DOES call _ensure_default_layout first (line 1667) — the guard exists and was wired into one of the three siblings.
reproduction: Reachable from the shipped card with no scripting. (1) A map with zero custom layouts. (2) User taps the Custom toggle: src/bindings/map.js:1228 -> set_segmentation_mode(mode='custom'). _handle_set_segmentation_mode line 1342-1345 soft-selects a layout only `if layouts:` — with `custom_layouts == {}` the branch is skipped, so the bucket is left at segmentation_mode='custom', active_custom_layout_id=None. (3) get_map_segments now serves segments=[] and companion_anchors={}. (4) The vacuum is docked, so the renderer falls through `if (!targetSeg) return this._mapAnimalDeviceFallback(...)` (src/renderers/map.js:1008) and draws the mascot with anchorKey='dock' — draggable. (5) User drags the mascot to park it. src/bindings/map.js:1944 optimistically updates local state and fires set_companion_anchor(mapId, 'dock', x, y), ignoring the response. Server writes into the throwaway dict, saves nothing, answers saved: True.
user_impact: The mascot visibly stays where the user parked it for the rest of the session (the card never refetches after an anchor write) and silently snaps back on the next page load — repeatedly, with no error and no way for the user to tell the write failed. The same hole applies to set_segment_room_link for any script/automation caller. This is a result-returning API whose failure is not merely discarded but actively reported as success.
guards_checked: _ensure_default_layout (line 1596) — the fix, wired into set_custom_segments only, absent from both other writers; _handle_set_segmentation_mode's soft-select (line 1342-1345) — gated on `if layouts:`, so it does not cover the zero-layout case that creates the state; _handle_delete_custom_layout's reassign-or-flip-to-cv (line 2422-2432) — covers deleting the last layout but not a map that never had one; _migrate_custom_layouts — seeds custom_layouts={} + active=None and returns, which is exactly the vulnerable state; the card's `if (!res?.saved)` check exists on compose-save but not on the anchor/link calls.
doc_checked: docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md §10.2 states 'When no layout resolves, empty **read-only** stores are returned' — the author knew these dicts were not writable, yet two of the three writers that consume the seam mutate them and report success. docs/dev/03-data-model.md 'AnchorRecord' documents the dock anchor as persisted per-scope. Code/doc divergence either way: the doc says read-only, the code lets writers write.

verdicts.reason: _resolve_active_scope's no-layout branch returns freshly-constructed literals unreachable from manager.data, and two of the three writers through that seam mutate them and return saved:True. The third writer calls _ensure_default_layout, proving the fix exists and was wired into exactly one sibling. The state is reachable from the shipped card: the Custom toggle calls set_segmentation_mode directly, whose soft-select is gated on `if layouts:` and therefore does nothing when a map has zero layouts.
verdicts.evidence: mapping_services.py:1550-1554: `return {"mode": "custom", "layout_id": None, "segments_store": {}, "links": {}, "anchors": {}, "backdrop_variant": None}`. _handle_set_companion_anchor:1890 `anchors: dict = _resolve_active_scope(map_bucket)["anchors"]` then :1900 `anchors[room_id] = {...}`, :1903 await manager.async_save(), :1908-1913 return {"saved": True, ..., "companion_anchors": dict(anchors)}. _handle_set_segment_room_link:1834 does the same with links. _handle_set_custom_segments:1667 calls _ensure_default_layout first. State creation: _handle_set_segmentation_mode:1336-1345 `map_bucket["segmentation_mode"] = mode` then `if mode == "custom" and not _active_custom_layout(...): layouts = ...; if layouts: map_bucket["active_custom_layout_id"] = sorted(layouts)[0]`. _migrate_custom_layouts:1487-1489 seeds custom_layouts={} + active_custom_layout_id=None.
