title: _backfill_saved_zone_area fails OPEN on an indeterminate active map and permanently persists area_m2 / room_number computed from the WRONG map's raster — the poisoned value never self-heals
brands: Eufy only — on Roborock async_get_map_data_dict returns None early (map_source_coordinator.py:683), so nothing is written.
observed_behavior: Line 1449: `if not (active_map_id is None or str(active_map_id) == str(map_id)): return False` — i.e. an indeterminate active map PROCEEDS ('Indeterminate active map -> attempt'). It then calls `manager.async_get_map_data_dict(vacuum_entity_id=...)`, which returns the fork's currently-cached map_data for whatever map is loaded, with no map-identity field to cross-check against map_id. The derived area_m2 / room_number are written onto the zone (lines 1466-1469) and the caller persists them (line 1276-1279). Crucially, the `pending` filter is `z.get('area_m2') is None` (line 1434-1437), so once a wrong value is written the zone leaves the pending set FOREVER — there is no re-validation when the correct map later becomes active. get_active_map_id returns None on a blank/unavailable/unknown active-map entity and during the boot window (rooms/room_discovery.py:69-84), so 'indeterminate' is a routine transient state, not an exotic one.
reproduction: Multi-floor Eufy household. Zone 'Under the dining table' was drawn on map B while map A was loaded, so create's identical guard left area_m2=None (this is precisely the population the backfill exists to repair). HA restarts (or the vacuum drops to unavailable) -> the active-map entity is blank -> get_active_map_id returns None. The user opens the card on map B; get_map_segments -> _backfill_saved_zone_area -> guard passes (active_map_id is None) -> async_get_map_data_dict returns map A's raster. Arithmetic, using zone_membership's own formula (area = Δnx*Δny*width*height*res²/10000): zone bbox Δnx=Δny=0.10. Map A width=800 height=600 res=5 -> 0.10*800*5 = 400 cm by 0.10*600*5 = 300 cm -> 12.0 m². Map B (the zone's real map) width=400 height=300 res=5 -> 200 cm by 150 cm -> 3.0 m². The zone is stamped 12.0 m² — 4x too large — plus a room_number taken from map A's room-id raster (Eufy room ids 1-11 are per-map, so 'room 3' on A is a different physical room from 'room 3' on B). manager.async_save() persists it, and because area_m2 is now non-None the zone is never re-examined.
user_impact: Permanently wrong zone size shown in the card, a zone filed under the wrong room in the browse list (grouped by room_number per docs/dev/frontend/saved-zones.md), and a wrong area feeding the learning/duration-estimate path — which this function's own docstring claims it exists to make reliable. Irreversible from the UI: nothing recomputes area_m2 once set, so the only repair is editing .storage by hand. The single-map household is unaffected (the loaded map IS the zone's map); it needs 2+ maps plus a blank active-map entity at read time.
guards_checked: The active-map guard at line 1449 itself — present, but the `active_map_id is None` arm inverts it; get_active_map_id's own sentinel handling (rooms/room_discovery.py:69) — it returns None precisely when it cannot tell, which is the arm that fails open; the create-time guard at line 2503 — identical shape, same fail-open, so the two paths agree on the wrong answer rather than one rescuing the other; map_data carries no map-id field to cross-check, and async_get_map_data_dict (map_source_coordinator.py:665) takes only vacuum_entity_id, so the callee cannot help; zone_membership is defensive but has no way to know which map it was handed; there is no re-heal path because `pending` keys on area_m2 being None.
doc_checked: docs/dev/frontend/saved-zones.md §4 + lines 57-59 (area_m2 'computed from map dims at author time (display + validation)', room_number 'auto-set at author by >=90% dominance'); map_source.zone_membership's own docstring ('Roborock has no per-pixel raster... area_m2 needs the Eufy width/height/resolution dims'); docs/dev/10-learning-system.md:632 (zone area feeds the estimate). No doc states or defends 'when the active map is unknown, size the zone against whatever raster is loaded' — the inline comment asserts the guard 'mirrors create's guard', which is true but is a claim about consistency, not about correctness.

verdicts.reason: The guard's None arm is permissive exactly as described, the map-data accessor takes no map_id so it cannot honour the caller's target, and the pending filter keys on area_m2 being None so a wrong value written once is never revisited. get_active_map_id returning None is a routine transient (sentinel state, or registered-but-no-state boot window), not an exotic case. The Eufy-only brand scoping is right.
verdicts.evidence: mapping_services.py:1445-1452: `if not (active_map_id is None or str(active_map_id) == str(map_id)): return False` with the comment 'Indeterminate active map -> attempt', then `map_data = await manager.async_get_map_data_dict(vacuum_entity_id=vacuum_entity_id)`. Pending filter at :1434-1437: `[z for z in zones.values() if isinstance(z, dict) and z.get("area_m2") is None]`. Writes at :1465-1469 zone["area_m2"] = area / zone["room_number"] = ...; caller persists at :1265-1268. async_get_map_data_dict (mapping/map_source_coordinator.py:665-667) signature is (*, vacuum_entity_id) only — no map identity in or out. get_active_map_id (rooms/room_discovery.py:69-84) returns None on is_blank_state and on registered-but-not-materialised. Brand scoping confirmed at map_source_coordinator.py:683-684: returns None unless map_state_source.backend == "storage" (Eufy).

verdicts.reason: The active-map guard's `active_map_id is None` arm proceeds, and async_get_map_data_dict takes no map_id, so the backfill sizes and files a zone against whatever raster is currently loaded. The `pending` filter keys on area_m2 being None, so the wrong value is never revisited. Severity corrected for parity with the identical create-time defect (A6-ZONE-C-4).
verdicts.evidence: mapping_services.py:1449 `if not (active_map_id is None or str(active_map_id) == str(map_id)): return False` — the None arm falls through, with the comment "Indeterminate active map -> attempt". rooms/room_discovery.py:43-84 returns None for any BLANK_STATE_VALUES state and for a registered-but-stateless entity (boot window). map_source_coordinator.py:665-667 `async_get_map_data_dict(self, *, vacuum_entity_id: str)` — no map_id parameter; returns the current map's dict. Pending filter at 1434-1437 is `z.get("area_m2") is None`, so once written the zone is permanently excluded. Arithmetic against the shipped formula (map_source.zone_membership:360-363 `dx_cm=(bx1-bx0)*width*res; dy_cm=(by1-by0)*height*res; area_m2=round(dx_cm*dy_cm/10000,1)`): Δnx=Δny=0.10, map A 800x600 @res 5 → 0.10*800*5=400 cm by 0.10*600*5=300 cm → 400*300/10000 = 12.0 m²; map B 400x300 @res 5 → 200 cm by 150 cm → 3.0 m². 4x wrong, persisted at 1466-1469 and saved by the caller at 1276-1279. Roborock is immune: map_source_coordinator.py:683 returns None for any non-"storage" backend. Correcting HIGH→MEDIUM: this is a wrong advisory record (size label, filing bucket, ETA input) — it never reaches the device and never alters the zone's geometry, and it is the same fail-open guard the finder's own A6-ZONE-C-4 rates MEDIUM at the create site.

title: _backfill_saved_zone_area overwrites a user's explicit 'Unassigned' filing — room_number=None means both 'never computed' and 'user chose Unassigned', and the read path cannot tell them apart
brands: Eufy only — zone_membership returns room_number=None on Roborock (no per-pixel raster), so the `membership.get('room_number') is not None` arm never fires there.
observed_behavior: Line 1467-1468: `if zone.get('room_number') is None and membership.get('room_number') is not None: zone['room_number'] = membership.get('room_number')`. The sentinel for 'not yet computed' is the same value the user's own override writes: _handle_set_saved_zone_room (line 2573) sets `zone['room_number'] = room_number` where SET_SAVED_ZONE_ROOM_SCHEMA (line 476-484) makes null an explicit, documented choice meaning Unassigned. There is no `filed_by`/`room_number_source` flag, no separate 'computed' key, and no boolean to distinguish the two states — classic absent-is-not-a-value conflation.
reproduction: (1) Zone created while a different map was loaded, or with no map data available -> area_m2=None, room_number=None. (2) User opens the zone panel and files it under 'Kitchen' (set_saved_zone_room room_number=5). area_m2 is still None, so the zone stays in `pending`. (3) User changes their mind and picks Unassigned (set_saved_zone_room room_number=null) -> room_number=None, persisted, exactly as documented. (4) The zone's map later becomes active and the user opens the card. _backfill_saved_zone_area sees area_m2 is None -> computes membership -> sets area_m2 AND, because room_number is None, re-files the zone under the >=90%-dominant room. The user's deliberate Unassigned is gone, on a READ, with no service call from them.
user_impact: A saved zone silently jumps out of the Unassigned section into a room section the user explicitly moved it out of. Filing only — docs are explicit that room_number never affects dispatch, so no wrong physical clean. Narrow: only bites zones that reached the user-editing stage while still unsized (i.e. authored off-active-map or with no map data). Once a zone has an area_m2 it is out of `pending` and immune.
guards_checked: The `zone.get('room_number') is None` test at line 1467 — it IS the bug, not a guard; the `pending` filter (line 1434) — narrows the population but does not exclude user-edited zones, because a user can file/unfile a zone whose area_m2 is still None; _handle_set_saved_zone_room (line 2557-2576) — writes room_number and bumps updated_at but records no provenance the backfill could consult; nothing in _create_saved_zone (line 1396-1417) distinguishes a computed None from a chosen None either.
doc_checked: docs/dev/frontend/saved-zones.md lines 57-59 ('room_number ... auto-set at author by >=90% dominance, else None ("Unassigned"); user-editable'), line 102 ('room_number is user-settable any time (a room picker; None = Unassigned)') and line 115-116 (set_saved_zone_room, 'null = Unassigned'). The doc states the user override as a first-class, persistent choice; it never says a later read may reverse it.

verdicts.reason: room_number=None is genuinely overloaded: it is the mint-time 'not computed' sentinel and the value the user's explicit Unassigned choice writes, with no provenance field anywhere to distinguish them, and the backfill re-files on that test during a READ. The population is narrow (a zone must still be unsized to stay in `pending`) but reachable.
verdicts.evidence: mapping_services.py:1467-1468 `if zone.get("room_number") is None and membership.get("room_number") is not None: zone["room_number"] = membership.get("room_number")`. SET_SAVED_ZONE_ROOM_SCHEMA:476-484 `vol.Optional("room_number", default=None): vol.Any(None, vol.Coerce(int))` with the comment 'null / omitted -> clear to Unassigned'. _handle_set_saved_zone_room:2573-2575 `zone["room_number"] = room_number; zone["updated_at"] = utc_now_iso()` — no source/provenance key. _create_saved_zone:1408-1409 mints area_m2=None and room_number=None with the same absent-sentinel. The pending filter (:1434) keys only on area_m2, so a user-edited but unsized zone stays eligible. Doc treats the override as first-class: docs/dev/frontend/saved-zones.md:102 and :115-116.

verdicts.reason: room_number=None is simultaneously the not-yet-computed sentinel and the user's explicit Unassigned value, no provenance field distinguishes them, and the backfill re-files on that test during a plain read.
verdicts.evidence: mapping_services.py:1467-1468 `if zone.get("room_number") is None and membership.get("room_number") is not None: zone["room_number"] = membership.get("room_number")`. SET_SAVED_ZONE_ROOM_SCHEMA (476-484) `vol.Optional("room_number", default=None): vol.Any(None, vol.Coerce(int))` with the comment "null / omitted -> clear to Unassigned"; _handle_set_saved_zone_room:2573 writes `zone["room_number"] = room_number` and bumps updated_at, recording no source flag. _create_saved_zone:1409-1410 seeds both area_m2 and room_number to None with no distinguishing key. The `pending` filter (1434) is `area_m2 is None`, which does NOT exclude a zone the user has already edited — a zone authored off its active map keeps area_m2=None through any number of set_saved_zone_room calls, so it stays in the pending set and gets re-filed on the next get_map_segments read (called from _handle_get_map_segments:1273-1279). Roborock immune (zone_membership returns room_number None with no raster). Filing only — docs are explicit it never affects dispatch.

title: _generate_saved_zone_id / _generate_custom_layout_id guarantee uniqueness only against LIVE ids, so an id is reused after a delete — and saved-zone ids are durably referenced by queue steps and run profiles
brands: Both — saved zones and queue zone steps exist for Eufy and Roborock alike.
observed_behavior: Both generators build `base = f'sz_|cl_{datetime.now().strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%S")}'` and only append `_2`, `_3`… while the candidate collides with a member of `existing`, which _create_saved_zone (line 1404) supplies as `set(zones)` — the CURRENTLY-LIVE ids of that map's saved_zones. A deleted id is not in that set, so the very next create in the same wall-clock second re-mints it. The docstrings assert these are 'Stable unique id' with a guard so 'rapid creates (and tests) never clash' — true for concurrent live ids, false across a delete. This matters because zone ids OUTLIVE the zone: core/manager.py:1736 stores `{'type': 'zone', 'zone_ids': [...]}` inside the map bucket's durable queue_breaks (and run-profile steps), and _handle_delete_saved_zone (line 2539-2554) pops the zone without sweeping a single one of those references. Resolution is by id at dispatch time (manager._resolve_saved_zone_rects, line 1855-1878), which 'silently skips' ids it cannot find.
reproduction: (1) Queue step exists: `{'after_index': 2, 'step': {'type': 'zone', 'zone_ids': ['sz_20260731T142530']}}` for the zone 'Litter corner'. (2) User deletes 'Litter corner' — the queue step keeps the dead id and now silently resolves to nothing. (3) Within the same second (scripted delete+create, a double-tap flow, or a card that deletes-and-redraws) the user creates 'Under the couch'. _generate_saved_zone_id computes base='sz_20260731T142530', finds it absent from the live set, and returns it unchanged. (4) The next run reaches the queue step, _resolve_saved_zone_rects resolves 'sz_20260731T142530' to the NEW zone's bbox and dispatch_zone_clean fires it. The vacuum zone-cleans 'Under the couch' where the step said 'Litter corner'. The clock source widens this beyond one second in one case: datetime.now() is naive LOCAL time, so a DST fall-back replays a whole hour of id space.
user_impact: Wrong physical area cleaned by a saved queue step or run profile, with no warning — the failure class is the most serious in this subsystem, but the window is narrow (delete and create must land in the same wall-clock second). The far more common outcome of the same missing-reference-sweep is benign: the step silently cleans nothing. Layout ids reuse the same way but nothing durable outside the bucket keys off them (the migrated layout's backdrop variant is the literal 'custom', and per-layout variants are re-derived on upload), so the layout side is latent.
guards_checked: The same-second collision loop at lines 1371-1373 / 1382-1385 — only tests membership of the live `existing` set; _create_saved_zone's `set(zones)` (line 1404) — the live map's zones only, so per-map and point-in-time; _handle_delete_saved_zone (line 2539) — no reference sweep of queue_breaks or profile steps; manager._resolve_saved_zone_rects (core/manager.py:1866-1878) — validates that the id RESOLVES and that the geometry has >=3 points, but has no way to know the id was recycled; dispatch_zone_clean's brand count/size caps — orthogonal; no uuid, no monotonic counter, no tombstone of retired ids anywhere.
doc_checked: docs/dev/03-data-model.md 'CustomLayout' ('layout_id is generated as "cl_{YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS}" (with a same-second collision guard)') and docs/dev/07-queue-engine.md:575-576 (zone steps resolved at materialization via manager._resolve_saved_zone_rects over the map's saved_zones geometry). The docs describe the same-second guard as the whole uniqueness story and never state that ids must be unique over TIME, which the durable zone_ids references silently require.

verdicts.reason: The generators genuinely only check the currently-live id set, so a delete frees the id for immediate reuse within the same wall-clock second, and delete_saved_zone sweeps no durable references. The wrong-physical-clean outcome is real but requires the delete and the create to land in the same second AND a durable queue/profile reference to the freed id AND that run to execute — narrow enough that MEDIUM overstates it next to findings whose trigger is a routine transient. The far commoner outcome of the same missing sweep is the silent phase-drop already carried by A6-ZONE-C-2.
verdicts.evidence: mapping_services.py:1379-1386 _generate_saved_zone_id: `base = f"sz_{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%dT%H%M%S')}"; if base not in existing: return base; ...` and :1369-1376 for _generate_custom_layout_id. Caller supplies the live set only: _create_saved_zone:1404 `zone_id = _generate_saved_zone_id(set(zones))` where zones = map_bucket.setdefault("saved_zones", {}). _handle_delete_saved_zone (mapping_services.py:2539-2554) pops the zone and saves — no scan of queue_breaks or run-profile steps. Resolution is by id with a silent skip: core/manager.py:1870-1883 _resolve_saved_zone_rects `zone = zones_store.get(str(zid)); if not isinstance(zone, dict): continue`, docstring 'Missing / degenerate zones are silently skipped'. datetime.now() is naive local time (no tz argument).

verdicts.reason: Both id generators test membership of the CURRENTLY-LIVE id set only, so a same-second delete-then-create re-mints the deleted id, and saved-zone ids are durably referenced from queue_breaks/run-profile steps that delete never sweeps.
verdicts.evidence: mapping_services.py:1379-1387 `base = f"sz_{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%dT%H%M%S')}"; if base not in existing: return base` with `existing = set(zones)` supplied by _create_saved_zone:1404 — the live map's saved_zones keys. _handle_delete_saved_zone:2539-2554 pops the zone and saves; grep of that handler shows no scan of queue_breaks or profile steps. Durable references verified: core/manager.py add_queue_zone (1719+) stores `{"type": "zone", "zone_ids": [...]}` into the map bucket's queue_breaks and its docstring states "Existence + brand caps on zone_ids are enforced at dispatch"; that enforcement is core/manager.py:1870-1883 `_resolve_saved_zone_rects`, whose own docstring says "Missing / degenerate zones are silently skipped" and whose loop `continue`s on a missing id. So a recycled id resolves to the NEW zone's bbox and dispatch_zone_clean fires it. datetime.now() is naive local time, so a DST fall-back replays an hour of id space. Window is genuinely one wall-clock second (or a DST repeat).

title: adjust_map_segment persists a map-level record keyed by a segment id that CV re-analysis recycles — a nudge authored for one room silently re-attaches to whichever segment inherits that id
brands: Eufy only in practice — image_segment_adjustments is written against the CV image_segments store, which only the Eufy CV segmentor populates.
observed_behavior: Line 1752 stores the accumulated transform in `map_bucket['image_segment_adjustments'][segment_id]`, a map-level dict keyed purely by segment_id, with no fingerprint of the geometry it was authored against (no analyzed_at, no polygon hash, no bbox). CV segment ids are positional: adapters/eufy/segmentor.py:1289 mints `f'segment_{segment_id}'` from a running counter over detected components. _handle_analyze_map_image (line 1174) replaces `map_bucket['image_segments']` wholesale on force_reanalyze and never clears or invalidates image_segment_adjustments, and _handle_get_map_segments (line 1205-1208) blindly re-applies the old records to the new segments by id.
reproduction: (1) User nudges 'segment_3' (the den) by delta_x=+40, delta_y=-25 to line its outline up with the backdrop; the record persists at image_segment_adjustments['segment_3']. (2) The robot re-explores and the user re-uploads the map image and taps Re-analyze (force_reanalyze=true). The segmenter now detects one extra component early in the scan, so the den is emitted as 'segment_4' and the hallway becomes 'segment_3'. (3) The next get_map_segments applies the stale record to the hallway: _apply_segment_adjustments shifts the hallway polygon by (+40, -25), rewrites its bbox and center_pixel, and tags it 'translated_manual' — while the den, which actually needed the nudge, renders unadjusted.
user_impact: A displayed room outline is silently offset from its true position and falsely labelled as manually adjusted, and the correction the user made is lost from the room it belonged to. Display/linking only — segment polygons are not the dispatch geometry (room cleans go by room id, zone cleans by saved-zone geometry), so nothing physical goes wrong. Only bites installs that both use segment nudges and re-analyze after the map changed; a re-analyze that reproduces the same component order is harmless.
guards_checked: The segment-existence check at line 1749-1750 — validates only at WRITE time and only against the current image_segments, so it cannot protect a record that outlives the segmentation it was written for; the zero-netting cleanup at line 1783-1794 — removes an entry only when the user manually nudges it back to zero; _handle_analyze_map_image (line 1174) — replaces image_segments and calls async_save with no adjustment invalidation; _apply_segment_adjustments (line 756-825) — matches purely on `str(seg.get('segment_id'))` with no cross-check that the polygon is the one the transform was authored against.
doc_checked: docs/dev/03-data-model.md 'AdjustmentRecord' ('CV-segment edits only — written by adjust_map_segment, applied to image_segments at read time', 'Deltas accumulate across calls') and docs/dev/03-data-model.md §image_segments ('Re-running CV re-segments and forces a relink (accepted)'). The doc explicitly accepts that re-analysis breaks segment_room_LINKS, but says nothing about adjustments — and links break VISIBLY (the room shows unlinked) whereas an adjustment re-attaches INVISIBLY to a different shape. docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md §467 documents a different, adjacent caveat (cross-scope id collision) and is not this.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed at the source: the adjustment record is map-level, keyed purely by segment_id, carries no fingerprint of the geometry it was authored against, and the re-analysis path neither clears nor validates it. This is the same root cause as A2-POLYGO-5 and A3-IMAGE--1 reported from a third angle — dedupe downstream. The write-time existence check cannot protect a record that outlives its segmentation.
verdicts.evidence: mapping_services.py:1752-1760 `adjustments[segment_id] = {"offset_x": ..., "vertex_moves": vertex_moves}` into `map_bucket.setdefault("image_segment_adjustments", {})` (:1728) — no analyzed_at, no polygon hash, no bbox. Existence check is write-time only: :1748-1750 `segments = (map_bucket.get("image_segments") or {}).get("segments") or []; if not any(str(seg.get("segment_id") or "") == segment_id for seg in segments): return {"saved": False, "reason": "segment_not_found"}`. Re-application: _apply_segment_adjustments:769-770 matches on str(seg.get("segment_id")) alone; issue tags added at :813-820. Positional ids: adapters/eufy/segmentor.py:1289.

title: set_custom_segments' user-facing description is two features stale — it claims map-level scope and an uploaded-backdrop requirement that the layout + live-dims paths superseded
observed_behavior: services.yaml:2449-2457 describes set_custom_segments as rebuilding 'the map's custom segment set' with no mention of custom layouts at all, and states 'Requires a custom backdrop image (uploaded via upload_map_image) for the pixel dimensions'. The code at line 1667 targets the ACTIVE LAYOUT (auto-creating one), and lines 1673-1684 accept backdrop_width/backdrop_height from the call for a live-image-backed layout with no uploaded backdrop, refusing with no_custom_backdrop only when BOTH are missing. The in-file docstring (line 1645-1653) is likewise map-scoped in its first line ('REPLACE-ALL into the map's custom_segments store') before contradicting itself further down.
reproduction: A user reads the service description in the HA Developer Tools > Actions UI (the only surface where a non-card caller learns this API), builds a script that authors segments, and reasonably concludes (a) that the write is map-scoped and layout-independent, and (b) that the call needs an uploaded backdrop. Both are wrong: the write silently targets whichever layout is active, and a live-backed layout works without an upload if backdrop_width/height are supplied — a parameter the description does not document at all.
user_impact: Documentation precision only, but it is the load-bearing kind: the description is exactly what would have warned a caller about CUSTOM-1's implicit target, and it omits the two parameters that make the live-layout path usable. No runtime effect.

title: map_id is documented as optional + auto-resolving on 6 presentation services but is vol.Required; a literal blank map_id silently mints and writes a phantom map bucket
observed_behavior: Every write handler in this block reads `map_id: str = call.data["map_id"]` (2108, 2150, 2195, 1943, 2010, 2053) and hands it straight to `ensure_map_bucket()`. Their schemas declare `vol.Required("map_id"): cv.string`. None of them calls `services/_common.py::resolved_call_data()`, the shared helper whose docstring states "the map_id field is optional on every service that takes one" and which explicitly handles the blank-string case; that helper is wired into 58 call sites across 9 modules in services/*.py and ZERO times in mapping_services.py. `_handle_set_map_overlay_visibility` (2242-2257) is the lone handler in this block that resolves an absent map_id — the forgotten-sibling shape exactly. `cv.string("")` returns "", and `ensure_map_bucket` does `data["maps"][vac].setdefault(str(map_id), {...})`, so "" mints a real, persisted bucket.
reproduction: Read the machine-readable service definition the HA Actions UI renders: services.yaml declares, for set_hidden_regions / set_area_label_anchor / set_live_map_rotation / set_furnished_art_placement / set_furnished_render_mode / set_room_viewport, `map_id: required: false` with the description "Leave blank to use the current active map." (A) Omit map_id: voluptuous rejects with `required key not provided @ data['map_id']` — the documented optional parameter does not exist. (B) Follow the description literally from a script/automation: `service: eufy_vacuum.set_live_map_rotation` with `{vacuum_entity_id: vacuum.x10, map_id: "", rotation: 90}`. cv.string accepts ""; ensure_map_bucket creates `data["maps"]["vacuum.x10"][""] = {map_id:"", metadata:{}, rooms:{}, summary:{}}`; the handler writes `live_map_rotation: 90` there, async_saves, and returns `{"saved": true, "live_map_rotation": 90}`. Every reader (get_dashboard_snapshot reads `.get(str(map_id), {})` for the REAL active map; get_map_segments likewise) never looks at bucket "", so the map never rotates. Same for a hidden-region set, an area-label drag, and all three furnished writes.
user_impact: The service reports success and the setting is permanently invisible — the classic silent-wrong-answer shape. It also leaves a ghost map in .storage that surfaces through get_vacuum_maps / diagnostics as an extra map with 0 rooms, and becomes a candidate for the `next(iter(vac_maps))` fallback in FURNIS-2. Blast radius is bounded: the card always sends a map_id (state/rooms.js activeMapId() falls back to "1" and can never return falsy), so only automation/script/Dev-Tools callers are affected. Branch (A) fails loudly and merely makes the published API wrong; branch (B) is the silent one. Fix is one line per handler (route through resolved_call_data, which already rejects the blank case correctly) — but see FURNIS-2 before copying its last-resort behaviour.

title: _handle_set_room_viewport is the only furnished writer with no clamp and a corner-valued default — zoom:0 and cx/cy:0.0 persist verbatim
observed_behavior: The viewport write is `{"cx": _round4(cx, 0.0), "cy": _round4(cy, 0.0), "zoom": _round4(zoom, 1.0)}` — no range clamp on any of the three. Forty lines above, the sibling in the same wave clamps scale to [0.05, 20] with a comment stating precisely why: "A raw 0 (or negative) would persist as 0.0 but the renderer coerces it back to 1x (`Number(scale) || 1`), so state and render would silently disagree; clamp here so the stored value is always renderable." Thirty lines below, `_handle_set_area_label_anchor` clamps pct to 0-100 and defaults a missing coordinate to 50.0 (centre). The viewport handler inherits neither guard, and its missing-coordinate default is 0.0 — a CORNER of the same 0-100 pct frame, not a centre.
reproduction: Room 7 has a saved viewport `{cx: 72.0, cy: 41.0, zoom: 2.5}`. (a) Partial update: `set_room_viewport {room_id: "7", zoom: 3.0}` — zoom is not None so the else-branch runs and stores `{cx: 0.0, cy: 0.0, zoom: 3.0}`; the framing snaps from the room's centre to the top-left corner of the map, and the old cx/cy are gone with no undo. (b) Degenerate zoom: `set_room_viewport {room_id: "7", cx: 50, cy: 50, zoom: 0}` stores `zoom: 0.0` — the exact value the sibling's comment says must never be persisted; a consumer doing `Number(zoom) || 1` renders 1x while storage says 0, and one dividing by zoom gets a ZeroDivisionError/Infinity. (c) Out of frame: `{cx: -400, cy: 9000, zoom: -3}` round-trips verbatim through resolve_furnished_render into the snapshot.
user_impact: Latent today — say so plainly: docs/advanced/08-map-configuration.md line 270 records the per-room viewport as "service-only today, not yet a panel control", and the card reads no viewport (src/state/map.js: "Per-room art / sub-tabs / saved viewport are Wave 2 — NOT read or written here"), so nothing renders it yet. The cost is that unrenderable values are being accepted and persisted NOW, so a Wave-2 consumer inherits a store the two sibling writers were explicitly hardened against, and any automation-authored viewport is already silently mis-stored.

title: area_label_anchors are keyed by device room id and nothing prunes them on a room rebuild, so a re-import silently re-aims one room's dragged label onto a different room
observed_behavior: `anchors: dict = map_bucket.setdefault("area_label_anchors", {})` then `anchors[room_id] = {pct_x, pct_y}`, keyed by the raw device room id, at the MAP-BUCKET level. The room set that gives those ids meaning is rebuilt by `maps/map_manager.py::rebuild_map_bucket`, which at line 201 does `map_bucket["rooms"] = rebuilt_rooms` — a wholesale replacement that drops rooms no longer discovered — and touches nothing else. Grepping maps/ and rooms/ for `area_label_anchors` / `companion_anchors` returns zero hits: no prune, no reconcile, no fingerprint of which room set an anchor was authored against.
reproduction: Map "1" has rooms 1..6; room 3 is the Kitchen. The user drags the Kitchen m² chip clear of its name label to the room's right edge: `area_label_anchors["3"] = {pct_x: 78.5, pct_y: 22.0}`. The vacuum is factory-reset / re-mapped (this project's own device notes record Eufy re-issuing room ids 1..N from scratch); rediscovery calls rebuild_map_bucket, which replaces `rooms` — now room 3 is the Bedroom on the opposite side of the house. `area_label_anchors["3"]` is still `{78.5, 22.0}` and the dashboard snapshot hands it out verbatim (core/manager.py:4176-4179), so the Bedroom's m² chip renders at 78.5%/22.0% of the map content box — over the Kitchen, detached from its room and possibly overlapping another room's label. A room that vanished entirely (say old room 6) keeps its anchor in storage forever.
user_impact: This is the direct answer to 'does the edit survive a re-import?': the bytes survive, their meaning does not, and nothing detects it. Cosmetic in consequence (a mis-placed m² chip, not a mis-cleaned room) but silently wrong and non-obvious — the user cannot tell that a chip is stale rather than mis-rendered. Reversible only by noticing and re-dragging (or calling the service with both pcts null). The same shape applies to the map-level `companion_anchors` and to each custom layout's furnished `rooms` map, which are keyed the same way and equally unpruned.
guards_checked: rebuild_map_bucket (maps/map_manager.py:109-250) — replaces `rooms` and `summary`, preserves per-room settings via RoomConfig, and never looks at the sibling UI-state keys; the `preserve_existing_settings` flag — governs room records only; the dashboard snapshot reader (core/manager.py:4176) — isinstance-guards the type and copies the dict, but does no key validation against the live room list; the write handler itself — no room-existence check (consistent with _handle_set_segment_room_link / _handle_set_companion_anchor, so this is a family-wide gap rather than one forgotten site).

title: hidden_regions are stored as normalized rects with no record of the frame they were authored against, so a re-map re-aims the masks onto different physical areas — and masks hide content by default
brands: both — sharpest on Roborock, whose rendered image is trimmed to the occupied extent
observed_behavior: The handler sanitizes each rect and replace-alls them into `map_bucket["hidden_regions"]` as normalized 0-1 of the RENDERED IMAGE. That is the only thing stored: no image_size, no map fingerprint, no authored-at stamp, no schema version. The reader hands them back unconditionally (core/manager.py:4180-4183 for the dashboard, plus the get_map_segments payload), and the card places them with the same letterbox transform the device overlays use (src/renderers/map.js::_renderHiddenRegions), painting background-coloured rects at z-index 5 — above room labels AND area chips — with `hidden_regions` defaulting to visible:true in OVERLAY_VISIBILITY_DEFAULTS.
reproduction: Arithmetic: the user masks porch noise sitting at columns 80-95 of a 100-column rendered map → stored `[0.80, 0.10, 0.95, 0.25]`. The robot later discovers a new area to the east and the rendered extent grows to 130 columns covering the same house plus 30 new columns. The same physical porch now sits at 80/130 = 0.615 to 95/130 = 0.731. The stored rect is unchanged, so it is now drawn at columns 0.80*130 = 104 through 0.95*130 = 123.5 — inside the newly discovered area. The porch reappears and a slice of the new room is covered by an opaque background-coloured rect that also swallows its label and m² chip. map_id is unchanged across the re-map, so the same bucket is reused and nothing signals a mismatch. Provable from code: no fingerprint is written at 2130 and no consumer validates one. The premise that the rendered extent changes across a re-map is device behaviour (sharpest on Roborock, whose map image is trimmed to the occupied bounding box) and is what needs a hardware check.
user_impact: Map content silently disappears with no indication of why, on a map the user never edited — the mask looks like a rendering bug rather than stale state. Recovery exists but is undiscoverable unless the user remembers the Hide-area tool: toggling the hidden_regions overlay off reveals what is under, and edit mode exposes a per-rect delete. Not destructive (nothing else is overwritten) and not a dispatch risk (masks are display-only; cleaning is by room id).
guards_checked: the sanitizer at 2111-2124 — correct for the values it sees (bool/NaN/inf rejected BEFORE the clamp, which matters: max(0.0,min(1.0,nan)) evaluates to 1.0 in CPython, so the comment's claim that NaN would clamp to an edge rather than drop is accurate; degenerate <0.001 rects dropped; min<max ordered) but it validates shape, never provenance; the in-place `regions.clear()/extend()` — safe, every reader copies (`list(...)`) so no cached snapshot aliases the stored list; the card's draw gate (src/state/map.js:815) — requires an aligned backdrop and rotation 0 to DRAW a mask, but does not gate RENDERING of existing masks; the overlay-visibility toggle — a manual escape hatch, not a guard.
doc_checked: docs/dev/17-map-manager.md lines 124-129 and 362 (defines the normalized frame and the sanitizer; silent on invalidation); docs/advanced/03-services.md §set_hidden_regions ("0-1 of the rendered image, top-left origin ... Hidden regions are physical, so they are stored at the map level and follow the map regardless of segmentation mode" — states the intent that they follow the map, without addressing the map's own frame changing); docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md §648 (lists hidden_regions on the get_map_segments payload, no lifecycle).

verdicts.reason: The source-level claim is exactly right: the handler stores four normalized floats and nothing else — no image_size, no map fingerprint, no authored-at stamp, no schema version — and no consumer validates provenance. The sanitizer's correctness (including its accurate NaN-before-clamp note) is confirmed but validates shape only. Correcting to LOW: the impact premise (that the rendered extent changes across a re-map) is device behaviour the finding itself flags as needing hardware verification, the effect is display-only and non-destructive, and recovery exists via the overlay toggle and per-rect delete.

Replace-all; each entry sanitized').

title: Clearing a home-scope art placement setdefaults an empty home_art dict, flipping the 'no furnished data' sentinel from None to a confident empty payload
observed_behavior: The clear path takes `target = layout.setdefault("home_art", {})` BEFORE deciding it is a clear, then pops the (absent) transform. On a layout with no art yet, that leaves `layout["home_art"] = {}` behind. The reader guards the per-room branch against exactly this — `if not any(entry.get(f) is not None for f in _FURNISHED_FIELDS): continue` skips empty room entries — but the home branch tests only `if home_art_raw is None`, and `{}` is not None. The forgotten sibling is in the reader; the writer mints the empty dict for both.
reproduction: Map in custom mode with an active layout carrying no art. Call `set_furnished_art_placement {scope: "home"}` with no coordinates. Response: `{saved: true, action: "cleared", furnished_render: {...}}` — and resolve_furnished_render, which returned None a moment earlier ('the map has no furnished data'), now returns `{active_layout_id: ..., render_mode: "live", home_art: {art_url: None, transform: None}, rooms: {}}`, both in that response and in every subsequent dashboard snapshot. The same setdefault-then-pop leaves permanent empty `rooms[<id>] = {}` entries via the room-scope clear (1967) and via _handle_set_room_viewport's clear (2071); those are absorbed by the reader's per-room guard but accumulate in storage with nothing to clean them.
user_impact: No visible effect today: the card's clear button only renders when hasArt is true (src/renderers/map.js:1581), so the empty-home_art state is unreachable from the UI, and the current consumers key off art_url/render_mode rather than the payload's presence. It matters because `furnished_render is None` is the documented 'no furnished data' sentinel that a Wave-2 consumer is likely to branch on, and a no-op clear permanently falsifies it for that layout.
guards_checked: resolve_furnished_render (map_source.py:111-137) — the `_FURNISHED_FIELDS` any()-check protects rooms only; the `if home_art_raw is None and not rooms_out: return None` early return at 129 — defeated by `{}` being non-None; _furnished_art_url — correctly returns None for a missing variant rather than raising, so nothing downstream errors; the card's hasArt gate — blocks the UI path but not the service path; test FURN-5 (test_clear_home_art_placement) — asserts only that the transform key is gone, and its setup sets a placement first, so it never exercises the mint-on-empty case.
doc_checked: docs/dev/03-data-model.md lines 213-233 ("They are schema-free and minted lazily — `rooms` starts `{}`; `home_art`/`render_mode` appear on first write" — an empty home_art from a CLEAR is not a 'first write' in that sense); map_source.py resolve_furnished_render docstring ("Returns None when ... the active layout carries no furnished data (no whole-home art AND no per-room furnished field)" — a claim this case falsifies); docs/dev/frontend/furnished-render.md line 27 ("All-null clears it").

verdicts.reason: Verified line for line: the writer takes `target = layout.setdefault("home_art", {})` BEFORE branching on the clear, so a no-op clear on a layout with no art leaves an empty dict behind, and the reader's home branch tests `is None` while the per-room branch has the any()-over-fields guard that would have caught it. The result is that resolve_furnished_render stops returning its documented 'no furnished data' None sentinel for that layout.
verdicts.evidence: mapping_services.py:1966-1971: `if scope == "room": target = layout.setdefault("rooms", {}).setdefault(room_id, {}) else: target = layout.setdefault("home_art", {})` then `if tx is None and ty is None and scale is None and rotation is None: target.pop("art_placement_transform", None); action = "cleared"`. Reader asymmetry in map_source.py:115-129: `_FURNISHED_FIELDS = ("art_variant", "art_placement_transform", "viewport", "render_mode")` with `if not any(entry.get(f) is not None for f in _FURNISHED_FIELDS): continue` for rooms, but `home_art_raw = layout.get("home_art") if isinstance(layout.get("home_art"), dict) else None` and `if home_art_raw is None and not rooms_out: return None` — {} is a dict, so home_art_raw is {} and the early return is defeated. The same setdefault-then-pop shape recurs at mapping_services.py:1967 (room scope) and :2071 (_handle_set_room_viewport clear). Card gate confirmed: the clear control renders only when hasArt (src/renderers/map.js:1581).

verdicts.reason: The clear path setdefaults home_art before deciding it is a clear, and the reader's early-return tests `is None` rather than emptiness — so a no-op clear permanently flips the documented 'no furnished data' sentinel from None to a populated payload.
verdicts.evidence: mapping_services.py:1969 `target = layout.setdefault("home_art", {})` executes before the branch at 1972 `if tx is None and ty is None and scale is None and rotation is None: target.pop("art_placement_transform", None)` — on a layout with no art this leaves `layout["home_art"] = {}`. map_source.py:111-129: the per-room branch guards with `if not any(entry.get(f) is not None for f in _FURNISHED_FIELDS): continue`, but the home branch is only `home_art_raw = layout.get("home_art") if isinstance(layout.get("home_art"), dict) else None` and the early return is `if home_art_raw is None and not rooms_out: return None` — `{}` is a dict and is not None, so the function now returns `{active_layout_id:..., render_mode:..., home_art: {"art_url": None, "transform": None}, rooms: {}}` where it previously returned None. The same setdefault-then-pop shape leaves empty `rooms[<id>] = {}` entries via the room-scope clear (1967) and _handle_set_room_viewport:2071, absorbed by the reader's per-room guard but accumulating in storage. Card path unreachable (the clear button renders only when hasArt).

title: Saved-zone clean dispatches to the device when the active-map signal is blank — the "active map only" guard is permissive, not a refusal
brands: Both. Roborock is more exposed: map_id is the vendor map NAME read off a select entity that goes `unavailable` whenever the upstream integration reloads, and the wrong-map projection can land on a different FLOOR.
observed_behavior: _handle_clean_saved_zone (2603-2612) and _handle_clean_saved_zones (2658-2667) resolve the active map, swallow any exception to None, then refuse only when `active_map_id is not None and str(active_map_id) != str(map_id)`. When get_active_map_id returns None the guard falls through and the zone is dispatched. get_active_map_id (rooms/room_discovery.py:43-84) returns None for any BLANK state — entity_helpers.BLANK_STATE_VALUES = {"", "unknown", "unavailable", "none", "null"} — and also when the entity is registered but has no state yet (boot/reload window). dispatch_zone_clean (dispatch/manager.py:86-107) explicitly does NOT send map_id ("the provider uses its own currently-loaded map"), so this service-layer check is the ONLY thing binding the geometry to a map.
reproduction: Roborock S6. Adapter declares active_map = select.<id>_selected_map, whose state is the map NAME (adapters/roborock/adapter.py:163,190). Saved zone "under the couch" on map_id="Main floor", geometry [[0.20,0.30],[0.30,0.30],[0.30,0.40],[0.20,0.40]] -> rect [0.20,0.30,0.30,0.40]. Robot currently has "Upstairs" loaded, and the Roborock integration is mid-reload so the select is `unavailable`. Call clean_saved_zone(map_id="Main floor", zone_id=...). is_blank_state("unavailable") -> True -> active_map_id=None -> guard passes. dispatch_zone_clean takes cfg zone_coords=="device_mm", calls get_live_mapdata_obj (mapping/map_source_coordinator.py:330-358) which returns whatever MapData is in the Roborock integration's memory WITHOUT checking it is "Main floor", and normalized_rects_to_mm (dispatch/zone_dispatch.py:102-131) fits the affine from THAT map's correspondences. Arithmetic: Main floor 60x60px @50mm/px origin (-1000,-1000) -> x0 = -1000 + 0.20*3000 = -400 mm, x1 = -1000 + 0.30*3000 = -100 mm; Upstairs 100x80px @50mm/px origin (2000,500) -> x0 = 2000 + 0.20*5000 = 3000 mm, x1 = 3500 mm. Same stored rect, two rectangles ~3.4 m apart. The residual check in normalized_rects_to_mm only validates the affine's self-consistency, so the wrong-map fit passes cleanly and the robot cleans a different physical area (on Roborock, a different floor). On Eufy the normalized rect is shipped verbatim and the fork de-normalizes against its own loaded map — same wrong-area outcome.
user_impact: The vacuum cleans a physically different area from the one the user named and tapped, with no error and no way to tell from the response (it returns {cleaned: true}). Requires the active-map entity to be blank (integration reload, cloud hiccup, HA restart window), so the common path is fine — but the failure is physical and silent, and an automation firing shortly after HA start sits exactly in that window.
guards_checked: (a) The `str(active_map_id) != str(map_id)` comparison itself — correct when a value exists, does nothing when None. (b) dispatch_zone_clean's degenerate-rect check (dispatch/manager.py:110-118) — checks side length only, not which map. (c) normalized_rects_to_mm's 50mm residual validation — validates the affine fit, not the map identity; a wrong-map affine is perfectly self-consistent. (d) get_live_mapdata_obj takes map_id as a parameter but only uses it to resolve the live image ENTITY, never to verify the returned MapData is that map. (e) The job path's map_mismatch guard (jobs/job_monitor.py:172, 254) is identically permissive (`selected_map_id_n and active_map_id_n and ...`), so this is the systemic permissive default, NOT a forgotten sibling.
doc_checked: docs/advanced/03-services.md:75 and :140/:153 — states the two clean services are "active-map-guarded (a zone's geometry is only valid on its own map)" unconditionally; docs/dev/frontend/backend-contract-and-data-shapes.md:71 — "requires the zone's map to be the active map"; docs/dev/frontend/saved-zones.md §6 (the "one hard rule"). All three state the requirement with no indeterminate-map exception, so code and doc diverge.

verdicts.reason: The guard is permissive by construction — it refuses only when a value EXISTS and differs — and get_active_map_id returns None for every blank/sentinel state and for the registered-but-no-state boot window, which are routine transients. dispatch_zone_clean deliberately does not send map_id, so this service-layer check is genuinely the only thing binding the stored geometry to a map, and the Roborock affine is fitted from whatever MapData is currently in memory with no identity cross-check.
verdicts.evidence: mapping_services.py:2603-2612 and :2658-2667: `try: active_map_id = get_active_map_id(...) except Exception: active_map_id = None` then `if active_map_id is not None and str(active_map_id) != str(map_id): return {"cleaned": False, "reason": "map_not_active", ...}` — the None arm falls through to dispatch. rooms/room_discovery.py:69-84: returns None on is_blank_state(value) (BLANK_STATE_VALUES = {"","unknown","unavailable","none","null"}) and None when the entity is registered but has no state. dispatch/manager.py:104-106 docstring: 'map_id is accepted because the service layer auto-resolves it, but it is intentionally NOT sent: the provider uses its own currently-loaded map'. dispatch/manager.py:146-149 `map_obj = self._manager.map_source.get_live_mapdata_obj(vacuum_entity_id=..., map_id=str(map_id or ""))` then `corr = _msr.correspondences_from_mapdata(map_obj)` — no verification that map_obj is the named map. The remaining guards are geometry-only: _MIN_SIDE at :110-118, zone_max at :129-135, area/side bounds at :164-177 and :202-234. Doc states the requirement unconditionally: docs/advanced/03-services.md:75.

verdicts.reason: The active-map guard is `active_map_id is not None and str(active_map_id) != str(map_id)`, so an indeterminate signal falls through and the zone is dispatched against whatever map the provider currently holds. This is the only map binding in the path — dispatch deliberately does not send map_id.
verdicts.evidence: mapping_services.py:2603-2612 and 2658-2667 are identical: `try: active_map_id = get_active_map_id(...) except: active_map_id = None` then `if active_map_id is not None and str(active_map_id) != str(map_id): return {"cleaned": False, "reason": "map_not_active", ...}` — the None case proceeds. rooms/room_discovery.py:43-84 returns None for any is_blank_state value (entity_helpers.BLANK_STATE_VALUES = {"","unknown","unavailable","none","null"}) and for a registered-but-stateless entity. dispatch/manager.py dispatch_zone_clean docstring: "map_id is accepted because the service layer auto-resolves it, but it is intentionally NOT sent: the provider uses its own currently-loaded map." On the device_mm branch it calls `self._manager.map_source.get_live_mapdata_obj(vacuum_entity_id=..., map_id=str(map_id or ""))`, and map_source_coordinator.py:330-358 uses map_id ONLY to resolve the live image entity, then returns the first MapData found by BFS with no identity check; `normalized_rects_to_mm(corr, zones)` then fits the affine from THAT map's correspondences — a wrong-map fit is perfectly self-consistent, so the residual gate cannot see it. On the Eufy branch `payload = {"zones": zones, "clean_times": int(clean_times)}` ships the normalized rects verbatim for the fork to de-normalize against its loaded map. Roborock's active_map is a select whose state is the map NAME (adapters/roborock/adapter.py:190) and which goes unavailable on an upstream reload. docs/advanced/03-services.md states the guard unconditionally.

title: delete_saved_zone performs no reference check; run-profile and queue `zone` steps keep the dead id and are silently dropped at run time while the UI still lists them
brands: Both — the zone step and its resolver are brand-agnostic.
observed_behavior: _handle_delete_saved_zone (2539-2554) pops the zone from map_bucket['saved_zones'] and saves. It scans nothing else. Saved-zone ids are referenced from a second persisted store: queue_breaks / run-profile steps of the form {"type": "zone", "zone_ids": [...]} (core/manager.py:1736, 1835). ProfileManager.normalize_run_profile_steps (profiles/manager.py:798-808) keeps the ids verbatim and documents that "existence ... [is] enforced at dispatch". That enforcement is a silent skip: MapManager._resolve_saved_zone_rects (core/manager.py:1870-1883) `continue`s on a missing zone, and RunPlan (planning/run_plan.py:866-872) does `if not rects: continue` — dropping the entire phase.
reproduction: Map has saved zones sz_A ("under the couch") and sz_B ("by the stove"). User builds a queue: Kitchen -> zone step [sz_A, sz_B] -> Bedroom (add_queue_zone, core/manager.py:1719). (1) Delete sz_B. Next run: _resolve_saved_zone_rects returns 1 rect; the phase dispatches ONE zone. The user's saved sequence silently cleans half of what it says. (2) Delete sz_A as well. rects == [] -> run_plan.py:871 `continue` -> the zone phase never enters the plan at all; the run goes Kitchen -> Bedroom. Meanwhile get_queue_steps (core/manager.py:1632-1678) rebuilds the step list straight from queue_breaks and still returns the zone step (normalize is shape-only), so the card's queue preview keeps showing it. The phase-runner's zone_timing snapshot (jobs/phase_runner.py:355-370) records zone_ids including the dead ids with zone_names falling back to the raw id string.
user_impact: A saved run silently stops doing part of what the user built, and the UI keeps advertising the step that no longer runs. There is no warning at delete time and no reason code — the divergence is only discoverable by watching the robot. Non-edge: deleting a zone is a normal one-tap card action (docs/dev/frontend/saved-zones.md §8 lists delete in the shipped Wave 3b UX).
guards_checked: (a) normalize_run_profile_steps — validates shape only, explicitly defers existence to dispatch. (b) _resolve_saved_zone_rects — the deferred-to enforcer; it skips rather than reports (its own docstring admits "Missing / degenerate zones are silently skipped"). (c) run_plan.py:871 `if not rects: continue` — drops the phase with no marker on the plan. (d) dispatch_zone_clean's `if not zones: raise` (dispatch/manager.py:108) would have surfaced it, but run_plan drops the phase before dispatch is ever reached. (e) learned_zones is NOT corrupted — ids are timestamp-minted and never reused, so a later zone cannot inherit a deleted zone's learning.
doc_checked: docs/dev/frontend/saved-zones.md §5 (delete_saved_zone) and §10 (Invalidation) — neither mentions reference cleanup or a refuse-if-referenced rule; docs/dev/07-queue-engine.md and docs/dev/30-phase-runner.md describe the zone step but not the dangling-id case. The behaviour is undocumented in either direction, so this is not a documented design choice.

verdicts.reason: delete_saved_zone genuinely scans nothing but the zones dict, the deferred-to enforcer silently skips missing ids, and run_plan drops the entire zone phase before dispatch is ever reached — so dispatch_zone_clean's own `if not zones: raise` can never surface it. Correcting HIGH to MEDIUM: the trigger is a user-initiated delete of the very object the step references, which is materially less surprising than the transient-triggered wrong-clean findings at HIGH here; the real defect is the absent warning and the UI continuing to advertise a step that no longer runs.
verdicts.evidence: mapping_services.py:2539-2554 _handle_delete_saved_zone: ensure_map_bucket, _migrate_saved_zones, `if zone_id not in zones: return {"saved": False, "reason": "zone_not_found"}`, `zones.pop(zone_id, None)`, await manager.async_save() — no other store is read. core/manager.py:1870-1883 _resolve_saved_zone_rects: `zone = zones_store.get(str(zid)); if not isinstance(zone, dict): continue`, docstring 'Missing / degenerate zones are silently skipped'. planning/run_plan.py:861-872: `rects = self._manager._resolve_saved_zone_rects(...); if not rects: continue` — the phase never enters the plan, so dispatch/manager.py:108 `if not zones: raise ValueError(...)` is unreachable for this case. Durable references exist at core/manager.py:1736 ({'type': 'zone', 'zone_ids': [...]}) and are kept verbatim by profiles/manager.py:798-808.

verdicts.reason: delete_saved_zone pops and saves with no reference scan, while the deferred-to enforcement is a silent skip that drops resolved rects and then the entire phase — and the queue UI keeps listing the dead step.
verdicts.evidence: mapping_services.py:2539-2554: `zones.pop(zone_id, None); await manager.async_save(); return {"saved": True, "deleted": True, "zone_id": zone_id}` — nothing else is inspected. Durable reference: core/manager.py add_queue_zone stores `{"type": "zone", "zone_ids": zone_ids}` into the map bucket's queue_breaks and its docstring defers existence "at dispatch". core/manager.py:1855-1883 `_resolve_saved_zone_rects` — docstring "Missing / degenerate zones are silently skipped"; loop body `zone = zones_store.get(str(zid)); if not isinstance(zone, dict): continue`. planning/run_plan.py:866-872 — `rects = self._manager._resolve_saved_zone_rects(...); if not rects: continue` — the zone phase is never appended, so dispatch_zone_clean's own `if not zones: raise` (dispatch/manager.py:108) is never reached. UI divergence confirmed: core/manager.py get_queue_steps (1632-1678) rebuilds steps straight from `self._map_queue_breaks(map_bucket)` via `steps.append(dict(breaks[bi]["step"]))` and then only shape-normalizes, so the deleted zone's step is still returned to the card. Partial case (one of two ids deleted) dispatches half the user's saved selection.

title: The `map_version` re-map invalidation the design doc specifies as the zone's safety key does not exist anywhere in the codebase
observed_behavior: docs/dev/frontend/saved-zones.md §3 declares SavedZone carries `"map_version": ...  # invalidation key (§6)`, and §10 states "Saved zones are keyed to the map version. A genuine re-map changes the room_pixels raster -> the stored geometry no longer means the same thing -> the map's saved zones invalidate". _create_saved_zone (mapping_services.py:1406-1415, called from my range at 2490) mints exactly {id, name, geometry, area_m2, room_number, kind, created_at, updated_at} — no map_version. `grep -rn map_version` across custom_components/, src/ and tests/ returns ZERO hits. Nothing stamps it, nothing checks it, and neither clean handler consults any freshness signal before dispatching.
reproduction: Eufy or Roborock. 1) Save zone "under the couch" on map "Main floor": geometry stored as normalized [[0.20,0.30]..[0.30,0.40]]. 2) User re-runs a full mapping scan (or the robot auto-remaps after furniture changes). The new raster has different extents, so the same physical couch now sits at normalized ~[0.26,0.24]..[0.36,0.33]. The map_id (Eufy numeric id / Roborock map name) is unchanged, so the SAME map bucket and the SAME saved_zones dict are reused. 3) Tap the zone -> clean_saved_zone -> rect [0.20,0.30,0.30,0.40] is projected onto the NEW map's frame -> the robot cleans a region offset by ~6% of map width/height from the couch. No invalidation, no warning, no stale flag. 4) The stored area_m2/room_number are equally stale and are NOT recomputed: _backfill_saved_zone_area (1431-1471) only touches zones where `area_m2 is None`, so a zone sized against the pre-remap raster keeps its old number forever and continues feeding zone ETA (core/manager.py:3643-3665) and zone learning.
user_impact: Every saved zone on a re-mapped floor silently points at the wrong physical spot, and the design's own stated defence against exactly this was never built. This is the direct failure of "survives a re-import": the edit does not survive, and nothing tells the user it stopped being valid. It is also irreversible from the UI — the only repair is delete + redraw every zone, and there is no signal telling the user which zones need it.
guards_checked: (a) _backfill_saved_zone_area (1431-1439) — the only self-heal path; gated on `area_m2 is None`, so it never revisits a stale-but-populated value. (b) The active-map guard in the clean handlers — checks WHICH map, never WHEN the geometry was authored; a re-map keeps the same map_id so the guard passes. (c) created_at/updated_at are stamped but no consumer compares them to any map timestamp. (d) map_bucket['metadata']['last_rebuild'] (maps/map_manager.py:203) exists and would be a usable version signal — no saved-zone code reads it.
doc_checked: docs/dev/frontend/saved-zones.md §3 (SavedZone schema, `map_version` line) and §10 (Invalidation) — the doc specifies the mechanism as built-in to the data model; docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md §8 storage keys list makes no mention of it either. Code/doc divergence: the doc describes a guarantee that has no implementation.

verdicts.reason: Verified by exhaustive grep: map_version appears exactly once in the repository, in the design doc's SavedZone schema, and zero times in custom_components/, src/ or tests/. The doc does not merely describe a behaviour — it specifies an invalidation key as part of the data model and devotes a section to the guarantee it provides. Nothing stamps it, nothing checks it, and the two self-heal/guard paths that could have compensated key on the wrong things.
verdicts.evidence: grep -rn 'map_version' custom_components/ src/ tests/ -> 0 hits; grep -rn 'map_version' docs/ -> 1 hit, docs/dev/frontend/saved-zones.md:61 `"map_version":   ...,            # invalidation key (§6)`. _create_saved_zone (mapping_services.py:1406-1415) mints exactly {id, name, geometry, area_m2, room_number, kind, created_at, updated_at}. The self-heal cannot re-validate a populated value: _backfill_saved_zone_area:1434-1437 selects only `z.get("area_m2") is None`. The active-map guard (:2607-2612) compares WHICH map, and a re-map keeps the same map_id. A usable version signal exists and is unread by saved-zone code: maps/map_manager.py:203-207 metadata['last_rebuild'].

verdicts.reason: The invalidation key the design doc names as the SavedZone's safety mechanism does not exist in the codebase at all, and no other freshness signal is consulted before dispatch.
verdicts.evidence: `grep -rn map_version --include=*.py --include=*.js --include=*.mjs custom_components/ src/ tests/` returns 0 hits. `grep -rn map_version docs/` returns exactly one: docs/dev/frontend/saved-zones.md:61 `"map_version": ...,  # invalidation key (§6)`, with §10 (line 169-173) stating "Saved zones are keyed to the map version. A genuine re-map changes the room_pixels raster -> the stored geometry no longer means the same thing -> the map's saved zones invalidate." _create_saved_zone (mapping_services.py:1406-1415) mints exactly {id, name, geometry, area_m2, room_number, kind, created_at, updated_at} — no map_version. Neither clean handler reads any freshness field; their only map test is the id equality at 2608/2663, and a re-map does not change map_id, so the guard passes. Self-heal cannot repair it: _backfill_saved_zone_area:1434-1437 selects only `z.get("area_m2") is None`. maps/map_manager.py:203 does write `map_bucket["metadata"]["last_rebuild"]` — a usable version signal that no saved-zone code reads (grep confirms).

title: create_saved_zone files area_m2 + room_number from whatever raster is live when the active map is indeterminate, and that wrong value can never be corrected

(c) _backfill_saved_zone_area's identical guard at 1449 — same permissive None branch, so the self-heal path can also write wrong-map values (and cannot overwrite one already written). title: create_custom_layout force-flips segmentation_mode to "custom" with no record of the prior mode; delete only restores "cv" when zero layouts remain, so create-then-delete strands the user on a layout they never chose
observed_behavior: _handle_create_custom_layout sets `map_bucket["segmentation_mode"] = "custom"` unconditionally at 2346, discarding the previous value. _handle_delete_custom_layout restores "cv" only inside the `else` branch at 2429-2432 — i.e. only when NO layouts remain. When any layout remains it reassigns active to `sorted(remaining, key=name)[0]` (2423-2428) and leaves the mode at "custom". The pair is asymmetric: create always mutates the mode, delete conditionally restores it.
reproduction: Install that has a legacy `custom_segments` store and segmentation_mode == "cv". First touch runs _migrate_custom_layouts (1483-1528), which mints layout cl_LEGACY named "Custom", sets it active, and deliberately does NOT change segmentation_mode — so the map is in CV mode with one dormant layout. User now: (1) calls create_custom_layout(name="Test") -> cl_NEW minted + activated, mode forced to "custom"; (2) decides against it and calls delete_custom_layout(cl_NEW). `layouts` still contains cl_LEGACY, so remaining is non-empty -> active_custom_layout_id = cl_LEGACY and segmentation_mode STAYS "custom". Final state: the map renders cl_LEGACY's authored segments, links and companion anchors instead of the CV segmentation the user was on before step (1). map_source.build_furnished_render (mapping/map_source.py:103-107) also flips on, so any furnished art on cl_LEGACY starts rendering. Undoing needs a separate set_segmentation_mode("cv") call that the delete response does not hint at (it returns segmentation_mode: "custom").
user_impact: Creating and then cancelling a layout silently changes what the map card renders — a different room-to-segment mapping, different mascot anchors, possibly a furnished art layer. Presentation-level only (room CLEAN dispatch keys off device room ids, not segmentation_mode — verified: the only non-mapping_services consumer of segmentation_mode is map_source.py:103), so it is not a wrong-clean, but it is a user-visible state change nobody asked for and it is not obviously reversible.
guards_checked: (a) The `if map_bucket.get("active_custom_layout_id") == layout_id` branch at 2422 — only asks whether the DELETED layout was active, never whether the mode was custom before any layout existed. (b) _handle_set_segmentation_mode's soft-select (1342-1345) — helps the opposite direction (custom with no active layout), not this one. (c) No prior-mode field is stored anywhere in the bucket, so restoring is not merely un-wired — the information is destroyed at 2346. (d) `remaining[0].get("id")` — additionally yields None if a layout dict lost its "id" key, leaving active=None while mode stays "custom".
doc_checked: docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md:755 (create: "then flip segmentation_mode to custom") and :757 (delete: "if none remain, set active_custom_layout_id = null and flip segmentation_mode back to cv"). Each half is documented; the doc never addresses the combination, and §10.1:648 claims "Flipping cv -> custom -> cv returns each segment set untouched" — true of the stores, but the MODE itself does not round-trip through create/delete.

verdicts.reason: The pair is asymmetric exactly as described — create writes segmentation_mode unconditionally, delete restores 'cv' only inside the no-layouts-remain branch — and the prior mode is not stored anywhere, so restoring it is not merely un-wired, the information is destroyed. The repro's premise checks out: _migrate_custom_layouts deliberately does not touch segmentation_mode, so a migrated install genuinely sits in cv mode with a dormant layout.
verdicts.evidence: mapping_services.py:2346 `map_bucket["segmentation_mode"] = "custom"` in _handle_create_custom_layout, with no capture of the previous value; the bucket has no prior-mode key anywhere. _handle_delete_custom_layout:2422-2432: `if map_bucket.get("active_custom_layout_id") == layout_id: remaining = sorted(...); if remaining: map_bucket["active_custom_layout_id"] = remaining[0].get("id") else: map_bucket["active_custom_layout_id"] = None; if map_bucket.get("segmentation_mode") == "custom": map_bucket["segmentation_mode"] = "cv"` — the restore is inside the else. _migrate_custom_layouts:1502-1528 mints the legacy layout, sets active_custom_layout_id, and never assigns segmentation_mode. Presentation-only consequence confirmed: the sole non-mapping_services consumer of segmentation_mode is map_source.py:103 `if (map_bucket.get("segmentation_mode") or "cv") != "custom": return None`. Delete's response echoes segmentation_mode: 'custom' (:2437).

verdicts.reason: create forces segmentation_mode to custom unconditionally and stores no prior value; delete restores cv only in the zero-layouts branch, so create-then-delete on a map that already had a dormant layout strands the user in custom mode.
verdicts.evidence: mapping_services.py:2346 `map_bucket["segmentation_mode"] = "custom"` — unconditional, and no prior-mode field is written anywhere in the bucket, so the information is destroyed. _handle_delete_custom_layout:2422-2432: the restore is inside `if map_bucket.get("active_custom_layout_id") == layout_id:` and then `if remaining: map_bucket["active_custom_layout_id"] = remaining[0].get("id") else: ... if map_bucket.get("segmentation_mode") == "custom": map_bucket["segmentation_mode"] = "cv"` — the cv restore is only in the else. The dormant-layout precondition is real: _migrate_custom_layouts:1483-1528 mints cl_LEGACY named "Custom", sets active_custom_layout_id, and deliberately never writes segmentation_mode. Consequence verified: _resolve_active_scope's custom branch then serves cl_LEGACY's segments/links/anchors, and map_source.py:103 `if (map_bucket.get("segmentation_mode") or "cv") != "custom": return None` means build_furnished_render also switches on. The delete response returns segmentation_mode:"custom" with no hint that a set_segmentation_mode("cv") call is needed. Presentation-level only — room dispatch keys off device room ids.

title: Every handler in the block mints a persisted map bucket for an unknown map_id — including on the pure not-found and read-only clean paths
brands: Both for the phantom-bucket mechanism. The rename trigger is Roborock-specific (map NAME as id); the Roborock select's state changing on an in-app rename is near-certain but is device behaviour I could not verify from source.
observed_behavior: All ten handlers open with ensure_map_bucket (2341, 2361, 2383, 2452, 2486, 2526, 2545, 2566, 2595, 2652), which setdefaults a full bucket into manager.data (maps/map_manager.py:17-28), followed by _migrate_saved_zones / _migrate_custom_layouts which setdefault further keys. This happens BEFORE the `zone_not_found` / `layout_not_found` / `map_not_active` early returns, and before the two clean handlers — which mutate nothing conceptually — do any work. The early returns skip async_save, so the phantom is in-memory at that moment; but manager.async_save() persists the whole blob (core/manager.py:803-805), so the next save from ANY handler in the integration writes the phantom bucket to .storage permanently.
reproduction: Roborock. map_id is the vendor map NAME read from select.<id>_selected_map (adapters/roborock/adapter.py:190: "reports the map NAME (\"Main floor\")"). The user has 6 saved zones and 2 custom layouts under data["maps"][vacuum]["Main floor"]. They rename the map to "Ground floor" in the Roborock app. The select's state becomes "Ground floor"; the card now passes map_id="Ground floor" to every call. clean_saved_zone -> ensure_map_bucket setdefaults a brand-new empty bucket under "Ground floor" -> _migrate_saved_zones writes saved_zones={} into it -> zone lookup misses -> returns {"cleaned": false, "reason": "zone_not_found"}. Every zone and layout is now unreachable (stranded under the old key) and a phantom empty bucket exists, which get_vacuum_maps_summary (maps/map_manager.py:87-100) reports as a real map with room_count 0. Simpler variant, no rename needed: any single service call with a typo'd map_id ("Kitchn") permanently adds that map to the vacuum's map list.
user_impact: All saved zones and custom layouts for a floor appear to vanish after a vendor-side map rename, with no error and no migration path — the data is intact in .storage under the old key but unreachable through any service. Separately, phantom maps accumulate in the map summary from typos or stale ids. Both are directly the "does the edit land on the map it names / survive a re-import" failure: the geometry is filed under a free-form, user-renameable key with no identity layer.
guards_checked: (a) ensure_map_bucket has no exists-only variant in use here — get_map_bucket (maps/map_manager.py:55-74) is the non-mutating reader and IS used elsewhere (core/manager.py:1865, 3650), so the read-only accessor exists and simply is not used by these handlers. (b) The `zone_not_found` / `layout_not_found` returns happen after the mutation, not before. (c) No migration or alias table keys buckets by anything other than the raw map_id string. (d) This is distinct from the known-lead entity-id-prefix HIGH: the mechanism here is bucket minting on unknown ids and the loss mode is rename-strands-geometry.
doc_checked: docs/dev/17-map-manager.md:22 (map bucket contents, written by mapping_services) and :48-50; docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md:616 ("keyed at data[\"maps\"][<vacuum>][<map_id>]"); docs/dev/03-data-model.md. None of them state that map_id is stable across a vendor-side rename, and none document bucket creation as a side effect of a failed lookup.

verdicts.reason: Every handler in the block opens with ensure_map_bucket before any not-found return, including the two read-only clean handlers, and the read-only accessor that would avoid it exists and is used elsewhere in the integration. The Roborock rename trigger is real at the source level (map_id is the free-text vendor map NAME read off a select entity). This is the same mechanism as A1-SERVIC-1 reported from the zone/layout side — dedupe downstream.
verdicts.evidence: ensure_map_bucket called before the lookup in every handler: mapping_services.py:2341, 2361, 2383, 2452, 2486, 2526, 2545, 2566, 2595, 2652 — e.g. _handle_delete_saved_zone:2545-2551 mints the bucket, runs _migrate_saved_zones (which setdefaults saved_zones={}), and only then returns {"saved": False, "reason": "zone_not_found"}. maps/map_manager.py:17-28 is a pure setdefault; the non-mutating sibling get_map_bucket (map_manager.py:55-74) exists and is used at core/manager.py:1865. get_vacuum_maps_summary (map_manager.py:78-106) reports every bucket key as a map with room_count len(rooms). Roborock map_id source: adapters/roborock/adapter.py:190 'active_map (select.{id}_selected_map) reports the map NAME ("Main floor")'; rooms/room_discovery.py:74 returns str(value).

verdicts.reason: Every handler in the block calls ensure_map_bucket (which setdefaults a full bucket) before any not-found return, including the two read-only clean paths, and the non-mutating reader that would avoid it exists and is used elsewhere in the codebase.
verdicts.evidence: ensure_map_bucket appears at mapping_services.py:2341, 2361, 2383, 2452, 2486, 2526, 2545, 2566, 2595, 2652 — always the first statement after the call.data unpack, always before the `zone_not_found` / `layout_not_found` / `map_not_active` returns. maps/map_manager.py:17-28 setdefaults `{map_id, metadata, rooms, summary}`; _migrate_saved_zones (1386-1389) then writes `saved_zones = {}` into it. The read-only alternative exists and is used: get_map_bucket (maps/map_manager.py:55-74) returns a detached default without mutating, and core/manager.py:1865 and 3650 use it. title: Both clean handlers ignore the zone's `kind`, so a zone saved with any non-"clean" kind is still dispatched as a clean
observed_behavior: CREATE_SAVED_ZONE_SCHEMA accepts `vol.Optional("kind"): cv.string` with no allow-list (453); _handle_create_saved_zone passes it through (2483) and _create_saved_zone persists it verbatim (1412). Neither _handle_clean_saved_zone (2614-2628) nor _handle_clean_saved_zones (2672-2698) reads zone['kind'] — they take the geometry's bbox and dispatch it unconditionally. `kind` has no consumer anywhere in custom_components/ or src/.
reproduction: Call eufy_vacuum.create_saved_zone with name="cat bowls", kind="no_go", geometry=[...] (the service is documented in docs/advanced/03-services.md and the field is described as "reserved for future kinds"). The zone is stored with kind="no_go". Call clean_saved_zone on it -> rect derived, dispatch_zone_clean sends it -> the robot drives into and cleans the region the user labelled as a keep-out.
user_impact: Latent today: no UI produces a non-"clean" kind, so only a direct service call reaches this. It matters because the field is publicly accepted, publicly documented as extensible, and the failure mode when someone uses it is physical rather than an error. Either reject unknown kinds at the schema or gate dispatch on kind == "clean".
guards_checked: (a) The schema's cv.string — no vol.In allow-list. (b) `(kind or "clean").strip() or "clean"` at 1412 — normalises empty to "clean" but passes any other string through. (c) dispatch_zone_clean — receives only rects, so it cannot see kind. (d) Card-side: src/actions/saved-zones.js:43-54 forwards `kind` if the caller supplies one and never sets it itself.
doc_checked: docs/dev/frontend/saved-zones.md §3 (`"kind": str, # "clean" (default); reserved for future kinds`) and §12 Non-goals ("Not map editing (no-go zones, virtual walls) — the app owns that"). The doc reserves the field without stating that dispatch ignores it.

verdicts.reason: Verified that `kind` is accepted free-form, normalised only for blank, persisted, and then has no consumer anywhere — the clean handlers take the geometry bbox and dispatch without ever reading it. The field is publicly accepted and publicly documented as extensible, so a caller using it as documented gets a physical clean of a region they labelled otherwise.
