title: Zone size limits are not enforced at author time, contradicting the doc — an un-cleanable zone can be saved and only fails when the user taps clean
brands: Both (Eufy 0.5-10 m per side, Roborock 1 ft²-3.05 m²), per the caps quoted in the _handle_clean_saved_zones docstring at 2641-2642.
observed_behavior: _handle_create_saved_zone validates the name (2479-2481) and lets the schema clamp coordinates, but performs no size check: the computed area_m2 (2507) is stored and never compared against the adapter's zone_min_area_m2 / zone_max_area_m2 capabilities. Those bounds are only applied inside dispatch_zone_clean (dispatch/manager.py:164-177), plus the near-zero-side check at 110-118.
reproduction: Roborock (zone_min_area_m2 ~0.093 m² / 1 ft²). Draw a small box, e.g. normalized [[0.50,0.50],[0.52,0.50],[0.52,0.52],[0.50,0.52]] on a 6m-wide map -> 0.12m x 0.12m = 0.014 m². create_saved_zone succeeds and returns {saved: true}; the zone appears in the panel with its m² label. Every subsequent clean_saved_zone on it raises ValueError -> HomeAssistantError "a zone is too small (0.01 m²)" (mapping_services.py:2629-2630). In a MULTI-select batch it is worse: one undersized zone raises inside dispatch_zone_clean and aborts the whole batch, so none of the selected zones get cleaned.
user_impact: A zone that can never be cleaned is savable and looks valid in the list. The failure is loud (an error toast) rather than silent, hence LOW — but it is discovered at the wrong moment, and in a batch it blocks the other zones too.
guards_checked: (a) _saved_zone_coord / _SAVED_ZONE_POINT (429-455) — validates coordinate sanity and point count, not area. (b) dispatch_zone_clean's _MIN_SIDE=0.01 normalized check — a normalized-units floor, unrelated to the device's m² bounds. (c) Card side: no min/max area gate found in src/actions/saved-zones.js or src/bindings/saved-zones.js, so the doc's "enforced at author" is unmet on both server and client.
doc_checked: docs/dev/frontend/saved-zones.md §9 Validation — "reject/auto-tile a too-big zone, block a too-small one ... Enforced at author + at clean-time", and §8 "the size/count limits gate here". Only the clean-time half exists.

verdicts.reason: Create validates the name and lets the coordinate coercer clamp, but performs no size check against the adapter's declared bounds; those bounds are applied only inside dispatch_zone_clean, which raises. The doc explicitly promises enforcement at author time as well. The batch-abort consequence follows from the raise propagating out of the single shared dispatch call.
verdicts.evidence: _handle_create_saved_zone mapping_services.py:2478-2512: name check at :2479-2481, then _create_saved_zone, then the best-effort membership compute — the computed area_m2 at :2507 is stored and never compared against anything. Bounds live only at dispatch: dispatch/manager.py:164-177 (zone_min_area_m2 / zone_max_area_m2, raising 'a zone is too small (%.2f m²)') and :202-234 (zone_min_side_m / zone_max_side_m), plus the normalized _MIN_SIDE=0.01 at :110-118. verdicts.evidence: _handle_create_saved_zone:2479-2512 — `if not name: return missing_name`, then _create_saved_zone, then the best-effort membership compute at 2497-2510 which STORES area_m2 without comparing it to anything. title: A raster containing ZERO rooms is published as present:True — decode's own room_ids signal is computed and discarded
observed_behavior: decode_roborock_v1_segments computes `room_ids = sorted(b for b in set(room_pixels) if 1 <= b <= MAX_ROOM_RID)` (line 116) — the one signal that says whether the decoded segment layer actually contains any rooms. roborock_render_data never reads it. Its only emptiness gate is `if not rp or not width or not height: return None` (line 158), and `rp` is an all-zero bytes object, which is truthy. So a raster with no room pixels at all is wrapped as `{present: True, ...}` with no `reason`, and `roborock_render_data_from_candidates` (map_source_runtime.py:411, `if rd is not None: return rd`) stops scanning further candidate roots because it got a non-None answer.
reproduction: Blob = 20-byte map header (map_header_len @0x02 = 20) + one IMAGE block (type 2, header_len 24, data_len 30000, top 0, left 0, height 150, width 200) + 30000 bytes of 0x07 (MAP_SCAN — the state of every pixel while the robot is part-way through its FIRST mapping run, or after a map reset). Executed against the shipped module: `decode_roborock_v1_segments(blob)` returns room_ids=[] with 0 non-zero pixels (resolve_rid(0x07)==0), and `roborock_render_data(dec, {16: 'Kitchen'})` returns `present=True, width=200, height=150, room_names={'16': 'Kitchen'}`. Expected: an absent marker so the caller falls through to `{present: False, reason: 'no_raw_map'}`.
user_impact: The card's `isVaRenderActive()` (src/state/map.js:1201) only tests `mapRenderData()?.present`, so the VA (▦) backdrop switches on over a completely blank canvas, replacing the live Roborock map image the user was looking at. Every pixel hit-test (`roomIdAtContentPct`, src/state/map.js:965) returns null because rid is 0 everywhere, so the auto-derived click targets vanish and rooms become unclickable; per-room colours and floor textures disappear with them. Nothing surfaces a reason — the card, and diagnostics' self_check 'map decoded' verdict, both read this as a successfully decoded map. Common path (a fully mapped device) is unaffected; this bites during a first/partial scan, after a map reset, or if the BFS locks onto a stale MapContent.
guards_checked: roborock_render_data:158 `if not rp or not width or not height` — rp is b'\x00'*30000, truthy, passes. decode_roborock_v1_segments:111-114 (`width<=0 or height<=0 or pixel_count>data_len`, `data_start+pixel_count>n`) — all satisfied by a well-formed but unassigned blob. decode's own room_ids (line 116-118) — computed, never consulted by any caller. map_source_runtime.py:411 `if rd is not None` — accepts. map_source_coordinator.py:622-630 format dispatch — no post-check on the returned payload. src/bindings/map.js:223 `if (!canvas || !rd || !rd.present) return` — present is True.
doc_checked: docs/dev/29-roborock-adapter.md §`map_render` (states the raster's purpose is per-room colour / floor textures / pixel-exact hit-test — an all-background raster delivers none of them, and the doc never contemplates one). docs/dev/31-map-source-coordinator.md §3.4, which states the contract as 'Degrades to {present: False, reason}'.

title: raster_room_bboxes runs an O(width*height) pure-Python per-pixel loop directly on the Home Assistant event loop
observed_behavior: `for i, rid in enumerate(rp)` at line 200 iterates EVERY pixel of the decoded raster in Python, doing `i % w`, `i // w`, a dict `.get`, and up to four comparisons per pixel. There is no size cap: decode_roborock_v1_segments bounds width/height only by the blob length (lines 111-114), so the loop length is whatever the device's IMAGE block is. The call chain is entirely synchronous: raster_room_bboxes ← geometry_drift (line 259) ← map_source_runtime.roborock_geometry_drift_from_candidates:434 ← diagnostics.py:503, which sits inside `_vacuum_diagnostics(...)` — a plain sync function invoked from the coroutine `async_get_config_entry_diagnostics` at diagnostics.py:571, in a list comprehension, once per vacuum, with no `async_add_executor_job`.
reproduction: Roborock S6, map_state_source.backend == 'memory', a decodable raw blob. Settings → Devices & Services → Vacuum Agent → ⋮ → Download diagnostics. For an IMAGE block of 700x700 (a routine crop for a whole-floor S6 map) that is 490,000 Python loop iterations with two integer divisions and a dict lookup each, executed on the event loop thread. Contrast the render path for the SAME raster: decode_roborock_v1_segments + roborock_render_data touch every pixel only through `bytes.translate`, `set()`, `base64.b64encode` and `hashlib.sha1` — all C-level. The drift path is the only per-pixel Python loop in the module, and it is the one that is not offloaded.
user_impact: Downloading diagnostics stalls the entire HA event loop — every integration, every automation trigger, the frontend websocket — for the duration of the scan. On x86 that is roughly 0.1-0.3 s for a mid-size map; on a Pi-class or NAS host with a large map it is comfortably into multiple seconds, long enough for HA's own loop-lag warnings and for a websocket-connected card to visibly freeze. It repeats once per configured Roborock vacuum in the same download. Not data loss, and only on a user-initiated diagnostics download — but it is the one path in this module with no cost bound at all.
guards_checked: diagnostics.py:496-505 — a bare try/except around the call, no executor hop, no size or timeout guard. diagnostics.py:533-574 — `async_get_config_entry_diagnostics` is a coroutine and calls `_vacuum_diagnostics` synchronously at :571. map_source_coordinator.py:620 comments 'In-memory + pure -> loop-safe' — that claim covers the RENDER path (roborock_render_data_from_candidates), which is genuinely C-level; it does not cover the drift path, and the drift path has no equivalent claim or guard. decode_roborock_v1_segments has no maximum-dimension check that would bound the loop. geometry_drift/raster_room_bboxes have no early-exit or sampling.
doc_checked: docs/dev/29-roborock-adapter.md §'Surfaced in diagnostics' — 'This drift-check runs automatically ... best-effort, never raises.' The doc's only stated non-functional property is 'never raises'; nothing is claimed or reasoned about loop cost. docs/dev/31-map-source-coordinator.md §3.4 explicitly reasons about loop-safety for the render reader but says nothing about the drift validator.

verdicts.reason: The per-pixel loop is pure Python with two integer divisions and a dict lookup per pixel, has no size cap (decode bounds width/height only by the blob length), and the entire call chain from the diagnostics coroutine down is synchronous — _vacuum_diagnostics is a plain function invoked directly from async_get_config_entry_diagnostics inside a list comprehension, once per vacuum, with no async_add_executor_job anywhere.
verdicts.evidence: roborock_raw_map.py:200-215 `for i, rid in enumerate(rp): if not (1 <= rid <= MAX_ROOM_RID): continue; x, y = i % w, i // w; b = acc.get(rid); ...`. No dimension cap: decode_roborock_v1_segments:111-114 checks only width<=0/height<=0, pixel_count>data_len, data_start+pixel_count>n. Chain: geometry_drift:259 calls raster_room_bboxes -> map_source_runtime.py:414-434 roborock_geometry_drift_from_candidates (plain def) -> diagnostics.py:496-505 inside `_vacuum_diagnostics` (a `def`, not `async def`) -> diagnostics.py:571 `vacuums = [_vacuum_diagnostics(hass, manager, vac) for vac in vacuum_ids]` inside `async def async_get_config_entry_diagnostics`. Contrast: the render path touches pixels only via bytes.translate / set() / base64 / hashlib (roborock_raw_map.py:117-124, 163-179), which is what map_source_coordinator.py's 'In-memory + pure -> loop-safe' comment covers.

verdicts.reason: The per-pixel Python loop and the un-offloaded synchronous call chain to the HA event loop are both exactly as described. Correcting to LOW: measured cost is ~75 ms for a 700x700 raster, on a user-initiated diagnostics download only.
verdicts.evidence: roborock_raw_map.py:200-215 `for i, rid in enumerate(rp): ... x, y = i % w, i // w; b = acc.get(rid); ...` — pure Python, one iteration per pixel, no cap (decode bounds width/height only by blob length at 111-114). Chain verified: raster_room_bboxes ← geometry_drift:259 ← map_source_runtime.roborock_geometry_drift_from_candidates:434 ← diagnostics.py:496-505 (bare try/except, no async_add_executor_job) inside `def _vacuum_diagnostics(` (diagnostics.py:313 — a plain def), which `async def async_get_config_entry_diagnostics` (diagnostics.py:533) calls synchronously at :571 in a list comprehension, once per vacuum. Measured on this x86 host: a 700x700 (490,000-pixel) raster with 8 rooms took 0.0744 s. The render path for the same raster is bytes.translate / set() / b64encode / sha1 — all C-level — so this is the module's only Python-loop path and the only one not offloaded, exactly as claimed. Correcting MEDIUM→LOW: sub-100 ms on x86 (a few hundred ms on Pi-class), on an explicit user action, with no data or device consequence — the finder's "comfortably into multiple seconds" is not supported by measurement.

title: `version` hashes the raster ONLY, while the payload also ships room_names — a room rename cannot invalidate a fetched render payload
brands: roborock (the identical raster-only version hash exists for eufy in map_source.eufy_version_of, out of scope here)
observed_behavior: Line 163: `version = hashlib.sha1(raw).hexdigest()[:12]` where `raw = bytes(rp)` is the room-id raster and nothing else. The payload returned two lines later also carries `room_names` (line 178), sourced live from managed rooms via map_source_coordinator._roborock_render_room_names. So the declared content hash covers one half of the payload's content and silently omits the half that changes when the user edits the map. There is no other identity in the payload either — no map_id, no room-set stamp.
reproduction: Roborock, VA (▦) render active, room segment 16 named 'Kitchen' with a per-room colour override and a floor type set. (1) Card fetches render data once: room_names={'16':'Kitchen'}, version=sha1(raster). (2) User renames the room to 'Cocina' in the card. The raster bytes are untouched (a rename does not re-map the device), so any recomputed version would be byte-identical — and the card does not refetch on version change anyway: src/bindings/map.js:199 refetches only `if (!rd ...)`, and src/bindings/map.js:195 clears rd only when `activeMapId` changes. (3) src/bindings/map.js:335-346 bridges raster rid → the user's room BY NAME: `rgbByName` is built from the CURRENT rooms ('cocina') and looked up with `norm(ridNames[ridStr])` = 'kitchen'. Lookup misses, `overrideByRid[16]` stays unset.
user_impact: Immediately after renaming a room, that room's custom fill colour and its floor-type material silently disappear from the rendered map and it reverts to the default palette fill — with no error and no way to tell why. It stays wrong until the user reloads the card or switches the active map. The card's own comment (src/bindings/map.js:326-330) states that the name bridge is the ONLY correct bridge ('Keying by room.id directly is WRONG — the raster rid and our stored room.id are DIFFERENT id spaces on real devices'), so there is no fallback path. This is squarely the 'does the edit survive?' question: the edit lands in storage but the map render keeps rendering against the pre-edit vocabulary. Note the Eufy sibling map_source.eufy_version_of:621-628 has the identical raster-only hash, so this is a shared contract, not a Roborock-only slip — but Roborock's is the one minted here.
guards_checked: roborock_render_data:162-163 — `version` is only auto-computed when the caller passes None; no caller passes anything, so the raster-only hash always wins. No room_names, map_id, or room-set contribution to the hash. src/bindings/map.js:190-201 — the only invalidation is `_renderDataMapId !== mapId`; a rename does not change map_id. src/state/map.js:1192-1197 — setMapRenderData/mapRenderVersion just store and read; nothing compares versions to decide a refetch. src/bindings/map.js:355-356 — the ImageData cache keys on `rd.version` AND `overrideSig`, but overrideSig is itself derived from the stale ridNames, so the cache is self-consistently stale rather than incoherent.
doc_checked: docs/dev/31-map-source-coordinator.md §3.4: 'The card calls this on demand ... and caches by the returned `version`; the raster is static (changes only on a re-map), so it's fetch-once'. The doc asserts the payload is static, which is true of the raster but false of room_names — the doc calmly documents the fetch-once policy without reconciling it against the mutable field in the same payload. docs/dev/29-roborock-adapter.md §map_render describes room_names as coming from 'the adapter's discovered rooms' with no freshness contract.

verdicts.reason: version is minted from the raster bytes alone while the payload also ships room_names sourced from live managed rooms; no caller ever passes a version, so the raster-only hash always wins. The card's only invalidation is a map-id change, and the per-room colour bridge keys on the CACHED payload's rid->name map against the CURRENT room names, so a rename makes the lookup miss and the override silently disappears.
verdicts.evidence: roborock_raw_map.py:161-179: `raw = bytes(rp); if version is None: version = hashlib.sha1(raw).hexdigest()[:12]` and the returned dict carries both "room_names": {str(k): str(v) for k, v in names.items()} and "version": version. Cache key at :354-356 uses rd.version AND overrideSig, both derived from the stale payload.

title: ro_dx/ro_dy are hardcoded 0 and the decoded top/left are discarded — the payload cannot express any offset between the raw IMAGE-block frame and the parser's rendered frame
observed_behavior: decode_roborock_v1_segments reads `top` and `left` from the IMAGE-block header (lines 97-98) and returns them (lines 122-123), and then no consumer in the module ever uses them: roborock_render_data ignores them and instead hardcodes `ro_dx: 0, ro_dy: 0` (lines 171-172) with `ro_width/ro_height` set equal to the canvas (lines 169-170), defended by the comment 'the raster IS the canvas (no outline frame)'. That comment is a CLAIM that the raw IMAGE-block frame is pixel-identical to the frame every other Roborock overlay is normalized to — namely map_source_runtime._mapdata_projector (:438-470), which normalizes by the PARSER's rendered `image.data.size` after `dims.to_img` has applied the parser's trim/scale. The ro_dx/ro_dy fields exist precisely to carry such an offset (Eufy fills them from _outline_geometry, map_source.py:662-663); Roborock is the sibling where the knob is present but pinned to 0.
reproduction: Conditional on the HA roborock integration's ImageConfig trim, which is not inspectable from this repo. If the parser trims T rows off the rendered image's bottom of an H-row block: raw row r normalizes to (H-1-r)/H in this module's frame (raster_room_bboxes:219) but to (H-T-1-r)/(H-T) in the parser frame. H=700, T=50, r=100 → 0.8557 vs 0.8446, a 0.011 normalized delta = 0.39 m on a 700 px x 50 mm/px (35 m) map. If T==0 the frames coincide and this is inert. The shipped geometry_drift diagnostic is exactly the instrument that settles it: one 'Download diagnostics' on the real S6 reports `aligned` (frames coincide, no defect) or a systematic `max_center_delta` (frames differ, defect live).
user_impact: IF the frames differ: the card draws the raster full-bleed at 0..1 while every overlay it composites on top — room bboxes, robot/dock anchors, no-go and no-mop quads, saved zones — comes from map_state_source in the parser frame, so overlays sit offset from the rooms they label; `roomIdAtContentPct` (src/state/map.js:931-966) names the wrong room for clicks near a boundary; and a zone drawn on the raster is converted to device mm through `correspondences_from_mapdata` (the PARSER frame) at dispatch/manager.py:154, so app_zoned_clean cleans a displaced rectangle — the robot physically cleans the wrong strip of floor. The round-trip refuse-gate cannot catch it: zone_dispatch.max_residual_mm validates the affine against parser-frame correspondences only, which are self-consistent, so the residual is ~0 and the dispatch proceeds. Discarding top/left removes the only data in the blob that could have detected or corrected the offset.
guards_checked: roborock_render_data:169-172 — ro_* hardcoded, no derivation from decoded top/left. decode_roborock_v1_segments:122-123 — top/left returned but consumed by nothing in the module or its callers (grepped). zone_dispatch.normalized_rects_to_mm:119 round-trip gate — validates the fit against the same parser-frame points it was fit from, so a frame MISMATCH between card and dispatch is invisible to it. src/state/map.js:940-942 letterbox aspect — falls back to rd.width/height when image_size is absent, with the comment 'Both derive from the same md.width/height, so this is byte-identical whenever both exist', which is true for Eufy but is the same unverified claim for Roborock. geometry_drift exists and would detect it, but it is diagnostics-only and its verdict gates nothing.
doc_checked: docs/dev/29-roborock-adapter.md §Drift-check states outright that a delta is expected and that 'a constant offset = the parser's trim' — i.e. the doc anticipates the frames differing, yet the render payload has no field to carry that offset and doc §map_render simultaneously asserts 'the raster IS the canvas (no separate outline frame → ro_* = the canvas, ro_dx/dy = 0)'. Those two statements in the same doc cannot both hold if the trim is nonzero. docs/dev/31-map-source-coordinator.md §3.4 restates the ro_* = canvas claim without independent evidence.

verdicts.reason: The source-level facts are all as stated: decode reads top/left and returns them, no consumer in the module or its callers uses them, and roborock_render_data hardcodes ro_dx/ro_dy to 0 with ro_width/ro_height set equal to the canvas, defended only by a comment. The payload therefore has no field capable of expressing an offset between the raw IMAGE-block frame and the parser's rendered frame. The finding is honest that whether the two frames actually differ depends on the HA roborock integration's ImageConfig trim, which cannot be settled from this repo — I could not verify that premise either, and the shipped geometry_drift diagnostic is indeed the instrument that would settle it on a real device.
verdicts.evidence: roborock_raw_map.py:97-100 reads top/left/height/width; :122-123 returns "top": top, "left": left. grep for decoded['top'] / .get('top') across the module and its callers (map_source_runtime.py, map_source_coordinator.py, diagnostics.py) finds no consumer. roborock_render_data:169-172 `"ro_width": int(width), "ro_height": int(height), "ro_dx": 0, "ro_dy": 0,` with the inline comment 'the raster IS the canvas (no outline frame)'. The knob is filled from real geometry for the sibling brand: map_source.py:662-663 (_outline_geometry). raster_room_bboxes normalizes by the RAW frame (roborock_raw_map.py:219-222, dividing by w/h), while map_source_runtime._mapdata_projector:438-470 normalizes by the parser's own dims.to_img output over image.data.size. The round-trip gate cannot catch a frame mismatch because it validates the affine against the same parser-frame correspondences it was fit from (dispatch/manager.py:152-158).

verdicts.reason: The source-level claim holds exactly: ro_dx/ro_dy are literal zeros, and the decoded top/left are returned by the decoder and consumed by nothing, so the payload has no field able to express an offset between the raw IMAGE-block frame and the parser's rendered frame. Whether that offset is nonzero on a real device is not settleable from this repo.
verdicts.evidence: roborock_raw_map.py:169-172 `"ro_width": int(width), "ro_height": int(height), "ro_dx": 0, "ro_dy": 0` — hardcoded, with the comment "the raster IS the canvas (no outline frame)". decode_roborock_v1_segments:97-98 reads top/left and 122-123 returns them; grep across the module and its callers (map_source_runtime.roborock_render_data_from_candidates / roborock_geometry_drift_from_candidates) shows no consumer. The Eufy sibling fills the same fields from _outline_geometry (map_source.py:662-663), so the knob is present and pinned only here. map_source_runtime._mapdata_projector normalizes by the parser's rendered `image.data.size` after `dims.to_img`, i.e. a different frame by construction if the parser trims. zone_dispatch.normalized_rects_to_mm validates the affine against parser-frame correspondences only, so a card/dispatch frame mismatch produces ~0 residual and passes. UNRESOLVED FROM SOURCE: the HA roborock integration's ImageConfig trim is not in this repo, so I cannot compute the actual delta; the finder's 0.011-normalized / 0.39 m figure is a worked hypothetical with an assumed T=50, not a measurement. The shipped geometry_drift diagnostic is the instrument that would settle it on hardware. docs/dev/29-roborock-adapter.md does contain both statements the finder flags (a constant offset "= the parser's trim", and "ro_dx/dy = 0").

title: Two functions in this module read the same `flip_y` key with OPPOSITE defaults, so a decoded dict missing the key renders flipped but drift-checks unflipped
observed_behavior: roborock_render_data reads `bool(decoded.get('flip_y', True))` (line 174) — default True. raster_room_bboxes reads `bool(decoded.get('flip_y'))` (line 198) — no default, so a missing key yields False. Same key, same module, same `decoded` dict shape, opposite absent-means semantics. This is the 'absent is not zero' pattern: the drift validator treats a missing orientation flag as 'not flipped' while the renderer treats it as 'flipped'.
reproduction: Run against the shipped module with `d = {'width': 2, 'height': 3, 'room_pixels': bytes([5,5,0,0,0,0])}` (flip_y key absent), room 5 occupying raw row 0 only. raster_room_bboxes(d) returns {5: [0.0, 0.0, 1.0, 0.3333]}; with 'flip_y': True present it returns {5: [0.0, 0.6667, 1.0, 1.0]}. roborock_render_data(d)['flip_y'] is True for the SAME dict. The two boxes do not intersect, so _bbox_iou is exactly 0.0 and geometry_drift reports min_iou 0.0 / aligned False.

title: The IMAGE-block dimension guard is `header_len >= 16`, but the four dims occupy the LAST 16 bytes of a header whose first 8 are the fixed type/len fields — anything under 24 reads dims out of the header's own metadata
observed_behavior: Line 96 gates the dim reads on `header_len >= 16`, then reads top/left/height/width at `pos + header_len - 16 .. -4` (lines 97-100). The block header's first 8 bytes are fixed: type (int16 @0x00), header_len (int16 @0x02), data_len (int32 @0x04). So the four dim int32s only occupy bytes the format actually reserves for them when `header_len >= 24` — which is what the real v1 layout uses (tests/unit/test_roborock_raw_map.py:45-55 builds exactly a 24-byte header with dims at offsets 8/12/16/20 == header_len-16/-12/-8/-4). For header_len in 16..23 the guard passes and the reads slide backwards over the type/header_len/data_len fields.
reproduction: A block with type=2, header_len=20, data_len=D: `top = _u32(raw, pos+4)` == D (the data_len field re-read as a coordinate), `left = _u32(raw, pos+8)`, `height = _u32(raw, pos+12)`, `width = _u32(raw, pos+16)`. With header_len=16: `top = _u32(raw, pos+0)` == type | (header_len << 16) == 2 | 0x100000. The values are then carried into `image` (line 101) and, if `width*height <= data_len` and `data_start + width*height <= n` happen to hold, into a returned raster with garbage dims — no further sanity check exists.
user_impact: Not reachable on a well-formed v1 blob (roborock uses >= 24-byte IMAGE headers). It matters as the module's stated defence posture: the docstring at lines 14-16 says the byte walk is 'mirrored from vacuum-map-parser-roborock ... so a firmware format change is a one-file fix', and a firmware/format change is precisely the event that would present a short header. A `>= 24` guard would reject it as unparseable (returning None, which the caller degrades cleanly); `>= 16` accepts it and can emit a plausible-shaped raster built on coordinates read out of the header's own length fields. The other unchecked-offset risks in this walk are genuinely covered (see clean_areas) — this is the one gate that is looser than the format it guards.
guards_checked: decode_roborock_v1_segments:91 `header_len < 8 or pos + header_len > n` — bounds the read but says nothing about whether 16 bytes of DIMS fit after the 8 bytes of fixed fields. Lines 111-114 (`width<=0 or height<=0`, `pixel_count > data_len`, `data_start + pixel_count > n`) reject most garbage but are satisfiable by chance — none of them cross-checks the dims against anything independent. resolve_rid / the LUT cannot detect it. There is no minimum/maximum plausible-dimension check anywhere in the module.
doc_checked: docs/dev/29-roborock-adapter.md §map_render 'v1 only' spells out the layout: 'IMAGE block type == 2; top/left/height/width = int32 @ header[header_len-16..-4]' and the module docstring lines 18-25 repeat it — both describe the offsets relative to header_len without stating the minimum header_len that makes them valid, which is how the off-by-8 guard slipped in.

verdicts.reason: The arithmetic is right: the block header's first 8 bytes are fixed type/header_len/data_len, so the four dim int32s at header_len-16..-4 only occupy bytes reserved for them when header_len >= 24, yet the gate is >= 16. For header_len in 16..23 the reads slide backwards over the header's own metadata. The finding is explicit that this is latent on well-formed v1 blobs, and my attempt to build a short-header blob that survives the downstream sanity checks returned None — consistent with the finding's own 'if width*height <= data_len and data_start + width*height <= n happen to hold' framing.
verdicts.evidence: roborock_raw_map.py:89-100: `header_len = _u16(raw, pos + 0x02); if header_len < 8 or pos + header_len > n: break; block_type = _u16(raw, pos); data_len = _u32(raw, pos + 0x04); ... if block_type == _BLOCK_TYPE_IMAGE and header_len >= 16: top = _u32(raw, pos + header_len - 16); left = _u32(raw, pos + header_len - 12); height = _u32(raw, pos + header_len - 8); width = _u32(raw, pos + header_len - 4)`. With header_len == 20 those offsets are pos+4 (the data_len field), pos+8, pos+12, pos+16; with header_len == 16 the first is pos+0 (type | header_len<<16). The real layout is 24: tests/unit/test_roborock_raw_map.py:45-55 builds a 24-byte header with dims at 8/12/16/20. Executed a header_len=20 blob: decode returned None (width read as 0 tripped :111), confirming the case is not reachable by accident on the fixture I could construct. Module docstring lines 18-25 and docs/dev/29-roborock-adapter.md state the offsets relative to header_len without a minimum.

verdicts.reason: Executed: the `header_len >= 16` gate admits headers too short to hold the four dim int32s after the 8 bytes of fixed fields, and the reads then slide back over type/header_len/data_len — producing a decode that returns a plausible raster built on coordinates read out of the header's own metadata.
verdicts.evidence: roborock_raw_map.py:96-100 `if block_type == _BLOCK_TYPE_IMAGE and header_len >= 16: top = _u32(raw, pos + header_len - 16); left = ...-12; height = ...-8; width = ...-4`. With header_len=20 (data_len=30000, height 150, width 200 at offsets 12/16): decode returned {'width': 200, 'height': 150, 'top': 30000, 'left': 0, ...} — `top` is the data_len field re-read as a coordinate. With header_len=16: decode returned {'width': 4, 'height': 4, 'top': 1048578, 'left': 16, ...}, and 1048578 == 2 | (16 << 16) == the type and header_len int16s read as one int32, exactly as predicted. In both cases the function returned a non-None raster because lines 111-114 (`width<=0 or height<=0 or pixel_count > data_len`, `data_start + pixel_count > n`) happened to be satisfiable. The real v1 layout uses a 24-byte header (tests/unit/test_roborock_raw_map.py:45-55 builds dims at offsets 8/12/16/20 == header_len-16/-12/-8/-4), so `>= 24` is the correct gate. Not reachable on a well-formed blob; it matters only on the firmware/format change the module docstring says it is designed to absorb.

title: `_image_variant`'s `custom_` escape hatch and the unvalidated `map_id` are interpolated straight into a filesystem path — an upload can write or overwrite a PNG outside the maps directory
brands: Both. The accidental "/"-in-name case is Roborock-specific (free-text map names); the deliberate case is brand-independent.
observed_behavior: `_image_variant` (313-318) looks like a whitelist but its second clause `or value.startswith("custom_")` accepts ANY suffix. `UPLOAD_MAP_IMAGE_SCHEMA` (321-337) and `DELETE_MAP_IMAGE_SCHEMA` (339-345) validate `map_id` as bare `cv.string`. Both values reach `file_path = os.path.join(base_dir, f"map_{map_id}{suffix}.png")` (line 896) and `os.remove(file_path)` (line 1004) with no containment check. `os.makedirs(base_dir, exist_ok=True)` (line 900) creates only base_dir; it does not constrain where the subsequent `open(file_path, "wb")` lands. `object_id` is safe (cv.entity_id validated), map_id and variant are not.
reproduction: Arithmetic. base_dir = <config>/eufy_vacuum/maps/<object_id>. Call upload_map_image with variant="default" (suffix="") and map_id="../../../../www/pwn". file_path = os.path.join(base_dir, "map_../../../../www/pwn.png"). Path components after <config>: [eufy_vacuum, maps, <object_id>, "map_..", "..", "..", "..", "..", www, pwn.png]. The four literal ".." components pop "map_..", <object_id>, maps, eufy_vacuum, leaving <config>/www/pwn.png. `<config>/www` exists on a stock HA install and is served UNAUTHENTICATED at /local/pwn.png. open(...,"wb") succeeds because the directory already exists, so an existing PNG at that path is silently overwritten. The same string reaches os.remove via the stored `entry["path"]` on delete_map_image (line 1000-1004). Accidental variant, no attacker needed: a Roborock map named "Ground/First" makes file_path <config>/eufy_vacuum/maps/<obj>/map_Ground/First_dark.png; the intermediate directory is never created, so `open()` raises FileNotFoundError inside the executor job at line 901 — uncaught (the only try/except in that function wraps the PIL measure, line 905-911), so the service raises a raw OSError instead of the {"saved": false, "reason": ...} shape every other failure path uses.
user_impact: Deliberate case: any authenticated HA user who can call services (including non-admin) can write an arbitrary PNG to any existing directory the HA process can write, including publicly-served /config/www, and can silently destroy an existing .png there. Accidental case: a map whose vendor-side name contains "/" makes every image upload for that map fail with an unhandled traceback rather than a handled reason code. Common path (numeric/plain map names) is unaffected.
guards_checked: `_image_variant` itself (the fixed tuple at line 316 is bypassed by the startswith clause on the same line); `cv.entity_id` on vacuum_entity_id (protects object_id only); `os.makedirs(base_dir, exist_ok=True)` line 900 (creates base_dir, performs no containment check); the PNG-magic / PIL re-encode check lines 882-891 (validates CONTENT, not destination); no os.path.realpath / os.path.commonpath / relative-path assertion anywhere in the module; tracker.py:150 (`re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9_]", "_", ...)`) proves the slugify pattern exists in this codebase and was not applied at this seam; StaticPathConfig("/eufy_vacuum/maps", maps_dir) in __init__.py:192 serves the intended dir only — a traversed write lands outside it.
doc_checked: docs/dev/11-mapping-system.md:521-522 documents exactly this path template (`<config_dir>/eufy_vacuum/maps/<vacuum_slug>/map_<map_id>[_<variant>].png` and the matching browser URL) and states no sanitization requirement for the map_id/variant components; docs/dev/17-map-manager.md §2 documents `image_variants` entries carrying `path`/`browser_url` verbatim. Documented, not decided.

verdicts.reason: The headline claim — that an upload can write or overwrite a PNG OUTSIDE the maps directory — is false, and the stated reproduction cannot occur. The filename is built as f"map_{map_id}{suffix}.png", so the FIRST path component after base_dir always begins with the literal prefix "map_" and can therefore never be "." or "..". POSIX pathname resolution walks components in order and resolves ".." only relative to the ALREADY-RESOLVED preceding component, so "map_.." must exist as a real directory or the walk fails with ENOENT — it never exists (os.makedirs at line 900 creates only base_dir, and every artifact written there is a .png file, never a directory). The finder performed a LEXICAL normalization (as os.path.normpath does) that neither os.path.join nor open() performs. I executed the exact reproduction and the write failed. The finding's own sentence "open(...,"wb") succeeds because the directory already exists" is the false premise. (Its arithmetic is separately off by one: normpath of that path lands in <config>/eufy_vacuum/www, not <config>/www.) The residual true observation — that a map_id containing "/" raises an uncaught FileNotFoundError out of _write_and_measure instead of the structured {"saved": false, "reason": ...} shape — is real but is already reported as part of A3-IMAGE--5 and does not support this finding's title, severity, or security framing.
verdicts.evidence: mapping_services.py:894-901: suffix = "" if variant == "default" else f"_{variant}"; file_path = os.path.join(base_dir, f"map_{map_id}{suffix}.png"); then inside _write_and_measure, os.makedirs(base_dir, exist_ok=True) followed by open(file_path, "wb"). Executed reproduction (this machine, py3.14): base=<tmp>/config/eufy_vacuum/maps/robovac (created), <tmp>/config/www (created), map_id="../../../../www/pwn" -> os.path.join gives '.../maps/robovac/map_../../../../www/pwn.png'; os.path.normpath collapses it to '.../config/eufy_vacuum/www/pwn.png' (NOT config/www); open(fp,'wb') raised FileNotFoundError [Errno 2]. The same test with the 'accidental' name map_Ground/First_dark.png also raised FileNotFoundError — i.e. the separator case is an unhandled exception, not a write. The only try/except in _write_and_measure wraps the PIL measure (lines 905-911), so that OSError propagates.

verdicts.reason: The claimed wrong result — a PNG written or overwritten OUTSIDE the maps directory — does not reproduce on the deployment platform. The literal `map_` prefix is glued to the first path component, so escaping requires an existing directory whose name begins with `map_`; none is ever created (os.makedirs makes base_dir only). POSIX pathname resolution walks component-by-component and requires every prefix to exist, so open() returns ENOENT rather than traversing. The finder's own lexical arithmetic is also wrong by one level.
verdicts.evidence: Executed the exact construction. map_id="../../../../www/pwn" → file_path = <base>/map_../../../../www/pwn.png → open(...,"wb") raised FileNotFoundError [Errno 2]; nothing written; the www/ directory stayed empty. posixpath.normpath("/config/eufy_vacuum/maps/robovac/map_../../../../www/pwn.png") = "/config/eufy_vacuum/www/pwn.png", NOT "/config/www/pwn.png" as the finding states — "map_.." plus only three ".." pops three levels, not four. title: set_map_overlay_visibility's last-resort map resolution guesses the first stored map and reports saved:true against it
observed_behavior: When map_id is absent and get_active_map_id returns None (sentinel/unavailable active-map sensor, or the boot window where the sensor is registered but has no state — both explicit return-None paths in room_discovery), the handler falls back to `map_id = next(iter(vac_maps), None)` — the first key in `data["maps"][vacuum_entity_id]` by dict insertion order. It then ensure_map_buckets that id, writes the visibility delta, and returns `{"saved": True, "map_id": <guessed>, "overlay_visibility": <resolved>}`.
reproduction: A vacuum with two maps: `data["maps"]["vacuum.x10"] = {"1": {...upstairs...}, "2": {...downstairs...}}`, currently on map "2". During the post-restart window sensor.x10_active_map is "unknown", so get_active_map_id returns None. Call `eufy_vacuum.set_map_overlay_visibility {vacuum_entity_id: vacuum.x10, visibility: {no_go: true}}`. next(iter(...)) yields "1"; the delta is written to the UPSTAIRS bucket and the response is `{saved: true, map_id: "1", overlay_visibility: {...no_go: true...}}`. The map actually being displayed ("2") is unchanged, and the pref silently appears on the other map later.
user_impact: A display-only preference lands on a map the caller never named, reported as a success. Bounded: the card always supplies map_id (activeMapId() never returns falsy), so this needs a hand-written call on a multi-map vacuum during a blank-active-map window — an edge case. Recorded mainly because FURNIS-1's fix will wire five more services into map_id resolution: the shared resolved_call_data helper deliberately does NOT guess (its docstring: "silent fallback to a wrong map would be worse"), and this handler's extra guess should not be propagated with it. FURNIS-1's phantom "" bucket is also a valid next(iter(...)) winner.
guards_checked: get_active_map_id (rooms/room_discovery.py:43-88) — its three documented return-None paths are exactly the ones that reach this fallback; the `if not map_id: return {saved: False, error: "no_map"}` guard at 2252 — only fires when the vacuum has NO maps at all, so it never catches the wrong-map case; the response's `map_id` echo — the card's setMapOverlayVisibility (src/actions/map.js:402-412) does its optimistic flip and never reconciles against the returned map_id.
doc_checked: docs/advanced/03-services.md ("Auto-resolves to the active map (then the first stored map) when omitted") and the schema comment at the SET_MAP_OVERLAY_VISIBILITY_SCHEMA definition — the behaviour IS documented; reported as a hazard to the FURNIS-1 fix rather than an undocumented defect. services/_common.py resolved_call_data docstring documents the opposite (and safer) contract for every other service.

verdicts.reason: This is documented, deliberate intent with affirmative evidence of a decision in three independent places, not a defect — and the finding itself concedes it is 'reported mainly as a hazard to the FURNIS-1 fix rather than an undocumented defect'. The behaviour is stated at the definition site as an inline design comment, spelled out in the user-facing doc as an explicit named exception to the section's map_id rule, and implemented identically by an established sibling elsewhere in the integration. That is more than a doc calmly recording behaviour: it is the intent written at the site, cross-referenced to the sibling it was copied from. The consequence is confined to a display-only preference.
verdicts.evidence: The intent is written at the schema: mapping_services.py:637-640 comment on SET_MAP_OVERLAY_VISIBILITY_SCHEMA — 'Optional — blank/absent auto-resolves to the active map (then the first stored map), like the dashboard-snapshot service.' The handler comment repeats it at :2241 'Resolve map_id when omitted: active map, then the first stored map.' before :2250-2251 `vac_maps = manager.data.get("maps", {}).get(vacuum_entity_id, {}); map_id = next(iter(vac_maps), None)`. title: remap_confirmed_floor_types mutates in place while iterating, losing confirmations whenever old and new id sets overlap
observed_behavior: PROVEN by execution. The loop pops str(old_id) and writes str(new_id) into the SAME dict it is iterating over, so a new_id that is also a later old_id consumes the entry just written. Measured: id_remap={1:2, 2:3, 3:4} with rooms 1,2,3 confirmed yields {'4': True} -- 2 of 3 confirmations destroyed. A swap {1:2, 2:1} moves the confirmation onto the WRONG room. Disjoint remaps ({16:27}) are correct, which is why it looks fine: EVERY existing test uses a disjoint remap, so the defect is invisible to the suite by construction. Overlap is not exotic -- it is what happens whenever a device re-segments and reissues ids from the same range, while the disjoint case needs it to jump to a fresh block. The consequence is precisely what this function's own docstring says it exists to prevent: renumbered-but-confirmed rooms read as unconfirmed and the start gate blocks cleaning with onboarding_required. Fix is a new dict rather than in-place mutation.

title: Deleting map N from vacuum.X sweeps every entity of vacuum.X_N from the registry
observed_behavior: PROVEN. Room entity ids are make_room_unique_id -> {vac_key}_{map_id}_{room_id}_{suffix}. The post-delete registry sweep matches on {vac_key}_{map_id}_, so deleting map 2 from vacuum.alfred builds prefix vacuum_alfred_2_ -- which every entity of the SEPARATE vacuum vacuum.alfred_2 starts with, on EVERY map. Measured: all 8 of the sibling entities across two maps matched, and registry.async_remove deletes them. That loses name/area/icon/hidden customisations and releases the entity_id reservations, so entities can return under different ids and silently break automations and dashboards. The result reports entities_removed: N without saying whose. HA auto-suffixes a duplicate entity_id with _2, so vacuum.alfred plus vacuum.alfred_2 is an ordinary two-vacuum install and Eufy map ids are small integers -- uncommon, not exotic. Sharp detail: the trailing underscore DOES correctly prevent the map_id 2-vs-20 collision (verified as a control), so the prefix was designed against one ambiguity axis and misses the other. Seven sites hand-copy the pattern (sensor/__init__.py x4, number.py:101, switch.py:71, delete.py:136); only delete.py removes, but the others mark entities stale on the same match. ESCALATION (agent-found, verified at source): not limited to the two-vacuum case. adapters/roborock/adapter.py:190 documents its active-map entity select.{id}_selected_map as reporting the map NAME ('Main floor'), and get_active_map_id returns str(state.state) verbatim, so on Roborock a map_id is a human string that can contain underscores. Maps named 'Main' and 'Main_floor' collide WITHIN one vacuum. That removes the 'needs two similarly-named vacuums' precondition entirely for Roborock users. A second agent independently confirmed the {map}_{room} boundary is NOT ambiguous (room_id is int-coerced), so the ambiguity is confined to the vacuum_key<->map_id boundary -- i.e. exactly this finding, and nowhere else.

title: The maintenance sensor's documented availability guard never fires; it publishes a fabricated full-life value
observed_behavior: CONSUMER SIDE OF DR-MNT-1 -- same root cause at maintenance/manager.py:713. CLUSTER THESE. The class docstring claims 'Returns available = False (and native_value = None) when the source entity is unavailable so stale hours are never silently reported' -- a claim, not evidence. source_available is set True whenever hass.states.get(source) is not None, which holds for an UNAVAILABLE entity; it returns None only when the entity does not exist. HA drops extra_state_attributes while unavailable, so usage_hours is absent, the `, 0` default wins, and current_usage becomes 0.0 with source_available True. Repro (numbers corrected by Stage B execution -- my original prose transposed them): a healthy source at 108h against a 66h baseline reads native_value 108.0 / used_since_reset 42.0; the upstream integration reloads; the next poll reports 150.0h remaining, used_since_reset 0.0, source_available true, and the warning transition never fires. state_class measurement means the recorder ingests the fabricated value into long-term statistics. Sibling proof in the same module: maintenance/manager.py:369 uses .get('usage_hours') with NO default, so a missing attribute raises and yields an honest None.

title: _LOCAL_TZ is a FIXED offset captured at import, so naive legacy timestamps get the wrong offset half the year

title: A raw stored null theme name renders as the string 'None' — valid, but not reachable in normal operation
observed_behavior: Split half B of the original SN-10, and the half both lenses agreed on. `str(entry.get('name', 'none'))` returns Python's str(None) == 'None' for a stored null rather than the intended 'none', and an empty string yields an empty state. CONFIRMED_EXECUTED by Stage B's reproducer at the line. REACHABILITY IS THE NARROW PART: no writer can produce it — import_theme stringifies, and _normalize_theme_entry gates stored entries — so it requires a direct .storage edit (discouraged; see the never-edit-.storage rule) or legacy pre-normalization data. Fix is one expression: `(entry.get('name') or 'none')`, which also handles the empty-string case. Low reachability, real defect, trivial repair — a candidate for `document_only` if Chris prefers.

title: The job-active warning asserts a run-time failure that is unreachable from the state triggering it — and computes presence from a stale snapshot
observed_behavior:
SETTLED ON HARDWARE. THE SYSTEM BEHAVES CORRECTLY; THIS IS A REPORTING-LAYER DEFECT ONLY.

When a Roborock idles out it drops the cloud connection and the upstream integration REMOVES the entities — HA reports them as no-longer-provided and vacuum.<vac> becomes a restored stub. Every layer reports this honestly: the integration says the entity stopped being provided, the card says no map is loaded, and binary_sensor.<vac>_cleaning is genuinely absent. See reference_roborock_idle_disconnect.md.

(1) THE WARNING IS UNREACHABLE-BY-CONSTRUCTION. It says "EVERY run will strand (never finalize). Check the upstream integration didn't drop this entity." But from that state NO RUN CAN BE STARTED — vacuum.<vac> is a restored stub with no platform behind it, so the dispatch service call has nothing to reach. The warning describes a run-time failure mode in a state where runs cannot be initiated, and its remedial advice points at an upstream regression when the real cause is an idle device that a single wake resolves. Cost: three successive wrong diagnoses in this campaign.

(2) RESIDUAL, AND THE PART WORTH FIXING: presence is computed from the wrong source. diagnostics.py:364 reads the LIVE adapter config for the entity id; :365 reads entity_resolution, built from get_vacuum_capabilities(refresh=False) — a STORED snapshot whose entity map lacks the job_active key entirely. That is latent today but WOULD produce a genuinely false alarm any time the snapshot lags while the entity exists. Same root as DR-DIAG-1; belongs in that cluster.

LOW because no user-visible product behaviour is wrong — only the wording of one diagnostic string and a latent source-of-truth error behind it. Fix: resolve job_active from hass.states via the adapter-declared id (as :364 already does), and reword to state the observed condition — device appears disconnected, wake it — instead of asserting permanent failure.
